1-5 This book contains the speeches that Moses made while Israel was in the land of Moab, camped near the town of Suph in the desert east of the Jordan River. The town of Paran was in one direction from their camp, and the towns of Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab were in the opposite direction.
Earlier, Moses had defeated the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. Moses had also defeated King Og of Bashan, who used to live in Ashtaroth for part of the year and in Edrei for the rest of the year.
Although it takes only eleven days to walk from Mount Sinai to Kadesh-Barnea by way of the Mount Seir Road, these speeches were not made until 40 years after Israel left Egypt.
The First Speech: Moses Reviews the Past
The Lord's Command at Mount Sinai
The Lord had given Moses his laws for the people of Israel. And on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses began explaining those laws by saying:
6People of Israel, when we were in our camp at Mount Sinai, the Lord our God told us:
You have stayed here long enough. 7Leave this place and go into the land that belongs to the Amorites and their neighbors the Canaanites. This land includes the Jordan River valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Southern Desert, the Mediterranean seacoast, the Lebanon Mountains, and all the territory as far as the Euphrates River. 8I give you this land, just as I promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Now you must go and take the land.
Leaders Were Appointed
(Exodus 18.13-27)
Moses said:
9Right after the Lord commanded us to leave Mount Sinai, I told you:
Israel, being your leader is too big a job for one person. 10The Lord our God has blessed us, and so now there are as many of us as there are stars in the sky. 11God has even promised to bless us a thousand times more, and I pray that he will. 12But I cannot take care of all your problems and settle all your arguments alone. 13Each tribe must choose some experienced men who are known for their wisdom and understanding, and I will make those men the official leaders of their tribes.
14You answered, “That's a good idea!” 15Then I took these men, who were already wise and respected leaders, and I appointed them as your official leaders. Some of them became military officers in charge of groups of 1,000, or 100, or 50, or 10, 16and others became judges. I gave these judges the following instructions:
When you settle legal cases, your decisions must be fair. It doesn't matter if the case is between two Israelites, or between an Israelite and a foreigner living in your community. 17And it doesn't matter if one is helpless and the other is powerful. Don't be afraid of anyone! No matter who shows up in your court, God will help you make a fair decision.
If any case is too hard for you, bring the people to me, and I will make the decision.
18After I gave these instructions to the judges, I taught you the Lord's commands.
Men Were Sent To Explore the Hill Country
(Numbers 13.1-33)
Moses said to Israel:
19The Lord had commanded us to leave Mount Sinai and go to the hill country that belonged to the Amorites, so we started out into the huge desert. You remember how frightening it was, but soon we were at Kadesh-Barnea, 20-21and I told you, “We have reached the hill country. It belongs to the Amorites now, but the Lord our God is giving it to us. He is the same God our ancestors worshiped, and he has told us to go in and take this land, so don't hesitate and be afraid.”
22Then all of you came to me and said, “Before we go into the land, let's send some men to explore it. When they come back, they can tell us about the towns we will find and what roads we should take to get there.”
23It seemed like a good idea, so I chose twelve men, one from each tribe. 24They explored the hill country as far as Bunch Valley 25and even brought back some of the fruit. They said, “The Lord our God is giving us good land.”
Israel Refused To Obey the Lord
(Numbers 14.1-45)
Moses said to Israel:
26 You did not want to go into the land, and you refused to obey the Lord your God. 27You stayed in your tents and grumbled, “The Lord must hate us—he brought us out of Egypt, just so he could hand us over to the Amorites and get rid of us. 28We are afraid, because the men who explored the land told us that the cities are large, with walls that reach to the sky. The people who live there are taller and stronger than we are, and some of them are Anakim. We have nowhere to go.”
29Then I said, “Don't worry! 30The Lord our God will lead the way. He will fight on our side, just as he did when we saw him do all those things to the Egyptians. 31 And you know that the Lord has taken care of us the whole time we've been in the desert, just as you might carry one of your children.”
32 But you still would not trust the Lord, 33even though he had always been with us in the desert. During the daytime, the Lord was in the cloud, leading us in the right direction and showing us where to camp. And at night, he was there in the fire.
34 You had made the Lord angry, and he said:
35You people of this generation are evil, and I refuse to let you go into the good land that I promised your ancestors. 36Caleb son of Jephunneh is the only one of your generation that I will allow to go in. He obeyed me completely, so I will give him and his descendants the land he explored.
37The Lord was even angry with me because of you people, and he said, “Moses, I won't let you go into the land either. 38Instead, I will let Joshua your assistant lead Israel to conquer the land. So encourage him.”
39Then the Lord spoke to you again:
People of Israel, you said that your innocent young children would be taken prisoner in the battle for the land. But someday I will let them go into the land, and with my help they will conquer it and live there.
40Now, turn around and go back into the desert by way of Red Sea Road.
41Then you told me, “We disobeyed the Lord our God, but now we want to obey him. We will go into the hill country and fight, just as he told us to do.” So you picked up your weapons, thinking it would be easy to take over the hill country.
42But the Lord said, “Moses, warn them not to go into the hill country. I won't help them fight, and their enemies will defeat them.”
43I told you what the Lord had said, but you paid no attention. You disobeyed him and went into the hill country anyway. You thought you were so great! 44But when the Amorites in the hill country attacked from their towns, you ran from them as you would run from a swarm of bees. The Amorites chased your troops into Seir as far as Hormah, killing them as they went. 45Then you came back to the place of worship at Kadesh-Barnea and wept, but the Lord would not listen to your prayers.
Israel Spent Years in the Desert
Moses said to Israel:
46After we had been in Kadesh for a few months, we obeyed the Lord and headed back into the desert by way of Red Sea Road.
translation_text:
1Etemila amɛni na Mose ɔ́kɔ lɛsa úte Israelƒuɔ uwi ɔni na bakya kalɔ kakwiidi kani na Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na kɔwɛ kemmo. Na mmɔ ɔkya Paran ku Totel ku Laban ku Haserot ku Di-Sahab ntɛ. 2Ɔ́si Sinai kɔbi úti útédu Kades-Barnea ɔdi emeyi leevu-unwi ulu busie si ásia Edom abi kalɔ ulu lɛlɔ.
3Ɔƒɛni na bana mmɔ bɔkya lɛkwa aavlenedi kemmo na kɔbuli leevu-unwi limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, Mose ɔ́kɔ lɛsa úte Israelƒuɔ ala ani na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔ́siku-ma lɛlɔ. 4Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, úukpo ɔ́di Amoriƒuɔ ɔga ɔni baalɔ Sihon na uli Hesbon ɔma kemmo lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́ɔdi Ɔga Og ɔni mɔɔnu Basan kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ na uli Astarot ku Edrei lɛma kemmo.
5Na Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na Moab kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, Mose úse kalɔ uudie Katɔti ɔda bubo etemila kalɔ teete-ma.
6Uwi ɔni kemmo na bɔ́kya Sinai kɔbi lɛlɔ ni, bula Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su-bu ɔnini, “Bíilie kɔbi kɔmɛni lɛlɔ bítu uwi bɛ́gya. 7Anwuɔsu bɛta mɛni na biteesie Amoriƒuɔ abi lɛlɔ kɔlɔ kɔni nkya amadɔ mmɔ ƒui ku Yordan Ketu kɔwɛ kemmo ku abi lɛlɔ ku ɔkwalɛ ɔmmɔ kemmo ku kada kakɛ ku Mediterenia kalɔ ƒia lɛlɔ. Na bisie Kanaanƒuɔ kalɔ ku nwuna kama kakɛ útédu Lebanon abi lɛlɔ útédu Euƒrate Ketu bonwu kɔtu. 8Bɛnu bɛti ka kalɔ kamɛni ƒui na líti muute-mii. Biteesie na bitéti-ka binwini bina kadikɔ. Kalɔ kammɔ na Lɛ́su líse ka ndubuti lite bina bati kuuku bani ndi Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob ku nwuna bawɔ.”
Mose Údie Litemi Batɛne
9Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ami Mose lɛ́su-mii ḿbavi uwi ɔni na bɔ́kya Sinai kɔbi lɛlɔ ka bina bɔtɔnku kabla kétulo-mi. Na ami lɛti naaakana kabla kamɛni bɔbla. 10Na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na bíimomo aani katɔ ayabi. 11Na muuvele nnii Katɔti ɔni ndi bina bati kuuku Unwoti ɔya na bɛsɔ bimomo mpim mpim bibu na ute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na lɛla biala kemmo aani kalɛ na ɔ́su úse. 12Nsu dɛ na wabla na ami lɛti mataatɛ bina ala ani muukpóku-mii ku unyeƒi si ɔdi ɔlɛku ɔdi? 13Ɔmɛni ɔsu amii ɔlati bɛƒuna bekyuli bani na báda anu na bebo ɔbu na báanu dii na kɔdua biala kemmo na ndubɔya na ama bataabla kabla kamɛni teete-mii. 14Amu na bɛ́su ka lɛla lɛni na lɛ́su mɛni ni, lɛdia.
15Anwuɔsu bekyuli bani náda anu na bebo ɔbu bani na amii alati bídie mɛni ni, lɛ́ya badi baanu bekyuli apim lɛlɔ na badi lɛnɔ baanu bekyuli eti anyɔ lɛlɔ na badi lɛnɔ baanu bekyuli liti lɛlɔ na badi lɛnɔ baanu bekyuli leevu lɛlɔ. Na ami lɛnɔ lɛ́sia-ma kɔnu ka batɔnku-mii. 16Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, líbo-ma ɔda ka litemi biala na ɔdi weti weboku na badi Israelƒuɔ banwa lɛti lɛti iye Israelni ku ɔƒɔ ntɛ na ɔƒɔ ɔmmɔ ɔkya-mii akɔ ni, batɛ-ni ulu lɛlɔ. 17Na ɔdi utanu anumi utatɛ litemi lɛdi. Mmomu batɛ-ni ulu lɛlɔ. Ɔlakɛne na ɔdi o-o, ɔwabane na ɔdi o-o ni, batayia ɔdi biala. Batɛku ɔdi biala litemi kalɛ kani na ɔ́manku-nwu. Na mɔɔsu-mii nnii kalɛ biala na litemi lɛmmɔ lise ni, Katɔti ɔdubute-ma kasusu na batɛ-ni ulu lɛlɔ. Na lɛ́su-ma ka si litemi bɔtɛ bɔdi bútulo-ma ni, beti litemi lɛmmɔ beboku-mi na lɛtɛ lite-ma. 18Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo lɛ́su-mii lɛla biala na ɔlɛka bɛbla.
Mose Údie Bekyuli Badi Ka Babɛ Besie Batánu Kades-Barnea
19Na bitayiƒala kalɛ na bɔ́ta Sinai kɔbi lɛlɔ na bɔkɛ kalɔ kakwiidi bonwu kani mɔɔda liƒu kemmo na bɔkɛ ulu búsela Amoriƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Katɔti úbo-bu ɔda, na bútédu Kades-Barnea. 20Asa na bɔdubuduo Amoriƒuɔ abi kalɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, lɛ́ya-mii bɛ́ti kesii kani na Bula Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka weti wete-bu. 21Anwuɔsu bɛɛnu kalɔ kammɔ ka kewi mmɔ. Biteesie na bitéti-ka aani kalɛ na Unwoti ɔni ndi bina bati kuuku Katɔti ɔ́su-mii. Na bitayia ukyuli ɔdi, na enu ataƒɛ-mii lɛnɔ.
22Nsu bínwini bíbo-mi kudɔ na bɛ́su-mi bɛnini, “Ya na bɔtala bekyuli badi na bagyu batɔ na betéyu kalɔ kammɔ banu. Na babasu-bu ulu ɔni ndia ntulo ka bɔsia, na basu-bu lɛnɔ lɛma libendi lɛni nkya amadɔ mmɔ.”
23Na lɛ́nu ka lɛla lɛbuni na bɛ́su. Anwuɔsu lídie nkyuli leevu-inyɔ lɛ́siku kɔdua biala kemmo. 24Na bekyuli bamɛni béti anumi bátina abi ulu útédu ka béduo Eskol Kɔwɛ kemmo na báka bámana na básia kalɔ kammɔ anu kaduɛɛ. 25Na béti edula ani nkya mmɔ adi bábatina-bu, na básu-bu ka bula Unwoti Katɔti kalɔ kani na úti úte-bu mmɔ ni, kaadia edula geen.
26Nsu bɛ́ta bínye nwuna ɔda ɔni na úbo-bu lɛlɔ, anwuɔsu kɔnu kútetuku-mii kalɔ kammɔ. 27Lɛnɔ ni, bɛ́kya bina nvo kemmo bítaatɛmi taakya enwu kemmo. Na bɛ́su bɛnii, “Katɔti uukisi-bu, anwuɔsu na ɔ́ya na bɔ́ta bɔ́lɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ kalɛ na uti-bu ute Amoriƒuɔ na bebo-bu badu.” 28Na bɛ́sɔ bɛ́su bɛnii, “Wɛ bɔdubusie ɔƒɛni? Ɔsika bekyuli bani na bɔ́tala mmɔ básu-bu ka bekyuli bani nkya mmɔ bebo ɔlɔkplu na bákuku betulo-bu. Na belie lɛma libendi lɛni nina awodu ákuku ésie kayaa. Na bɔ́nu bekyuli bani na baalɔ-ma Anakƒuɔ lɛnɔ ka bakya mmɔ.”
29Nsu lɛ́su-mii nnii, “Bitayia bekyuli bammɔ. 30Ɔsika bina Unwoti ndubo-mii bɔtɔnku, na ɔdubo bina kekpo ƒui bukpo bute-mii aani kalɛ na bɛ́nu kalɛ na úkpo úte-mii na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ 31ku kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo. Na bɛ́nu kalɛ na ɔ́da-mii na úti-mii úbedu kesii kani bɔkya mɛni aani kalɛ na ubi ɔti ɔɔda ubidi.”
32Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui ni, bítaƒɔ bina Unwoti Katɔti bítadi, 33ina ka anwu nágyu ɔtɔ-mii na útáwia ekpo ani na bɛdubulie na bɛnwuna úte-mii. Na anwu kani nátaawia ulu teete-mii. Anwu néteete-mii ogya na ɔɔtɔnku-mii usien na ɔɔyá na liƒlukutu lɛɛtɔnku-mii na limeyi kemmo.
Katɔti Ɔ́ni Israelƒuɔ Kɔtu
34Na ka bina ɔbladu ulayɔ Katɔti kaƒɔ ɔsu ni, ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen. Ɔmɛni ɔsu úse kenye na ɔ́su ɔnini, 35“Bina kaba kekpidi kamɛni kadi biala ɔgba ɔɔɔdubo bɔnya kalɔ kabuni kani na lɛ́su líse ka meti mete bina bati kuuku mmɔ lɛlɔ 36amu ntu Yeƒune ubidi ɔnanabi Kaleb lɛti. Anwu kani nwuna lɛgba ndubo kalɔ kammɔ bɔnya. Na anwu ku nwuna bawɔ lɛti ndubo kalɔ kammɔ bɔdi. Ɔsika ɔ́ƒɔ Katɔti ɔ́di ku nwuna kayi ƒui.”
37Na ami Mose lɛnɔ mɔɔsu-mii nnii ɔ́si amii ɔsu na Katɔti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-mi na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ina awɔ Mose muedi ni, ƒula ɔgba ɔɔɔdubo kalɔ kammɔ bɔnya. 38Nsu Nun ubidi ɔni baalɔ Yosua na unye-ɔ anumi mmɔ anwu ni, nwuna ɔgba ɔdubo kalɔ kammɔ bɔnya. Anwuɔsu kya-nwu ogya, ɔsika anwu ndubo Israelƒuɔ bɔtɔnku na betélie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.”
39Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su bula ƒui ɔnini, “Bina bebi bani nátabi tɔ lɛlɔ kalɛ banu lɛbuni ku likpidi bati ni, bana lɛgba ndubɔnya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Bebi bani bɛ́kya bítaasu bɛnii bina bekisine badubukpo bɔƒɔ ni, ama ndubo kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ bulie. 40Nsu amii ni, binwini kama na bɛsia Ɛpugyie ulu ɔni ntɔ-mii anumi mmɔ lɛlɔ.”
41Amu na amii ɔlati bídie kenye bɛnii, “Mose, sɔsɔ bɔ́ta búnye bula Unwoti Katɔti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔƒɛni ni, bɔdubɔdi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Na bɔdubɔta busie abi ammɔ lɛlɔ na butékpo ku bekyuli bammɔ aani kalɛ na Katɔti ɔ́su-bu mmɔ.” Anwuɔsu bɛ́ta na bíti bina ekpola adala bɛ́kya na bɛ́tu akpagya. Amii bɛ́kali ka abi kalɔ lɛlɔ bɔkɔ busie bɔtɛ kalɔ.
42Nsu Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Bo-ma ɔda ka ɔdi biala utata utetékpo. Ɔsika lɛɛɛdubo-mii kama bunye. Na bina bekisine badubɔdi-mii lɛlɔ.” 43Lɛ́su-mii ala ani na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ka nsu-mii. Nsu bina ɔdi biala úteti nwuna litemi. Mmomu bɔta na bɛ́ta bínye nwuna litemi lɛlɔ. Na amii alati bíti bina ekpola na bɛ́ta na bina lɛkantakpi kemmo bísie abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ka bitékpo. 44Na ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na Amoriƒuɔ bani nli abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kammɔ amadɔ báta bábabi básiaku-mii aani kalɛ banwɛnwɛ lisu bonwu lɛɛta. Na bábi básiaku-mii na bádu-mii kaduɛ básiku Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ mmɔ laa útédu Horma. 45Anwuɔsu bɛ́va bɛ́kpali Katɔti ka ubebunku-mii. Nsu útakpete-mii.
46Amu na bílie Kades uwi gyɔlɔɔ kalɛ bɛɛyɔ́.

english_text:
1 We spent many years wandering around outside the hill country of Seir, 2until the Lord said:
Moses, 3Israel has wandered in these hills long enough. Turn and go north. 4 And give the people these orders: “Be very careful, because you will soon go through the land that belongs to your relatives, the descendants of Esau. They are afraid of you, 5but don't start a war with them. I have given them the hill country of Seir, so I won't give any of it to you, not even enough to set a foot on. 6And as you go through their land, you will have to buy food and water from them.”
7The Lord has helped us and taken care of us during the past 40 years that we have been in this huge desert. We've had everything we needed, and the Lord has blessed us and made us successful in whatever we have done.
8We went past the territory that belonged to our relatives, the descendants of Esau. We followed Arabah Road that starts in the south at Elath and Ezion-Geber, then we turned onto the desert road that leads to Moab.
9 The Lord told me, “Don't try to start a war with Moab. Leave them alone, because I gave the land of Ar to them, and I will not let you have any of it.”
Tribes That Lived near Canaan
10Before the Lord gave the Moabites their land, a large and powerful tribe lived there. They were the Emim, and they were as tall as the Anakim. 11The Moabites called them Emim, though others sometimes used the name Rephaim for both the Anakim and the Emim.
12The Horites used to live in Seir, but the Edomites took over that region. They killed many of the Horites and forced the rest of them to leave, just as Israel did to the people in the land that the Lord gave them.
Israel Crossed the Zered Gorge
Moses said to Israel:
13When we came to the Zered Gorge along the southern border of Moab, the Lord told us to cross the gorge into Moab, and we did. 14 This was 38 years after we left Kadesh-Barnea, and by that time all the men who had been in the army at Kadesh-Barnea had died, just as the Lord had said they would. 15-16The Lord kept getting rid of them until finally none of them were left.
17Then the Lord told me, 18“Moses, now go past the town of Ar and cross Moab's northern border 19 into Ammon. But don't start a war with the Ammonites. I gave them their land, and I won't give any of it to Israel.”
More Nations That Lived near Canaan
20Before the Ammonites conquered the land that the Lord had given them, some of the Rephaim used to live there, although the Ammonites called them Zamzummim. 21The Zamzummim were a large and powerful tribe and were as tall as the Anakim. But the Lord helped the Ammonites, and they killed many of the Zamzummim and forced the rest to leave. Then the Ammonites settled there. 22The Lord helped them as he had helped the Edomites, who killed many of the Horites in Seir and forced the rest to leave before settling there themselves.
23A group called the Avvim used to live in villages as far south as Gaza, but the Philistines killed them and settled on their land.
Israel Crossed the Arnon Gorge
Moses said:
24After we went through Ammon, the Lord told us:
Israel, pack up your possessions, take down your tents, and cross the Arnon River gorge. The territory of the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon lies on the other side of the river, but I now give you his land. So attack and take it! 25Today I will start making all other nations afraid of you. They will tremble with fear when anyone mentions you, and they will be terrified when you show up.
The Defeat of King Sihon of Heshbon
(Numbers 21.21-30)
Moses said to Israel:
26After we had crossed the Arnon and had set up camp in the Kedemoth Desert, I sent messengers to King Sihon of Heshbon, telling him that his nation and ours could be at peace. I said:
27Please let Israel go across your country. We will walk straight through, without turning off the road. 28-29You can even sell us food and water, and we will pay with silver. We need to reach the Jordan River and cross it, because the Lord our God is giving us the land on the west side. The Edomites and Moabites have already let us cross their land. Please let us cross your land as well.
30-31But Sihon refused to let us go across his country, because the Lord made him stubborn and eager to fight us. The Lord told me, “I am going to help you defeat Sihon and take his land, so attack him!”
32We met Sihon and his army in battle at Jahaz, 33and the Lord our God helped us defeat them. We killed Sihon, his sons, and everyone else in his army. 34Then we captured and destroyed every town in Sihon's kingdom, killing everyone, 35but keeping the livestock and everything else of value. 36The Lord helped us capture every town from the Arnon River gorge north to the boundary of Gilead, including the town of Aroer on the edge of the gorge and the town in the middle of the gorge.
37However, we stayed away from all the Ammonite towns, both in the hill country and near the Jabbok River, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Israelƒuɔ Bélie Kalɔ Kakwiidi Kemmo Akwa Adi
1Amu na bɔ́sɔ búnwini búti búsela kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ lɛlɔ na bɔkɛ Ɛpugyie ulu lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Katɔti ɔ́su-bu. Na mmɔ na bɔ́kya bɔ́ka bɔmana Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ mmɔ bútu uwi gyɔlɔɔ.
2Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, 3“Bɛ́ɛka bɛ́mana abi amɛni lɛlɔ bítu uwi bɛ́gya. Anwuɔsu bɛta na biti bina anumi bɛtina kɔmii kakɛ.” 4Na ɔ́su-mi ka mbo-mii ɔda ɔmɛni ɔnini, “Kásɔ kébu blii na biduo bina banwani bani nási Esau kaba kemmo na beli Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ akɔ. Badubɔyia-mii, nsu mɔɔsú-mii nnii bɛ́nu kaduɛ na bana lɛlɔ. 5Bitakya-ma kɔnyi kalɛ na bata bekpoku-mii. Ɔsika lɛɛɛdubo bana kalɔ kadi muedi buti bute-mii. Ɔsika ami líti Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ ku kana amadɔ ƒui líte Esau na úti ɔ́bla nwuna kadikɔ. 6Na si bídu Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ mmɔ ni, biti sika ɔƒualadi bɛƒɔ adila ku ntu bɔni na bɛdubɔdi na bɛni mmɔ kayu.”
7Na bínyimo kalɛ na bina Unwoti Katɔti úte-mii kusɛ kusɛ na bina kabla biala kemmo. Na anwu nákya-mii akɔ na ɔ́nu-mii lɛlɔ na kalɔ kakwiidi bonwu kamɛni kemmo akwa aavlene sɔɔn na bítayaki lɛla lɛdi.
8Anwuɔsu ka bɔ́vi Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kesii kani na bula banwani bani ndi Esau kaba béli mmɔ bɔ́wɔlɔ ni, búnwini anumi bɔ́tina Yordan Ketu kɔwɛ kada kakɛ ulu ɔni ntɛ Elat na Esion-Geber na bɔ́vi bɔkɛ kalɔ kakwiidi ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie Moab kalɔ kemmo.
9Na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Lɛ́su-mi ka ɔdi biala útakya Moabƒuɔ bani nkya mmɔ kɔnyi na bata bekpoku-mii. Si bɛ́bla lɛni ni, lɛɛɛdubo bana kalɔ kadi buti bute-mii. Ɔsika ami néti Ar ɔma ɔmmɔ líte Lot bawɔ ka beti mmɔ babla bana kadikɔ.”
10Uwi ɔdi kemmo ni, nka bekyuli bani baalɔ banii Emiƒuɔ nli Ar ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Bekyuli bammɔ bákuku na bemomo na bebo ɔlɔkplu lɛnɔ aani Anakƒuɔ. 11Na Anakƒuɔ bamɛni ni, Moabƒuɔ bátaalɔ-ma banii Emiƒuɔ. Na kadi bamba baalɔ Emiƒuɔ bamɛni ku Anakƒuɔ bamɛni banii Raƒaƒuɔ. 12Na nka Horiƒuɔ nli Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ asa na Esau bawɔ bábabɔku-ma na báyila-ma udu na béti kalɔ kammɔ beli aani kalɛ kani na Israelƒuɔ badubo bana bekisine bɔbɔku budie kalɔ kani na Katɔti úti úte-ma kemmo na bayila-ma udu.
13Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su-bu ɔnini, “Bɛta na bɛvia Sered Ketu.” Na abu lɛnɔ bɔ́bla lɛni.
14Na akwa ani búti bɔ́ta bɔ́si Kades-Barnea úbédu uwi ɔni na bɔ́via Sered Ketu adi akwa Avlaatɛ-maane. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo na bekyuli bani ƒui na bédu kekpo busie békpi bása aani kalɛ na Katɔti ɔ́su úse. 15Na Katɔti útete-ma bɔnwuna úti útédu ka ɔ́yila bana udu ƒui.
16Amu uwi ɔni bekyuli bani nédu kekpo busie mɛni békpi bása ƒui basa ni, 17Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, 18“Ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni bɛdubɔsia Ar na Moab kalɔ kemmo na bitávia ɔmii na katɔ kakɛ. 19Na si bɛ́vi mmɔ bɛ́wɔlɔ ni, bɛdubudu Arnonƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na si bíduo mmɔ ni, bitakya-ma kɔnyi na bata bekpoku-mii. Na si bɛ́bla lɛni lɛɛɛdubo Arnonƒuɔ kalɔ kammɔ kadi buti bute-mii. Ɔsika líti-ka líte Lot bawɔ ka beti-ka babla bana kadikɔ.”
20Asa na Arnonƒuɔ badubukpo baƒɔ kalɔ kani na Katɔti úti úte-ma mmɔ ni, na nka Reƒateƒuɔ nli mmɔ. Na ama na Arnonƒuɔ bátaalɔ banii Samsumƒuɔ. 21Ama lɛnɔ bákuku aani Anakƒuɔ. Na bemomo na bebo ɔlɔkplu lɛnɔ, nsu Katɔti ɔ́yila-ma udu ƒui na ɔ́ƒɔ bana kalɔ na úti-ka úte Arnonƒuɔ na bétélie mmɔ. 22Lɛni kani na Katɔti ɔ́bla úte Esau bawɔ bani nli Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ. Lɛni kani na ɔ́yila Horiƒuɔ udu na bana anumi, na úti kalɔ kani lɛlɔ beli ɔmwi mɛni úte-ma. 23Na Awiƒuɔ bani nli akpaklɔ ani nsiaku lɛlɔ úti útédu Gasa ni, Kaƒtorƒuɔ bani nási Kaƒtor bébo bábadu-ma na béti bana kɔlɔ na belie mmɔ.
24Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su-bu ɔnini, “Bɛklibi lɛlɔ na bítávia Arnon Kɔwɛ. Ɔsika líti Hesbon Ɔga Sihon ɔni ndi Amorini kalɔ lɛ́kya-mii enu kemmo. Bise kalɔ bitaadi kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ na biteekpoku-ma. 25Na mɔɔsu-mii nnii ɔ́si ɔmwi ni, ndubuse kalɔ liti liƒu ntaakya kadi biala nkya ɔƒɛ kalɔ lɛlɔ kemmo na amii ɔsu. Badubuteenu bina lɛlɔ litemi na liƒu libendi lɛdubo-ma bɔda na amii ɔsu.”
Israelƒuɔ Bádi Amoriƒuɔ Ɔga Sihon Lɛlɔ
26Amu ka búdu Kedemot kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ni, mmɔ na lɛ́tala batu badi ku keyi buɛɛ kenye kadi ka batásu Ɔga Sihon ɔni nási Hesbon ka mɔɔsu nnini, 27“Buvele na nda-a, ya na Israelƒuɔ bavi bina kalɔ lɛlɔ. Bɔdubusie siin bɔvia ɔni na buledie ulu bamba ɔdi. 28Na ntu ku adila biala bɔdubɔni na bɔdi ni, bɛbu kuye bite-bu na bɔdubɔƒɔ-mii kayu. Lɛla lɛni kani na buuvele-ɔ ndi ka aya na bɔsia ƒula kalɔ kemmo. 29Lɛni na Esau bawɔ bani nli Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ ku Moabƒuɔ bani nli Ar bénu kalɔ na bɔ́via bana lɛmii ku Yordan Ketu asa na búduo kalɔ kani na Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka weti wete-bu kemmo.” 30Nsu Ɔga Sihon anwu útenu kalɔ ka bɔsia bana kalɔ kemmo. Bina Unwoti Katɔti nábla-nwu na nwuna kayi káyu ɔkplu kalɛ na bukpoku-nwu na bɔdi-nwu lɛlɔ.
31Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Bɛta na bitékpoku Ɔga Sihon ku nwuna bekyuli na bɛdi-ma lɛlɔ na biti bana kɔlɔ.”
32Amu na Ɔga Sihon ɔ́ta ku nwuna bekyuli ka bebekpoku-bu na ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Yahas. 33Nsu bula Unwoti Katɔti uti Ɔga Sihon ku nwuna bebi ku nwuna bekyuli ƒui ɔ́kya-bu enu kemmo na bɔ́du bana ƒui kede kede. 34Uwi ɔmmɔ kani si búdu nwuna ɔma biala buukpóku ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli na bɔ́du ukyuli biala, ɔnana ɔdi o-o uleku ɔdi o-o iye ɔnamu ɔdi o-o ni, bɔɔdú-nwu ɔni na buláda ukyuli ɔdi taanyonu. 35Na bebuo bani nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ku bana ala ƒui ni, bɔ́da-nya búti búnwini abu adi. 36Na ɔdanku ɔ́si Aroer ɔni ntɛ Arnon Kɔwɛ kenye ku lɛma lɛni nkya mmɔ ƒui úti útédu Gilead. Ɔma biala uuubo ɔni bútadi-ma lɛlɔ. Bula Unwoti Katɔti úti lɛma lɛmmɔ ƒui ɔ́kya-bu enu kemmo. 37Nsu bútani bútede Arnonƒuɔ kɔlɔ ku Yabok Ketudɔ ku abinkpo kalɔ lɛma lɛni na bula Unwoti Katɔti úbo-bu ɔda ɔnii butesie. Mmɔ kani na bútesie.

english_text:
The Defeat of King Og of Bashan
(Numbers 21.31-35)
Moses said to Israel:
1When we turned onto the road that leads to Bashan, King Og of Bashan led out his whole army to fight us at Edrei. 2But the Lord told me, “Moses, don't be afraid of King Og. I am going to help you defeat him and his army and take over his land. Destroy him and his people, just as you did with the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon.”
3-6The Lord our God helped us destroy Og and his army and conquer his entire kingdom of Bashan, including the Argob region. His kingdom had lots of villages and 60 towns with high walls and gates that locked with bars. We completely destroyed them all, killing everyone, 7but keeping the livestock and everything else of value.
8Sihon and Og had ruled Amorite kingdoms east of the Jordan River. Their land stretched from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, and we captured it all. 9Mount Hermon is called Mount Sirion by the people of Sidon, and it is called Mount Senir by the Amorites. 10We captured all the towns in the highlands, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, two of the towns that Og had ruled.
Og's Coffin
11King Og was the last of the Rephaim, and his coffin is in the town of Rabbah in Ammon. It is made of hard black rock and is four meters long and almost two meters wide.
The Land East of the Jordan River Is Divided
(Numbers 32.1-42)
Moses said to Israel:
12-17I gave some of the land and towns we captured to the tribes of Reuben and Gad. Their share started at the Arnon River gorge in the south, took in the town of Aroer on the edge of the gorge, and went far enough north to include the southern half of the Gilead region. The northern part of their land went as far east as the upper Jabbok River gorge, which formed their border with the Ammonites. I also gave them the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, from Lake Galilee south to the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
I gave the northern half of Gilead and all of the Bashan region to half the tribe of Manasseh. Bashan had belonged to King Og, and the Argob region in Bashan used to be called the Land of the Rephaim. Jair from the Manasseh tribe conquered the Argob region as far west as the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. The Israelites even started calling Bashan by the name “Villages of Jair,” and that is still its name. I gave the northern half of Gilead to the Machir clan.
18-19 At that time I told the men of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
The Lord our God told me to give you this land with its towns, and that's what I have done. Now your wives and children can stay here with your large flocks of sheep and goats and your large herds of cattle. But all of you men that can serve in our army must cross the Jordan River and help the other tribes, because they are your relatives. 20The Lord will let them defeat the enemy nations on the west side of the Jordan and take their land. Afterwards, you can come back here to the land I gave you.
21-22Then I told Joshua, “You saw how the Lord our God helped us destroy King Sihon and King Og. So don't be afraid! Wherever you go, the Lord will fight on your side and help you destroy your enemies.”
God Refused To Let Moses Enter Canaan
Moses said to Israel:
23 At that time I prayed and begged, 24“Our Lord, it seems that you have just begun to show me your great power. No other god in the sky or on earth is able to do the mighty things that you do. 25The land west of the Jordan is such good land. Please let me cross the Jordan and see the hills and the Lebanon Mountains.”
26But the Lord was angry with me because of you people, and he refused to listen. “That's enough!” he said. “I don't want to hear any more. 27Climb to the top of Mount Pisgah and look north, south, east, and west. Take a good look, but you are not going to cross the Jordan River. 28Joshua will lead Israel across the Jordan to take the land, so help him be strong and brave and tell him what he must do.”
29After this we stayed in the valley at Beth-Peor.
translation_text:
Israelƒuɔ Bádi Ɔga Og Lɛlɔ
1Ɔmmɔ kama búnwini na bútásia ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie Basan kalɔ kemmo. Na Ɔga Og ɔni mɔɔdi Basan kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ku nwuna bekpone ƒui báta ka bebekpoku-bu na ɔma ɔni nde Edrei. 2Nsu Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Tayia ɔga ɔmmɔ. Ɔsika líti Ɔga ɔmmɔ ku nwuna bekpone ƒui ku nwuna kɔlɔ lɛ́kya-a enu kemmo. Anwuɔsu kalɛ na ábla Amoriƒuɔ Ɔga Sihon ɔni nádi lɛga na Hesbon na kekpo kemmo ni, lɛni kani na adubɔbla Ɔga Og.”
3Anwuɔsu Unwoti úti Ɔga Og ku nwuna bekpone ƒui ɔ́kya-bu enu kemmo na bɔ́du-ma ƒui kede kede. 4Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo búukpo bɔ́ƒɔ nwuna kalɔ kani baalɔ banii Argob ƒui ku lɛma libendi lɛni bumomo ndubɔbla liti ku leevu na Basan kalɛkɛ kani lɛlɔ na Ɔga Og ɔɔdi mmɔ. Na ɔma biala uuubo ɔni na bútaƒɔ bútasiku-nwu enu kemmo. 5Na lɛma lɛni ƒui kɔtɛ na mɔɔtɛmi-mii mɛni ni, bátu awodu ebendi báka bámana-nya na ana kɔyakun ni, abuala kɔlɛmikɔ sɔɔn na kɔdi na béti bábala-ku. Na akpaklɔ adi lɛnɔ akya na ébomo, nsu anya amu ni, bátatu awodu bátaka bátatamana-nya. 6Bɔ́yila-ma udu ƒui na lɛma ku akpaklɔ ammɔ kemmo. Na bɔ́du banana ku beleku ku banamu bammɔ ƒui aani kalɛ na bɔ́bla Ɔga Sihon ɔni mɔɔdi lɛlɔ na Hesbon. 7Nsu bana ɔmantɛ bebuo ama ni, bútadu-ma. Mmomu búti-ma ku bana ala ƒui búnwini bula adi.
8Anwuɔsu uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, búkpo bɔ́ƒɔ lɛmii lɛni nkya Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ bɔ́lɛku Amoriƒuɔ baga inyɔ bammɔ enu kemmo. Úti ɔ́si Arnon Kɔwɛ ɔvi útédu Hermon Kɔbi lɛlɔ. 9Hermon Kɔbi kɔmɛni na Sidomƒuɔ bátaalɔ banii Sirion. Na Amoriƒuɔ bátaalɔ-ku banii Senir. 10Búkpo bɔ́ƒɔ lɛma lɛni ƒui nwi ɔtantɛ ku Gilead kalɛkɛ ku Basan úti útédu Salka ku Edrei. Na lɛma lɛmɛni ni, nka Basanƒuɔ Ɔga Og útaadi-ni lɛlɔ. 11Na Raƒa bekyuli ƒui kemmo ni, Ɔga Og lɛti pɛ nébu. Na binu! Nwuna lɛla lɛni lɛlɔ na ɔɔtɛ ni, nwuna bune butulo lɛgba leevu-ɛtɛ. Na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ bɔbla aani lɛgba ɛku. Na abuala lɛti lɛti na béti bábla lɛla lɛmmɔ. Na kamu kese Arnonƒuɔ ɔma ubendi ɔni baalɔ banii Raba ɔmwi kadi.
Béle Kalɔ Kammɔ Béte Kaba Biala
12Uwi ɔni kemmo búkpo bɔƒɔ kɔlɔ kɔni mɔɔsu mɛni ni, líti kalɔ kani nkya Aroer katɔ kakɛ kani nde Arnon Kɔwɛ ku Gilead abi lɛlɔ kalɔ ntɛ bule lɛma lɛni nkya-ni kemmo líte Ruben kɔdua bekyuli ku Gad kɔdua bekyuli. 13Na Gilead abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kakladi kani nébu ku Basan kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na Ɔga Og útaadi ni, líti líte Manase kɔdua bekyuli kakɛ kenwi. Na Argob kalɛkɛ na Basan kalɔ kemmo ni, mmɔ na Raƒaƒuɔ beli. 14Na Yair ɔni nási Manase kɔdua ni, anwu náƒɔ Argo kalɛkɛ ƒui na Basan kalɔ kemmo úti útédu Gesur ku Maakatƒuɔ ɔmii. Na úti nwuna lɛnyi ɔ́sia lɛma lɛmmɔ, anwuɔsu na baalɔ mmɔ ɔmwi ɔmwi banii Yair lɛma. 15Na líti Gilead abi lɛlɔ kalɔ líte Makir. 16Na Ruben kɔdua bekyuli ku Gad kɔdua bekyuli ni, líti kalɔ kani nwi ɔ́si Gilead úti ɔɔyu útédu Arnon Kɔwɛ úti útédu Yabok Ketu ɔni ndi Arnon bebi ɔmii líte-ma. 17Na nwuna ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ na Yordan Ketu kakya ɔ́si Galilea Ɛpu na katɔ kakɛ ɔ́yu úbedu Mma Ɛpu na ɔkɛ ɔdanku Pisga Kɔbi.
18Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, líbo-ma ɔda nnini, “Bula Unwoti Katɔti néti kalɔ kani nkya Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ úte-mii ka biti bɛbla bina kadikɔ. Nsu ɔƒɛni mɔɔsu bina bekpone ƒui ka bavia Yordan Ketu na bagyu batɔ-bu na betékpo baƒɔ kɔlɔ kɔni nkya mmɔ bete Israel adua akladi na beti babla bana kadikɔ. 19Nsu bɛda bina beleku ku bebi ku bebuo pii bani na bibo mmɔ bɛkya kama. 20Binye ku bina banwani na bikpo bɛƒɔ kɔlɔ kɔni na Katɔti ɔ́su ka wete ama lɛnɔ na Yordan Ketu ɔvi ɔmmɔ útédu ka ama lɛnɔ bákɛ bana kadikɔ aani kalɛ na amii lɛnɔ bɛ́kɛ kɔdikɔ kɔni na líti líte-mii asa na bɛsɔ binwini bibo bina keliekɔ.”
21Ɔmmɔ kama líbo Yosua ɔda nnini, “Awɔ ɔlati, ánu ku ƒula anumi lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́bla Ɔga Sihon ku Ɔga Og. Lɛni kani na Katɔti ɔdubɔbla ɔga biala ɔni na wata wenye-mii lɛlɔ. 22Anwuɔsu tayia-ma, ɔsika ƒula Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubukpo ƒula kekpo biala ute-ɔ.”
Katɔti Ɔ́su Mose Ka Nwuna Ɔgba Ulanya Kanaan
23Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, lɛ́kpali katɔ na lívele Unwoti kpakplaa nnii, 24“O Ɔyikune Ƒui Katɔti, awɔ nése kalɔ eedie ƒula ɔyikun bonwu taatina ami ƒula kabla ɔblane ku ƒula akɔla budie taatina. Na ɔyikun ɔdi uuubo na katɔ iye kalɔ na ɔkana akɔla ebendi ani na aabla mɛni bɔbla. 25Anwuɔsu muuvele-ɔ nnii ya na lɛvia lisie kalɔ kabunidi kani nwi Yordan Ketu ɔvi ngye na ntánu abi lɛlɔ kɔlɔ kɔbunidi kɔni nkya mmɔ ku Lebanon abi kalɔ kabuni kammɔ.”
26Nsu ɔ́si amii ɔsu ni, Katɔti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-mi na útakpete-mi. Mmomu úbo-mi ɔda ɔnini, “Da bɔtɛmi ya! Takpali-mi na ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ lɛnɔ! 27Kɔ sie na eténye Pisga Kɔbi lili na asia kalɔ kammɔ anu amana kaduɛ. Ɔsika aaadubo Yordan Ketu kamɛni bɔvia. 28Mmomu lɔ Yosua na ebo-nwu ɔda na bekyuli bammɔ anumi na akya-nwu ogya, ɔsika kalɔ kani na ánu mmɔ ni, anwu ndubɔkpanku bekyuli bammɔ ɔvia Yordan Ketu na betéti mmɔ babla bana kadikɔ.” 29Anwuɔsu bɔ́sɔ búlie kɔwɛ kɔni nde Bet-Peor ɔma kakɛ.

english_text:
Israel Must Obey God
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to these laws and teachings! If you obey them, you will live, and you will go in and take the land that the Lord is giving you. He is the God your ancestors worshiped, 2 and now he is your God. I am telling you everything he has commanded, so don't add anything or take anything away.
3 You saw how he killed everyone who worshiped the god Baal Peor. 4But all of you that were faithful to the Lord your God are still alive today.
5-8 No other nation has laws that are as fair as the ones the Lord my God told me to give you. If you faithfully obey them when you enter the land, you will show other nations how wise you are. In fact, everyone that hears about your laws will say, “That great nation certainly is wise!” And what makes us greater than other nations? We have a God who is close to us and answers our prayers.
9You must be very careful not to forget the things you have seen God do for you. Keep reminding yourselves, and tell your children and grandchildren as well. 10Do you remember the day you stood in the Lord's presence at Mount Sinai? The Lord said, “Moses, bring the people of Israel here. I want to speak to them so they will obey me as long as they live, and so they will teach their children to obey me too.”
11 Mount Sinai was surrounded by deep dark clouds, and fire went up to the sky. You came to the foot of the mountain, 12and the Lord spoke to you from the fire. You could hear him and understand what he was saying, but you couldn't see him. 13 The Lord said he was making an agreement with you, and he told you that your part of the agreement is to obey the Ten Commandments. Then the Lord wrote these Commandments on two flat stones.
14 That's when the Lord commanded me to give you the laws and teachings you must obey in the land that you will conquer west of the Jordan River.
Don't Worship Idols
Moses said to Israel:
15When God spoke to you from the fire, he was invisible. So be careful 16 not to commit the sin of worshiping idols. Don't make idols to be worshiped, whether they are shaped like men, women, 17 animals, birds, 18reptiles, or fish. 19And when you see the sun or moon or stars, don't be tempted to bow down and worship them. The Lord put them there for all the other nations to worship. 20 But you are the Lord's people, because he rescued you from Egypt, that fiery furnace.
21 The Lord was angry with me because of what you said, and he told me that he would not let me cross the Jordan River into the good land that he is giving you. 22So I must stay here and die on this side of the Jordan, but you will cross the river and take the land.
23Always remember the agreement that the Lord your God made with you, and don't make an idol in any shape or form. 24 The Lord will be angry if you worship other gods, and he can be like a fire destroying everything in its path.
25-26Soon you will cross the Jordan River and settle down in the land. Then in the years to come, you will have children, and they will give you grandchildren. After many years, you might lose your sense of right and wrong and make idols, even though the Lord your God hates them. So I am giving you fair warning today, and I call the earth and the sky as witnesses. If you ever make idols, the Lord will be angry, and you won't have long to live, because the Lord will let you be wiped out. 27 Only a few of you will survive, and the Lord will force you to leave the land and will scatter you among the nations. 28There you will have to worship gods made of wood and stone, and these are nothing but idols that can't see or hear or eat or smell.
29-30 In all of your troubles, you may finally decide that you want to worship only the Lord. And if you turn back to him and obey him completely, he will again be your God. 31The Lord your God will have mercy—he won't destroy you or desert you. The Lord will remember his promise, and he will keep the agreement he made with your ancestors.
32-34When the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, you saw how he fought for you and showed his great power by performing terrifying miracles. You became his people, and at Mount Sinai you heard him talking to you out of fiery flames. And yet you are still alive! Has anything like this ever happened since the time God created humans? No matter where you go or who you ask, you will get the same answer. No one has ever heard of another god even trying to do such things as the Lord your God has done for you.
35-36 The Lord wants you to know he is the only true God, and he wants you to obey him. That's why he let you see his mighty miracles and his fierce fire on earth, and why you heard his voice from that fire and from the sky.
37The Lord loved your ancestors and decided that you would be his people. So the Lord used his great power to bring you out of Egypt. 38Now you face other nations more powerful than you are, but the Lord has already started forcing them out of their land and giving it to you.
39So remember that the Lord is the only true God, whether in the sky above or on the earth below. 40Today I am explaining his laws and teachings. And if you always obey them, you and your descendants will live long and be successful in the land the Lord is giving you.
Safe Towns
41-43 Moses said, “People of Israel, you must set aside the following three towns east of the Jordan River as Safe Towns: Bezer in the desert highlands belonging to the Reuben tribe; Ramoth in Gilead, belonging to the Gad tribe; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to the Manasseh tribe. If you kill a neighbor without meaning to, and if you had not been angry with that person, you can run to one of these towns and find safety.”
The Second Speech: Moses Tells What the Lord Demands
Israel at Beth-Peor
44-46The Israelites had come from Egypt and were camped east of the Jordan River near Beth-Peor, when Moses gave these laws and teachings. The land around their camp had once belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon. But Moses and the Israelites defeated him 47and King Og of Bashan, and took their lands. These two Amorite kings had ruled the territory east of the Jordan River 48from the town of Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River gorge, north to Mount Hermon. 49Their land included the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, as far south as the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
translation_text:
Mose Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Ka Badi Katɔti Litemi Lɛlɔ
1Bɛdi ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui mɔɔtina-mii mɛni lɛlɔ kalɛ na bɛdubɔkana na bilie kalɔ kani na Katɔti ɔni ndi Bina Bati Kuuku Katɔti úti uute-mii lɛlɔ. 2Na biteti ɔda bubo bɔbambadi bɔdi bitebunku ɔda bubo bɔmɛni lɛlɔ. Iye bitada ɔdi bitedie lɛnɔ. Mmomu bɛdi Unwoti ɔni ndi bina Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔni líti muute-mii mɛni lɛlɔ.
3Amii alati bɛ́nu ku bina anumi lɛlɔ lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́bla na Peor Kɔbi lɛlɔ, kalɛ na ɔ́yila ukyuli biala ɔni muuti ala taatákpa baƒiɔ banii baalɔ Baal udu. 4Nsu amii bani nsiaku Katɔti kama kpakplaa bɛmu bilie ngba úti úbedu ɔmwi kadi.
5Binu! Mina Unwoti Katɔti bunyimi bɔni na úbo-mi ɔda ka ntina-mii ni, lɛ́tina-mii ƒui. Na mɔɔsu-mii nnii bɛdi-mu lɛlɔ ƒui na kalɔ kani bísela bitéti binwini bina kadikɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ. 6Na nsɔ mɔɔsu-mii nnii bɛdi-mu lɛlɔ kaduɛ, na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na kadi bamba bekyuli bani nkya mmɔ badubɔnu bɔti kalɛ na bɛ́da anu. Na si bánu kalɛ na bɛɛdi ɔda bubo bɔmɛni lɛlɔ ni, bekyuli bammɔ badubɔsu banii, “Kadi bekyuli lisu bonwu bamɛni báda anu na beenú ala kalɔ geen.” 7Na kadi bekyuli badi beeebo ɔni na bana baƒiɔ bede-ma aani kalɛ na bula Unwoti Katɔti ude-bu mɛni na ɔɔtuna teete-bu si bɔ́kpali-nwu. 8Na kadi bamba bekyuli ina bebo lɛnyi muedi ni, bana ɔda bubo bulédu ɔda bubo siin bɔni na lɛ́tina-mii ɔmwi kadi mɛni.
9Nsu uwi ɔni na bilie ngba mɛni ni, binye kagyumana uwi biala kemmo kalɛ na bilayiƒala ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ. Na ala ani ƒui na bíti bina anumi bɛ́nu ni, biti bɛsu bina bebi ku bina bawɔ. 10Na binyimo limeyi lɛni na bíbasiaku bina Unwoti Katɔti na Sinai kɔbi kaƒɔna. Mmɔ na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Sala-ma lisu. Ɔsika mɔɔyɔ́ ka binu lɛla lɛni na mbo nte-mii kalɛ na bitaayia-mi na bitaabu-mi lɛnɔ uwi ɔni na bilie ngba mɛni. Na biti etemila ani bínu mmɔ bɛtina bina bebi na babla basiaku-nya lɛlɔ lɛni kani.”
11Bíbo bíbenye kɔbi kɔmmɔ kaƒɔna na liƒlukutu bili bili bonwu lɛ́ƒɔ-ku lɛlɔ ƒui na ɔ́bla suu geen na ogya ɔɔda taasi-ku lɛlɔ teetédu katɔ ƒui na ɔ́bla suu geen. 12Katɔti ɔ́tɛmi úte-mii ɔ́siku ogya ɔmɛni kemmo. Na bínu-nwu lɛdi bɛ́siku ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo, nsu bítanu-nwu udu biala bítati. 13Na ɔ́tɛmi úte-mii ɔ́siku ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na bɛdubɔsia na bɛdi nwuna lɛla lɛni na únyimiku-mii lɛlɔ na bitaadi Ɔda Bubo Leevu bɔni na únweni ɔ́sia atabi bɛbɛ anyɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ. 14Na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ka ntina-mii ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ ƒui kalɛ na bɛdi-mu lɛlɔ si bɛ́via Yordan Ketu bísela bitéti kalɔ kammɔ binwini bina kadikɔ.
Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Na Ala Avɔdi Lɛlɔ
15Limeyi lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́tɛmi úte-mii ɔ́siku ogya kemmo na Sinai Kɔbi lɛlɔ ni, bítanu nwuna udu biala bítati. Anwuɔsu bɛnu lɛlɔ kemmo kaduɛ. 16Na bitabla likpidi na bɛvɔ iye bɛnwi lɛla lɛni udu na lɛ́lɛ ɔnana iye uleku, 17iye aasɛ ɔni muuveyi taavi ɔdi, 18iye kubweyi kɔni mɔɔkpɛ́ kaƒɔ lɛlɔ, iye kɔkpaku. 19Na bitaya na lɛla lɛdi lɛkɔku-mii na bɛta bitákpa ala ani nkya kayaa na bina anumi aanu aani ɔƒɛ ku kɔbuli ku ayabi. Ɔsika anya na Unwoti Katɔti údie úte kayawi bekyuli ƒui. 20Nsu amii amu ni, Katɔti nékpo údie-mii ɔ́lɛku lɛbibo lɛni mɔɔda aani ogya gaganga kemmo na Egyipte kalɔ ka bɛbla nwuna bekyuli bani na bɛdi ɔmwi mɛni.
21Ɔ́si amii ɔsu ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-mi na úse kenye ka ami Mose mina ɔgba ɔɔɔdubo bɔvia Yordan Ketu na liduo kalɔ kabuni kani na úti uute-mii na kenwini bina kadikɔ mɛni kemmo. 22Mmomu ndubukpi bɔtɛ kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ ɔni na mina ɔgba ulavia Yordan Ketu kani na bɛdubo bɔvia ɔƒɛni busie kalɔ kabuni kani na bísela bitéti binwini bina kadikɔ mɛni lɛlɔ. 23Na bɛnu kaduɛ na bitayiƒala lɛla lɛni na Katɔti únyimiku-mii mmɔ. Na bɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ bɔni násu-mii ka bitavɔ iye bitanwi lɛla lɛdi bitese bitete lɛlɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ. 24Ɔsika si bɛ́bla lɛni ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubuti kɔnyi. Ɔsika uukpó kogyulo na use aani Ogya na ɔkana na ɔkyula-mii.
25Ina bílie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ bítu uwi na bɛ́wɔ bebi ku bawɔ tɛtɛ na ɔmmɔ kama bɛ́vɔ baƒiɔ badi bíse bíte lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti ɔdubuti kɔnyi ɔkya-mii. Ɔsika ala ammɔ bene ƒui adi likpidi na nwuna anumi. 26Anwuɔsu mɔɔsu-mii na katɔ ku kalɔ anumi ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni ka si bítadi litemi lɛni na lɛ́su-mii mɛni lɛlɔ ni, uwi uletu asa na Katɔti ɔdubɔyila-mii udu na kalɔ kani na bísela bitéti binwini bina kadikɔ mɛni lɛlɔ si bɛ́via Yordan Ketu. 27Na mɔɔsu-mii lɛnɔ nnii, Katɔti ɔdubo-mii bugyingya bɔkya kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ ɔni na bina ɛlɛɛ badi kani ndubo bubu na bana akɔ mmɔ. 28Na mmɔ na bɛdubo ala ani na bekyuli béti egyii ku atabi bánwi na bávɔ bɔkpa. Na kugyikɛ ku atabi ala ammɔ ebo anumi, nsu alákana bɔnu. Na ebo atu, nsu alákana lɛla lɛdi bunu. Na alákana adila adi bɔdi, iye enwenyi lɛla lɛdi enu. 29Nsu si bɛdubuti bina kayi ƒui bɛwia Unwoti Katɔti kama ulu na kesii kani na bɛkya mmɔ ni, bɛdubɔnu-nwu. 30Na si bíduo bukpoku bɔdi kemmo na ala amɛni aalɛ́ku-mii ni, mmɔ na bɛdubunwini bisie Unwoti kudɔ na binu nwuna litemi. 31Ɔsika Katɔti ubo lɛƒɔndia na ulada-mii ulanyonu iye ɔyila-mii udu na ulayiƒala bunyimi bɔni na anwu ɔlati únyimi ku bina bati kuuku.
32Na amii alati bɛwia bɛsiku uwi ɔni návi asa na báwɔ-mii. Na bɛwia bɛsiku uwi ɔni na Katɔti úti údie ukyuli. Na bɛwia kayawi kammɔ ƒui kemmo si ukyuli ɔdi únu ka ala ebendi amɛni udu álɛ dii. 33Kadi bamba bekyuli badi bétenu dii ka Katɔti ɔtɛmi ɔsiku ogya kemmo na belie ngba aani kalɛ na amii bínu na bilie ngba. 34Na muuye-mii nnii baƒiɔ badi bésie kalɔ kadi lɛlɔ dii na bétédie bekyuli bálɛku kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ na béti-ma bábla nwuna bekyuli aani kalɛ na bina Unwoti Katɔti údie-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ? Na bina anumi lɛlɔ ni, údie nwuna ɔyikun ɔ́tina-mii na ɔ́ya na lɛlɛ lidu lidu líbo bekyuli lɛlɔ, na údie akɔla lidu lidu ku ala ani mɔɔda liƒu geen ɔ́tina.
35Na Unwoti údie amɛni ƒui úti ɔ́tina-mii ka anwu lɛti ndi Katɔti na ɔdi biala ɔsɔ uuubo. 36Na ɔ́ya na bínu nwuna lɛdi bɛ́siku katɔ kalɛ na ɔda-mii kpakplaa na ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na ɔdi ka bɛsia lɛlɔ. Na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ni, ɔ́ya na bɛ́nu nwuna ogya ɔni mɔɔda bonwu na ɔ́tɛmi ɔ́siku ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo úte-mii. 37Ka ɔɔyɔ́ bina bati kuuku ɔsu ni, ɔ́ƒuna-mii ka binwini nwuna badi. Na anwu ɔlati úbo úbedie-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ku nwuna ɔyikun bonwu. 38Na ɔni na bíti bísela ni, ɔ́bɔku kɔlɔ kɔni bekyuli mbo ɔyikun betulo-mii kalɛ na amii bɛkɛ kuƒi na biti kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ binwini bina kadikɔ aani kalɛ na use ɔmwi. Na aka ndi kalɔ kani lɛlɔ bilie mɛni.
39Anwuɔsu bɛti nwaa ka Unwoti lɛti ndi katɔ ku kalɔ Ɔti. Na ɔdi biala ɔsɔ uuubo. 40Na nwuna ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui líti líte-mii ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ ni, bɛdi-mu ƒui lɛlɔ. Na lɛla biala na bɛɛbla ni, lɛdubɔtɛ lite-mii kaduɛ ku bina bawɔ ƒui. Na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na bilie kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti uute-mii mɛni ka biti-ka bɛbla bina kadikɔ uwi ƒui.
Báda Lɛma Libendi Béte Kabɛkɔ
41Amu na Mose údie lɛma libendi ɛtɛ lɛni nkya Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ úse 42ka si ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi asa na ɔ́du ukyuli ɔni naaadi nwuna ukisine ni, ɔkana na ukeli utábɛ lɛma lɛmɛni ɔdi biala kemmo. Na si úduo ɔdi kemmo ni, utalɛka badu ukyuli ɔdune ɔmmɔ. 43Na lɛma lɛmmɔ ndi Beser ku Romot ku Golum. Na Beser ɔdi Ruben kɔdua bekyuli ɔma ɔni ndi abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kakwiidi ɔma ɔni nsia ɔtantɛ. Na Romot ɔma ɔni nkya Gilead kalɔ kemmo ni, ɔdi Gad kɔdua bekyuli ɔdi. Na Golum na Basan kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔdi Manase kɔdua bekyuli ɔdi.
Mose Údie Katɔti Ɔda Bubo Keyi
44Ɔmɛni ndi ɔda bubo bɔni na Mose údie ɔ́tina Israelƒuɔ ka basia-mu kama. 45Ɔda bubo bɔmɛni ku ala ani ƒui na adanku mmɔ ni, údie-nya ɔ́tina-ma uwi ɔni na bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. 46Uwi ɔmmɔ na bébo beli kɔwɛ kɔni nde ɔma ɔni baalɔ Bet-Peor na Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na kalɔ kammɔ kadi Ɔga Sihon ɔni ndi Amoriƒuɔ ɔga na uli Hesbon ɔma kemmo. Mose ku Israelƒuɔ békpo bádi ɔga ɔmɛni lɛlɔ. 47Na báƒɔ-nwu kalɔ bénwini bana kadikɔ. Békpo Ɔga Og ɔni ndi Amoriƒuɔ ɔga unyɔdi ɔni mɔɔdi lɛga na Basan kalɔ lɛlɔ na báƒɔ anwu kadi lɛnɔ. Baga inyɔ bamɛni mɔɔdi lɛlɔ na Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na ɔvi ɔmmɔ. 48Na kalɔ kamɛni kadanku ɔ́si Aroer ɔni ntɛ Aron Kɔwɛ kenye úti útédu Sion Kɔbi kɔni baalɔ banii Hermon 49ku kɔwɛ kakɛ kani nkya Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ úti útédu Mma Ɛpu si éti ésela Pisga Kɔbi kaƒɔna ƒui kadi bana ɔdi.

english_text:
The Ten Commandments
(Exodus 20.1-17)
1Moses called together the people of Israel and said:
Today I am telling you the laws and teachings that you must follow, so listen carefully. 2The Lord our God made an agreement with our nation at Mount Sinai. 3That agreement wasn't only with our ancestors but with us, who are here today. 4The Lord himself spoke to you out of the fire, 5but you were afraid of the fire and refused to go up the mountain. So I spoke with the Lord for you, then I told you that he had said:
6I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
7Do not worship any god except me.
8 Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth. 9 Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me and worship idols, I will punish your families for three or four generations. 10But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
11 Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
12 Show respect for the Sabbath Day—it belongs to me. 13 You have six days when you can do your work, 14but the seventh day of the week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your oxen or donkeys or any other animal, not even those foreigners who live in your towns. And don't make your slaves do any work. 15This special day of rest will remind you that I reached out my mighty arm and rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
16 Respect your father and mother, and you will live a long and successful life in the land I am giving you.
17 Do not murder.
18 Be faithful in marriage.
19 Do not steal.
20 Do not tell lies about others.
21 Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else.
22 When we were gathered at the mountain, the Lord spoke to us in a loud voice from the dark fiery cloud. The Lord gave us these commands, and only these. Then he wrote them on two flat stones and gave them to me.
The People Were Afraid
(Exodus 20.18-21)
Moses said to Israel:
23When fire blazed from the mountain, and you heard the voice coming from the darkness, your tribal leaders came to me 24and said:
Today the Lord our God has shown us how powerful and glorious he is. He spoke to us from the fire, and we learned that people can live, even though God speaks to them. 25But we don't want to take a chance on being killed by that terrible fire, and if we keep on hearing the Lord's voice, we will die. 26Has anyone else ever heard the only true God speaking from fire, as we have? And even if they have, would they live to tell about it? 27Moses, go up close and listen to the Lord. Then come back and tell us, and we will do everything he says.
28The Lord heard you and said:
Moses, I heard what the people said to you, and I approve. 29I wish they would always worship me with fear and trembling and be this willing to obey me! Then they and their children would always enjoy a successful life.
30Now, tell them to return to their tents, 31but you come back here to me. After I tell you my laws and teachings, you will repeat them to the people, so they can obey these laws in the land I am giving them.
Moses said:
32Israel, you must carefully obey the Lord's commands. 33Follow them, because they make a path that will lead to a long successful life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
translation_text:
Mose Úte-ma Katɔti Ɔda Bubo Leevu
1Amu na Mose ɔ́lɔ Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ala amɛni.
Israel kadi bekyuli, binu ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui líti muute-mii ɔmwi mɛni. Bɛtɛya ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ na bɛnu ka bɛdi-mu lɛlɔ. 2Bula Unwoti Katɔti ku abu búnyimi linyese lɛdi na Sinai Kɔbi lɛlɔ. 3Na ɔɔɔdi bula bati kuuku ku Katɔti nényimi linyese lɛmɛni. Mmomu abu bani nli ngba mɛni ɔsu na únyimi linyese lɛmɛni. 4Na kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, amii alati binu ka Katɔti ɔ́tɛmiku-mii ɔ́siku lɛgyavonku lɛni mɔɔda kemmo. 5Nsu ka bɛɛyia lɛgyavonku lɛmmɔ na bilayɔ ka bɛkɔ bisie kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili ɔsu ni, ami nénye amii ku Katɔti ntɛ na lɛ́su-mii ala ani na Katɔti ɔ́su. Na ami nénye Katɔti ku bina ntɛ uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo na lɛ́su-mii ala ani Katɔti ɔ́su.
6“Ami ndi bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nédie-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani nka bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bɛɛbla bana kabla.
7Bitese benwoti badi bitebunku-mi lɛlɔ.
8Bitavɔ iye bɛnwi lɛla lɛni nálɛ ala ani nkya kayaa iye kalɔ lɛlɔ iye ntu bɔni na kalɔ kemmo na bitaakpa. 9Na tebo kalɔ takya baƒiɔ badi lili kalɔ iye akpa ɔdi. Ɔsika ndi bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔni muukpó kɔgyulo. Na mɔɔní bekyuli bani muukisi-mii kɔtu ɔ́si bati ku bebi lɛlɔ útédu kaba katɛdi ku kenedi lɛlɔ. 10Nsu mɔɔbla lɛƒɔndia teete nkyuli ɛlɛ ɛlɛ bani mɔɔyɔ́-mi na baadi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.
11Takpali Unwoti ƒula Katɔti lɛnyi keeke. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubɔni ukyuli ɔni mɔɔlɔ-nwu lɛnyi keeke kɔtu.
12Se lɛnwunameyi likpo na abla-ni kedee, aani kalɛ na ami ɔni ndi bina Unwoti Katɔti líbo-mii ɔda. 13Emeyi aku na ɔlɛka eti abla ƒula kabla. 14Nsu limeyi maatɛdi ndi ami Unwoti ƒula Katɔti Lɛnwunameyi lɛni kemmo na útalɛ ka abla kabla kadi, awɔ iye ƒula bebi iye ƒula kabla bablane iye ƒula bebuo iye baƒɔ bani nkya-a kudɔ babla kabla kadi. Na útalɛka bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla teete-ɔ babla kabla kadi lɛnwunameyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na awɔ lɛnɔ alábla kabla kadi. 15Na ɔlɛka binyimo ka uwi ɔni návi kemmo ni, bɛdi bekyuli bani na bénye-mii lɛlɔ ka bitaabla kabla teete-ma. Na ami ɔni ndi bina Unwoti Katɔti néti mina ɔyikun bonwu ku ɔlɔkplu kpakplaa na lídie-mii lɛ́lɛku mmɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na muubó-mii ɔda ka bitabla kabla kadi lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ.
16Bu ƒula ɔti ku ƒ'ini aani kalɛ na ami bina Unwoti líbo-mii ɔda na adubulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ na keyi kadubɔyɔku-ɔ na kalɔ kani na líti muute-ɔ lɛlɔ.
17Tadu ukyuli.
18Tadi kɔsɔnɔ.
19Teyu.
20Tada ukyuli ɔdi kenye.
21Taya anumi egyie-ɔ-na ƒula ukyulikpana ulekudi iye nwuna kaduli iye nwuna kabla ɔblane iye nwuna kalɔ iye nwuna ɔmantɛ bakɔ iye nwuna bebuo ala betine iye nwuna lɛla biala na ubo lɛlɔ!”
22Ɔda bubo bɔmɛni na Unwoti úti úte-mii uwi ɔni bɛ́sala binye kɔbi kɔmmɔ kaƒɔna. Na mmɔ bínu-nwu lɛdi bonwu bɛ́siku lɛgyavonku kemmo ku liƒlukutu bili bili kemmo na mmɔ use suu geen. Na únweni ala ammɔ ɔ́sia atabi anyɔ lɛlɔ na úti úte-mii. Na ɔ́sɔ útasu lɛla lɛdi útebunku ɔmmɔ.
Liƒu Lɛ́da Israelƒuɔ
23Uwi ɔni na bínu Unwoti lɛdi bɛ́siku kasuudikɔ mmɔ uwi ɔni na kɔbi kɔmmɔ kɔɔda mmɔ ni, bina benengu ku bina adua benengu ku baduɔti bébo-mi kudɔ na básu-mi banini, 24“Bɔ́nu bula Unwoti Katɔti ɔyikun ku bukeye uwi ɔni na búnu-nwu lɛdi bɔ́siku lɛgyavonku lɛmmɔ kemmo. Na ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni na bɔ́nu bɔ́ti geen ka ukyuli ɔkana ulie ngba ina Katɔti ɔ́tɛmiku-nwu. 25Nsu buuye bɔnii bi ɔsu na buuti bula ngba butákya ɔgbankpi kemmo? Ɔsika lɛgyavonku lɛmmɔ lɛdubo-bu ngba bɔyila. Na bɔɔtí nwaa ka bɔdubo bukpi si bɔ́sɔ búnu bula Unwoti Katɔti lɛdi. 26Na buuye bɔnii ukyuli ɔdi uulie ngba dii ka únu Katɔti ɔni nlie ngba lɛdi ɔ́siku lɛgyavonku kemmo? 27Anwuɔsu Mose, awɔ kani teesie na eteenu lɛla biala na bula Unwoti Katɔti ɔsu-bu. Na enwini abasu-bu. Na lɛla biala ɔdubo-bu bɔsu ni, bɔdubo-ni lɛlɔ bɔdi.”
28Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Línu lɛla lɛni na bekyuli bamɛni básu-ɔ. Na lɛla lɛmmɔ lɛdia. 29Si lɛni na bekyuli bamɛni badubutaabla na beteeti ɔbu teete-mi na bataadi mina ɔda bubo ƒui lɛlɔ ni, lɛla biala lɛdubuteesie kaduɛ teete-ma, ama ku bana kaba bekyuli ƒui, ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela uwi ƒui.”
30Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Teesie na atásu bekyuli bammɔ na benwini beteesie bana kɔkyakɔ. 31Nsu awɔ Mose amu adubɔsɔ bɔkya-mi kudɔ mɛni na ndubuti mina ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ ƒui lite-ɔ. Na atina bekyuli bammɔ ɔda bubo etemila ammɔ kalɛ badi-nya lɛlɔ na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ bésela betélie mmɔ.”
32Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ, bɛnu kaduɛ na bɛdi ɔda ɔni na bina Unwoti Katɔti úbo mɛni ƒui lɛlɔ. 33Bɛdi-mu lɛlɔ ƒui kalɛ na lɛla biala bɛdubɔbla lɛtɛ lite-mii na keyi kadubɔyɔku-mii na bilie ngba gyɔlɔɔ na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ bísela bitélie mmɔ.

english_text:
The Most Important Commandment
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord told me to give you these laws and teachings, so you can obey them in the land he is giving you. Soon you will cross the Jordan River and take that land. 2And if you and your descendants want to live a long time, you must always worship the Lord and obey his laws. 3Pay attention, Israel! Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he promised to give us this land that is rich with milk and honey. Be careful to obey him, and you will become a successful and powerful nation.
4 Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the only true God! 5 So love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength. 6 Memorize his laws 7and tell them to your children over and over again. Talk about them all the time, whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 8Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and foreheads to help you obey them. 9Write these laws on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
Worship Only the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10 The Lord promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you this land. Now he will take you there and give you large towns, with good buildings that you didn't build, 11and houses full of good things that you didn't put there. The Lord will give you wells that you didn't have to dig, and vineyards and olive orchards that you didn't have to plant. But when you have eaten so much that you can't eat any more, 12don't forget it was the Lord who set you free from slavery and brought you out of Egypt. 13 Worship and obey the Lord your God with fear and trembling, and promise that you will be loyal to him.
14Don't have anything to do with gods that are worshiped by the nations around you. 15If you worship other gods, the Lord will be furious and wipe you off the face of the earth. The Lord your God is with you, 16 so don't try to make him prove that he can help you, as you did at Massah. 17Always obey the laws that the Lord has given you 18-19and live in a way that pleases him. Then you will be able to go in and take this good land from your enemies, just as he promised your ancestors.
20Someday your children will ask, “Why did the Lord give us these laws and teachings?”
21Then you will answer:
We were slaves of the king of Egypt, but the Lord used his great power and set us free. 22We saw him perform miracles and make horrible things happen to the king, his officials, and everyone else. 23The Lord rescued us from Egypt, so he could bring us into this land, as he had promised our ancestors. 24-25That's why the Lord our God demands that we obey his laws and worship him with fear and trembling. And if we do, he will protect us and help us be successful.
translation_text:
Ɔmɛni Ndi Ɔda Bubo Bunengudi
1Ɔda bubo bɔmɛni na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti úte-mi ka ntina-mii. Na bɛdi-mu lɛlɔ na kalɔ kani na bɛdubo Yordan Ketu bɔvia na bitéti binwini bina kadikɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ. 2Na bina ngba bulie uwi ƒui ni, bɛnu ka amii ku bina bebi ku bawɔ bíti ɔbu bíte bina Unwoti Katɔti. Na bɛ́di nwuna ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui líti muute-mii mɛni, lɛlɔ kalɛ na bilie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ bitu uwi. 3Israelƒuɔ, binu! Bɛnu kaduɛ na bɛdi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na lɛla biala lisieku-mii kaduɛ. Na bɛdubo bumomo bubu na kalɔ kani egyiibi ntu mɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii na bísela bitélie mmɔ lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti ɔni ndi Bula Bati Kuuku Katɔti ɔ́su úse.
4Israelƒuɔ, binu kaduɛ! Unwoti ndi bula Katɔti, na anwu lɛti pɛ kani nkya. 5Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka bɛyɔ-nwu ku bina kayi ƒui ku bina kɔyu ƒui ku bina ɔyikun ƒui. 6Na bɛda ɔda bubo bɔni líti muute-mii ɔmwi kadi kamɛni lɛlɔ kaduɛ na bina kayi kemmo. 7Biti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bitaatina bina bebi kaduɛ uwi ndi uwi. Na bitaatɛmi-mu lɛlɔ si bɛkya kaduli iye bɛkɛ bísela kesii kadi iye si bilie bɛɛnwuna iye si bɛkya bina kabla akɔ. 8Binweni-mu bɛsia lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ na binyimi-mu bɛda bina enu ku atɛntɛ lɛlɔ aani linyimola. 9Na binweni-mu bɛmana bina lɛtɔ kɔyaku eli ku kɔduli ɔban kɔyakun.
Lɛla Lɛni Ndubɔlɛku-mii Si Bítadi Ɔda Bubo Bɔmmɔ Lɛlɔ
10Bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubuti-mii ubeduoku kalɔ kani na ɔ́su úse ka weti wete bina bati kuuku bani ndi Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob ku amii lɛnɔ. Kalɔ kammɔ ni, lɛma libendi lɛkya-ka kemmo ku ala ani náƒɔ kuye na ɔɔɔdi amii alati náda lɛma lɛmmɔ. 11Na ala abuni éyi lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo ɔni na ɔɔɔdi amii náwia ala ammɔ bɛ́kya-ni kemmo ku abiɔ ani na ɔɔɔdi amii néku ku mmo bɔni na ɔɔɔdi amii nátuma-mu ku nnɔ egyii ani na ɔɔɔdi amii nálɛ-nya. Na si bɛ́di na bímo ni, 12bɛnu kaduɛ kalɛ na bina kasusu kalálɛ bina Unwoti ɔni náda-mii údie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani nka bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bɛɛbla-ma kabla mmɔ.
13Bɛyia bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔmmɔ na bɛkpa anwu lɛti. Na si biisé kenye kadi ni, bise-ka na anwu lɛti lɛnyi kemmo. 14Na bitakpa bekyuli bani nli amadɔ mmɔ baƒiɔ badi betebunku-nwu lɛlɔ. 15Na si bɛ́yu atuɔkplu na bɛkya bɛɛkpá baƒiɔ bammɔ badi ni, Katɔti kɔnyi kɔdubo-mii lɛlɔ aani ogya na ɔdubɔkyula-mii na ɔyila bina udu ƒui ɔlɛku kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika Bina Katɔti ɔdi Katɔti ɔni muukpó kogyulo. 16Na ɔdi utakɔku bina Unwoti Katɔti utanu aani kalɛ na bɛ́kɔku-nwu bɛnu na kesii kani baalɔ banii Masa mmɔ. 17Na bɛnu kaduɛ na bɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui na úti úte-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ na bɛsiaku-mu kama. 18Na bɛbla ala ani nse siin na adia na Katɔti anumi kalɛ na lɛla biala lisie siin lite-mii. Na bɛkana na bisie bitéti kalɔ kabuni kani na Unwoti úse kenye úse ka weti-ka wete bina bati kuuku mmɔ binwini bina kadikɔ. 19Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na wabɔku bina bekisine ƒui wete-mii aani kalɛ na ɔ́su úse.
20Na uwi ɔdi ɔdubo ɔni na bina bebi badubo-mii buye banii, “Bi ɔsu na bula Unwoti Katɔti úbo-bu ɔda ka bɔdi nwuna ɔda bubo bɔmɛni ƒui lɛlɔ?”
21Na bɛsu-ma bɛnini, “Uwi ɔdi nábavi ni, nka bɔdi bekyuli bani na Egyipteƒuɔ bénye-bu lɛlɔ na bɔɔbla-ma kabla. Na Unwoti néti nwuna ɔyikun unengudi úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ-bu ɔ́lɛku nwuna enu kemmo. 22Bɔ́nu ku bula anumi lɛlɔ kalɛ na Katɔti ɔ́bla akɔla budie taatina enengudi lidu lidu ku ala ani mɔɔda liƒu úti úkpoku Egyipteƒuɔ ku Ɔga Ƒarao ku nwuna kabla bablane benengu. 23Na údie-bu úboku mɛni kalɛ na uti kalɔ kani na ɔ́su bula bati kuuku úse ka wete-ma ute-bu. 24Ɔmɛni ɔsu na bula Unwoti Katɔti úbo-bu ɔda ka bɔdi nwuna ɔda bubo ƒui lɛlɔ na buti ɔbu bute-nwu lɛnɔ. Na si bɔɔbla ɔmɛni ni, uwi biala ɔdubo-bu lɛlɔ butaanu na bɔlɛ lili aani kalɛ bɔɔnu ɔƒɛni. 25Na si bɔ́sia anu na bɔɔdi ɔda bubo biala na Katɔti úbo-bu lɛlɔ ni, ɔdubɔnu-bu aani bekyuli bani nse siin.”

english_text:
Force the Other Nations Out of the Land
(Exodus 34.11-16)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, the Lord your God will help you take the land of the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. These seven nations have more people and are stronger than Israel, but when you attack them, 2the Lord will force them out of the land. Then you must destroy them without mercy. Don't make any peace treaties with them, 3and don't let your sons and daughters marry any of them. 4If you do, those people will lead your descendants to worship other gods and to turn their backs on the Lord. That will make him very angry, and he will quickly destroy Israel.
5 So when you conquer these nations, tear down the altars where they worship their gods. Break up their sacred stones, cut down the poles that they use in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and throw their idols in the fire.
The Lord's Chosen People
Moses said:
6 Israel, you are the chosen people of the Lord your God. There are many nations on this earth, but he chose only Israel to be his very own. 7You were the weakest of all nations, 8but the Lord chose you because he loves you and because he had made a promise to your ancestors. Then with his mighty arm, he rescued you from the king of Egypt, who had made you his slaves.
9 You know that the Lord your God is the only true God. So love him and obey his commands, and he will faithfully keep his agreement with you and your descendants for a thousand generations. 10But if you turn against the Lord, he will quickly destroy you. 11So be sure to obey his laws and teachings I am giving you today.
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
(Deuteronomy 28.1-14; Leviticus 26.3-13)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If you completely obey these laws, the Lord your God will be loyal and keep the agreement he made with you, just as he promised our ancestors. 13The Lord will love you and bless you by giving you many children and plenty of food, wine, and olive oil. Your herds of cattle will have many calves, and your flocks of sheep will have many lambs. 14God will bless you more than any other nation—your families will grow and your livestock increase. 15You will no longer suffer with the same horrible diseases that you sometimes had in Egypt. You will be healthy, but the Lord will make your enemies suffer from those diseases.
Destroy the Nations and Their Gods
Moses said to Israel:
16When the Lord helps you defeat your enemies, you must destroy them without pity! And don't get trapped into worshiping their gods.
17You may be thinking, “How can we destroy these nations? They are more powerful than we are.” 18But stop worrying! Just remember what the Lord your God did to Egypt and its king. 19You saw how the Lord used his tremendous power to work great miracles and bring you out of Egypt. And he will again work miracles for you when you face these enemies you fear so much. 20Some of them may try to survive by hiding from you, but the Lord will make them panic, and soon they will be dead. 21So don't be frightened when you meet them in battle. The Lord your God is great and fearsome, and he will fight at your side.
22As you attack these nations, the Lord will force them out little by little. He won't let you get rid of them all at once—if he did, there wouldn't be enough people living in the land to keep down the number of wild animals. 23-24But when you attack your enemies, the Lord will make them panic, and you will easily destroy them. You will defeat their kings one after another until they are gone, and no one will remember they ever lived.
25After you conquer a nation, burn their idols. Don't get trapped into wanting the silver or gold on an idol. Even the metal on an idol is disgusting to the Lord, 26so destroy it. If you bring it home with you, both you and your house will be destroyed. Stay away from those disgusting idols!
translation_text:
Katɔti Ɔ́bɔku Kadi Bamba Bekyuli
1Amii Israelƒuɔ, si uwi ɔni na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́kpanku-mii úboku kalɔ kani na bɛdubuti binwini bina ɔdi kemmo ni, ɔdubɔbɔku Hitiƒuɔ ku Girgasiƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Hewiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ lɛnɔ ute-mii. Kadi maatɛ bamɛni bekyuli bemomo betulo-mii na bebo ɔkplu lɛnɔ betulo-mii. 2Unwoti ɔdubo-ma budie bute-mii na bɛbɔku-ma bɛlɛku kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ na ɔlɛka bɛyila-ma udu ƒui na bitanu ɔdi biala kɔnyana lɛnɔ. Amii ku-ma bitenyimi lɛla biala bitete lɛlɔ. 3Na bitaya na amii ku kadi bamba bammɔ bekyuli biti lɛlɔ. Biteti bina bebi beleku bitete-ma iye biti bana belekubi bite bina bananabi. 4Na si bɛ́ya na bábla lɛni ni, bekyuli bammɔ badubɔkpanku bina bebi na batátaakpa baƒiɔ na benwini kama bakya bana Unwoti. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na Katɔti uti kɔnyi ɔkya-mii na ɔyila-mii udu kɔnakunwi. 5Anwuɔsu ni, bibo bana akpabi ƒui bɛbwɛ. Na bibo bana atabi ani baalɔ banii atabi kedee lɛnɔ bɛbwɛ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. Na bɛƒɛ bana lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ béte bana baƒiɔ beledi bani baalɔ Asera baƒiɔ. Na bibo bana baƒiɔ ƒui bɛkya ogya kemmo.
Amii Ndi Katɔti Bekyuli Baƒunadi
6Bɛdi Unwoti Katɔti bekyuli kedee bani na ɔ́ƒuna ɔ́bla nwuna badi na kayawi bekyuli ƒui akɔ. Na bɛ́ƒɔ-nwu kuye geen.
7Katɔti útaƒuna-mii ka bimomo bitulo kadi bamba bekyuli ɔsu, ɔsika amii nse blii suɛ ntulo. 8Nsu Katɔti ɔ́ƒuna-mii, ɔsika ɔɔyɔ́-mii litemi na úse bina bati kuuku kenye úse ɔsu. Na ɔkɛnku nwuna ɔyikun bonwu kenye na úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga enu kemmo kesii kani na nka únye-mii lɛlɔ na bɛ́kya bɛɛbla kabla teete-nwu. 9Na bɛti nwaa ka bina Unwoti Katɔti kani ndi Katɔti ɔni nkya na ɔɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ uwi ndi uwi na ulalɛ-ni kama. Na ɔɔdi nwuna bunyimi lɛlɔ na uudie nwuna bɔyɔ taatina bekyuli bani mɔɔyɔ́-nwu na baadi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ útédu kaba apim apim.
10Nsu bani muukisi-nwu ni, ulenye taanu-ma gyɔlɔɔ mmomu uudie taalɛ-ma anumi ku anumi na ɔyila-ma udu kɔnakunwi. 11Anwuɔsu bɛsia anu na bitaadi nwuna ɔda bubo ku ala ani mɔɔtina-mii ɔmwi kadi mɛni lɛlɔ.
Katɔti Ɔdubute-mii Kusɛ Kusɛ Si Bɛ́di Nwuna Ɔda Bubo Lɛlɔ
12Si bɛ́di ɔda bubo bɔmɛni ƒui lɛlɔ kaduɛ ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubɔdi nwuna linyese lɛlɔ na utaayɔ-mii uwi ndi uwi aani kalɛ na ɔ́su bula bati kuuku úse. 13Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na ɔyɔ-mii litemi na bimomo na ute amii ku bina bebi kusɛ kusɛ na bɛkɛ edula pii na bina adingyii ku nnɔ egyii mmo bɔbla kaduɛ. Na bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu lɛnɔ bawɔ pii na kalɔ kani na ɔ́su bina bati kuuku úse ka wete-mii lɛlɔ. 14Katɔti ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ utulo kadi bamba bekyuli biala. Na uláya na udinkɔ ɔdi wakya amii iye bina bebuo akɔ. 15Na Katɔti ɔɔɔdubo bɔya na ɔlɛ ɔdi ubo-mii lɛlɔ. Na uláya na lɛlɛ buɛ lɛni nébo na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔdi webo-mii lɛlɔ. Mmomu kadi biala mekisi-mii ni, ɔdubɔya lɛlɛ lɛmmɔ udu libo bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ.
Bɛyila Ɔma Biala Ku Bana Baƒiɔ Udu
16Si Unwoti Katɔti úbunku-mii na bíkpo bɛ́di bina bekisine lɛlɔ ni, bɛnu ka bɛ́yila lɛla biala udu. Na bitanu ukyuli biala kɔnyana. Na bɛnu kaduɛ kalɛ na ɔdi uleduo bukpoku taanu bɔdi kemmo na ɔkpa bana baƒiɔ bammɔ badi. 17Na ɔdi utéye lɛlɔ ɔnii, “Dɛ na wabla asa na bɔkana bekyuli bamɛni udu bɔyila? Ɔsika bebo ɔyikun bétulo-bu.” 18Biteti kasusu kammɔ udu bitekpoku lɛlɔ. Mmomu binyimo kaduɛ lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́bla Egyipteƒuɔ ku bana ɔga. 19Na bɛ́nu kalɛ na ɔkɛnku Unwoti Katɔti ɔyikun bonwu ku akɔla lidu lidu budie taatina lɛlɔ na Katɔti ɔ́da-mii údie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na lɛni kani na ɔdubɔbla akɔla na bina akɔ si bɛ́siaku bina bekisine bani mɔɔda-mii liƒu mmɔ. 20Na bekisine bani mekeli matábɛ ku bani ƒui mekeli kukpi ni, Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubɔya na ɔtɔtɔ bonwu ɔgyu-ma na bekpi kɔnakunwi.
21Anwuɔsu si bɛ́da bɛ́lɛ-ma lɛlɔ na kekpo kemmo ni, bitaya bana lɛlɔ liƒu lɛda-mii. Ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti údu na ɔkya-mii akɔ na ɔɔda liƒu, na anwu ndubukpo ute-mii. 22Na Katɔti ɔɔyɔ́ ka bitaayila kadi bamba bekyuli bammɔ udu blii blii, na ɔɔɔdi kɔnakunwi. Ɔsika si bítabla lɛni ni, beƒiebuo badubumomo betulo-mii. 23Nsu si bísie bítékpoku bina bekisine ni, Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubɔya na bana kasusu keƒu na ɔbla-ma gyuma gyuma utédu ka bɛ́yila-ma udu ƒui. 24Na bɛdubɔdi baga bammɔ lɛlɔ na ɔdi ɔsɔ ulenyimo si bélie ngba dii. Na ɔdi ulakana-mii bunye bɔsiaku lɛnɔ.
25Na si bɛ́di kadi bekyuli badi lɛlɔ ni, bɛkyula bana baƒiɔ bani na bátu bálɛ. Nsu ɔdi biala ɔnu kaduɛ na anumi etegyie-nwu na bana sika ugyiedi iye ɔƒualadi ɔni na béti bámana bana baƒiɔ bammɔ lɛlɔ na ɔdi ɔsu ɔnii uuti ɔdi. Ɔsika Katɔti ukisi ala ammɔ na adi kakpagyuɛ ete-mii. 26Anwuɔsu bɛyila lɛla biala na Katɔti ukisi mmɔ udu. Ɔsika si ɔdi úti lɛla lɛmmɔ udu úboku nwuna kaduli ni, Katɔti ɔdubɔyila ukyuli ɔni nábla lɛla lɛmmɔ ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui udu. Anwuɔsu ukyuli biala ɔda lɛlɔ ɔmami lɛƒiɔkpa lɛlɔ, ɔsika Katɔti ɔdubudie ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu use lɛti ka ɔkyula.

english_text:
The Lord Takes Care of You
Moses said:
1Israel, do you want to go into the land the Lord promised your ancestors? Do you want to capture it, live there, and become a powerful nation? Then be sure to obey every command I am giving you.
2Don't forget how the Lord your God has led you through the desert for the past 40 years. He wanted to find out if you were truly willing to obey him and depend on him, 3 so he made you go hungry. Then he gave you manna, a kind of food that you and your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was teaching you that people need more than food to live—they need every word that the Lord has spoken.
4Over the past 40 years, your clothing hasn't worn out, and your feet haven't swollen. 5 So keep in mind that the Lord has been correcting you, just as parents correct their children. 6Obey the commands the Lord your God has given you and worship him with fear and trembling.
7The Lord your God is bringing you into a good land with streams that flow from springs in the valleys and hills. 8-9You can dig for copper in those hills, and the stones are made of iron ore. And you won't go hungry. Wheat and barley fields are everywhere, and so are vineyards and orchards full of fig, pomegranate, and olive trees, and there is plenty of honey.
Don't Forget the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10After you eat and are full, give praise to the Lord your God for the good land he gave you. 11 Make sure that you never forget the Lord or disobey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. If you always obey them, 12you will have plenty to eat, and you will build good houses to live in. 13You will get more and more cattle, sheep, silver, gold, and other possessions.
14But when all this happens, don't be proud! Don't forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and that it was the Lord who set you free. 15Remember how he led you in that huge and frightening desert where poisonous snakes and scorpions live. There was no water, but the Lord split open a rock, and water poured out so you could drink. 16He also gave you manna, a kind of food your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was testing you to make you trust him, so that later on he could be good to you.
17When you become successful, don't say, “I'm rich, and I've earned it all myself.” 18Instead, remember that the Lord your God gives you the strength to make a living. That's how he keeps the promise he made to your ancestors.
19-20But I'm warning you—if you forget the Lord your God and worship other gods, the Lord will destroy you, just as he destroyed the nations you fought.
translation_text:
Biteenyimo Katɔti Uwi Ndi Uwi
1Si bɛ́sia anu na bɛɛdi ɔda bubo bɔni muute-mii ɔmwi mɛni ƒui lɛlɔ ni, bɛdubusie na bitélie kalɔ kani na Unwoti úse kenye ka weti wete bina bati kuuku mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na bɛdubulie mmɔ na bimomo na biti kalɔ kammɔ binwini bina ɔdi. 2Na bitayiƒala kalɛ na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́tɔnku-mii na kalɔ kakwiidi kamɛni kemmo akwa aavlene. Ɔ́bla ɔmɛni ɔnii ɔɔnu si bɛdubɔti ka anwu nda-mii. Na ɔkɔku-mii ɔnu si bina kasusu kadubɔsia-nwu lɛlɔ na bɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. 3Anwuɔsu ɔ́ya na kɔka kɔ́da-mii na úte-mii adila ani baalɔ banii manna ɔ́siku Katɔ na bɛ́di. Na adila ammɔ udu ni, bina bati kuuku iye amii bina ɔdi útanu-nya kudii. Ɔ́bla ɔmɛni ɔ́tina-mii na biti bɛtɛya ala ka ɔɔɔdi lɛdila lɛti pɛ muute ukyuli ngba. Mmomu litemi biala na lɛ́si Katɔti kudɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi muute ngba geen bɔmmɔ. 4Na bɛnu bɛti ka akwa aavlene amɛni ulu busie kemmo ƒui ni, ɔdi biala awu útabwɛ na ɔdi ɔgba lɛnɔ úteƒu. 5Anwuɔsu bɛya na ɔbla-mii kasusu ka kalɛ kani na si bina bebi bábla ala ani naaadia na bɛɛdɔnku-ma ni, lɛni kani na si amii lɛnɔ bɛ́bla ala ani naaadia Unwoti Katɔti lɛnɔ na ɔdubɔdɔnku-mii.
6Bɛdi ɔda bubo bɔni na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti úte-mii mɛni lɛlɔ, na bɛsia-mu kama na biti ɔbu bite-nwu. 7Ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubuti-mii ubeduoku kalɔ kani na kadia kemmo. Ntukpa búyi-ka, na aba ntu lɛnɔ bɔkya mmɔ, na abiɔ ntu aalɛ́ abinkpo lɛlɔ ku awɛ kemmo. 8Na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ni, edula ebi aani anta ku kakpa ku ana lidu pii lɛkya ku egyiibi bamba lidu ku nnɔ egyii ku uwɔ. 9Na si bílie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ni, kɔka kulada-mii kudii iye bilayaki lɛla lɛdi. Na atakpɛ ammɔ kemmo ni, bɛdubɔkɛ abuala ani na beeti taakywɛ kɔlɛmii. Na abuala kpakplaa ku ani nse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ lɛnɔ akya abi ammɔ kemmo.
Bitedie Atu Na Nwuna Ɔda Bubo Lɛlɔ
10Si bɛ́di na bímo ni, binyimo na biti linugya bite bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔkɛnku kalɔ kabuni kani na úti úte-mii ɔsu. 11Na bise likpo na bitayiƒala Unwoti Katɔti. Na bitedie atu na nwuna ɔda bubo ku nwuna ala bɔtina bɔni líti muute-mii ɔmwi mɛni lɛlɔ. 12Na si bɛ́di bímo na bɛ́tu lɛtɔ lɛbuni na bilie-ni kemmo 13na bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu báwɔ pii na sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku akɛla bamba émomo ni, 14bɛnu kaduɛ na bilatalaku lɛlɔ katɔ na bɛyiƒala bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nébedie-mii na Egyipteƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani na bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bɛɛbla bana kabla.
15Na binyimo kalɛ na ɔ́tɔnku-mii na kalɔ kakwiidi bonwu kamɛni kemmo, kesii kani na balakpi bekpidi ku batamlukpa bakya. Ntu bútakya mmɔ, nsu Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na ntu bɔ́bwɛ bɔ́lɛ lɛtakpɛ kemmo na bɛ́ni. 16Na úte-mii adila ani ndi manna na kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo. Na adila ɔmmɔ udu ni, bina bati kuuku muedi bátati-nya kudii. Na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́bla ɔmɛni ɔnii ɔɔnu si bɛdubɔti ka anwu nda-mii, na ɔkɔku bina bɔƒɔtaadi ɔnu kalɛ na weti ala abuni wete-mii na kawɔlɔkɔ ku kaƒɔ ƒaa.
17Na si bɛ́kɛ akɛla amɛni udu ni, ɔdi utasu ɔnini, “Akɛla pii ani na mbo mɛni ni, ami ɔlati ɔyikun ku ɔlɔkplu na líti lɛ́kɛ-nya.” 18Mmomu binyimo ka bina Unwoti Katɔti néte-mii ɔyikun ɔmmɔ asa na bɛ́bla akɛla ammɔ na úti ɔɔtina ka ɔ́di kenye kani na úse ku bina bati kuuku úse lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na use ɔmwi mɛni.
19Nsu mɔɔsu-mii nwaa ɔmwi ka si bínwini kama bɛ́kya bina Unwoti Katɔti na bísie bɛɛkpá ala bamba ni, Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubɔyila bina ƒui udu. 20Kalɛ na ɔ́yila kadi bamba bekyuli bani nákya bina ulu lɛlɔ ni, lɛni kani na ɔdubo-mii udu bɔyila si bítadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ.

english_text:
Why the Lord Will Help Israel
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to me! You will soon cross the Jordan River and go into the land to force out the nations that live there. They are more powerful than you are, and the walls around their cities reach to the sky. 2Some of these nations are descendants of the Anakim. You know how tall and strong they are, and you've heard that no one can defeat them in battle. 3But the Lord your God has promised to go ahead of you, like a raging fire burning everything in its path. So when you attack your enemies, it will be easy for you to destroy them and take their land.
4-6After the Lord helps you wipe out these nations and conquer their land, don't think he did it because you are such good people. You aren't good—you are stubborn! No, the Lord is going to help you, because the nations that live there are evil, and because he wants to keep the promise he made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
When Israel Made an Idol
(Exodus 32)
Moses said to Israel:
7Don't ever forget how you kept rebelling and making the Lord angry the whole time you were in the desert. You rebelled from the day you left Egypt until the day you arrived here.
8At Mount Sinai you made the Lord so angry that he was going to destroy you. 9-11 It happened during those 40 days and nights that I was on the mountain, without anything to eat or drink. He had told me to come up there so he could give me the agreement he made with us. And this agreement was actually the same Ten Commandments he had announced to you when he spoke from the fire on the mountain. The Lord had written them on two flat stones with his own hand. But after giving me the two stones, 12he said:
Moses, hurry down the mountain to those people you led out of Egypt. They have already disobeyed me and committed the terrible sin of making an idol.
13I've been watching the Israelites, and I've seen how stubborn and rebellious they are. 14So don't try to stop me! I am going to wipe them out, and no one on earth will remember they ever lived. Then I will let your descendants become an even bigger and more powerful nation than Israel.
Moses said:
15Fire was raging on the mountaintop as I went back down, carrying the two stones with the commandments on them. 16I saw how quickly you had sinned and disobeyed the Lord your God. There you were, worshiping the metal idol you had made in the shape of a calf. 17So I threw down the two stones and smashed them before your very eyes.
18-20I bowed down at the place of worship and prayed to the Lord, without eating or drinking for 40 days and nights. You had committed a terrible sin by making that idol, and the Lord hated what you had done. He was angry enough to destroy all of you and Aaron as well. So I prayed for you and Aaron as I had done before, and this time the Lord answered my prayers.
