21It was a sin for you to make that idol, so I threw it into the fire to melt it down. Then I took the lump of gold, ground it into powder, and threw the powder into the stream flowing down the mountain.
22 You also made the Lord angry when you were staying at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-Hattaavah. 23 Then at Kadesh-Barnea the Lord said, “I am giving you the land, so go ahead and take it!” But since you didn't trust the Lord, you rebelled and disobeyed his command. 24In fact, you've rebelled against the Lord for as long as he has known you.
25After you had made the idol in the shape of a calf, the Lord said he was going to destroy you. So I lay face down in front of the Lord for 40 days and nights 26and prayed:
Our Lord, please don't wipe out your people. You used your great power to rescue them from Egypt and to make them your very own. 27Israel's ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob obeyed you faithfully. Think about them, and not about Israel's stubbornness, evil, and sin. 28If you destroy your people, the Egyptians will say, “The Lord promised to give Israel land, but he wasn't powerful enough to keep his promise. In fact, he hated them so much that he took them into the desert and killed them.” 29But you, our Lord, chose the people of Israel to be your own, and with your mighty power you rescued them from Egypt.
translation_text:
Israelƒuɔ Bábla Atuɔkplu
1Bise atu na binu! Ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ ni, bɛdubo Yordan Ketu bɔvia na bisie bitáƒɔ kalɔ kani na kana bekyuli bemomo na bebo ɔyikun betulo-mii binwini bina kadikɔ. Na bana lɛma linengudi líbomo kaduɛ na lɛma lɛmmɔ awodu ákuku ésie kayaa geen. 2Na bekyuli bammɔ alati bákuku na bebo ɔyikun na baalɔ-ma Anakƒuɔ. Na bínu ka básu dii ka bekyuli badi beeebo na bakana bunye bɔsiaku-ma. 3Nsu ɔƒɛni amii ɔlati bɛdubo bɔnu ka bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo bɔgyu bɔtɔ-mii anumi aani ogya ɔni mɔɔkyula ala kalɛ. Na ɔdubo-ma udu bɔyila na ɔdi-ma lɛlɔ uwi ɔni na bɛ́kpɛ bíde-ma kalɛ na bɛkɛ kuƒi na bɛbɔku-ma bɛlɛku bana lɛma. Na ɔdia na bɛyila-ma udu pla aani kalɛ úse kenye úse.
4Na si bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́bɔku-ma úte-mii ni, bitasu lɛlɔ ka úti-mii úboku kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ, ɔsika amii bise siin ɔsu. Oowo! Ɔɔɔdi lɛni na use. Mmomu lɛla lɛni ɔsu na Unwoti ɔɔbɔku-ma ndi ka bekyuli bammɔ badi bekyuli bekpidi ɔsu. 5Na ɔɔɔdi ka bɛdi bekyuli babuni na bɛɛbla ala ani nse siin ɔsu na Unwoti ɔ́ya na bísie bitéti bana kalɔ bínwini bina kadikɔ. Mmomu Unwoti ɔdubo-ma bɔbɔku, ɔsika bekyuli bammɔ badi bekyuli bekpidi. Na ka ɔɔyɔ́ ka ɔdi nwuna linyese lɛlɔ ute bina bati kuuku bani ndi Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob lɛnɔ ɔsu na ɔɔbɔku bekyuli bammɔ. 6Anwuɔsu bɛnu ka ɔɔɔdi bina ala bɔbla ulu lɛlɔ ɔsu na Unwoti úti kalɔ kani na kélie lɛmwi mɛni uute-mii. Ɔsika batuɔkplune na amii lɛnɔ bɛdi.
7Bitayiƒala kalɛ na bɛ́ya na Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-mii na kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo. Úti ɔ́si limeyi lɛni lɛlɔ na bɛ́ta Egyipte kalɔ úti úbedu limeyi lɛni bíbeduo mɛni ni, lɛni kani na bɛkya bɛɛta teenye Unwoti lɛlɔ. 8Na bɛ́kya Unwoti kɔnyi geen na Sinai Kɔbi lɛlɔ ɔni na úbu blii nka ɔyila-mii udu ƒui. 9Lɛ́kɔ lísie kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili nnii ntáƒɔ kenye kani na únyimiku-mii na únweni ɔ́sia atabi bɛbɛ anyɔ ammɔ lɛlɔ. Lílie kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili emeyi aavlene usien ku ɔƒɛ ɔni na ńtadi na ńtani. 10Mmɔ na Unwoti úti atabi anyɔ ammɔ na anwu ɔlati úti nwuna kɔnu na únweni etemila ani na ɔ́tɛmiku-mii ɔ́siku lɛgyavonku kemmo na limeyi lɛni bɛ́sala lisu na kɔbi kɔmmɔ kaƒɔna úte-mi.
11Na emeyi aavlene ammɔ kama na Unwoti úti atabi anyɔ ani lɛlɔ na únweni kenye kani na únyimiku-mii ɔ́sia mmɔ úte-mi. 12Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Yu teesie kɔbi kɔmmɔ kalɔ kɔnakunwi. Ɔsika bekyuli bani na ákpanku álɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ báƒiɔ-mi geen. Na bálɛ ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na lɛ́su-ma ka basia na bávɔ baƒiɔ mmomu bese lɛlɔ lɛlɔ baakpá.”
13Na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ami Unwoti ngyi ka bekyuli bamɛni bebo atuɔkplu geen. 14Anwuɔsu te-mi kuƒi na lɛyila bekyuli bamɛni udu. Na linine bana anyi lidie na ɔƒɛ kalɔ. Na ndubudie kadi bekyuli bani ndubɔyu ɔyikun geen na bimomo bitulo-ma lɛsiku-ɔ kemmo.”
15Anwuɔsu líti atabi anyɔ bɛbɛ ani na Katɔti únweni kenye kani na únyimiku-mii ɔ́sia mmɔ na lɛ́yu kɔbi kɔni mɔɔda ku ogya bonwu mmɔ líbo. 16Na ka mɔɔnu ni, lɛ́nu ka bɛ́bla likpidi bɛ́ƒiɔ bina Unwoti Katɔti. Ɔsika bɛ́vɔ ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔkɔdi ɔgyani udu na bɛɛkpá-nwu aani baƒiɔ na bínwini kama bɛ́kya Katɔti ɔƒɛni kani ɔdi ɔmɛni. 17Anwuɔsu líƒwimi atabi anyɔ ammɔ lɛ́va na ábwɛ kɔkɛ kɔkɛ na bina anumi.
18Amu na kunyɔdi lɛnɔ ntayu lɛ́tɛ Unwoti anumi na líti mina anumi líbi kalɔ emeyi aavlene usien ku ɔƒɛ ɔni na ntadi iye ntani lɛla lɛdi. Lɛ́bla ɔmɛni ƒui ɔ́si likpidi lɛni bɛ́bla Unwoti na bɛɛbla lɛla lɛni naaayɔ-nwu kaƒɔ ɔsu. Na bɛ́ya na ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi. 19Ka mɔɔyia Unwoti kɔnyi ɔsu ku kalɛ ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi kpakplaa kɔni na úti ku kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́ ka ɔyila-mii udu ɔsu ni, lɛ́bla ɔmɛni ƒui. Na Unwoti kaƒɔ káyɔ-nwu na únu mina buvele. 20Lɛni kani na Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya Aaron na ɔ́yɔ ka ɔdu-nwu, na lívele líte-nwu uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani. 21Amu na líti lɛla likpidi lɛni bɛ́vɔ mmɔ aani ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔgyani ɔkɔdi na líƒwimi lɛ́kya ogya kemmo. Na lídie-nwu na lɛ́ƒɛ-nwu eku eku, na lɛ́kɔ-nwu na únwini ntɔ, na líbo ntɔ bɔmmɔ líwi ketu kani mɔɔgbá taayu kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.
22Na uwi ɔni na bílie kesii kani baalɔ Tabera ku Masa ku Kibrot-Hataawa ni, lɛni kani na bɛ́kya bina Unwoti Katɔti kɔnyi.
23Ka bɛ́kya Kades Barnea ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-mii ɔnii, “Biteesie na bitéti kalɔ kani na líti muute-mii mmɔ binwini bina kadikɔ.” Nsu bítaƒɔ-nwu bítadi na bítabu nwuna litemi lɛni na ɔ́su-mii mmɔ. Mmomu bɔta na bɛ́ta binye-nwu lɛlɔ. 24Na ɔ́si uwi ɔni na ami Mose lɛ́ti-mii ni, bɔta kani na bɛɛta teenye Unwoti lɛlɔ.
25Anwuɔsu lɛ́yu lɛ́tɛ kalɔ na línwini anumi libi kalɔ na Unwoti anumi emeyi aavlene ammɔ kemmo usien ku ɔƒɛ. Ɔsika línu ka Unwoti ɔ́su ka ɔdubɔyila-mii udu. 26Mmɔ na lɛ́kpali-nwu lívele-nwu nnii, “O Ɔyikune Ƒui Katɔti, tayila ƒula bekyuli bani na ɔkɛnku ƒula ɔyikun ku ɔlɔkplu na édie-ma álɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ udu. 27Na enyimo ƒula kabla bablane bani ndi Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob, na alakpete bekyuli bamɛni atuɔkplu ku likyulikpi ku bana ekpidi ani bábla. 28Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, Egyipteƒuɔ badubɔsu banii átakana na akpanku ƒula bekyuli bammɔ esienku kalɔ kani ásu ése ka éti-ma éselaku mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na badubɔsu lɛnɔ banii bɔkpanku na ákpanku ƒula bekyuli bammɔ esienku kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo na átadu-ma. Ɔsika eekisi-ma. 29Ɔmɛni ƒui kama ni, bekyuli bamɛni na áƒuna na éti-ma ábla ƒula badi. Na ama na édie álɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku ƒula ɔyikun bonwu ku ɔlɔkplu ɔsu.”

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Exodus 34.1-10)
Moses said to the people:
1The Lord told me to chisel out two flat stones, just like the ones he had given me earlier. He also commanded me to make a wooden chest, then come up the mountain and meet with him. 2He told me that he would write on the new stones the same words he had written on the ones I broke, and that I could put these stones in this sacred chest.
3So I made a chest out of acacia wood, and I chiseled two flat stones like the ones I broke. Then I carried the stones up the mountain, 4where the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them, just as he had done the first time. The commandments were exactly what he had announced from the fire, when you were gathered at the mountain.
After the Lord returned the stones to me, 5I took them down the mountainside and put them in the chest, just as he had commanded. And they are still there.
Aaron Died
(Numbers 20.22-29)
Moses said to Israel:
6 Later we set up camp at the wells belonging to the descendants of Jaakan. Then we moved on and camped at Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became the priest. 7Next, we camped at Gudgodah and then at Jotbathah, where there are flowing streams.
The Levites Were Appointed To Carry the Chest
Moses said to Israel:
8 After I put the two stones in the sacred chest, the Lord chose the tribe of Levi, not only to carry the chest, but also to serve as his priests at the place of worship and to bless the other tribes in his name. And they still do these things. 9The Lord promised that he would always provide for the tribe of Levi, and that's why he won't give them any land, when he divides it among the other tribes.
The Lord Answered the Prayers of Moses
(Exodus 34.9,10,27-29)
Moses said to Israel:
10 When I had taken the second set of stones up the mountain, I spent 40 days and nights there, just as I had done before. Once again, the Lord answered my prayer and did not destroy you. 11Instead, he told me, “Moses, get ready to lead the people into the land that I promised their ancestors.”
What the Lord Wants
Moses said:
12People of Israel, what does the Lord your God want from you? The Lord wants you to respect and follow him, to love and serve him with all your heart and soul, 13and to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. Do this, and all will go well for you.
14Everything belongs to the Lord your God, not only the earth and everything on it, but also the sky and the highest heavens. 15Yet the Lord loved your ancestors and wanted them to belong to him. So he chose them and their descendants rather than any other nation, and today you are still his people.
16Remember your agreement with the Lord and stop being so stubborn. 17 The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind. 18 The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing. 19And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
20Respect the Lord your God, be faithful, and serve only him, making promises in his name. 21Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
22 When your ancestors went to live in Egypt, there were only 70 of them. But the Lord has blessed you, and now there are more of you than there are stars in the sky.
translation_text:
Katɔti Ɔ́sɔ Únweni Ɔda Bubo Leevu Bɔni Na Mose Úbo Ɔ́buɛ Mmɔ
1Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Sɔ nwi atabi anyɔ bamba aani edeedi kalɛ. Na anwi ugyii adaka ɔdi na eti atabi ammɔ na akɔ. Na eti adaka ɔmmɔ na akɔ ebo-mi kudɔ na kɔbi lɛlɔ mɛni. 2Na nsɔ ndubo ala edeedi ani na línweni lɛ́sia atabi ani na ébo ábwɛ mmɔ lɛlɔ bunweni bɔsia awɔdi amɛni lɛlɔ. Na si línweni lɛ́wɔlɔ ni, na eti atabi ammɔ akya adaka ɔmmɔ kemmo.”
3Anwuɔsu líti Akasia kugyii na lɛ́nwi adaka ɔni na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi mmɔ na lɛ́nwi atabi awɔdi aani kalɛ kani na atabi edeedi ammɔ ese pɛpɛɛpɛ na líti-nya lísienku kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. 4Amu na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ únweni ɔda bubo etemila leevu ɔ́sia atabi ammɔ lɛlɔ. Etemila ani kani na únweni ɔ́sia atabi edeedi ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na adi ɔda bubo etemila ani kani na ɔ́kɔ lɛsa úte-mii ɔ́siku ogya bonwu ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔni na bɛ́sala binye kɔbi kɔmmɔ kaƒɔna mmɔ. 5Amu ka Unwoti úti atabi ammɔ úte-mi ni, líti-nya líboku kɔbi kada na líti-nya lɛ́kya adaka ɔmmɔ kemmo aani kalɛ na ɔ́su-mi na akya mmɔ úbedu ɔmwi kadi.
6Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ bákya kesii kani na Yaakan kadi bekyuli abiɔ ákya. Na báta mmɔ bésie Mosera. Na mmɔ na Aaron úkpi na báva-nwu. Nwuna kama ni, ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ banii Eleasar úti-nwu keliekɔ aani Katɔti Ɔkpane. 7Na ka bási Mosera ni, báta bétélie Gudgod. Na ka bási Gudgod ni, bésie Yotba kesii kani na ntukpa bɔkya kaduɛ. 8Na uwi ɔni na líti atabi ammɔ lɛ́yulaku kɔbi ḿbakya Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Unwoti údie Lewi kɔdua bekyuli ka ama nteeti adaka ɔmmɔ. Na bénwini Unwoti Bakpane. Na ama ndubo kusɛ kusɛ buteeti teete Israelƒuɔ na Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo. Na bataabla-nwu kabla aani kalɛ na use ɔmwi. 9Ɔmɛni ɔsu na Lewi kɔdua bekyuli beeebo kadikɔ kadi na kalɔ kammɔ kemmo aani kalɛ na adua akladi bebo kalɛ. Mmomu bana kadikɔ kakya Katɔti bɛkpa kabla kani na baabla kemmo aani kalɛ na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse.
10Uwi ɔni na kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, lɛ́kya mmɔ emeyi aavlene usien ku ɔƒɛ emeyi aani kalɛ kani na lɛ́kya kudeedi. Na Unwoti únu mina buvele na bina lili. Anwuɔsu na útayila-mii udu. 11Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ta na atɔnku ƒula bekyuli na betélie kalɔ kani na lɛ́su líse ka meti mete bina bati kuuku mmɔ lɛlɔ.”
Katɔti Ɔɔwia Lɛla Lɛdi Ɔsiku Israelƒuɔ Kudɔ
12Lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔɔwia ɔsiku bina kudɔ ndi ka biti ɔbu bite-nwu na bɛsia nwuna ulu ɔni na ɔ́tina-mii na bɛyɔ-nwu ku bina kayi ƒui ku bina kɔyu ƒui. 13Na bɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo bɔni na líti muute-mii mɛni ƒui lɛlɔ. Na si bɛ́bla lɛni ni, lɛla biala lɛdubɔtɛ lite-mii.
14Bɛti nwaa ka ala ani ƒui nkya kayawi kemmo ni, adi bina Unwoti Katɔti adi. Na kayaa ku ala ani ƒui nkya-ka kemmo lɛnɔ adi nwuna adi. 15Nsu ka Unwoti ɔɔyɔ́ bina bati kuuku geen ɔsu na amii kani na úti ɔ́bla nwuna bekyuli. Na bɛmu bɛdi nwuna bekyuli. 16Anwuɔsu bɛda likpidi biala bidie bina kayi kemmo na bɛda atuɔkplu bɔbla bɛya.
17Ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti ubo ɔyikun utulo ɔyikun biala na ɔlɛka buti ɔbu bute-nwu geen. Na ɔdi Unwoti ɔni na ulánu anumi taabla lɛla lɛdi na ulabɛ taaƒɔ lɛla lɛdi ukyuli kudɔ. 18Na ɔdi-nwu lɛyɔla ka bekpinebi ku bekpinele baakɛ́ bana kadikɔ. Na ɔɔyɔ́ baƒɔ litemi na uute-ma adila ku adala. 19Anwuɔsu amii lɛnɔ bidie bina bɔyɔ bɛtina baƒɔ bammɔ. Ɔsika amii lɛnɔ bɛ́ɛbla baƒɔ dii na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. 20Na biti ɔbu bite bina Unwoti Katɔti na bitaakpa anwu lɛti pɛ. Bɛsiaku-nwu kama kpakplaa. 21Biteemwi-nwu uwi ndi uwi, ɔsika ɔdi bina Unwoti Katɔti. Na bina ɔdi biala ɔ́nu ku nwuna lɛnumi ala ebendi ani na ɔ́bla úte-mii ku ani mɔɔda liƒu. 22Uwi ɔni na bina bati kuuku báta bésie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, na bana bumomo bɔbla liti ku aavlanyɔ kani. Nsu ɔƒɛni ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na bímomo aani katɔ ayabi.

english_text:
If You Are Loyal to the Lord, He Will Bless You
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord is your God, so you must always love him and obey his laws and teachings. 2Remember, he corrected you and not your children. You are the ones who saw the Lord use his great power 3 when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people. 4 And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
5You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here. 6 And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
7With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
8Soon you will cross the Jordan River, and if you obey the laws and teachings I'm giving you today, you will be strong enough to conquer the land 9that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time. 10It's better land than you had in Egypt, where you had to struggle just to water your crops. 11But the hills and valleys in the promised land are watered by rain from heaven, 12because the Lord your God keeps his eye on this land and takes care of it all year long.
13 The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him, 14-15he will send rain at the right seasons, so you will have more than enough food, wine, and olive oil, and there will be plenty of grass for your cattle.
16But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods, 17the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
18 Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them. 19Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 20Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates. 21Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
22Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants, 23he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack. 24 You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea. 25No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
26You have a choice—do you want the Lord to bless you, or do you want him to put a curse on you? 27Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you. 28But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
29 After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal. 30You know that these two mountains are west of the Jordan River in land now controlled by the Canaanites living in the Jordan River valley. The mountains are west of the road near the sacred trees of Moreh on the other side of Gilgal.
31Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there, 32be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
translation_text:
Katɔti Údie Nwuna Litemi Lɛlɔ Bɔdi Ɔ́tina
1Bɛyɔ bina Unwoti Katɔti na bitaadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ uwi ndi uwi. 2Na binyimo kalɛ na ɔ́ni-mii kɔtu ku kalɛ na údie nwuna ɔyikun kpakplaa ɔ́tina-mii. Nsu bina bebi ama ni, Katɔti útani-ma kɔtu kɔdi. 3Bebi bammɔ bátanu akɔla budie taatina lidu lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔ́tina Egyipteƒuɔ ku bana ɔga na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. 4Na bátanu kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́yila Egyipteƒuɔ bekpone ku bana bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɔni mɔɔní-ma udu. Na ɔ́ya na Ɛpugyie úti-ma uwi ɔni na bábi básiaku-mii mmɔ. 5Na baaagyi lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́bla úte-mii na kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo asa na bíbedu mɛni. 6Binyimo lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́bla Datan ku Abiram bani ndi Eliab bebi bani nási Ruben kɔdua kemmo. Na bina ƒui anumi ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na kalɔ kébimi kenye na kébweli-ma ku bana kaduli bekyuli ku bana adi kevo kani bátu ku bana bebuo ƒui. 7Na amii ndi bekyuli bani nánu ala ebendi ani na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́bla mɛni.
Katɔti Úse Kenye Ka Wete Israelƒuɔ Kusɛ Kusɛ Si Béduo Kalɔ Kawɔdi Kammɔ Lɛlɔ
8Bɛnu kaduɛ na bɛdi ɔda bubo ku ala ani na lɛ́tina-mii ɔmwi kadi mɛni lɛlɔ ƒui kalɛ na bɛkɛ ɔyikun na bɛvia Yordan Ketu na bitélie kalɔ kammɔ kemmo. 9Na ɔmmɔ ndubɔya na bilie bitu uwi na kakɔ kani egyiibi ntu mɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii mmɔ lɛlɔ. Kalɔ kammɔ na Unwoti Katɔti úse kenye ka wete bina bati kuuku ku bana bawɔ. 10Na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela bitélie mmɔ ni, keeese aani Egyipteƒuɔ kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bílie mmɔ. Ɔsika Egyipteƒuɔ kalɔ kammɔ ni, si bɛ́va edula ni, ɔlɛka bibo abi na biwi-nya ntu asa na edula ammɔ adia. 11Nsu kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela mɛni aka ni, kadi abi ku ɔkwalɛ kalɔ na ɔnantu ntu mɔɔdia edula na mmɔ. 12Ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔɔnu kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ lɛkwa limodi.
13Anwuɔsu bɛdi ɔda bubo bɔni mɔɔsu-mii ɔmwi kadi mɛni lɛlɔ nnii bɛyɔ bina Unwoti Katɔti na biti bina kayi ƒui bitaakpa-nwu. 14Na si bɛɛdi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubɔya na ɔnantu utaana kaƒɛndi ku ketudi na bilayaki edula aani antabi ku ntɛ ku nnɔ. 15Na ɔdubɔya na livo litaakwɛ pii kalɛ na bina ɔmantɛ bebuo bataakɛ-nya taakun. Na amii lɛnɔ kɔka kulada-mii.
16Na bitaya na ukyuli ɔdi ɔtɔlɔ-mii na bɛlɛ bina Unwoti kama na bitákpa baƒiɔ badi. 17Ɔsika si bɛ́lɛ-nwu kama ni, ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na uti kɔnyi ɔkya-mii geen na ɔya na ɔnantu ɔda bɔna ɔya na kalɔ kabuni kani na úte-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ na kakwii. Na si bɛ́va edula adi ni, alakana bɔkwɛ. Na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na bikpi bɛkya kalɔ kammɔ kemmo. 18Bɛtɛya ɔda bubo etemila ammɔ bɛkya bina lili kemmo na biteeti-nya lɛlɔ kasusu. Na binweni-nya bɛsia kɔkunkɛ lɛlɔ na bibo bɛda bina enu ku atɛntɛ. Na si bɛ́bla lɛni ni, ɔdububunku-mii na bitaadi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. 19Na bɛya na bina bebi batɛya ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ. Na si bɛkya kaduli iye bɛkɛ ulu bísela kesii kadi iye bilie bɛɛnwuna iye bɛkya bɛɛbla kabla kadi ni, biti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ binwini bina kɔtɛ kɔni na bɛɛtɛmi. 20Na binweni ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɛmana bina lɛtɔ kɔyakun ku kɔduli kɔyakun anumi. 21Na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti úse kenye ka weti wete bina bati kuuku ni, amii ku bina bebi bɛdubulie-ka lɛlɔ bítu uwi aani kalɛ na kayaa kammɔ kebi kalɔ lɛlɔ késela uwi ƒui.
22Bɛdi ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti úte-mii mɛni lɛlɔ kaduɛ na bɛyɔ-nwu. Na bɛbla lɛla biala na wasu-mii. Na bɛda-nwu kpakplaa. 23Na si bɛɛsia nwuna ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ anu ni, Katɔti ɔdubɔbɔku kadi bamba bekyuli ƒui udie bana kɔlɔ lɛlɔ na amii bitéti kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ ina ka bekyuli bammɔ bemomo na bebo ɔyikun bétulo-mii. 24Na kesi kesii na bina lɛgba lɛɛnya ni, kalɔ kammɔ kadubɔbla bina kadi ɔ́si kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo na kada kakɛ úti útédu Lebanon na katɔ kakɛ na ɔ́si Euƒrate Ketudɔ na ɔƒɛ katukɔ úti utédu Mediterenia Ɛpu na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ. 25Na kesi kesii bísela ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubɔya na bekyuli bani nlie kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ bayia-mii geen aani kalɛ na ɔ́su úse. Na uláya na ukyuli ɔdi unye utile-mii ulu.
26Bɛnu! Nda kusɛ kusɛ ku ewida mɔɔvá-mi anumi ɔmwi kadi. Bidie ɔni na bɛɛyɔ́. 27Kusɛ kusɛ ɔdubɔsiaku-mii si bɛɛdi bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔni na líti muute-mii ɔmwi kadi mɛni lɛlɔ. 28Nsu ewida adubɔsiaku-mii si bɛ́lɛ-nwu kama na bísie bɛɛkpá baƒiɔ bani na bɛɛɛgyi kudii. 29Na si uwi ɔni na Unwoti ɔ́ya na bíduo kalɔ kani na ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ ni, na bɛkɔ kusɛ kusɛ ɔmɛni lɛsa na Gerisim Kɔbi lɛlɔ. Na bɛkɔ ewida amɛni lɛsa na Ebal Kɔbi lɛlɔ. 30Bɛgyi ka abi anyɔ amɛni ede ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Gilgal na Araba Kɔwɛ kemmo na Yordan kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ ɔkya Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kesii kani baalɔ More na egyii enengudi enye mmɔ. 31Na ɔƒɛni ni, bɛdubo Yordan Ketu bɔvia na biteesie bitélie kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii lɛlɔ. Na si bísie bítélie mmɔ ni, 32bɛnu ka bɛɛdi ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui na líti muute-mii ɔmwi kadi mɛni lɛlɔ.

english_text:
Only One Place To Worship the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
1Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land. 2But the nations that live there worship other gods. So after you capture the land, you must completely destroy their places of worship—on mountains and hills or in the shade of large trees. 3 Wherever these nations worship their gods, you must tear down their altars, break their sacred stones, burn the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and smash their idols to pieces. Destroy these places of worship so completely that no one will remember they were ever there. 4Don't worship the Lord your God in the way those nations worship their gods.
5-19 Soon you will cross the Jordan, and the Lord will help you conquer your enemies and let you live in peace, there in the land he has given you. But after you are settled, life will be different. You must not offer sacrifices just anywhere you want to. Instead, the Lord will choose a place somewhere in Israel where you must go to worship him. All of your sacrifices and offerings must be taken there, including sacrifices to please the Lord and any gift you promise or voluntarily give him. That's where you must also take one tenth of your grain, wine, and olive oil, as well as the first-born of your cattle, sheep, and goats. You and your family and servants will eat your gifts and sacrifices and celebrate there at the place of worship, because the Lord your God has made you successful in everything you have done. And since Levites will not have any land of their own, you must ask some of them to come along and celebrate with you.
Sometimes you may want to kill an animal for food and not as a sacrifice. If the Lord has blessed you and given you enough cows or sheep or goats, then you can butcher one of them where you live. You can eat it just like the meat from a deer or gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat. But you must not eat the blood of any animal—let the blood drain out on the ground.
20-21The Lord has promised that later on he will give Israel more land, and some of you may not be able to travel all the way from your homes to the place of worship each time you are hungry for meat. But the Lord will give you cattle, sheep, and goats, and you can butcher any of those animals at home and eat as much as you want. 22It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
23-24 But don't eat the blood. It is the life of the animal, so let it drain out on the ground before you eat the meat. 25Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
26-27All sacrifices and offerings to the Lord must be taken to the place where he chooses to be worshiped. If you offer a sacrifice to please the Lord, all of its meat must be burned on the altar. You can eat the meat from certain kinds of sacrifices, but you must always pour out the animal's blood on the altar.
28If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful.
Worship the Lord in the Right Way
Moses said:
29Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.
30But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?” 31No, you should not! The Lord hates the disgusting way those nations worship their gods, because they even burn their sons and daughters as sacrifices.
32 Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
translation_text:
Katɔti Ɔdubɔtina-mii Kalɛ Na Ɔlɛka Bɛkpa-nwu
1Ɔni na bísela bitélie kalɔ kani na bina bati kuuku Unwoti Katɔti úti uute-mii mɛni lɛlɔ ni, ɔmɛni ndi ɔda bubo bɔni lɛlɔ na ɔlɛka bɛdi uwi ɔni na bilie-ka lɛlɔ mmɔ. Anwuɔsu bise atu na binu ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ kaduɛ! 2Na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela bitélie mmɔ ni, bɛnu ka bɛyila baƒiɔ biala udu bani na bekyuli baakpá na kesi kesii na abi ku abinkpo lɛlɔ ku egyii ani mbo ɔyuli mmɔ ƒui kalɔ kede kede. 3Bibo bana akpabi ƒui bɛbwɛ. Na bibo bana atabi ani baalɔ atabi kedee lɛnɔ bɛbwɛ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. Na bɛƒɛ bana lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ béte bana baƒiɔ beledi bani baalɔ Asera baƒiɔ. Na bibo bana baƒiɔ ƒui bɛkya ogya kemmo kalɛ na ukyuli ɔdi ulenyimo ka báakpa baƒiɔ badi na mmɔ kudii.
4Na ɔdi utakpa bina Unwoti Katɔti na ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na kadi bammɔ bekyuli baakpá bana baƒiɔ. 5Unwoti ɔlati ɔdubɔwia kesii kani námanku ute bina adua leevu-anyɔ ammɔ ƒui na bitaakpa-nwu. 6Na mmɔ na bɛdubuti bina akpala akyuladi ku akpala bamba ku bina etela ku bina akɛla lɛkpa leevudi ku etela ani bíse kenye ka bɛdubute Unwoti ku bina kaƒɔ ƒaa etela ku bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bese bebi bedeedi biboku na bɛkpa bite-nwu. 7Na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔni néte amii ku bina bebi kusɛ kusɛ ɔsu na bɛ́kɛ ala ani na bíti bina enu bɛ́bla mɛni ni, bitaadi ala ammɔ na nwuna anumi mmɔ ku kubiti ku lɛlɔyɔ.
8Na si uwi ɔmmɔ údu ni, utalɛka bɛbla ala ani na bɛɛbla mɛni. Na úti úbedu ɔƒɛni ni, bɛɛkpá-nwu kalɛ na amii ɔlati bɛɛyɔ́. 9Ɔsika bíteduo tɔ bɔnwuna kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ. 10Na si bɛ́via Yordan Ketu bɛ́wɔlɔ ni, bina Unwoti ɔdubuti kalɔ kammɔ ute-mii na bɛsɔ bilie mmɔ. Na ɔdubo bunye butile bina bekisine ulu na bɛdubulie mmɔ ku atu bɔyɔ. 11Na Unwoti ɔlati ɔdubudie kesii kadi use na bitaakpa-nwu. Na mmɔ na bɛdubuti bina akpala ani ƒui na úbo-mii ɔda biboku. Na akpala ammɔ ndi akpala akyuladi ku akpala bamba ku bina akɛla lɛkpa leevudi ku bina etela ku etela ani bíse kenye ka bɛdubute Unwoti.
12Na amii ku bina bebi ku bina kabla bablane banana ku beleku ku Lewiƒuɔ bɛdi limeyi na mmɔ na lɛlɔ litaayɔ-mii na Katɔti anumi. Na binyimo ka Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ beeebo kadikɔ kadi na mmɔ. 13Na biteti bina akpala akyuladi bitatákpa kesi kesii na bɛɛyɔ́. 14Mmomu biti-nya bisienku kesii kani na bina Unwoti ɔdubɔtina na bina adua leevu-anyɔ ammɔ kemmo. Na mmɔ kani na bɛdubuti bina akpala ku ala ani ƒui na úbo-mii ɔda biboku bibákpa.
15Nsu bibo kuƒi ka bɛdu bina bebuo na bɛkun bana lɛna na kesii biala na bilie aani kalɛ kani na bɛɛkun baƒɛ ku lɛku kemmo bakɔ ɔƒɛni. Bibo kuƒi ka bɛdi kalɛ na bɛkana aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti úte-mii. Ɔdi biala ubo kuƒi kɔmmɔ. Si ɔ́bla lɛlɔ kedee ɔdi iye útabla ni, ubo kuƒi ka ɔkun lɛna lɛmmɔ. 16Nsu ɔdi utadi bana ubugya. Na bɛya na bana ubugya ɔmmɔ uwi kalɔ aani kalɛ na beewilimi ntu teewi kalɔ kalɛ. 17Na ɔdi utadi lɛla lɛni na ɔdubuti ɔkpa ute Unwoti na kesii kani na ulie. Bitadi bina edula lɛkpa leevudi iye bina ntɛ bɔwɔdi iye bina nnɔ iye bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bese bebi bedeedi iye etela ani bíse kenye ka bɛdubuti bite Unwoti iye bina kaƒɔ ƒaa etela iye etela biala na bina kuliekɔ mmɔ. 18Bɛnu ka amii ku bina bebi ku bina kabla bablane banana ku beleku ku Lewiƒuɔ bani nlie bina lɛma ni, bɛ́di akpala ammɔ na Unwoti Katɔti anumi na kesii kani na ɔdubɔtina-mii. Na lɛlɔ litaayɔ-mii na ala ani bɛ́kɛ mmɔ ɔsu. 19Na ɔni bilie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ni, bɛnu ka bítenwini kama bítakya Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ.
20Si uwi ɔni na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na bina lɛmii lɛ́bɛbɛ lítédu kalɛ na ɔ́su úse na bɛnii bɛɛkun lɛna ka lɛɛda-mii ɔkwɛ ɔsu ni, bibo kuƒi ka bɛkun lɛna uwi biala bɛɛyɔ́. 21Na si bɛ́nu ka kesii kani na bilie kágyunku nwuna kakpakɔ kani na ɔ́tina-mii mmɔ ni, bibo kuƒi ka bɛdu bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ iye baƒonu ku bese bani na bina Unwoti úte-mii mmɔ badi bɛkun na bina kɔduli aani kalɛ kani na lɛ́su-mii ḿbavi. 22Na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́bla lɛlɔ kedee ɔdi iye útabla ni, ubo kuƒi ka ɔkun lɛna lɛmmɔ aani kalɛ kani na bɛɛkun baƒɛ ku lɛku kemmo bakɔ ɔƒɛni. 23-24Nsu bitadi bana ubugya. Ubugya ɔmmɔ ndi bana ngba. Anwuɔsu biwilimi ubugya ɔmmɔ ƒui biwiakun asa bɛkun lɛna lɛmmɔ. 25Na si bɛɛdi ɔda bubo bɔmɛni lɛlɔ ni, kaƒɔ kadubɔyɔ Unwoti na ɔdubɔya na amii ku bina bawɔ keyi kayɔ.
26Na biti bina etela ku akpala ani bɛ́su bíse ka bɛdubute Unwoti bisienku kesii kani na Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ. 27Na biti bina akpala ani na ese ete ka bɛkyula ku lɛna ku ubugya bisienku Unwoti lɛkpabi lɛni na ɔ́tina-mii lɛlɔ na bɛbla akpala ammɔ mmɔ. Bibo kuƒi ka bɛkun lɛna lɛmmɔ, nsu ubugya ɔmmɔ anwu ni, biwilimi biwi bina Unwoti Katɔti lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ɔƒɛnyi. 28Na si bɛɛdi ɔda bubo bɔni na bina Unwoti Katɔti úte-mi mɛni lɛlɔ ni, ɔmɛni ndubɔya na uteebunku amii ku bina bawɔ na lɛla biala na bɛɛbla lɛtɛ lite-mii.
Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Na Lɛƒiɔkpa Lɛlɔ
29-30Bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo bekyuli bani nlie lɛma lɛni bísela mmɔ udu bɔyila. Na si ɔ́yila-ma udu ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, na mmɔ unwini bina keliekɔ. Na ɔdi utasiaku bana lɛƒiɔkpa kama iye utawia utenu kalɛ na baakpá bana baƒiɔ taavinku kalɛ amii lɛnɔ bitaakpa bina Katɔti na ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na si bɛ́bla lɛni ni, ɔgbankpi ɔdubɔsiaku-mii. 31Na bitakpa bina Unwoti Katɔti na ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na baakpá bana baƒiɔ. Ɔsika ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na baakpá bana baƒiɔ ni, ɔdi lɛla lɛni muusé Katɔti lɛlɔ na uláwia ulanu. Ɔsika baakana na beeti bana bebi taakpa lɛgyavonku kemmo na bana akpabi lɛlɔ.
32Na bɛnu ka bɛ́bla lɛla biala na líbo-mii ɔda nnii bɛbla. Na bitada ɔdi bitedie iye biteti ɔdi bitebunku.

english_text:
Don't Worship Other Gods
Moses said to Israel:
1-2Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.” 3If the prophet says this, don't listen! The Lord your God will be watching to find out whether or not you love him with all your heart and soul. 4You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling, 5because he rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
If a prophet tells you to disobey the Lord your God and to stop worshiping him, then that prophet is evil and must be put to death.
6-10 Someone else may say to you, “Let's worship other gods.” That person may be your best friend, your brother or sister, your son or daughter, or your own dear wife or husband. But you must not listen to people who say such things. Instead, you must stone them to death. You must be the first to throw the stones, then others from the community will finish the job. Don't show any pity.
The gods worshiped by other nations have never done anything for you or your ancestors. People who ask you to worship other gods are trying to get you to stop worshiping the Lord, who rescued you from slavery in Egypt. So put to death anyone who asks you to worship another god. 11And when the rest of Israel hears about it, they will be afraid, and no one else will ever do such an evil thing again.
12After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns. 13You may hear that some worthless people have talked everyone there into worshiping other gods, even though these gods had never done anything for them. 14You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country, 15you must take your swords and kill every one of them, and their livestock too. 16-17Gather all the possessions of the people who lived there, and pile them up in the marketplace, without keeping anything for yourself. Set the pile and the whole town on fire, and don't ever rebuild the town. The whole town will be a sacrifice to the Lord your God. Then he won't be angry anymore, and he will have mercy on you and make your nation stronger, just as he promised your ancestors. 18That's why you must do what the Lord your God says is right. I am giving you his laws and teachings today, and you must obey them.
translation_text:
1Binye kagyumana bite kenye bediene badi iye bekyuli bani muudie ana ani bégye kalɔ. Ɔdi ɔdubo ubese kenye kadi ka ɔdubo akɔla lidu lidu budie bɔtina, 2nsu kasusu kani na ɔda ndi ka ɔtɔlɔ-mii kalɛ na bitákpa baƒiɔ bani bítakpa kudii. Ina ka kenye kani na úse mmɔ kébo kéte lɛni ni, 3bitenu-nwu litemi. Ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔɔsia-mii anu geen na ɔɔkɔ́ku-mii taanu si bɛɛyɔ́-nwu ku kayi ƒui. 4Bɛsiaku bina Unwoti lɛti pɛ kama na biti ɔbu bite-nwu. Na bɛdi nwuna etemila ku ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui na úte-mii lɛlɔ. Na bɛkpa-nwu na ulu ɔni na ɔɔwia lɛlɔ na bɛda-nwu kpakplaa. 5Bɛdu ukyuli biala ɔni ndi ɔkɔ kenye udiene iye ɔdi ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ teedie ana ani bégye kalɔ. Ɔsika bekyuli bammɔ udu beenwíni bekyuli kasusu teedie Katɔti lɛlɔ anwu ɔni nédie-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na kesii kani nka bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bɛɛbla kabla teete bekyuli bamba. Ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu ɔdi ukyuli ukpidi, na ɔɔyɔ́ ka ɔda-mii kasusu udie ngba bɔni na Unwoti ɔɔyɔ́ ka bilie lɛlɔ. Ɔlɛka bɛdu ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu kalɛ na bilasiaku nwuna udu ukpidi ɔmmɔ kama.
6Binye kagyumana bite bina ɔnwani iye bina ubidi ɔnanabi iye ulekubi iye bina beleku bani na bɛɛyɔ́ geen iye ƒula ɔkpana geen ɔni ndubo bɔbɛ bubasu-mii ka bibo na bitákpa baƒiɔ bani udu na amii iye bina bati kuuku bítakpa kudii. 7Na si bana akɔ ɔdi úbasu-mii ɔnii bibo na bitákpa baƒiɔ bani nkya lɛma lɛni nde-mii iye lɛma lɛni nkya ɔgyu kemmo ni, 8bitenu kalɔ na bitakpete ukyuli ɔmmɔ. Na bitanu ukyuli ɔmmɔ kɔnyana. Na nwuna lɛlɔ litakywi ɔdi kaƒɔ, na teti ukyuli ɔmmɔ tabɛla. 9Mmomu awɔ ni, bo ukyuli ɔmmɔ kudu kɔnakunwi, na ese kalɔ eteebo-nwu atabi asa na bekyuli bakladi bebebunku-ɔ. 10Bibo-nwu atabi bɛdu. Ɔsika ɔɔyɔ́ ka ɔtɔlɔ-mii na ɔda bina kasusu udie bina Unwoti Katɔti lɛlɔ anwu ɔni nédie-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipteƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani nka bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bɛkya bɛɛbla bekyuli bamba kabla. 11Na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na Israelƒuɔ ƒui benu lɛla lɛni nálɛ mɛni na liƒu lɛda ukyuli biala. Na ɔdi biala uleti lɛlɔ ulakya udu ukpidi ɔmmɔ kemmo kudii.
12Na si bínu bɛ́siku lɛma lɛni na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti uute-mii ka bitélie-ni kemmo mmɔ 13ka bekyuli bekpidi badi báta na bina akɔ na bátɔlɔ ama ɔlati ɔma bekyuli ka bitákpa baƒiɔ bani bítakpa kudii ni, bi na bɛdubo bɔbla? 14Si bínu etemila ammɔ bene udu ni, biwi lɛlɔ na bɛwia-nya kemmo bɛti kaduɛ. Na si bɛ́wia bɛ́ti ka sɔsɔ na etemila ammɔ adi ni, 15bɛdu bekyuli bani ƒui nlie ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na bɛdu bana bebuo ƒui lɛnɔ. Na bɛnu ka bɛ́yila ɔma ɔmmɔ udu ƒui. 16Na akɛla ani na ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli bebo ƒui ni, bɛla-nya ƒui bitéwi kuyeya na bɛkyula ala ammɔ ku ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui. Na ala akyuladi ammɔ ƒui adubunwini akpala ete bina Unwoti Katɔti. Na ɔma ɔmmɔ unwini ɔma ɔni na úbie na ɔsɔ uladia bɔsɔku bɔda kudii. 17Na ɔdi uteti ala ani na ɔ́su-mii ka bɛkyula mmɔ adi utese lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni ndubɔya na nwuna kɔnyi kati kati kɔyɔ na ɔnu-mii kɔnyana. Ɔdubɔnu-mii kɔnyana na ɔya na bimomo bibu aani kalɛ na ɔ́su bina bati kuuku úse. 18Ɔsika biinú bina Unwoti Katɔti litemi na bɛɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo bɔni na uute-mii ɔmwi mɛni lɛlɔ. Na bɛɛbla ala ani nse siin na nwuna anumi ɔsu.

english_text:
Don't Mourn like Other Nations
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, you are the Lord's children, so when you mourn for the dead, you must not cut yourselves or shave your forehead. 2 Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods.
Animals That Can Be Eaten
(Leviticus 11.1-47)
3 Don't eat any disgusting animals.
4-5You may eat the meat of cattle, sheep, and goats; wild sheep and goats; and gazelles, antelopes, and all kinds of deer. 6It is all right to eat meat from any animals that have divided hoofs and also chew the cud.
7But don't eat camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. These animals chew the cud but do not have divided hoofs. You must treat them as unclean. 8And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!
9You can eat any fish that has fins and scales. But there are other creatures that live in the water, 10and if they do not have fins and scales, you must not eat them. Treat them as unclean.
11You can eat any clean bird. 12-18But don't eat the meat of any of the following birds: eagles, vultures, falcons, kites, ravens, ostriches, owls, sea gulls, hawks, pelicans, ospreys, cormorants, storks, herons, and hoopoes. You must not eat bats. 19Swarming insects are unclean, so don't eat them. 20However, you are allowed to eat certain kinds of winged insects.
21 You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. You may give it to foreigners who live in your town or sell it to foreigners who are visiting your town.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Give the Lord Ten Percent of Your Harvest
Moses said:
22 People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest. 23Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.
24But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest, 25then sell this part and take the money there instead. 26When you and your family arrive, spend the money on food for a big celebration. Buy cattle, sheep, goats, wine, beer, and if there are any other kinds of food that you want, buy those too. 27And since people of the Levi tribe won't own any land for growing crops, remember to ask the Levites to celebrate with you.
28Every third year, instead of using the ten percent of your harvest for a big celebration, bring it into town and put it in a community storehouse. 29The Levites have no land of their own, so you must give them food from the storehouse. You must also give food to the poor who live in your town, including orphans, widows, and foreigners. If they have enough to eat, then the Lord your God will be pleased and make you successful in everything you do.
translation_text:
Bitabla Kekwa Aani Kalɛ Na Kadi Bamba Bekyuli Baabla
1Amii Israelƒuɔ bɛdi bekyuli bani na bina Unwoti Katɔti údie úte lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu si bɛɛbla ukpine ɔdi kekwa ni, ɔdi uteti lɛla lɛdi utekulo nwuna ɔlɔna kakɛ kadi, na ɔdi utekpeyi nwuna lɛtɛntɛ na ukpine ɔdi ɔsu aani kalɛ na kadi bamba bekyuli baabla. 2Ɔsika amii bɛdi Unwoti Katɔti ɔdi na anwu náƒuna-mii ɔ́lɛku kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ na kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui ka bɛbla nwuna ɔdi.
Mose Ɔ́tina-ma Bebuo Bani Udu Na Bakun
3Bitakun lɛna biala lɛni na Katɔti úbo-mii ɔda ka liisé-nwu lɛlɔ. 4Na bebuo bani na béte kuƒi ka bɛdu na bɛkun ndi bebuo bamɛni. 5-6Ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bete ku bese ku baƒɛ ku bana udu biala na lɛku kemmo bani muukpó taalɛku ɔkwɛ kemmo taakun na bana lɛgba agbanvuo kemmo kábwɛ inyɔ lɛnɔ bibo kuƒi ka bɛdu bebuo bammɔ bɛkun. 7Na bitakun ebuo ɔni neeekpo taalɛku ɔkwɛ kemmo taakun na uuubo agbanvuo ani kemmo nábwɛ inyɔ. Na bitakun bagbɛnɛgbɛnɛ bebuo bani na bana atu éne gyɔlɔɔ gyɔlɔɔ mmɔ ku bebuo ala betine benengudi ku keƒu bani nkya kalɔ kakwiidi mmɔ. Bebuo bamɛni beekpó taakun, nsu bana lɛgbanvuo kemmo lítabwɛ kemmo inyɔ. 8Na bitakun ɔplakuo. Ɔsika bebuo bamɛni beesé lɛlɔ. Bebo agbanvuo ani kemmo nábwɛ inyɔ, nsu belekpo taakun. Na ɔdi utakun bebuo bamɛni iye biteti bina enu bitetuku bana ukpine.
9Na lɛna biala na lɛkya ntukpa ku ɛpu kemmo na libo atula ku akpa ni, bibo kuƒi ka bɛkun-ni. 10Nsu lɛna biala na lɛkya ketu kemmo na liiibo akpa ku lɛƒɛnyi atula ni, bitakun. Ɔsika lɛna lɛmmɔ liisé lɛlɔ.
11Bɛkana na bɛkun aasɛ biala ɔni neeese lɛlɔ. 12-18Nsu baasɛ bani anyi ndubo bɔlɔ mɛni ni, bitakun-ma. Kɔdigbo aasɛ, likuku, okum ku nwuna lidu lidu, ɔsansa, kasangbii ku nwuna lidu soholi, lɛkpaƒɛɛlɛ, ligbini, kwakwadabi, ɛpu kemmo kwakwadabi, likuku ku nwuna lidu lidu, ntu kemmo kɔdigbo aasɛ, aasɛ ku limɔ gyɔlɔɔ ku nwuna lidu lidu, lɛpan ku baƒelelee.
19Na kubweyi pii kɔkya na kuuveyi na lisu kemmo ni, bitakun-ku, ɔsika beesé lɛlɔ. 20Na kɔni muuveyi na kulese lɛlɔ aku ni, bɛkana na bɛkun aku.
21Na bitakun ebuo biala na úkpi ɔtɛ. Mmomu bɛkana na biti ebuo ɔmmɔ bite baƒɔ bani nli-mii akɔ iye biti biye bite baƒɔ bani nási baaví. Ɔsika amii bɛdi bekyuli bani na Katɔti údie úse sɛsɛɛ úte lɛlɔ. Na biteti ese uni lɛnyi ntu biteƒulo nwuna ubi lɛna.
Ɔda Bubo Na Etela Lɛkpa Leevudi Lɛlɔ
22Lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa ni, ɔdi biala udie nwuna edula ani ƒui na ɔ́kɛ lɛkpa leevudi use sɛsɛɛ ute Katɔti. 23Na si bɛ́bla ɔmɛni bɛ́wɔlɔ ni, na bisie kesii kani bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ƒuna úse ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ. Na si bíduo mmɔ ni, ɔdi biala uti nwuna ala lɛkpa leevudi ani ndi edula ku ntɛ bɔwɔdi ku nnɔ bɔni na bídie ku bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bina baƒonu ku bese bebi bedeedi bani na báwɔ na bɛdu-ma na bɛkun lɛna lɛmmɔ ku ala akladi ammɔ na Katɔti anumi. Na si bɛ́bla lɛni ni, ala amɛni ndubɔya na bɛtɛya kalɛ na biteeti ɔbu teete bina Unwoti Katɔti uwi biala. 24Na si úte-mii kusɛ kusɛ na bɛ́kɛ ala pii na bilakana ala lɛkpa leevudi lɛmmɔ ƒui buti busienku mmɔ ka mmɔ kágyunku-mii ɔsu ni, 25na biti ala ammɔ biye na kesii kani na bilie na biti egulabi ammɔ bisienku liku linwi pɛ lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́ƒuna úse mmɔ. 26Na si bíduo mmɔ ni, biti egulabi ani bɛ́kɛ mmɔ biye lɛla biala na bɛɛyɔ́, aani ɔmantɛ bakɔ iye baƒonu iye ntɛ na amii ku bina kaduli bekyuli bɛni na bɛdi ala ammɔ na bina Unwoti Katɔti anumi mmɔ. 27Na bitedie Lewiƒuɔ bani nkya bina lɛma mmɔ atu. Mmomu bite-ma ala ammɔ adi. Ɔsika ama beeebo kadikɔ kadi na kese kete-ma.
28Na lɛkwa lɛtɛdi biala lɛlɔ ni, biti bina edula lɛkpa leevudi biboku na bɛkya-nya unwu kemmo bise bina lɛma. 29Na edula ammɔ adi Lewiƒuɔ ku baƒɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele bani nkya bina lɛma ɔdi. Na badubuteebo taabaƒɔ ala ani na baawia na badi bemo. Na si bɛɛbla ɔmɛni ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubuteete-mi kusɛ kusɛ na bina kabla biala kemmo.

english_text:
Loans
(Leviticus 25.1-7)
Moses said:
1-2Every seven years you must announce, “The Lord says loans do not need to be paid back.” Then if you have loaned money to another Israelite, you can no longer ask for payment. 3This law applies only to loans you have made to other Israelites. Foreigners will still have to pay back what you have loaned them.
4-6No one in Israel should ever be poor. The Lord your God is giving you this land, and he has promised to make you very successful, if you obey his laws and teachings that I'm giving you today. You will lend money to many nations, but you won't have to borrow. You will rule many nations, but they won't rule you.
7 After the Lord your God gives land to each of you, there may be poor Israelites in the town where you live. If there are, then don't be mean and selfish with your money. 8Instead, be kind and lend them what they need. 9Be careful! Don't say to yourself, “Soon it will be the seventh year, and then I won't be able to get my money back.” It would be horrible for you to think that way and to be so selfish that you refuse to help the poor. They are your relatives, and if you don't help them, they may ask the Lord to decide whether you have done wrong. And he will say that you are guilty. 10You should be happy to give the poor what they need, because then the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
11 There will always be some Israelites who are poor and needy. That's why I am commanding you to be generous with them.
Setting Slaves Free
(Exodus 21.1-11)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If any of you buy Israelites as slaves, you must set them free after six years. 13And don't just tell them they are free to leave— 14give them sheep and goats and a good supply of grain and wine. The more the Lord has given you, the more you should give them. 15I am commanding you to obey the Lord as a reminder that you were slaves in Egypt before he set you free. 16But one of your slaves may say, “I love you and your family, and I would be better off staying with you, so please don't make me leave.” 17Take the slave to the door of your house and push a sharp metal rod through one earlobe and into the door. Such slaves will belong to you for life, whether they are men or women.
18Don't complain when you have to set a slave free. After all, you got six years of service at half the cost of hiring someone to do the work.
First-Born Animals
(Leviticus 27.26,27; Numbers 18.15-18)
Moses said to Israel:
19 If the first-born animal of a cow or sheep or goat is a male, it must be given to the Lord. Don't put first-born cattle to work or cut wool from first-born sheep. 20Instead, each year you must take the first-born of these animals to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped. You and your family will sacrifice them to the Lord and then eat them as part of a sacred meal.
21But if the animal is lame or blind or has something else wrong with it, you must not sacrifice it to the Lord your God. 22You can butcher it where you live, and eat it just like the meat of a deer or gazelle that you kill while hunting. Even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some. 23 But you must never eat the blood of an animal—let it drain out on the ground.
translation_text:
Lɛkwa Maatɛdi Lɛlɔ Kalabla
1Na lɛkwa maatɛdi biala lɛlɔ ni, si Israelni ɔdi ɔda ɔkpanadi kayu ni, na uti kayu kani na ɔda-nwu mmɔ ɔkyiɛ-nwu na lɛkwa lɛmmɔ kemmo. 2Ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔlɛka bɛbla ala amɛni bɛsiaku. Ukyuli biala ɔni névo egulabi úte nwuna Israelnikpana ni, uti kayu kammɔ ɔkyiɛ-nwu. Na utenye ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ka ɔɔwia nwuna lɛla lɛni na ɔda-nwu mmɔ. Ɔsika Katɔti ɔlati nése uwi ɔni na bekulo kayu biala nkya úse. 3Nsu si ukyuli ɔni naaadi Israelni ɔda ɔdi kayu kadi ni, ubo kuƒi ka ɔƒɔ lɛla lɛni na ɔda-nwu mmɔ ɔsiku-nwu kudɔ. Nsu ƒula Israelni ɔkpana anwu ni, ti kayu kammɔ kyiɛ-nwu lɛkwa maatɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.
4Na bina akɔ ɔdi ulénwini ɔwabane. Ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ geen na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ bísela bitélie mmɔ. 5Si bɛɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo bɔni na úte-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ na bɛɛbla taasiaku lɛla biala na ɔ́su-mii lɛlɔ kaduɛ ni, kusɛ kusɛ ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔsiaku-mii. 6Katɔti ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ aani kalɛ kani na úse kenye úse. Na bɛdubuvo egulabi bite kadi kadi bekyuli, nsu amii ni, bilésie bana kudɔ biletévo egulabi adi. Na bɛdubɔdi kadi kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ, nsu ɔdi biala ulakana-mii lɛlɔ bɔdi.
7Na si bina Unwoti Katɔti úti kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela bitélie mmɔ úte-mii na bísie bilie-ka lɛlɔ na bina ɔnwa ɔdi ɔɔyaki lɛla lɛdi na lɛma lɛmmɔ ɔdi kemmo ni, bitabla-nwu lili ɔkplu. 8Mmomu ute-nwu kebunku kani na ɔɔwia ku kayi ƒaa. 9Na utasu ɔnii kayu butitaakyiɛ lɛkwa lɛdaku budu ɔsu, ulete ukyuli ɔmmɔ kebunku kani na ɔɔwia. Ɔdi utaya na kasusu kekpidi kammɔ udu keduo-nwu lili kemmo. Na si ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔ́bla nwuna ɔnwani ulikplu na útete-nwu kevonkɔ kani na ɔɔwia mmɔ na ukyuli ɔmmɔ úwulo na ɔ́kpali Katɔti ni, Katɔti ɔdubɔni ulikplune ɔmmɔ kɔtu geen. 10Na bɛnu ka biite lɛlɔ ala ku kayi ƒaa ɔni na kasusu kekpidi kadi keeebo-nwu kemmo. Na si bɛɛbla lɛni ni, Katɔti ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na lɛla biala bɛɛbla kemmo. 11Na bawabane badubɔkya bina akɔ uwi ndi uwi na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela bitélie mmɔ. Anwuɔsu muubo-mii ɔda nnii, biteebunku bawabane bammɔ ku bekyuli bani ƒui mɔɔyáki lɛla lɛdi.
Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Na Bekyuli Bani Mɔɔbla Bekyuli Bamba Kabla Lɛlɔ
12Si Israelni biala ɔdi ɔnana iye uleku úti lɛlɔ úye úte ɔdi na ɔ́bla-nwu kabla utédu lɛkwa lɛkundi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka banyonu ukyuli ɔmmɔ na lɛkwa maatɛdi kemmo na uteesie kesii kani na ɔ́si. 13Na si uwi údu ka bana ɔdi úsela ni, utalɛka ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́bla kabla úte mmɔ ɔnyonu-nwu na ɔtɔlɔ ku enukplu. 14Mmomu te-nwu lɛla lɛdi siku ala ani ƒui na Katɔti ɔ́ya na ákɛ ɔkɛnku kusɛ kusɛ ɔni na úte-ɔ ɔsu ku kaƒɔ ƒaa. Bite-ma baƒonu ku bese ku edula ani bɛ́ƒɛ ku ntɛ bɔni bídie bíse kalɛ na ɔ́manku. 15Na binyimo ka amii lɛnɔ bɛ́ɛbla bekyuli kabla na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ dii. Nsu bina Unwoti Katɔti úbada-mii údie lɛbibo lɛmmɔ kemmo na bɛ́kɛ bɔnwuna. Anwuɔsu na uubó-mii ɔda ɔmɛni.
16Nsu si lɛkwa maatɛdi lɛmmɔ lídu na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla ukyuli bamba kabla mmɔ ɔ́bla kasusu ka wasɔ wakya nwuna unwoti kudɔ ka ɔɔyɔ́-nwu ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-nwu ka ɔsɔ ɔkya ɔsu ni, kuƒi kɔtɛ. 17Na asa na wasɔ wakya ni, da ukyuli ɔmmɔ kɔtu tamana ƒula kayakun ɔpunu lɛlɔ na awia lɛla lɛdi eti aƒuaala-nwu kɔtu. Na si ábla ɔmɛni áwɔlɔ ni, na ukyuli ɔmmɔ únwini ukyuli ɔni ndubutaabla kabla teete-ɔ nwuna akwa ƒui. Lɛni kani na bɛdubɔbla beleku bani mɔɔyɔ́ ka basɔ bakya bana benwoti kudɔ lɛnɔ. 18Na si uwi údu ka bɛnyonu bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla mɛni ni, ɔdi utakyaku-ma unyeƒi ɔdi. Ɔsika akwa aku ani na bákya-mii kudɔ mmɔ kabla kani na bábla béte-mii ni, kétulo ama bani mɔɔƒɔ́ limeyi ndi limeyi lɛyuƒɔla kunyɔ. Na si bɛ́bla ɔmɛni ni, Katɔti ɔdubuteete-mii kusɛ kusɛ na lɛla biala bɛɛbla kemmo.
Bebuo Bedeedi Bani Na Báwɔ Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ
19Na bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bese ubi ɔgyani udeedi biala ni, bidie-nwu bise sɛsɛɛ bite Katɔti. Na biteti bakɔ bitesienku na batábla kabla kadi iye bikulo baƒonu bammɔ linwini bɛbla unwo uwi ɔdi. 20Mmomu lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa ni, amii ku bina kaduli bekyuli biti bebuo bammɔ bisienku liku linwi pɛ lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́su-mii ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ. Na bitádu-ma bɛkpa bite-nwu na bɛkun-ma na Katɔti anumi mmɔ. 21Nsu si ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔdi ɔ́ƒɛ uwi kalɔ iye anumi abwɛ-nwu ni, iye lɛla bamba lɛdi lɛda-nwu ni, biteti ebuo ɔmmɔ udu bitakpa bitete bina Unwoti Katɔti. 22Na bibo kuƒi ka bɛdu ebuo ɔmmɔ udu bɛkun na bina kɔduli. Na si ukyuli ɔdi úkisi lɛlɔ iye útekisi lɛlɔ ni, ubo kuƒi ka ɔkun lɛna lɛmmɔ aani kalɛ kani na bɛɛkun bete ku baƒɛ. 23Nsu biteti bana ubugya bitabla adila na bɛdi. Mmomu biwilimi bana ubugya biwi kalɔ aani kalɛ na beebó ntu teewiakun.

english_text:
Passover
(Exodus 12.1-20; Leviticus 23.4-8)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, you must celebrate Passover in the month of Abib, because one night in that month years ago, the Lord your God rescued you from Egypt. 2The Passover sacrifice must be a cow, a sheep, or a goat, and you must offer it at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. 3-4Eat all of the meat of the Passover sacrifice that same night. But don't serve bread made with yeast at the Passover meal. Serve the same kind of thin bread that you ate when you were slaves suffering in Egypt and when you had to leave Egypt quickly. As long as you live, this thin bread will remind you of the day you left Egypt.
For seven days following Passover, don't make any bread with yeast. In fact, there should be no yeast anywhere in Israel.
5Don't offer the Passover sacrifice in just any town where you happen to live. 6It must be offered at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Kill the sacrifice at sunset, the time of day when you left Egypt. 7Then cook it and eat it there at the place of worship, returning to your tents the next morning.
8Eat thin bread for the next six days. Then on the seventh day, don't do any work. Instead, come together and worship the Lord.
The Harvest Festival
(Exodus 34.22; Leviticus 23.15-21)
Moses said to Israel:
9 Seven weeks after you start your grain harvest, 10-11go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped and celebrate the Harvest Festival in honor of the Lord your God. Bring him an offering as large as you can afford, depending on how big a harvest he has given you. Be sure to take along your sons and daughters and all your servants. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. 12Remember that you used to be slaves in Egypt, so obey these laws.
The Festival of Shelters
(Leviticus 23.33-43; Numbers 29.12-38)
Moses said to Israel:
13-15 After you have finished the grain harvest and the grape harvest, take your sons and daughters and all your servants to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
The Lord will give you big harvests and make you successful in everything you do. You will be completely happy, so celebrate this festival in honor of the Lord your God.
Three Festivals at the Place of Worship
(Exodus 23.14-17)
Moses said:
16Each year there are three festivals when all Israelite men must go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. These are the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters. And don't forget to take along a gift for the Lord. 17The bigger the harvest the Lord gives you, the bigger your gift should be.
Treat Everyone with Justice
Moses said to Israel:
18-19 After you are settled in the towns that you will receive from the Lord your God, the people in each town must appoint judges and other officers. Those of you that become judges must be completely fair when you make legal decisions, even if someone important is involved. Don't take bribes to give unfair decisions. Bribes keep people who are wise from seeing the truth and turn honest people into liars.
20People of Israel, if you want to enjoy a long and successful life, make sure that everyone is treated with justice in the land the Lord is giving you.
Don't Set Up Sacred Poles or Stones
Moses said to Israel:
21 When you build the altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God, don't set up a sacred pole for the worship of the goddess Asherah. 22 And don't set up a sacred stone! The Lord hates these things.
translation_text:
Úbo-ma Ɔda Na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi Bɔdi Lɛlɔ
1Bise kɔbuli kɔni baalɔ Abib likpo na bataadi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi teete bina Unwoti Katɔti. Ɔsika Abib kɔbuli kɔmmɔ kemmo na ɔ́da-mii údie Egyipteƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ usien unwi. 2Na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi bɔdi bɔmmɔ ni, bɛdu bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bese na biti-ma bɛkpa bite bina Unwoti na kesii kani na ɔdubudie use ute lɛlɔ mmɔ. 3Na si bɛɛdi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia adila ammɔ ni, biteti bɔnyi bɔni mɔɔyá na ɔlaaƒɔ uuƒu bitasala bodobodo ɔmmɔ kemmo. Biti emeyi maatɛ bɛdi bodobodo ɔni neeeƒu aani kalɛ kani na bɛ́bla limeyi lɛni na bɛ́babla na bɛ́tɔlɔ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na si bɛɛdi bodobodo ɔmmɔ udu ni, bɛsia-nwu lɛnyi bɛnii Lɛbibo Adila Bɔdi kalɛ na biteenyimo na bina ngba bulie ƒui kemmo abi ani na bíbo uwi ɔni bɛ́kya Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. 4Na emeyi maatɛ kemmo ɔdi biala uteti bɔnyi bɔni mɔɔyá na ɔlaaƒɔ uuƒu utese nwuna kaduli. Na ebuo ɔni na bɛ́du na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi lideedi useyi uwi ni, na bɛkun lɛna lɛmmɔ useyi ɔmmɔ kani. Bitebu ɔdi bitese lɛlɔ.
5-6Bebuo bani nse nte ka beti-ma bakpa bete Katɔti na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bɛnu ka bɛ́du bebuo bammɔ ƒui na kesii kani na Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ kani, na ɔɔɔdi lɛma lɛni na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii. Bɛdu bebuo bammɔ na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi bɔdi useyi ɔmmɔ biti bɛtina uwi ɔni kemmo na bíti bɛɛlɛ́ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. 7Na biƒulo lɛna lɛmmɔ ƒui na kesii kani na Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ. Na bɛkun-ni ƒui na mmɔ. Na bɛtɔlɔ nwuna lɛdigye bisie kɔduli. 8Na emeyi aku ani nébu ni, bitaadi bodobodo ɔni néteƒu kani. Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, bɛsala lɛlɔ na bimwi bina Unwoti Katɔti, na ɔdi utabla kabla kadi limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.
Úbo-ma Ɔda Na Edula Ebi Bɔƒɛ Limeyi Bɔdi Lɛlɔ
9-10Na kwasida maatɛdi lɛlɔ ɔ́si uwi ɔni na bíse kalɔ ku bina edula bɔƒɛ ni, bisie kesii kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ na bitádi Edula Bɔƒɛ Limeyi. Na si bísela ni, biti edula ammɔ adi bɛda aani kalɛ na Katɔti úte-mii kusɛ kusɛ kenye, na biti bɛtina ka bɛɛbu-nwu. 11Na si bísela ni, biti bina bebi ku bina kabla bablane banana ku beleku ku baƒɔ bani nkya-mii akɔ ku Lewiƒuɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele bani nkya bina lɛma kemmo ƒui bɛda. Na biti kubiti bɛdi limeyi lɛmmɔ na Katɔti anumi. 12Na bɛnu ka bɛ́di ɔda bubo bɔmɛni lɛlɔ. Na bitayiƒala ka Egyipteƒuɔ bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bítaabla-ma kabla dii.
Úbo-ma Ɔda Na Edula Bɔƒɛ Ku Kevo Kemmo Bulie Limeyi Bɔdi Lɛlɔ
13Si bɛ́ƒɛ bina edula na bíti bina adingyii ebi bɛ́bla ntɛ bɛ́wɔlɔ ni, na bɛdi Kevo Kemmo Bulie Emeyi. Biti emeyi maatɛ bɛdi limeyi lɛmmɔ. 14Na si bísela bitádi limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, biti bina bebi ku bani mɔɔbla-mii kabla ku Lewiƒuɔ ku baƒɔ bani nkya-mii kudɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele bani ƒui nkya bina lɛma kemmo bɛda na bitádi limeyi lɛmmɔ ku kubiti. 15Na bɛya na lɛlɔyɔ lɛƒɔ limeyi lɛmmɔ kaduɛ, ɔsika Unwoti néte-mii kusɛ kusɛ na ɔ́ya na bina enu kemmo kabla kammɔ kádia. Na bɛbla ɔmɛni na emeyi maatɛ kemmo na kesii kani na bina Unwoti ɔ́su ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ.
16Na lɛkwa biala kemmo ni, Israelƒuɔ ƒui banana ɔlɛka bebo Unwoti anumi kɔtɛ babakpa-nwu na kesii kani na ɔ́su úse ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ. Na emeyi ani badubɔdi mmɔ ndi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi ku Edula Bɔƒɛ Limeyi ku Kevo Kemmo Bulie Emeyi. Na ukyuli ɔdi utebo Katɔti anumi mmɔ ku enukplu. 17Na si ɔnana biala ɔdubo ni, uti etela uboku bina Unwoti Katɔti aani kalɛ na úte-mii kusɛ kusɛ na ɔ́kɛ edula ammɔ kenye. Na ukyuli ɔdi utebo Katɔti anumi mmɔ ku enukplu.
Israelƒuɔ Bédie Litemi Batɛne
18Bidie litemi batɛne ku bakutine na ɔma biala kemmo. Na bekyuli bamɛni banu ka baatɛ bekyuli etemila na ulu lɛlɔ. 19Na beteƒu litemi geen lɛmmɔ batakya na batanu bekyuli anumi lɛnɔ. Na bataƒɔ egulabi na bɔbɛ kemmo, ɔsika etela ammɔ udu aabwɛ banundane ku bekyuli bani lɛlɔ mbo ɔbu anumi, na balátɛ litemi siin. 20Na bɛnu ka litemi lɛlɔ bɔdi ulu lɛlɔ bɔ́ƒɔ bina ƒui akɔ. Na si bɛbla lɛni ni, anwu ndubɔya na bilie kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti uute-mii lɛlɔ.
Úbo-ma Ɔda Na Lɛƒiɔkpa Lɛlɔ
21Si bɛɛtú lɛkpabi lɛdi bite bina Unwoti Katɔti ni, biteti baƒiɔ beledi bani baalɔ banii Asera ɔƒiɔgyii bitalɛ Katɔti lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ. 22Na biteti lɛtabi lɛdi bitabla baƒiɔ na bitaakpa-ni. Ɔsika Katɔti ukisi ala ammɔ bene.

english_text:
Sacrifices That Have Something Wrong with Them
Moses said to Israel:
1If an ox or a sheep has something wrong with it, don't offer it as a sacrifice to the Lord your God—he will be disgusted!
Put To Death People Who Worship Idols
Moses said to Israel:
2-3 The Lord your God is giving you towns to live in. But later, a man or a woman in your town may start worshiping other gods, or even the sun, moon, or stars. I have warned you not to worship other gods, because whoever worships them is disobeying the Lord and breaking the agreement he made with you. 4So when you hear that someone in your town is committing this disgusting sin, you must carefully find out if that person really is guilty. 5-7 But you will need two or three witnesses—one witness isn't enough to prove a person guilty.
Get rid of those who are guilty of such evil. Take them outside your town gates and everyone must stone them to death. But the witnesses must be the first to throw stones.
Difficult Cases
Moses said to Israel:
8-12It may be difficult to find out the truth in some legal cases in your town. You may not be able to decide if someone was killed accidentally or murdered. Or you may not be able to tell whether an injury or some property damage was done by accident or on purpose. If the case is too difficult, take it to the court at the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped.
This court will be made up of one judge and several priests who serve at the Lord's altar. They will explain the law to you and give you their decision about the case. Do exactly what they tell you, or you will be put to death. 13When other Israelites hear about it, they will be afraid and obey the decisions of the court.
The King
Moses said:
14 People of Israel, after you capture the land the Lord your God is giving you, and after you settle on it, you will say, “We want a king, just like the nations around us.”
15Go ahead and appoint a king, but make sure that he is an Israelite and that he is the one the Lord has chosen.
16 The king should not have many horses, especially those from Egypt. The Lord has said never to go back there again. 17 And the king must not have a lot of wives—they might tempt him to be unfaithful to the Lord. Finally, the king must not try to get huge amounts of silver and gold.
18The official copy of God's laws will be kept by the priests of the Levi tribe. So, as soon as anyone becomes king, he must go to the priests and write out a copy of these laws while they watch. 19Each day the king must read and obey these laws, so that he will learn to worship the Lord with fear and trembling 20and not think that he's better than everyone else.
If the king completely obeys the Lord's commands, he and his descendants will rule Israel for many years.
translation_text:
1Biteti ɔmantɛ bakɔ iye koƒonu kɔni na kɔ́sɔ bitakpa bitete bina Unwoti Katɔti. Ɔsika Katɔti ukisi ala ammɔ bene.
2Na si úbo úte ka bina akɔ ɔdi únu ka ɔnana iye uleku ɔdi ɔda ɔvia Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔni na úte-mii lɛlɔ iye ɔ́bla likpidi lɛdi na útadi lɛla lɛni na Katɔti únyimiku-mii lɛlɔ 3na úsie utákpa baƒiɔ badi iye kɔbuli iye ɔƒɛ iye ayabi uwi ɔni na Katɔti ɔ́su ka ɔdi utabla lɛni kudii ni, 4na bínu litemi lɛmmɔ ni, biwi lɛlɔ na bɛwia-ni kemmo kaduɛ. Na si bɛ́wia-ni kemmo na litemi lɛmmɔ lɛdi sɔsɔ ka ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔ́bla likyulikpi lɛla lɛmmɔ udu na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, 5na biti ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu bɛlɛku bisienku bina ɔma kabanye na bibo-nwu atabi bɛdu. 6Nsu asa na bɛdububo-nwu atabi ni, bɛya na nkyuli inyɔ iye ɛtɛ bebenye litemi lɛmmɔ kama ka sɔsɔ na ɔdi. Nsu si ukyuli unwi kani nnye litemi lɛmmɔ kama ni, na bitebo ukyuli ɔmmɔ atabi. 7Na asa na bɛdububo ukyuli ɔmmɔ atabi ni, bɛya na bekyuli bani nnye litemi lɛmmɔ kama baka-nwu atabi bubo asa na bekyuli bakladi beteebo-nwu atabi. Ɔmɛni ndi kalɛ na bɛda likpidi lɛmɛni udu bidie bina akɔ.
8Bɛya na buti-nwu bɔnii etemila adi akya na étulo-mii bɔtɛ aani ukyuli bɔdu na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ litemi iye ukyuli bubo bɔkya ɔlɛ litemi ku etemila bɔni teenene na litemi katɛkɔ. Na si etemila amɛni udu álɛ ni, bisie kesii kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́tina-mii ka bitaakpa-nwu mmɔ. 9Na biti etemila ammɔ bite Katɔti bakpane bani ndi Lewiƒuɔ ku litemi ɔtɛne ɔni nkya mmɔ na beduo etemila ammɔ kemmo na batɛ litemi lɛmmɔ bete-mii. 10Na si kalɛ biala bátɛ litemi lɛmmɔ bávinku ni, na binu kalɔ. 11Bɛƒɔ bana litemi lɛmmɔ ku kalɛ biala bébo-mii ɔda bávinku. 12Na ukyuli biala na ɔnii ulénu litemi ɔtɛne iye Katɔti ɔkpane litemi lɛni bátɛ mmɔ kalɔ ni, na bebo-nwu badu. Na bitaada bekyuli likpidi lɛmɛni udu teedie bina akɔ. 13Na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na ukyuli biala unu lɛla lɛni nálɛ mɛni, na ɔya na ukyuli biala ɔyia na basɔ balata belenye litemi ɔtɛne litemi lɛlɔ.
Úbo-ma Ɔda Na Lɛga Bɔdi Lɛlɔ
14Si bísie na bitélie kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔmmɔ kama bíti kasusu na bɛ́nu ka bɛɛwia ɔga ɔdi na utaadi Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na kɔlɔ bamba bebo bagadine ni, 15na bɛnu kaduɛ na bidie ɔga ɔni na Unwoti lɛnɔ ɔ́ƒuna. Ɔlɛka ɔbla ukyuli ɔni nási bina kadi bekyuli akɔ. Na biteti kadi bamba ukyuli ɔni naaadi Israelni ɔdi bitese lɛga. 16Na ɔga ɔni na bɛdubuse ni, utalɛka ɔwia bapɔnkɔ pii ute lɛlɔ. Na utalɛka ukyuli ɔdi use Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ utéye bapɔnkɔ badi ɔ́siku mmɔ uboku-nwu. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́su-mii ka ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ utesie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ lɛnɔ. 17Na ɔga ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ utawia beleku pii uteti, ɔsika si ɔ́bla lɛni ni, nwuna kasusu kadubɔlɛ nwuna Unwoti lɛlɔ. Na ɔga ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ utawia sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi pii utese lɛlɔ.
18Na si ɔga ɔmmɔ úbo úbelie nwuna liboku lɛlɔ ni, ɔƒɔ Ɔda Bubo Ɔku Kedee ɔmmɔ na Katɔti bakpane bani ndi Lewiƒuɔ kudɔ na anwu lɛnɔ unweni etemila ammɔ ɔkya ɔku kemmo ute lɛlɔ. 19Na uti ɔku ɔmmɔ na utaaka-nwu teenu Katɔti ɔda bubo etemila teeti taada nwuna ngba emeyi ƒui. Mmɔ na ɔdubuteeti ɔbu teete Katɔti na ɔkana na uteemwi-nwu na ulu lɛlɔ. Na utaadi nwuna ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. 20Na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na ulátaakɔliku lɛlɔ katɔ teetulo nwuna banwa Israelƒuɔ bakladi. Na ɔdububunku-nwu lɛnɔ na ulénwini kama ulakya Katɔti ɔda bubo. Na si ɔ́bla lɛni ni, ɔdubɔya na anwu ku nwuna kaba bekyuli belie liboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ badi lɛga na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ bétu uwi.

english_text:
Special Privileges for Priests and Levites
(Numbers 18.8-32)
Moses said to Israel:
1The people of the Levi tribe, including the priests, will not receive any land. Instead, they will receive part of the sacrifices that are offered to the Lord, 2 because he has promised to provide for them in this way.
3When you sacrifice a bull or sheep, the priests will be given the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach. 4In addition, they will receive the first part of your grain harvest and part of your first batches of wine and olive oil. You must also give them the first wool that is cut from your sheep each year. 5Give these gifts to the priests, because the Lord has chosen them and their descendants out of all the tribes of Israel to be his special servants at the place of worship.
6Any Levite can leave his hometown, and go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, 7and then be a special servant of the Lord there, just like all the other Levites. 8Some Levites may have money from selling family possessions, and others may not. But all Levites serving at the place of worship will receive the same amount of food from the sacrifices and gifts brought by the people.
Don't Do Disgusting Things
Moses said to Israel:
9Soon you will go into the land that the Lord your God is giving you. The nations that live there do things that are disgusting to the Lord, and you must not follow their example. 10-11 Don't sacrifice your son or daughter. And don't try to use any kind of magic or witchcraft to tell fortunes or to cast spells or to talk with spirits of the dead.
12The Lord is disgusted with anyone who does these things, and that's why he will help you destroy the nations that are in the land. 13 Never be guilty of doing any of these disgusting things!
A Prophet like Moses
Moses said to Israel:
14You will go in and take the land from nations that practice magic and witchcraft. But the Lord your God won't allow you to do those things. 15 Instead, he will choose one of your own people to be a prophet just like me, and you must do what that prophet says. 16You were asking for a prophet the day you were gathered at Mount Sinai and said to the Lord, “Please don't let us hear your voice or see this terrible fire again—if we do, we will die!”
17Then the Lord told me:
Moses, they have said the right thing. 18So when I want to speak to them, I will choose one of them to be a prophet like you. I will give my message to that prophet, who will tell the people exactly what I have said. 19 Since the message comes from me, anyone who doesn't obey the message will have to answer to me.
20But if I haven't spoken, and a prophet claims to have a message from me, you must kill that prophet, and you must also kill any prophet who claims to have a message from another god.
Moses said to Israel:
21You may be asking yourselves, “How can we tell if a prophet's message really comes from the Lord?” 22You will know, because if the Lord says something will happen, it will happen. And if it doesn't, you will know that the prophet was falsely claiming to speak for the Lord. Don't be afraid of any prophet whose message doesn't come from the Lord.
translation_text:
Katɔti Ndi Nwuna Bakpane Kadikɔ
1Katɔti bakpane bani ndi Lewiƒuɔ beeebo kadikɔ kadi na Israelƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ. Mmomu bana kadikɔ ndi etela ku akpala ani na bekyuli beeboku-ma ka bakyula bete Unwoti. 2Na Lewiƒuɔ bamɛni beeebo kuƒi ka bakɛ kalɔ kadi bete lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na adua bakladi bekyuli bebo kalɛ. Bana kɔsia kani ndi ka badi bakpane bete Unwoti aani kalɛ na anwu Unwoti úse kenye úse.
3Na uwi biala na Israelƒuɔ badubɔdu ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu beti bakpa bete Unwoti ni, bedie bebuo bammɔ enu ku ɔnungla ku bana kaƒɔ ala bete Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ. 4Ɔƒɛni ni, bina edula edeedi ani na bɛ́ƒɛ ku ntɛ ku nnɔ ku bina baƒonu linwini lɛni na bíti bɛ́bla unwo ni, biti ala ammɔ bite Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ. 5Ɔsika na bina adua kemmo ni, Unwoti nédie kɔdua kunwi na ama ndi Lewiƒuɔ bamɛni ka benwini bakpane bete-nwu uwi ƒui.
6Na Lewini biala ɔni nlie Israel ɔma biala kemmo na ɔ́bla kasusu ka use utélie kesii kani na Unwoti ɔ́su úse ka bataakpa-nwu mmɔ, ubo kuƒi ka utélie mmɔ. 7Na ɔkana na utaabla nwuna ɔkpane kabla na Katɔti anumi mmɔ aani Lewiƒuɔ bakladi bani nlie mmɔ kalɛ. 8Na ɔlɛka bete-nwu adila aani kalɛ na beete bakpane bani nlie mmɔ adila ina ka nwuna kaduli bekyuli béte-nwu egulabi adi.
Bitasiaku Bayawine Ala Kama
9Si bísie bítéduo kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii mmɔ kemmo ni, ɔdi utasiaku kadi bamba bekyuli bani nde-mii mmɔ ala ani muusé Katɔti lɛlɔ mmɔ kama. 10Na ɔdi uteti ubidi utatákya ogya kemmo ɔnii uuti-nwu ɔkpa. Na bitatɛya kalɛ na beesié teetéye ala teenu. Iye utenwini ukyuli ɔni muubó like iye unwini kabɔ ɔdune iye 11bekyuli bani mɔɔwia ala bati na ayu bamba kudɔ iye bitesie bekpine kudɔ ka bitéye-ma ala binu. 12Na ukyuli biala na meti lɛlɔ mete ala amɛni udu bɔbla ni, ɔdubuse Katɔti lɛlɔ, ɔsika ala ammɔ udu adi ekisila ete bina Unwoti Katɔti. Na ɔmɛni ɔsu na ɔdubɔku kadi bammɔ bekyuli na bina anumi. 13Na bɛnu kaduɛ kalɛ na lɛla lɛdi lilada-mii na bina Unwoti anumi.
Katɔti Úse Kenye Ka Weti Kenye Udiene Ɔdi Wemene
14Na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela bitélie ni, bekyuli basiaku bekyuli bani muubó like kama na baawia ama bani ndubɔsu-ma ala ani ndubo bɔlɛ. Nsu ami amu ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ulayɔ ka bɛbla lɛni. 15Mmomu ɔdubuti kenye udiene ɔdi umene aani ami Mose kalɛ. Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔsi bina kadi bekyuli akɔ. Na si úbo ni, na ɔdi biala unu-nwu litemi.
16Limeyi lɛni na amii Israelƒuɔ bɛ́sa na Sinai kɔbi kaƒɔna ni, bívele-mi bɛnii bɛsɔ bilayɔ ka bɛsɔ binu bina Unwoti lɛdi iye bɛnu kalɛ na ogya bonwu ɔmmɔ ɔɔda lɛnɔ. Ɔsika bɛkya bɛyia ka bɛdubukpi. 17Ɔmɛni ɔsu Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Béti lɛnunda béye lɛla lɛbuni. 18Anwuɔsu Ami Katɔti ndubumene kenye udiene ɔdi aani awɔ Mose kalɛ lɛkya-ma. Na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔsi ama alati kadi bekyuli akɔ. Na lɛla biala na líbo-nwu ɔda ni, anwu ndubɔsu-ma ana ƒui. 19Na si ubo ni, lɛla biala wasu-ma ni, ɔdubɔsu-ni na mina lɛnyi kemmo. Na ukyuli biala na ulénu-nwu litemi ni, Ami Katɔti ndubɔni-nwu kɔtu. 20Nsu si kenye udiene ɔdi ɔ́su-ma litemi lɛdi na mina lɛnyi kemmo uwi ɔni na ɔɔɔdi Ami Katɔti nátala-nwu iye kenye udiene ɔdi ɔda baƒiɔ kɔyu ɔɔsu-ma lɛla lɛdi ni, na bayila bekyuli bammɔ udu.”
21Bɛdubuye lɛlɔ bɛnii, “Dɛ na wabla asa bɔnu bɔti ka kenye udiene ɔmɛni litemi lɛni na ɔɔsu mɛni lítasi Unwoti kudɔ?” 22Binu kalɛ na bɛdubuti bɛnu ka litemi lɛmmɔ lɛ́si iye lítasi Katɔti kudɔ. Si kenye udiene ɔdi úti Katɔti lɛnyi na ɔ́su lɛla lɛdi na lɛla lɛmmɔ lítebo-nwu kemmo ni, na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ kenye kátasi Katɔti kudɔ. Mmomu kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔlati néti nwuna kasusu ɔ́su lɛla lɛmmɔ. Anwuɔsu bitayia ukyuli ɔmmɔ.

english_text:
Safe Towns
(Numbers 35.9-28; Joshua 20.1-9)
Moses said to Israel:
1 Soon you will go into the land and attack the nations. The Lord your God will destroy them and give you their lands, towns, and homes. Then after you are settled, 2-4you must choose three of your towns to be Safe Towns. Divide the land into three regions with one Safe Town near the middle of each, so that a Safe Town can be easily reached from anywhere in your land.
Then, if one of you accidentally kills someone, you can run to a Safe Town and find protection from being put to death. But you must not have been angry with the person you killed.
5For example, suppose you and a friend go into the forest to cut wood. You are chopping down a tree with an ax, when the ax head slips off the handle, hits your friend, and kills him. You can run to one of the Safe Towns and save your life. 6You don't deserve to die, since you did not mean to harm your friend. But he did get killed, and his relatives might be very angry. They might even choose one of the men from their family to track you down and kill you. If it is too far to one of the Safe Towns, the victim's relative might be able to catch you and kill you. 7That's why I said there must be three Safe Towns.
8-9Israel, the Lord your God has promised that if you obey his laws and teachings I'm giving you, and if you always love him, then he will give you the land he promised your ancestors. When that happens, you must name three more Safe Towns in the new territory. 10You will need them, so innocent people won't be killed on your land while they are trying to reach a Safe Town that is too far away. You will be guilty of murder, if innocent people lose their lives because you didn't name enough Safe Towns in the land the Lord your God will give you.
11But what if you really do commit murder? Suppose one of you hates a neighbor. So you wait in a deserted place, kill the neighbor, and run to a Safe Town. 12If that happens, the leaders of your town must send messengers to bring you back from the Safe Town. They will hand you over to one of the victim's relatives, who will put you to death.
13Israel, for the good of the whole country, you must kill anyone who murders an innocent person. Never show mercy to a murderer!
Property Lines
Moses said to Israel:
14 In the land the Lord is giving you, there are already stones set up to mark the property lines between fields. So don't move those stones.
Witnesses Must Tell the Truth
Moses said to Israel:
15 Before you are convicted of a crime, at least two witnesses must be able to testify that you did it.
16If you accuse someone of a crime, but seem to be lying, 17-18then both you and the accused must be taken to the court at the place where the Lord is worshiped. There the priests and judges will find out if you are lying or telling the truth.
If you are lying and the accused is innocent, 19-21 then you will be punished without mercy. You will receive the same punishment the accused would have received if found guilty, whether it means losing an eye, a tooth, a hand, a foot, or even your life.
Israel, the crime of telling lies in court must be punished. And when people hear what happens to witnesses that lie, everyone else who testifies in court will tell the truth.
translation_text:
Bidie Lɛma Ɛtɛ Bise Bite Kabɛkɔ
1Si uwi ɔni na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́yila bekyuli bani nli kɔlɔ kɔni bɛdubo bulie mmɔ udu ɔ́wɔlɔ na bɛ́bɔku-ma na bɛ́ƒɔ-ma lɛma ku kɔduli bilie ni, 2bɛlɛ lɛma ɛtɛ anumi na ekpo ekpo bise bite lɛlɔ na kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti ɔ́su úse ka weti wete-mii mmɔ kemmo. 3Na bile kalɔ kammɔ akpa atɛ bɛmana lɛma lɛmmɔ na bɛbwɛ lilu bisienku-ni kemmo. Na lɛma lɛmmɔ linwini kesii kani na ukyuli ɔdune ɔdi ɔkana na ukeli usie utábɛ.
4Na ukyuli ɔdune biala ɔkana na ukeli usie lɛma lɛmmɔ ɔdi kemmo kalɛ na baládu-nwu, ɔsika ɔɔɔgyi uuuse asa na ɔ́du nwuna ɔkpana ɔni naaadi nwuna ukisine. 5Bɛya na buti-nwu bɔnii nkyuli inyɔ bésie lɛku kemmo na bésie baadá egyii. Na ka bakya baadá egyii ammɔ ni, ukyuli unwi kadadi ubi ɔ́lɛ ugyii ɔmmɔ kemmo na ɔ́vi útádu ɔkpanadi. Ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔkana na ukeli usie lɛma lɛmmɔ unwi kemmo kalɛ na baládu-nwu. 6Na si ɔma unwi pɛ kani nkya na ɔgbankpi ɔ́siaku ɔdi na kesii kani nágyu ni, bekyuli bakana beƒie ukyuli ɔni na ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ ɔ́siaku na badu-nwu na kɔnyi kɔni bákɛ ɔsu. Nsu ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔɔɔgyi uuuse asa na ɔ́du ukyuli ɔni naaadi nwuna ukisine mmɔ. 7Ɔmɛni ɔsu na líbo-mii ɔda ka bidie lɛma ɛtɛ bise lɛlɔ.
8Ɔƒɛni si bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na kalɔ kammɔ lɛmii lɛ́bɛbɛ lísie kama aani kalɛ na ɔ́su bina bati kuuku úse na ka wete-mii ni, 9na bidie lɛma ɛtɛ bibunku lideedi lɛmmɔ. Na si bɛɛdi ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui na líti muute-mii ɔmwi na bɛɛyɔ́ bina Unwoti Katɔti ni, ɔdubɔbla ɔmɛni ute-mii. 10Bɛbla ɔmɛni kalɛ na biládu bekyuli bani nátaƒiɔ. Na bilákɛ kɔtɔ bɔdu bɔdi na kukpi kɔmɛni udu lɛlɔ na kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti úti uute-mii mɛni kemmo.
11Nsu si ukyuli ɔdi uukisi nwuna ukyuli ɔkpana na útábɛ ɔɔtú-nwu na ɔ́du-nwu na úkeli úsie lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛdi biala kemmo utátamiku-ma ni, 12benengu bani nkya ɔma ɔni kemmo na ukyuli ɔdune ɔmmɔ ɔ́si ɔlɛka batala na betétiku-nwu beboku, na beti-nwu bete ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́du mmɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli, na ama lɛnɔ badu-nwu. 13Bitanu ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu kɔnyana. Na bɛnu ka bɛ́da bekyuli badune bídie Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ kalɛ na lɛla biala lisieku-mii kaduɛ.
Bitavumana Ɔmii Ɔkukudi Ɔdi
14Na ɔdi utavumana ɔmii ɔkukudi ɔni na básia bése na kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti uute-mii mɛni lɛlɔ.
Nkyuli Inyɔ Iye Ɛtɛ Bedie Lɛla Kenye
15Útalɛka ukyuli unwi kani udie lɛla likpidi lɛni na ɔdi ɔ́bla kenye. Bɛya na nkyuli inyɔ iye ɛtɛ benye-nwu litemi kama. 16Na si ukyuli ɔ́nyi ɔkɔ ɔ́sia ukyuli ɔdi ni, 17ukyuli ɔni na bányi ɔkɔ básia mmɔ ku ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ mmɔ ƒui ɔlɛka besie kesii kani na baakpá Katɔti na batánu bakpane bani mɔɔbla akpala kabla mmɔ ku litemi batɛne bani nkya mmɔ na batɛ litemi lɛmmɔ. 18Na litemi batɛne bammɔ badubuduo etemila ammɔ kemmo kaduɛ na si bánu báti ka ɔkɔ na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́nyi ɔ́sia nwuna ɔkpana Israelni ni, 19ɔlɛka beti kɔtu bɔni bɔmmɔ bani ɔkɔ ɔnyine ɔmmɔ. Lɛni na bɛdubudie likpidi lɛmɛni udu bɛlɛku bina akɔ. 20Na ɔmɛni ndubɔya na ukyuli biala únu litemi lɛmmɔ na liƒu lɛda-nwu kalɛ ɔdi ɔsɔ ulabla lɛla likpidi lɛmmɔ udu. 21Na etemila ammɔ bene lɛlɔ ni, bitanu ɔdi kɔnyana. Na kɔtu kɔni na ɔlɛka bani-nwu ndi ka si ukyuli ɔ́du ni, ɔlɛka badu anwu lɛnɔ. Si ukyuli lɛnumi na ɔ́bwɛ ni, ɔlɛka babwɛ anwu lɛdi lɛnɔ. Na si lɛnyi na ɔ́kpa ni, ɔlɛka bakpa nwuna lɛdi lɛnɔ. Na si nwuna kɔnu na úkulo ni, ɔlɛka bekulo nwuna kɔdi lɛnɔ. Na si ɔgba na úkulo ni, ɔlɛka bekulo nwuna ɔdi lɛnɔ.

english_text:
Laws for Going to War
Moses said to Israel:
1If you have to go to war, you may find yourselves facing an enemy army that is bigger than yours and that has horses and chariots. But don't be afraid! The Lord your God rescued you from Egypt, and he will help you fight. 2Before you march into battle, a priest will go to the front of the army 3and say, “Soldiers of Israel, listen to me! Today when you go into battle, don't be afraid of the enemy, and when you see them, don't panic. 4The Lord your God will fight alongside you and help you win the battle.”
5Then the tribal officials will say to the troops:
