If any of you have built a new house, but haven't yet moved in, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to live in your new house.
6If any of you have planted a vineyard but haven't had your first grape harvest, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to enjoy your grapes.
7If any of you are engaged to be married, you may go back home and get married. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to marry the woman you are engaged to.
8Finally, if any of you are afraid, you may go home. We don't want you to discourage the other soldiers.
9When the officials are finished giving these orders, they will appoint officers to be in command of the army.
10-15Before you attack a town that is far from your land, offer peace to the people who live there. If they surrender and open their town gates, they will become your slaves. But if they reject your offer of peace and try to fight, surround their town and attack. Then, after the Lord helps you capture it, kill all the men. Take the women and children as slaves and keep the livestock and everything else of value.
16Whenever you capture towns in the land the Lord your God is giving you, be sure to kill all the people and animals. 17He has commanded you to completely wipe out the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. 18If you allow them to live, they will persuade you to worship their disgusting gods, and you will be unfaithful to the Lord.
19When you are attacking a town, don't chop down its fruit trees, not even if you have had the town surrounded for a long time. Fruit trees aren't your enemies, and they produce food that you can eat, so don't cut them down. 20You may need wood to make ladders and towers to help you get over the walls and capture the town. But use only trees that you know are not fruit trees.
translation_text:
Katɔti Ɔɔnu-mii Lɛlɔ Na Kekpo Uwi
1Si bísela bitékpoku bina bekisine badi na bɛ́nu ka bekyuli bammɔ belie bapɔnkɔ ku kɛɛkɛ ɔni na bapɔnkɔ baaní lɛlɔ ni, na bɛ́nu bekyuli bumomo bɔni ntulo amii ni, bitanu-ma bitayia. Ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔni náda-mii údie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, anwu ndubukpo ute-mii. 2Na asa na bɛdubuse kalɔ ku bukpo ni, ɔlɛka Katɔti ɔkpane ɔdi ɔlɛ ubo ubenye bina anumi na ɔsu bekpone bammɔ ɔnini, 3“Israel bananabi, bise atu na binu. Ɔmwi kadi ni, bísela bitékpo. Bitayia bina bekisine bammɔ na enu ataƒɛ-mii na ɔtɔtɔ utagyu-mii. 4Ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔkya-mii akɔ na ɔdubɔya na bɛdi lɛlɔ.”
5Na baduɔti bammɔ lɛnɔ badubɔlɛ bebo na betemi bete bekpone bammɔ na beye-ma banini, “Ɔnana ɔdi ɔkya-mii akɔ mɛni na ɔ́tu ɔtɔ ɔwɔdi na útesie útetélie-nwu kemmo tɔ?” Na si ɔdi údie kenye ka “Ɛɛn” ni, na unwini uteesie kaduli. Na si ɔɔɔdi lɛni na ɔ́ta na útékpi na kekpo kammɔ kemmo ni, ukyuli ɔbambadi ndubo kaduli kammɔ kemmo bulie. 6Na basɔ beye bekpone bammɔ benu si ɔnana ɔdi ɔkya-ma akɔ na ɔ́tuma adingyii kemo kadi, nsu útakɛ kɔnu útaƒɛ edula ammɔ tɔ? Na si ɔdi ɔtuna ka “Ɛɛn” ni, bɛya na unwini usie kaduli. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni na ɔ́ta úsie kekpo kammɔ na útékpi ni, ukyuli bamba ndubɔni kɔdingyii kɔmmɔ ntɛ bute-nwu. 7Na basɔ beye bekpone bammɔ si ɔnana ɔdi ɔkya-ma akɔ na ɔ́bla uleku lili ala use, nsu útawɛɛ-nwu tɔ. Si ɔdi ɔ́tuna ka “Ɛɛn” ni, na bɛya na unwini usie kaduli. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, ukyuli bamba ndubuti uleku ɔmmɔ. 8Na basɔ beye bekpone bammɔ kɔkladi banini, “Bina akɔ ɔdi ɔkya na ɔtɔtɔ ɔɔgyú-nwu iye enu áƒɛ-nwu?” Na si badi bátuna banii “Ɛɛn” ni, na bɛya na benwini kalɛ na lɛlɔ lilawiɛ bekpone bakladi. 9Na si baduɔti bammɔ bátɛmiku-ma báwɔlɔ ni, na bedie bekpone baƒanti bete bekpone bammɔ.
10Asa na bɛdubusie bitékpo ɔma ɔdi bekyuli ni, bɛka-ma buye si badubute lili. 11Na si bénu kalɔ ka bete lili na bálɛmi ɔma ɔmmɔ kayakun béte-mii ni, bekyuli bani nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo badubo kabla kpakplaa butaabla teete-mii. 12Nsu si bétenu kalɔ ka bete lili ni, bɛka bɛmana ɔma ɔmmɔ na bikpoku-ma. 13Na si bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na bɛ́di-ma lɛlɔ ni, na bɛdu ɔnana biala na ɔkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. 14Na bɛɛyɔ́ ni, bɛkana biti bana beleku ku bebi ku bebuo ku lɛla biala lɛni nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na bibo kuƒi ka bɛblaku lɛla biala na bina bekisine bammɔ bebo kalɛ na bɛɛyɔ́. Ɔsika bina Unwoti néti-nya úte-mii. 15Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni buse bute lɛma lɛni na lɛ́gyunku-mii kakaaka kani. Na ɔɔɔdanku kalɔ kani lɛma na Katɔti úti uute-mii mmɔ ɔdi.
16Nsu si bɛ́di lɛma lɛni nkya kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ ni, na bɛyila lɛla biala nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo udu. 17Na lɛma lɛmmɔ ndi Hetiƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Hewiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ lɛma aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-mii ɔda úse ka bɛbla-ma mmɔ. 18Bɛyila-ma udu kalɛ na balátɔlɔ-mii na bitaabla ala ani muusé-nwu lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku bana lɛƒiɔkpa ablala lɛlɔ. Na ɔdi uláƒiɔ bina Unwoti Katɔti.
19Na si bítáka ɔma ɔdi bɛ́kya ka bikpoku-ma na kekpo kammɔ keetu uwi ni, bitada adingyii ammɔ. Ɔsika bɛkana na bɛdi ebi ani na aanwu mmɔ adi. Ɔsika egyii ammɔ aaadi bekyuli bani na bítáka bɛ́kya ka bikpo. 20Nsu bɛkana bɛda egyii ani naaadi adingyii bɛbla ala ani ndubɔya na bɛkɛ kenyekɔ bɛka bɛmana ɔmmɔ na biƒie-ma enu enu.

english_text:
Unsolved Murder
Moses said to Israel:
1Suppose the body of a murder victim is found in a field in the land the Lord your God is giving you, and no one knows who the murderer is. 2The judges and other leaders from the towns around there must find out what town is the closest to where the body was found. 3The leaders from that town will go to their cattle herds and choose a young cow that has never been put to work. 4-5They and some of the priests will take this cow to a nearby valley where there is a stream, but no crops. Once they reach the valley, the leaders will break the cow's neck.
The priests must be there, because the Lord your God has chosen them to be his special servants at the place of worship. The Lord has chosen them to bless the people in his name and to be judges in all legal cases, whether property or injury is involved.
6The town leaders will wash their hands over the body of the dead cow 7and say, “We had no part in this murder, and we don't know who did it. 8-9But since an innocent person was murdered, we beg you, our Lord, to accept this sacrifice and forgive Israel. We are your people, and you rescued us. Please don't hold this crime against us.”
If you obey the Lord and do these things, he will forgive Israel.
Marrying a Woman Taken Prisoner in War
Moses said to Israel:
10From time to time, you men will serve as soldiers and go off to war. The Lord your God will help you defeat your enemies, and you will take many prisoners. 11-13One of these prisoners may be a beautiful woman, and you may want to marry her. But first you must bring her into your home, and have her shave her head, cut her nails, get rid of her foreign clothes, and start wearing Israelite clothes. She will mourn a month for her father and mother, then you can marry her.
14Later on, if you are not happy with the woman, you can divorce her, and she can go free. But you have slept with her as your wife, so you cannot sell her as a slave or make her into your own slave.
Rights of a First-Born Son
Moses said to Israel:
15-17Suppose a man has two wives and loves one more than the other. The first son of either wife is the man's first-born son, even if the boy's mother is the wife the man doesn't love. Later, when the man is near death and is dividing up his property, he must give a double share to his first-born son, simply because he was the first to be born.
A Son Who Rebels
Moses said to Israel:
18A father and a mother may have a stubborn and rebellious son who refuses to obey them even after he has been punished. 19If a son is like that, his parents must drag him to the town gate, where the leaders of the town hold their meetings. 20The parents will tell the leaders, “This son of ours is stubborn and never obeys. He spends all his time drinking and partying.”
21The men of the town will stone that son to death, because they must get rid of the evil he brought into the community. Everyone in Israel will be afraid when they hear how he was punished.
The Body of a Criminal
Moses said to Israel:
22If a criminal is put to death, and you hang the dead body on a tree, 23 you must not leave it there overnight. Bury it the same day, because the dead body of a criminal hanging on a tree will bring God's curse on the land. The Lord your God is giving this land to you, so don't make it unclean by leaving the bodies of executed criminals on display.
translation_text:
Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Na Ukyuli Bɔdu Lɛlɔ
1Si bɛ́nu ka ukyuli ɔdi úkpi ɔtɛ kemo na kalɔ kani kemmo na bina Unwoti ɔ́su ka wete-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ na bɛɛɛgyi ukyuli ɔni nádu-nwu ni, 2lɛla lɛni na ɔdi ka bɛbla ndi ka bina benengu ku litemi batɛne besie kemo kani na ukyuli ɔmmɔ úkpi ɔtɛ na batákɔku eluku ani nkya mmɔ bɔgyu ɔ́si kemo kammɔ útédu lɛma lɛni nde mmɔ banu. 3Na ɔmɛni kama ni, ɔma ɔni nde kesii kani na ukpine ɔtɛ benengu bawia ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔkɔdi ɔni na béteti-nwu bátabla kabla kadi kudii. 4Na beti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔmɛni besienku kɔwɛ kɔni kemmo na ketu kani nátakwii kudii katɛ na bátatuma mmɔ iye bátava edula adi mmɔ kudii. Na si bésie mmɔ ni, na beti lɛla lɛdi baƒiɛmi ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔmmɔ limɔ kama badu. 5Na bɛya na Katɔti bakpane bani ndi Lewiƒuɔ badi basiaku-ma uwi ɔni na bésela batábla ala ammɔ. Ɔsika ama na Katɔti ɔ́ƒuna ka bakpa-nwu na benye-nwu lɛnyi kenye bete bekyuli kusɛ kusɛ na batɛ etemila aani kalɔ etemila ku ukyuli bubo bɔkya ɔlɛ etemila.
6Na si bekyuli bamɛni ƒui bása báwɔlɔ ni, na benengu bani nde ɔma ɔni na ukyuli ɔmmɔ úkpi ɔtɛ mmɔ baƒɔ bana enu bewi ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔmmɔ kama. 7Na si baaƒɔ bana enu ammɔ ni, na basu banini, “Ɔɔɔdi abu nádu ukyuli ɔni nékpi mmɔ. Na bɔɔɔgyi ukyuli ɔni nádu-nwu. 8Anwuɔsu Unwoti, ti ƒula bebi Israelƒuɔ bani na áda édie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ekpidi kyiɛ-ma. Ti kyiɛ-bu na tasu anii abu nádu ukyuli ɔni nékpi mmɔ.” Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na kɔtɔ bɔdu bulasia benengu bammɔ lɛlɔ. 9Na si bɛ́bla lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-mii mɛni ni, uleti ukyuli ɔni nékpi mmɔ kɔtɔ bɔdu ulasia bina kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ.
Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Na Beleku Bani Na Béƒie-ma Kekpo Kemmo Lɛlɔ
10Si bísie kekpo kadi na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na bɛ́di-ma lɛlɔ na bíƒie bekyuli badi 11na ɔdi ɔ́nu uleku ɔni mɔɔdia-nwu bɔnu na bana akɔ na ɔɔyɔ́ ka uti-nwu ni, kuƒi kɔtɛ. 12Nsu asa na ɔdi weti uleku ɔmmɔ ɔdi ni, ɔlɛka uti uleku ɔmmɔ usienku kaduli na ukpeyi-nwu lili na ukulo-nwu aƒiɔ. 13Na ɔvumana-nwu adala ani na unyimi. Na ɔya na uleku ɔmmɔ ulie-nwu kaduli kɔbuli kumodi na uwulo nwuna bawɔne. Na si ɔ́bla ɔmɛni ƒui ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, asa na uti-nwu. 14Na si éti-nwu na ánu ka asɔ alayɔ-nwu ni, eeebo kuƒi ka anu-nwu aani ukyuli uyedi na eti-nwu eye. Ɔsika awɔ ku-nwu bɛ́tɛ na ébile-nwu. Anwuɔsu nyonu-nwu na uteesie ƒaa.
Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Na Bananabi Bedeedi Ala Bɔdi Kuƒi Lɛlɔ
15Bɛya na buti-nwu bɔnii ɔnana ɔdi ɔkya-mii akɔ na ubo beleku inyɔ na ɔdi biala ɔ́ka ɔnanabi bɔwɔ bute-nwu. Na uleku udeedi ɔni náka bɔwɔ ɔdi uleku ɔni na ɔgyani kayi kalayɔ. 16Na si uwi údu ka ɔgyani ule nwuna akɛla ute nwuna bebi ni, utasu ɔnii uute ubidi ɔnamudi nwuna akɛla utulo ka ɔɔyɔ́ uni teetulo ɔsu na ute ubidi unengudi ala blii suɛ ka ulayɔ uni ɔsu. 17Mmomu ɔdi ka ule nwuna akɛla kemmo akpa atɛ na uti akpa anyɔ ute ubidi ɔnanabi udeedi ɔmmɔ. Ɔsika ubidi ɔmmɔ nédie ɔti lɛnanabi keyi. Na anwu mbo ɔnanabi udeedi ala bɔdi kuƒi ina ka ɔti ulayɔ uni.
Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Na Bebi Bani Mbo Atuɔkplu Lɛlɔ
18Na lɛnɔ ni, bɛya na buti-nwu bɔnii ɔnana ɔdi ɔkya-mii akɔ na ubo ubi atuɔkplune na ɔɔta teenye nwuna bawɔne lɛlɔ. Na ubi ɔmmɔ ulenu bawɔne litemi ina báni-nwu kɔtu. 19Ubi ɔmmɔ udu bawɔne ni, ɔlɛka beti ubi ɔmmɔ besienku ɔma ɔni kemmo bakya mmɔ benengu anumi na kabanye kesii kani na benengu bammɔ beelie na beye-nwu kenye litemi. 20Na si bawɔne bammɔ béti-nwu bésienku-ma anumi ni, lɛla lɛni na ɔdi ka bawɔne bammɔ basu ndi ɔnini, “Bula ubi ɔmɛni ubo atuɔkplu na ɔɔta teenye-bu lɛlɔ na si bɔ́su-nwu lɛla lɛdi uléti na ubo lɛkantakpi na ɔdi ntɛkpine ubendi.” 21Na si bawɔne bammɔ básu ɔmɛni báwɔlɔ ni, ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli bebo-nwu atabi bádu. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na bɛdubɔda bekyuli bekpidi bidie bina akɔ. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na Israelƒuɔ kadi ƒui benu lɛla lɛmɛni, na ukyuli biala ɔdubɔyia na ɔti lɛlɔ bɔda.
Úbo-ma Ɔda Na Ala Bamba Lɛlɔ
22Si bébo ukyuli bádu ɔkɛnku likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla na béti ukpine ɔmmɔ báƒala ugyii lɛlɔ ni, 23utalɛka ukpine ɔmmɔ ɔƒa mmɔ ugye kadi. Ɔlɛka bava-nwu limeyi lɛmmɔ kani. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, bɛdububile kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti uute-mii mmɔ. Ɔsika ukyuli ɔni na báƒala-nwu ugyii lɛlɔ ɔdanku Katɔti ewida.

english_text:
Helping Others
Moses said to Israel:
1 If you see a cow or sheep wandering around lost, take the animal back to its owner. 2If the owner lives too far away, or if you don't know who the owner is, take the animal home with you and take care of it. The owner will come looking for the animal, and then you can give it back. 3That's what you should do if you find anything that belongs to someone else. Do whatever you can to help, whether you find a cow or sheep or donkey or some clothing.
4Oxen and donkeys that carry heavy loads can stumble and fall, and be unable to get up by themselves. So as you walk along the road, help anyone who is trying to get an ox or donkey back on its feet.
Don't Pretend To Be the Opposite Sex
Moses said to Israel:
5Women must not pretend to be men, and men must not pretend to be women. The Lord your God is disgusted with people who do that.
Don't Take a Mother Bird
Moses said to Israel:
6-7As you walk along the road, you might see a bird's nest in a tree or on the ground. If the mother bird is in the nest with either her eggs or her baby birds, you are allowed to take the baby birds or the eggs, but not the mother bird. Let her go free, and the Lord will bless you with a long and successful life.
Put a Wall around Your Flat Roof
8If you build a house, make sure to put a low wall around the edge of the flat roof. Then if someone falls off the roof and is killed, it won't be your fault.
Laws against Mixing Different Things
Moses said to Israel:
9 If you plant a vineyard, don't plant any other fruit tree or crop in it. If you do plant something else there, you must bring to the place of worship everything you harvest from the vineyard.
10Don't hitch an ox and a donkey to your plow at the same time.
11When you weave cloth for clothing, you can use thread made of flax or wool, but not both together. 12 And when you make a coat, sew a tassel on each of the four corners.
When a Husband Accuses His Wife
Moses said to Israel:
13Suppose a man starts hating his wife soon after they are married. 14He might tell ugly lies about her, and say, “I married this woman, but when we slept together, I found out she wasn't a virgin.”
15If this happens, the bride's father and mother must go to the town gate to show the town leaders the proof that the woman was a virgin. 16Her father will say, “I let my daughter marry this man, but he started hating her 17and accusing her of not being a virgin. But he is wrong, because here is proof that she was a virgin!” Then the bride's parents will show them the bed sheet from the woman's wedding night.
18The town leaders will beat the man with a whip 19because he accused his bride of not being a virgin. He will have to pay her father 100 pieces of silver and will never be allowed to divorce her.
20But if the man was right and there is no proof that his bride was a virgin, 21the men of the town will take the woman to the door of her father's house and stone her to death.
This woman brought evil into your community by sleeping with someone before she got married, and you must get rid of that evil by killing her.
Laws about Illegal Sex
Moses said:
22People of Israel, if a man is caught having sex with someone else's wife, you must put them both to death. That way, you will get rid of the evil they have done in Israel.
23-24If a man is caught in town having sex with an engaged woman who isn't screaming for help, they both must be put to death. The man is guilty of having sex with a married woman. And the woman is guilty because she didn't call for help, even though she was inside a town and people were nearby. Take them both to the town gate and stone them to death. You must get rid of the evil they brought into your community.
25 If an engaged woman is raped out in the country, only the man will be put to death. 26Do not punish the woman at all; she has done nothing wrong, and certainly nothing deserving death. This crime is like murder, 27because the woman was alone out in the country when the man attacked her. She screamed, but there was no one to help her.
28 Suppose a woman isn't engaged to be married, and a man forces her to have sex with him. If he is caught, 29they will be forced to get married. He must give her father 50 pieces of silver as a bride-price and can never divorce her.
30 A man must not marry a woman who was married to his father. This would be a disgrace to his father.
translation_text:
1Si bina kemmo ɔdi ɔ́nu ka ɔnwani ɔmantɛ akɔ iye koƒonu kɔdi ka kɔkɛ kɔɔví na kulati kaduli ulu ni, utanyonu ebuo ɔmmɔ. Mmomu uti-nwu usienku ɔlati. 2Nsu si ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔlati kaduli kágyunku kesii kani na awɔ elie mmɔ iye alanu ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔlati ni, awɔ ɔni nánu ebuo ɔmmɔ ti ebuo ɔmmɔ sienku ƒula kaduli. Na si ebuo ɔlati úbanu ebuo ɔmmɔ na ƒula kaduli ni, na eti nwuna ebuo ete-nwu. 3Lɛni kani na ɔlɛka bɛbla si bɛ́nu ukyuli ɔdi ɔƒlumu iye kɔdi iye lɛla bamba biala lɛni na ƒula ukyulikpana ɔ́yila. Na bitedie ala ammɔ atu.
4Na si ƒula ukyulikpana ɔƒlumu iye ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔdi uti etila na ubuli na ulakana bɔta ni, bunku ɔlati ɔmmɔ na bɛtalaku ebuo ɔmmɔ binyene.
5Uleku utakya ɔnana awu. Lɛni kani na ɔnana lɛnɔ utakya uleku awu. Na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubukisi ukyuli ɔni ndubɔbla ala ammɔ bene udu.
6Si bina akɔ ɔdi útánu aasɛ lɛyu lɛdi na kugyii lili iye ɔ́nu ka lɛyu lɛmmɔ lɛtɛ kalɔ na aasɛ ɔmmɔ ku bebi bakya-nwu kemmo iye ubi avala lɛlɔ ni, teƒie aasɛ ɔmmɔ ku nwuna bebi ƒui tatɔlɔku. 7Akana na eƒie bebi bammɔ iye eti avala ammɔ, nsu teƒie uni ɔmmɔ. Si bɛɛbla lɛni ni, bɛdubulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ na keyi kadubɔyɔku-mii.
8Na si ɔdi ɔ́tu lɛsa ɔtɔ ɔwɔdi ni, ɔnu ka ɔ́tu lɛsa ɔsangya na ɔ́kuku kalɛ na ɔdi ulánu na lɛsa lili na wekpi na básu banii anwu nádu-nwu.
9Ɔdi utava edula lidu inyɔ utakya nwuna adingyii kemo kani na ɔ́tuma kemmo. Si ɔdi ɔ́bla lɛni ni, uuubo kuƒi ka ɔƒɛ edula ammɔ adi iye ude ebi ammɔ adi.
10Na ɔdi utabala ɔpɔnkɔ ku ɔmantɛ akɔ anwami kɔgba utasala na begulu kalɔ bete-nwu.
11Na ɔdi utakya awu ɔni béti unwo ku koƒonu linwini bédi básala.
12Biti linwo lɛni na bébo-ni ekpo wɛlɛ wɛlɛ básala bɛkya bina adi avwi ene ammɔ atu akya.
Úbo-ma Ɔda Na Kɔgya Ku Ule Lɛlɔ
13Na bɛya na buti-nwu bɔnii ɔnana ɔdi úti uleku na kama ɔ́nu ka ɔsɔ ulayɔ uleku ɔmmɔ. 14Anwuɔsu ɔ́nyi ɔkɔ ɔ́sia uleku ɔmmɔ ka ɔɔɔdi adagyaa asa na úti-nwu.
15Si ɔ́lɛ lɛni ni, uleku ɔmmɔ bawɔne besie ɔma ɔmmɔ benengu kudɔ na ɔma ɔmmɔ kabanye kesii kani na beelie mmɔ na betédie bana ubi kenye ka uleku ɔmmɔ ɔdi adagyaa asa na ɔnana ɔmmɔ úti-nwu. 16Ɔmmɔ kama uleku ɔmmɔ ɔti ɔdubɔta unye na kadi akɔ mmɔ, na ɔsu benengu bammɔ ɔnini, “Líti mina ubi ulekubi ɔmɛni líte ɔnana ɔmɛni ka uti-nwu. Na ka bélie blii ni, ɔnii ɔsɔ ulayɔ-nwu. 17Na kenye kani na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔɔdá-nwu ndi ka úti-nwu na ɔɔɔdi adagyaa. Nsu bɛɛnu lɛdiku lɛni lɛlɔ na báka bɔtɛ. Bɛɛnu ubugya ɔni néduo-nwu kemmo mɛni. Ɔmɛni ɔɔtina ka ɔdi adagyaa asa na ɔnana ɔmmɔ úti-nwu.” 18Si ɔ́lɛ lɛni ni, na ɔma ɔmmɔ benengu bata na bebo ɔnana ɔmmɔ kugyiimi kaduɛ! 19Na bakya ɔnana ɔmmɔ kayu sika ɔƒualadi antabi akyami bɔkɔku eti anyɔ na beti ala ammɔ bete ulekubi ɔmmɔ ɔti. Ɔsika ɔnana ɔmmɔ úti kɔƒa úboku Israelni uleku lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔlɛka belie beteesie aani ɔgya ku ule. Na uwi ɔni na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔmu uli ngba ni, uuubo kuƒi kɔdi ka ɔnyonu ulekubi ɔmmɔ.
20Nsu si kenye kani na ɔgyani ɔmmɔ údie ɔdi sɔsɔ ka ulekubi ɔmmɔ ɔɔɔdi adagyaa asa na úti-nwu ni, 21na bakpanku ulekubi ɔmmɔ besienku ɔti kaduli na ɔma ɔmmɔ bananabi bebo-nwu atabi badu na ɔti kaduli kayakun kenye. Ɔsika ulekubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́di kɔsɔnɔ uwi ɔni na úlie ɔti kesii na útelie tɔ kɔgya. Na ɔmɛni ɔdi kɔƒa litemi. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na bɛdubɔsia na bɛda likpidi lɛmmɔ udu bidie bina akɔ.
22Na si bíƒie ɔnana ɔdi ka úsie ɔɔtɛnku ukyuli ɔdi ulekudi ni, bibo ɔnana ku uleku ɔmmɔ bɛdu. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na bɛdubɔsia na bɛda likpidi lɛmmɔ udu bidie bina akɔ.
23Na si bíƒie ɔnana ɔdi ka úsie ɔɔtɛnku uleku ɔni na bévele-nwu béte ɔnana ɔbamba na ɔma ɔdi kemmo ni, 24na bɛkpanku ɔnana ku uleku ɔmmɔ bisienku ɔma kabanye na bibo bana inyɔ atabi bɛdu. Ɔlɛka badu uleku ɔmmɔ, ɔsika úni na útava útakpali ka babaƒɔ-nwu ina ka ɔma kemmo na bakya uwi ɔni na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔnii anwu ku-nwu baatɛ. Na lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ɔlɛka badu ɔnana ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ndi ka úsie ɔɔtɛnku uleku ɔni bévele béte ukyuli bamba. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na bɛdubɔsia na bɛda likpidi lɛmmɔ udu bidie bina akɔ.
25Na si ɔnana ɔdi útéƒie uleku ɔni na bévele-nwu béte ɔnana bamba na ɔ́yɔ-nwu na alakpiakɔ ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ kani na ɔlɛka badu. 26Nsu ulekubi ɔmmɔ útalɛka badu-nwu, ɔsika útabla likpidi lɛni námanku kukpi. Na litemi lɛmɛni lise aani kalɛ na ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔsiáku nwuna ukyulikpana na ɔnii uubó-nwu ɔdu. 27Ɔsika uwi ɔni na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔkya ɔɔtɛnku-nwu mmɔ ni, ɔ́va ka ukyuli ɔdi úbaƒɔ-nwu. Nsu útakɛ ɔdi.
28Na si ɔnana ɔdi ɔ́nu adagyaa ɔni bétete tɔ kɔgya na úƒie-nwu ɔkya ɔɔtɛnku na bánu-nwu ni, 29ɔlɛka bakya-nwu kayu sika ɔƒualadi antabi akyami bɔkɔku liti ute uleku ɔmmɔ ɔti. Na ɔmmɔ kama uleku ɔmmɔ unwini ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔgyani. Ɔsika úwi-nwu anumi kalɔ. Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ uuubo kuƒi kɔdi na ɔnyonu ulekubi ɔmmɔ na nwuna ngba emeyi ƒui kemmo.
30Na ɔnana biala ku nwuna ɔti ulekudi ɔdi biala batatɛ. Na si ɔdi ɔ́bla lɛni ni, ɔdi kɔƒa kubendi kute-nwu.

english_text:
Who Cannot Become One of the Lord's People
Moses said to Israel:
1If a man's private parts have been crushed or cut off, he cannot fully belong to the Lord's people.
2No one born outside of a legal marriage, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can fully belong to the Lord's people.
3 No Ammonites or Moabites, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can become part of Israel, the Lord's people. 4 This is because when you came out of Egypt, they refused to provide you with food and water. And besides, they hired Balaam to put a curse on you. 5 But the Lord your God loves you, so he refused to listen to Balaam and turned Balaam's curse into a blessing. 6Don't even think of signing a peace treaty with Moab or Ammon.
7But Edomites are your relatives, and you lived as foreigners in the country of Egypt. Now you must be kind to Edomites and Egyptians 8and let their great-grandchildren become part of Israel, the Lord's people.
Keep the Army Camp Acceptable
Moses said to Israel:
9When you men go off to fight your enemies, make sure your camp is acceptable to the Lord.
10For example, if something happens at night that makes a man unclean and unfit for worship, he must go outside the camp and stay there 11until late afternoon. Then he must take a bath, and at sunset he can go back into camp.
12Set up a place outside the camp to be used as a toilet area. 13And make sure that you have a small shovel in your equipment. When you go out to the toilet area, use the shovel to dig a hole. Then, after you relieve yourself, bury the waste in the hole. 14You must keep your camp clean of filthy and disgusting things. The Lord is always present in your camp, ready to rescue you and give you victory over your enemies. But if he sees something disgusting in your camp, he may turn around and leave.
Runaway Slaves from Other Countries
Moses said:
15When runaway slaves from other countries come to Israel and ask for protection, you must not hand them back to their owners. 16Instead, you must let them choose which one of your towns they want to live in. Don't be cruel to runaway slaves.
Temple Prostitutes
Moses said:
17 People of Israel, don't any of you ever be temple prostitutes. 18The Lord your God is disgusted with men and women who are prostitutes of any kind, and he will not accept a gift from them, even if it had been promised to him.
Interest on Loans
Moses said:
19 When you lend money, food, or anything else to another Israelite, you are not allowed to charge interest. 20You can charge a foreigner interest. But if you charge other Israelites interest, the Lord your God will not let you be successful in the land you are about to take.
Sacred Promises to the Lord
Moses said:
21 People of Israel, if you make a sacred promise to give a gift to the Lord, then do it as soon as you can. If the Lord has to come looking for the gift you promised, you will be guilty of breaking that promise. 22On the other hand, if you never make a sacred promise, you can't be guilty of breaking it. 23You must keep whatever promises you make to the Lord. After all, you are the one who chose to make the promises.
Eating Someone Else's Produce
24If you go into a vineyard that belongs to someone else, you are allowed to eat as many grapes as you want while you are there. But don't take any with you when you leave. 25In the same way, if you are in a grain field that belongs to someone else, you can pick heads of grain and eat the kernels. But don't cut down the stalks of grain and take them with you.
translation_text:
Katɔti Úni Bekyuli Badi Na Nwuna Bekyuli Akɔ
1Ukyuli ɔni ndi ɔsaɛ ni, bitaya na uduo Unwoti bebi kasalakɔ.
2Na ubi ɔni na kɔsɔnɔ badi báwɔ-nwu ni, bitaya na utéduo Unwoti bebi kasalakɔ ɔ́si nwuna lɛlɔ útédu bana kaba leevudi lɛlɔ.
3Bitaka Amonni iye Moabni iye bana kaba kadi utédu bana kaba leevudi lɛlɔ bitakya Unwoti bebi akɔ. 4Ɔsika uwi ɔni bɛ́lɛ Egyipteƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ na bíbedu bana lɛma ni, ɔdi utéte-mii adila adi na bɛdi iye ntu na bɛni. Mmomu buti na bététi Bileam ɔni ndi Boer ubidi ɔni nási ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Petor na Mesopotamia kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ ka ubewida-mii. 5Nsu bina Unwoti Katɔti útakpete Bileam ewida ammɔ. Mmomu búti na úti ewida ammɔ únwini kusɛ kusɛ úte-mii. Ɔsika ɔɔyɔ́-mii litemi. 6Na bitabla unwi ku Arnonƒuɔ ku Moabƒuɔ bamɛni na bitawia-ma bɔdia lɛnɔ kudii.
7Nsu Edomƒuɔ ama ni, bɛƒɔ-ma, ɔsika badi bina bekyuli. Na biteni Egyipteƒuɔ, ɔsika bíilie bana kalɔ lɛlɔ dii aani baƒɔ. 8Na ɔ́si bana kaba katɛdi lɛlɔ úsela ni, bɛkana na bɛka bana bebi bibunku Unwoti bebi akɔ.
Kalɛ Na Ɔlɛka Bekpone Bada Lɛlɔ
9Na si bɛ́sala lisu bɛɛklibi lɛlɔ bite kekpo kadi ni, ɔdi utabla lɛla lɛni ndubɔya na nwuna lɛlɔ lilabla sɛɛn. 10Na si ɔdi úgye kɔna na lɛlɔ líbo-nwu na ɔmmɔ ɔsu na uuuse sɛɛn ni, ɔlɛka ɔlɛ kesii kani na bekpone bammɔ básala lisu bakya mmɔ na utákya kesii bamba. 11Na si úsela useyi uwi ni, ɔlɛka ɔkpi na ɔsɔ unwini ubo bekpone kakyakɔ mmɔ uwi ɔni na ɔƒɛ ɔ́nu.
12Na bɛwia kesii bamba na bina kakyakɔ kama na biti bɛbla bina kuvodɔ kesekɔ. 13Na si ɔdi úsela kuvodɔ ni, ɔwia lɛnwami blii lɛdi ɔda na uku ubu asa na use kuvodɔ. Na uwi-ku lɛti si ɔ́wɔlɔ. 14Ka Katɔti ɔkya-mii akɔ uusié taasɔ na kesii kani na bɛkya na ɔɔgyumana-mii kalɛ na bɛdi bina bekisine lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, bɛbla bina keliekɔ sɛɛn kalɛ na ulanu lɛla lɛni maya na wenwini kama wakya-mii.
Úte-ma Ɔda Bubo Bɔbambadi
15Si kabla ɔblane ɔdi úkeli nwuna unwoti kudɔ na úbo úbawia kabɛkɔ na bina ɔdi kudɔ ni, bɛƒɔ ukyuli ɔmmɔ na bitasɔku-nwu bitemene nwuna unwoti. 16Na bite ukyuli ɔmmɔ kuƒi na ɔkya-mii akɔ na ɔma ɔni na ɔɔyɔ́. Na bitenye-nwu lɛlɔ bɛnii ɔbla lɛla lɛdi ulikplu kemmo.
17Na Israelni ɔnana iye uleku ɔdi utenwini ɔyalɛ na koƒiodu kɔdi. 18Ɔƒɛni egulabi biala na ukyuli ɔmɛni udu ɔdubɔkɛ na kabla kani na ɔɔbla mɛni kemmo ni, uteti egulabi ammɔ adi uteboku bina Unwoti Katɔti kakpakɔ ɔnii ubedie lili na kenye kani na úse ɔsu. Ɔsika Katɔti bayalɛ beesé Katɔti lɛlɔ.
19Na si ɔdi úvo egulabi iye adila iye lɛla bamba lɛdi úte nwuna Israelni ɔkpana ni, utaƒɔ-nwu kuvonsia kɔdi. 20Nsu si úvo lɛla lɛdi úte ɔƒɔ ɔni nkya-mii akɔ ni, ɔkana na ɔƒɔ-nwu kuvonsia. Nsu Israelni ɔkpana anwu ni, bitaƒɔ kuvonsia kɔdi kalɛ na bina Unwoti Katɔti wete-mii kusɛ kusɛ na lɛla biala bíti bina enu bɛ́bla na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela bitélie mmɔ kemmo.
21Na si ɔdi úse kenye kadi úte nwuna Unwoti Katɔti ni, ɔnu ka ɔ́ƒɔ kayu kammɔ. Na utabla atuɔkplu na kenye kani úse mmɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ɔdi likpidi ka ése kenye na aladi-ka lɛlɔ, ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubo-ɔ buye. 22Na ɔɔɔdi likpidi lɛdi si étese kenye kadi étete Unwoti. 23Nsu lɛla lɛni na awɔ ɔlati néti ƒula bɔyɔ kemmo ásu na ése Katɔti kenye kadi bɔdi ni, nu ka ádi kenye kammɔ lɛlɔ.
24Na si ɔdi ɔkɛ ɔɔví na útáda ɔ́lɛ ɔkpanadi adingyii kemo na ɔ́nu ka ebi ammɔ adi égyie ni, ɔkana na ude ɔdi na ɔdi umo. Nsu uuubo kuƒi ka uti kɔdingyii kɔmmɔ ebi adi uwi lɛla lɛdi kemmo usienku kaduli.
25Na si ɔdi ɔ́kɛ ɔɔví na útáda ɔ́lɛ ɔkpanadi edula kemo ni, ubo kuƒi ka uti kɔnu na ukpeli edula ammɔ adi na ɔdi kalɛ na ɔkana. Nsu uuubo kuƒi ka ukulo adi ɔtɔlɔku.

english_text:
A Law about Divorce
Moses said to Israel:
1 Suppose a woman was divorced by her first husband because he found something disgraceful about her. He wrote out divorce papers, gave them to her, and sent her away. 2Later she married another man, 3who then either divorced her in the same way or died. 4Since she has slept with her second husband, she cannot marry her first husband again. Their marriage would pollute the land that the Lord your God is giving you, and he would be disgusted.
Newlyweds
Moses said to Israel:
5If a man and a woman have been married less than one year, he must not be sent off to war or sent away to do forced labor. He must be allowed to stay home for a year and be happy with his wife.
Loans
Moses said to Israel:
6When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that they will pay back the loan. But don't take one or both of their millstones, or else they may starve. They need these stones for grinding grain into flour to make bread.
Kidnapping
Moses said to Israel:
7 If you are guilty of kidnapping Israelites and forcing them into slavery, you will be put to death to remove this evil from the community.
Skin Diseases
Moses said to Israel:
8 I have told the priests what to do if any of you have leprosy, so do exactly what they say. 9 And remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam after you left Egypt.
Loans
Moses said to Israel:
10 When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that the money will be paid back. But you must not go into their house to get it. 11Wait outside, and they will bring out the item you have agreed on.
12Suppose someone is so poor that a coat is the only thing that can be offered as a guarantee on a loan. Don't keep the coat overnight. 13Instead, give it back before sunset, so the owner can keep warm and sleep and ask the Lord to bless you. Then the Lord your God will notice that you have done the right thing.
Poor People's Wages
Moses said:
14 If you hire poor people to work for you, don't hold back their pay, whether they are Israelites or foreigners who live in your town. 15Pay them their wages at the end of each day, because they live in poverty and need the money to survive. If you don't pay them on time, they will complain about you to the Lord, and he will punish you.
The Death Penalty
Moses said to Israel:
16 Parents must not be put to death for crimes committed by their children, and children must not be put to death for crimes committed by their parents. Don't put anyone to death for someone else's crime.
Don't Mistreat the Powerless
Moses said to Israel:
17 Make sure that orphans and foreigners are treated fairly. And if you lend money to a widow and want to keep something of hers to guarantee that she will pay you back, don't take any of her clothes. 18You were slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws.
Leave Some of Your Harvest for the Poor
Moses said to Israel:
19 If you forget to bring in a stack of harvested grain, don't go back in the field to get it. Leave it for the poor, including foreigners, orphans, and widows, and the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
20When you harvest your olives, don't try to get them all for yourself, but leave some for the poor. 21And when you pick your grapes, go over the vines only once, then let the poor have what is left. 22You lived in poverty as slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws.
translation_text:
Uleku Utidi Bɔnyonu Ku Bɔsɔku Buti Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ
1Bɛya na buti-nwu bɔnii ɔnana ɔdi úti uleku, na buti bɔmmɔ kama ɔ́nu lɛla lɛdi ɔ́siku uleku ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔsɔ ulayɔ-nwu. Anwuɔsu ɔnana ɔmmɔ úte uleku ɔmmɔ kakunkɛ ka ɔ́nyonu-nwu na údie-nwu ulu na ɔ́tɔlɔ-nwu kaduli. 2Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔnana bamba ɔ́nu uleku ɔmɛni na úti-nwu, 3na anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́nu ka ɔ́sɔ ulayɔ-nwu na úte-nwu kakunkɛ ka ɔ́nyonu-nwu na údie-nwu ulu na ɔ́tɔlɔ-nwu kaduli iye si bukpi na ɔgyani unyɔdi ɔmɛni úkpi muedi ni, 4ɔnana udeedi ɔmmɔ ɔsɔ uuubo kuƒi ka utéti uleku ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ. Ɔlɛka ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔnu uleku ɔmmɔ aani ukyuli ɔni na béwi-nwu anumi kalɔ. Na si ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ úti-nwu ni, ɔdi lɛla lɛni muusé Unwoti lɛlɔ. Na ɔdi utatábla lɛla lɛni udu muusé bina Unwoti Katɔti mmɔ na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela bitélie mmɔ.
Úbo-ma Ɔda Ɔbambadi
5Na si ɔnana ɔdi úti uleku ɔwɔdi ni, batakpanku ɔnana ɔmmɔ betesienku kekpo iye kabla kadi kemmo. Ɔlɛka bete-nwu kuƒi lɛkwa linwi na anwu ku ulekudi bakɛ kubiti.
6Na si ɔdi úvo lɛla lɛdi úte ɔkpanadi ni, utaƒɔ nwuna kukɔ iye lɛklɔyi lɛni na uuti taakɔ ɔlaaƒɔ utése ɔkpa. Si ɔdi ɔ́bla lɛni ni, ukyuli ɔmmɔ údie nwuna ɔkpanadi ɔmmɔ lɛdila ɔ́lɛku ɔnwani kenye kemmo. Ɔsika kukɔ kɔmmɔ na uuti taakɔ ɔlaaƒɔ na anwu ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli baadi.
7Na si ɔdi úƒie nwuna Israelni ɔkpana na úti ukyuli uƒiedi ɔmmɔ únwini ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla kabla teete-nwu iye úti-nwu uuyé ni, ɔlɛka bebo ukyuli ɔni néƒie ɔkpanadi uuyé mmɔ badu. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na bɛdubo likpidi lɛmmɔ udu bɔda budie bina akɔ.
8Na si ukyuli ɔdi uuƒi ɔlɛ buɛ ni, ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔsia anu kaduɛ na ɔbla ɔsiaku lɛla lɛni na bakpane bani ndi Lewiƒuɔ badubɔsu-nwu ka ɔbla lɛlɔ. Na bɛnu ka bɛ́di ɔda ɔni líbo-mii mɛni lɛlɔ. 9Na binyimo lɛla lɛni na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́bla Miriam uwi ɔni na bɛ́si bɛɛlɛ́ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.
10Na si bina ɔdi évo lɛla lɛdi éte ƒula ɔkpanadi na úti nwuna kɔdi úse ɔkpa úte-ɔ ni, tesie tetéduo ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔtɔ kemmo na etéti kɔdi kɔmmɔ awɔ ɔlati. 11Mmomu sɔ nye keyi na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔlati utéti kɔdi kɔmmɔ uboku-ɔ. 12Na si ɔwabane névo lɛla lɛmmɔ na kɔdi na úti úse ɔkpa úte-ɔ ni, taƒɔ kɔdi kɔmmɔ tese lɛlɔ tetédu useyi uwi. 13Mmomu useyi uwi ni, ti ɔwabane ɔmmɔ kɔdi boku-nwu na ubi lɛlɔ ɔtɛ. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔda-nwu kubiti na kaƒɔ kadubɔyɔ bina Unwoti Katɔti.
14Tanya Israelni ɔwabane iye ɔƒɔ ɔwabane ɔni nkya-mii akɔ takya si éti-nwu anii ubabla kabla na limeyi lɛyuƒɔla kenye ute-ɔ. 15Nu ka áƒɔ-nwu nwuna limeyi kabla kenye kayu asa na ɔƒɛ ɔ́nu. Ɔsika bɔwia na ɔwabane ɔmmɔ ɔɔwia egulabi ammɔ ɔbla lɛla lɛdi. Na si átaƒɔ-nwu kayu kammɔ na úwulo ɔ́kpali Unwoti na lɛla lɛni na ábla-nwu mmɔ ɔsu ni, Katɔti ɔdubɔdu awɔ unwoti ɔmmɔ likpidi kɔtɔ.
16Kuƒi kuuubo ka badu bawɔne na likpidi lɛni na bana bebi bábla ɔsu, na batadu bebi na likpidi lɛni na bana bawɔne bábla ɔsu. Mmomu ɔdi biala ɔ́manku ka badu-nwu na anwu ɔlati likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔsu.
17Bɛsi litemi lɛlɔ siin bite baƒɔ bani nkya-mii akɔ ku bekpinebi. Na ɔdi utaƒɔ ukpinele ɔdi kɔdi utese ɔkpa si ɔɔwia kevonkɔ kadi. 18Na binyimo ka dii uwi ɔdi kemmo ni, Egyipteƒuɔ bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bítaabla kabla teete-ma asa na bina Unwoti Katɔti úbaƒɔ-mii ɔ́lɛku bana enu kemmo. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na muubó-mii ɔda amɛni udu.
19Na si bísie bitáƒɛ bina edula adi na bɛ́yiƒala adi bíse ni, bɛsɔ bitenwini bitetéti-nya. Mmomu bɛda biwi baƒɔ bani nkya-mii akɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele. Na bitesie bitetéti edula ammɔ. Na si bɛɛbla lɛni ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubuteete-mii kusɛ kuse na lɛla biala bɛɛbla kemmo. 20Kunwi pɛ kani na ɔlɛka bisie bitála bina adingyii ebi na bɛsɔ bitesie bitatála ɔdi lɛnɔ. Bɛda ɔkladi bise bite bekyuli bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele. 21Na si bísie bítála bina adingyii ebi ni, bɛsɔ bitesie kunyɔdi lɛnɔ. Na bɛda ɔkladi biwi bise bite bekyuli bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele. 22Na bitaya na ɔlɛ-mii kasusu kemmo ka uwi ɔdi kemmo ni, bɛdi bekyuli bani na bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bɛɛbla kabla teete Egyipteƒuɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na líbo-mii ɔda ɔmɛni.

english_text:
Whipping as Punishment for a Crime
Moses said to Israel:
1-2Suppose you and someone else each accuse the other of doing something wrong, and you go to court, where the judges decide you are guilty. If your punishment is to be beaten with a whip, one of the judges will order you to lie down, and you will receive the number of lashes you deserve. 3 Forty lashes is the most that you can be given, because more than that might make other Israelites think you are worthless.
Don't Muzzle an Ox
Moses said to Israel:
4 Don't muzzle an ox while it is threshing grain.
A Son for a Dead Brother
Moses said to Israel:
5-6 Suppose two brothers are living on the same property, when one of them dies without having a son to carry on his name. If this happens, his widow must not marry anyone outside the family. Instead, she must marry her late husband's brother, and their first son will be the legal son of the dead man.
7 But suppose the brother refuses to marry the widow. She must go to a meeting of the town leaders at the town gate and say, “My husband died without having a son to carry on his name. And my husband's brother refuses to marry me so I can have a son.”
8The leaders will call the living brother to the town gate and try to persuade him to marry the widow. But if he doesn't change his mind and marry her, 9she must go over to him while the town leaders watch. She will pull off one of his sandals and spit in his face, while saying, “That's what happens to a man who won't help provide descendants for his dead brother.” 10From then on, that man's family will be known as “the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off.”
When Two Men Fight
Moses said to Israel:
11If two men are fighting, and the wife of one man tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the other man's private parts, 12you must cut off her hand. Don't have any mercy.
Be Honest in Business
Moses said to Israel:
13-14 Don't try to cheat people by having two sets of weights or measures, one to get more when you are buying, and the other to give less when you are selling. 15If you weigh and measure things honestly, the Lord your God will let you enjoy a long life in the land he is giving you. 16But the Lord is disgusted with anyone who cheats or is dishonest.
Wipe Out Amalek
Moses said:
17 People of Israel, do you remember what the Amalekites did to you after you came out of Egypt? 18You were tired, and they followed along behind, attacking those who could not keep up with the others. This showed that the Amalekites have no respect for God.
19The Lord your God will help you capture the land, and he will give you peace. But when that day comes, you must wipe out Amalek so completely that no one will remember they ever lived.
translation_text:
1Bɛya na buti-nwu bɔnii Israelni ku Israelni bákɛ litemi na béti litemi lɛmmɔ bésienku litemi batɛne kudɔ na bátɛ na béte unwi ubo na bádu ɔkladi kɔtɔ. 2Na ukyuli ɔni bádu kɔtɔ mmɔ nwuna kɔtu bɔni ndi ka bebo-nwu kugyiimi. Na asa na badububo-nwu kugyiimi kɔmmɔ ni, litemi ɔtɛne ɔmmɔ ɔlɛka unwini ukyuli ɔmmɔ anumi ubi kalɔ asa na beteewi-nwu kugyiimi kɔmmɔ. Na likpidi lɛni udu na ɔ́bla ndubɔtina kugyiimi bumomo bɔni na ɔlɛka bebo-nwu. 3Bakana na bebo-nwu kugyiimi aavlene. Na ɔmmɔ kama basɔ betebo-nwu lɛnɔ. Si útulo lɛni ni, badubo-nwu kɔƒa bɔkya na bekyuli akɔ.
4Na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔmantɛ akɔ unye ɔɔbla kabla teete-nwu ni, utenyimi-nwu kenye.
Úbo-ma Ɔda Na Ukpinele Litemi Lɛlɔ
5Si banwa inyɔ beli básala na bana kemmo unwi úkpi na útawɔ asa na úkpi ni, ukpinele ɔmmɔ utalɛka utélie kɔgya na ɔtɔ bamba kemmo. Mmomu ɔgyani ɔni nékpi mmɔ ɔnwani ɔlɛka uti-nwu. 6Na si anwu ku uleku ɔmmɔ báwɔ ubi udeedi ni, na ubi ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ɔnwani ɔni nékpi mmɔ ubi. Ɔmɛni ndubɔya na ɔnwani ɔni nékpi mmɔ lɛnyi lilayi na Israel. 7Nsu si uleku ɔmmɔ ɔgyani ɔnwani úni ɔnii uleti-nwu ni, uleku ɔmmɔ usie ɔma benengu anumi na ɔsu ɔnini, “Mina ɔgyani ɔnwani ɔnii ulayɔ-mii. Na ulayɔ ka ɔnwani ɔni nékpi ɔkɛ kaba kadi ɔkya Israel kaba kemmo.” 8Na si uleku ɔmɛni ɔ́su lɛni ni, ɔlɛka ɔma benengu bamɛni balɔ ɔnana ɔmmɔ na bakɛ lɛla lɛdi basu-nwu. Na si básu-nwu na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́mu unye ɔɔsu ka ulayɔ uleku ɔmmɔ ɔsu uleti-nwu ni, 9na ukpinele ɔmmɔ ɔta usie ɔma benengu bammɔ anumi na ɔda ɔnana ɔmmɔ lɛgbanvuo udie-nwu lɛgba na ɔbwɛ lisuo uwi-nwu anumi na ɔsu ɔnini, “Ati bene, ukyuli ɔmɛni néni ka ɔnwani utakɛ kaba kadi.” 10Na ɔmɛni ɔsu ukyuli biala ɔdubɔnu bɔti kalɛ na ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ use. Na bekyuli basu banii ɔtɔ ɔmɛni kemmo na ɔnana ɔni bedie-nwu lɛgbanvuo ɔ́si.
Úte-ma Ɔda Bubo Bɔbambadi
11Na si banana inyɔ badi beekpó na unwi ulekudi ɔ́lɛ ɔnii utáƒɔ ɔgyani na úse kalɔ ɔɔda ɔnana ɔkladi ɔmmɔ agobɛɛ taani ni, ɔlɛka beƒie uleku ɔmmɔ kɔnu bekulo. 12Na batanu-nwu kɔnyana kɔdi. 13Na lɛbuala lɛni beeti taakɔku ala unu taanu ni, bitabla-nwu ɔgya ku ule na biti bitaanya bekyuli taakya. 14Lɛni kani na bitawia akyami ani baakɔ́ku ala ɔgya ku ule bitese lɛlɔ biti bitaanya bekyuli taakya. 15Bɛnu ka lɛbuala lɛni na bɛɛkɔ́ku ala unu ku akyami ani na bɛɛkya ala bumomo ƒui adi akɔkula ani námanku. 16Ɔsika Unwoti ulayɔ ukyuli ɔni mbo kasisi na ɔɔnu ukyuli anumi ƒui na ɔɔnya-nwu taakya.
Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Ka Badu Amalekƒuɔ
17Na bitayiƒala lɛla lɛni na Amalekƒuɔ bábla-mii uwi ɔni na bɛ́si Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ bɛkɛ ulu bísela. 18Bátina ka beeebo Katɔti bɔyia biala na bana kemmo. Anwuɔsu ka bánu báti ka lɛlɔ líitu-mii na bina ulu busie kemmo ɔsu ni, báta na békpoku-mii na bádu bani nábla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. 19Anwuɔsu si bítéduo kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́ya na bɛ́kɛ bɔnwuna bɛ́siku bina bekisine enu kemmo ni, bɛnu ka bɛ́du Amalekƒuɔ ƒui kalɛ na ukyuli ɔdi ulenyimo-ma muedi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu bise litemi lɛmɛni likpo na bitayiƒala!

english_text:
Give the Lord the First Part of Your Harvest
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord is giving you the land, and soon you will conquer it, settle down, 2 and plant crops. And when you begin harvesting each of your crops, the very first things you pick must be put in a basket. Take them to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped, 3and tell the priest, “Long ago the Lord our God promised our ancestors that he would give us this land. And today, I thank him for keeping his promise and giving me a share of the land.”
4The priest will take the basket and set it in front of the Lord's altar. 5Then, standing there in front of the place of worship, you must pray:
My ancestor was homeless,
an Aramean who went to live
in Egypt.
There were only a few
in his family then,
but they became great
and powerful,
a nation of many people.
6The Egyptians were cruel
and had no pity on us.
They mistreated our people
and forced us into slavery.
7We called out for help
to you, the Lord God
of our ancestors.
You heard our cries;
you knew we were in trouble
and abused.
8Then you terrified the Egyptians
with your mighty miracles
and rescued us from Egypt.
9You brought us here
and gave us this land
rich with milk and honey.
10Now, Lord, I bring to you
the best of the crops
that you have given me.
After you say these things, place the basket in front of the Lord's altar and bow down to worship him.
11Then you and your family must celebrate by eating a meal at the place of worship to thank the Lord your God for giving you such a good harvest. And remember to invite the Levites and the foreigners who live in your town.
Ten Percent of the Harvest
Moses said to Israel:
12 Every year you are to give ten percent of your harvest to the Lord. But every third year, this ten percent must be given to the poor who live in your town, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. That way, they will have enough to eat. 13Then you must pray:
Our Lord and our God, you have said that ten percent of my harvest is sacred. I have obeyed your command and given this to the poor, including the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
14I have not eaten any of this sacred food while I was in mourning; in fact, I never touched it when I was unclean. And none of it has been offered as a sacrifice to the spirits of the dead. I have done everything exactly as you commanded.
15Our Lord, look down from your temple in heaven and bless us and our land. You promised our ancestors that you would give us this land rich with milk and honey, and you have kept your promise.
The Lord Is Your God, and You Are His People
Moses said to Israel:
16Today the Lord your God has commanded you to obey these laws and teachings with all your heart and soul.
17In response, you have agreed that the Lord will be your God, that you will obey all his laws and teachings, and that you will listen when he speaks to you.
18 Since you have agreed to obey the Lord, he has agreed that you will be his people and that you will belong to him, just as he promised. 19The Lord created all nations, but he will make you more famous than any of them, and you will receive more praise and honor. You will belong only to the Lord your God, just as he promised.
translation_text:
Edula Edeedi Ku Ala Lɛkpa Leevudi Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ
1Si bísie bítéduo kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ ni, na bɛ́bla bina keliekɔ bɛ́wɔlɔ ni, 2ɔdi biala na ɔ́bla edula edeedi na ɔ́ƒɛ-nya ni, uti edula edeedi ammɔ adi uwi kagyigyɛ kemmo na uti-nya usienku kesii kani na Katɔti kakpakɔ kakya. 3Na utánu Katɔti ɔkpane ɔni mɔɔbla-nwu kabla uwi ɔmmɔ na ɔsu-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni líti edula amɛni líboku na líti mɔɔtina ka líduo kalɔ kani na mina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka weti wete bula bati kuuku kemmo.”
4Si ásu lɛni áwɔlɔ ni, Katɔti ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔƒɔ kagyigyɛ kammɔ na uti-ka utásia bina Katɔti lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ anumi. 5Na ɔmmɔ kama bɛdubɔsu etemila amɛni na Unwoti anumi bɛnini, “Kuuku ni, mina ɔti ndi Aramni ɔni neeebo keliekɔ kadi. Bulie kani na uulie taata. Na útélie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na asa na ɔdubusie utélie mmɔ ni, nwuna badi beeemomo. Nsu ɔƒɛni búmomo na búnwini bekyuli bani mbo ɔyikun. 6Ka búsie bútélie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ ni, Egyipteƒuɔ bammɔ bábla-bu kalala na bénye-bu lɛlɔ ka butaabla kabla teete-ma. 7Amu na búwulo bɔ́kpali Unwoti ɔni ndi bula bati kuuku Katɔti ka ubo ubebunku-bu. Na sɔsɔ ni, únu bula bɔkpali na ɔ́nu bula lɛbibo ku kalala kani kemmo bɔkya. 8Na ɔkɛnku nwuna ɔyikun ku ɔlɔkplu kemmo na ɔ́ƒɔ-bu ɔ́lɛku Egyipteƒuɔ enu kemmo. Na ɔ́bla akɔla budie taatina lidu lidu. Na ɔ́ya na liƒu ala lidu lidu ébo-ma lɛlɔ. 9Amu na ɔ́ya na búbo búlie kalɔ kani egyiibi ntu mɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii mɛni lɛlɔ. 10Anwuɔsu líti mina edula edeedi ani na Katɔti úti úte-mi mɛni muuboku-nwu.”
Na si ásu lɛni áwɔlɔ ni, na eti kagyigyɛ kammɔ ese bula Unwoti Katɔti anumi na emwi-nwu.
11Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, awɔ ku Lewiƒuɔ ku bekyuli bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ bɛkɛ ebiti na lɛla libendi lɛni na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́bla úte awɔ ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli ɔsu.
12Na lɛkwa lɛtɛdi biala kemmo ni, biti bina edula lɛkpa leevudi bite Lewiƒuɔ ku bekyuli bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele kalɛ na bakɛ badi na bemo na bina lɛma kemmo. 13Ɔmmɔ kama na asu anini, “Mina ala lɛkpa leevudi lɛni na lídie líse sɛsɛɛ líte awɔ mina Katɔti ni, ntada ntese mina kaduli. Mmomu líti ala ammɔ ƒui líboku Lewiƒuɔ ku bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele aani kalɛ na ébo-mii ɔda anii mbla. Na ntata ntenye iye lɛ́yiƒala ƒula ɔda bubo bɔni ndanku ala lɛkpa leevudi bute lɛlɔ.”
14Na asɔ asu anini, “Ńtadi ala ammɔ adi uwi ɔni mɔɔbla kekwa iye lídie ɔdi uwi ɔni na liiise sɛɛn iye líti ɔdi líte ukpine ɔdi. Mmomu lɛ́di mina Unwoti Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ. Na lɛ́bla lɛ́siaku ala ani ƒui na ásu-mi anii mbla na ala lɛkpa leevudi lɛlɔ. 15Anwuɔsu, Katɔti, nwini anumi na anu-mi asiku katɔ ƒula keliekɔ kedee kesii kani na elie mmɔ. Na ete ƒula bekyuli Israelƒuɔ kusɛ kusɛ na ete kalɔ kani na éti éte-bu mmɔ lɛnɔ kusɛ kusɛ aani kalɛ na ése kenye éte bula bati kuuku, kalɔ kani egyiibi ntu mɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii mmɔ.”
Bɛdi Katɔti Bekyuli Geen
16Ɔmwi kadi ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti uubó-mii ɔda ɔnii bɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo ƒui lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu biti bina kɔyu ku kayi ƒui bɛdi-mu lɛlɔ sɔsɔ. 17Na ɔmwi ni, bɛ́lɛ ugyii ka Unwoti ndi bina Katɔti, na bíse kenye ka bɛdubunu-nwu litemi na bɛdubɔdi nwuna ɔda bubo ƒui lɛlɔ, na lɛla biala wasu-mii ni, bɛdubuti-ni. 18Na ɔmwi kadi ni, Unwoti lɛnɔ ɔ́lɛ ugyii ka bɛdi nwuna bekyuli aani kalɛ na ɔ́su úse. Na ɔɔsu-mii ɔnii bɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo ƒui lɛlɔ. 19Na ɔdubɔya na bɛyu ɔkplu bitulo bekyuli bani ƒui nkya kayawi. Na amii ndubuti ɔbu ku bumwi bite nwuna lɛnyi. Na bɛdubɔbla bekyuli kedee bite bina Unwoti Katɔti aani kalɛ na ɔ́su úse.

english_text:
Build an Altar on Mount Ebal
1Moses stood together with the leaders and told the people of Israel:
Obey all the laws and teachings that I am giving you today. 2-4 Soon you will enter the land that the Lord your God is giving to you. He is the God your ancestors worshiped, and he has promised that this land is rich with milk and honey.
After you cross the Jordan River, go to Mount Ebal. Set up large slabs of stone, then cover them with white plaster and write on them a copy of these laws.
5 At this same place, build an altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God. But don't use stones that have been cut with iron tools. 6Look for stones that can be used without being cut. Then offer sacrifices to please the Lord, burning them completely on the altar. 7Next, offer sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing, and serve the meat at a sacred meal where you will celebrate in honor of the Lord.
8Don't forget to write out a copy of these laws on the stone slabs that you are going to set up. Make sure that the writing is easy to read.
Curses on Those Who Disobey
9Moses stood together with the priests and said, “Israel, be quiet and listen to me! Today you have become the people of the Lord your God. 10So you must obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you.”
11That same day, Moses gave them the following instructions:
12-13 After you cross the Jordan River, you will go to Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. The tribes of Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin will go up on Mount Gerizim, where they will bless the people of Israel. The tribes of Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali will go up on Mount Ebal where they will agree to the curses.
14-26 The people of the Levi tribe will speak each curse in a loud voice, then the rest of the people will agree to that curse by saying, “Amen!” Here are the curses:
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who makes an idol or worships idols, even secretly. The Lord is disgusted with idols.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on all who do not show respect for their father and mother.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who moves the rocks that mark property lines.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who tells blind people to go the wrong way.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who keeps the poor from getting justice, whether these poor are foreigners, widows, or orphans.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on any man who sleeps with his father's wife; that man has shown no respect for his father's marriage.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who has sex with an animal.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on any man who sleeps with his sister or his half sister or his mother-in-law.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who commits murder, even when there are no witnesses to the crime.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who accepts money to murder an innocent victim.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who refuses to obey his laws.
And so, to each of these curses, the people will answer, “Amen!”
translation_text:
Binweni Ɔda Bubo Etemila Ammɔ Bɛsia Atabi Lɛlɔ
1Amu na Mose ku Israelƒuɔ ɔma batɔnkune bammɔ ƒui básu bekyuli bammɔ banini, “Bɛdi ɔda bubo etemila ani búti buute-mii ɔmwi mɛni ƒui lɛlɔ. 2Na limeyi lɛni na bɛdubɔvia Yordan Ketu na bisie bitéduo kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti uute-mii mɛni lɛlɔ ni, bɛwia atabi bonwu bonwu na bɛkwaa-nya lɛlɔ ku uƒi. 3Na binweni etemila ani ƒui na nwuna ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔdanku bɛsia-nya lɛlɔ nwaa si uwi ɔni na bɛ́via na bɛdubo buduo kalɔ kani egyiibi ntu mɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii, na bina bati kuuku Katɔti úse kenye ka weti wete-mii kemmo. 4Na si uwi ɔni na bɛ́via Yordan Ketu kammɔ ni, na bɛtɛ atabi ammɔ bise Ebal Kɔbi lɛlɔ aani kalɛ kani na buubó-mii ɔda ɔmwi mɛni. Na bɛnu ka bɛ́kwaa atabi ammɔ lɛlɔ ku uƒi. 5Na bɛtu Katɔti lɛkpabi bɛlɛ mmɔ bite bina Unwoti Katɔti, na biti atabi bɛtu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ. Na biteti lɛbuala lɛdi bitamana-nwu lɛlɔ. 6Biti atabi ani na bátanwi na bɛtu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ bite bina Unwoti Katɔti, na bitaabla akpala teete-nwu. 7Na bitaabla unwi bɔbla akpala na mmɔ na bitaadi unwi bɔbla akpala adila na bitaakɛ kubiti na bina Unwoti Katɔti anumi na mmɔ. 8Na binweni etemila ani ƒui na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔdanku bɛsia atabi ani na bɛ́tɛ mmɔ lɛlɔ nwaa.”
Ewida Adi Adubɔsi Ebal Kɔbi Lɛlɔ
9Amu na Mose ku Katɔti bakpane bani ndi Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ básu Israelƒuɔ banini, “Bɛba lɛsɛ na bise atu! Ɔƒɛni ni, bínwini bina Unwoti Katɔti bekyuli. 10Anwuɔsu binu-nwu litemi na bɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui na úti uute-mii ɔmwi mɛni lɛlɔ.”
11Limeyi lɛmmɔ kani na Mose úbo bekyuli bammɔ ɔda ɔnini, 12“Si bɛ́via Yordan Ketu ni, adua ani bekyuli ndubunye Gerisim Kɔbi lɛlɔ na bete Israelƒuɔ kusɛ kusɛ anyi ndi Simeon ku Lewi ku Yuda ku Isakar ku Yoseƒ ku Benyamin. 13Na adua ani bekyuli ndubunye Ebal Kɔbi lɛlɔ na benu kalɛ na Katɔti uuwida bekyuli ndi Ruben ku Gad ku Aser ku Sebulon ku Dan ku Naƒtali.
14“Na Lewiƒuɔ ndubɔva momoomo basu Israel bekyuli ƒui banini,
15“ ‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni nánwi iye ɔ́vɔ baƒiɔ badi na úti ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni muusé Unwoti lɛlɔ. Ɔsika lɛla ndi lɛla lɛni udu na ukyuli úti nwuna kɔnu ɔ́bla úse úte lɛlɔ na bɔbɛ kemmo ni, ɔ́ƒiɔ Katɔti.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli bammɔ ƒui basu banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
16‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni naaabu ɔti iye uni.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli ƒui batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
17‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni mavumana ɔkpanadi ɔmii.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna basu banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
18‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni mɔɔtɔnku ɔnumbwɛne kalɛ na ɔyii ulu.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
19‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnya bekyuli bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ ku bekpinebi ku bekpinele taakya.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
20‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni na anwu ku ɔti ulekudi baatɛ. Ɔsika ɔ́ya na ɔti katɛnkɔ keesé lɛlɔ.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
21‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni na anwu ku ebuo baatɛ.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
22‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni na anwu ku ɔnwani ulekubi iye ɔtibi iye unibi baatɛ.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
23‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni na anwu ku nwuna uleni baatɛ.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
24‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni ndubɔbɛ ɔdu ukyuli.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
25‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni maƒɔ egulabi adi na badu ukyuli ɔni nátaƒiɔ.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’
26‘Ewida asiaku ukyuli ɔni naaadi Katɔti ɔda bubo ku nwuna ala bɔtina ƒui lɛlɔ.’
Na ɔlɛka bekyuli batuna banii, ‘Ɔsia lɛni.’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
Moses said to Israel:
1-2 Today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. Always obey them, and the Lord will make Israel the most famous and important nation on earth, and he will bless you in many ways.
3The Lord will make your businesses and your farms successful.
4You will have many children. You will harvest large crops, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats will produce many young.
5You will have plenty of bread to eat.
6The Lord will make you successful in your daily work.
7The Lord will help you defeat your enemies and make them scatter in all directions.
8The Lord your God is giving you the land, and he will make sure you are successful in everything you do. Your harvests will be so large that your storehouses will be full.
9If you follow and obey the Lord, he will make you his own special people, just as he promised. 10Then everyone on earth will know that you belong to the Lord, and they will be afraid of you.
11The Lord will give you a lot of children and make sure that your animals give birth to many young. The Lord promised your ancestors that this land would be yours, and he will make it produce large crops for you.
12The Lord will open the storehouses of the skies where he keeps the rain, and he will send rain on your land at just the right times. He will make you successful in everything you do. You will have plenty of money to lend to other nations, but you won't need to borrow any yourself.
13Obey the laws and teachings that I'm giving you today, and the Lord your God will make Israel a leader among the nations, and not a follower. Israel will be wealthy and powerful, not poor and weak. 14But you must not reject any of his laws and teachings or worship other gods.
The Lord Will Put Curses on You if You Disobey
(Leviticus 26.14-46)
Moses said:
15Israel, today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. And if you don't obey them all, he will put many curses on you.
16Your businesses and farms will fail.
17You won't have enough bread to eat.
18You'll have only a few children, your crops will be small, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats won't produce many young.
19The Lord will make you fail in everything you do.
20No matter what you try to accomplish, the Lord will confuse you, and you will feel his anger. You won't last long, and you may even meet with disaster, all because you rejected the Lord.
21-23The Lord will send terrible diseases to attack you, and you will never be well again. You will suffer with burning fever and swelling and pain until you die somewhere in the land that you captured.
The Lord will make the sky overhead seem like a bronze roof that keeps out the rain, and the ground under your feet will become as hard as iron. Your crops will be scorched by the hot east wind or ruined by mildew. 24He will send dust and sandstorms instead of rain, and you will be wiped out.
25The Lord will let you be defeated by your enemies, and you will scatter in all directions. You will be a horrible sight for the other nations to see, 26and no one will disturb the birds and wild animals while they eat your dead bodies.
27The Lord will make you suffer with diseases that will cause oozing sores or crusty itchy patches on your skin or boils like the ones that are common in Egypt. And there will be no cure for you! 28You will become insane and go blind. The Lord will make you so confused, 29that even in bright sunshine you will have to feel your way around like a blind person, who cannot tell day from night. For the rest of your life, people will beat and rob you, and no one will be able to stop them.
30A man will be engaged to a woman, but before they can get married, she will be raped by enemy soldiers. Some of you will build houses, but never get to live in them. If you plant a vineyard, you won't be around long enough to enjoy the first harvest. 31Your cattle will be killed while you watch, but you won't get to eat any of the meat. Your donkeys and sheep will be stolen from you, and no one will be around to force your enemies to give them back. 32Your sons and daughters will be dragged off to a foreign country, while you stand there helpless. And even if you watch for them until you go blind, you will never see them again.
33You will work hard on your farms, but everything you harvest will be eaten by foreigners, who will mistreat you and abuse you for the rest of your life.
34What you see will be so horrible that you will go insane, 35and the Lord will punish you from head to toe with boils that never heal.
36The Lord will let you and your king be taken captive to a country that you and your ancestors have never even heard of, and there you will have to worship idols made of wood and stone. 37People of nearby countries will shudder when they see your terrible troubles, but they will still make fun of you.
38You will plant a lot of seed, but gather a small harvest, because locusts will eat your crops. 39You will plant vineyards and work hard at taking care of them, but you won't gather any grapes, much less get any wine, because the vines themselves will be eaten by worms. 40Even if your olive trees grow everywhere in your country, the olives will fall off before they are ready, and there won't be enough olive oil for combing your hair.
41Even your children will be taken as prisoners of war.
42Locusts will eat your crops and strip your trees of leaves and fruit.
43Foreigners in your towns will become wealthy and powerful, while you become poor and powerless. 44You will be so short of money that you will have to borrow from those foreigners. They will be the leaders in the community, and you will be the followers.
More Curses for Disobedience
Moses said:
45Israel, if you don't obey the laws and teachings that the Lord your God is giving you, he will send these curses to chase, attack, and destroy you. 46Then everyone will look at you and your descendants and realize that the Lord has placed you under a curse.
47If the Lord makes you wealthy, but you don't joyfully worship and honor him, 48he will send enemies to attack you and make you their slaves. Then you will live in poverty with nothing to eat, drink, or wear, and your owners will work you to death.
49Foreigners who speak a strange language will be sent to attack you without warning, just like an eagle swooping down. 50They won't show any mercy, and they will have no respect for old people or pity for children. 51They will take your cattle, sheep, goats, grain, wine, and olive oil, then leave you to starve.
52All over the land that the Lord your God gave you, the enemy army will surround your towns. You may feel safe inside your town walls, but the enemy will tear them down, 53while you wait in horror. Finally, you will get so hungry that you will eat the sons and daughters that the Lord gave you. 54-55Because of hunger, a man who had been gentle and kind will eat his own children and refuse to share the meal with his brother or wife or with his other children. 56-57 A woman may have grown up in such luxury that she never had to put a foot on the ground. But times will be so bad that she will secretly eat both her newborn baby and the afterbirth, without sharing any with her husband or her other children.
Disobedience Brings Destruction
Moses said to Israel:
58You must obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Because if you don't respect the Lord, 59he will punish you and your descendants with incurable diseases, 60like those you were so afraid of in Egypt. 61Remember! If the Lord decides to destroy your nation, he can use any disease or disaster, not just the ones written in The Book of God's Law.
62There are as many of you now as the stars in the sky, but if you disobey the Lord your God, only a few of you will be left. 63The Lord is happy to make you successful and to help your nation grow while you conquer the land. But if you disobey him, he will be just as happy to pull you up by your roots.
64Those of you that survive will be scattered to every nation on earth, and you will have to worship stone and wood idols that never helped you or your ancestors. 65You will be restless—always longing for home, but never able to return. 66You will live in constant fear of death. 67Each morning you will wake up to such terrible sights that you will say, “I wish it were night!” But at night you will be terrified and say, “I wish it were day!”
68I told you never to go back to Egypt. But now the Lord himself will load you on ships and send you back. Then you will even try to sell yourselves as slaves, but no one will be interested.
translation_text:
Katɔti Ɔdubute Israelƒuɔ Kusɛ Kusɛ Si Beenú-nwu Litemi
1Si bɛɛdi bina Unwoti Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ kaduɛ na bɛɛsiaku nwuna ɔda ɔni na uubó-mii ɔmwi mɛni kama ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubɔtalaku-mii katɔ utulo bekyuli bani ƒui nkya kayawi. 2Na kusɛ kusɛ ɔmɛni ɔdubɔsiaku-mii si biinú bina Unwoti Katɔti litemi. 3Unwoti ɔdubutemi-mii kusɛ kusɛ na bina lɛma ku bina mmo.
4Unwoti ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na bɛwɔ bebi pii na bɛkɛ edula pii lɛnɔ. Na ɔdubɔya na bɛkɛ ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu pii.
5Unwoti ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na bina edula ani bɛ́va adia kaduɛ na adila ani na bɛdubuti edula ammɔ bɛnwa lɛnɔ eƒu na emomo.
6Na Unwoti ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na lɛla biala na bɛɛbla kemmo.
7Na Unwoti ɔdubɔdi bina bekisine lɛlɔ ute-mii si bata banii bebekpoku-mii. Bekisine bammɔ badubɔsia ulu unwi bebo, nsu badubɔsia lilu maatɛ lɛlɔ bekeli.
8Unwoti ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na bina kabla kani bɛɛbla kemmo. Na ɔdubɔya na bina linwu liyi ku bina edula ani na bɛdubɔƒɛ. Na ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na kalɔ kani na úti uute-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ.
9Si biinú bina Unwoti Katɔti litemi na bɛɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ƒui ni, ɔdubuti-mii ɔbla nwuna bekyuli aani kalɛ na ɔ́su. 10Na kayawi bekyuli ƒui badubɔnu bɔti ka Unwoti náƒuna-mii ɔ́bla anwu ɔlati bekyuli. Ɔmɛni ɔsu badubutaayia-mii. 11Unwoti ɔdubɔya na bɛwɔ bebi pii na bɛkɛ ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku edula pii na kalɔ kani na úti uute-mii mɛni lɛlɔ. Na aka na ɔ́su úse ka weti wete bina bati kuuku.
12Na Unwoti ɔdubɔlɛmi Katɔ kesii kani na ntu bɔ́bu bɔkya na ɔya na ɔnantu utaana teewi bina kalɔ lɛlɔ na nwuna uwi lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na bina kabla kadia. Na amii bɛdubute kadi pii kevonkɔ. Nsu amii bilésie bilatáwia kevonkɔ kadi na bana kudɔ. 13Si bɛɛdi Unwoti ɔda ɔni na úbo-mii mɛni lɛlɔ na bɛɛsia-mu anu kaduɛ ni, ɔdubɔya na bɛdi lili na biladi ɔka kudii. Na lɛla biala kemmo bɛdubo bɔbla udeedi na bilabla ukplodi. 14Na ɔda ɔni na uubó-mii ɔmwi mɛni ni, ɔdi utada utavia utesie kɔdianu iye kɔmii na utákpa baƒiɔ badi.
Ewida Adubɔsiaku-mii Si Bítadi Ɔda Bubo Bɔmmɔ Lɛlɔ
15Nsu si bítadi ɔda bubo bɔni na muute-mii ɔmwi mɛni lɛlɔ na bítasia nwuna ala ani na ɔ́tina-mii anu kpakplaa ni, ewida amɛni ndubo-mii lɛlɔ.
16Unwoti ɔdubo bina lɛma ku bina mmo buwida. 17Unwoti ɔdubo bina edula ani bɛ́va ku adila ani bɛ́nwa bise buwida.
18Unwoti ɔdubo-mii buwida na bilawɔ bebi pii, na bina edula lɛnɔ aaadubo bɔdia, na bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu belemomo.
19Unwoti ɔdubo bina lɛla biala na bɛdubɔbla buwida.
20Na si bɛ́bla likpidi na bíni bina Unwoti ni, ɔdubuti ala ani na aadu kɔnyana geen na ese basa basa uboku-mii lɛlɔ. Na ala ani muukpóku ukyuli kani ndubo buteebo-mii lɛlɔ úti útédu ka ɔ́yila-mii udu ƒui. 21Na ɔdubuti lɛlɛ lidu lidu uboku-mii lɛlɔ uti utédu ka ɔdi biala ɔsɔ uuuli ngba na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bísela bitélie mmɔ lɛlɔ. 22Unwoti ɔdubuti lɛlɛ kpakplaa ukpoku-mii. Na ɔdubɔya na eƒula eteeƒu-mii na lɛlɔ bɔbi lɛnɔ buteekpoku-mii. Na ɔdubɔya na kaƒɛndi kekpidi kataalɛ, na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ukpidi uteekpo kalɛ na ubie bina edula. Na ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni ɔdubɔkya-mii akɔ uti utédu ka bina ƒui bíkpi. 23Ɔnantu lɛnɔ ulana na bina kalɔ kadubɔyu ɔkplu aani lɛbuala kalɛ. 24Uwi ɔni na binye bɛɛnu ɔnantu anumi ni, Unwoti ɔdubuti ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ku kɔnwinimi uyile kayaa uti utédu ka ɔyila-mii udu ƒui.
25Unwoti ɔdubɔya na bina bekisine badi-mii lɛlɔ. Na bɛdubɔsia ulu unwi bɛnii bitékpoku-ma, nsu bɛdubɔsia lilu maatɛ lɛlɔ bikeli bɛtɔlɔ. Na si ɔmɛni udu ɔ́lɛ lɛni ni, ɔdubɔbla kayawi bekyuli ƒui kalɛ kadi. Na badubuye lɛlɔ ka bi mɔɔlɛ́ na bina lɛlɔ mɛni. 26Na si bíkpi ni, baasɛ ku bebuo ndubo bina lɛna bɔkun. Na lɛla biala liiibo na lɛbɔku-ma. 27Unwoti ɔdubɔya na eƒula eteeƒu-mii aani kalɛ na ɔ́ya na éƒu Egyipteƒuɔ úbavi. Na ɔdubɔya na bina ɔlɔna utaabla alɛbi na ulie ntu na utaadu-mii. Nsu kuvo kɔdi kuuubo kɔni mabwi-mii. 28Unwoti ɔdubɔya na biteekpi libuo na kasusu keteeƒu-mii na anumi ataabuɛ-mii. 29Na ɔƒiiwi bɛduti bina enu bitaawia ala taanɔ aani banumbwɛne kalɛ. Na lɛla biala bɛdubɔbla limeyi ndi limeyi ni, lilatɛ lilete-mii. Bɛdubo abi bubo na bekyuli beteekpeli bina ala taaƒɔ, nsu ukyuli biala uuubo na ukpo ute-mii.
30Bɛdubɔnu beleku na bɛbla-ma elila, nsu banana bamba ndubukpeli-ma bɔƒɔ na beti-ma beti. Bɛdubɔtu lɛtɔ, nsu bilelie-ni kemmo. Bɛdubɔbla adingyii mmo, nsu bilákɛ egyiibi ammɔ biladi. 31Bekyuli badubɔdu bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ na bina anumi, nsu bilákɛ bana lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛdi bilakun. Na bekyuli badubuti bina bapɔnkɔ wɛlɛ wɛlɛ batɔlɔku na bina anumi. Nu basɔ beleti-ma beleboku. Na bina bekisine badubo bebeti bina baƒonu batɔlɔku, nsu ukyuli biala uuubo na ukpo ute-mii. 32Bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ badubo bebeti bina bebi bananabi ku belekubi batɔlɔku na bina anumi na batátaabla-ma kabla. Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, bɛdubɔnu-ma anumi ka benwini bebo, nsu keeke. 33Na ɔgyu kakaaka kadi bekyuli badubo na babaƒɛ bina edula ani bíbo abi bɛ́va batɔlɔku, nsu baaadubo-mii kayu kadi bɔƒɔ. Lɛbibo kama lɛbibo na bɛdubɔnu. 34Na lɛbibo lɛdubɔya na bina kasusu keƒu-mii. 35Na Unwoti ɔdubɔya na ekpegyiibi alɛ-mii lɛgba, nsu bilákɛ-nya kuvo. Na alɛbi ku eƒula adubɔsia-mii ɔ́si bina lili úti útédu bina lɛgba lɛlɔ.
36Na Unwoti ɔdubɔya na bekyuli bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ beƒie amii ku bina ɔga batɔlɔku besienku kalɔ bamba lɛlɔ kesii kani na amii iye bina bati kuuku bételie kudii na bitélie mmɔ. Na mmɔ na bɛdubɔkpa baƒiɔ bani béti ligyii ku atabi bánwi. 37Unwoti ɔdubugyingya-mii ɔkya kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubɔbla kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ bekyuli dɛye dɛye na beye banii bi ɔsu na ɔ́lɛku-mii lɛni. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu badubɔma-mii.
38Na bɛdubɔva edula pii, nsu blii suɛ kani na bɛdubo bɔƒɛ. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubɔya na baalɔlɔ bebebile-nya evete ammɔ. 39Na bɛdubɔtuma adingyii mmo na biwi lɛlɔ bɛnu-nya lɛlɔ kaduɛ. Nsu bilákɛ-nya ebi bilala iye bɛkɛ ebi ammɔ adi bɛbla ntɛ. Ɔsika beklubi badubuduo egyiibi ammɔ kemmo. 40Nnɔ egyii adubɔkwɛ bina kalɔ kesi kesii, nsu bɛɛɛdubo nnɔ biala bɔkɛ bɔsiku-ni kemmo. Ɔsika nnɔ ebi ammɔ adubɔnu ebie ewi kalɔ. 41Bɛdubɔkɛ bebi bananabi ku belekubi pii, nsu bilákɛ-ma kɔsia kɔdi. Ɔsika bekyuli bamba badubo bebekpoku-mii na beƒie-ma batɔlɔku. 42Na baalɔlɔ yuu badubo bina egyii ku edula bubile.
43Na bekyuli bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ na bakya-mii akɔ badubo katɔ butaakɔ, nsu amii bɛdubo kalɔ butaayu. 44Na ama ndubo-mii kevonkɔ bute, nsu ama belévo lɛla lɛdi na bina kudɔ. Na kawɔlɔkɔ ni, ama ndubo-mii lɛlɔ bɔdi.
45Lɛbibo lɛmɛni ndubo-mii lɛlɔ buteebo na eteekpoku-mii úti útédu ka bina ƒui bɛ́yii udu. Ɔsika bítenu bina Unwoti Katɔti litemi na bítadi nwuna ala bɔtina lɛlɔ. 46Na ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni ndubɔbla likposela ku akɔla budie taatina bɔni ndubo buse bute amii ku bina bawɔ. 47Ɔsika bítemwi bina Unwoti Katɔti ku ebiti ku lɛlɔyɔ na bina lɛkɛ kemmo. 48Anwuɔsu kɔka ku utukwɛ ku kɔwaba bonwu kɔdubɔda-mii na bɛkɛ ku kasɔngya bitaabla kabla teete bina bekisine bani enu kemmo na Unwoti ɔdubuti-mii ɔ́kya. Na Unwoti ɔdubɔya na bibo abi laa wetédu ka bina ƒui bíkpi bɛ́yii udu.
49Na Unwoti ɔdubɔya na kadi bamba bekyuli bani na si bátɛmi na bilénu kalɔ basi ɔgyu kakaaka bada balɛ-mii lɛlɔ kɔnakunwi aani kalɛ na kasangbii kaayu teeƒie lɛkɔkɔbi kalɛ. 50Na bekyuli bammɔ badubɔbla lili ɔkplu na balanu ukyuli biala kɔnyana, unengu ɔdi o-o iye ɔnamu ɔdi o-o, balanu-nwu kɔnyana. 51Na bekyuli bammɔ badubo bina edula bɔdi na badu bina bebuo bakun ƒui na kɔka kɔda-mii kaduɛ úti útédu ka bíkpi bɛ́sa ƒui. Na bekyuli bammɔ baaadubo edula iye ntɛ iye nnɔ iye ɔmantɛ bakɔ iye baƒonu badi bɔda buse-mii. Badubɔkyula ala ammɔ ƒui kede kede na bikpi bɛsa. 52Na bekyuli bammɔ badubo bebekpoku bina lɛma lɛni ƒui bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo buti bute-mii. Na bina awodu ani na bɛ́tu bínyene ƒui na anya na bɛ́sia anu na kekpo uwi adubo bɔƒɛ.
53Na kalala kani na bina bekisine bammɔ badubo-mii bɔbla si báda-mii bákya uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔsu ni, bɛdubo bina bebi bananabi ku belekubi bani na bina Unwoti Katɔti úte-mii bɔdu bɔkun. 54Ina ukyuli ɔni nse buɛɛ iye ubo kasusu geen ulanu ɔwani iye ulekudi ɔni na ɔɔyɔ́ geen iye nwuna bebi bani nébu kɔnyana. 55Na ubidi lɛna lɛni na ɔ́kɛ ɔɔkun mmɔ ni, ulete bana akɔ bani nébu lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛdi ɔnii ɔkun. 56-57Na uleku ɔni nse buɛɛ na ubo kasusu geen na ubo akɛla ɔsu na ulesie kesi kesii muedi ni, si bina bekisine bammɔ báda bálɛ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, anumi adubugyie uleku ɔmmɔ na adila lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubo bɔbɛ na ɔdu ubidi ɔni na ɔ́wɔ ɔkun ku awɔla ammɔ. Na ulete ɔgyani ɔni na ɔɔyɔ́ iye ubidi bamba lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛdi ɔnii ɔkun.
58Na si bítewi lɛlɔ na bɛdi ɔda bubo ala bɔtina bɔni bénweni bákya ɔku ɔmɛni kemmo na biti ɔbu unengudi ɔni na bɔyia bɔkya-nwu kemmo bite bina Unwoti Katɔti ni, 59Unwoti ɔdubuti lɛlɛ lidu lidu lɛni mɔɔví bekyuli na ukyuli biala ulakana-ni bɔbwi uboku amii ku bina bawɔ lɛlɔ. 60Na ɔdubɔya na lɛlɛ likpidi lɛni ƒui na ɔ́ya na líbo Egyipteƒuɔ lɛlɔ uwi ɔni na bɛ́kya Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na bɛ́yia geen mmɔ libo-mii lɛlɔ na ɔdi ulákɛ-nwu kuvo. 61Na ɔdubɔya na lɛlɛ lidu lidu lɛni mɔɔví bekyuli na batalɔ-ni anyi bátakya Katɔti ɔda bubo ɔku ɔmɛni kemmo libo-mii lɛlɔ na bikpi bɛyii udu. 62Na ina ka bimomo aani katɔ ayabi kalɛ ni, bɛdubɔsa bɛbla blii suɛ, ɔsika bítenu bina Unwoti Katɔti litemi. 63Kalɛ kani na ɔ́yɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ na ɔbla-mii lɛƒɔndia na bímomo bíbu ni, lɛni kani na ɔdubɔyɔ-nwu kaƒɔ ka ɔyila-mii udu na bina lɛma lɛbla kuliekɔ kukpludi. Na ɔda-mii udie kalɔ kani na nka bísela bitéti binwini bina kadikɔ na bilie mmɔ lɛlɔ.
64Bina Unwoti ɔdubɔya na bigyingya bɛkya kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Mmɔ na bɛdubo baƒiɔ bani na béti egyii ku atabi bánwi bɔkpa, baƒiɔ bani na bina bati kuuku bátakpa kudii. 65Na kadi bamba bekyuli bammɔ akɔ ni, bɛɛɛdubo bɔkɛ atubɔyɔ, na ɔdi ulalɔ-mii lɛnyi lɛbuni lɛdi. Na bina Unwoti ɔdubɔya na ɔtɔtɔ utaagyu-mii na binwini bekyuli bani neeebo kɔsia kɔdi na biteewulo kɔnyana na bina kɔyi kemmo. 66Na uwi biala ni, bina ngba bɔdubɔkya ɔgbankpi kemmo usien ku ɔƒɛ. Na bɛdubo butaayia uwi ndi uwi ka badubo-mii bɔdu. 67Bina kayi kadubo buyi ku liƒu. Na lɛla biala bɛdubɔnu ni, lɛdubo-mii liƒu bɔda. Na si kadi kégye ni, bɛdubuye bɛnii uwi ɔmani na kadi kadubɔsa. Na si kása lɛnɔ ni, bɛdubuye bɛnii uwi ɔmani na kadubugye. 68Na bina Unwoti ɔdubuti lɛkɔlɔ libendi libendi na uti-mii ɔkya-ni kemmo na unwini-mii usienku Egyipte kalɔ kesii kani na ɔ́su ka bɛsɔ bilésie kudii. Na si bíduo mmɔ ni, bɛdubuti lɛlɔ biye bite Egyipte kalɔƒuɔ bammɔ na bitaabla kabla teete-ma. Nsu ukyuli biala uláyɔ ka uye-mii.

english_text:
The Agreement in Moab
1So Moses finished telling the Israelites what they had to do in order to keep the agreement the Lord was making with them in Moab, which was in addition to the one the Lord had made with them at Mount Sinai.
The Third Speech: Israel Must Keep Its Agreement with the Lord
The Lord Is Your God
2-3Moses called the nation of Israel together and told them:
When you were in Egypt, you saw the Lord perform great miracles that caused trouble for the king, his officials, and everyone else in the country. 4-6He has even told you, “For 40 years I, the Lord, led you through the desert, but your clothes and your sandals didn't wear out, and I gave you special food. I did these things so you would realize that I am your God.”
But the Lord must give you a change of heart before you truly understand what you have seen and heard.
7 When we first camped here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan attacked, but we defeated them. 8 Then we captured their land and divided it among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
Keep the Agreement
Moses said:
9Israel, the Lord has made an agreement with you, and if you keep your part, you will be successful in everything you do. 10-12Today everyone in our nation is standing here in the Lord's presence, including leaders and officials, parents and children, and even those foreigners who cut wood and carry water for us. We are at this place of worship to promise that we will keep our part of the agreement with the Lord our God.
13-15In this agreement, the Lord promised that you would be his people and that he would be your God. He first made this promise to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and today the Lord is making this same promise to you. But it isn't just for you; it is also for your descendants.
16-17When we lived in Egypt, you saw the Egyptians worship disgusting idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. Then as we traveled through other nations, you saw those people worship other disgusting idols. 18 So make sure that everyone in your tribe remains faithful to the Lord and never starts worshiping gods of other nations.
If even one of you worships idols, you will be like the root of a plant that produces bitter, poisonous fruit. 19You may be an Israelite and know all about the Lord's agreement with us, but he won't bless you if you rebel against him. You may think you can get away with it, but you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you. 20-21The Lord will be furious, and instead of forgiving you, he will separate you from the other tribes. Then he will destroy you, by piling on you all the curses in The Book of God's Law, and you will be forgotten forever.
22The Lord will strike your country with diseases and disasters. Your descendants and foreigners from distant countries will see that your land 23 has become a scorching desert of salt and sulfur, where nothing is planted, nothing sprouts, and nothing grows. It will be as lifeless as the land around the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, after the Lord became angry and destroyed them.
24People from other nations will ask, “Why did the Lord destroy this country? Why was he so furious?”
25And they will be given this answer:
Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, but after he brought them out of Egypt and made an agreement with them, they rejected the agreement 26and decided to worship gods that had never helped them. The Lord had forbidden Israel to worship these gods, 27-28and so he became furious and punished the land with all the curses in The Book of God's Law. Then he pulled up Israel by the roots and tossed them into a foreign country, where they still are today.
29The Lord our God hasn't explained the present or the future, but he has commanded us to obey the laws he gave to us and our descendants.
translation_text:
Katɔti Bunyimi Bɔni Na Ɔ́sɔ Únyimi Ku Israelƒuɔ
1Bunyimi bɔmɛni na Katɔti úbo Mose ɔda ka unyimi ku Israelƒuɔ na uwi ɔni bákya Moabƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na úti-mu úbunku bunyimi bɔni na únyimiku-ma uwi ɔni na bákya Sinai kɔbi lɛlɔ.
2Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Mose ɔ́lɔ Israelƒuɔ ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ala amɛni.
Amii alati bɛ́nu ku bina anumi ala ani na Unwoti ɔ́bla Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ku nwuna kabla bablane ku ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui bekyuli. 3Na bɛ́nu Unwoti ɔyikun bonwu ɔni na údie keyi na ala ebendi ku akɔla budie taatina lidu lidu ani na ɔ́bla úti úkpoku-ma. 4Nsu úti úbedu ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ útaya na binu kalɔ iye bɛnu bɛti lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ala ammɔ álɛ lɛni. 5Na akwa aavlene kemmo ni, Unwoti ɔ́tɔnku-mii na kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ɔni na ukyuli ɔdi adala iye agbanvuo étebie. 6Na bɛɛɛda bodobodo iye ntɛ bɔdi, nsu Unwoti úte-mii ala ani ƒui bɛɛwia. Ɔ́bla lɛni úti ɔ́tina ka anwu ndi Katɔti.
7Na uwi ɔni búbedu kesii kani bɔkya mɛni ni, Ɔga Sihon ɔni nási Hesbon ku Ɔga Og ɔni nási Basan báta bébekpoku-bu. Nsu bɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ. 8Na búti bana kɔlɔ na búle kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ búte Ruben ku Gad kaba, na búti kakɛ lɛnɔ búte Manase kaba.
9Anwuɔsu bɛdi bunyimi bɔmɛni lɛlɔ kaduɛ kalɛ na lɛla biala bɛdubɔbla lɛtɛ lite-mii.
10-11Ɔmwi kadi ni, bina ƒui binye bina Unwoti Katɔti anumi, batɔnkune ku kabla bablane ku banana ku belekubi ƒui ku bina bebi ku bekyuli bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ na bakya-mii kudɔ na baadá bina egyii na beesié ketu teete-mi. 12Ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni ni, bina ƒui binye mɛni ka binu bunyimi bɔni na bina Unwoti Katɔti únyimiku-mii. Na bɛbla bɛsia lɛla biala na ɔ́su-mii lɛlɔ. 13Na Unwoti ɔlɛ-nwu ugyii ka bɛdi nwuna bekyuli. Na anwu lɛnɔ ɔbla bina Katɔti aani kalɛ na úse kenye úte amii ku bina bati kuuku bani ndi Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob. 14Na ɔɔɔdi amii lɛti kani na Unwoti únyimiku linyese lɛmɛni. 15Mmomu uunyimi-mu ku abu bani ƒui nnye-nwu anumi ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni ku bula bawɔ bani na bátawɔ tɔ lɛnɔ.
