4Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept. 5When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
6Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood.
Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
7Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said:
You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army. 8Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them. 9The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
10When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people.
Asa Dies
(1 Kings 15.23,24)
11Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 12In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help. 13He died two years later.
14Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_text:
Israel Ɔga Baasa Úkpo Yuda
1Na Asa lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa avlaatɛ-lɛkundi kemmo ni, Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Basa útátu awodu ɔ́mana Rama kalɛ na busie teetenku lɛlɔ bɔdi bɔsɔ bulakya ama ku Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Asa ku nwuna bekyuli ntɛ.
2Ka Asa únu ɔmɛni ni, úti sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ɔ́siku nwuna lɛgakadikɔ ku Unwoti kakpakɔ na úti úmene Aram Ɔga Benhadad na Damasko ɔnii batásu-nwu kenye kamɛni banini, 3“Mɔɔyɔ ka abu ku-ɔ bɔbla unwi aani kalɛ na ƒ'ɔti ku mina ɔti bábla unwi dii. Nu, líti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔmɛni muumene-ɔ, na ekulo unwi bɔbla bɔni nkya awɔ ku Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Basa ntɛ, na ɔda nwuna bekpone udie mina ɔmii lɛlɔ.”
4Benhadad ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni na Asa ɔ́su-nwu na úti Siriaƒuɔ bekpone úmene Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na bétékpo Iyon ku Dan ku Abel-Maim ku Neƒtali lɛma lɛni kemmo na baaklibi ala buse ƒui na béƒie-ni báƒɔ. 5Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Basa únu lɛla lɛni nálɛ ni, ɔ́da Rama bɔtu ɔ́ya na údie kabla kammɔ atu.
6Amu na Asa údie lɛdi úte ukyuli biala na ɔkya Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔnii beti atabi ku ligyii lɛni na Baasa ɔ́ya na béti bébewi Rama mmɔ ka batu bamana-nwu na ɔbla kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa mmɔ batɔlɔku mmɔ. Na ɔ́ya na béti atula ammɔ kani bátu bámana Geba ku Mispa.
Kenye Udiene Hanani Ɔ́du Ɔga Asa Kɔtɔ
7Na ala ammɔ bɔlɛ bɔwɔlɔ kama uwi klukwii ɔdi kama ni, Kenye Udiene Hanani úsie Asa kudɔ na útásu-nwu ɔnini, “Siriaƒuɔ ɔga lɛlɔ na éti ƒula anu ásia na ɔni na eti ƒula anu asia Unwoti ƒula Katɔti lɛlɔ? Ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, aaadubo bɔkana na adi Siriaƒuɔ bekpone lɛlɔ kudii. 8Nyimo Kus ku Libia bekpone kalɛ na bebo ɔkplu geen ku bana bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku bekpone bapɔnkɔ beliene bammɔ! Nsu ka éti ƒula anu ásia Unwoti lɛlɔ ka ubunku-ɔ na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔsu ni, ákana-ma lɛlɔ bɔdi. 9Unwoti ɔɔsia ukyuli biala anu uwi biala na uuti nwuna ɔyikun teete bani na béti bana anu básia-nwu lɛlɔ na basiaku-nwu kama siin uwi biala. Nsu kɔdɔlɔ lɛla na awɔ ábla mɛni. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu keyi buɛɛ kasɔ kaaadubo ƒula lɛgakadikɔ kammɔ bɔkya uwi ɔdi lɛnɔ.”
10Ka Asa únu lɛla lɛmɛni ni, úti kɔnyi geen na ɔ́ya na bákya Hanani aban ɔtɔ. Na lɛni kani na ɔ́bla anwu ɔlati nwuna bekyuli kalala.
Asa Úkpi
11Lɛla biala na Ɔga Asa ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-ni bákya Yudaƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ baga ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo. 12Na nwuna lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa avlaatɛ-yaalenwidi kemmo ni, Asa úbakɛ ɔgba ɔdi na ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́yu-nwu ɔkplu geen. Nsu nwuna anu ƒui ásia alakpi bablane lɛlɔ kani na ɔɔɔdi Unwoti ka ubunku-nwu. 13Na akwa anyɔ kama ni, úbekpi.
14Amu na asa na uwi ɔmɛni ubo lɛni ni, Ɔga Asa ɔ́ya na béku nwuna kaƒiɔtɔ bése na ɔdi atabi ubu ɔni na bédie na Yerusalem atakpɛ kɔbi kɔdi lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu mmɔ na báva-nwu. Na béti kesudi ku ugyulo nnɔmii ƒɛƒɛɛ bɔdi béwi kɔƒiɔtɔ kammɔ kemmo ƒui tɛɛ. Na bákyula likpose ekyweni livongu bonwu lɛdi béte-nwu na mmɔ béti bákɔliku-nwu lɛnyi katɔ.

english_text:
King Jehoshaphat of Judah
1Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king and strengthened his defenses against Israel. 2He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
3-4When Jehoshaphat's father had first become king of Judah, he was faithful to the Lord and refused to worship the god Baal as the kings of Israel did. Jehoshaphat followed his father's example and obeyed and worshiped the Lord. And so the Lord blessed Jehoshaphat 5and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected, 6he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
7In the third year of Jehoshaphat's rule, he chose five officials and gave them orders to teach the Lord's Law in every city and town in Judah. They were Benhail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah. 8Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along. 9They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
10The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat. 11Philistines brought him silver and other gifts to keep peace. Some of the Arab people brought him 7,700 rams and the same number of goats.
12As Jehoshaphat became more powerful, he built fortresses and cities 13where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers 14from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans.
Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had 300,000 soldiers under his command. 15Jehohanan was second in command, with 280,000 soldiers under him. 16Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with 200,000 soldiers under him.
17Eliada was a brave warrior who commanded the troops from Benjamin. He had 200,000 soldiers under his command, all of them armed with bows and shields. 18Jehozabad was second in command, with 180,000 soldiers under him. 19These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
translation_text:
Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Yehosaƒat Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ
1Ɔga Asa ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ banii Yehosaƒat nébenwini Yudaƒuɔ ɔga na ɔ́sɔku nwuna lɛgakadikɔ ɔyikun ɔ́bla ɔwɔdi kalɛ na benye basiaku Israelƒuɔ bukpoku biala kenye. 2Na úti bekpone úmene Yudaƒuɔ lɛma linengudi lɛni ndi bana kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa mmɔ kemmo ku lɛma bamba kemmo lɛnɔ úbunku lɛma lɛni nkya Eƒraim kalɛkɛ kani na ɔti Asa úkpo ɔƒɔ kemmo lɛnɔ.
3-4Uwi ɔni na Yehosaƒat ɔti úse kalɔ ku lɛga bɔdi na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, útaadi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ kaduɛ na úni na útakpa Baal baƒiɔ aani kalɛ na baga bani nágyu bátɔ-nwu bábla kalɛ. Na Yehosaƒat lɛnɔ úse kalɔ ɔsiku ɔti ɔbladu kama. Na útaabu Unwoti geen na ɔɔkpá-nwu lɛnɔ. Anwuɔsu úte-nwu kusɛ kusɛ 5na úbunku-nwu na ɔ́ya na ɔɔkana na ɔɔdi nwuna lɛgakadikɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ kaduɛ ku ɔyikun. Na Yuda kadi bekyuli bammɔ beeboku-nwu etela ɔni náya na úbenwini ɔlakɛne geen na beete-nwu ɔbu. 6Ɔ́siaku Unwoti kama siin na ulu biala lɛlɔ na ɔ́sɔ útalɛ-nwu kama. Na kadi bamba baƒiɔ bani ƒui na bávɔ béte lɛlɔ na mmɔ ni, ɔ́ya na bábwɛ bana ƒui na Yuda mmɔ ku kesii kani na baakpá Asera baƒiɔ lɛnɔ.
7Amu na lɛkwa lɛtɛdi lɛni kemmo na Yehosaƒat ɔɔdi lɛga mmɔ kemmo ni, ɔ́ƒuna bakutine ɛlɔ na úte-ma ɔda bubo bɔdi ɔnii batina Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ na ɔma unengudi biala kemmo na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na bakutine bammɔ ndi Benhail ku Obadia ku Sekaria ku Netanel ku Mikaia. 8Na bebo Lewiƒuɔ bebunkune yaalenwi badi bani ndi Semaia ku Netania ku Sebadia ku Asahel ku Semiramot ku Yehonatan ku Adonia ku Tobia ku Tob-Adonia. Na Katɔti bakpane inyɔ badi lɛnɔ basiaku-ma bani na baalɔ banii Elisama ku Yehoram. 9Na ɔni na bakɛ ulu ƒui ni, na bada Unwoti ɔda bubo ɔku ɔmmɔ na kesi kesii na bésela na nwuna kemmo na baatina bekyuli bammɔ ala taasiku.
10Amu na kadi bekyuli bani ƒui náka bámana Yuda kalɔ mmɔ baayia Unwoti ɔyikun ɔni na ubo geen, anwuɔsu badi bátakana na bata bekpoku Yehosaƒat. 11Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ béboku-nwu sika ɔƒualadi ku etela bamba kalɛ na keyi buɛɛ kakya ama ku Yehosaƒat. Na Arabiaƒuɔ lɛnɔ béboku-nwu baƒonu mpim maatɛ ku eti leevu-ine. Na bese lɛnɔ lɛni kani.
12Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kalɛ na Yehosaƒat ɔɔkɛ́ ɔyikun teebu ni, lɛni kani na ɔɔtú kɔgyumanakɔ lɛma kpakplaa ku lɛma linengudi lɛnɔ 13kesii kani na uusé ala. Na ɔ́ya na bekpone babuni geen bakya Yerusalem. 14Na bási Yuda ku Benyamin adua kemmo. Na básala bekpone bammɔ na bana adua adua kenye.
Amu na bábla Adna, na ɔdi bekpone bani nási Yuda ɔtɔnkune na bekpone mpim eti aku bakya-nwu kalɔ na ɔɔnu-ma lɛlɔ.
15Na Yehoanan ndi nwuna ubunkune. Na bekpone mpim eti alɔ ku avlaatɛ lɛlɔ nkya nwuna kalɔ na ɔɔnu-ma lɛlɔ.
16Na Sikri ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Amasia, na anwu ɔlati úti lɛlɔ úte ka utaabla Unwoti kabla, ɔdi ubunkune ɔtɛdi. Na bekpone mpim eti ene nkya-nwu kalɔ na ɔɔnu-ma lɛlɔ.
17Elida ɔdi ukpone ɔni na ubo kayi ku ogya geen, na anwu ntɔnku bekpone mpim eti ene bani nási Benyamin kɔdua kemmo. Na bana akɔ ɔdi biala ɔda kataminta ku kekpo agyumanala.
18Yehosabad ndi nwuna ubunkune na ɔdanku bekpone mpim eti alɔ ku avlaatɛ na bakya-nwu kalɔ.
19Bekpone bamɛni ndi bekpone bani mɔɔgyumana ɔga ɔmmɔ na Yerusalem. Nsu bani na úte kabla na bakya kɔgyumanakɔ lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ kemmo na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ baaakɛ.

english_text:
Micaiah Warns King Ahab of Israel
(1 Kings 22.1-28)
1Jehoshaphat was now very rich and famous. He signed a treaty with King Ahab of Israel by arranging the marriage of his son and Ahab's daughter.
2One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead, 3and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?”
“Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command. 4But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
5Ahab sent for 400 prophets and asked, “Should I attack the city of Ramoth?”
“Yes!” the prophets answered. “God will help you capture the city.”
6But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
7“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 8Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
9All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
10Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
11All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
12Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
13“I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
14Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
15Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
16 Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
17Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
18Micaiah replied:
I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 19The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 20then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
21“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
22Ahab, this is exactly what has happened. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
23Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
24Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
25Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 26Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
27Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(1 Kings 22.29-35)
28Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 29Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
30The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 31So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop. 32And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
33However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
34The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_text:
Mikaia Ɔ́lɛ Israel Ɔga Ahab Kpakplaa
1Na uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ni, Yehosaƒat únwini ɔlakɛne geen na ɔ́ƒɔ lɛnyi lɛnɔ. Na anwu ku Israel Ɔga Ahab bényimi lɛla lɛdi ɔkɛnku ubidi ɔnanabi ku Ɔga Ahab ubidi ulekubi lɛlɔ buti lɛlɔ. Na bétu bunyimi bɔmmɔ kɔba na ɔ́kya kɔnu ɔku ɔmmɔ kalɔ.
2Amu na limeyi linwi na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yehosaƒat ɔ́vi ɔgbami úsie Ahab kudɔ na Samaria ɔma unengudi kesii kani na uli mmɔ. Na Ahab lɛnɔ ɔ́du baƒonu ku bebuo bamba na ɔ́di limeyi úte Yehosaƒat ku nwuna benengu bani na basiaku-nwu ƒui. Mmɔ na Ahab ɔ́tɛmi Yehosaƒat kɔtɛ ɔ́siku kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́ ka ukpo Ramot ɔma na Gilead kalɔ kemmo. 3Ahab úye Yehosaƒat ɔnini, “Adubo ebebunku-mi na butékpoku Ramot-Gilead?”
Amu na Yehosaƒat údie Israelƒuɔ ɔga kenye ɔnini, “Nse aani ƒula kalɛ na mina bekyuli badi ƒula bekyuli na bɔdubunyeku-ɔ na kekpo kammɔ kemmo.”
4Nsu Yehosaƒat ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔnini, “Mmomu, ka Unwoti kasusu bɔwia asa.”
5Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́lɔ kenye bediene eti maane (400) ɔ́sala na úye-ma ɔnini, “Nteesie Ramot-Gilead na ntékpoku-ma munuu ntesie?”
Amu na kenye bediene bammɔ básu-nwu banini, “Teesie! Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubo-ma buti bɔkya awɔ ɔga enu kemmo.”
6Nsu Yehosaƒat úye Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔnini, “Unwoti kenye udiene biala ɔ́sɔ uuubo mɛni na buye-nwu litemi lɛmɛni bunu?”
7Amu na Israelƒuɔ ɔga údie Yehosaƒat kenye ɔnini, “Kenye udiene unwi ɔdi úbu ɔni na bɔkana buye-nwu Unwoti kasusu bunu nsu muukisi-nwu. Ɔsika uledie kenye kabuni biala na mina lɛlɔ. Na kenye biala wasu mina lɛlɔ kaaadia. Na anwu baalɔ Imla ubidi Mikaia.”
Amu na Yehosaƒat ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔnini, “Útalɛka asu lɛni.”
8Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́lɔ nwuna kabla ɔblane unwi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tiku Imla ubidi Mikaia boku mɛni ɔƒaani.”
9Na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ku Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Yehosaƒat bakya bana baga ala na beli bana baga eboku lɛlɔ. Na beli Samaria ulu lɛlɔ na kesii kani baakɔ́ ɔlaaƒɔ. Na kenye bediene bammɔ ƒui béli-ma kudɔ baasú ala na bana anumi. 10Na Kenaana ubidi Sedekia úti lɛbuala na ɔ́bla bebuo ese anyɔ adi na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu ɔnini, ‘Ése amɛni na adubuti akya Siriaƒuɔ ɔlɛ lɛlɔ útédu ka áyila-ma udu ƒui.’ ”
11Na lɛni kani na kenye bediene bakladi ƒui lɛnɔ baasu banini, “Biteesie bitékpoku Ramot-Gilead na bɛdubɔdi-ma lɛlɔ, ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubuti-ma ɔkya ɔga enu kemmo.”
12Na ɔtalane ɔni bátála ka útéti Mikaia uboku mmɔ ɔɔsu Mikaia ɔnini, “Nu, awɔ lɛti pɛ ndi kenye udiene ɔni nébu. Na kenye bediene bakladi baasu lɛla lɛni ndia teete ɔga. Anwuɔsu, ya ƒula etemila ku bani ngye adi abla unwi. Na asu lɛla lɛni ndubɔyɔ ɔga kaƒɔ.”
13Nsu Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Na Unwoti ɔni nli ngba lɛnyi kemmo ni, lɛla lɛni na mina Katɔti ɔ́su-mi kani ndubo bɔsu.”
14Uwi ɔni na Mikaia úbeduo ni, ɔga úye-nwu ɔnini, “Nsie ntékpoku Ramot-Gilead munuu ntesie?”
Amu na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Teesie na etékpoku-ma, na adubɔdi lɛlɔ ɔsika badubo-ma buti bɔkya-a enu enu kemmo.”
15Mmɔ na ɔga ɔmmɔ úye Mikaia ɔnini, “Kɔlɛ na ɔlɛka lɛya-a na ese kenye ka alasu lɛla lɛdi eletulo lɛla lɛni ndi sɔsɔ geen litemi na Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo?”
16Mmɔ na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu ka Israelƒuɔ ƒui bégyingya bewi abi eli aani baƒonu bani na beeebo lɛlɔ ɔnune. Na Unwoti ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Bekyuli bamɛni beeebo ɔtɔnkune, anwuɔsu ɔdi biala unwini uteesie nwuna kaduli ku atu bɔyɔ.’ ”
17Amu na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́su Yehosaƒat ɔnini, “Ńtasu-ɔ ka ukyuli ɔmɛni ulásu lɛla lɛbuni na mina lɛlɔ ntu likpidi kani?”
18Amu na Mikaia úsie anumi ku nwuna kenye budie ɔnini, “Ɔmmɔ ɔsu binu Unwoti litemi. Lɛ́nu ka Unwoti úli nwuna liboku lɛlɔ na katɔ batu ƒui bénye-nwu kɔmii ku kɔdianu. 19Na Unwoti úye-ma ɔnini, ‘Ɔma ndubɔkana na ɔtɔlɔ Ahab na usie Ramot kesii kani na badubo-nwu bɔdu mmɔ?’
“Na bani nása bénye mmɔ bátɛmi básiku ɔmɛni lɛlɔ uwi klukwii ɔdi. 20Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, kɔyu kunwi kɔ́lɛ kúbenye Unwoti anumi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, ‘Ndubɔkana na ntátɔlɔ-nwu.’
“Mmɔ na Unwoti úye-ku ɔnini, ‘Dɛ na adubo bɔbla?’
21“Mmɔ na kɔyu kɔmmɔ kɔnini, ‘Ndubusie na liti ɔkɔ etemila lɛkya kenye bediene bammɔ ƒui kenye.’
“Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, ‘Adubɔkana-nwu bɔtɔlɔ sɔsɔ, anwuɔsu teesie na atábla lɛni.’
22“Anwuɔsu ni, Ahab, lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu mɛni geen nálɛku-ɔ lɛni kani pɛpɛɛpɛ. Unwoti ɔ́ya na ƒula kenye bediene bányi ɔkɔ bátɔlɔ-ɔ na ɔgyi lɛnɔ ka blii kani nébu na badubo-ɔ udu bɔyila ƒui kede kede.”
23Ɔmmɔ kama Kenaana ubidi Sedekia úsie na útáƒiɛmi Mikaia lɛtukpo. Na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ka Unwoti kɔyu kɔlɛ-mi kemmo ni, wɛ kakɛ na kɔ́vi kɔ́sia asa na kubetemiku-ɔ?”
24Amu na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Limeyi lɛdi lɛdubo na adubo bɔnu ka ɔlɛka abɛla lɛlɔ na ɔtɔ ɔdi kama kesii kadi.”
25Mmɔ na Ahab ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔ́su ɔnini, “Biƒie Mikaia! Biti-nwu bisienku ɔga ubi Yosa ku Samaria aban ɔgadine Amon kudɔ. 26Na asu-ma ka lɛni na ɔga ɔɔsu, ‘Biti okloƒu ɔmɛni bɛkya ɔtɔ. Na bitete-nwu lɛla biala na ɔdi, si ɔɔɔdi bodobodo ku ntu kani wetédu ka línwini ḿbeduo buɛɛ.’ ”
27Amu na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Si énwini ébeduo buɛɛ ni, na agyi anii Unwoti útatɛmi útasiaku-mi lɛlɔ.” Amu na ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Bise mina litemi lɛni lɛ́su mmɔ likpo!”
Ahab Úkpi Na Ramot
28Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ahab ku Yehosaƒat bɔtɔnku bana bekpone na báyu ulu bésie Ramot na Gilead kalɔ lɛlɔ. 29Na asa na badubusie kekpokɔ kammɔ ni, Ahab ɔ́su Yehosaƒat ɔnini, “Yehosaƒat, ndubo lɛlɔ udu bɔvumana, nsu awɔ kya ƒula agala.” Anwuɔsu Ahaba ɔ́vumana lɛlɔ udu na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kekpokɔ.
30Na uwi ɔmmɔ kani lɛlɔ ni, Siriaƒuɔ ɔga úubo nwuna bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ batɔnkune ka Ahab lɛti kani na ɔdi ka bekpoku kaduɛ. 31Anwuɔsu ka bekpone bammɔ bánu Yehosaƒat na nwuna agala kemmo ni, bábu ka Ɔga Ahab ɔmmɔ na ɔdi mmɔ. Anwuɔsu bése kalɔ nka beteekpoku-nwu geen. Nsu Yehosaƒat ɔ́kpali Unwoti úvele-nwu kpakplaa na Unwoti lɛnɔ ɔ́ya na Siriaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ báda báya. 32Na ka bánu báti ka ɔɔɔdi Ahab na ɔdi mmɔ ɔsu ni, báda-nwu bukpoku báya na bágyu bátɔlɔ-nwu kudɔ na báda anwu lɛti bényene.
33Na tabla tabla uwi ɔni na kekpo kammɔ kéti késela anumi ni, ukpone ɔdi úbo nwuna kataminta lɛtula lɛdi na lɛ́vi Ahab kekpo agyumanala anyɔ ani nda-nwu lɛlɔ mmɔ kuƒi blii kɔdi ntɛ na lɛ́tu-nwu, nsu ɔɔɔdi bɔsusu na ɔ́susu mmɔ asa na úbo lɛtula lɛmmɔ. Mmɔ kani na Ahab ɔ́va ɔ́kpali nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɔkane ɔnini, “Babla na abada-mi edie likpo lɛmɛni, ɔsika ukpone ɔdi lɛtula lɛ́kɛ-mi!”
34Kekpo kammɔ késie anumi limeyi limodi na bákada Ahab békpo nwuna kɛɛkɛ kemmo kalɛ na ɔkana na utaanu Siriaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ teemene. Na úlie mmɔ laa útédu useyi uwi na uwi ɔni na ɔƒɛ utaanu kani na úkpi.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem. 2But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said:
By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you! 3But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord.
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
5He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah 6and told them:
Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide. 7So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
8Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem. 9He told them:
Faithfully serve the Lord! 10The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
11Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_text:
1Amu na Yehosaƒat anwu ɔ́sɔ únwini úbeduo Yerusalem buɛɛ na nwuna ɔga kesii. 2Nsu Hanani ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni ndi Kenye Udiene Yuhu úbasiaku-nwu na ulu lɛlɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Na kebunku kani na éte Ahab ɔlalane ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, éti lɛlɔ énwini ukyuli ɔni muukisi Unwoti ɔkpana. Anwuɔsu Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-a! 3Nsu ɔɔɔdi ala ƒui nébie na ƒula lɛlɔ. Awɔ náƒɛ Asera baƒiɔ lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ na baakpá-ma na lise-ma kedee ƒui na ɔmmɔ lɛti ɔɔtina ka aayɔ́ ka ataadi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ.”
Yehosaƒat Ɔ́ƒuna Litemi Batɛne Bani Ndubo Etemila Butaatɛ
4Yerusalem na Yehosaƒat ɔ́kya, nsu ɔɔyɔ́ busie taatávi nwuna lɛgakadikɔ kammɔ kemmo ɔ́si Beerseba na kalɔ kammɔ kada kakɛ útédu Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kammɔ kawɔkɔ na katɔ kakɛ. Na ɔɔtɛmiku bekyuli bammɔ teedie ala kalɔ teete-ma kalɛ na basɔ benwini bebo Unwoti kudɔ na batakpa-nwu kalɛ kani na ɔni na bana bati kuuku bákpa kalɛ.
5Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ƒuna litemi batɛne úte kagyumakɔ lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ ƒui na Yuda kalɔ kemmo 6na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛnu lɛlɔ kemmo kaduɛ si uwi ɔni na bɛɛlɛ bina etemila adi ugyii na bina litemi katɛkɔ. Ɔsika Unwoti kadi bekyuli na badi mɛni. Na lɛla biala na bɛ́lɛ ugyii ni, lɛdi lɛɛɛdubo-nwu bɔbɛ. 7Anwuɔsu bɛnu ka bɛ́bla bina kabla ƒui na bíti ɔbu bíte-nwu. Na bɛti lɛnɔ ka ɔɔɔdubo-mii kuƒi bute na bɛnu ukyuli ɔdi anumi bɛbla lɛla lɛdi iye bɛbɛ bɛƒɔ lɛla lɛdi bɛsiku ɔdi kudɔ bɛdi.”
8Yehosaƒat ɔ́ƒuna Lewiƒuɔ badi lɛnɔ ku bakpane ku lɛtɔ benengu badi ka benwini litemi batɛne bamɛni na Yerusalem. 9Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛbla Unwoti kabla siin na bitalɛ-nwu kama! 10Yudaƒuɔ kadi bekyuli badubo etemila lidu lidu buti buboku-mii kudɔ banii bɛtɛ bite-ma ku bekyuli bɔdu etemila muedi. Ɔdi ka bɛtɛ etemila amɛni udu ƒui na bibo bekyuli bammɔ ɔda ka bada ekpidi bɔbla bɔƒiɔ Unwoti baya kalɛ na uleti kɔnyi ulakya Yudaƒuɔ ƒui na ɔni-ma kɔtu. Na binyimo ka si bɛ́siaku ala ani kalɔ na muudie teete-mii mɛni lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔɔɔdubo-mii bɔƒiɔ bɔdi budie na uubo ka bani-mii kɔtu kɔdi.
11“Na lɛla biala na lɛdanku bɔƒɔtaadi ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔkpane unengudi ɔni ndi Amaria ni, anwu kani ndubo bɔkana na ɔlɛ ugyii. Na Ismael ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni ndi Sebadia na ɔdi Yudaƒuɔ ɔtɔnkune ni, anwu ndubɔkana na ɔlɛ etemila bamba anya ugyii. Na Lewiƒuɔ bakladi badubo-ɔ kebunku buteete. Nye kpakplaa na ndubo Unwoti buteevele teete-ɔ kalɛ na ubunku-ɔ na akana na ataabla lɛbuni lɛmmɔ uwi biala.”

english_text:
Moab and Ammon Are Defeated
1Some time later, the armies of Moab and Ammon, together with the Meunites, went to war against Jehoshaphat. 2Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
3Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow. 4They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
5After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard 6and prayed:
You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you. 7 Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever. 8Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you. 9They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
10 You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed. 11Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us. 12Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
13While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple, 14the Lord's Spirit suddenly spoke to Jahaziel, a Levite from the Asaph clan. 15 Then Jahaziel said:
Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side! 16So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley. 17 You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
18Jehoshaphat bowed low to the ground and everyone worshiped the Lord. 19Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
20Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.” 21Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing:
“Praise the Lord!
His love never ends.”
22As soon as they began singing, the Lord confused the enemy camp, 23so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
24When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground. 25So Jehoshaphat and his troops went into the camp to carry away everything of value. They found a large herd of livestock, a lot of equipment, clothes, and other valuable things. It took them three days to carry it all away, and there was still some left over.
26Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
27-28Jehoshaphat led the crowd back to Jerusalem. And as they marched, they played harps and blew trumpets. They were very happy because the Lord had given them victory over their enemies, so when they reached the city, they went straight to the temple.
29When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid 30to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace.
Jehoshaphat Dies
(1 Kings 22.41-50)
31Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. 32Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, 33but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
34Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
35While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel. 36They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber. 37But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_text:
Bekisine Bádi Moab Ku Amon Lɛlɔ
1Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Moab kadi bekyuli ku Amon kadi bekyuli básala lɛlɔ ku Meuniƒuɔ badi na báta bétékpo Yehosaƒat. 2Na batu bábasu Yehosaƒat banini, “Bekisine bekpone lisu bonwu lɛdi lɛ́si Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kemmo na Ɛpugyie ɔmmɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ bébo na bébekpo bula kalɔ na béedu kesii kani na baalɔ En Gedi.”
3Amu na Yehosaƒat ɔ́kpali Unwoti na úvele-nwu ɔnii ɔtina-nwu lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka ɔbla, ɔsika ɔ́yia geen. 4Anwuɔsu kɔnakunwi ni, báyu ulu bésie Yerusalem kesii kani na bétevele-nwu ka ubunku-ma.
5Amu na uwi ɔni na bekyuli bani na bási Yuda ku Yerusalem mmɔ bábasa na Unwoti kakpakɔ mmɔ báwɔlɔ ni, Yehosaƒat ɔ́ta únye kakpakɔ kaduli kawɔdi kammɔ anumi na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui anumi 6na ɔ́kpali Unwoti úvele ɔnini, “Awɔ Unwoti ndi Katɔti ɔni na bula bati kuuku bákpa. Na eli katɔ kakaaka mmɔ na aadi kayawi kamɛni kadi biala bekyuli lɛlɔ. Na ebo ɔyikun geen ɔni na ukyuli ɔdi biala ulakana-a lɛlɔ bɔdi. 7Bula Katɔti, awɔ nábɔku kadi bekyuli bani ƒui na nka beli mɛni kukuuku álɛku mɛni asa na ƒula kadi bekyuli bani ndi abu Israelƒuɔ búbelie mɛni. Na awɔ néti kalɔ kamɛni éte ƒula ɔkpana ɔni ndi Abraham bebi ku bawɔ ka kenwini bana kadikɔ uwi ƒui. 8Mɛni na bula bati kukuuku béli na bátu kakpakɔ béte-ɔ kalɛ na bataakpa-a teete-ɔ ɔbu. 9Na báƒɔ bádi ka uwi biala na kekpo iye ɔlɛ iye kɔka kúbo kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ ni, ƒula kadi bekyuli bamɛni bakana na beduo ƒula kakpakɔ kamɛni kemmo na bakpali-ɔ na adubudie-ma.
10“Aanu ka Amonƒuɔ ku Moabƒuɔ ku Edomƒuɔ bekpone benye beekpó-bu! Badi kɔlɔ kɔni bekyuli na nka awɔ Unwoti átatuna ka bula kadi bekyuli bekpo-ma uwi ɔni na bɔkɛ ulu bɔ́si Egyipte bɔdubo, anwuɔsu na bátayii udu. 11Nsu ɔƒaani ni, aanu-ma nási badubo bebeƒie kalɔ kani na éte-bu baƒɔ-bu kudɔ benwini ama kadi. 12Aaadubo-ma kɔtu bɔni? Buuubo kenyekɔ kadi na bekpone bamɛni udu anumi si banii beekpó-bu sɔsɔ. Bɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni na bɔbla, anwuɔsu kebunku kani na buuvele.”
13Amu na uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ banana ku beleku ku banamu bammɔ ƒui benye kakpakɔ anumi mmɔ ni, 14Unwoti Kɔyu kútemiku Yahasiel ɔni ndi Lewini na ɔ́si Asaƒ kɔdua kemmo kɔnakunwi. 15Mmɔ na Yahasiel ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔga Ɔbune ku ukyuli biala na ɔ́si Yuda ku Yerusalem, Unwoti ɔnii utalɛka bina ɔdi ɔyia iye bekpone bayikune bamɛni ɔbladu ɔdi ɔda-mii ɔƒɛ na enu aƒɛ-mii. Katɔti ɔdubo kekpo kammɔ bukpo bute-mii! 16Anwuɔsu binu lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka bɛbla. Kɔnaadi ni, bekisine bekpone bammɔ badubo lɛlɔ bɔsiaku na babwɛ bavi kalɔ kakwiidi kani náka kámana Yeruel ɔma mmɔ. Amii lɛnɔ bisie na bitásiaku-ma na Sis ɔma kemmo si uwi ɔni na béti bákɔ baalɛ́ kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo. 17Amii bitasu bɛnii biikpó-ma munu munu. Mmomu bɛwia kunyekɔ na binye bitaanu kalɛ na Unwoti ɔdubo-mii budie bɔlɛku-ma enu kemmo. Bitayia. Amii bɛbla bɛsiaku lɛla lɛni na bínu lɛlɔ. Na uwi ɔni na bɛdubo busie buteesie mmɔ kɔnaadi ƒui ni, Unwoti anwu ɔdubo bɔgyu bɔtɔ uténye mmɔ kukuuku.”
18Amu na Yehosaƒat úboku lɛlɔ kalɔ buɛɛ na ɔ́kya lili kalɔ úte Unwoti na bakladi ƒui lɛnɔ bábla lɛni kani. 19Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Lewiƒuɔ badi na bási Kohat ku Kora adua kemmo báta bénye na bédie bumwi lɛnu béte Unwoti Israel Katɔti.
20Amu na kadi kegye ɔtanta tutuutu uwi ɔni na ukyuli biala ɔdaku lɛlɔ bɔklibi ka bayu ulu beteesie kakɔ kakwiidi kani nde Tekoa mmɔ ni, Yehosaƒat ɔ́ta únye na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Banwa, binu! Si bula ƒui búti bula kɔyi bɔ́sia Unwoti lɛlɔ na bɔ́ƒɔ lɛla lɛni na kenye bediene básu-bu mmɔ bɔ́di ni, Unwoti ɔdubo-bu bubunku na bɔdi lɛlɔ.” 21Mmɔ na údie ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na badubo bɔsia busie mmɔ ɔ́tina-ma. Na ɔ́ƒuna bekyuli badi batɔ bakladi ƒui anumi na baatu lɛnu teemwi Unwoti taasu kalɛ na nwuna ɔyikun ɔni na ubo use kedee taasu banini,
“Bɛgya Unwoti enu, ɔsika ɔdia
na ɔɔyɔ́-bu uwi ndi uwi.”
22Na ɔni kani na bése kalɔ beedie bumwi lɛnu lɛmɛni kani na Unwoti ɔ́ya na bekisine bammɔ bábla gyugyuugyu na bana kɔkyakɔ. 23Anwuɔsu Amonƒuɔ ku Moabƒuɔ básala lɛlɔ na békpo Edomƒuɔ na bádu-ma ƒui. Na ɔmmɔ kama bana akpa anyɔ lɛnɔ bénwini bálɛku lɛlɔ na békpoku lɛlɔ na bádu lɛlɔ béwi bana kakyakɔ bewi kalɔ kede kede na asɔ alanu ukyuli ɔdi na bana nvo bɔmmɔ kemmo!
24Amu na uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ bédu ɔma kagyumanakɔ kani na si enye na aanu kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ teemene ni, bánu ka bekisine bekpone bammɔ ƒui ɔdi biala ukpi ɔtɛ kalɔ na bana nvo bɔmmɔ kemmo. 25Anwuɔsu Yehosaƒat ku nwuna bekpone béduo bésie bekisine bammɔ nvo kemmo mmɔ na bátála bana ala ani náƒɔ kuye na ana lɛlɔ ebo kɔsia ƒui bátɔlɔku. Na ala ani na bánu mmɔ adi ndi ɔmantɛ bebuo ku adi ku kabla lidu lɛlɔ kabla ablala ku ala abuni bamba pii lɛnɔ. Na emeyi atɛ na béti bála ala ammɔ na adi muedi ásɔ ébu ewi.
26Amu na limeyi linedi lɛlɔ ni, ukyuli biala ɔ́lɛ úbo na bábasa na kɔwɛ kɔni na baalɔ banii Baraka Kɔwɛ kemmo. Na mmɔ na bédie lɛnu bémwi Unwoti. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu na baalɔ mmɔ banii Bumwi Kɔwɛ.
27-28Yehosaƒat ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tɔnku bekyuli bammɔ na bénwini bésie Yerusalem. Na bakɛ baagyá lɛbentaa na baavwi kɔkpɛɛ. Na lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-ma geen, ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́ya na bádi bana bekisine lɛlɔ. Na ka bébeduo ɔma kemmo ni, bávi bésie kakpakɔ kɔnakunwi.
29Amu ka kadi bamba bekyuli bani na beli bede mmɔ bénu kalɛ na Unwoti úkpo Yuda bekisine úte-ma ni, liƒu bonwu líƒie-ma na báyia geen 30kalɛ na ɔdi ɔsɔ ɔta ɔnii utékpo Yuda. Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Yehosaƒat lɛgakadikɔ kákɛ keyi buɛɛ ku atu bɔyɔ.
Yehosaƒat Úkpi
31Akwa avlaatɛ-alɔ na Yehosaƒat ɔ́ƒɔ asa na únwini Yudaƒuɔ ɔga. Na úlie Yerusalem mmɔ ɔ́di lɛga akwa aavlanyɔ-alɔ. Na uni baalɔ Asuba na unieku baalɔ Silhi. 32Yehosaƒat ɔ́di Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na ɔti ɔni baalɔ Asa lɛnɔ ɔ́bla. 33Nsu anwu Yehosaƒat útabwɛ baƒiɔ bani na bekyuli bávɔ bése abi lɛlɔ bátaakpa mmɔ. Anwuɔsu bekyuli básiaku lɛƒiɔkpa ala bɔbla kama na ɔni na basiaku Unwoti kama siin aani kalɛ na bana bati kuuku bábla kalɛ.
34Na lɛla biala na Yehosaƒat ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔ́di lɛga ni, bénweni-mi bákya Yehu ɔni ndi Hanani ubidi ɔnanabi ala alɛdi Israel baga ablala ɔku kemmo.
35Uwi ɔni na Yehosaƒat ɔ́di lɛga ni, anwu ku Israel ɔga ɔlalane ɔni baalɔ Ahasia bényimi unwi bɔbla lɛla lɛdi bése. 36Na bénu kalɔ lɛnɔ ka banwi lɛkɔlɔ libendi lɛni ndubo ntu anumi buteesie ntu anumi. 37Nsu Kenye Udiene Elieser ɔ́lɛ Yehosaƒat kpakplaa ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔdubo lɛkɔkɔ lɛmɛni udu bɔyila, ɔsika ébunku Ahasia.” Na sɔsɔ ni, lɛkɔlɔ lɛmɛni lɛ́bwɛ na lítasia ntu anumi lítabla kabla kadi.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Jehoram of Judah
(2 Kings 8.16-24)
2King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. 3Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
4After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders. 5He was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled eight years from Jerusalem.
6Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong, 7 but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
8 While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king. 9Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night, 10but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time.
Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped. 11Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
12One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said:
I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather. 13Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
14Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own. 15You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
16The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram. 17They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
18After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease. 19About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
20Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled 8 years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_text:
1Yehosaƒat úbekpi na báva-nwu na kesii kani na nwuna bati kuuku bátɛ na Yerusalem na ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Yehoram ubenwini ɔga.
Yehoram Úbenwini Yuda Ɔga
2Bebi maatɛ na Ɔga Yehosaƒat ɔ́wɔ. Na ama ndi Yehoram ku Asaria ku Yehiel ku Sekaria ku Asariahu ku Mikael ku Seƒatia. 3Yehosaƒat úte bana ɔdi biala sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku ala bamba ani náƒɔ kuye geen. Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ya na bénwini lɛlɔ badine na kɔgyumanakɔ lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ kemmo na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ubidi udeedi anwu ni, ɔ́ƒuna-nwu ka unwini ɔga na nwuna kenye.
4Uwi ɔni na Yehoram ɔ́nu ka nwuna ɔyikun ɔ́di Yuda ƒui lɛlɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́ya na bádu nwuna banwani bakladi ƒui ku Yuda kadi batɔnkune badi. 5Akwa avlaatɛ-anyɔ na Yehoram ɔ́ƒɔ asa na únwini ɔga. Na akwa maane na úli Yerusalem ɔ́di lɛga.
6Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Yehoram úti Ahab ubidi ulekubi na ɔ́siaku Ahab ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ɔbladu ukpidi ku Israel baga bamba udunkpi ala bɔbla kama. Na úni Unwoti litemi bunu na ɔɔƒiɔ́-nwu mmomu. 7Nsu ka Unwoti úse kenye ka Dawid bebi ku bawɔ akɔ na ukyuli ɔdubɔsi uwi biala na ɔdi lɛga na Yuda ɔsu ni, útayila Dawidi ɔtɔ kemmo bebi ku bɔwɔ udu.
8Amu na uwi ɔni na Yehoram ɔɔdi lɛga mmɔ ni, Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ bekyuli báta bénye-nwu lɛlɔ na báƒuna bana ɔga. 9Anwuɔsu Yehoram ku nwuna bakutine ku bapɔnkɔ beliene báta bésie Edom. Na mmɔ ni, Edom bekpone bábaka-ma bákya na anwu úkeli ku usien. 10Nsu ɔ́bla bi ɔ́bla dɛ ni, Yuda ɔ́sɔ útakana Edomƒuɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi. Na Libna ɔma bekyuli muedi báta bénye Yehoram lɛlɔ uwi ɔmmɔ.
Na ala amɛni ƒui álɛ lɛni, ɔsika Yehoram únwini kama ɔ́kya Unwoti ɔni ndi nwuna bati kuuku Katɔti. 11Yehoram ɔ́tu baƒiɔ ɔ́lɛ abi eli na bekyuli béteesie taatákpa na ɔ́ya na bekyuli báƒiɔ Unwoti.
12Amu na limeyi linwi lɛdi ni, Kenye Udiene Elia únweni ɔku ɔdi úte Yehoram na ɔdanku kenye kadi ɔnini,
“Lɛ́ƒɔ linyesia lɛdi lɛ́siku Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na bula ɔti kuuku Dawid ɔ́kpa líboku-ɔ. Na kenye kammɔ ndi ka Unwoti ɔnii ɔgyi ka átasiaku ƒ'ɔti Yehosaƒat ɔbladu kama iye Nana Asa ɔbladu kama. 13Mmomu elie ngba aani Israel baga bekpidi bammɔ kalɛ na ákya Yuda kadi bekyuli ka bada Unwoti bɔkpa baya kalɛ kani na Ahab ku nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli bábla kalɛ. Na awɔ ɔlati ƒula banwani bani na nka badia betulo-ɔ ƒui muedi ádu-ma.
14“Na alaekpidi bonwu ani na ábla mɛni ɔsu ni, Unwoti ɔdubo ƒula lɛgakadikɔ bekyuli ku ƒula ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli kɔtu bɔni geen na ubile ala ani ƒui na ebo na ayii udu kede kede. 15Na kaƒɔ ɔlɛ kpakplaa ɔdi ɔdubo-ɔ bubo na ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ na adubo buƒi ebo abi laa na eti ekpi.”
16Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ƒilistiƒuɔ ku Arabiaƒuɔ bani na beli bede Kus mmɔ béti kɔnyi bákya Yehoram. 17Kadi kamɛni bekyuli bébo bébekpo Yuda na béyu-ma agala ƒui bátɔlɔku básiku ɔga kesii mmɔ. Na béƒie Yehoram ulekudi ku bebi ƒui bátɔlɔku aani batɔntɛne kalɛ. Na ubi unwi ɔni kani nébu ndi ɔnamudi ƒui ɔni baalɔ Ahasia.
18Amu ka ala amɛni álɛ lɛni áwɔlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na kaƒɔ ɔ́lɛ ɔdi úbo Yehoram ɔni na ukyuli biala ulakana bɔbwi. 19Na ɔbla akwa anyɔ kama ni, Yehoram úbekpi na únu ɔlɛ geen. Na bátakyula likpose livongu lɛdi bétete-nwu ka úkpi ina ka lɛni na bekyuli bammɔ bábla béte nwuna bati kuuku.
20Akwa avlaatɛ-anyɔ na Yehoram ɔ́ƒɔ asa na únwini ɔga. Na úlie Yerusalem mmɔ ɔ́di lɛga akwa maane. Na ukyuli ɔdi útewulo kɔnyana ka úkpi asa na badubuti-nwu batáva na Yerusalem, nsu ɔɔɔdi kesii kani na baavá baga.

english_text:
King Ahaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 8.25-29; 9.21,27,28)
1Earlier, when the Arabs led a raid against Judah, they killed all of Jehoram's sons, except Ahaziah, the youngest one. So the people of Jerusalem crowned him their king. 2He was 22 years old at the time, and he ruled only one year from Jerusalem.
Ahaziah's mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel, 3and she encouraged her son to sin against the Lord. He followed the evil example of King Ahab and his descendants. 4In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors.
Their advice led to his downfall. 5He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle, 6and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him. 7It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death.
When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family, 8and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot, 9then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord.
There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah.
Queen Athaliah of Judah
(2 Kings 11.1-3)
10As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that, 11but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah. 12Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_text:
Ahasia Únwini Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga
1Uwi ɔni na Arabiaƒuɔ báagyu bátɔ bébekpo Yuda asa na Ahasia ɔdubunwini ɔga ni, bádu nwuna banwani bananabi bana ƒui na Ahasia ɔmɛni kani nébu. Anwuɔsu na Yerusalemƒuɔ bése-nwu lɛga ka utaadi-ma lɛlɔ. 2Akwa aavlanyɔ-anyɔ na ɔ́ƒɔ asa na únwini ɔga. Na lɛkwa linwi kani na ulie Yerusalem ɔ́di lɛga.
Ahasia uni baalɔ Atalia na ɔdi Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔni baalɔ banii Omri uwɔ. 3Na anwu nébile ubidi ɔnanabi atu ɔnii ɔbla likpidi ɔƒiɔ Unwoti. Na ɔ́siaku Ɔga Ahab ku nwuna bebi ku bawɔ udu ukpidi kama. 4Geen na ɔti kukpi kama ni, Ahasia ɔ́bla likpidi ɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti na uwi ɔni na útáƒuna Ahab lɛlɔ bekyuli ka benwini-nwu kasusu bakyane.
Na ɔkɛnku kasusu kani na baakya-nwu ɔsu na úbo kalɔ. 5Bana litemi na únu ɔsu na úsie útásiaku Israel Ɔga Yoram na bétékpo Ɔga Hasael ku Siriaƒuɔ bekpone na Ramot ɔma kemmo na Gilead kalɔ lɛlɔ. Kekpo kammɔ kemmo na Ɔga Yoram ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ kaduɛ 6na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Yesreel ɔma utábwi lɛlɔ. Na Ahasia úsie mmɔ kama kama útánu-nwu. 7Na Ahasia mmɔ busie butánu Yoram kemmo na Katɔti ɔ́ya na úkpi.
Amu na uwi na Ahasia útéduo Yesreel mmɔ ni, anwu ku Yoram bésie bátása ku Yehu ɔni ndi Nimsi uwɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́ɔsu Yehu ɔnii ɔdu ɔnanabi biala na Ahab ɔtɔ kemmo. 8Na uwi ɔni na Yehu ɔdaku ɔmɛni bɔbla ni, ɔ́nu ka Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune badi ku Ahasia ɔnwani bebi bananabi badi bani na ama ku Ahasia nébo ɔma mmɔ bébo mmɔ. Na mmɔ mmɔ kani na Yehu ɔ́du-ma 9na ɔ́kya batu ɔnii batáwia Ahasia ɔmmɔ ɔlati beboku. Na Yehu batu bamɛni bátánu-nwu ka ɔ́bɛ ɔkya Samaria. Mmɔ na bákpanku Ahasia béboku Yehu na ɔ́du anwu lɛnɔ kɔnakunwi. Na ka baabu Yehosaƒat ɔsu ni, báva Ahasia ukyuli bɔva, ɔsika nwuna nana ndi Yehosaƒat ɔmɛni na anwu ɔ́sia ulu biala lɛlɔ ka ɔdi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ.
Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ uuubo na Ahasia kaduli na bese-nwu Yudaƒuɔ lɛga.
Yudaƒuɔ Beleku Ɔga Úti Kasusu Kekpidi
10Amu na uwi ɔni kani na Atalia únu ka bádu ubidi ɔnanabi Ahasia ni, ɔ́bla kasusu ka ɔdu Ahasia lɛlɔ bekyuli bani ndi bagadine mmɔ ɔdi biala. Na ɔ́ɔkɛ kuƒi kɔmmɔ lɛnɔ, 11nsu Yehoseba ɔni ndi Yehoram ubidi ulekubi na ɔdi Ahasia ɔtibi údie Yoas na ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni kemmo uwi ɔni kani lɛlɔ na nka báasala nwuna banwani bakladi na badubo-ma bɔdu. Yehoseba ɔmɛni ulieku ɔkpane ɔni baalɔ Yehoiada. Anwuɔsu ɔ́kana na útiku Ahasia ubidi ɔnanabi ɔnamu blii ɔni ndi Yoas ɔmɛni ku nwuna kabla ɔblane lɛlɔ ɔnune útábɛla ɔtɔ ɔtɛdi ɔdi kemmo na kakpakɔ mmɔ na úkeli Atalia kasusu kekpidi kani na ɔdanku mɛni. 12Yoas ɔ́bɛ ɔ́kya kakpakɔ mɛni akwa aku uwi ɔni na Atalia ɔɔdi Yuda lɛlɔ aani uleku ɔga.

english_text:
Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah
(2 Kings 11.4-21)
1After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri. 2These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem 3 and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash.
Jehoiada said to them:
Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king. 4Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple, 5one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards. 6Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded. 7You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
8The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty. 9Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders. 10They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
11Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
12As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple. 13There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
14At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!” 15She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
16Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed, 17then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
18Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing. 19Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
20Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah. 21Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_text:
Yehoiada Úse Yoas Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga
1Amu na uwi ɔni na Ahasia ubidi ɔnanabi Yoas ɔ́bɛla lɛlɔ na kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ akwa aku kama ni, Yehoiada ɔni ndi ɔkpane mmɔ ɔ́nu ɔti ka ɔlɛka babla lɛla lɛdi. Anwuɔsu ɔ́sia ulu biala lɛlɔ na ɔ́nu ka bekpone benengu bammɔ ketulodikɔ benye-nwu kama. Na bana badi ndi Yehoram ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Asaria ku Yehonan ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Ismael ku Obed ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Asaria ku Adaia ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Maaseia ku Sikri ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Elisaƒat. 2Nkyuli ɛlɔ bamɛni bésie Yuda lɛma kemmo na bátálɔ Lewiƒuɔ ku adua benengu bammɔ na bébo Yerusalem. 3Na bábasala na kakpakɔ kesii kani na bénu kalɔ ka bebunku Yoas.
Mmɔ na Yehoiada ɔ́su ɔnini, “Yoas ndubo bula Yudaƒuɔ ɔga bunwini. Ɔsika ɔ́si kukuuku ni, Unwoti ɔ́su úse ka Dawid ɔtɔ kemmo ubi na ɔga ɔdubɔsi ɔdi Yudaƒuɔ ɔga na uwi bilala kemmo. 4Na ndubo-mii bɔtina lɛla lɛni na ɔdi bɔbla. Bakpane kasala esu atɛ ku Lewiƒuɔ badi badubunye kagyumana na Lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ. Na lisu linwi lɛdubo kakpakɔ ɔban kenye butaagyumana. 5Na lisu linwi litaagyumana ɔga kesii. Na lisu lɛkladi litaagyumana kakpakɔ ɔka ɔmmɔ ɔban ɔmmɔ kayakun. Na amii bekyuli bakladi ƒui binye kagyumana na kakpakɔ kɔduli kɔmmɔ kemmo. 6Na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bani mbo kabla limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ kani ndubɔkana na beduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. Ɔsika ama kani nábla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔni na baaka bɔbla asa na akana kakpakɔ kemmo buduo. Na ɔlɛka bakladi basɔ benye kakpakɔ kɔduli kɔmmɔ kemmo kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔɔtina kalɛ. 7Na amii Lewiƒuɔ ni, ɔlɛka bɛgyumana Ɔga Yoas. Na bina anumi atatimi-nwu lɛlɔ! Na binye kagyumana ku bina kuwii na bɛdu ukyuli bamba biala mebo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo.”
8Amu na Lewiƒuɔ ku bakpane bammɔ ƒui básiaku Yehoiada ulu ɔni na ɔ́tina ka babla ala basiaku mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na bagyumane bani na bana kabla káwɔlɔ muedi beeebo kuƒi ka batɔlɔ besie kɔduli. Anwuɔsu ɔtɔnkune biala ku nwuna kabla bablane bani náwɔlɔ kabla ku bɔwɔdi bani ndubo kabla kalɔ buse ƒui benye mmɔ bese. 9Na Yehoiada úduo kakpakɔ na útédie kuwi ku kekpo agyumanala ani na ndi Dawid adi mmɔ ɔ́lɛku keyi na úle-nya úte batɔnkune bammɔ ƒui. 10Ama lɛnɔ béle-nya béte bagyumane bammɔ na Yehoiada ɔ́nu ka ɔdi biala unye kagyumana na kesii kani na ɔ́tina ka benye bamana kakpakɔ kammɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ ƒui kalɛ na bagyumana ɔga ɔmmɔ na lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ.
11Amu na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yehoiada úsie útákpanku Yoas ɔ́lɛku úboku kesii kani na béti kagabwa bébi-nwu lili na úti kakunkɛ kani mɔɔtina ɔga kalɛ na ɔdi nwuna kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ bákya-nwu kɔnu. Na béwi-nwu lɛga buse nnomii lili béti bátina ka bése-nwu lɛga sɔsɔ. Mmɔ na kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ béte yiiduu ku kɔvanu básu banini, “Ɔga ulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ!”
12Amu ka beleku Ɔga Atalia únu ka bekyuli bammɔ béte yiiduu ku kɔvanu lɛni ni, ɔ́ta kɔnakunwi úsie kakpakɔ mmɔ. 13Na mmɔ na útánu ka Yoas unye lɛkpa lɛdi na lide kayakun kammɔ kudɔ kesii kani na kadi baga kenyekɔ mmɔ. Na bagyumanane batɔnkune ku kɔkpɛɛ bavwine benye-nwu kudɔ. Na bagyane ku lɛnu bediene batɔnku bekyuli bammɔ na baakɛ́ lɛlɔyɔ teedie lɛnu ku ebiti. Mmɔ na Atalia ɔ́ni nwuna lɛwu ɔ́bwɛ na kɔnyi kemmo na ɔ́va ɔ́su ɔnini, “Amii mina bekisine bɛ́lɛ-mi kama na bɛ́kya-mi kakya!”
14Amu na Yehoiada údie lɛdi kɔnakunwi ɔ́su bagyumanane batɔnkune bɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Bitadu-nwu na Unwoti kakpakɔ kudɔ mmɔ. Bɛgyunku-nwu bɛlɛku bekpone bammɔ anumi na bɛnu ka bɛ́du nwuna kama basiakune lɛnɔ ƒui!” 15Na ɔ́wia ulu ka nka ukeli, nsu batɔnkune bammɔ béƒie-nwu na bádu-nwu na ɔban kenye kesii kani na beeti bapɔnkɔ taasiaku teeduoku ɔga kesii mmɔ.
16Amu na Yehoiada úvele Ɔga Yoas ku bekyuli bakladi bammɔ ƒui ka bablaku-nwu unwi na basiaku Unwoti kama siin na basɔ balálɛ-nwu kama. Na bana ƒui bénu kalɔ 17na bakɛ-nwu lisu kɔnakunwi békeli bésie bétébo Baal kakpakɔ ɔƒiɔtɔ bábwɛ béwi kalɔ. Na bábwɛ nwuna akpabi ammɔ ƒui ku ala ani na bávɔ bényene na bádu Baal ɔmmɔ ɔkpane ɔni baalɔ Matan na akpabi ammɔ anumi.
18Amu na Yehoiada úle kabla úte bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ na kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ kalɛ kani na Dawid ɔ́bla. Na mɔɔnu akpala bɔbla teete Unwoti ti kabla lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Mose ɔda bubo bɔɔtina. Na ama kani na ɔlɛka batɔnku bɔkpa bɔmmɔ ablala ƒui ku lɛnɔ budie. 19Na úbo bagyumanane bani nnye ɔban kɔyakun kɔmmɔ ƒui kenye ka babɔku ukyuli biala na neeese sɛɛn ka uduo kakpakɔ kammɔ batɔlɔku.
20Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, Yehoiada ɔ́lɔ bagyumanane batɔnkune bammɔ ku Yuda kadi benengu belidi belidi ku bakutine bammɔ ɔ́sala ku aban bagadine benengu bammɔ. Na bekyuli lisu lɛkladi lɛmmɔ basiaku-ma kama uwi ɔni na bákpanku Ɔga Yoas básiaku kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo na bátávi ɔban kayakun katɔdi kemmo bétéduoku ɔga kesii. Na mmɔ na útélie kalɔ na nwuna kesii aani Yudaƒuɔ ɔga. 21Na ukyuli ɔ́tɔ ku ebiti, ɔsika bádu beleku Ɔga Atalia na keyii buɛɛ kásɔ kébo Yerusalem ɔƒaamu.

english_text:
King Joash of Judah
(2 Kings 12.1-16)
1Joash was only 7 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 40 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zibiah was from the town of Beersheba.
2While Jehoiada the priest was alive, Joash obeyed the Lord by doing right. 3Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
4Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple. 5He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.”
But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders. 6 So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent. 7And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
8Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple. 9He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
10The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box. 11Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside.
This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected. 12Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
13These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new. 14They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple.
Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived. 15He died at the ripe old age of 130 years, 16and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple.
Joash Turns Away from the Lord
17After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted. 18The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, 19but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
20 God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
21-22King Joash forgot that Zechariah's father had always been a loyal friend. So when the people of Judah plotted to kill Zechariah, Joash joined them and gave orders for them to stone him to death in the courtyard of the temple. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “I pray that the Lord will see this and punish all of you.”
Joash Is Killed
23In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus. 24The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
25-26Joash was severely wounded during the battle, and as soon as the Syrians left Judah, two of his officials, Zabad and Jehozabad, decided to revenge the death of Zechariah. They plotted and killed Joash while he was in bed, recovering from his wounds. Joash was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. 27The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_text:
Yoas Únwini Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga
1Akwa maatɛ kani na Yoas ɔ́ƒɔ asa na únwini Yudaƒuɔ ɔga. Na úlie Yerusalem ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ akwa aavlene. Na uni ɔni baalɔ Sibia ni, ɔ́si Beerseba.
2Na uwi ɔni na ɔkpane unengudi Yehoiada uli ngba ƒui ni, na Yoas útaayia Unwoti na útaadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ na ɔɔbla ala ani na ese siin. 3Na Yehoiada ɔ́wia beleku inyɔ muedi úte-nwu ɔnii uti-ma kalɛ na udie kaba.
4Amu na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Yoas ɔ́bla kasusu ka uwi údu ka básɔku kakpakɔ kammɔ baklibi. 5Anwuɔsu ɔ́lɔ bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Biteesie Yuda kalɔ kesi kesii na bitáƒɔ lɛkwa kuyii bɛsiku bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ biboku. Na mɔɔwia ka bɛbla ɔmmɔ ɔƒɛni kani ɔni na uwi bubile buuubo, ɔsika ɔlɛka bɔsɔku kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔklibi.”
Nsu ɔmmɔ ƒui kama ni, Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bátababla na babla lɛla lɛni na ɔga ɔ́su-ma 6Ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na bátálɔ Yehoiada béboku na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na átatala Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ na besie batáƒɔ lɛkwa kuyii kɔmmɔ beboku? Unwoti kabla ɔblane Mose ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bénu kalɔ ɔ́si kukuuku ƒui ka beteete kuyi kɔmɛni na beti-ku bataanu Katɔti kevo kammɔ lɛlɔ. 7Na ɔƒaani ni, bɔɔwia egulabi ammɔ kpakplaa na buti bɔklibi kakpakɔ kammɔ, ɔsika Atalia uleku ukpidi ɔmmɔ bebi bananabi bébeduo mɛni na bebile ala geen na mmɔ. Na béti ala ani na ese kedee muedi bátɔlɔku bésie baakpá Baal baƒiɔ.”
8Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoas údie lɛdi úte nwuna kabla bablane ɔnii banwi ugyii adaka ɔdi bese keyi bedenku kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔban kayakun. 9Na únweni ɔku úmene Yuda kalɔ kesi kesii ɔnii ukyuli biala ubo ubaƒɔ nwuna kuyi na kakpakɔ mmɔ kalɛ kani na Mose úbo bana bati kuuku ɔda ɔnii bataabala.
10Amu na bekyuli bammɔ ku bana batɔnkune ƒui bénu kalɔ na béti bana kuyi béboku Yerusalem bábakya adaka ɔmmɔ kemmo. 11Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ beeti adaka ɔmmɔ teeduoku kakpakɔ ɔtɔ kemmo na bewilimi egulabi ammɔ bewi ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔku unwenine ku ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ubunkune anumi na baka-nwu na basɔku adaka ɔmmɔ betése keyi na kesii kani na beesé-nwu mmɔ.
Lɛni na bátaabla limeyi ndi limeyi na uwi útetu asa na bákɛ egulabi pii. 12Na Yoas ku Yehoiada béti egulabi ammɔ béte bekyuli bani mɔɔnu kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔklibi ala lɛlɔ na béti báwia atabi banwine ku ligyii banwine ku abuala kpakplaa ku abuala egyiedi lɛlɔ kabla bablane babuni geen.
13Amu na bése kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔklibi kalɔ na uwi ɔni na báwɔlɔ ni, kakpakɔ kammɔ kábla aani si kawɔdi na básɔku bátu. 14Na ɔɔɔdi egulabi ammɔ ƒui na béti bábla kabla kammɔ, anwuɔsu egulabi ani nébu ni, béti-nya béte Yoas ku Yehoiada na ama lɛnɔ béti béte na bábla kakpakɔ sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi akyami lidu lidu bese kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo.
Na uwi ɔni ƒui na ɔkpane Yehoiada úlie ngba ƒui ni, bátaabla ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ Katɔti kaƒɔ akpala bɔkyula ɔdi teete Unwoti limeyi ndi limeyi. 15Na úlie ngba útu uwi geen na ɔ́ƒɔ akwa eti anyɔ ku avlaatɛ asa na úkpi. 16Na báva-nwu na kɔƒiɔtɔ kɔni kemmo na baavá bagadine na Yerusalem, ɔsika ɔ́bla ɔdi úte Israelƒuɔ ku Katɔti ku kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui.
Yoas Únwini Kama Ɔ́kya Unwoti
17Amu na uwi ɔni na Yehoiada úkpi ni, Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune bammɔ bésie bátátɔlɔ Yoas mini mini na ɔ́tunaku-ma ka ɔbla lɛla lɛni na baawia. 18Anwuɔsu bétebile uwi ɔdi munu munu asa na báda Unwoti Katɔti bɔkpa báya na nwuna kakpakɔ na bése kalɔ baakpa ala ani na bávɔ béte Asera baƒiɔ beledi bammɔ. Na ɔkɛnku ɔmɛni ɔsu Unwoti Katɔti úti kɔnyi kpakplaa ɔ́kya Yudaƒuɔ ku Yerusalemƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui. 19Nsu ɔmmɔ ƒui kama ni, Unwoti ɔmu uumene-ma nwuna kenye bediene kalɛ na batálɛ-ma na benwini bebo-nwu kudɔ, nsu béni na bátaƒɔ-ma litemi.
20Amu na Katɔti Kɔyu kútemiku Yehoiada ubidi ɔnanabi Sakaria na ɔ́sɔku ɔ́su ukyuli biala ka kɔyu kɔmmɔ kɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na bíni na bɛɛbla atuɔkplu na mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ? Lɛtuni kani bɛɛni teewi bina lɛlɔ! Bídie-mi atu, anwuɔsu ami lɛnɔ ndubo-mii atu budie.”
21-22Ɔga Yoas ɔ́ɔyiƒala ka Sakaria ɔmɛni ɔti Yehoiada ni, anwu ku-nwu bádi bɔkpana babuni geen. Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni na bekyuli bammɔ bátása lili likpidi Sakaria lɛlɔ ka badu-nwu ni, anwu lɛnɔ únu ku-ma kalɔ na udie lɛdi ka bebo-nwu atabi badu na kakpakɔ kaduli kemmo mmɔ. Amu na uwi ɔni na Sakaria ɔdaku bɔyula ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Muuvele Unwoti nnii ɔnu lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ mɛni na ɔni bina ƒui kɔtu.”
Bádu Yoas
23Amu na lɛkwa lɛni nsia ketudi uwi ni, Siriaƒuɔ báta bébekpo Yuda ku Yerusalem na bádu bana batɔnkune bammɔ ƒui. Na béti bana ala ani náƒɔ-ma kuye mmɔ ƒui bátɔlɔku bésienku bana ɔga na Damasko. 24Siriaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ beeemomo munu munu, nsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na bádi Yudaƒuɔ bekpone pii bammɔ lɛlɔ, ɔsika Yoas ku Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ geen na Unwoti ɔɔwia ɔni kɔtu na kalɛ na bénwini kama bákya-nwu ɔsu.
25-26Amu na kekpo kammɔ kemmo ni, Yoas ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ geen na uwi ɔni kani na Siriaƒuɔ bammɔ bátɔlɔ ni, nwuna bakutine inyɔ badi bani ndi Sabad ku Yehosabad bábla kasusu ka bedie Sakaria kukpi kasi. Anwuɔsu ka Yoas ɔdaku bɔnwanya na ɔtɛ limeyi linwi ni, bésie na bátádu-nwu. Na báva-nwu na Yerusalem, nsu ɔɔɔdi kɔni kemmo na baavá bana bagadine bammɔ. 27Na baga bammɔ ablala ku bana uwi ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo ni, bénweni ala básiku nwuna bebi lɛlɔ ku ala ani na kenye bediene básu-nwu ku kalɛ na ɔ́klibi kakpakɔ kammɔ etemila bákya bébu. Na Yoas ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Amasia úbenwini ɔga na ɔti kukpi kama.

english_text:
King Amaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 14.1-6)
1Amaziah was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem, the hometown of his mother Jehoaddin.
2Even though Amaziah obeyed the Lord by doing right, he refused to be completely faithful. 3For example, as soon as he had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father. 4 But the children of those officers were not killed; the Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished.
Edom Is Defeated
(2 Kings 14.7)
5Amaziah sent a message to the tribes of Judah and Benjamin and called together all the men who were 20 years old and older. Three hundred thousand men went to Jerusalem, all of them ready for battle and able to fight with spears and shields. Amaziah grouped these soldiers according to their clans and put them under the command of his army officers. 6Amaziah also paid about 3.4 tons of silver to hire 100,000 soldiers from Israel.
7One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel, 8and so he will let your enemies defeat you, even if you fight hard. He is the one who brings both victory and defeat.”
9Amaziah replied, “What am I supposed to do about all the silver I paid those troops?”
“The Lord will give you back even more than you paid,” the prophet answered.
10Amaziah ordered the troops from Israel to go home, but when they left, they were furious with the people of Judah.
11After Amaziah got his courage back, he led his troops to Salt Valley, where he killed 10,000 Edomite soldiers in battle. 12He captured 10,000 more soldiers and dragged them to the top of a high cliff. Then he pushed them over the side, and they all were killed on the rocks below.
13Meanwhile, the Israelite troops that Amaziah had sent home, raided the towns in Judah between Samaria and Beth-Horon. They killed 3,000 people and carried off their possessions.
14After Amaziah had defeated the Edomite army, he returned to Jerusalem. He took with him the idols of the Edomite gods and set them up. Then he bowed down and offered them sacrifices. 15This made the Lord very angry, and he sent a prophet to ask Amaziah, “Why would you worship these foreign gods that couldn't even save their own people from your attack?”
16But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.”
The prophet stopped. But then he added, “First you sinned and now you've ignored my warning. It's clear that God has decided to punish you!”
Israel Defeats Judah
(2 Kings 14.8-14)
17King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
18Jehoash sent back a reply that said:
Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
19Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
20God made Amaziah stubborn because he was planning to punish him for worshiping the Edomite gods. Amaziah refused to listen to Jehoash's warning, 21so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops. 22During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home, 23and Jehoash captured Amaziah.
Jehoash took Amaziah with him when he went to attack Jerusalem. Jehoash broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly 200 meters long. 24He carried away the gold, the silver, and all the valuable furnishings from God's temple where the descendants of Obed-Edom stood guard. He robbed the king's treasury, took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
Amaziah Is Killed
(2 Kings 14.15-20)
25Amaziah lived 15 years after Jehoash died. 26Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
27As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there. 28His body was taken to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
translation_text:
Bése Amasia Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga
1Amasia ɔ́ƒɔ akwa aavlanyɔ-alɔ asa na bése-nwu lɛga. Na úlie Yerusalem ɔni ndi uni Yehoadin ɔma mmɔ ɔ́di lɛga akwa aavlanyɔ-yaalenwi.
2Ina ka Amasia ɔ́bla lɛbuni na Katɔti anumi ni, útadi nwuna etemila ƒui lɛlɔ ku nwuna kayi ƒui kede kede. 3Na ala ammɔ adi bene ndi ka uwi ɔni kani na nwuna lɛgadi lílie kalɔ na ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun na Yuda lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́ya na béƒie bakutine bani nádu ɔti mmɔ. Na anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́ya na bádu ama lɛnɔ. 4Nsu bakutine bammɔ bebi ama ni, útaya na badu-ma, ɔsika nwuna anu asia Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔni nkya Mose ɔku kemmo ka bekyuli bani na báƒiɔ ni, ama alati na ɔdi ka bani kɔtu na ɔɔɔdi ka bani ubi ɔdi kɔtu na ɔti kenye iye bani ubi ɔti ɔdi kɔtu na ubidi kenye.
Bádi Edom Lɛlɔ
5Amu na Amasia ɔ́kya Yuda ku Benyamin adua bekyuli ɔtu na bálɔ banana bani ƒui náaƒɔ ɔ́si akwa aavlanyɔ ku ka kama ƒui básala. Bekyuli bamɛni ƒui bumomo bɔbla aani nkyuli mpim eti aku na báklibi lɛlɔ béte kekpo. Na badi bekyuli bani ndubɔkana na bada kekpo agyumanala ku atula na bekpo. Anwuɔsu Amasia lɛnɔ ɔ́sala-ma esu esu na bana adua kenye na úti-ma ɔ́kya nwuna bekpone batɔnkune kalɔ. 6Amasia úsie útáƒɔ bekpone mpim eti anyɔ bamba ɔ́siku Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na kayu kenye. Na ɔdubɔƒɔ kayu kani mabla aani sika ɔƒualadi antabi aƒo bonwu aavlene unu na bana lili.
7Amu na Katɔti kenye bediene bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Mina Ɔga Ɔbune, taya na Israelƒuɔ bekpone bamɛni besie basiaku-ɔ besie kekpokɔ, ɔsika bana lɛgakɔdikɔ kɔni na kɔkya katɔ kakɛ mmɔ ƒui ni, Katɔti úni ka ute bana akɔ ukyuli ɔdi kebunku. 8Anwuɔsu si ina bi lɛnanabi na ádi na kekpokɔ muedi ni, ƒula bekisine badubo-ɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi. Katɔti mɔɔyá na ukyuli ɔɔdi lɛlɔ iye badi ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.”
9Mmɔ na Amasia údie kenye na úye kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Na dɛ na ndubo bɔbla asa na masɔ makɛ mina sika ɔƒualadi ɔni ƒui na líti lɛƒɔ kayu na Israelƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ lili?”
Amu na Katɔti kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔdubɔkana na ɔsɔku sika ɔmmɔ ute-ɔ utulo ɔni na éti áƒɔ kayu kammɔ muedi.”
10Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Amasia úbo Israelƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ ɔda ɔnii bátɔlɔ beteesie bana kalɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu uwi ɔni na báyu ulu bésela ni, béti kɔnyi bákya Yuda kadi bekyuli geen.
11Amu na kama ƒui uwi ɔni na Amasia kayi kásɔ kénwini kélie-nwu kalɔ káwɔlɔ ni, ɔ́tɔnku nwuna bekpone na bésie kesii kani baalɔ banii Mma Kɔwɛ kemmo na bátádu Edomƒuɔ bekpone mpim leevu na kekpokɔ mmɔ. 12Na úƒie bekpone bamba ngba ngba na bákpanku-ma bákɔliku kɔbi kɔdi lili bétényene lɛtakpɛ gegenge kɔdi lili. Mmɔ na bédi-ma bábaƒiɛmi atabi lɛlɔ na kɔwɛ voo kɔmmɔ kemmo na bábwɛ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.
13Na uwi ɔni na ala amɛni ƒui aalɛ́ ni, Israelƒuɔ bekpone bani na Ɔga Amasia údie ulu ka batɔlɔ mmɔ bésie bétékpoku Yuda lɛma lɛni Samaria ku Bet-Horon lɛma ntɛ. Na bádu nkyuli mpim leevu na béƒie-ma ala ƒui báƒɔ bátɔlɔku.
14Uwi ɔni na Amasia úsie útádi Edomƒuɔ lɛlɔ na kekpokɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, úti bana báƒiɔ ala anwidi ku avɔdi ɔ́tɔlɔku úboku Yerusalem. Mmɔ na úbese-ma na ɔɔkpá-ma na ɔɔkya lili kalɔ teete-ma. 15Na ɔbladu ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na Katɔti ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen. Anwuɔsu ɔ́tala kenye udiene ɔdi ɔ́kya-nwu ɔnii utéye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ɔdi ka eti kadi bamba baƒiɔ bani na bátakana na bekpo bete ama alati kadi bekyuli muedi ebese ataakpa?”
16Nsu kenye udiene ɔmmɔ útawɔlɔ tɔ lɛla lɛni na uuye asa na Ɔga Amasia ɔ́tu-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Aaadi mina kasusu bakyane akɔ ɔdi! Anwuɔsu si aaagyi na ásɔ ébimi kenye ásu lɛla lɛdi ɔƒɛni ni, ndubɔya na badu-ɔ.”
Mmɔ kani na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́da butemi ɔ́ya. Nsu ɔ́su ɔ́sia ɔnini, “Katɔti úse ka ɔyila-a udu geen! Ɔsika kudeedi ni, ábla likpidi na ásɔ éni mina bɔlɛ.”
Israel Ɔ́di Yuda Lɛlɔ
17Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Amasia ku nwuna bakutine benengu bábla kelisa na ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Yehoas ɔni ndi Yehu ubidi ɔnanabi ɔtu ɔnini, “Klibi lɛlɔ na ebo na ami ku-ɔ bɔsa anumi ku anumi na kekpokɔ!”
18Mmɔ na Yehoas lɛnɔ ɔ́sɔku ɔtu ɔ́kya-nwu úmene ɔnini, “Dii ni, liyu alakpi adi na Lebanon ákya kugyii bonwu kpakplaa kɔdi na Lebanon mmɔ kani ɔtu ɔnii, ‘Mɔɔwia ka eti ƒ'ubidi ulekubi ete-mi na lite mina ɔnanabi na uti.’ Nsu alakpi akɔ ebuo bonwu ɔdi úbo na úbanya liyu alakpi ammɔ úsusu ɔ́mana kalɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. 19Amasia, aanu lɛlɔ ka ebo ɔyikun geen ka ékpo ádi Edomƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu. Sɔ lie ƒula ɔma na ataakɛ ƒula kubiti. Bi ɔsu na aawia lɛlɔ lɛsɛ na adubo bɔya na awɔ ku ƒula Yuda lɛgakadikɔ ƒui bɛyii ku udu?”
20Nsu Katɔti ɔ́bla-nwu atu kpakplaa na Yehoas kenye kammɔ kátabla Ɔga Amasia kasusu kadi munu munu, ɔsika Katɔti úuse úse kalɛ na ɔdubuti ɔni-nwu kɔtu na Edomƒuɔ baƒiɔ bani na útéti úbese ɔɔkpá mɛni ɔsu. 21Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yehoas ɔ́tɔnku nwuna bekpone na anwu ku Amasia bekpone bása na Bet-Semes na Yuda kalɔ kemmo. 22Na bésusu Yudaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ kaduɛ na bábɔku-ma na békeli bénwini bésie ɔma ƒui kede kede 23na Yehoas úƒie Amasia.
Amu na uwi ɔni Yehoas úsie utábwɛ Yerusalem ni, ɔ́kpanku Amasia ɔni na úƒie na kekpokɔ ɔda. Na Yehoas ɔ́bwɛ awodu bonwu ani na bátu bámana ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔ́si kesii kani baalɔ Eƒraim ɔban kenye útédu kesii bamba kani baalɔ banii Okodo ɔban kenye. Na mmɔ bune ɔdubɔdi lɛgba eti leevu-anyɔ. 24Na kesii kani geen na Obed-Edom kaba kemmo bebi beenye taagyumana mmɔ geen na ɔ́ya na béti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ku ala bamba ani na áƒɔ kuye geen mmɔ na ese Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ bátalɔku ƒui kede kede. Na egulabi ani na ese Ɔga egulabi kesekɔ mmɔ ku ala bamba na úƒie bekyuli bamba lɛnɔ na ɔ́tɔlɔku-ma ƒui úsienku Samaria kalɔ lɛlɔ.
25Ka Yehoas úkpi kama ni, Amasia ɔ́sɔ úlie akwa leevu-alɔ. 26Na ala bamba ani ƒui na Amasia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, bénweni ana ƒui bákya Yudaƒuɔ baga ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo.
27Amu na uwi ɔni kani na Amasia úse kalɔ ɔɔta teenye Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ ni, bekyuli badi na Yerusalem mmɔ bása lili na Amasia lɛlɔ. Nsu Amasia úbati na ɔ́wia kuƒi na úkeli úsie ɔma ɔni baalɔ Lakis kemmo, nsu kasala bamba báwia-nwu kama ulu na bátánu-nwu béƒie na bádu-nwu na mmɔ. 28Bágyu-nwu ukpine básia ɔpɔnkɔ lɛlɔ bésienku Yerusalem bátáva kesii kani na nwuna nana ati bene batɛ.

english_text:
King Uzziah of Judah
(2 Kings 14.21,22; 15.1-7)
1-3After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only 16 at the time. Uzziah ruled 52 years from Jerusalem, the hometown of his mother Jecoliah. During his rule, he recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath.
4He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done. 5Zechariah was Uzziah's advisor and taught him to obey God. And so, as long as Zechariah was alive, Uzziah was faithful to God, and God made him successful.
6While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia. 7God helped him defeat the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-Baal, and the Meunites. 8Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
9In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward. 10He also built defense towers out in the desert.
He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
11Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials. 12-13There were 307,500 trained soldiers, all under the command of 2,600 clan leaders. These powerful troops protected the king against any enemy. 14Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging. 15Some of his skilled workers invented machines that could shoot arrows and sling large stones. Uzziah set these up in Jerusalem at his defense towers and at the corners of the city wall.
God helped Uzziah become more and more powerful, and he was famous all over the world.
Uzziah Becomes Too Proud
16Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall.
One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him. 17Azariah the priest and 80 other brave priests followed Uzziah into the temple 18 and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
19Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead! 20Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
21Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
22Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. 23 Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_text:
Usia Úbenwini Yuda Ɔga
1Ka Ɔga Amasia úkpi ni, Yudaƒuɔ béƒie ubidi ɔni baalɔ banii Usia na basɔ baalɔ-nwu lɛnɔ banii Asaria bése lɛga na ɔti kenyekɔ. 2Anwu násɔku Elat ɔma ɔ́tu úte Yudaƒuɔ na ɔti bukpi kama.
3Akwa leevu-aku na Usia ɔ́ƒɔ asa na bése-nwu lɛga. Na úlie liboku lɛlɔ akwa liti ku inyɔ.
