Uni na baalɔ banii Yekolia na ɔ́si Yerusalem. 4Únu Katɔti litemi na ɔ́di-ni lɛlɔ na ɔɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ aani kalɛ ɔti ɔ́bla. 5Sakaria ndi ukyuli ɔni nátina Usia ala na ɔ́tina-nwu kalɛ na unu Katɔti litemi na ɔdi-ni lɛlɔ lɛnɔ. Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni kemmo na Sakaria úlie ngba ƒui ni, Usia útaadi Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ kaduɛ na Katɔti lɛnɔ ɔ́ya na ala átɛku-nwu.
6Na Usia lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, útékpo Ƒilistiƒuɔ na ɔ́bwɛ bana lɛma lɛni ndi Gat ku Yabne ku Asdod lɛma awodu ani na bátu bámana-ni. Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́sɔku lɛma bamba ɔ́tu na Asdod amadɔ mmɔ ku ekpo bamba ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. 7Katɔti úbunku-nwu na ɔ́di Ƒilistiƒuɔ ku Arabiaƒuɔ bani na bakya Gur-Baal ku Meunite mmɔ bene ƒui. 8Na Amonƒuɔ muedi bátaaƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔdine kuyi teete Usia aani nwuna kalɔ bakyane kalɛ. Nwuna lɛnyi ku ɔyikun ɔni na ubo úsie ɔgyu geen ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ bani na bakya ɔgyu kakaaka muedi bénu-nwu kɔku.
9Usia ɔ́tu ɔma kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa únyene Yerusalem na Okodo ɔban kenye ku Kɔwɛ ɔban kenye ku kesii kani na bátu kowodu kɔmmɔ béduoku aani kekpokpo. 10Na ɔ́tu kɔgyumanakɔ bamba únyene kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo.
Na ubo bebuo na bemomo-nwu geen na bakya abi ammɔ kaƒɔna ku kalɔ ƒiaa kani nwi mmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́ya na bátu abiɔ lɛnɔ na emomo kalɛ na utaaƒɔ ntu teete-ma uwi biala kemmo. Na ka ɔɔyɔ́ kemo busie ɔsu ni, ubo edula ku adingyii lidu mmo geen na abi lɛlɔ kesii kani na kalɔ kammɔ kadia geen ƒui na ɔ́ƒɔ bekyuli ɔ́kya mmɔ na baanu mmo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔɔƒɔ-ma kayu.
11Usia bekpone benye kagyumana bete kekpo uwi biala. Na Yeiel ku Maaseia ndi bakutine benengu bani mɔɔnu bekpone bammɔ bumomo bɔka lɛlɔ ala uwi biala. Na nkyuli inyɔ bamɛni lɛnɔ bakya Usia benengu akɔ unwi ɔni na baalɔ banii Hanania kalɔ. 12Na atɔƒi benengu bani ndi bekpone bamɛni batɔnkune bumomo bɔdi nkyuli 2,600. 13Na bekpone bani na bátina-ma kekpo bukpo kɔkwɛ geen ama alati bebo 307,500. 14Usia úte bekpone bamɛni kayi agyumanala ku atula ku kekpo kɔbwa ku agyumanala bamba kɔtaminta ku kavwinvwi atabi. 15Na nwuna bakywɛɛne babuni bani na ubo ku kabla lidu bamba bablane bani na bebo kasusu geen béti abuala bábla ekpola ani alati mɔɔkana na eebó atula ku atabi taasiaku bekisine. Na Usia úti abuala amɛni ɔ́lɛ Yerusalem na kesii kani bene na ɔ́tu ɔma kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kɔmmɔ únyene mmɔ.
Katɔti ɔ́ya na Usia ɔyikun ku lɛnyi lɛ́ku lísie ɔgyu geen na kɔlɔ ƒui bekyuli akɔ.
16Amu na ɔyikun ɔni na úbakɛ mɛni ku kalɛ na nwuna lɛnyi lísie ɔgyu ɔsu ni, Usia úse kalɔ ɔɔkɔliku lɛlɔ katɔ na ɔmmɔ náya-nwu na úbo kalɔ.
Limeyi linwi ni, Usia útenu Unwoti nwuna Katɔti litemi na ɔ́ta útéduo kakpakɔ na úsie útéti oloƒui ɔdi ɔɔkyula aani akpala ute-nwu. 17Mmɔ na Asaria ɔni ndi ɔkpane ku bakpane liti ku avlaatɛ bamba bése kayi básia-nwu kama bétéduo-nwu kudɔ na kakpakɔ mmɔ. 18Béye-nwu etemila geen na básu-nwu banini, “Ɔɔɔdi ulu ka ɔbla lɛla lɛni udu na aabla mɛni, ɔsika Aaron bebi bani na bése likpo aani bakpane kani na ɔlɛka babla bɔkyula ɔdi ɔmɛni udu. Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka avi alɛ mɛni! Ábla likpidi áƒiɔ Unwoti ɔni na nwuna kusɛ kusɛ ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo-ɔ bɔsiaku.”
19Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Usia ɔda oloƒui libui lɛmmɔ unye ka use kalɔ ku oloƒui ɔmmɔ bɔkyula asa na Ɔkpane Asaria ɔɔdɔnku-nwu na ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen. Na uwi ɔni na kɔnyi kɔmmɔ kɔɔkɔ́-nwu lɛni ni, ɔlɛ buɛ ɔdi ɔ́lɛ-nwu atɛntɛ. 20Na Asaria ku bakpane bakladi bánu ɔmɛni báti kɔnakunwi na básu banii ɔvi ɔlɛ kakpakɔ mmɔ. Usia ɔlati ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Unwoti náni-nwu kɔtu, anwuɔsu ɔ́babla ka ɔvi ɔlɛ mmɔ.
21Na ɔlɛ buɛ ɔmɛni úbaƒɔ Usia lɛlɔ ƒui nwuna ngba emeyi akladi ƒui kemmo. Anwuɔsu básɔ bétete-nwu kuƒi ka uduo kakpakɔ mmɔ iye ɔga kesii mmɔ muedi mmomu úlie kesii bamba. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na ubidi Yonatan na béti bése-nwu kenye aani ɔga kalɛ.
22Na ala bamba ani ƒui na Usia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, bénweni-nya bákya Kenye Udiene Yesaia ɔni ndi Amos ubidi ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo. 23Na ɔlɛ buɛ ɔni na Usia úƒi ɔsu ni, bátakana na bava-nwu na baga katɛnkɔ mmomu bátáva-nwu na bekyuli kavakɔ kalɔ bamba kani na baga bammɔ kani béye bése. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, bése ubidi Yonatan lɛga.

english_text:
King Jotham of Judah
(2 Kings 15.32-38)
1Jotham was 25 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years. Jerushah his mother was the daughter of Zadok.
2Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
3Jotham rebuilt the Upper Gate of the temple and did a lot of work to repair the wall near Mount Ophel. 4He built towns in the mountains of Judah and built fortresses and defense towers in the forests.
5During his rule he attacked and defeated the Ammonites. Then every year for the next three years, he forced them to pay 3.4 tons of silver, 1,000 tons of wheat, and 1,000 tons of barley.
6Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
7Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah. 8After he had ruled Judah 16 years, he died at the age of 41. 9He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_text:
Bese Yonatan Yuda Ɔga
1Akwa aavlanyɔ-alɔ na Yonatan ɔ́ƒɔ asa na bése-nwu Yudaƒuɔ lɛga. Na úlie Yerusalem ɔdi lɛga akwa leevu-aku. Sadok ubidi ulekubi ɔni baalɔ banii Yerusa ndi uni.
2Yonatan úlie ngba bɔbuni aani ɔti kalɛ, nsu anwu útetéduo kakpakɔ mmɔ kudii ɔnii ɔɔkyula oloƒui kalɛ na ɔti ɔ́bla dii mmɔ. Mmomu bekyuli bammɔ ala bana likyulikpi ala ani na baabla taata teenye Katɔti lɛlɔ kani nátakɔsi.
3Yonatan ɔ́sia ulu biala lɛlɔ na ɔ́sɔku kakpakɔ ɔban kayakun kani nésie kɔtɔ kakɛ mmɔ ɔ́tu na ɔ́bla kabla bamba lidu na kowodu kakɛ kani nde kesii kani baalɔ banii Oƒel Kɔbi mmɔ. 4Ɔ́tu lɛma lɛwɔdi ɔ́kya Yudaƒuɔ abi ammɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́tu kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa lidu ɔ́kya aku ammɔ kemmo ƒui.
5Na uwi ɔni na ɔɔdi lɛga ni, úkpo na ɔ́di Amonƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na akwa atɛ kemmo ɔ́si ɔmmɔ kama ni, bátaaƒɔ ukyuli kalɔ bakya kuyi teete-nwu ɔni ndi sika ɔƒualadi antabi aƒo bonwu aavlene unu ku edula aani antabi akyami mpim liti ku leevu ku edula bamba lɛnɔ aani kakpa akyami mpim liti ku leevu.
6Yonatan ɔ́siaku Unwoti Katɔti kama siin na úbenwini ɔga ɔyikune geen.
7Na ala bamba ani ƒui na Yonatan ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla ku kekpo kani ƒui na úkpo na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israel ku Yudaƒuɔ baga alɛ alɛdi ɔku kemmo. 8Yonatan ɔ́di lɛga akwa leevu-aku na úbekpi uwi ɔni na ɔ́ƒɔ akwa aavlene-unwi. 9Báva-nwu na Yerusalem na ubidi Ahas nébenwini ɔga.

english_text:
King Ahaz of Judah
(2 Kings 16.1-4)
1Ahaz was 20 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years.
Ahaz was nothing like his ancestor David. Ahaz disobeyed the Lord 2and was as sinful as the kings of Israel. He made idols of the god Baal, 3and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 4Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
Syria and Israel Attack Judah
(2 Kings 16.5,6)
5-6 Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them.
The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed 120,000 of its bravest soldiers in one day. 7During that battle, an Israelite soldier named Zichri killed three men from Judah: Maaseiah the king's son; Azrikam, the official in charge of the palace; and Elkanah, the king's second in command. 8The Israelite troops captured 200,000 women and children and took them back to their capital city of Samaria, along with a large amount of their possessions. They did these things even though the people of Judah were their own relatives.
Oded the Prophet Condemns Israel
9Oded lived in Samaria and was one of the Lord's prophets. He met Israel's army on their way back from Judah and said to them:
The Lord God of your ancestors let you defeat Judah's army only because he was angry with them. But you should not have been so cruel! 10If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
11Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
12About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong, 13and they said:
If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
14So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah. 15The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria.
Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help
(2 Kings 16.7-9)
16-18Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places.
Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help. 19But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning. 20So Tiglath Pileser came to Judah, but instead of helping, he made things worse. 21Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz.
The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
22Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before. 23He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
24Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem. 25In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
26Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 27 Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_text:
Bése Ahas Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga
1Ahas ɔ́ƒɔ akwa aavlanyɔ asa na bése-nwu Yudaƒuɔ ɔga. Na úlie Yerusalem mmɔ ɔ́di lɛga akwa leevu-aku.
Ahas ngba bulie bútasiaku nwuna nana ati Dawid bɔdi lɛlɔ na ulu biala lɛlɔ munu munu, ɔsika Ahas útasiku Unwoti kama siin. 2Anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́bla likpidi aani Israel baga bamba kalɛ na ɔ́bla baƒiɔ na Baal udu kenye úse úte lɛlɔ. 3Ɔ́bla akpala úte ala bamba na kesii kani baalɔ banii Ben-Hinom Kɔwɛ kemmo. Na ɔni na utulo ƒui ndi ɔni na ɔsiaku kadi bamba ɔbladu kama na úti ubidi ɔnanabi ɔ́kyula ɔ́kpa. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdi lɛla lɛni muusé Katɔti lɛlɔ geen. Anwuɔsu na ɔ́bɔku-ma ɔ́lɛku Israel kɔlɔ kemmo. 4Ahas ɔ́kɛ ekpo ekpo ƒui ɔɔkyula oloƒui na aƒiodu ani nkya abi eli ku egyii enengudi ani mbo ɔyuli kalɔ.
5Ahas ku Yuda kadi bekyuli ƒui bábla likpidi báƒiɔ Unwoti na bénwini kama bákya Katɔti ɔni na bana bati kuuku bákpa. Anwuɔsu na Katɔti úti-ma ɔ́kya Aram kadi bekyuli enu kemmo na bétiku nwuna bekyuli pii bátɔlɔku aani bekyuli biƒiedi bésienku Damasko.
Na lɛni kani na Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ bésusu-ma geen na kekpo kammɔ kéƒie bana bekyuli pii bátɔlɔku. 6Limeyi linwi kemmo ni, Remalia ubidi Peka ɔ́du bekpone mpim eti anyɔ ku aavlanyɔ na Yuda ɔ́si ɔni na bédie Unwoti ɔni ndi bana bati Katɔti ɔsu. 7Na kekpo kammɔ kemmo ni, Israelni ɔnana ɔni baalɔ banii Sikri ɔ́du Yudaƒuɔ banana ɛtɛ. Na ama ndi Maaseia ɔni ndi ɔga ubidi ku Asrikam ɔkutine ɔni mɔɔnu ɔga kesii kammɔ lɛlɔ. Na ukyuli ɔtɛdi ɔmmɔ ndi Elkana ɔni muunye ɔga kenye. 8Na Israelƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ béƒie beleku ku banamu mpim eti ene bátɔlɔku bésienku Samaria ɔni ndi bana ɔma unengudi. Na bétiku ala bamba pii lɛnɔ bátɔlɔku ina ka bagyi ka Yudaƒuɔ bani bana lɛlɔ bekyuli.
Kenye Udiene Oded Ɔ́du Israel Kɔtɔ
9Samaria mmɔ na Oded ɔmɛni ɔ́kya na ɔdi Unwoti Katɔti kenye udiene. Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bási kekpokɔ na Yuda badubo ni, útásiaku-ma na ulu lɛlɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Unwoti bina bati kuuku Katɔti ɔ́ya na bɛ́di Yudaƒuɔ bekpone lɛlɔ, ɔsika úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-ma. Nsu ɔɔɔdi lɛni ƒui na ɔdi ka bɛbla-ma ulikplu ala bitédu. 10Na si bíti Yudaƒuɔ ku Yerusalemƒuɔ bínwini bina kabla bablane ni, amii lɛnɔ bɛ́bla likpidi aani kalɛ na ama bábla báƒiɔ Unwoti. 11Bɛsɔku bekyuli beƒiedi bammɔ bimene bana ɔma, ɔsika bina lɛlɔ bekyuli kani na badi. Na si bítabla ɔmɛni ni, Unwoti ɔdubo-mii kɔtu bɔni ku kɔnyi geen.”
12Uwi ɔni kani na benye baasu ɔmɛni ni, Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune ine badi báda bábalɛ. Na ama ndi Yohanan ubidi Asaria ku Mesilemot ubidi Berekia ku Salum ubidi Yehiskia ku Hadlai ubidi Amasa. Na ama lɛnɔ bénu kalɔ ka lɛla lɛni a Israelƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ bábla ni, lɛɛɛdia sɔsɔ. 13Na básu lɛnɔ banini, “Si bíti bekyuli bamɛni bíboku Samaria ni, ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔdubɔsɔ unwini likpidi bamba lɛni na bɔ́bla bɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti. Ɔsika bɔ́ɔbla ala pii bɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti na nwuna kɔnyi kɔsia-bu lɛlɔ.”
14Anwuɔsu na bɔtɔnkune bammɔ ku bekyuli bakladi anumi ni, bekpone bammɔ bányonu beƒiene bammɔ ku ala ani ƒui na béti bátɔlɔku Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. 15Anwuɔsu batɔnkune bammɔ béti adi awɔdi ku lɛgbanvuo ku adila béte bekyuli bani mɔɔyaki adi na bényimi-ma lɛlɛ ku nnɔmii. Na bani na bábla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ni, bágyu-ma básia bebuo ala betine lɛlɔ na bákpanku bana ƒui básɔku bésienku bana banwani kudɔ na Yeriko kesii kani na ebo akya geen. Ɔmmɔ kama na batɔnkune bammɔ bénwini bébo Samaria.
16-20Amu na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Edomƒuɔ básɔ bésie bétékpo Yuda lɛma lɛni nkya katɔ kakɛ na béƒie bekyuli bátɔlɔku. Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛnɔ bétékpo lɛma lɛni nkya ɔƒɛ kanukɔ na abi ammɔ kaƒɔna ku kalɔ kakwiidi kani na kewi késie kada kakɛ mmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ na uwi ɔmmɔ kani kemmo na bádi Bet-Semes ku Aiyalon ku Gederot ku Soko ku Timna ku Gimso ku akpaklɔ ani nkya amadɔ mmɔ. Ɔmmɔ kama na Ƒilistiƒuɔ badi bésie bétélie mmɔ.
Ahas ɔ́kya Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Tiglat Pileser ɔtu na úvele-nwu ka ubebunku-nwu. 21Na Ahas úti etela ɔ́siku Unwoti kakpakɔ ku ɔga kesii mmɔ ku Israelƒuɔ benengu bamba kɔduli úmene-nwu, nsu Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔmɛni úni ka ubunku Ahas.
Likpidi Likplodi Lɛni Na Ahas Ɔ́bla Ku Nwuna Kukpi
22Ala enengudi ani nálɛku Ahas mɛni ƒui kama ni, ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla alaekpidi enengudi ani nébie etulo kudeedi ƒui ɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti. 23Ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Use-mi aani Siriaƒuɔ baƒiɔ bamɛni nébunku-ma ɔsu na bákana-mi lɛlɔ bɔdi. Anwuɔsu ɔƒɛni kalɛ si lɛ́bla akpala líte-ma ni, badubɔkana na bebunku-mi.” Ɔmmɔ ndi likpidi likplodi lɛni na Ahas ɔ́bla na lítiku-nwu lítákya kukpi kemmo ku Yuda bekyuli udu bɔyii.
24Ala ani ƒui na bánwi bése kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, Ahas útiku-nya ɔ́lɛku na útáƒɛ-nya ekuku ekuku na ɔ́kalɛ kakpakɔ kammɔ únyene. Ɔmmɔ kama na úsie útátu akpabi ɔ́lɛ lilu ƒui lɛlɔ na Yerusalem úte kadi bamba baƒiɔ. 25Na lɛma linengudi ku lɛma lɛkladi ƒui kemmo na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, Ahas ɔ́tu baƒiɔ ɔ́mana kalɛ na bekyuli bataakpa. Na ala amɛni bene ƒui náya na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen.
26Na ala bamba ani ƒui na Ahas ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Yudaƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ baga ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo. 27Ahas úbekpi na báva na Yerusalem, nsu ɔɔɔdi baga kɔƒiɔtɔ kemmo. Na ɔmmɔ kama bése ubidi Hesekia lɛga na nwuna kenyekɔ.

english_text:
King Hezekiah of Judah
(2 Kings 18.1-3)
1Hezekiah was 25 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem. His mother was Abijah daughter of Zechariah. 2Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done.
The Temple Is Purified
3In the first month of the first year of Hezekiah's rule, he unlocked the doors to the Lord's temple and had them repaired. 4Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple 5and said:
It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord. 6Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple. 7They locked the doors, then let the lamps go out and stopped burning incense and offering sacrifices to him. 8The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were 9our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
10So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us. 11Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
12-14When Hezekiah finished talking, the following Levite leaders went to work:
Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the Kohath clan; Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel from the Merari clan; Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah from the Gershon clan; Shimri and Jeuel from the Elizaphan clan; Zechariah and Mattaniah from the Asaph clan; Jehuel and Shimei from the Heman clan; Shemaiah and Uzziel from the Jeduthun clan.
15These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
16The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
17The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month 18they went back to Hezekiah and said:
Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils. 19And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar.
Worship in the Temple
20At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple. 21They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
22The priests killed the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, then splattered the blood on the altar. 23They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals. 24The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
25Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan. 26 The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
27As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments, 28and everyone worshiped the Lord. This continued until the last animal was sacrificed.
29After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord. 30Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
31Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.”
The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices. 32Seventy bulls, 100 rams, and 200 lambs were brought as sacrifices to please the Lord; 33600 bulls and 3,000 sheep were brought as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing. 34There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned. 35Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar.
So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord. 36Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_text:
Bése Hesekia Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga
1Akwa aavlanyɔ-alɔ na Hesekia ɔ́ƒɔ asa na bése-nwu Yudaƒuɔ lɛga. Na úlie Yerusalem mmɔ ɔ́di lɛga akwa aavlanyɔ-yaalenwi. Na uni ndi Sekaria ubidi ɔni baalɔ Abiya. 2Hesekia únu Unwoti litemi na ɔ́siaku-nwu kama siin aani nwuna nana ati Dawid kalɛ.
Básɔku Kakpakɔ Kammɔ Bábla Kedee
3Na nwuna lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa lideedi lɛmmɔ kɔbuli kudeedi kɔni baalɔ bani Abib iye Nisan kemmo ni, Hesekia ɔ́ya na bálɛmi Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ kɔyakun na bɔsɔku-ku báklibi. 4Na ɔ́ya na bálɔ bakpane bammɔ ku lewiƒuɔ bammɔ usienku kakpakɔ kaduli kani na kewi késie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. 5Mmɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Uwi údu ka bɔsɔku bula bati kuuku Unwoti Katɔti kakpakɔ bɔbla kedee. Na amii Lewiƒuɔ na ɔdi ka bɛka lɛlɔ bɔbla kedee ɔdi ɔmmɔ bɔbla kalɛ na biduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo na bitéti ala ani ƒui muusé lɛlɔ na Katɔti ulawia-nya ulanu mmɔ bɛlɛku. 6Bula bati kuuku badi ɔbladu útadia bɔnu munu munu, ɔsika bátasiaku-nwu kama siin. Na ɔɔɔdi ɔmmɔ lɛti mmomu béni Katɔti kakpakɔ muedi ƒui kede kede. 7Bákalɛ kakpakɔ kammɔ bényene na lɛsogya lɛmmɔ ƒui líni. Na basɔ balákyula oloƒui ɔdi iye babla akpala adi bete Katɔti lɛnɔ.
8“Kɔnyi kpakplaa geen na Katɔti úti ɔ́kya Yuda kadi bekyuli ku Yerusalemƒuɔ. Na ala ani ƒui na ɔ́bla úti ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu adi liƒu ala geen ete bekyuli bani nánu ala amɛni kalɛkɔ. Na ɔɔɔdi 9bukpi kani na bula bati kuuku békpi na kekpokɔ, mmomu béƒie abu alati bula bebi ku beleku lɛnɔ bátɔlɔku. 10Anwuɔsu lɛ́lɛ ugyii geen ka bɔsɔku abu ku Israel Unwoti Katɔti ntɛ bunyimi bɔbla ɔwɔdi. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ si bɔ́bla ɔmɛni ni, nwuna kɔnyi na bula lɛlɔ kɔdubɔyɔ-nwu. 11Anwuɔsu ni, banwa, bitaya na bubile uwi. Amii na Unwoti ɔ́ƒuna ka bɛbla nwuna bakpane na biti akpala bite-nwu.”
12-14Amu na uwi ɔni na Hesekia ɔ́wɔlɔ-ma bɔtɛmiku ni, Lewiƒuɔ batɔnkune bani nsia bésie mmɔ bése kabla kalɔ kɔnakunwi. Na bana anyi ndubo mɛni.
Amasai ubidi Mahat ku Asaria ubidi Yoel bani nási Kohat kɔdua kemmo.
Na Abdi ubidi Kis ku Yehalel ubidi Asaria ama lɛnɔ bási Merari kɔdua kemmo.
Na Sima ubidi Yoa ku Yoa ubidi Eden ama lɛnɔ bási Gerson kɔdua kemmo.
Na Simri ku Yeuel bási Elsaƒan kɔdua.
Na Sekaria ku Matania ama bási Asaƒ kɔdua.
Na Yehuel ku Simei bási Heman kɔdua.
Na Semaia ku Usiel bási Yedutun kɔdua.
15Batɔnkune bamɛni bátásala Lewiƒuɔ bakladi na bana ƒui bábla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ kalɛ na bese sɛɛn. Na ɔmmɔ kama bése kalɔ baabla kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛnɔ kedee ɔkɛnku Unwoti ɔda bubo kenye aani kalɛ na Ɔga Hesekia úbo ɔda kalɛ.
16Bakpane bammɔ béduo kakpakɔ kemmo na bátáda ala ani ƒui na muusé lɛlɔ mmɔ bédie bébewi kakpakɔ kaduli kemmo. Na ɔmmɔ kama Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bála-nya bálɛku ɔmmɔ kemmo bétéwi kesii kani baalɔ banii Kidron Kɔwɛ kemmo.
17Bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bése kabla kamɛni kalɔ na kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ. Na uyolu unwi na béti bábla kakpakɔ kaduli kamɛni sɛɛn. Na uyolu unyɔdi lɛnɔ na béti bábla kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔlati lɛnɔ sɛɛn.
Anwuɔsu limeyi leevu-lɛkundi lɛlɔ ni, 18bénwini bésie Ɔga Hesekia kudɔ na bátásu-nwu banini, “Ɔga Ɔbune, bɔ́wɔlɔ bula kabla na kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui kese sɛɛn. Na Katɔti lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ku ebui ku akyami ammɔ ƒui ku bodobodo kedee ɔmmɔ kasiakɔ ka akyami ani kemmo na beeƒí-nwu mmɔ bene ƒui ese sɛɛn. 19Ɔƒɛni ala ani ƒui na Ɔga Ahas uti ɔ́lɛku kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo uwi ɔni na útadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ mmɔ ni, bɔ́sɔku-nya búboku na bɔ́bla-nya sɛɛn na búti-nya búse ana kesekɔ na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ anumi.”
Bekyuli Bammɔ Bésie Kakpakɔ Bátábla Akpala
20Mmɔ kani na Hesekia ɔ́lɔ Yerusalemƒuɔ bakutine bammɔ ɔ́sala na bɔ́tɔlɔ bésie kakpakɔ mmɔ. 21Na badanku ɔmantɛ bɔkɔ maatɛ ku baƒonu bagyani maatɛ ku baƒonu bɔkɔdi maatɛ ku betukpa leevu bani na badubuti babla ekpidi lili buvele akpala na Hesekia ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli lili ku Yuda kadi bekyuli ƒui lili ku kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui bɔbla kedee ɔsu. Anwuɔsu Hesekia ɔ́su bakpane bani ndi Aaron kaba kemmo bebi ɔnii beti bebuo bammɔ bakpa na Katɔti lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.
22Amu na bakpane bammɔ lɛnɔ bádu ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ ku baƒonu bagyani bammɔ na bákuna béwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. 23Na béti bese bammɔ ama bésienku Hesekia ku bekyuli bani nébo kakpakɔ mmɔ na béti bana enu básia-ma eli. 24Ɔmmɔ kama bakpane bammɔ bádu bese bammɔ na béti bana ubugya bákuna béwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ aani ekpidi lili buvele akpala na Israelƒuɔ ƒui lili.
25Amu na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Hesekia ɔ́ya na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bésie béténye bana kunyekɔ na bana kabla kenye na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. Na úti enukpɛ agyala ku lɛbentaa ku agyala bamba ani na béti kɔbuli bábla úte-ma aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Ɔga Dawid ku kenye bediene bani ndi Gad ku Natan ɔda kalɛ. 26Na Lewiƒuɔ báklibi lɛlɔ na benye kagyumana ka bagya agyala ani adi Ɔga Salomo adi mmɔ. Na bakpane bammɔ lɛnɔ báklibi na benye kagyumana ka bavwi kɔkpɛɛ kɔmmɔ.
27Amu na uwi ɔni kani na Hesekia údie kɔnu ɔ́tina bekyuli bammɔ ka bese kalɔ ku akpala ammɔ bɔkyula na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bagyane bammɔ lɛnɔ bése kalɔ beedie bumwi lɛnu na baagyá bana agyala 28na ukyuli biala ɔɔkya lili kalɔ teete Unwoti na bábu-nwu. Na ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani na bewi útédu ka bákyula lɛla biala báwɔlɔ.
29Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Hesekia ku kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bálɛ akɔnkɔ kalɔ na bákya lili kalɔ béte Unwoti. 30Na Hesekia ku nwuna bakutine benengu bammɔ bébo Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔda banii beteedie bumwi lɛnu lɛni na Ɔga Dawid ku Kenye Udiene Asaƒ bénweni bése mmɔ. Anwuɔsu béboku eli kalɔ na bédie bumwi lɛnɔ béte Unwoti ku lɛlɔyɔ.
31Amu na Hesekia ɔ́su kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Ka bɔ́sɔku lɛlɔ bɔ́bla ɔwɔdi búte bula Unwoti ɔsu ni, biti bina etela ku akpala biboku na biti bibagya-nwu enu.”
Bekyuli bammɔ bábla lɛni na bádi muedi béti bebuo béboku ku kaƒɔ ƒaa banii badu-ma bakpa. 32Na bebuo bammɔ bumomo bɔdi ɔmantɛ bakɔ liti ku aavlanyɔ ku baƒonu bagyani eti anyɔ ku baƒonu bakɔdi eti ene banii beti bakyula na babla akpala ani mɔɔyɔ́ Unwoti kaƒɔ. 33Na bada ɔmantɛ bakɔ eti leevu-anyɔ ku baƒonu mpim ɛtɛ béboku banii bakyula na béti ɔmmɔ beevele Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ ka ɔsiaku-ma. 34Nsu bakpane bammɔ beeemomo kalɛ na bakana bebuo bammɔ ƒui lɛku budie, ɔsika ɔɔɔdi bakpane bammɔ ƒui nákana lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ bɔbla kalɛ na babla kabla kammɔ. Nsu ka Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ama bana ƒui bábla lɛlɔ sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, bébunku bakpane bammɔ útédu ka bédie ebuo ukplodi ɔku báwɔlɔ. 35Na bebuo bani na bádu bákyula bábla akpala ammɔ kama ni, beti bana ƒui lɛmwi bábakyula kede aani unwi bɔbla akpala na béti ntɛ akpala ammɔ ƒui lɛnɔ béwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.
Anwuɔsu kakpakɔ kammɔ kásɔ kénwini kébese aani kuuku kalɛ, na baakpá Unwoti na mmɔ. 36Na Hesekia ku Yuda kadi bekyuli bammɔ bádi limeyi na lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-ma, ɔsika Unwoti úbunku-ma na bákana na bábla ɔmɛni kɔnakunwi.

english_text:
Hezekiah Prepares To Celebrate Passover
1-4 Passover wasn't celebrated in the first month, which was the usual time, because many of the priests were still unclean and unacceptable to serve, and because not everyone in Judah had come to Jerusalem for the festival. So Hezekiah, his officials, and the people agreed to celebrate Passover in the second month.
Hezekiah sent a message to everyone in Israel and Judah, including those in the territories of Ephraim and West Manasseh, inviting them to the temple in Jerusalem for the celebration of Passover in honor of the Lord God of Israel. 5Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
6Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter:
People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry. 7Don't follow the example of your ancestors and your Israelite relatives in the north. They were unfaithful to the Lord, and he punished them horribly. 8Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry, 9and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
10The messengers went to every town in Ephraim and West Manasseh as far north as the territory of Zebulun, but people laughed and insulted them. 11Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem. 12God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded.
Passover Is Celebrated
13In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread. 14They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
15-17Then, on the fourteenth day of that same month, the Levites began killing the lambs for Passover, because many of the worshipers were unclean and were not allowed to kill their own lambs. Meanwhile, some of the priests and Levites felt ashamed because they had not gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean. They immediately went through that ceremony and went to the temple, where they offered sacrifices to please the Lord. Then the priests and Levites took their positions, according to the Law of Moses, the servant of God.
As the Levites killed the lambs, they handed some of the blood to the priests, who splattered it on the altar.
18-19Most of the people that came from Ephraim, West Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not made themselves clean, but they ignored God's Law and ate the Passover lambs anyway. Hezekiah found out what they had done and prayed, “Lord God, these people are unclean according to the laws of holiness. But they are worshiping you, just as their ancestors did. So, please be kind and forgive them.” 20The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
21The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments. 22Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration.
The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors. 23Everyone was so excited that they agreed to celebrate seven more days.
24So Hezekiah gave the people 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep to be offered as sacrifices and to be used as food for the sacred meals. His officials gave 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep, and many more priests agreed to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. 25Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel. 26It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David. 27The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
translation_text:
Hesekia Ɔ́klibi Lɛlɔ Ka Ɔdi Kukpi Lili Bɔvi Limeyi
1Hesekia ɔ́sia Israel ku Yuda kadi bekyuli kenye ka bebo Unwoti Katɔti kakpakɔ na Yerusalem na badi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi. Na ɔ́sia Eƒraim ku Manase kalɛkɛ badi lɛnɔ ƒui kenye ka bebo. 2Na Ɔga ku nwuna bakutine benengu ku kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ na Yerusalem bálɛ ugyii ka badi Kukpi Likpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi lɛmmɔ na kɔbuli kunyɔdi kemmo. 3Bátakana limeyi lɛmɛni bɔdi na kɔbuli kedeedi kemmo aani kalɛ na use use, ɔsika bakpane pii bátakana lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ bɔbla na baklibi lɛlɔ bete limeyi lɛmmɔ bɔdi. Na bekyuli pii lɛnɔ bátakana bubo bubasala na Yerusalem mmɔ. 4Na Ɔga ku kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bánu ka kasusu kammɔ kadia. 5Anwuɔsu básia Israel kalɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui kenye ɔ́si Beerseba útédu Dan na bálɔ-ma ka bebo Yerusalem mmɔ na badi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi bete Unwoti Israel Katɔti. Na benengu bammɔ alati baatina ka ɔ́si kuuku ƒui ni, bátasiaku bekyuli lisu lɛmɛni udu ka bebo limeyi lɛmɛni kadikɔ lɛni kudii.
6Amu na Hesekia batu bani na ɔ́tala mmɔ báyu ulu linyesia ɔku ɔmɛni bésienku Israel kesii biala. Na ɔku ɔmmɔ kenye kaasu kanini,
“Israel kadi bekyuli, ka kuli kɔ́dia-bu na bɔ́lɛ Asiria baga enu kemmo na kekpo kéteƒie-bu ƒui ni, bɛya na ɔƒɛni anwu bunwini bubo Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na bula bati kuuku Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob bákpa kudɔ. Na si bɛ́bla ɔmɛni ni, ɔdubɔda kɔnyi buti bɔkya-bu ɔya. 7Bitasiaku bina bati kuuku ku Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli bani na bakya kalɔ kammɔ kɔtɔ kakɛ mmɔ. Bátasiaku Unwoti kama siin, anwuɔsu na ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu geen. 8Na bitabla atuɔkplu aani bina bati kuuku bammɔ. Bɛlɛ ugyii geen ɔƒɛni ka bɛdubɔdi Unwoti bula Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ! Bibo Yerusalem na bibadi limeyi na bɛkpa-nwu na nwuna kakpakɔ kani ndubɔdi nwuna kadi uwi ƒui na ɔdubɔda kɔnyi buti bɔkya-bu ɔya.
9“Na bekisine bani néƒie bina lɛlɔ bekyuli badi bátɔlɔku ni, badubɔya na basɔ benwini bebo ɔma. Unwoti Katɔti ubo lɛƒɔndia na ɔɔnu kɔnyana. Na si bínwini bíbo-nwu kudɔ ni, ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo nwuna kama bunwini bɔkya-mii kudii.”
10Na sɔsɔ ni, batu bammɔ lɛnɔ bésie ɔma biala kemmo na Eƒraim kalɛkɛ ku Manase kalɛkɛ na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ. Na béti bákɔ bésie katɔ ƒui bétédu Sebulon kalɛkɛ kemmo, nsu bɔma kani ukyuli biala ɔ́ma-ma na bédumi-ma. 11Nkyuli ɛlɛɛ badi kani nási Aser ku Manase kakɛ kani nésie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ku Sebulon adua kemmo béboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na bébo Yerusalem. 12Na Katɔti ɔlati ɔ́ya na lɛlɔ kemmo kaatɔ́ ɔdi biala na Yuda ƒui ka babla lɛla lɛni na Hesekia ku nwuna benengu básu mmɔ.
13Na kɔbuli kunyɔdi kemmo ni, bekyuli lisu bonwu lɛdi líbo líbasala na Yerusalem ka badi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi. 14Na akpabi ani na bátu bálɛ Yerusalem béte kadi bamba baƒiɔ biala ku oloƒui kɔkyulakɔ ƒui ni, bágyu ala ammɔ bene ƒui bétébo béwi Kidron Kɔwɛ kemmo.
15-17Amu na kɔbuli kunyɔdi kɔmmɔ kuna limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ ni, Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bése kalɔ ku baƒonu bakɔdi bɔdu úte Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi Bɔdi, ɔsika bekyuli bani nébo babakpa mmɔ pii beeese sɛɛn na ɔdi kenye na bétete-ma kuƒi ka badu bebuo bammɔ ama alati. Na lɛnɔ ni, bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ badi lɛnɔ bátabla lɛlɔ sɛɛn bétese na ɔdi ɔmmɔ kenye na kɔƒa geen kuukpó-ma. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu usi na bakɛ na bábla ɔmmɔ kɔnakunwi na béduo kakpakɔ na bátákyula akpala ani mɔɔyɔ́ Unwoti kaƒɔ béte-nwu. Ɔmmɔ kama bakpane bammɔ ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bésie béténye bana kunyekɔ aani kalɛ na Katɔti kabla ɔblane Mose ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔ́tina.
18-19Bekyuli bani na bási Eƒraim ku Manase ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ ku Isakar ku Sebulon bébo mmɔ akɔ pii bátakana lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ kemmo bɔvi, nsu bédie Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ atu na ama lɛnɔ bádi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia adila ammɔ. Hesekia ɔ́nu ɔmmɔ ɔ́ti, anwuɔsu ɔ́kpali Katɔti na úvele-nwu ɔnini, “Unwoti Katɔti bekyuli bamɛni beeese sɛɛn na lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ kenye, nsu ama lɛnɔ benye baakya lili kalɔ teete-ɔ aani kalɛ na bana bati kuuku bábla, anwuɔsu muuvele-ɔ nu-ma kɔnyana na eti akyiɛ-ma.” 20Na Unwoti lɛnɔ únu kalɛ na Hesekia ɔ́kpali-nwu úvele mmɔ na úti bana bɔƒiɔ bɔmmɔ ɔ́kyiɛ-ma sɔsɔ na útani-ma kɔtu.
21Lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ Israelƒuɔ bani nkya Yerusalem mmɔ geen na bádi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi emeyi maatɛ sɔɔn. Na Lewiƒuɔ ku bakpane bammɔ bédie lɛnu bémwi Unwoti limeyi ndi limeyi na baagyá bana agyala ammɔ ƒui. 22Hesekia ɔ́gya Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ enu na kabla kabuni kani na bábla ɔsu ku kalɛ na bátɔnku lɛkpa na emeyi ammɔ bɔdi kemmo.
Bekyuli bani nébo mmɔ bábakpa lɛnɔ bádi limeyi lɛmmɔ emeyi maatɛ sɔɔn na béteeboku etela ani na béti bákpa na baadi adila kedee na baagyá bana bati kuuku Unwoti Katɔti enu. 23Limeyi bɔdi bɔmɛni bɔ́da ukyuli biala ebiti geen ɔni na bana ƒui bénu kalɔ besie anumi badi-ni emeyi maatɛ bamba bebu.
24Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Hesekia úte bekyuli bammɔ ɔmantɛ bakɔ apim unwi ku baƒonu mpim maatɛ ka beti bakpa na badi-nya lɛnɔ aani adila kedee. Na nwuna benengu ama béte ɔmantɛ bakɔ apim unwi ku baƒonu mpim leevu. Bakpane pii lɛnɔ bénu kalɔ ka babla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ.
25Lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ ukyuli biala geen ku bani na bási Yuda ku Israel ku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui ku baƒɔ bani na bakya Yuda ku Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. 26Na ka ɔ́si Dawid ubidi Ɔga Salomo uwi ƒui ni, limeyi lɛni ndi limeyi linengudi ƒui lɛmɛni udu, bátadi-ni kudii. 27Bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bévele Katɔti ka ɔya na nwuna kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku bekyuli bammɔ na sɔsɔ ni, únu-ma buvele ɔ́siku nwuna keliekɔ kedee kammɔ na katɔ ƒui.

english_text:
The People Destroy the Local Shrines
(2 Kings 18.4)
1After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. They destroyed all the local shrines and foreign altars in Judah, as well as those in the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and West Manasseh. Then everyone went home.
Offerings for the Priests and Levites
2Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates. 3 Hezekiah provided animals from his own herds and flocks to use for the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as for the sacrifices during the Sabbath celebrations, the New Moon Festivals, and the other religious feasts required by the Law of the Lord.
4 He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work. 5As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops. 6The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord. 7The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later. 8When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
9Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings. 10The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
11So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed, 12-13all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah. 14Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites. 15-16He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah.
Every priest and every Levite over 30 years old who worked daily in the temple received part of these offerings, according to their duties. 17The priests were listed in the official records by clans, and the Levites 20 years old and older were listed by their duties. 18The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
19Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
20-21Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
translation_text:
Bábwɛ Kadi Bamba Baƒiɔ Biala Na Kalɔ Kammɔ
1Ka bádi limeyi lɛmmɔ báwɔlɔ ni, bekyuli bammɔ bésie Yuda lɛma ƒui kemmo na bátábwɛ atabi baƒiɔ bani ƒui na bátu bálɛ lɛma lɛmmɔ kemmo. Na békulo lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ béte Asera baƒiɔ mmɔ ƒui béwi kalɔ. Na baƒiɔ lidu biala na bátu na abi eli ku bana akpabi ƒui ni, bábwɛ-ma na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui ku Benyamin ku Eƒraim ku Manase ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ ƒui béwi kalɔ na bátɔlɔ bésie bana kɔduli.
Ɔlɛka Beboku Bakpane Ku Lewiƒuɔ Etela
2Hesekia úle bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔ́kya kasala esu esu kemmo ɔkɛnku bana kabla kenye. Na úti akpala bɔkyula ku unwi bɔbla akpala kabla ɔ́kya-ma enu kemmo. Na úte babambadi ka beteete kebunku na bataabla bekyuli kabla na kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na badi lɛnɔ beteedie bumwi lɛnu na kakpakɔ lɛban kenye. 3Hesekia úte bebuo ɔ́siku nwuna bebuo akɔ bani na badubuti bataabla akpala na ɔtanta ku useyi uwi ku lɛnwunameyi biala ku emeyi buni bɔdi kemmo ku kɔbuli kɔwɔdi bɔlɛ limeyi bɔdi ku emeyi buni bamba ani na Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔtina kalɛ.
4Hesekia ɔ́su Yerusalemƒuɔ bammɔ ka beboku etela ani na badubuti bete bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ kalɛ na bakɛ uwi babla Katɔti kabla na bana kabla kani kenye na benye kemmo. 5Uwi ɔni kani na bekyuli bamɛni bénu lɛla lɛni na ɔga ɔɔwia ka babla mmɔ ni, béti bana akɛla lɛkpa leevudi béboku úbunku anta ku kamu udu edula ani na bebo ku nnɔ ku uwɔ ku edula bamba lɛnɔ. 6Lɛni kani na bekyuli bani na bási Yuda lɛma bamba kemmo lɛnɔ béti bana bebuo bani na bebo lɛkpa leevudi ku ala ani ƒui na béti béte Katɔti na bábla-nya kedee mmɔ lɛkpa leevudi béboku. 7Bekyuli bammɔ bése kalɔ beeti bana etela teeboku Yerusalem na kɔbuli kɔtɛdi kɔni na baalɔ banii Sivan kemmo. Na abuli ene kama asa na béboku etela akladi. 8Ka Hesekia ku nwuna benengu bánu ala amɛni ni, bágya Unwoti ku bekyuli bammɔ enu.
9Amu na Hesekia úye ɔkpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ kalɛ na etela esu ani na beeboku-ma mmɔ ese. 10Na ɔkpane unengudi ɔni nákya uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo na baalɔ-nwu Asaria ɔni ndi Sadok kaba kemmo ubi ni, údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔ́si uwi ɔni bekyuli bammɔ bése kalɔ ku ala amɛni buboku ni, bɔ́kɛ adila ku ala bamba na etulo kalɛ na bɔɔwia muedi. Na bɔ́nu bɔ́ti ka Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku bula bekyuli sɔsɔ. Nu ala ani udu nébu!”
11Amu na ɔga ɔ́ya na bátu ala kesekɔ na kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ. Na ka báwɔlɔ-ka bɔtu ni, 12-13etela bamba ani lɛlɔ kabla na baaadubo bɔbla kɔnakunwi kɔmmɔ ni, baaklibi-nya teese mmɔ. Na Ɔga Hesekia ku ɔkpane unengudi Asaria báƒuna Lewini ɔni baalɔ Konania na ɔɔnu ala ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔnwani Simei ndi nwuna ubunkune ku Lewiƒuɔ bamba bani ndi Yehiel ku Asasia ku Natan ku Asahel ku Yerimot ku Yosabad ku Eliel ku Ismakia ku Mahat ku Benaia. 14Na Imna ubidi Kore na báƒuna ka utaanu ɔban kenye kani nkya késie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na anwu kani mɔɔƒɔ́ kaƒɔ ƒaa etela ani na bekyuli beeboku Katɔti na uule-nya teete bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ. 15-16Kore ɔmɛni ubo bebunkune ɛku bamba bani mɔɔnu ka ala ani na béle mɛni édu bakpane bakladi bani na bakya Yuda lɛma bamba ƒui kemmo. Na bana anyi ndi Eden ku Miniamin ku Yesua ku Semaia ku Amaria ku Sekania.
Ɔƒɛni ɔkpane ku Lewini biala na ɔ́ɔƒɔ utulo akwa avlaatɛ na ɔɔbla kabla limeyi ndi limeyi na kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ bebo kadikɔ na etela amɛni kemmo ɔkɛnku bana kabla kenye. 17Bénweni bakpane bamɛni anyi bákya bakpane ɔku ɔni na ɔtɛ use na adua ammɔ kemmo. Na Lewiƒuɔ bani náaƒɔ akwa aavlanyɔ ku bani na betulo lɛni ni, bénweni-ma anyi na bana kabla kani na baabla kenye. 18Na anyi bunweni lɛku lɛmɛni lɛdanku bana beleku ku bebi ƒui lɛnɔ, ɔsika ama lɛnɔ baadi litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na baabla lɛlɔ sɛɛn na báƒɔ Unwoti anu ka babla-nwu kabla.
19Hesekia ɔ́ƒuna bekyuli badi úse kalɛ na beti bakpane kadikɔ kamɛni besienku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bani na bakya akpaklɔ na bebuo kadikɔ na Yuda lɛma ku amadɔ mmɔ ƒui. Nsu ɔlɛka bakpane bammɔ babla Aaron kaba kemmo bebi na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ ɔlɛka bana anyi akya Lewiƒuɔ lɛku lɛni na lɛtɛ lise kemmo.
20-21Ala ani ƒui na Hesekia ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔɔdi Yuda lɛga ku ala ani ƒui na ɔ́bla úse kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo na Yerusalem ni, adia na ese siin. Nwuna lɛgadi lɛ́lɛ kɔsia, ɔsika ɔ́di Unwoti Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ ku nwuna kayi ƒui.

english_text:
King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah
(2 Kings 18.13-37; Isaiah 36.1-22)
1After King Hezekiah had faithfully obeyed the Lord's instructions by doing these things, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded Judah. He attacked the fortified cities and thought he would capture every one of them.
2As soon as Hezekiah learned that Sennacherib was planning to attack Jerusalem, 3-4he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.
5Hezekiah's workers also repaired the broken sections of the city wall. Then they built defense towers and an outer wall to help protect the one already there. The landfill on the east side of David's City was also strengthened.
He gave orders to make a large supply of weapons and shields, 6and he appointed army commanders over the troops. Then he gathered the troops together in the open area in front of the city gate and said to them:
7Be brave and confident! There's no reason to be afraid of King Sennacherib and his powerful army. We are much more powerful, 8because the Lord our God fights on our side. The Assyrians must rely on human power alone.
These words encouraged the army of Judah.
9When Sennacherib and his troops were camped at the town of Lachish, he sent a message to Hezekiah and the people in Jerusalem. It said:
10I am King Sennacherib of Assyria, and I have Jerusalem surrounded. Do you think you can survive my attack? 11Hezekiah your king is telling you that the Lord your God will save you from me. But he is lying, and you'll die of hunger and thirst. 12Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? And didn't he tell you people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
13You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us? 14None of those gods kept their people safe from the kings of Assyria. Do you really think your God can do any better? 15Don't be fooled by Hezekiah! No god of any nation has ever been able to stand up to Assyria. Believe me, your God cannot keep you safe!
16The Assyrian officials said terrible things about the Lord God and his servant Hezekiah. 17Sennacherib's letter even made fun of the Lord. It said, “The gods of other nations could not save their people from Assyria's army, and neither will the God that Hezekiah worships.” 18The officials said all these things in Hebrew, so that everyone listening from the city wall would understand and be terrified and surrender. 19The officials talked about the Lord God as if he were nothing but an ordinary god or an idol that someone had made.
The Death of King Sennacherib
(2 Kings 19.14-19,35-37; Isaiah 37.14-20; 37.36-38)
20Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz begged the Lord for help, 21and he sent an angel that killed every soldier and commander in the Assyrian camp.
Sennacherib returned to Assyria, completely disgraced. Then one day he went into the temple of his god where some of his sons killed him.
22The Lord rescued Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib and also protected them from other enemies. 23People brought offerings to Jerusalem for the Lord and expensive gifts for Hezekiah, and from that day on, every nation on earth respected Hezekiah.
Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies
(2 Kings 20.1-11; Isaiah 38.1-8)
24About this same time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. He prayed, and the Lord gave him a sign that he would recover. 25But Hezekiah was so proud that he refused to thank the Lord for everything he had done for him. This made the Lord angry, and he punished Hezekiah and the people of Judah and Jerusalem. 26Hezekiah and the people later felt sorry and asked the Lord to forgive them. So the Lord did not punish them as long as Hezekiah was king.
Hezekiah's Wealth
(2 Kings 20.12-19; Isaiah 39.1-8)
27Hezekiah was very rich, and everyone respected him. He built special rooms to store the silver, the gold, the precious stones and spices, the shields, and the other valuable possessions. 28Storehouses were also built for his supply of grain, wine, and olive oil; barns were built for his cattle, and pens were put up for his sheep. 29God made Hezekiah extremely rich, so he bought even more sheep, goats, and cattle. And he built towns where he could keep all these animals.
30It was Hezekiah who built a tunnel that carried the water from Gihon Spring into the city of Jerusalem. In fact, everything he did was successful! 31Even when the leaders of Babylonia sent messengers to ask Hezekiah about the sign God had given him, God let Hezekiah give his own answer to test him and to see if he would remain faithful.
Hezekiah Dies
(2 Kings 20.20,21)
32Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including how faithful he was to the Lord, is included in the records kept by Isaiah the prophet. These are written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 33When Hezekiah died, he was buried in the section of the royal tombs that was reserved for the most respected kings, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem honored him. His son Manasseh then became king.
translation_text:
Asiria Ɔga Sanaherib Úkpo Yudaƒuɔ
1Ka Ɔga Hesekia ɔ́di Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ na ɔ́bla ala amɛni ƒui ɔ́wɔlɔ lɛni ni, Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Sanaherib ɔ́bla kasusu ka usie utékpoku Yuda. Na útékpo lɛma linengudi lɛni na bátu awodu bonwu bámana mmɔ na ɔ́kali ka ɔdubɔkana-ni bɔbwɛ na uƒie-ma ɔtɔlɔku.
2Uwi ɔni kemmo na Ɔga Hesekia ɔ́ti ka kasusu kamɛni udu na Sanaherib uuti na Yerusalem lɛlɔ ni, 3-4anwu ku nwuna benengu bábla kasusu ka abiɔ ku ntu bɔni ƒui na bɔkya keyi na awodu ammɔ kama ni, beekúlo-mu kalɛ na si Asiriaƒuɔ bébo mmɔ ni, na balákɛ ntu bɔdi baláni.
5Amu na Hesekia ɔ́ya na batune badi bátásɔku ɔma ɔmmɔ kowodu kesii kani nábwɛ mmɔ báklibi. Na ɔ́ya na bátu kɔgyumanakɔ, na bátu kowodu bamba kɔni nábwɛ mmɔ kama. Na awodu kugyikpo kɔni na bátu bédi Dawid ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ awodu ani nésie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ lɛnɔ ni, básɔ báklibi-nya bɔtu kaduɛ.
Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ya na bábla ekpola ku kekpo kayi agyumanala pii. 6Na ɔ́ƒuna bekpone batɔnkune bani ndubɔtɔnku bekpone esu esu ammɔ. Amu na ɔ́lɔ bekpone esu esu ammɔ ɔ́sala kanwaadikɔ na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ anumi na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, 7“Bise kayi na bɛƒɔ lɛlɔ bɛdi! Naaanu lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ɔlɛka bɛyia Ɔga Sanaherib ku nwuna bekpone kpakplaa bammɔ. Abu bubo ɔyikun butulo-nwu ƒui. 8Ɔsika Unwoti bula Katɔti muukpó bula kekpo teete-bu. Na Asiriaƒuɔ ama ni, bekyuli keeke ɔyikun lɛlɔ na bana anu asia.”
Ka Yudaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ bénu etemila amɛni ni, ákya-ma kayi ogya geen.
9Amu na uwi ɔni na Ɔga Sanaherib ku nwuna bekpone bébo bábada keliekɔ na bakya Lakis ɔma ni, ɔ́kya Ɔga Hesekia ku Yerusalemƒuɔ ɔtu ɔdi ɔnini,
10“Ami Siriaƒuɔ Ɔga Sanaherib mɔɔyá-a na ati ka lɛ́ɛka lɛ́mana Yerusalem na muuye-ɔ si aakali ka adubɔkana-mi kekpo kenye bunye na akɛ ngba? 11Amii Yerusalemƒuɔ bina Ɔga Hesekia ɔɔsu-mii ka bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo bukpo bute-mii na ɔƒɔ-mii ngba, nsu bɔtɔlɔ na ɔda-mii na bɛdubo mmɔ bɔkya na kɔka ku ntukwɛ ɔdu-mii. 12Ɔɔɔdi Hesekia ɔlati ntɔnku-mii na úbo baƒiɔ akpabi ƒui ku ani na akya abi eli ƒui ɔ́bwɛ na ɔ́su amii Yuda ku Yerusalemƒuɔ ɔnini, ‘Lɛkpabi linwi pɛ lɛlɔ na ɔdi ka bɛkpa na bɛkyula oloƒui’?
13“Bínu lɛla lɛni na ami ku mina bati kuuku bɔ́bla kadi bamba bekyuli ƒui. Bɔkana na bana baƒiɔ badi bákana kadi kadi bekyuli bɔƒɔ? 14Mɔɔsu-mii ka baƒiɔ badi bátakana bana bekyuli ngba bɔƒɔ na bakɛ bɔnwuna na Siriaƒuɔ baga ɔdi enu kemmo. Na bɔkali geen na amii bɛda bɛnii bina Katɔti anwu ɔdubɔkana lɛla lɛdi bɔbla butulo baƒiɔ bamba bammɔ? 15Bitaya na Hesekia use-mii lisusu lɛmmɔ udu! Baƒiɔ badi bátakana bunye bɔsiaku Asiria kudii na baƒɔ bana kadi bekyuli badi. Anwuɔsu bɛƒɔ-mi bɛdi ka bina Katɔti lɛnɔ ɔɔɔdubo-mii bɔkana bɔƒɔ!”
16Asiriaƒuɔ benengu bammɔ bátɛmi enyekpi na bédumi Unwoti Katɔti ku nwuna kabla ɔblane Ɔga Hesekia. 17Na ɔku ɔni na Sanaherib únweni kemmo ni, ɔ́kya Unwoti lɛlɔ lɛma na ɔ́su ɔnini,
“Kadi bamba baƒiɔ bátakana bana kadi bekyuli bɔƒɔ bɔsiku Asiriaƒuɔ enu kemmo na Hesekia Katɔti ɔni na ɔɔkpá lɛnɔ ɔɔɔdubo lɛla lɛdi bɔkana bɔbla.”
18Na ala amɛni ƒui ni, Yudaƒuɔ lɛdi kemmo na Asiria benengu bammɔ benye baasu-nya kalɛ na si Yerusalemƒuɔ bani na bakya ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo na awodu ammɔ kemmo bénu ni, na bayia na bete lili. 19Na geen ni, bɔtɛmi kani na benengu bammɔ benye baatɛmi Unwoti Katɔti lɛlɔ kɔtɛ aani baƒiɔ keeke badi iye ala ani na bekyuli keeke nábla-ma bése lɛlɔ.
Ɔga Sanaherib Úkpi
20Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Hesekia ku Amos ubidi Kenye Udiene Yesaia bévele Unwoti ka ubunku-ma. 21Na Unwoti úmene nwuna ɔtu ɔdi na úbo na úbadu ukpone biala ku bana kekpo batɔnkune ƒui na Asiriaƒuɔ keliekɔ kani na báda na belie mmɔ kemmo.
Amu na Sanaherib ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie Asiria ku kɔƒa geen. Na ɔmmɔ kama limeyi lɛdi ni, úsie nwuna koƒiodu na ɔƒiɔtɔ kemmo mmɔ na anwu ɔlati bebi bananabi bádu-nwu.
22Unwoti údie Hesekia ku Yerusalemƒuɔ ƒui na Sanaherib enu ku bekisine bamba enu kemmo. 23Bekyuli béti etela béboku Unwoti na Yerusalem na béboku Hesekia ala ani na áƒɔ kuye geen. Na ka ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, kadi bamba bekyuli baabu Hesekia geen.
24Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na ɔlɛ ɔdi úbebo Hesekia ɔni na ɔ́yu-nwu ɔkplu na ɔɔyɔ́ ukpi muedi. Mmɔ na ɔ́kpali Unwoti úvele-nwu na anwu lɛnɔ údie lɛla lɛdi ɔ́tina-nwu ka ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔba-nwu. 25Nsu Hesekia úbo ɔɔtalaku lɛlɔ katɔ geen ɔni na ɔ́yiƒala Unwoti enu muedi bɔgya. Na ɔmɛni ɔdi lɛla lɛni néƒi Unwoti livo, anwuɔsu ɔ́ni Hesekia ku Yuda ku Yerusalemƒuɔ ƒui kɔtu. 26Na kama ƒui ni, bekyuli bamɛni bánu ka báƒiɔ na békpi kɔtɔ na bévele Unwoti banii uti ɔkyiɛ-ma. Anwuɔsu Unwoti ɔ́sɔ útani-ma kɔtu uwi ɔni ƒui na Hesekia ɔ́sɔ úlie utaadi lɛga mmɔ.
Hesekia Ɔ́kɛ Lɛkɛ Geen
27Hesekia úbenwini ɔlakɛne geen na ukyuli biala ɔɔbu-nwu. Ɔ́tu egulabi kesiekɔ kesii kani na uusé nwuna sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku atabi bamba ani na áƒɔ kuye ku kutu akyala ku kekpo kayi agyumanala ku ala lidu bamba ani lɛnɔ náƒɔ kuye geen. 28Ɔ́tu kesii bamba na mmɔ na uusé nwuna edula aani kamu ku antabi udu ku nnɔ. Na ɔ́tu bebuo lidu lidu kɔkyakɔ lɛnɔ, ɔsika Unwoti úte-nwu lɛkɛ geen. 29Katɔti úse ɔ́ya na kɔnu kemmo kadia Hesekia geen, anwuɔsu ɔ́sɔ úye bese ku baƒonu pii úbu ku ɔmantɛ bɔkɔ lɛnɔ. Na ɔ́da akpakɔlɔ pii ute-ma.
30Na údie ubu ɔni kemmo na beeti ntu taasiaku ɔ́si Gihon libiɔ útéduoku Yerusalem ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na sɔsɔ ni, ala ani ƒui na Hesekia ɔ́bla ni, álɛ kɔsia na átɛ geen.
31Na uwi ɔni na Babilonƒuɔ batɔnkune bátala batu badi banii betéye Hesekia na ɔ́su-ma ala adi ɔsiku akɔla budie taatina ani nálɛ na nwuna kalɔ kemmo mmɔ ni, Katɔti únye ɔ́nu Hesekia na anwu ɔlati udie kenye na anwu ɔlati kasusu kenye na ɔnu si ɔmu ɔsiaku-nwu kama siin.
Hesekia Úkpi
32Lɛla bamba biala na Hesekia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔɔdi lɛga mmɔ ku kalɛ na ɔ́siaku Unwoti kama siin ni, bénweni-ni bákya Kenye Udiene Yesaia ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo. 33Uwi ɔni na Hesekia úkpi ni, báva-nwu na kesii kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ ka bataava baga bani lɛlɔ mbo ɔbu geen. Na ukyuli biala na Yuda ku Yerusalem bábu-nwu. Ɔmmɔ kama na bébese ubidi Manase Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga.

english_text:
King Manasseh of Judah
(2 Kings 21.1-9,17,18)
1Manasseh was 12 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 55 years from Jerusalem. 2 Manasseh disobeyed the Lord by following the disgusting customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 3He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. And he continued to worship the stars.
4In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods 5and the stars. He placed these altars in both courtyards of the temple 6-7 and even set up a stone image of a foreign god. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own sons in Hinnom Valley. He did many other sinful things and made the Lord very angry.
Years ago, God had told David and Solomon:
Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there in the temple I will be worshiped forever. 8If my people will faithfully obey all the laws and teaching I gave to my servant Moses, I will never again force them to leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
9But the people of Judah and Jerusalem listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
10The Lord tried to warn Manasseh and the people about their sins, but they ignored the warning. 11So he let Assyrian army commanders invade Judah and capture Manasseh. They put a hook in his nose and tied him up in chains, and they took him to Babylon. 12While Manasseh was held captive there, he asked the Lord God to forgive him and to help him. 13The Lord listened to Manasseh's prayer and saw how sorry he was, and so he let him go back to Jerusalem and rule as king. Manasseh knew from then on that the Lord was God.
14Later, Manasseh rebuilt the eastern section of Jerusalem's outer wall and made it taller. This section went from Gihon Valley north to Fish Gate and around the part of the city called Mount Ophel. He also assigned army officers to each of the fortified cities in Judah.
15Manasseh also removed the idols and the stone image of the foreign god from the temple, and he gathered the altars he had built near the temple and in other parts of Jerusalem. He threw all these things outside the city. 16Then he repaired the Lord's altar and offered sacrifices to thank him and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He gave orders that everyone in Judah must worship the Lord God of Israel. 17The people obeyed Manasseh, but they worshiped the Lord at their own shrines.
18Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his prayer to the Lord God and the warnings from his prophets, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 19Hozai wrote a lot about Manasseh, including his prayer and God's answer. But Hozai also recorded the evil things Manasseh did before turning back to God, as well as a list of places where Manasseh set up idols, and where he built local shrines and places to worship Asherah. 20Manasseh died and was buried near the palace, and his son Amon became king.
King Amon of Judah
(2 Kings 21.19-26)
21Amon was 22 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 2 years. 22Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done, and he worshiped and offered sacrifices to the idols his father had made. 23Manasseh had turned back to the Lord, but Amon refused to do that. Instead, he sinned even more than his father.
24Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace. 25But the people of Judah killed the murderers of Amon and made his son Josiah king.
translation_text:
Manase Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Yuda
1Akwa leevu-anyɔ na Manase ɔ́ƒɔ asa na bése-nwu lɛga na Yuda. Na úlie Yerusalem mmɔ ɔ́di lɛga akwa liti ku ɛlɔ. 2Manase útenu Unwoti litemi mmomu ɔsiaku kadi bamba bekyuli bani na ɔ́bɔku ɔ́lɛku bana kɔlɔ kemmo na Israelƒuɔ anumi mmɔ ɔdi ɔni muusé Unwoti lɛlɔ mmɔ kama. 3Ɔ́sɔku kadi bamba bekyuli bammɔ aƒiodu ani na ɔti Hesekia ɔ́bwɛ mmɔ ɔ́tu. Na ɔ́tu lɛkpabi úte Baal baƒiɔ na ɔ́sɔku Asera baƒiɔ beledi lɛƒiɔgyii ɔ́lɛ. Na ɔsiaku ayabi kama ɔɔkpá-nya.
4Na kakpakɔ geen kemmo muedi kesii kani na nka Unwoti lɛti kani na ɔlɛka bakpa ni, Manase ɔ́tu kadi bamba baƒiɔ akpabi ɔ́lɛ ku 5akpabi bamba úse ka bataakpa ayabi lɛnɔ. Na ɔ́ya na bálɛ akpabi amɛni na Unwoti kakpakɔ kɔduli akpa anyɔ ammɔ kemmo. 6Ɔ́kyula nwuna bebi bananabi ɔ́kpa na Ben Hinom Kɔwɛ kemmo. Na uubó like na ɔɔbla evo ala na ɔɔkpali bekpine ku ayu bamba na ɔ́bla ekpidi bonwu bonwu lidu lidu na Unwoti anumi na ɔ́ya na Unwoti úti kɔnyi geen.
7Manase ɔ́nwi atabi baƒiɔ badi na úti útálɛ Unwoti kakpakɔ. Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Dawid ku ubidi Salomo ɔnini, “Kakpakɔ kamɛni kemmo ku Yerusalem ɔma ɔni na lɛ́ƒuna na Israel bekyuli ƒui akɔ ni, mmɔ na ndubɔsia mina lɛnyi ute uwi ƒui. 8Si mina bekyuli badubɔsia anumi na badi ɔda bubo bɔni na mina kabla ɔblane Mose úte-ma ni, nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo-ma bɔbɔku bɔlɛku kalɔ kani na líti líte bana bati kuuku ka beti benwini bana ɔdi kemmo kudii. 9Nsu Yuda ku Yerusalem bekyuli ƒui béni na bénu Manase litemi mmomu na bábla alaekpidi enengudi ani na etulo ani na kadi bamba bekyuli bani na lɛ́bɔku lɛ́lɛku-ma anumi muedi bábla.”
10Unwoti ɔ́dɔnku Manase ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui kɔlɛ kɔlɛ, nsu béni. 11Anwuɔsu na ɔ́ya na Asiria bekpone benengu bébekpo Yuda na béƒie Manase na béti lɛbuala lɛdi bákya-nwu enwu na bébo-nwu kɔgba na béti-nwu bésienku Babilon. 12Uwi ɔni na kekpo kéƒie Manase na úusie ɔkya mmɔ ni, úvele Unwoti Katɔti ɔnii uti nwuna ekpidi ɔkyiɛ-nwu na ubunku-nwu. 13Unwoti únu-nwu buvele na ɔ́nu kalɛ na nwuna ekpidi éduo-nwu. Anwuɔsu ɔ́ya na ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie Yerusalem na ɔ́sɔ úsie ɔɔdi lɛga. Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ úsela ni, Manase ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Unwoti ndi Katɔti sɔsɔ.
14Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Manase ɔ́sɔku Yerusalem kowodu kɔmadi kɔni nésie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ɔ́tu na ɔ́ya na kɔ́kuku kúbu. Kowodu kakɛ kamɛni kási kesii kani baalɔ banii Gihon Kɔwɛ na ɔkɛ mmɔ na ɔ́kɔ úsie kesii kani baalɔ banii Kabɛ Ɔban kenye. Na ɔ́ka ɔ́mana ɔma kakɛ kani na baalɔ Oƒel Kɔbi. Na lɛma linengudi lɛni na bátu awodu bámana na Yuda ƒui ni, ɔ́ya na bekpone benengu baagyumana-ni.
15Amu na kadi bamba baƒiɔ ku baƒiɔ lɛtabi lɛni na ɔ́tu únyene Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ ni, ɔ́ya na báda-nya ƒui bágyu bédie mmɔ. Na akpabi ammɔ ƒui ni, básala-nya na bálɛku-nya bétéwiakun ɔma ɔmmɔ kama. 16Na ɔ́sɔku Unwoti lɛkpabi ɔ́klibi na bábla unwi bɔbla akpala nwuna lɛlɔ na bágya Unwoti enu na bévele-nwu kusɛ kusɛ. Na úbo bani ƒui na bakya Yuda mmɔ ɔda ka ɔdi biala utaakpa Israel Unwoti Katɔti. 17Bekyuli bammɔ bénu lɛla lɛni na Manase ɔ́su-ma, nsu ama alati bana aƒiodu na baakpá Unwoti.
18Na lɛla biala na Manase ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔdi ɔga ku kalɛ na útaakpali Katɔti teevele ku kalɛ na kenye bediene bálɛ-nwu bávinku ƒui ni, bénweni bákya Israel ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo. 19Kenye udiene Hosai únweni ala pii ɔ́siku Manase lɛlɔ úbunku kalɛ na útaakpali Katɔti ku kalɛ na Katɔti únu-nwu bɔkpali. Nsu ala ekpidi ani na ɔ́bla lɛnɔ asa na ɔdubɔsɔ unwini kayi ni, únweni ana ƒui. Na únweni ala ɔ́siku kesii kani bene na ɔ́tu kadi bamba baƒiɔ ku aƒiodu ɔ́lɛ ku kesii kani na ɔ́ya na bátaakpa Asera baƒiɔ beledi bammɔ. 20Manase úbekpi na báva-nwu na baga kaduli kevomadɔ mmɔ na ubidi Amon úbenwini Ɔga.
21Akwa aavlanyɔ-inyɔ na Amon ɔ́ƒɔ asa na úbenwini ɔga na Yuda. Na Yerusalem mmɔ na úlie ɔ́di lɛga akwa anyɔ. 22Amon útenu Unwoti litemi kalɛ kani na ɔti Manase ɔ́bla na ɔ́kpa baƒiɔ bani na ɔti ɔ́tu. 23Manase únwini kayi úbo Unwoti kudɔ, nsu ubidi Amon anwu úni na útabla ɔmɛni mmomu ekpidi enengudi na ɔ́bla ɔ́sia kama útulo ɔti ƒui.
24Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Amon alati benengu badi bényimi-nwu lɛlɔ na bádu-nwu na baga kesii mmɔ kani. 25Nsu Yudaƒuɔ lɛnɔ bádu Amon badune bammɔ na béti ubidi Yosia bése lɛga.

english_text:
King Josiah of Judah
(2 Kings 22.1,2)
1 Josiah was 8 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 31 years from Jerusalem. 2He followed the example of his ancestor David and always obeyed the Lord.
Josiah Stops the Worship of Foreign Gods
(2 Kings 23.4-20)
3When Josiah was only 16 years old he began worshiping God, just as his ancestor David had done. Then, 4 years later, he decided to destroy the local shrines in Judah and Jerusalem, as well as the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah and the idols of foreign gods. 4 He watched as the altars for the worship of the god Baal were torn down, and as the nearby incense altars were smashed. The Asherah poles, the idols, and the stone images were also smashed, and the pieces were scattered over the graves of their worshipers. 5 Josiah then had the bones of the pagan priests burned on the altars.
And so Josiah got rid of the worship of foreign gods in Judah and Jerusalem. 6He did the same things in the towns and ruined villages in the territories of West Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as the border of Naphtali. 7Everywhere in the northern kingdom of Israel, Josiah tore down pagan altars and Asherah poles; he crushed idols to dust and smashed incense altars.
Then Josiah went back to Jerusalem.
Hilkiah Finds The Book of God's Law
(2 Kings 22.3-20)
8In the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah, after he had removed all the sinful things from the land and from the Lord's temple, he sent three of his officials to repair the temple. They were Shaphan son of Azaliah, Governor Maaseiah of Jerusalem, and Joah son of Joahaz, who kept the government records.
9These three men went to Hilkiah the high priest. They gave him the money that the Levite guards had collected from the people of West Manasseh, Ephraim, and the rest of Israel, as well as those living in Judah, Benjamin, and Jerusalem. 10Then the money was turned over to the men who supervised the repairs to the temple. They used some of it to pay the workers, 11and they gave the rest of it to the carpenters and builders, who used it to buy the stone and wood they needed to repair the other buildings that Judah's kings had not taken care of.
12The workers were honest, and their supervisors were Jahath and Obadiah from the Levite clan of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the Levite clan of Kohath. Other Levites, who were all skilled musicians, 13were in charge of carrying supplies and supervising the workers. Other Levites were appointed to stand guard around the temple.
14While the money was being given to these supervisors, Hilkiah found the book that contained the laws that the Lord had given to Moses. 15Hilkiah handed the book to Shaphan the official and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.”
16Shaphan took the book to Josiah and reported, “Your officials are doing everything you wanted. 17They have collected the money from the temple and have given it to the men supervising the repairs. 18But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it aloud.
19When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow. 20At once he called together Hilkiah, Shaphan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, and his own servant Asaiah. He said, 21“The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Israel and Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
22Hilkiah and the four other men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home, 23she said:
You were sent here by King Josiah, and this is what the Lord God of Israel says to him: 24“Josiah, I am the Lord! And I intend to punish this country and everyone in it, just as this book says. 25The people of Judah and Israel have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I can't stand it any longer. I am furious.
26-27“Josiah, listen to what I am going to do. I noticed how sad you were when you heard that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry. 28So before I destroy this place, I will let you die in peace.”
The men left and reported to Josiah what Huldah had said.
Josiah Reads The Book of God's Law
(2 Kings 23.1-3)
29King Josiah called together the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem. 30Then he went to the Lord's temple, together with all the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, and the Levites.
Finally, when everybody was there, he read aloud The Book of God's Law that had been found in the temple.
31After Josiah had finished reading, he stood in the place reserved for the king. He promised in the Lord's name to faithfully obey the Lord and to follow his laws and teachings that were written in the book. 32Then he asked the people of Jerusalem and Benjamin to make that same promise and to obey the God their ancestors had worshiped.
33Josiah destroyed all the idols in the territories of Israel, and he commanded everyone in Israel to worship only the Lord God. The people did not turn away from the Lord God of their ancestors for the rest of Josiah's rule as king.
translation_text:
Yuda Ɔga Yosia Ɔ́klibi Ala
1Akwa maane na Yosia ɔ́ƒɔ asa na úbenwini Yudaƒuɔ ɔga. Na úlie Yerusalem ɔ́di lɛga akwa avlaatɛ-unwi. 2Na Yosia ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni mɔɔƒɔ́ Unwoti anu. Na ɔ́siaku ɔti kuuku Ɔga Dawid ɔbladu kama siin. Na ɔ́di Katɔti ɔda bubo ƒui lɛlɔ.
Yosia Ɔ́ya Na Báda Kadi Bamba Baƒiɔ Bɔkpa Báya
3Yosia úse kalɔ ku Katɔti bɔkpa uwi ɔni kani na ɔ́ƒɔ akwa leevu-aku aani nwuna nana Dawid kalɛ. Na akwa ene kama ni, ɔ́lɛ ugyii ka ɔ́yila kadi bamba baƒiɔ ku aƒiodu ani ƒui na akya Yuda ku Yerusalem ku lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ béte Asera baƒiɔ beledi ka bataakpa. 4Na anwu ɔlati unye ɔɔnu asa na beebó Baal akpabi ammɔ ku abi ani lɛlɔ na baakyula oloƒui mmɔ taabwɛ ku Asera lɛƒiɔgyii ku baƒiɔ lidu lɛni ƒui na bátu mmɔ. Na béti ala abwɛdi ammɔ bégyingya béwi bekyuli bani nákpa baƒiɔ bammɔ kɔƒiɔtɔ lɛlɔ. 5Ɔmmɔ kama Yosia ɔ́ya na bákyula babwɛlɛ bammɔ ekubi na bana akpabi ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ ɔɔtina ka akpabi ammɔ eesé lɛlɔ na ásɔ átamanku ka bakpa baƒiɔ badi na ana lɛlɔ.
Ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na Yosia ɔ́sia na ɔ́da lɛƒiɔkpa údie Yuda ku Yerusalem. 6Na lɛni kani na ɔ́bla na lɛma libliidi kemmo ƒui lɛnɔ na Manase ku Eƒraim ku Simon kɔlɛkɛ útédu Neƒtali ɔmii ku amadɔ mmɔ ƒui. 7Na kesii biala na Israel lɛga kadikɔ kani na katɔ kakɛ ni, lɛni kani na Yosia ɔ́bwɛ baƒiɔ bammɔ ku ana akpabi ƒui ku Asera lɛƒiɔgyii lɛmmɔ ku oloƒui kɔkyulakɔ ƒui kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ únwini ɔtumu.
Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yosia ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie Yerusalem.
Hilkia Ɔ́nu Katɔti Ɔda Bubo Bunweni Kedee Ɔku
8Na lɛkwa leevu-maanedi ka Yosia ɔɔdi lɛga na ɔɔwia ka ɔklibi kalɔ kammɔ na ɔbla Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ kedee ni, ɔ́tala nwuna benengu ɛtɛ badi ka batásɔku Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ baklibi. Na ama ndi Asalia ubidi Saƒan ku Yerusalem aban ɔgadine unengu Maaseia ku Yoahas ubidi Yoas bani mɔɔda aban ala alɛdi ɔku mmɔ.
9Na nkyuli ɛtɛ bamɛni bésie ɔkpane unengudi Hilkia kudɔ na béti egulabi ani na Lewiƒuɔ bagyumanane báƒɔ básiku bekyuli bani nkya Manase ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ku Eƒraim kalɛkɛ ku Israel kakɛ kakladi ƒui kudɔ ku bani na beli Yuda ku Benyamin ku Yerusalem lɛnɔ béboku. 10Na béti egulabi ammɔ béte bekyuli bani mɔɔnu kabla kammɔ lɛlɔ na béti adi báƒɔ kabla bablane kayu. 11Na béti ɔkladi béte banwine ku batune na béti béye atabi ku ligyii lɛni na baawia na beti baklibi lɛtɔ bamba lɛni na Yuda baga bani néelie bábavi bátakana bɔklibi.
12Kabla bablane bammɔ bádi bana litemi lɛlɔ siin na bana lɛlɔ banune ndi Yahat ku Obadia ɔni nási Lewiƒuɔ kɔdua kɔni ndi Merari ku Sekaria ku Mesulam bani nási Lewiƒuɔ kɔdua kɔni baalɔ banii Kohat kemmo. Na Lewiƒuɔ bamba bani na bagyi lɛnu budie kaduɛ ni, 13ama muuti atula teesienku kabla bablane bammɔ na baanu kabla bablane bammɔ lɛlɔ. Na Lewiƒuɔ bamba benye baagyumana kakpakɔ kammɔ bámana.
14Ɔƒɛni uwi ɔni na beeti egulabi ammɔ teete kabla lɛlɔ banune bammɔ ni, Hilkia úbanu Katɔti ɔda bubo ɔku ɔni na úte Mose. 15Na Hilkia úti ɔku ɔmmɔ úte unengu Saƒan na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Nu! Lɛ́nu Ɔda Bubo Ɔku na Katɔti kakpakɔ.”
16Amu na Saƒan ɔ́ƒɔ ɔku ɔmmɔ na úti úsienku Yoas na útásu-nwu ɔnini, “Ƒula benengu badaku kabla kammɔ kalɛ na aawia ka babla-ka. 17Báƒɔ egulabi básiku kakpakɔ mmɔ na béti bésienku bekyuli bani mɔɔnu ekpo ammɔ bɔklibi kabla lɛlɔ. 18Nsu ni, Ɔbune, lɛla bamba lɛnɔ lɛ́lɛ. Aanu ɔku ɔni na Ɔkpane Hilkia úti úte-mi.” Mmɔ ni, Saƒan ɔ́ka ɔku ɔmmɔ momoomo úte-nwu na únu.
19Na ka Yosia únu ala ani na akya Katɔti Ɔda Bubo Ɔku ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ɔ́ni nwuna awu ɔni na ɔkya ɔ́bwɛ ku kɔnyana. 20Kɔnakunwi ni, ɔ́ya na bálɔ Hilkia ku Saƒan ku Saƒan ubidi Ahikam ku Mika ubidi Abdon na ɔ́ya na bálɔ Miaya ubidi Akbor lɛnɔ ku anwu ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔlati kabla ɔblane bábasala na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, 21“Mɔɔnu ka Katɔti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-mi ku ukyuli biala na ɔkya Israel ku Yuda kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ, ɔsika bula bati kuuku bátadi ɔda bubo bɔni nkya ɔku ɔmɛni kemmo lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu bisie na bitáwia lɛla lɛni ka Katɔti ɔɔwia ka bɔbla.”
22Amu na Hilkia ku nkyuli ine bakladi bani na ɔga ɔ́tala ni, bátɔlɔ mmɔ kɔnakunwi bésie uleku Kenye Udiene Hulda kudɔ batátɛmiku-nwu. Na Hulda ɔgyani ndi Salum. Na Salum ɔmɛni ni, Hasra ubidi ɔni na baalɔ Tokat náwɔ-nwu. Na Hasra mɔɔnu ɔga adala kesekɔ lɛlɔ. Hulda keliekɔ kakya Yerusalem katɔ kakɛ.
Na uwi ɔni na bása na nwuna kaduli mmɔ ka batɛmi ni, 23kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔga Yosia nátala-mii. Na Unwoti Israel Katɔti ɔnini, 24‘Yosia, ami ndi Unwoti! Na lɛ́lɛ ugyii ka lɛni ukyuli biala na ɔkya kalɔ kamɛni kemmo kɔtu kalɛ na ɔku ɔmɛni kemmo etemila aatina. 25Yuda ku Israel bekyuli ƒui béni-mi. Na bábla akpala béte kadi bamba baƒiɔ ku ala ani na ama alati bávɔ béte lɛlɔ. Na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bɔkana bunye bɔnu ɔmɛni gyɔlɔɔ, ɔsika livo liiƒí-mi geen.
26“ ‘Binwini na bitásu Yuda ɔga ɔni nátala-mii ɔnii bibeye kenye udiene binu lɛla lɛni na ami Israel Katɔti mɔɔkali ɔ́siku ala ani na únu ɔ́siku ɔku ɔmmɔ kemmo lɛlɔ. 27Ka kayi kágyu-ɔ uwi ɔni na énu ala ani na lɛ́su ka mabla kalɔ kamɛni ku kana bekyuli ni, éboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na kayi kemmo na áni ƒula awu ábwɛ na éwulo na mina anumi. Na mɔɔsu-ɔ geen ka línu ƒula buvele. Anwuɔsu nu lɛla lɛni na ndubo bɔbla. 28Ndubo-ɔ bɔkpanku bɔtɔlɔku busienku ƒula bati kudɔ na badubɔva-a ku keyi buɛɛ. Na ƒula anumi alanu ɔgbankpi ɔni ndubo bɔlɛku kalɔ kamɛni ku kana bekyuli lɛlɔ.’ ”
Amu na bekyuli bammɔ bénwini bátásu Yosia ala ani na bénu básiku uleku Kenye Udiene Hulda kudɔ.
Yosia Ɔ́ka Katɔti Ɔda Bubo Ɔku Ɔmmɔ
29Mmɔ ni, Ɔga Yosia ɔ́lɔ Yuda ku Yerusalem benengu bammɔ ɔ́sala. 30Na anwu ku Yuda ku Yerusalem bekyuli bɔmmɔ ƒui ku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bétéduo kakpakɔ mmɔ.
Amu na kawɔlɔ ƒui uwi ɔni na bana ƒui báasa buduo ni, ɔ́ka Katɔti ɔda bubo ɔku ɔni na bánu na kakpakɔ mmɔ kemmo etemila momoomo na bénu.
31Na uwi ɔni na ɔ́ka ɔku ɔmmɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, Yosia úsie úténye kesii kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte baga mmɔ. Na ɔ́lɔ Katɔti lɛnyi úse kenye ka ɔdubɔdi Unwoti ɔda bubo ku nwuna etemila ƒui lɛlɔ siin aani kalɛ na ɔkya ɔku ɔmmɔ kemmo. 32Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔ́lɔ Yerusalemƒuɔ ku bani na bási Benyamin kɔdua kemmo mmɔ ƒui ka ama lɛnɔ bakpali Unwoti bese kenye kammɔ bete-nwu ka badubɔdi ɔda bubo ku etemila ani ƒui na Unwoti Katɔti ɔni bana bati kuuku bákpa mmɔ úte-ma lɛlɔ siin. Na bábla lɛni sɔsɔ.
33Amu na Yosia ɔ́yila baƒiɔ bani ƒui na bakya Israel kalɛkɛ kammɔ lɛlɔ na úbo bana ƒui ɔda na Israel mmɔ ka bataakpa Unwoti Katɔti lɛti kani. Na básɔ bétenwini kama bátakya Unwoti Katɔti kudii na Yosia lɛga bɔdi uwi.

english_text:
Passover Is Celebrated
(2 Kings 23.21-23)
1Josiah commanded that Passover be celebrated in Jerusalem to honor the Lord. So, on the fourteenth day of the first month, the lambs were killed for the Passover celebration.
2On that day, Josiah made sure the priests knew what duties they were to do in the temple. 3He called together the Levites who served the Lord and who taught the people his laws, and he said:
No longer will you have to carry the sacred chest from place to place. It will stay in the temple built by King Solomon son of David, where you will serve the Lord and his people Israel. 4 Get ready to do the work that David and Solomon assigned to you, according to your clans. 5Divide yourselves into groups, then arrange yourselves throughout the temple so that each family of worshipers will be able to get help from one of you. 6When the people bring you their Passover lamb, you must kill it and prepare it to be sacrificed to the Lord. Make sure the people celebrate according to the instructions that the Lord gave Moses, and don't do anything to make yourselves unclean and unacceptable.
7Josiah donated 30,000 sheep and goats, and 3,000 bulls from his own flocks and herds for the people to offer as sacrifices. 8Josiah's officials also voluntarily gave some of their animals to the people, the priests, and the Levites as sacrifices. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, who were the officials in charge of the temple, gave the priests 2,600 sheep and lambs and 300 bulls to sacrifice during the Passover celebration. 9Conaniah, his two brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, as well as Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad were leaders of the Levites, and they gave the other Levites 5,000 sheep and goats, and 500 bulls to offer as sacrifices.
10When everything was ready to celebrate Passover, the priests and the Levites stood where Josiah had told them. 11Then the Levites killed and skinned the Passover lambs, and they handed some of the blood to the priests, who splattered it on the altar. 12The Levites set aside the parts of the animal that the worshipers needed for their sacrifices to please the Lord, just as the Law of Moses required. They also did the same thing with the bulls. 13 They sacrificed the Passover animals on the altar and boiled the meat for the other offerings in pots, kettles, and pans. Then they quickly handed the meat to the people so they could eat it.
14All day long, the priests were busy offering sacrifices and burning the animals' fat on the altar. And when everyone had finished, the Levites prepared Passover animals for themselves and for the priests.
15 During the celebration some of the Levites prepared Passover animals for the musicians and the guards, so that the Levite musicians would not have to leave their places, which had been assigned to them according to the instructions of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's prophet. Even the guards at the temple gates did not have to leave their posts.
16So on that day, Passover was celebrated to honor the Lord, and sacrifices were offered on the altar to him, just as Josiah had commanded. 17 The worshipers then celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread for the next seven days.
18People from Jerusalem and from towns all over Judah and Israel were there. Passover had not been observed like this since the days of Samuel the prophet.
