young people and old,
come praise the Lord!
13All creation, come praise
the name of the Lord.
Praise his name alone.
The glory of God is greater
than heaven and earth.
14Like a bull with mighty horns,
the Lord protects
his faithful nation Israel,
because they belong to him.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
1Bɛya na bumwi Unwoti.
Bimwi Unwoti Katɔti na bibo-nwu kudu
bɛsiku katɔ ku kayaa kakaaka ƒui!
2Amii Katɔti batu ku amii nwuna kabla bablane
lisu ƒui, bimwi-nwu!
3Ɔƒɛ ku kɔbuli ku ayabi
ku ala ani ƒui muukeye na kayaa ƒui, bimwi-nwu.
4Amii kayaa ala ku ntu bɔni nƒa katɔ kakaaka ƒui,
bimwi Unwoti Katɔti.
5Bimwi-nwu, ɔsika Unwoti Katɔti údie lɛdi
na údie lɛla biala ku nwuna kenye litemi.
6Ɔ́ya na ala ammɔ enye ana kunyekɔ
úti úsela uwi ƒui.
Na lɛla lɛdi lilakana ala ani na ɔ́bla úse mɛni
bɔvumana uwi ɔdi kudii.
7Amii ala ani ƒui na údie ɔ́kya kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui,
bimwi-nwu lɛnyi!
Na amii bani ƒui nkya ɛpu kemmo lɛnɔ
bimwi-nwu lɛnyi!
8Ogya ku etubankɛ ku ulɔyɔ ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa ɔni muukpó
na biinú-nwu lɛdi ƒui bimwi-nwu.
9Abi ku abinkpo
ku adingyii ku egyii enengudi ƒui
10ku beƒiebuo ku bebuo bamba ƒui na aku kemmo
bani mɔɔkpɛ́ kaƒɔ lɛlɔ ku kayaa baasɛ
bani muunú-nwu litemi ƒui, bimwi-nwu.
11Kalɔ lɛlɔ baga ku bekyuli ƒui
ku lɛlɔ badine ku kalɔ lɛlɔ litemi batɛne
12ku bakloƒu ku begblebi, banana ku beleku ku banamu ƒui,
bimwi Unwoti Katɔti lɛnyi.
13Bina ƒui bɛya na bemwi Blɔti,
ɔsika anwu lɛti kani nse kede kede ƒui.
Na nwuna bukeye bɔ́ƒɔ kayawi ƒui,
na bɔ́kɔ búbo bɔ́vi kalɔ ƒui.
14Ɔ́ya na nwuna kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ
bani mma-nwu lɛlɔ bálɛ lili,
ɔsika ɔɔgyumana-ma kpakplaa
aani akɔ ɔni mbo ɔyikun ku ese kangyaa.
Bɛya na bumwi Unwoti.

english_text:
A New Song of Praise
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Sing him a new song of praise
when his loyal people meet.
2People of Israel, rejoice
because of your Creator.
People of Zion, celebrate
because of your King.
3Praise his name by dancing
and playing music on harps
and tambourines.
4The Lord is pleased
with his people,
and he gives victory
to those who are humble.
5All of you faithful people,
praise our glorious Lord!
Celebrate and worship.
6 Praise God with songs
on your lips
and a sword in your hand.
7Take revenge and punish
the nations.
8Put chains of iron
on their kings and rulers.
9Punish them as they deserve;
this is the privilege
of God's faithful people.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
1Bɛya na bumwi Unwoti.
Bidie ɔnu ɔwɔdi bite-nwu.
Na bimwi-nwu na bekyuli kedee ƒui akɔ.
2Israel, lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-mii, amii bani na Unwoti Katɔti údie.
Na amii Sion bebi ku bawɔ ni, lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-mii na bina ɔga lɛlɔ.
3Bɛtɔ katɔ na biti bimwi-nwu lɛnyi.
Na biti enukpɛ agyala ku lɛbentaa bidie lɛnu bimwi-nwu.
4Ɔsika lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ Unwoti Katɔti na nwuna bekyuli lɛlɔ.
Na ɔdubɔya na bani nse buɛɛ ƒui balɛ lili,
ɔsika ɔdubɔƒɔ-ma.
5Bɛya na bekyuli kedee ƒui bakɛ lɛlɔyɔ
na bekeye na bana kɔtɛnkɔ.
Na bedie lɛnu momoomo!
6Bɛya na buteenu bana bumwi lɛnu kɔku na bana inye kemmo.
Na beti kuwii kɔni bádɔ-ku lɛvi inyɔ bada.
7Na beti bedie baƒiɔkpane kasi
na bani bekyuli kɔtu.
8Na bana baga ku batɔnkune ni,
bebo-ma kɔgba.
9Na batɛku-ma litemi na badu-ma kɔtɔ
aani kalɛ na bénweni bése.
Kenyekɔ ku ɔbu ɔmmɔ udu na béti béte bekyuli kedee bamɛni.
Bɛya na bumwi Unwoti.

english_text:
The Lord Is Good to His People
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Praise God in his temple.
Praise him in heaven,
his mighty fortress.
2Praise our God!
His deeds are wonderful,
too marvelous to describe.
3Praise God with trumpets
and all kinds of harps.
4Praise him with tambourines
and dancing,
with stringed instruments
and woodwinds.
5Praise God with cymbals,
with clashing cymbals.
6Let every living creature
praise the Lord.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
1Bɛya na bumwi Unwoti.
Amii kadi bekyuli ƒui,
bimwi Unwoti Katɔti na nwuna kakpakɔ kedee kemmo!
Bimwi anwu ɔni nédie kayaa na uli-ka lɛlɔ mmɔ ku ɔyikun.
2Bimwi-nwu na nwuna ala ebendi ani na ɔ́bla ɔsu.
Na nwuna bumwi bɔkɔ katɔ
butédu kalɛ na ɔ́bla ala abuni útédu kenye.
3Bɛvwi kɔkpɛɛ biti bimwi-nwu.
Na bɛgya agyangba ku lɛbentaa biti bimwi-nwu.
4Bɛgya agyala ani mɔɔku na bɛtɔ biti bimwi-nwu.
Biti agyala ani na bédi ku kɔbuli bimwi-nwu ku atoloyii.
5Bimwi-nwu ku enukpɛ agyala ani mɔɔku
ku agyala ani muusié ɔgyu.
6Bɛya na Unwoti Katɔti ala ediedi
ani ƒui mbo ngba emwi-nwu.
Bɛya na bumwi Unwoti.

english_text:
How Proverbs Can Be Used
1 These are the proverbs
of King Solomon of Israel,
the son of David.
2Proverbs will teach you
wisdom and self-control
and how to understand
sayings with deep meanings.
3You will learn what is right
and honest and fair.
4From these, an ordinary person
can learn to be smart,
and young people can gain
knowledge and good sense.
5If you are already wise,
you will become even wiser.
And if you are smart,
you will learn to understand
6proverbs and sayings,
as well as words of wisdom,
and all kinds of riddles.
7 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of knowledge.
Only a fool rejects wisdom
and good advice.
Warnings against Bad Friends
8My child, obey the teachings
of your parents,
9and wear their teachings
as you would a pretty hat
or a lovely necklace.
10Don't be tempted by sinners
or listen 11when they say,
“Come on! Let's gang up
and kill somebody,
just for the fun of it!
12They're well and healthy now,
but we'll finish them off
once and for all.
13We'll take their valuables
and fill our homes
with stolen goods.
14If you join our gang,
you'll get your share.”
15Don't follow anyone like that
or do what they do.
16They are in a big hurry
to commit some crime,
perhaps even murder.
17They are like a bird
that sees the bait,
but ignores the trap.
18They gang up to murder someone,
but they are the victims.
19The wealth you get from crime
robs you of your life.
Wisdom Speaks
20 Wisdom shouts in the streets
wherever crowds gather.
21She shouts in the marketplaces
and near the city gates
as she says to the people,
22“How much longer
will you enjoy
being stupid fools?
Won't you ever stop sneering
and laughing at knowledge?
23Listen as I correct you
and tell you what I think.
24You completely ignored me
and refused to listen;
25you rejected my advice
and paid no attention
when I warned you.
26“So when you are struck
by some terrible disaster,
27or when trouble and distress
surround you like a whirlwind,
I will laugh and make fun.
28You will ask for my help,
but I won't listen;
you will search,
but you won't find me.
29No, you would not learn,
and you refused
to respect the Lord.
30You rejected my advice
and paid no attention
when I warned you.
31“Now you will eat the fruit
of what you have done,
until you are stuffed full
with your own schemes.
32Sin and self-satisfaction
bring destruction and death
to stupid fools.
33But if you listen to me,
you will be safe and secure
without fear of disaster.”
translation_text:
Agba Adanku Kasusu Kadi
1Agba amɛni na Dawid ubidi Salomo ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Ɔga úbo.
2Na lɛla lɛni na agba amɛni adanku ndi
ka atina bekyuli na bakana badi lɛlɔ lɛlɔ
na benu asugba kalɔ.
3Na bekyuli batɛya kalɛ na bada lɛlɔ kaduɛ
na belie ngba buni,
na babla ala na ulu lɛlɔ siin na adia lɛnɔ.
4Agba amɛni ndubɔya na bani na bana
kasusu kásɔ bati lɛla.
Na begblebi ku bakloƒu bati lɛla
na babla kasusu na bana keliela lɛlɔ.
5Na bani na báda anu ni,
bana lɛnunda lɛɛkɔ́ katɔ teebu.
Na bani mɔɔnu ala kemmo taati lɛnɔ
bati bana kasiakɔ.
6Na benu agba ku kenwini etemila kalɔ
na benu banundane agyolo ku kekuma atɛ kalɔ.
7Unwoti bɔyia ndi ukyuli lɛlati kalɔ kesekɔ.
Nsu badɔlɔdi beení lɛnunda etemila
ku kalɛ na badi lɛlɔ lɛlɔ kaduɛ.
Da Anu Ɔkɛnku Kalɛ Na Ƒ'ɔti Ɔɔlɛ-ɔ Kpakplaa Lɛlɔ
8Ubi, se atu na enu ƒ'ɔti ɔda bubo.
Na teni ƒ'ini lɛla lɛni na ɔɔtina-a.
9Lɛla lɛni na átɛya bana kudɔ
ɔdubunwini kagabwa kebi-ɔ lili.
Na unwini asɛɛ abuni akya-a limɔ.
10Mina ubi, si bekyuli bekpidi baadɔ́dɔ-ɔ ni,
nwini kama kya-ma!
11Badubɔkana na basu-ɔ banini, “Bo, basiaku-bu.
Na aya na bɔbɛ na bɔdu ukyuli ɔdi!
Na bubi kesii kadi butaatu bekyuli
bani nátabla-bu lɛla lɛdi.
12Ya na bubweli-ma ngba ngba aani kaƒiɔtɔ,
na bɔyila-ma udu ƒui aani bekyuli
bani nánu béduo ubu kemmo.
13Na bana ala abuni ani na búƒie bɔ́ƒɔ ni,
bɔdubuyile bula lɛtɔ ku-nya!
14Bo na ebenyeku-bu kpakplaa,
na abu ku-ɔ bɔdubule ala ani na búƒie bɔ́ƒɔ mmɔ.”
15Ubi, tesie ku bekyuli bammɔ udu!
Tani tede bana kɔvinkɔ munu munu!
16Baababla ku usi taatábla ekpidi.
Na baababla teewi ubugya kalɔ.
17Keeke na aakywɛɛ kakpagyuɛ
si baasɛ benye baanu!
18Nsu uuuse lɛni ku bekyuli bammɔ udu.
Ama alati lɛlɔ na bebi baatú,
na kubu na baasia ama alati lɛlɔ.
19Bekyuli bani ƒui na anumi eegyie-ma
na lɛkɛ likpidi lɛlɔ ni,
lɛni na bana kawɔlɔkɔ kaabla.
Bɔlɛ Ute Bekyuli Bani Muuní Lɛnunda
20Lɛnunda lise aani ukyuli ɔni muubó kudu na lilu lɛlɔ.
Na uute kenye na kɔsalakɔ ƒui.
21Na ɔɔkpali bani ƒui nkɛ ulu unengudi
ɔni lɛlɔ baaní lɛsɛ, na uubó kudu
taasiku awodu eli.
Na ɔɔsu nwuna kenye na ɔma unengudi
ɔmmɔ awoduku kɔyakun kenye.
22Lɛnunda ɔ́kpali ɔnini,
“Amii bani na bina kasusu kásɔ ni,
uwi ɛlɛ na bɛdubusie anumi ku bina ngba
bɔni násɔ bulie bitédu?
Uwi ɛlɛ na amii bani mɔɔmá litemi geen
lɛmmɔ bɛdubɔbla lɛni bitédu?
Na amii badɔlɔdi bikisi lɛlati?
23Si bunu na bínu-mi bɔdɔnku ni,
nka ala ani ƒui nkya-mi kayi kemmo
na ndubudie lɛsu-mii,
na lɛya na bɛti mina lili kemmo kakali ƒui.
24“Nsu bítakpete-mi uwi ɔni na lɛ́kpali-mii.
Na uwi ɔni na lídie enu nnii mɔɔƒɔ́-mii ni,
ɔdi útenwini útanu-mi.
25Na ka bíni mina bɔlɛ
na bilátuna bɛnii ndɔnku-mii ɔsu ni,
26Ami lɛnɔ ndubo-mii bɔma
si uwi ɔni na ɔgbankpi úbo-mii lɛlɔ.
Na lɛpii-mii si uwi ɔni na lilikpi ala eekpóku-mii,
27na ese aani ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa
uwi ɔni na ɔgbankpi ɔda-mii ɔɔvínku
aani ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔkya ligede
na ala ani nétulo-mii áya na kayi kaakpulu-mii.
28“Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, bɛdubɔkpali ami Lɛnunda,
nsu naaakpete-mii.
Na bɛdubɔwia-mi na bilanu-mi.
29Ɔsika bíkisi lɛlati na bítaƒuna
ka bitaayia Unwoti ku ɔbu.
30Bíni mina bɔlɛ
na bíveli atu na mina bɔdɔnku ɔsu
31na ngba bɔni udu na bilie ni,
nwuna ebi na bɛdubo bɔdi.
Na ulu ɔni na bɛ́ƒuna ka bɛsia ni,
nwuna ala emo-mii.
32Ɔsika bekyuli bani na bana kasusu kásɔ ni,
ngba bukpidi bɔni na belie ndubo-ma bɔdu.
Na ala ani na badɔlɔdi baakali ka átɛ áwɔlɔ ƒui
ndubo bɔya na bayii ku udu.
33Nsu bani ƒui muunú-mi litemi ni,
badubulie ngba na atu bɔyɔ kemmo,
na lɛla lɛdi lilékpoku-ma
na balayia ka ukpidi ɔdi walɛku-ma lɛnɔ.”

english_text:
Wisdom and Bad Friends
1My child, you must follow
and treasure my teachings
and my instructions.
2Keep in tune with wisdom
and think what it means
to have common sense.
3Beg as loud as you can
for good common sense.
4Search for wisdom
as you would search for silver
or hidden treasure.
5Then you will understand
what it means to respect
and to know the Lord God.
6 All wisdom comes from the Lord,
and so do common sense
and understanding.
7God gives helpful advice
to everyone who obeys him
and protects those
who live as they should.
8God sees that justice is done,
and he watches over everyone
who is faithful to him.
9With wisdom you will learn
what is right
and honest and fair.
10Wisdom will control your mind,
and you will be pleased
with knowledge.
11Sound judgment and good sense
will watch over you.
12Wisdom will protect you
from evil schemes
and from those liars
13who turned from doing good
to live in the darkness.
14Most of all they enjoy
being mean and deceitful.
15They are dishonest themselves,
and so are all their deeds.
Wisdom and Sexual Purity
16Wisdom will protect you
from the smooth talk
of a sinful woman,
17who breaks her wedding vows
and leaves the man she married
when she was young.
18The road to her house leads
down
to the dark world
of the dead.
19Visit her, and you will never
find the road to life again.
20Follow the example
of good people
and live an honest life.
21If you are honest and innocent,
you will keep your land;
22if you do wrong
and can never be trusted,
you will be rooted out.
translation_text:
Lɛnunda Libo Kɔsia
1Mina ubi, si áƒɔ mina etemila,
na áklibi mina ɔda bubo ése éte lɛlɔ,
2na ƒula kɔtu kɔsia lɛnunda etemila lɛlɔ
na áya na ƒula kayi kasia ala kalɔ bunu lɛlɔ
3na eevele ala kemmo bɔnu taati
na eevele ala kalɔ bunu kpakplaa
4na aawia-nya aani kalɛ baawia sika ɔƒualadi
na asia-nya kama aani akɛla abɛladi ni,
5na ɔdubɔya na enu kalɛ na baayia Unwoti kalɔ
na ati-nwu lɛnɔ.
6Ɔsika Unwoti muute lɛnunda!
Na nwuna etemila aayá na ukyuli ɔɔtí lɛla
na ɔɔdá anu.
7Bekyuli bani nse siin ni,
uusé-ma kama ka badi lɛlɔ.
Na ɔdi lɛgyumanala ute bekyuli
bani na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma na bana kasiakɔ.
8Na bekyuli bani mɔɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ siin ni,
ɔɔgyumana-ma na bana kasiakɔ.
Na ɔɔda bani nsiaku-nwu kama siin
taasiaku bana kɔvinkɔ.
9Na adubunu lɛla lɛni ndia na lɛdi ulu lɛlɔ siin kalɔ
na ulu buni biala lɛlɔ.
10Ɔsika lɛnunda lɛdubuduo-ɔ kayi kemmo
na lɛlati lɛƒɔ-ɔ kɔyu kemmo ku ebiti.
11Na ala anu bɔsia taabla-nya ulu lɛlɔ
ɔdubɔgyumana-a
na ala kalɔ bunu bɔda-a kɔkɔɔkɔ.
12Lɛnunda lɛmmɔ lɛdubɔƒɔ-ɔ
lɛsiku bekyuli bekpidi kasiakɔ,
na alásala lɛlɔ ku bani mɔɔtɛmi enyekpi.
13Bekyuli bamɛni udu baada ulu geen ɔmmɔ taava
na beeti ulu ukpidi ɔni néti-ma úselaku kasuudikɔ.
14Na ebiti aada-ma ka bataabla likpidi
na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-ma na bana likyulikpi ala bɔbla lɛlɔ.
15Bana ala bɔbla ƒui buse gontii
na bana ablala adi likyulikpi sɔɔn.
16Lɛnunda lɛdubɔda-a lidie
uleku ɔsɔnɔdine unyemi kudɔ,
uleku ɔmmɔ ɔdi ɔgya uliene
ɔni mɔɔlɛ́ ɔgyani kama katɔlɔ.
17Ɔ́lɛ nwuna ligblebi uwi kɔgya kɔni na úlie
na údie lɛla lɛni na únyimiku-nwu
na Unwoti anumi atu.
18Nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo buduo ɔdi ulu
ɔni néti úsela kekpine,
na nwuna kavinkɔ ƒui kadi bekpine kakyakɔ ulu.
19Ɔdi uleduo-nwu kudɔ taasɔ teenwini
iye ɔsɔ ɔnu ngba ulu geen ɔmmɔ ɔsia.
20Sia bekyuli babuni kasiakɔ mmomu,
na asia bekyuli bani nse siin kavinkɔ.
21Ɔsika bekyuli bani kayi kemmo ablala nse siin
kani ndubulie ngba na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.
Na bani na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma kani
ndubɔkya-ka kemmo.
22Nsu belikplune ama ni,
Unwoti ɔdubɔda-ma udie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.
Na bani mɔɔlɛ́-nwu kama ni,
na ɔkpɛ-ma ɔlɛku-ka kemmo.

english_text:
Trust God
1My child, remember
my teachings and instructions
and obey them completely.
2They will help you live
a long and prosperous life.
3Let love and loyalty
always show like a necklace,
and write them in your mind.
4 God and people will like you
and hold you in high esteem.
5With all your heart
you must trust the Lord
and not your own judgment.
6Always let him lead you,
and he will clear the road
for you to follow.
7 Don't ever think that you
are wise enough,
but respect the Lord
and stay away from evil.
8This will make you healthy,
and you will feel strong.
9Honor the Lord by giving him
your money and the first part
of all your crops.
10Then you will have
more grain and grapes
than you will ever need.
11 My child, don't turn away
or become bitter
when the Lord corrects you.
12 The Lord corrects
everyone he loves,
just as parents correct
a child they dearly love.
The Value of Wisdom
13God blesses everyone
who has wisdom
and common sense.
14Wisdom is worth more
than silver;
it makes you much richer
than gold.
15Wisdom is more valuable
than precious jewels;
nothing you want
compares with her.
16In her right hand
Wisdom holds a long life,
and in her left hand
are wealth and honor.
17Wisdom makes life pleasant
and leads us safely along.
18Wisdom is a life-giving tree,
the source of happiness
for all who hold on to her.
19By his wisdom and knowledge
the Lord created
heaven and earth.
20By his understanding
he let the ocean break loose
and clouds release the rain.
21My child, use common sense
and sound judgment!
Always keep them in mind.
22They will help you to live
a long and beautiful life.
23You will walk safely
and never stumble;
24you will rest without a worry
and sleep soundly.
25So don't be afraid
of sudden disasters
or storms that strike
those who are evil.
26You can be sure that the Lord
will protect you from harm.
27 Do all you can for everyone
who deserves your help.
28Don't tell your neighbor
to come back tomorrow,
if you can help today.
29Don't try to be mean
to neighbors who trust you.
30Don't argue just to be arguing,
when you haven't been hurt.
31Don't be jealous
of cruel people
or follow their example.
32The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is dishonest,
but he lets good people
be his friends.
33He places a curse on the home
of everyone who is evil,
but he blesses the home
of every good person.
34 The Lord sneers at those
who sneer at him,
but he is kind to everyone
who is humble.
35You will be praised
if you are wise,
but you will be disgraced
if you are a stubborn fool.
translation_text:
Ti Ƒula Anu Sia Unwoti Lɛlɔ
1Mina ubi, tayiƒala ala ani na lɛ́tina-a.
Mmomu da mina ɔda bubo kya ƒula kayi kemmo.
2Ɔsika ɔmmɔ ndubɔya na elie ngba gyɔlɔɔ
na ala adianku-ɔ na keyi kayɔku-ɔ.
3Tanyonu lɛƒɔndia bɔbla ku litemi kama bɔsiaku siin.
Ti ala amɛni bo bala ƒula limɔ
na aya na akɛ keliekɔ na ƒula kayi kemmo.
4Ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na aƒɔ lɛnyi na adia
na Unwoti ku bekyuli ƒui anumi.
5Ti ƒula anu ku kayi ƒui sia Unwoti lɛlɔ.
Na teti anu tasia awɔ ɔlati ƒula ala kalɔ bunu lɛlɔ.
6Nu-nwu ti na ƒula lilu ƒui lɛlɔ,
na ɔdubɔtɔnku-ɔ na ƒula kasiakɔ ƒui.
7Ƒula anumi atatɔlɔ-ɔ na anu lɛlɔ ɔnundane.
Mmomu yia Unwoti na enwini kama akya likpidi.
8Ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na akɛ ɔlɔkplu na ɔlɔna kemmo
na lɛlɔ ekubi asa-a kpakplaa.
9Ti ƒula lɛkɛ teemwi Unwoti.
Na eti ƒula edula biala ebi edeedi ete-nwu.
10Ɔdubɔya na ƒula linwu liyi ku edula abuni
na akpambui lɛnɔ eyi ku ntɛ mini mini.
11Mina ubi, teni si Unwoti ɔɔní-ɔ kɔtu ka ɔklibi-ɔ.
Na utekpoku-ɔ si ɔɔdɔnku-ɔ lɛnɔ.
12Ɔsika bekyuli bani na Unwoti ɔɔyɔ́ ni,
ama na ɔɔlɛ kpakplaa
aani kalɛ na ubi ɔti ɔdi ɔɔní ubidi
ɔni na ɔɔyɔ́ kɔtu.
13Lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ ukyuli ɔni nákɛ lɛnunda
na uunú ala kalɔ.
14Ɔsika ubo kɔsia utulo sika ɔƒualadi.
Na nwuna lɛkɛ litulo sika ugyiedi.
15Lɛnunda lɛ́ƒɔ kuye litulo asɛɛ ebi
ani náƒɔ kuye geen muedi.
Na lɛla bamba lɛni na ukyuli ɔɔwia
lɛdi lítaƒɔ kuye liiitulo ɔmɛni.
16Lɛnunda lɛdanku ngba gyɔlɔɔ na nwuna kɔdianu.
Na nwuna kɔmiinu lɛnɔ kɔdanku lɛkɛ ku ɔbu.
17Nwuna lilu lɛdi kasiakɔ kabuni.
Na lɛdi keyi buɛɛ lilu.
18Ngba kugyii ndi lɛnunda ute bani nda-nwu kpakplaa.
Lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ bani nébo enu báda-nwu.
19Lɛnunda na Unwoti úti ɔ́kya kalɔ kammɔ ɔka kalɔ.
Na ala kalɔ bunu na úti údie katɔ ɔ́ƒala kayaa.
20Na ɔkɛnku nwuna lɛlati lɛlɔ
na úle ntu bonwu bɔmmɔ akpa akpa.
Na ɔɔyá na liƒlukutu lɛnɔ lɛɛyu amii.
21Mina ubi, sia ala bɔnu taati anu
ku etemila kemmo bɔƒuna kaduɛ
na tada ɔdi tava.
22Ɔsika ɔmmɔ ndi ƒula ngba.
Na ɔdubunwini aani sika asɛɛ
na ƒula limɔ ani ndubɔkya-a bɔdia.
23Na adubusie ƒula ngba ulu kɔkɔɔkɔ.
Na ƒula ɔgba uletulo iye agbanta.
24Si áyu átɛ ni, liƒu biala lilada-a,
mmomu adubɔlɛɛ na lɛlɛɛ lɛyu-ɔ.
25Tayia ɔgbankpi ɔni muuyú bekyuli taatu
iye ala ani muubieku balalane.
26Ɔsika Unwoti lɛlɔ na ése kayi
na anwu ndubudie-ɔ
na alakya kakpagyuɛ kadi ɔgba.
27Teni lɛbuni bɔbla bute ukyuli
ɔni mɔɔwia-a kebunku
si ánu ka ébo ɔyikun ɔmmɔ.
28Tasu ƒula ukyulikpana anini,
“Teesie, kɔnaadi na ebo abaƒɔ,”
si lɛla lɛni na uuvele-ɔ lise-ɔ ɔmwi.
29Awɔ ku ukyuli ɔdi bitasa lili likpidi
na ƒula liku ɔkpana lɛlɔ,
ka bilie bide ku ebiti.
30Tada ƒula ɔkpana kenye kekeeke
si útabla-a lɛla lɛdi.
31Anumi etegyie-ɔ na bekyuli bekpidi
bani mɔɔkya lɛsɛ lɛlɔ.
Na tasiaku bana ɔbladu kama.
32Bekyuli bekpidi bammɔ ala eesé Unwoti lɛlɔ geen.
Nsu bekyuli bani nse siin ni,
ulábɛla-ma nwuna kasusu.
33Unwoti uuwida bekyuli bekpidi kɔduli.
Nsu nwuna kusɛ kusɛ ɔɔsiaku bekyuli bani nse siin.
34Na ɔɔpii bekyuli bani mɔɔpii bekyuli
ka baatalaku lɛlɔ katɔ ɔsu.
Mmomu uubunku bani muuboku lɛlɔ kalɔ.
35Banundane baakɛ́ ɔbu kese.
Nsu badɔlɔdi ama ni, kɔƒa na beli bete.

english_text:
Advice to Young People
1My child, listen closely
to my teachings
and learn common sense.
2My advice is useful,
so don't turn away.
3When I was still very young
and my mother's favorite child,
my father 4said to me:
“If you follow my teachings
and keep them in mind,
you will live.
5Be wise and learn good sense;
remember my teachings
and do what I say.
6“If you love Wisdom
and don't reject her,
she will watch over you.
7The best thing about Wisdom
is Wisdom herself;
good sense is more important
than anything else.
8If you value Wisdom
and hold tightly to her,
great honors will be yours.
9It will be like wearing
a glorious crown
of beautiful flowers.”
The Right Way and the Wrong Way
10My child, if you listen
and obey my teachings,
you will live a long time.
11I have shown you the way
that makes sense;
I have guided you
along the right path.
12Your road won't be blocked,
and you won't stumble
when you run.
13Hold firmly to my teaching
and never let go.
It will mean life for you.
14Don't follow the bad example
of cruel and evil people.
15Turn aside and keep going.
Stay away from them.
16They can't sleep or rest
until they do wrong or harm
some innocent victim.
17Their food and drink
are cruelty and wickedness.
18The lifestyle of good people
is like sunlight at dawn
that keeps getting brighter
until broad daylight.
19The lifestyle of the wicked
is like total darkness,
and they will never know
what makes them stumble.
20My child, listen carefully
to everything I say.
21Don't forget a single word,
but think about it all.
22Knowing these teachings
will mean true life
and good health for you.
23Carefully guard your thoughts
because they are the source
of true life.
24Never tell lies or be deceitful
in what you say.
25Keep looking straight ahead,
without turning aside.
26 Know where you are headed,
and you will stay
on solid ground.
27Don't make a mistake by turning
to the right or the left.
translation_text:
Lɛnunda Lɛ́ƒɔ Kuye Litulo Lɛla Biala
1Mina bebi, bise atu na binu ami bina ɔti ɔda bubo.
Bise atu na bɛkɛ ala kalɔ bunu.
2Ala ani ndi etemila geen na áƒɔ kuye
na mɔɔtina-mii.
Anwuɔsu bitenwini kama bitakya-nya.
3Uwi ɔni na ndi ɔnamu na lɛ́kya mina ɔti kaduli,
na ami kani ndi mina uni ubi ɔnanabi ni,
4Ɔ́tina-mi ala na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini,
“Ƒie mina etemila da kpakplaa ku ƒula kayi ƒui.
Di mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ na adubulie ngba.
5Nu ka ebo lɛnunda ku ala kalɔ bunu.
Na tayiƒala mina etemila iye edeyi-nya kudɔ
esie kesii bamba.
6Tenwini kama takya lɛnunda, na lɛdubo-ɔ bɔgyumana.
Yɔ lɛnunda na lɛdubo-ɔ lɛlɔ bɔnu.
7Lɛla linengudi ƒui lɛni na ɔlɛka awia ndi lɛnunda.
Ina ka ɔdanku ƒula lɛla biala ni,
nu ka ebo ala kalɔ bunu
na lɛla biala na aabla kemmo.
8Ya lɛnunda lɛ́ƒɔ-ɔ kuye geen
na lɛdubɔkɔliku-ɔ katɔ.
Kya-nwu kɔgbu na ɔbu ɔdubɔkya-a lɛlɔ.
9Ɔdubudi lɛka lɛni mɔɔdia bɔnu ɔsia-a lili
na akɛ kagabwa kani muukeye.”
10Ubi, nu-mi litemi na aƒɔ lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu-ɔ.
Ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na elie ngba na akwa emomo-ɔ.
11Lɛnunda lilu na mɔɔtina-a.
Na lɛtɔnku-ɔ lɛsiaku lilu lɛbuni lɛlɔ.
12Na si akɛ eesié ni, elekpuulo.
Na si usi lɛnɔ na akɛ eekeli ni, alatutu.
13Da mina ala ani na lɛ́tina-a na tanyonu-mu
Da-mu kaduɛ, ɔsika ala ammɔ ndi ƒula ngba.
14Tasiaku balalane lɛgba kanyakɔ.
Na tasia lilu lɛni na bekyuli bekpidi bakɛ.
15Die-ma kasiakɔ ƒui atu na tasia mmɔ munu munu
Sɔ bana lilu ƒui lɛlɔ
na enwini asia ƒula kasiakɔ bamba.
16Ɔsika bekyuli bekpidi balátuna bɔtɛ talɛɛ
útédu ka bábla likpidi.
Likyulikpi bɔbla liiyú-ma lɛlɛlɛ wetédu ka
bebile ukyuli ɔdi ngba.
17Ulikplu bɔbla búnwini-ma adila,
na kalala bɔbla ndi bana ntu bɔni na baaní!
18Ukyuli ɔni nse siin kavinkɔ keekeye
aani ɔtanta kadi kani négye kadubo
na keekeye teebu utédu ka ɔbla nwaa ƒui.
19Nsu bekyuli bekpidi kavinkɔ aka kese
aani ubu ɔni nse suu geen.
Na balati lɛla lɛni mɔɔyá na beetulo taagbanta.
20Ubi, nu lɛla lɛni mɔɔsu-ɔ kaduɛ.
Na ƒula kasusu kasia litemi biala lɛlɔ geen.
21Taya na mina etemila avi-ɔ anu.
Mmomu ya na eduo-ɔ kayi kemmo geen.
22Ɔsika adi ngba ete ukyuli ɔni nákɛ-nya,
na aayá na awɔ ukyuli umodi ɔmmɔ aakɛ́ ɔlɔkplu.
23Na lɛla lɛni ntulo ƒui ni,
da ƒula kayi kemodi kammɔ kaduɛ,
ɔsika ngba libiɔ lɛni mɔɔyu ntu kadi.
24Ya na kɔyalɛtɛ kusie kama ƒui na ƒula kudɔ
Na etemila ani muusé lɛlɔ ƒui atalɛ-ɔ kenye.
25Taanu ƒula anumi ligeen uwi biala si akɛ,
na ƒula anumi asia kesii kani na ésela kani.
26Sia ƒula kasiakɔ anu kaduɛ ka kese-ɔ siin
asa na ánya ésela.
Nu ka ɔdi ulu kpakplaa na ulegyiileku-ɔ.
27Tedeyi tesie kɔmii iye kɔdianu.
Na edie ƒula ɔgba na likpidi bɔbla kemmo.

english_text:
Be Faithful to Your Wife
1My son, if you listen closely
to my wisdom and good sense,
2you will have sound judgment,
and you will always know
the right thing to say.
3The words of an immoral woman
may be as sweet as honey
and as smooth as olive oil.
4But all that you really get
from being with her
is bitter poison and pain.
5If you follow her,
she will lead you down
to the world of the dead.
6She has missed the path
that leads to life
and doesn't even know it.
7My son, listen to me
and do everything I say.
8Stay away from a bad woman!
Don't even go near the door
of her house.
9You will lose your self-respect
and end up in debt
to some cruel person
for the rest of your life.
10Strangers will get your money
and everything else
you have worked for.
11When it's all over,
your body will waste away,
as you groan 12and shout,
“I hated advice and correction!
13I paid no attention
to my teachers,
14and now I am disgraced
in front of everyone.”
15You should be faithful
to your wife,
just as you take water
from your own well.
16And don't be like a stream
from which just any woman
may take a drink.
17Save yourself for your wife
and don't have sex
with other women.
18Be happy with the wife
you married
when you were young.
19She is beautiful and graceful,
just like a deer;
you should be attracted to her
and stay deeply in love.
20Don't go crazy over a woman
who is unfaithful
to her own husband!
21The Lord sees everything,
and he watches us closely.
22Sinners are trapped and caught
by their own evil deeds.
23They get lost and die
because of their foolishness
and lack of self-control.
translation_text:
Bɔlɛ Na Lɛsɔnɔdi Lɛlɔ
1Ubi, nu mina lɛnunda etemila kaduɛ.
Na enu-mi lɛlati etemila ani mɔɔsu-ɔ.
2Mmɔ na adubɔtɛya kalɛ na baabla ala ulu lɛlɔ,
na ƒula enyekuli aklibi lɛlati ala ese lɛlɔ.
3Uleku ɔsɔnɔ ɔdine ni,
nwuna enyekuli aatɛmi ala mini mini aani uwɔ.
Na etemila ani mɔɔlɛ́-nwu kenye
aayu kayi buɛɛ aani nnɔmii.
4Nsu lɛla lɛni mɔɔsia kama teebo lɛɛyu ɔdu kati kati
na use yayaaya aani kewii kani bádɔ-ka lɛvi inyɔ.
5Kekpine ulu na nwuna lɛgba lɛtɔ lísela.
Na kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo kani na ɔdubo buduo.
6Ɔsika ɔɔɔda ngba lɛda munu munu.
Lilu gonti lɛlɔ kani na ɔkɛ úsela na anwu ɔlati ɔɔɔgyi.
7Ɔƒaani ni, mina bebi, bise atu na binu.
Na lɛla lɛni na ndubo-mii bɔsu mɛni ni,
ɔdi utedeyi utesie kesii bamba.
8Sia ulu ɔni nse sɛsɛɛ
na ɔ́gyunku uleku ɔmɛni udu kakyakɔ.
Na tani tede nwuna ɔtɔ kayakun,
9si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, adubɔda ƒula ɔyikun ala abuni ƒui
ewi bekyuli bamba.
Na ɔlalane ɔdi enu kemmo na ƒula ngba bɔdubɔwɔlɔ.
10Na baƒɔ ndubo ƒula lɛkɛ bɔƒɔ bunwini bana lɛdi.
Na ƒula lɛbibo ƒui ebi enwini bekyuli bamba kaduli lɛkɛ kese.
11Na ɔmɛni ƒui kama ni,
ɔlɛ kemmo na adubo bɔtɛ buteedumo
uwi ɔni na éesusu ƒula ɔlɔna
ku ɔlɔgyii ɔmmɔ ébile áwɔlɔ.
12Mmɔ na awɔ ɔlati adubɔsu lɛlɔ anini,
“Ńtenu bɔlɛ!
Na líni na mina kayi kemmo ka lɛƒɔ bɔklibi
bɔni na baaklibi-mi.
13Ńtadi mina ala batinane litemi lɛlɔ.
Na ńtaƒɔ bekyuli bani mɔɔtina-mi ulu buni bɔlɛ.
14Líibo ḿbedu ubu kɔtu
kesii kani na mina ngba bɔyii udu ƒui,
na kadi bekyuli ƒui anumi.”
15Du ntu na awɔ ɔlati ƒula libiɔ kemmo ni,
ntu buni bɔni mɔɔgbá taasi ƒula libiɔ kemmo.
16Bɔda na aada ƒula libiɔ ntu buni ese
na buyi bɔgba butéwi lilu lɛlɔ?
Na aya na ƒula ntukpa buni ntu bamamba bɔgba
butéwi ɔma kemmo kadi ƒui kasakɔ?
17Ya na ala amɛni ƒui ese ete awɔ lɛti kani.
Na tele-nya tete baƒɔ.
18Ya na ƒ'ulekudi unwini libiɔ lɛni ndanku kusɛ kusɛ.
Na lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-ɔ na uleku ɔni ndi-ɔ lɛkloƒu uwi uleku
ɔni na éti mmɔ lɛlɔ.
19Use aani akwa ubi ɔkɔdi ɔni mɔɔdia bɔnu ku lɛlɔyɔ.
Ya na nwuna anyii ani nlɛ-nwu kayi emo-ɔ uwi ndi uwi.
Na nwuna bɔyɔ butaada-a kayi uwi ƒui.
20Mina ubi, bi ɔsu na ɔyalɛ mmomu ala
na ɔlɛka ada-a kayi,
na ataaƒuƒuɛ ukyuli bamba uleku anyii?
21Ɔsika Unwoti ɔɔnu ukyuli biala lɛla lɛni na ɔɔbla,
na ɔɔkɔ́ku nwuna kasiakɔ biala taanu.
22Ukyuli ukpidi ni, nwuna ekpidi lɛlɔ
na baasia teeƒie-nwu.
Na nwuna ablala muunwíni kɔbuli kɔni muudie-nwu.
23Na nwuna lɛlɔ lɛlɔ takana bɔdi ɔsu na ɔdubo bukpi.
Na nwuna kɔdɔlɔ pii ɔsu na ɔdubo bɔyii.

english_text:
Don't Be Foolish
1 My child, suppose you agree
to pay the debt of someone,
who cannot repay a loan.
2Then you are trapped
by your own words,
3and you are now in the power
of someone else.
Here is what you should do:
Go and beg for permission
to call off the agreement.
4Do this before you fall asleep
or even get sleepy.
5Save yourself, just as a deer
or a bird tries to escape
from a hunter.
6You lazy people can learn
by watching an anthill.
7Ants don't have leaders,
8but they store up food
during harvest season.
9How long will you lie there
doing nothing at all?
When are you going to get up
and stop sleeping?
10 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
11Suddenly, everything is gone,
as though it had been taken
by an armed robber.
12Worthless liars go around
13 winking and giving signals
to deceive others.
14They are always thinking up
something cruel and evil,
and they stir up trouble.
15But they will be struck
by sudden disaster
and left without a hope.
16There are six or seven
kinds of people
the Lord doesn't like:
17Those who are too proud
or tell lies or murder,
18those who make evil plans
or are quick to do wrong,
19those who tell lies in court
or stir up trouble
in a family.
20Obey the teaching
of your parents—
21always keep it in mind
and never forget it.
22Their teaching will guide you
when you walk,
protect you when you sleep,
and talk to you
when you are awake.
23The Law of the Lord is a lamp,
and its teachings
shine brightly.
Correction and self-control
will lead you through life.
24They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
25Don't let yourself be attracted
by the charm and lovely eyes
of someone like that.
26A woman who sells her love
can be bought for as little
as the price of a meal.
But making love
to another man's wife
will cost you everything.
27If you carry burning coals,
you burn your clothes;
28if you step on hot coals,
you burn your feet.
29And if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you pay the price.
30We don't put up with thieves,
not even with one who steals
for something to eat.
31And thieves who get caught
must pay back
seven times what was stolen
and lose everything.
32But if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you will destroy yourself
by your own stupidity.
33You will be beaten
and forever disgraced,
34because a jealous husband
can be furious and merciless
when he takes revenge.
35He won't let you pay him off,
no matter what you offer.
translation_text:
Tɛya Lɛla Lɛdi Limeyi Ndi Limeyi
1Mina ubi, si ákya ɔku ɔdi kɔnu éte ƒula ɔkpana
iye enye-nwu kama na nwuna kayu kadi ɔsu,
nsu aaagyi-nwu kaduɛ,
2iye si ényimi lɛlɔ ku linyese lɛdi na ánu áti ka
ábala lɛlɔ na lɛla lɛni na ásu ɔsu ni,
3babla na awia ulu na edie lɛlɔ!
Use aani ka éti lɛlɔ ése ɔkpa éte-nwu.
Anwuɔsu sie-nwu kudɔ na etéboku lɛlɔ kalɔ
na evele ƒula ɔkpana ɔmmɔ kpakplaa!
4Tatɛ litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ talɛɛ
na lɛlɛɛ biala litasia-a anumi.
5Keli ɔgbankpi aani kalɛ na akwa uukeli ɔgbini
iye aasɛ uukeli kakpagyuɛ kani na bákywɛ-nwu.
6Amii bakɔsɔne bɛnu balalɛ na bɛtɛya lɛla.
Bɛnu bana ablala na bɛda anu!
7Beeebo ukyuli ɔni muudie lɛdi taasu-ma
lɛla lɛni babla,
na beeebo ukyuli ɔni mɔɔví taanu-ma lɛlɔ
iye lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔdi.
8Nsu baaklibi edula buse kaƒɛndi uwi,
na baasála-nya na edula ɔƒɛwi.
9Na amii bakɔsɔne ni, uwi ɛlɛ sɔɔn
na bɛdubɔtɛ butaalɛɛ butédu?
Na uwi ɔmani na bɛdubɔta bina kalɛɛkɔ?
10Si ánu ka átɛ ávili, iye eli aalɛɛ teesie taasɔ,
iye eti enu ényimi kayi eli aanwuna ukpludi ni,
11kɔwaba kɔdubo-ɔ buyu bɔtu aani uyune kalɛ.
Na ayaki adubo-ɔ bukpoku aani kekpo ukpone kalɛ.
12Ukyuli ukpidi ku ɔlalane ni,
bɔkɛ kani na ɔɔkɛ taavi uwi ƒui ku ɔkɔ etemila.
13Anumi na baamana bekyuli.
Na lɛgba na baata ala taasia kalɔ
teeti taatina bekyuli ala.
Na animi na beedie kayaa teeti taatɛmi.
14Bana kayi kemmo kasusu kekpidi kaayá
na likpidi kɔkwɛ kani na baakya.
Na baakya lɛsɛ uwi ndi uwi.
15Nsu ɔgbankpi ɔdubɔsiaku-ma kɔnakunwi.
Na badubɔyii udu ɔni na baaagyi beeese,
na kakwɛ kadi keeebo.
16Alakpa aku adi akya na Unwoti ukisi geen.
Na maatɛ adi eesé-nwu lɛlɔ,
17ɔnusɛ ukpidi ukyuli bɔnu,
ku unyemi ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ,
ku enu ani mɔɔta pla pla taadu bekyuli
bani nátabla lɛla lɛdi,
18ku kayi kani muulie taakya likpidi kakwɛ,
ku lɛgba lɛni mɔɔta pla pla na likpidi lɛlɔ,
19ɔkɔ kenye litemi bediene
bani mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ taaka ala.
Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔkya bekyuli ntɛ taabla ala
ani na ubile banwani ntɛ.
Bɔlɛ Na Lɛsɔnɔdi Lɛlɔ
20Mina ubi, da ami ƒ'ɔti ɔda bubo kaduɛ,
na teni ala ani na ƒ'ini ɔɔtina-a.
21Bo-nya da ƒula kayi lɛlɔ uwi ƒui.
Na ebo-nya ada ƒula limɔ.
22Na ala ammɔ adubɔtina-a ulu kesi kesii na akɛ.
Si atɛ alɛɛ ni, adubɔgyumana-a.
Na si áta katɛnkɔ ni, adubɔtɛmiku-ɔ.
23Ɔsika ɔda bubo bɔmɛni bɔdi asogya,
na ala bɔtina bɔmɛni bɔdi-ɔ bukeye.
Na kalɛ na etemila amɛni aaklibi-ɔ
na ati lɛlɔ bɔda ni,
adi ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na adubɔsia na akɛ ngba.
24Ɔdubɔda-a udie uleku ɔyalɛ enu kemmo
ku uleku ɔsɔnɔdine kenyemini etemila kudɔ.
25Ƒula kayi ketenwini katasia nwuna bɔdia lɛlɔ
na ɔda-a limɔ.
Taya na uti nwuna anumi ani na uusé ɔtɔlɔ-ɔ
na uƒu-ɔ kasusu.
26Ɔsika ɔyalɛ ɔdubɔyila-a udu
butédu ƒula limeyi bodobodo muedi.
Na ngba bumodi bɔmmɔ geen
na uleku ɔsɔnɔdine ɔɔtú-ɔ uƒie aani eƒiebuo.
27Si ukyuli édie ogya ku agyabi ásia lɛlɔ ni,
webulo-ɔ bɔkyula ku ƒula adala?
28Na si ésie ávi ogya ku agyabi lɛlɔ ni,
lɛgba lɛdubo bubulo-ɔ bɔnani?
29Lɛni geen na use ute ukyuli
ɔni matɛ nwuna ɔkpana ulekudi kudɔ.
Na ukyuli ɔni makya ɔkpana uleku kɔgbu ni,
badubɔni-nwu kɔtu.
30Bekyuli beleni uyune si úyu
ɔsika kɔka mɔɔdú-nwu ɔsu na úyu ɔnii ɔɔdi umo.
31Nsu si béƒie-nwu ni, ɔdubɔƒɔ eyula ammɔ
kayu akpa maatɛ
ina nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo ala ƒui
na ɔdi ka uti uye asa waƒɔ kayu kammɔ.
32Na ɔnana ɔni nádi kɔsɔnɔ ni, ɔdɔlɔdi geen na ɔdi,
ɔsika ɔɔyila nwuna lɛlɔ udu ƒui.
33Anwu ku alɛlɛbi ku kɔƒa.
Na kɔƒa kɔmmɔ kulása-nwu lɛlɔ kudii.
34Ɔsika uleku ɔmmɔ ɔgyani kogyulo
kɔdubɔya na kɔnyi kutaakɔ-nwu.
Anwuɔsu ɔɔɔdubo kɔnyana bɔnu si uudie-nwu kasi.
35Na kɔnu bɔsia ku etela biala aaadubo-nwu kaƒɔ bɔyɔ
si ina dɛ na etela ammɔ emomo.

english_text:
The Foolishness of Unfaithfulness
1My son, pay close attention
and don't forget
what I tell you to do.
2Obey me, and you will live!
Let my instructions be
your greatest treasure.
3Keep them at your fingertips
and write them
in your mind.
4Let wisdom be your sister
and make common sense
your closest friend.
5They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
6From the window of my house,
I once happened to see
7some foolish young men.
8It was late in the evening,
sometime after dark.
9One of these young men
turned the corner
and was walking by the house
of an unfaithful wife.
10She was dressed fancy
like a woman of the street
with only one thing in mind.
11She was one of those women
who are loud and restless
and never stay at home,
12who walk street after street,
waiting to trap a man.
13She grabbed him and kissed him,
and with no sense of shame,
she said:
14“I had to offer a sacrifice,
and there is enough meat
left over for a feast.
15So I came looking for you,
and here you are!
16The sheets on my bed
are bright-colored cloth
from Egypt.
17And I have covered it
with perfume made of myrrh,
aloes, and cinnamon.
18“Let's go there
and make love all night.
19My husband is traveling,
and he's far away.
20He took a lot of money along,
and he won't be back home
before the middle
of the month.”
21And so, she tricked him
with all of her sweet talk
and her flattery.
22At once he followed her
like an ox on the way
to be slaughtered,
or like a fool on the way
to be punished
23and killed with arrows.
He was no more than a bird
rushing into a trap,
without knowing
it would cost him his life.
24My son, pay close attention
to what I have said.
25Don't even think about
that kind of woman
or let yourself be misled
by someone like her.
26Such a woman has caused
the downfall and destruction
of a lot of men.
27Her house is a one-way street
leading straight down
to the world of the dead.
translation_text:
Bɔlɛ Na Beleku Basɔnɔdine Lɛlɔ
1Ubi, ƒie mina ɔda bubo da kaduɛ,
na aklibi-mu ese na bɔƒɔ-ɔ lɛlɔ kemmo.
2Da-mu kaduɛ na adubulie ngba.
Gyumana-mu aani kalɛ na adubɔgyumana ƒula lɛnumi.
3Nyimi-mu da ƒula animi lɛlɔ,
Na enweni-mu akya ƒula kayi kemmo.
4Su lɛnunda anini, “Awɔ ndi mina ɔnwani ulekubi.”
Na alɔ ala kalɔ bunu anii ƒula lɛlɔ ukyuli.
5Na ala amɛni adubudie-ɔ na uleku ɔsɔnɔdine enu kemmo.
Na edie-ɔ na uleku ɔni mɔɔlɛ́ ɔgyani kama
asɔnɔtɛ ani mɔɔní ukyuli taatákya likpidi kemmo kudɔ.
6Nnye mina ƒansili kudɔ dii,
na lɛ́nu lɛ́vinku kalɛmikɔ liƒi lɛdi.
7Na lɛ́nu bani na bana kasusu kásɔ mmɔ.
Badi bakloƒu bani nási baakɔ́ mɛni akɔ unwi.
Na ɔɔɔgyi lɛbuni ku likpidi kavumana.
8Okloƒu ɔmɛni ɔ́sia ɔblɔnu ɔdi lɛlɔ ɔɔyu úsela okodo ɔdi.
Na ulu ɔmmɔ ɔkɛ ɔ́vi uleku ɔmɛni ɔtɔ kudɔ.
9Na ɔ́ɔbla kadi buɛɛ na use susuusu
uwi ɔni na keyi kadaku buti.
10Uleku ɔdi ɔ́lɛ úbasiaku-nwu
na ɔ́da lɛlɔ aani ɔyalɛ kalɛ na ɔda ɔnana ɔkwɛ.
11Ɔsika uleku ɔni mbo kudu na kɔƒa kulekpo na ɔdi.
Na ulélie kaduli uwi ɔdi.
12Ɔgbami ku eyeya kani na adubɔnu-nwu
Na ɔkɛ amadɔ amadɔ ɔɔƒulu taavi.
13Uleku ɔmɛni ɔ́kya okloƒu ɔmmɔ kɔgbu na ɔ́ƒiɔ-nwu kenye.
Na úƒi anumi ɔ́kun na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini,
14“Lɛ́bla mina unwi bɔbla akpala.
Na ɔmwi lɛ́wɔlɔ lɛla biala ɔkɛnku kenye kani na líse lɛlɔ.
15Anwuɔsu na lɛ́lɛ líbo mbasiaku-ɔ
Lɛ́sia-a anu geen na ḿbanu-ɔ sɔsɔ!
16Lɛ́ɛva mina atɛla líse.
Adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ abuni ani nási Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ
ku kunweni lidu na adi.
17Na lɛ́ya na ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔ́ƒɔ mina atɛla ammɔ.
Nnɔmii bɔni baalɔ mira ku lidu bamba
na lɛ́kuna líwi-nya lɛlɔ.
18Bo, na butátɛ na bunu lɛlɔ emini usien umodi
wetédu kadi bugye.
Na bɔƒuƒuɛ lɛlɔ kaduɛ ku bɔyɔ!
19Mina ɔgyani uuubo kaduli.
Úsie ulugyuɔ ɔdi.
20Úyile nwuna egulabi kavumi ku egulabi
na úti ɔda ulu.
Na ɔɔɔdubo tɔ wetédu kɔbuli kumodi ƒui!”
21Ɔmmɔ ɔsu uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́tɔlɔ-nwu
útásiaku ulu bamba lɛlɔ
ku nwuna atɛ mini mini ammɔ.
Na nwuna katɔlɔ ɔsu úƒie-nwu kayi.
22Na únwini ɔ́siaku-nwu kɔnakunwi
aani ebuo ɔni bésela batádu
iye akwa ɔni nánu kakpagyuɛ,
23na unye ɔgya ka lɛtula lɛƒuala-nwu kayi.
Na útavumanaku aasɛ ɔni muuveyi taatánu kamia
na ɔɔɔgyi ɔnii ɔgbankpi kemmo na úsela.
24Mina bebi, binu ala ani mɔɔsu-mii
Na bise atu na ala ani mɔɔsu
eduo-nya kemmo kaduɛ.
25Bitaya na bina kayi katɔlɔ-mii
na bɛsiaku-nwu kama.
Na bitayii ulu na bɛsiaku ulu ukpidi
ɔni lɛlɔ na úti-mii ɔɔsiaku lɛlɔ.
26Ɔsika anwuɔsu na banana pii báyii udu,
na bani na ɔ́ɔdu lɛnɔ bemomo.
27Uleku ɔmɛni ɔtɔ ni, kaƒiɔtɔ ulu unengudi na ɔdi.
Na ɔtɛ úsie kekpine ubu kalɔ kemmo lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_text:
In Praise of Wisdom
1 With great understanding,
Wisdom is calling out
2as she stands at the crossroads
and on every hill.
3She stands by the city gate
where everyone enters the city,
and she shouts:
4“I am calling out
to each one of you!
5Good sense and sound judgment
can be yours.
6Listen, because what I say
is worthwhile and right.
7I always speak the truth
and refuse to tell a lie.
8Every word I speak is honest,
not one is misleading
or deceptive.
9“If you have understanding,
you will see that my words
are just what you need.
10Let instruction and knowledge
mean more to you than silver
or the finest gold.
11 Wisdom is worth much more
than precious jewels
or anything else you desire.”
Wisdom Speaks
12I am Wisdom—Common Sense
is my closest friend;
I possess knowledge
and sound judgment.
13If you respect the Lord,
you will hate evil.
I hate pride and conceit
and deceitful lies.
14I am strong, and I offer
sensible advice
and sound judgment.
15By my power kings govern,
and rulers make laws
that are fair.
16Every honest leader rules
with help from me.
17I love everyone who loves me,
and I will be found by all
who honestly search.
18I can make you rich and famous,
important and successful.
19What you receive from me
is more valuable
than even the finest gold
or the purest silver.
20I always do what is right,
21and I give great riches
to everyone who loves me.
22 From the beginning,
I was with the Lord.
I was there before he began
23to create the earth.
At the very first,
the Lord gave life to me.
24When I was born,
there were no oceans
or springs of water.
25My birth was before
mountains were formed
or hills were put in place.
26It happened long before God
had made the earth
or any of its fields
or even the dust.
27 I was there when the Lord
put the heavens in place
and stretched the sky
over the surface of the sea.
28I was with him when he placed
the clouds in the sky
and created the springs
that fill the ocean.
29I was there when he set
boundaries for the sea
to make it obey him,
and when he laid foundations
to support the earth.
30I was right beside the Lord,
helping him plan and build.
I made him happy each day,
and I was happy at his side.
31I was pleased with his world
and pleased with its people.
32 Pay attention, my children!
Follow my advice,
and you will be happy.
33Listen carefully
to my instructions,
and you will be wise.
34Come to my home each day
and listen to me.
You will find happiness.
35By finding me, you find life,
and the Lord will be pleased
with you.
36But if you don't find me,
you hurt only yourself,
and if you hate me,
you are in love with death.
translation_text:
Lɛnunda Lɛɛkpali Ka Bekyuli Benu-nwu Ala Bɔtina
1Ɔɔɔdi bɔkpali na lɛnunda lɛda bekyuli?
Na ɔɔɔdi ala kalɔ bunu muubó kudu momoomo mmɔ?
2Unye lilu lɛlɔ na kesii kani nákuku ƒui.
Na uudí teenye elukpo ƒui lɛlɔ.
3Unye lɛban lɛni ƒui na baasia
teeduo ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo kenye
na ɔɔkɔ́ lɛsa na kɔyakun kɔmmɔ ƒui ɔnini,
4“O amii bekyuli na mɔɔkpali.
Amii kadi ƒui bekyuli na mɔɔtalaku lɛdi katɔ
kalɛ na binu.
5Bina kasusu kásɔ bibo na lite-mii lɛnunda.
Bɛ́dɔlɔ bibo na lite-mii ala kalɔ bunu.
6Bise atu na binu! Ɔsika ndanku ala abuni geen
na ndubo-mii bɔsu.
Ala ani ndi ulu na muubimi mina kenye taatɛmi.
7Na lɛla lɛni ndi litemi geen lɛmmɔ na mina kenye kaasu.
Na mina enyekuli ekisi ulikplu ala.
8Mina kenye etemila adi etemila geen.
Na lɛla biala líteƒu lítakya iye lɛbla gontii
na etemila ammɔ kemmo.
9Mina etemila ese nwaa ete ukyuli
ɔni muunú ala kalɔ.
Na bani na bagyi lɛla badubɔnu
ka bɔƒiɔ bɔdi buuubo-nya kemmo.
10Ƒuna mina ala bɔtina utulo sika ɔƒualadi.
Na aƒuna lɛlati etulo sika ugyiedi.
11Ɔsika lɛnunda lɛ́ƒɔ kuye litulo sika asɛɛ
ani náƒɔ kuye geen.
Na lɛla lɛdi liiibo na ukyuli ɔɔwia na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ
na bakana-ni buti bɔkɔku lɛnunda.
12“Ami ndi lɛnunda, na nli na unwi bɔbla kemmo
ku litemi bɔtɛ na ulu geen ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.
Mbo lɛlati ku ala kemmo bɔnu taati.
13Unwoti bɔyia ndi likpidi bukisi.
Nkisi lɛlɔ katɔ bɔtalaku ku bekyuli lɛlɔ bɔta teenye.
Na nkisi likyulikpi ala bɔbla ku enyekpi bɔtɛmi.
14Ami mɔɔlɛ ukyuli na mɔɔtɛ etemila siin.
Ami mbo ɔyikun na muunú ala kemmo nwaa.
15Mina lɛlɔ na baga baasia taadi bekyuli lɛlɔ.
Na lɛlɔ badine beeti ɔda bubo bɔbuni teete bekyuli.
16Ɔkɛnku-mi lɛlɔ na bagadine baadi bekyuli lɛlɔ
ku babune bani mɔɔtɔnku bekyuli ulu lɛlɔ siin.
17“Bekyuli bani ƒui mɔɔyɔ́-mi ni, ami lɛnɔ mɔɔyɔ́-ma.
Na bani mɔɔwia-mi kama ulu baanu-mi.
18Mina kudɔ na lɛkɛ ku ɔbu ɔɔsí.
Na ɔdi lɛkɛ lɛni muutu uwi na ala aatɛku ukyuli.
19Na ala ani muute mmɔ eekeye
teetulo sika ugyiedi.
Na kayu kani mɔɔƒɔ bekyuli ɔdia
utulo sika ɔƒualadi buni ƒui.
20Ulu ɔni nse siin lɛlɔ na mɔɔsia,
na mɔɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ.
21Bekyuli bani ƒui mɔɔyɔ́-mi ni, lɛkɛ na muusé-ma kama,
na muuyile bana egulabi kɔvumi.
22“Ami na Unwoti ɔdanku asa na ɔdubuse kalɔ
ku lɛla biala budie
ku kuuku ala ani ƒui nákya.
23Únyene-mi mina kenyekɔ
asa na lɛla biala lɛdubuse kalɔ.
Na nli asa na ɔdubudie kayawi.
24Báawɔ-mi asa na Unwoti
údie ɛpu,
na nli uwi ɔni na abiɔ ku ntukpa ƒui bútebo tɔ.
25Asa na abi adubɔkɛ kenyekɔ
na abinkpo akɔ alɛ ni, báawɔ-mi kukuuku.
26Asa na Unwoti wedie kalɔ kamɛni ku egyii ku livo
iye lɛti lɛni lɛlɔ na ákwɛ enye ni, nkya kukuuku.
27“Nnye mɔɔnu asa na údie kayaa
na ɔ́bla-ka aani ligegu útébi ɛpu lɛlɔ.
28Na nnye mɔɔnu asa na ɔ́bla ulɔyɔ ɔ́ƒala kayaa
ku uwi ɔni na ɔ́bla ntukpa bonwu
bɔni nágyu voo mmɔ ɔ́kya kalɔ lɛlɔ.
29Na mɔɔnu asa na ɔ́sia kalɔ ubili
aani ɔmii úte ɛpu ɔmmɔ ƒui
kalɛ na uleyi ulavia mmɔ.
Na kalɛ na úse kalɔ kammɔ ɔka kalɔ ni,
nnye mɔɔnu.
30Geen ni, ami ndi-nwu kabla kammɔ
kakwɛ ɔkyane na nwuna kɔmadɔ.
Na mɔɔkɛ́ ebiti limeyi ndi limeyi
na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-mi na nwuna anumi uwi ndi uwi.
31Na ami lɛnɔ ni, lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-mi
na kayawi kammɔ ƒui ɔsu
na ebiti áƒɔ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui
na kadi ƒui bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ.
32“Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, mina bebi, binu-mi litemi,
ɔsika lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ bekyuli bani ƒui mɔɔsia-mi kasiakɔ.
33Binu mina ala bɔtina na bɛda anu
na biteni-mu.
34“Lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ bekyuli bani muunú-mi litemi
na baanu-mi ulu limeyi ndi limeyi
na benye bagya-mi na mina kayakun kenye.
35Ɔsika ukyuli biala nánu-mi ɔti ni, ɔ́kɛ ngba,
na nwuna lɛlɔ lɛdubɔda Unwoti ebiti.
36Nsu bekyuli bani na báyii ulu na bátanu-mi ni,
bábla lɛlɔ kalala.
Na bani muukisi-mi ni,
bati ka kukpi na baayɔ́.”

english_text:
Wisdom Gives a Feast
1Wisdom has built her house
with its seven columns.
2She has prepared the meat
and set out the wine.
Her feast is ready.
3She has sent her servant women
to announce her invitation
from the highest hills:
4“Everyone who is ignorant
or foolish is invited!
5All of you are welcome
to my meat and wine.
6If you want to live,
give up your foolishness
and let understanding
guide your steps.”
True Wisdom
7Correct a worthless bragger,
and all you will get
are insults and injuries.
8Any bragger you correct
will only hate you.
But if you correct someone
who has common sense,
you will be loved.
9If you have good sense,
instruction will help you
to have even better sense.
And if you live right,
education will help you
to know even more.
10 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of wisdom.
To have understanding,
you must know the Holy God.
11I am Wisdom. If you follow me,
you will live a long time.
12Good sense is good for you,
but if you brag,
you hurt yourself.
A Foolish Invitation
13Stupidity is reckless,
senseless, and foolish.
14She sits in front of her house
and on the highest hills
in the town.
15She shouts to everyone
who passes by,
16“If you are stupid,
come on inside!”
And to every fool she says,
17“Stolen water tastes best,
and the food you eat in secret
tastes best of all.”
18None who listen to Stupidity
understand that her guests
are as good as dead.
translation_text:
Lɛnunda Ku Kɔdɔlɔ Baalɔ Bekyuli
1Lɛnunda lɛ́tu ɔtɔ, na nwuna kemmo kéwi.
Na ɔtɔ ntɛ akpa maatɛ ada-nwu.
2Ɔ́nwa adila na úse kadikɔ bonwu ku ntɛ lidu lidu
úse ka bekyuli babadi.
3Na ɔ́tala nwuna kabla bablane
ka batálɔ bekyuli ƒui bavi na bebo.
Unye kesii kani nákuku
na ɔɔnu ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ƒui.
4Mmɔ na ɔ́kpali ɔ́su bani na bana kasusu kásɔ
na baaagyi bana kɔmii iye kɔdianu ɔnini,
5“Bibo na bibadi mina adila
na bɛni mina ntɛ bɔni na lɛ́sala líse.
6Na bɛda bina adɔlɔla bɔbla bɛya
na bise kalɔ ku ngba geen bulie na bɛda anu lɛnɔ.”
7Awɔ ɔni madɔnku ukyuli
ɔni na bekyuli anyikpi kani na ɔɔlɔ ni,
kenye na ɔdubo-ɔ bɔtu.
Na ukyuli ɔni madɔnku ukyuli ukpidi ni,
kalala na ɔdubo-ɔ bɔbla.
8Anwuɔsu tekpoku lɛlɔ ka adɔnku ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu.
Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, badubo-ɔ bukisi.
Nsu si ádɔnku banundane ama ni,
badubo-ɔ bɔyɔ bubu.
9Tina banundane ala na badubɔda anu bebu.
Na atina ama bani nlie siin ala na badubɔti ala bebu.
10Si aayia Unwoti ni, ese kalɔ aadá anu.
Na si ánu Unwoti Kedee ɔmmɔ áti ni,
agyi anii ése kalɔ adubo lɛla bɔti.
11Lɛnunda lɛdubɔya na ƒula emeyi emomo ebu.
Na akwa asia-a akwa lɛlɔ.
12Na si áda anu ni, awɔ ndubɔkɛ kɔsia.
Na si apii lɛnunda ni, awɔ ndubo abi bubo.
13Uleku ɔni básia lɛnyi banii Kɔdɔlɔ ni,
ubo lɛsɛ na uláƒalɛ.
Ɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛdi, nsu anwu ɔlati ɔɔɔgyi lɛni.
14Uulie nwuna kayakun na kesii kani náta kákɔ,
na ɔɔnu ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ taamana.
15Ɔɔkpali banana bani nkɛ bésela bana kabla kadi akɔ
unwi unwi teemene ɔnini,
16“Bo-mi kudɔ na abanu lɛla lɛdi na mina kaduli!”
Na bani neeebo kasusu ni, ɔɔsu-ma ɔnini,
17“Ntu bɔni na éyu kesii kadi áni ni,
amu mɔɔyu kayi geen.
Na adila ani na ábɛ átádi ni,
anya mɔɔyu emini geen!”
18Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ni, banana bammɔ baaagyi ka
bana bani na uleku ɔmɛni ɔ́ɔka bɔkpali lɛni
na bésie ni, kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo na bátáwɔlɔ.

english_text:
Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some proverbs
of Solomon:
Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
make them sad.
2What you gain by doing evil
won't help you at all.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
3If you obey the Lord,
you won't go hungry;
if you are wicked,
God won't let you have
what you want.
4Laziness leads to poverty;
hard work makes you rich.
5At harvest season
it's smart to work hard,
but stupid to sleep.
6Everyone praises good people,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
7Good people are remembered
long after they are gone,
but the wicked
are soon forgotten.
8If you have good sense,
you will listen and obey;
if all you do is talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
9You will be safe,
if you always do right,
but you will get caught,
if you are dishonest.
10Deceit causes trouble,
and foolish talk
will bring you to ruin.
11The words of good people
are a source of life,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
12 Hatred stirs up trouble;
love overlooks the wrongs
that others do.
13If you have good sense,
it will show when you speak.
But if you are stupid,
you will be beaten
with a stick.
14If you have good sense,
you will learn all you can,
but foolish talk
will soon destroy you.
15Great wealth can be a fortress,
but poverty
is no protection at all.
16If you live right,
the reward is a good life;
if you are evil,
all you have is sin.
17Accept correction,
and you will find life;
reject correction,
and you will miss the road.
18You can hide your hatred
by telling lies,
but you are a fool
to spread lies.
19You will say the wrong thing
if you talk too much—
so be sensible and watch
what you say.
20The words of a good person
are like pure silver,
but the thoughts
of an evil person
are almost worthless.
21Many are helped
by useful instruction,
but fools are killed
by their own stupidity.
22When the Lord blesses you
with riches,
you have nothing to regret.
23Fools enjoy doing wrong,
but anyone with good sense
enjoys acting wisely.
24What evil people dread most
will happen to them,
but good people will get
what they want most.
25Those crooks will disappear
when a storm strikes,
but God will keep safe
all who obey him.
26Having a lazy person on the job
is like a mouth full of vinegar
or smoke in your eyes.
27If you respect the Lord,
you will live longer;
if you keep doing wrong,
your life will be cut short.
28If you obey the Lord,
you will be happy,
but there is no future
for the wicked.
29The Lord protects everyone
who lives right,
but he destroys anyone
who does wrong.
30Good people will stand firm,
but the wicked will disappear
from the land.
31Honest people speak sensibly,
but deceitful liars
will be silenced.
32If you obey the Lord,
you will always know
the right thing to say.
But no one will trust you
if you tell lies.
translation_text:
Salomo Úbo Agba Adi
1Salomo agba bamba ndi amɛni.
Lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ bawɔne bani bebi mɔɔdá anu.
Nsu ubi ɔdɔlɔdi bawɔne ni,
badubuwulo ku kɔnyana.
2Lɛkɛ lɛni na ukyuli ɔ́sia ulu ukpidi ɔdi lɛlɔ ɔ́kɛ ni,
liiibo kɔsia.
Nsu si elie ngba na ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ ni,
adubɔkɛ ngba bɔƒɔ.
3Unwoti ɔɔɔdubo bɔya na kɔka kɔdu nwuna ukyuli
ɔni mɔɔbla nwuna lɛƒɔyɔ.
Na bekyuli bekpidi ama ni,
Unwoti ulenu-ma ala ani na beevele-nwu.
4Bakɔsɔne beeebo bawabane bunwini.
Mmomu bagyoklone mɔɔkɛ́ lɛkɛ.
5Okloƒu ɔni na ɔ́da anu ni,
uunye kabla lɛlɔ kpakplaa ɔtumawi ƒui.
Na okloƒu ɔni mɔɔtɛ taalɛɛ
uwi ɔni na nka katuma kuƒi kɔ́lɛmi-nwu ni,
kɔƒa na uuboku kaduli.
6Kusɛ kusɛ ɔɔsiaku bekyuli bani mɔɔbu Unwoti.
Na bekyuli bekpidi baabɛla bana kasusu
kekpidi kɔkwɛ.
7Bekyuli kasusu kaasia bekyuli babuni lɛlɔ,
nsu balalane anyi muedi aayii kede kede.
8Ebiti aada banundane si baalɛ-ma.
Nsu katɛ batɛne badɔlɔdi ni,
beebuli teeti anumi teebi kalɔ.
9Na bekyuli bani mɔɔdi litemi lɛlɔ ulu lɛlɔ ni,
balánya teegyiile.
Nsu bani kasiakɔ nse gontii ni,
badubo bugyiile bubuli.
10Bekyuli bani mɔɔnu likpidi
taamana bekyuli lɛnumi ni,
baakya lɛsɛ.
Nsu si átanu ukyuli anumi na ádɔnku-nwu mmomu
na likpidi lɛdi ɔsu ni, eeboku keyi buɛɛ.
11Bekyuli babuni etemila aakpanku ukyuli
teesienku ngba kemmo.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi beeti ala
teebi bana kasusu kekpidi.
12Ukyuli bukisi bɔɔkya kadɔ ɔgya.
Nsu bɔyɔ bɔsɔ bulánu likpidi na ukyuli lɛlɔ.
13Bekyuli bani muunú ala kalɔ ni,
baatɛmi lɛnunda etemila.
Nsu badɔlɔdi ama ni,
kegyiimi na badubuti bani-ma kɔtu.
14Lɛlati lɛ́ƒɔ banundane kuye,
nsu badɔlɔdi adɔlɔtɛ eeboku lɛlɔ bukpoku.
15Balakɛne baanu bana lɛlakɛ aani kɔbi bonwu
kɔni na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana bɔƒuaala.
Na bawabane kɔwaba ndi bana ɔgbankpi.
16Bekyuli babuni lɛyuƒɔla muubunku bana keliela.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ama ni,
likyulikpi ala bɔbla lɛlɔ beewiakun bana egulabi.
17Bekyuli bani mɔɔtuna na baalɛ-ma ni,
baasia ngba ulu lɛlɔ.
Nsu bani muuní ɔmɛni ni,
baakpanku bekyuli bamba lɛnɔ taatáyila.
18Ukyuli ɔni muukisi ukyuli na ɔɔbɛla-mu ɔdi ɔkɔ ɔnyine.
Na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔlɔ bekyuli anyikpi ɔdi ɔdɔlɔdi.
19Sɔ tatɛmi pii, ɔsika atɛ pii aadanku likpidi.
Da anu na akɔsi atɛ bumomo!
20Bekyuli babuni etemila ese
aani sika ɔƒualadi ɔni bekyuli bánu ka ɔdia.
Nsu ukyuli ukpidi kayi
kemmo ni,
kɔsia kɔdi kulalɛ.
21Bekyuli babuni baalɛ ukyuli ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ama baayii udu
na bana lɛla tati ɔsu.
22Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ mɔɔyá na ukyuli uunwíni ɔlakɛne,
na kɔnyana kɔdi kulásia ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.
23Badɔlɔdi ebiti ndi ka belie bataabla likpidi.
Nsu banundane ebiti ndi ka bada udu buɛɛ
na babla ala lɛnunda kemmo.
24Ala ani na balalane baayia ka atalɛku-ma ni,
anya geen ndubɔlɛku-ma.
Na lɛni kani na bekyuli babuni ala
ani lɛlɔ na bebo lɛnunsia adububo ete-ma.
25Ɔgbankpi uubo bekyuli bekpidi lɛlɔ
aani ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔkya ligede, na uuti-ma ƒui.
Nsu bekyuli babuni kɔwodu kalɔ ɔka
ɔni bákya uunye teetu uwi.
26Bakɔsɔne baakya bekyuli bani kabla na baabla ɔlɛ.
Na bese aani uyɔ ɔni muuduo ukyuli anumi
iye ntɛ bɔnani bɔni mɔɔyá na kenye anyi aanyi.
27Si aayia Unwoti ni, ngba buune-ɔ.
Nsu balalane ngba bɔɔdá likuku.
28Bekyuli babuni lɛnunsia liiboku ebiti,
nsu ala ani na bekyuli bekpidi baasia anu
eenwíni lɛƒua.
29Unwoti ɔɔgyumana bekyuli bani nse siin,
na ɔɔyila balalane udu.
30Lɛla biala lɛɛɛdubo bekyuli babuni bukpoku.
Nsu balalane ni, badubudie-ma bana kunyekɔ
na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ.
31Kasusu buni na ukyuli ɔbuni uute ukyuli.
Nsu unyemi ɔnii mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ badubo-nwu bukulo budie.
32Etemila ani mebunku ukyuli na ukyuli ɔbuni ɔɔtɛmi.
Nsu etemila ani muusé lɛlɔ na balalane baatɛmi.

english_text:
Watch What You Say and Do
1The Lord hates anyone
who cheats,
but he likes everyone
who is honest.
2Too much pride
can put you to shame.
It's wiser to be humble.
3If you do the right thing,
honesty will be your guide.
But if you are crooked,
you will be trapped
by your own dishonesty.
4When God is angry,
money won't help you.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
5If you are truly good,
you will do right;
if you are wicked,
you will be destroyed
by your own sin.
6Honesty can keep you safe,
but if you can't be trusted,
you trap yourself.
7When the wicked die,
their hopes die with them.
8Trouble goes right past
the Lord's people
and strikes the wicked.
9Dishonest people use gossip
to destroy their neighbors;
good people are protected
by their own good sense.
10When honest people prosper
and the wicked disappear,
the whole city celebrates.
11Good people bring prosperity
to their city,
but deceitful liars
can destroy a city.
12It's stupid to say bad things
about your neighbors.
If you are sensible,
you will keep quiet.
13A gossip tells everything,
but a true friend
will keep a secret.
14 A city without wise leaders
will end up in ruin;
a city with many wise leaders
will be kept safe.
15It's a dangerous thing
to guarantee payment
for someone's debts.
Don't do it!
16A gracious woman
will be respected,
but a ruthless man
will only get rich.
17Kindness is rewarded—
but if you are cruel,
you hurt yourself.
18Meanness gets you nowhere,
but goodness is rewarded.
19Always do the right thing,
and you will live;
keep on doing wrong,
and you will die.
20The Lord hates sneaky people,
but he likes everyone
who lives right.
21You can be sure of this:
All crooks will be punished,
but God's people won't.
22A beautiful woman
who acts foolishly
is like a gold ring
on the snout of a pig.
23Good people want what is best,
but troublemakers
hope to stir up trouble.
24Sometimes you can become rich
by being generous
or poor by being greedy.
25Generosity will be rewarded:
Give a cup of water,
and you will receive
a cup of water in return.
26Charge too much for grain,
and you will be cursed;
sell it at a fair price,
and you will be praised.
27Try hard to do right,
and you will win friends;
go looking for trouble,
and you will find it.
28Trust in your wealth,
and you will be a failure,
but God's people will prosper
like healthy plants.
29Fools who cause trouble
in the family
won't inherit a thing.
They will end up as slaves
of someone with good sense.
30Live right, and you will eat
from the life-giving tree.
And if you act wisely,
others will follow.
31 If good people are rewarded
here on this earth,
all who are cruel and mean
will surely be punished.
translation_text:
1Unwoti ukisi uyedine mɔɔnya ukyuli akya.
Nsu lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-nwu si ɔɔkɔ́ku ala teete-ma.
2Si aatalaku lɛlɔ katɔ ni, kɔƒa bɔdi nsia.
Nsu si eeboku lɛlɔ kalɔ ni, na aadá anu.
3Bekyuli babuni ni, bana litemi lɛni lɛlɔ
baadi ulu lɛlɔ mɔɔtina-ma kasiakɔ.
Na balalane ama ni, bana litemi lɛlɔ tadi
mɔɔyila-ma udu.
4Ukyuli lɛkɛ lɛɛɛdubo-nwu bubunku
Unwoti litemi bɔtɛ limeyi.
Nsu ngba buni bulie muudie ukyuli na kukpi kemmo.
5Bekyuli babuni ni, bana litemi lɛlɔ bɔdi ulu lɛlɔ
mɔɔtina-ma kasiakɔ.
Na balalane ama ni, bana ekpidi unu
mɔɔsia-ma lɛlɔ.
6Ngba buni bɔni na bekyuli babuni belie
muudie-ma ɔgbankpi kemmo.
Na lɛla lɛni lɛlɔ na balalane anumi eegyie ni,
ani muunwíni kakpagyuɛ teedie-ma.
7Si balalane békpi ni, ama ku bana lɛnunsia ƒui lɛ́yii udu,
ɔsika bana ɔyikun ɔni neeenye ligeen lɛlɔ kani na basia anu.
8Unwoti uudie bekyuli babuni na ɔgbankpi kemmo.
Na balalane ama uunye taanu
na beesié taatátua ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ.
9Enyekpi aayila ukyuli ɔkpana udu.
Na ala bɔnu bɔti na lɛnunda kemmo
uudie bekyuli babuni.
10Si ala aatɛ teete ukyuli
ɔbuni ni,
ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli baakɛ́ lɛlɔyɔ.
Lɛni kani si ukyuli ukpidi úkpi ni,
kaƒɔ kaayɔ́-ma.
11Bekyuli bani nse siin beete ɔma kusɛ kusɛ
na ɔɔlɛ́ lili.
Nsu balalane etemila eele bekyuli ntɛ
na balakana bɔsala.
12Si eedie ukyuli kalɔ ni, kɔdɔlɔ kɔdi.
Na ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́da anu ni,
uubile nwuna kenye kpoo.
13Katɛ ɔtɛne keeke mɔɔví teebo abɛla kudu.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni báƒɔ bádi ka ulátɛmi kalɛ kalɛ ni,
baasu-nwu kɔbɛtɛ.
14Si kadi badi bekyuli beeebo ɔtɔnkune ɔnundane ni,
ɔma ulábla ɔma.
Nsu si bébo kasusu betine pii ni,
ɔma ɔmmɔ uusié kaduɛ.
15Aawia ɔgbankpi teete lɛlɔ
si éténye ɔƒɔ ɔdi kama na nwuna kayu ɔsu.
Si ébulo ni, ɔdia utulo
ka ebeteebo abi adi kama.
16Beleku bani mbo lɛƒɔndia baakɛ́ ɔbu teetulo banana
bani mbo ulikplu na baakɛ́ egulabi.
17Si aabla lɛƒɔndia ni, awɔ ɔlati ƒula kɔyu mɔɔlɛ́ lili.
Nsu si aabla kalala ni, aayila lɛlɔ udu.
18Bekyuli bekpidi ni, uwi klukui kani
na bana lɛkɛ liilie.
Nsu bekyuli babuni akɛla ni, eetu uwi.
19Bekyuli babuni baakɛ́ ngba.
Na bekyuli bekpidi baasiáku kukpi.
20Unwoti ukisi bekyuli bani na bana kayi
kaaakɛ ulu unwi.
Nsu bani mɔɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ ulu lɛlɔ
baayɔ́-nwu kaƒɔ.
21Ɔbla-a nwaa ka Unwoti ɔdubɔni bekyuli bekpidi kɔtu.
Nsu bekyuli babuni bebi ni,
badubɔlɛ sɛɛn ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lilabla-ma.
22Uleku ɔni mɔɔdia bɔnu na ɔɔɔgyi lɛbuni
ku likpidi kavumana ni,
nwuna ablala ese aani sika kakwɛnimi
kani nda ɔplakuo enwu kemmo.
23Bekyuli babuni mɔɔsia anu ka badubɔkɛ ebiti.
Na bekyuli bekpidi ama ni,
kɔtu bɔni kani na badubɔnu ulu bete.
24Bekyuli badi bakya na beete bekyuli ala ku kaƒɔ,
nsu bana lɛkɛ limomo teebu.
Nsu babambadi lɛnɔ baabla lɛnumi,
nsu baayila lɛla biala na bebo.
25Bekyuli bani muute bekyuli ala ƒaa ni,
ala aadianku-ma na eedú-ma ɔkwɛ.
Lɛni kani na bekyuli bani muubunku bekyuli
kalɛ na belie ku kayi ƒaa ni,
ama alati lɛnɔ badubulie ku kayi ƒaa.
26Beyedine bani mɔɔbɛla ala teese
na basɔku beye kuye
kpakplaa ni,
bekyuli beewida-ma.
Na bani muuyé ala teete-ma
uwi ɔni na baayaki ala
ammɔ ni,
bekyuli beete-ma kusɛ kusɛ.
27Si aawia lɛbuni teete bekyuli ni,
bekyuli badubɔnu-ɔ kɔnyana.
Nsu si aawia-ma likpidi ni,
ɔgbankpi ndubo-ɔ bɔsiaku.
28Si éti anu ásia ƒula egulabi
lɛlɔ ni,
adubo bɔyii udu!
Nsu bekyuli babuni badubɔlɛ lili
aani ketudi evete wɔwɔɔwɔ.
29Bekyuli bani mɔɔkya lɛsɛ
na beeti kayu teeboku
kaduli ni,
lɛƒua na beesé-ma kama.
Na badɔlɔdi ni, ama muunwíni banundane kabla bablane.
30Bekyuli babuni bese aani egyii
ani mɔɔnwu ebi buni ani baadi teelie ngba.
Na bani muudie bekyuli na ɔgbankpi kemmo ni,
báda anu.
31Si ɔdubɔyu bekyuli babuni muedi ɔkplu
na kalɔ kamɛni kemmo ni,
bi malɛku ala ekpidi bablane ama?

english_text:
You Can't Hide behind Evil
1 To accept correction is wise,
to reject it is stupid.
2The Lord likes everyone
who lives right,
but he punishes everyone
who makes evil plans.
3Sin cannot offer security!
But if you live right,
you will be as secure
as a tree with deep roots.
4A helpful wife is a jewel
for her husband,
but a shameless wife
will make his bones rot.
5Good people have kind thoughts,
but you should never trust
the advice of someone evil.
6Bad advice is a deadly trap,
but good advice
is like a shield.
7Once the wicked are defeated,
they are gone forever,
but no one who obeys God
will ever be thrown down.
8Good sense is worthy of praise,
but stupidity is a curse.
9It's better to be ordinary
and have only one servant
than to think you are somebody
and starve to death.
10Good people are kind
to their animals,
but a mean person is cruel.
11Hard working farmers have more
than enough food;
daydreamers are nothing more
than stupid fools.
12An evil person tries to hide
behind evil;
good people are like trees
with deep roots.
13We trap ourselves
by telling lies,
but we stay out of trouble
by living right.
14We are rewarded or punished
for what we say and do.
15Fools think they know
what is best,
but a sensible person
listens to advice.
16Losing your temper is foolish;
ignoring an insult is smart.
17An honest person
tells the truth in court,
but a dishonest person
tells nothing but lies.
18Sharp words cut like a sword,
but words of wisdom heal.
19Truth will last forever;
lies are soon found out.
20An evil mind is deceitful,
but gentle thoughts
bring happiness.
21Good people never have trouble,
but troublemakers
have more than enough.
22The Lord hates every liar,
but he is the friend of all
who can be trusted.
23Be sensible and don't tell
everything you know—
only fools spread
foolishness everywhere.
24Work hard, and you
will be a leader;
be lazy, and you
will end up a slave.
25Worry is a heavy burden,
but a kind word
always brings cheer.
26You are better off to do right,
than to lose your way
by doing wrong.
27Anyone too lazy to cook
will starve,
but a hard worker
is a valuable treasure.
28Living right is a pathway
that leads to life
and away from death.
translation_text:
1Si aayɔ́ atɛya ala ni, ɔlɛka atuna na batumini-ɔ.
Kɔdɔlɔ kɔdi-ɔ si alayɔ anii bedie-ɔ bɔƒiɔ.
2Lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ Unwoti na bekyuli babuni lɛlɔ.
Nsu ulátunaku balalane kɔkwɛ kukpidi kɔni na baakya.
3Ulikplu ala bɔbla buléboku keliela buni ku atu bɔyɔ.
Mmomu bekyuli babuni muudie lidu teesie ɔgyu.
4Uleku ɔbuni ɔni lɛlɔ basia
kayi ni,
anwu ndi ɔgyani lɛlɔyɔ
na use aani kagabwa na kebi ɔnana ɔmmɔ lili.
Nsu uleku ɔni mɔɔbla kɔƒa
ala ni,
ɔɔƒɛ ɔgyani enu, na ɔyikun ɔɔsá-nwu.
5Kɔkwɛ kɔni na ukyuli ɔbuni ɔɔkya kɔɔsia ulu lɛlɔ.
Nsu ɔlalane bɔlɛ bɔdanku ɔgbankpi.
6Ɔlalane etemila ese aani kalɛ na ebuo ukpidi ɔɔbɛ́
taatɛ kuludɔ kalɛ na uƒie lɛla lɛdi.
Nsu ukyuli ɔbuni etemila aaƒɔ́ ukyuli ngba.
7Bekyuli bekpidi beekpi taayii udu ƒui,
nsu bekyuli babuni bebi ama beenye kpakplaa uwi biala.
8Ukyuli ɔni na ubo kasusu kabuni lɛlɔ
lɛɛda bekyuli ƒui ebiti,
na beení bani nsiaku
kalala ulu.
9Si bekyuli balanu-ɔ banii adi ukyuli
nsu ebo kabla bablane ni,
ɔdia utulo ukyuli ɔni mɔɔkɔliku lɛlɔ katɔ ɔnii ɔƒɔ kuye,
nsu uuubo lɛla lɛni na ɔdi muedi.
10Bekyuli babuni ni, baawia bana bebuo
bani na baatumini muedi bɔdia.
Nsu lɛƒɔndia lɛni na ulikplune ɔɔbla ukyuli ni,
lɛdanku kasusu kekpidi.
11Bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla kpakplaa
bebo adila pii na badi bemo.
Nsu si éni kabla na akɛ eebile uwi taavi ni,
ɔdi kɔdɔlɔ.
12Beyune ni, bana lɛlɔ ala ani na buyu
na bétéyu-nya muedi eegyie bana lɛlɔ anumi.
Nsu bekyuli babuni ni, ama alati mɔɔnwu bana ebi.
13Bekyuli bekpidi ni, bana kenye etemila
muudie-ma teete.
Nsu bekyuli babuni ama baalɛ́ ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kemmo.
14Bekyuli baakana na baasia bana kenye etemila lɛlɔ
na baakɛ́ ala pii.
Lɛni kani na bana enu kabla lɛnɔ kaayá
na baakɛ́ kɔsia pii.
15Badɔlɔdi mɔɔkali banii
baláwia ka
ukyuli ɔdi ɔkya-ma kasusu.
Nsu banundane beesé atu teenu bekyuli bamba bɔlɛ.
16Ɔdɔlɔdi uuubo kɔnyi buti.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni náda anu ni,
si ina bédumi-nwu muedi ɔɔkɛ́ kayi buɛɛ.
17Ukyuli ɔni muudie lɛla lɛni na ɔ́nu kenye ulu lɛlɔ ni,
ɔɔsu litemi geen lɛmmɔ.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni muudie lɛla lɛni na útanu kenye ni,
ɔdi ɔkɔ ɔnyine.
18Bekyuli badi beedie ala taalɛ bekyuli
na aatu kayi.
Nsu banundane etemila aabwi bekyuli
bani kayi muunú ɔlɛ.
19Litemi geen liláyii udu uwi ɔdi kudii.
Na likpidi lɛnɔ liiibo keyi bɔlɛ.
20Ɔkɔ etemila aaƒɔ́ bekyuli bani muuti
likpidi kasusu kayi kemmo ƒui.
Na bani lɛnɔ na keyi buɛɛ kasusu na beeti ni,
lɛlɔyɔ mɔɔkya-ma kayi kemmo.
21Ɔgbankpi kpakplaa ɔdi ulébo bekyuli babuni lɛlɔ.
Nsu balalane ni, ɔgbankpi ulalɛ-ma ɔtɔ kemmo.
22Unwoti ukisi bekyuli bani naaadi bana linyese lɛlɔ.
Na bani mɔɔbla taasiaku-mu lɛlɔ baayɔ́-nwu kaƒɔ.
23Banundane belebo bana lɛlati kudu.
Nsu badɔlɔdi ama beedie bana kɔdɔlɔ keyi.
24Si aabla kabla kpakplaa ni,
adubɔtɔnku bekyuli.
Na si aabla kɔkɔsɔ ni, adubunwini kabla ɔblane
ete bekyuli bamba.
25Ukyuli ulalɛ lili si kasusu keekpóku-nwu.
Na etemila ani muusé kayi aayá na lɛlɔ lɛɛƒɛnimi-nwu.
26Bekyuli babuni baakya bana bakpana kasusu kabuni.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ama baatɔ́lɔ bana bakpana taatáyila.
27Kɔkɔsɔ kɔɔdi bekyuli lɛlɔ ɔni na ebuo ɔni bádu muedi
ukyuli bamba muuƒulo-nwu teete-ma.
Nsu bani mɔɔsia bana
kabla anu ni,
baada-ka kaduɛ.
28Bekyuli babuni kasiakɔ kaakpanku-ma
teesienku ngba kemmo, na ɔɔɔdi kekpine.

english_text:
Wise Friends Make You Wise
1Children with good sense
accept correction
from their parents,
but stubborn children
ignore it completely.
2You will be well rewarded
for saying something kind,
but all some people think about
is how to be cruel and mean.
3 Keep what you know to yourself,
and you will be safe;
talk too much,
and you are done for.
4No matter how much you want,
laziness won't help a bit,
but hard work will reward you
with more than enough.
5A good person hates deceit,
but those who are evil
cause shame and disgrace.
6Live right, and you are safe!
But sin will destroy you.
7Some who have nothing
may pretend to be rich,
and some who have everything
may pretend to be poor.
8The rich may have
to pay a ransom,
but the poor don't have
that problem.
9The lamp of a good person
keeps on shining;
the lamp of an evil person
soon goes out.
10Too much pride causes trouble.
Be sensible and take advice.
11Money wrongly gained
will disappear bit by bit;
money earned little by little
will grow and grow.
12Not getting what you want
can break your heart,
but a wish that comes true
is a life-giving tree.
13If you reject God's teaching,
you will pay the price;
if you obey his commands,
you will be rewarded.
14Sensible instruction
is a life-giving fountain
that helps you escape
all deadly traps.
15Sound judgment is praised,
but people without good sense
are on the way to disaster.
16If you have good sense,
you will act sensibly,
but fools act like fools.
17Whoever delivers your message
can make things better
or worse for you.
18All who refuse correction
will be poor and disgraced;
all who accept correction
will be praised.
19It's a good feeling
to get what you want,
but only a stupid fool
hates to turn from evil.
20 Wise friends make you wise,
but you hurt yourself
by going around with fools.
21You are in for trouble
if you sin,
but you will be rewarded
if you live right.
22If you obey God,
you will have something
to leave your grandchildren.
If you don't obey God,
those who live right
will get what you leave.
23Even when the land of the poor
produces good crops,
they get cheated
out of what they grow.
24If you love your children,
you will correct them;
if you don't love them,
you won't correct them.
25If you live right,
you will have plenty to eat;
if you don't live right,
you will go away empty.
translation_text:
1Ubi ɔni na ɔ́da anu ni, ɔɔtuna na nwuna bawɔne
baatumini-nwu kalɛ na ɔ́manku.
Na ɔnamu ɔni muuti lɛla biala taakya bɔƒia ni,
ulenu litemi.
2Bekyuli babuni baadi
kɔsia kɔni na
kɔ́lɛ kɔ́si kasusu kabuni
kani bákya bekyuli kemmo.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ni,
ama kadɔ ku unyeƒi
kani baanu ulu teete.
3Bekyuli bani ngyi kalɛ baada
bana unyemi ni,
beelie ngba gyɔlɔɔ.
Na kenye bɔtu bɔlɛ ukyuli ɔɔkana na uubile lɛla biala.
4Bakɔsɔne baawia ala pii,
nsu ɛlɛɛ muutúku-ma kɔnu.
Nsu bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla kpakplaa ni,
bana kabla kadubɔtɛ na badi bemo.
5Bekyuli babuni bekisi ɔkɔ ala.
Na balalane ama ni, kɔƒa muubo-ma lɛlɔ
na anumi eewi-ma kalɔ.
6Ngba buni bulie buubunku ukyuli
nwuna ngba emeyi kemmo ƒui.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ama ni,
bana kalala ndubɔya na bayii udu.
7Bawabane badi baabla lɛlɔ aani balakɛne.
Na babambadi bani ndi balakɛne lɛnɔ
baabla lɛlɔ aani bawabane.
8Balakɛne baakana na baƒɔ kayu biala
na beti baƒɔ bana lili ngba.
Nsu bawabane ama ni, bana lɛlɔ lilégyie anumi
na beduo ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ udu kemmo muedi.
9Bekyuli babuni ni, lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-ma
na bana keliela keekeye uwi ndi uwi.
Nsu ɔƒɛ ɔɔsá taakya alaekpidi bablane na ɔɔbla-ma suu.
10Bekyuli bani mɔɔtalaku lɛlɔ katɔ baakya unyeƒi pii.
Na bekyuli bani muunú bɔlɛ baadá anu.
11Lɛkɛ lɛni baasia ulu gontii lɛlɔ taakɛ liiibo bɔyii.
Nsu lɛla lɛni na aakɛ́ blii blii na ulu lɛlɔ lɛɛwɔ teebu.
12Si ukyuli ɔ́yila lɛnunsia ni, kayi keekpóku-nwu.
Nsu si ƒula ala ani na eegyé kɔna taanu aasia-a ni,
eenú ngba emini na lɛlɔ lɛnɔ lɛɛyɔ́-ɔ.
13Bekyuli bani muuní ka bekyuli balɛ-ma ni,
ɔgbankpi kemmo kani na badubo buduo.
Na bani mɔɔbu bekyuli bɔlɛ ni,
badubo bukpo bɔlɛ.
14Banundane bɔlɛ buse aani libiɔ lɛni mɔɔyu ntu
na baaní teelie ngba ute-ɔ.
Na ɔɔyá na ekeli liƒu lɛni na kukpi kɔɔkya-bu.
15Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla kasusu buni na ala lɛlɔ ni,
bekyuli baabu-nwu.
Na ukyuli ukpidi anwu ni, nwuna kasiakɔ
atakpɛ lɛlɔ na kaasia.
16Banundane baaka kasusu bɔbla
asa na baabla ala.
Uuuse lɛni ku badɔlɔdi, na baakun lɛmɛnɛ lɛnɔ
taasia ɔmmɔ kama.
17Ɔtalane ɔni naaagyi kalɛ beesié lɛtu ni,
uuti lɛlɔ taatákya ɔgbankpi kemmo.
Nsu ɔtalane ɔni ngyi kalɛ na baasu kenye ni,
ɔɔyá na kayi kaayɔ́ bekyuli.
18Ukyuli ɔni na alayɔ ka bedie-ɔ bɔƒiɔ ni,
kɔwaba ku kɔƒa ndubo-ɔ buƒie.
Nsu si átuna anii bédie-ɔ
bɔƒiɔ ni,
bekyuli ƒui badubo-ɔ bɔbu.
19Ebiti aada ukyuli si ƒula ayɔla ani na aawia
ébo-nwu kemmo lɛni.
Nsu badɔlɔdi belenu kalɔ teenwini bana ekpidi kama
kalɛ na ubo-nwu kemmo ute-ma lɛni.
20Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdiku banundane kɔkpana ni,
anwu lɛnɔ ɔɔdá anu.
Lɛni kani na ukyuli ɔni na badɔlɔdi
na ɔɔdiku kɔkpana ni, anwu lɛnɔ ɔɔdɔlɔ.
21Alaekpidi bablane ni, ɔgbankpi mɔɔbi taasiaku-ma.
Na kusɛ kusɛ ɔɔsia bekyuli babuni kama uwi ndi uwi.
22Bekyuli babuni ni,
ama muusé bana bebi ku bawɔ kama.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi lɛkɛ ni,
liinwíni bekyuli babuni lɛdi.
23Ina ɔwabane ɔ́kya edula pii ni,
ama bani naaabla ala ulu lɛlɔ baakana
na baƒɔ kɔsia kɔmmɔ baatɔlɔku.
24Si éni na átatumini ƒula bebi ni,
ɔɔtina ka alayɔ-ma.
Na si aayɔ́-ma bɔdi ni, ɔlɛka enye kpakplaa
na ada-ma kalɛ na ɔ́manku.
25Bekyuli babuni ni, ala ani bebo eemó-ma.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ni, bana ala elemo-ma.

english_text:
Wisdom Makes Good Sense
1A woman's family
is held together
by her wisdom,
but it can be destroyed
by her foolishness.
2By living right, you show
that you respect the Lord;
by being deceitful, you show
that you despise him.
3Proud fools are punished
for their stupid talk,
but sensible talk
can save your life.
4Without the help of an ox
there can be no crop,
but with a strong ox
a big crop is possible.
5An honest witness
tells the truth;
a dishonest witness
tells nothing but lies.
6Make fun of wisdom,
and you will never find it.
But if you have understanding,
knowledge comes easily.
7Stay away from fools,
or you won't learn a thing.
8Wise people have enough sense
to find their way,
but stupid fools get lost.
9Fools don't care
if they are wrong,
but God is pleased
when people do right.
10No one else can really know
how sad or happy you are.
11The tent of a good person
stands longer than the house
of someone evil.
12 You may think you are
on the right road
and still end up dead.
13Sorrow may hide
behind laughter,
and happiness may end
in sorrow.
14You harvest what you plant,
whether good or bad.
15Don't be stupid
and believe all you hear;
be smart and know
where you are headed.
16Only a stupid fool
is never cautious—
so be extra careful
and stay out of trouble.
17Fools have quick tempers,
and no one likes you
if you can't be trusted.
18Stupidity leads to foolishness;
be smart and learn.
19The wicked will come crawling
to those who obey God.
20You have no friends
if you are poor,
but you have lots of friends
if you are rich.
21It's wrong to hate others,
but God blesses everyone
who is kind to the poor.
22It's a mistake
to make evil plans,
but you will have loyal friends
if you want to do right.
23Hard work is worthwhile,
but empty talk
will make you poor.
24Wisdom can make you rich,
but foolishness leads
to more foolishness.
25An honest witness
can save your life,
but liars can't be trusted.
26If you respect the Lord,
you and your children
have a strong fortress
27and a life-giving fountain
that keeps you safe
from deadly traps.
28Rulers of powerful nations
are held in honor;
rulers of weak nations
are nothing at all.
29It's smart to be patient,
but it's stupid
to lose your temper.
30It's healthy to be content,
but envy can eat you up.
31If you mistreat the poor,
you insult your Creator;
if you are kind to them,
you show him respect.
32In times of trouble
the wicked are destroyed,
but even at death
the innocent have faith.
33Wisdom is found in the minds
of people with good sense,
but fools don't know it.
34Doing right brings honor
to a nation,
but sin brings disgrace.
35Kings reward servants
who act wisely,
but they punish those
who act foolishly.
translation_text:
1Uleku ɔnundane ɔgyi kalɛ na baada ɔtɔ na uunye.
Nsu uleku ɔdɔlɔdi anwu ɔlati mɔɔbwɛ nwuna ɔtɔ.
2Bekyuli bani mɔɔsia ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ ni, baayia Unwoti.
Na bani mɔɔsia ulu ukpidi lɛlɔ beení Unwoti.
3Badɔlɔdi enyekpi muunwíni kugyiimi
kɔni mɔɔsia-ma kama.
Nsu banundane ala ani na
baasu ni,
eedie-ma na ɔgbankpi kemmo.
4Bebuo lɛyu lɛni kemmo na ebuo ɔdi uuubo ni, liisé sɛɛn.
Nsu kɔsia kɔdi kulasi lɛyu likpludi lɛmmɔ kemmo.
5Ukyuli ɔni nánu lɛla lɛdi na uudie litemi geen
lɛmmɔ kenye ni, ulanyi ɔkɔ.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni na útanu lɛla lɛmmɔ ɔɔnyi ɔkɔ.
6Ukyuli ɔni na uuti lɛla biala taakya bɔƒia ni,
si ina ɔɔwia lɛnunda muedi ulákɛ-ni.
Nsu bekyuli bani muunú ala kalɔ ni, baatí lɛla.
7Da lɛlɔ mami badɔlɔdi lɛlɔ,
ɔsika aaadubo lɛla lɛdi bɔti bana kudɔ.
8Banundane ni, baanu uwi ɔni ntɔ anumi ɔdubo ƒui
taati lɛla lɛni ndubo libalɛ.
Nsu badɔlɔdi ama bana lɛlɔ kani na baatɔ́lɔ.
9Badɔlɔdi beeti bana bɔƒiɔ taabla lɛmala.
Nsu bekyuli babuni baanu bana bɔƒiɔ taati
na beevele ka basɔ babla unwi ku ukyuli ɔni na báƒiɔ.
10Ukyuli biala ku kalɛ na lɛla lɛdi liikpóku-nwu kayi.
Na ukyuli uláti kalɛ geen na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ukyuli bamba
na nwuna kayi kemmo.
11Balalane kaduli kadubo bɔbwɛ.
Nsu ukyuli ɔbuni kevo kadubɔlɛ lili na bemomo.
12Ukyuli biala ɔɔnu kasiakɔ kadi na nwuna
ngba kemmo ka nka kadia,
nsu nwuna kawɔlɔkɔ ni, kekpine kani na ɔɔdá taalɛ.
13Lɛma lɛɛyá na ɔɔbla aani si lɛla lɛni
muukpóku ukyuli lɛ́sa.
Nsu si lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛ́vi ni,
lɛla lɛni muukpóku ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛ́sɔ línwini keku.
14Bekyuli bani muunwíni ulu ɔbuni ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni,
baakɛ́ bana lɛyuƒɔla.
Na bekyuli babuni baakɛ bana lɛbuni kɔsia.
15Bekyuli bani kasusu násɔ ni,
ama mɔɔƒɔ́ lɛla biala taadi.
Nsu bani mɔɔsia lɛlɔ anu
kaduɛ ni,
baabu lɛla biala lɛlɔ taanu asa na beedie ɔgba.
16Banundane baatí lɛlɔ kalɛ
na beekeli ɔgbankpi.
Badɔlɔdi ama baatu lili taakya lɛla biala kemmo
ku kayi kekpidi.
17Bekyuli bani muuti kɔnyi
pla pla ni,
baabla adɔlɔla.
Na bekyuli bani mɔɔbɛ́ taabla ala kalɔ kalɔ ni,
bekyuli beekisi-ma.
18Bekyuli bani kasusu násɔ ni, utulo ka kɔdɔlɔ awu bakya.
Na banundane ni, lɛlati línwini aani kagabwa kebi-ma lili.
19Bekyuli bekpidi badubɔkya
lili kalɔ
bete bekyuli bani mɔɔbla ala
ulu lɛlɔ.
Na balalane badubɔkya lili kalɔ
bete bekyuli babuni na bana ɔba kenye.
20Bawabane ni, ama alati
bana bekyuli muedi
balánu-ma taakya lɛla
lɛdi akɔ.
Nsu balakɛne ama ni, balakana-ma bakpana bɔka.
21Si eekisi ƒula ɔkpana ni,
likpidi lɛdi-ɔ.
Kusɛ kusɛ ɔdubɔsiaku bekyuli
bani muubunku bawabane.
22Si aawia ukyuli likpidi ni,
adubo bɔyii.
Nsu si lɛbuni na aawia
ukyuli ni,
Unwoti ɔdubɔyɔ-ɔ uwi ndi uwi
na ɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ ute-ɔ.
23Kabla keeboku kɔsia.
Nsu atɛ keeke adanku kɔwaba.
24Lɛlakɛ lɛdi kagabwa kete banundane.
Na badɔlɔdi kogyoklo ƒui ni, adɔlɔla ebi na aanwu.
25Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnu litemi geen teedie-ni kenye
ɔɔƒɔ́ bekyuli ngba.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ teedie litemi kenye ni,
uudie bekyuli teete.
26Lɛla lɛdi lilekpoku bekyuli bani mɔɔyia Unwoti.
Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdi katamikukɔ ute bana bebi.
27Si aayia Unwoti ni, ɔdi libiɔ lɛni mɔɔyu ntu
baaní teelie ngba ute-ɔ.
Na ɔɔyá na ekeli liƒu lɛni na kukpi kɔɔkya-bu.
28Si kadi kadi bekyuli beemomo ni,
lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ɔga ɔmmɔ.
Nsu si baasá ni, baayii udu.
29Bekyuli bani mɔɔkana bana kɔnyi bɔbala ni,
bebo lɛlati.
Na bani muuti kɔnyi pla pla ni, badubo bɔƒiɔ.
30Si áda kayi áva kalɔ buɛɛ ni, ngba buune-ɔ.
Nsu kogyulo lɛnungyie lɛɛdú ukyuli.
31Bekyuli bani muukpóku bawabane ni,
beedumi Unwoti.
Nsu bani muubunku-ma ni, baabu Unwoti.
32Bekyuli bekpidi ni, bana alaekpidi mɔɔyila-ma udu.
Nsu bekyuli babuni bebo katamikukɔ si békpi.
33Ukyuli ɔni muunú ala kalɔ ni, ubo lɛnunda
na lɛ́ƒɔ-nwu kuye geen na nwuna kayi kemmo.
Nsu badɔlɔdi balánu lɛnunda kɔsia.
34Kadi bani mɔɔyia Unwoti ni, baalɛ́ lili ku ɔyikun.
Nsu likpidi lɛdi kɔƒa ala ute kadi biala.
35Lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ɔga na kabla bablane bani ngyi bana kabla
na baabla-ka ulu lɛlɔ lɛlɔ.
Na bani na lɛsɛ kani na baakya
na balásia kabla anu ni, ɔɔkɛ́ku-ma kɔnyi.

english_text:
The Lord Sees Everything
1A kind answer
soothes angry feelings,
but harsh words
stir them up.
2Words of wisdom
come from the wise,
but fools speak foolishness.
3The Lord sees everything,
whether good or bad.
4Kind words are good medicine,
but deceitful words
can really hurt.
5Don't be a fool
and disobey your parents.
Be smart! Accept correction.
6Good people become wealthy,
but those who are evil
will lose what they have.
7Words of wisdom
make good sense;
the thoughts of a fool
make no sense at all.
8The Lord is disgusted
by gifts from the wicked,
but it makes him happy
when his people pray.
9The Lord is disgusted
with all who do wrong,
but he loves everyone
who does right.
10If you turn from the right way,
you will be punished;
if you refuse correction,
you will die.
11If the Lord can see everything
in the world of the dead,
he can see in our hearts.
12Those who sneer at others
don't like to be corrected,
and they won't ask help
from someone with sense.
13Happiness makes you smile;
sorrow can crush you.
14Anyone with good sense
is eager to learn more,
but fools are hungry
for foolishness.
15The poor have a hard life,
but being content is as good
as an endless feast.
16It's better to obey the Lord
and have only a little,
than to be very rich
and terribly anxious.
17A simple meal with love
is better than a feast
where there is hatred.
18Losing your temper
causes a lot of trouble,
but staying calm
settles arguments.
19A lazy person refuses
to clear a thorny path,
but everyone who does right
walks on a smooth road.
20Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
despise them.
21Stupidity brings happiness
