to senseless fools,
but everyone with good sense
follows the straight path.
22Without good advice
everything goes wrong—
it takes careful planning
for things to go right.
23Giving the right answer
at the right time
makes everyone happy.
24All who are wise follow a road
that leads upward to life
and away from death.
25The Lord destroys the homes
of those who are proud,
but he protects the property
of widows.
26The Lord hates evil thoughts,
but kind words please him.
27Being greedy causes trouble
for your family,
but you protect yourself
by refusing bribes.
28Good people think
before they answer,
but the wicked speak evil
without ever thinking.
29The Lord never even hears
the prayers of the wicked,
but he answers the prayers
of all who obey him.
30A friendly smile
makes you happy,
and good news
makes you feel strong.
31Healthy correction is good,
and if you accept it,
you will be wise.
32You hurt only yourself
by rejecting instruction,
but it makes good sense
to accept it.
33Showing respect to the Lord
will make you wise,
and being humble
will bring honor to you.
translation_text:
1Kɔnyi kulakɔ ukyuli
si éboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na édie
litemi kenye buɛɛ.
Nsu etemila bɔtu taalɛ ukyuli ɔɔyá kɔnyi kuubo.
2Ɔnundane ni, ala bɔtɛya bɔdi-nwu ebiti.
Na badɔlɔdi ni, bágyu kenye beti beedie kɔdɔlɔ keyi.
3Unwoti ɔɔnu kesi kesii,
na nwuna lɛnumi lɛsia bekyuli bekpidi ku babuni lɛlɔ.
4Etemila ani mɔɔyu buɛɛ aayá na ukyuli
uulie ngba na ɔɔkɛ́ ɔyikun.
Na unyemi ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ ɔɔdú ukyuli kɔyu.
5Ɔdɔlɔdi kani muuní ka nwuna bawɔne batumini-nwu.
Ukyuli biala ɔni matɛya lɛla
lɛdi wasiku bɔƒiɔ
bɔni bédie-nwu lɛlɔ ni,
ɔ́da anu.
6Lɛlakɛ lɛbuni liisé bekyuli babuni kesii.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ala ani na baakɛ́ adanku ɔgbankpi.
7Banundane kani mɔɔkana na baakya ukyuli kasusu buni.
Na badɔlɔdi balakana ɔmɛni bɔbla.
8Bekyuli bekpidi akpala ni, Unwoti ukisi-nya.
Nsu lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-nwu si bekyuli bani nse siin baakpali-nwu.
9Bekyuli bekpidi kɔsiakɔ ƒui kulayɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ.
Nsu bekyuli bani mɔɔwia kpakplaa
ka belie ngba bɔbuni ni, Unwoti ɔɔyɔ́-ma.
10Ukyuli biala na únwini kama ɔ́kya ulu geen ɔmmɔ ni,
Unwoti ɔdubɔni-nwu kɔtu kpakplaa.
Na ukyuli ɔni nkisi ka bedie-nwu bɔƒiɔ ni,
ɔdubo bukpi.
11Unwoti ɔgyi kukpi kalɔ
ku kalɛ na ukyuli ɔɔkywí taayii udu.
Anwuɔsu ukyuli kayi kemmo lɛla lɛdi lilábɛ-nwu!
12Bekyuli bani muuti lɛla biala taabla lɛmala ni,
balayɔ bekyuli bani mɔɔdɔnku-ma.
Anwuɔsu na balani teede banundane.
13Kayi kani kemmo na lɛlɔyɔ lɛkya ni,
kana anumi muukeye ku lɛma.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni náyila
lɛnunsia ni,
enu aaƒɛ-nwu.
14Ɔnundane ni, litemi geen kama bɔsia kɔka mɔɔda-nwu.
Na ɔdɔlɔdi ni, ala ani neeebo kɔsia lɛlɔ na ɔɔkɛ́ ebiti.
15Ɔwabane ni, limeyi biala ala eekpóku-nwu.
Nsu bani na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ni,
ngba bumodi bɔdi limeyi bɔdi bute-ma.
16Ɔdia si aayia Unwoti ina eeebo ala pii utulo
si ebo lɛlakɛ na bɔnwuna buuubo-ɔ kaduli.
17Si awɔ ku ƒula ɔkpana ɔdi bɛ́sa
na kutukplu lɛkyami kalɔ ni,
ɔdia utulo si awɔ ku ƒula ukisine bɛ́sa na ɔkyimu kalɔ.
18Ukyuli ɔni na uuubo kayi buɛɛ ɔɔkya kekpo.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́da kayi ɔ́va kalɔ buɛɛ ni,
ɔɔyala kekpo kammɔ.
19Ɔkɔsɔne ni, ala aláda-nwu bukpoku taaya
nwuna ngba kemmo ƒui.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔsia nwuna kabla anu ni,
nwuna keyi kaabla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.
20Bebi bani kasusu nse nwaa baayá lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ bana ɔti.
Na bebi badɔlɔdi muuní bana uni.
21Badɔlɔdi ni, ama na kubiti kɔɔda si baanu adɔlɔla.
Na ɔnundane ɔɔsia ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ uwi ndi uwi.
22Ukyuli kabla kɔkwɛ kɔni na ɔɔkya kuubie-nwu
si ulaƒɔ kasusu na bekyuli kudɔ.
Nsu si eeye bekyuli pii kasusu ni, ƒula ala aatɛ.
23Lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ukyuli ɔni muudie lɛla lɛdi kenye
teete ɔnwani ulu lɛlɔ nwaa.
Ɔdi lɛla lɛni mɔɔyu kayi si ásu lɛla lɛdi
na uwi ɔni na basu-ni lɛlɔ.
24Ɔnundane kasiakɔ kási mɛni késela
ngba ƒui kemmo na katɔ,
ɔsika kaƒiɔtɔ kelénwini-ma keliekɔ uwi ƒui.
25Bekyuli bani mɔɔkɔli lɛlɔ katɔ ni,
Unwoti ɔɔbwɛ-ma kɔduli na baayii udu.
Nsu ɔɔgyumana bekpinele ala ani na bebo.
26Unwoti ulayɔ bekyuli bekpidi kasusu kani beeti.
Nsu lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-nwu si bekyuli baatɛmi etemila
ani mɔɔdia bunu.
27Lɛlakɛ lɛni naaakɛ ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ líduo lɛkɔkɔ ni,
Unwoti ɔɔyá na lɛbibo liiduo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo.
Nsu ama bani naaabɛ taaƒɔ ala bekyuli kudɔ taadi ni,
ama ndubulie ku keyi buɛɛ.
28Bekyuli babuni baaka kasusu buti
asa na baasu lɛla lɛdi.
Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ama bɔtu kani
na baatu etemila teebewi.
29Unwoti ɔ́gyunku bekyuli bekpidi kudɔ ƒui.
Nsu uunú bekyuli babuni kenye si baakpali-nwu.
30Si áƒɛnimi anumi ákya ukyuli ni, kayi kaayɔ́-nwu.
Na si énu kenye buni ni, ɔɔkya ɔlɔna ɔkplu.
31Si ukyuli údie-ɔ bɔƒiɔ
na ɔ́tina-a kasiakɔ ni,
adubɔkɛ kelie na
banundane akɔ.
32Si éni anii ukyuli utedie-ɔ
bɔƒiɔ ni,
awɔ ɔlati lɛlɔ na aabla kalala.
Nsu si áda lɛlɔ na bédie
ƒula bɔƒiɔ bátina-a ni,
adubɔkɛ lɛlati na eteenu
ala kalɔ.
33Si aayia Unwoti ni, ɔɔtina kalɛ na áda anu.
Na lɛlɔ kalɔ buboku mɔɔtɔ asa na ɔbu ɔɔsia.

english_text:
The Lord Has the Final Word
1We humans make plans,
but the Lord
has the final word.
2We may think we know
what is right,
but the Lord is the judge
of our motives.
3Share your plans with the Lord,
and you will succeed.
4The Lord has a reason
for everything he does,
and he lets evil people live
only to be punished.
5The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is conceited—
you can be sure
they will be punished.
6 If we truly love God,
our sins will be forgiven;
if we show him respect,
we will keep away from sin.
7When we please the Lord,
even our enemies
make friends with us.
8 It's better to be honest
and poor
than to be dishonest
and rich.
9We make our own plans,
but the Lord decides
where we will go.
10Rulers speak with authority
and are never wrong.
11The Lord watches to see
if we are fair
or if we cheat others.
12Justice makes rulers powerful.
They should hate evil
13and like honesty and truth.
14An angry ruler
can put you to death.
So be wise!
Don't make one angry.
15When a ruler is happy
and pleased with you,
it's like refreshing rain,
and you will live.
16It's much better to be wise
and sensible
than to be rich.
17God's people avoid evil ways,
and they protect themselves
by watching where they go.
18Too much pride
will destroy you.
19You are better off
to be humble and poor
than to get rich
from what you take by force.
20If you know what you're doing,
you will prosper.
God blesses everyone
who trusts him.
21Good judgment proves
that you are wise,
and if you speak kindly,
you can teach others.
22Good sense is a fountain
that gives life,
but fools are punished
by their foolishness.
23You can persuade others
if you are wise
and speak sensibly.
24Kind words are like honey—
they cheer you up
and make you feel strong.
25 Sometimes what seems right
is really a road to death.
26The hungrier you are,
the harder you work.
27Worthless people plan trouble.
Even their words burn
like a flaming fire.
28 Gossip is no good!
It causes hard feelings
and comes between friends.
29Don't trust violent people.
They will mislead you
to do the wrong thing.
30When someone winks
or grins behind your back,
trouble is on the way.
31Gray hair is a glorious crown
worn by those
who have lived right.
32Controlling your temper
is better than being a hero
who captures a city.
33We make our own decisions,
but the Lord alone
determines what happens.
translation_text:
1Bɔɔkana bɔɔsála kasusu lidu lidu,
nsu Unwoti mɔɔtina lɛla lɛni geen
ndi litemi geen lɛmmɔ.
2Bekyuli baanu ka bana ablala akɛ ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ.
Nsu Unwoti mɔɔkɔ́ku lɛla biala taanu kalɛ na lɛdia.
3Ti ƒula kabla biala kya Unwoti kɔnu
na kadubɔtɛ-ɔ.
4Unwoti nábla lɛla biala ɔkɛnku nwuna kasusu
kani kenye na ɔɔwia lɛla lɛmmɔ.
Na bekyuli bekpidi muedi benye bete
ka bani-ma kɔtu.
5Unwoti ukisi ka ukyuli ɔtalaku lɛlɔ katɔ.
Anwuɔsu ɔbla ukyuli biala nwaa
ka bani mɔɔtalaku lɛlɔ katɔ ni,
Unwoti ɔdubɔni-ma kɔtu.
6Bɔyɔ bɔni neeebo kawɔkɔ ku litemi lɛlɔ bɔdi
uwi ndi uwi uuti ala teebi likpidi.
Na si aayia Unwoti ni, eekeli likpidi.
7Si bekyuli ablala aayɔ́ Unwoti kaƒɔ ni,
ɔɔyá na ama ku bana bekisine muedi beelie
na atu bɔyɔ kemmo.
8Si adi ɔwabane na aabu
Unwoti ni,
ɔdia utulo si ebo lɛlakɛ
na aládi litemi geen
lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.
9Bɔɔkana na bɔɔbla kasusu ku kɔkwɛ na lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ,
nsu Unwoti mɔɔtina bula kasiakɔ.
10Ɔga ɔɔtɛmi lɛnunda etemila ku Unwoti ɔyikun,
na utalɛka ɔnu anumi ɔtɛ litemi.
11Unwoti ɔɔwia ka bɔbla lɛla biala siin
na liyedi kemmo,
na ɔ́tina ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na ɔlɛka bɔsia lɛnɔ úse.
12Ɔga ɔdi ulayɔ likyulikpi ala bɔbla,
ɔsika litemi geen lɛlɔ bɔdi lɛlɔ na ɔɔsia taadi bekyuli lɛlɔ.
13Bekyuli bani enyekuli mɔɔtɛmi ala
ani nse siin mɔɔyɔ́ ɔga kaƒɔ.
Na ɔɔyɔ́ bani mɔɔsu litemi geen lɛni nkɛ ulu lɛlɔ mmɔ.
14Ɔga kɔnyi kenye kelenu bunye kuubile ala.
Na banundane baasia ulu biala lɛlɔ ka
bayala-nwu kaƒɔ.
15Si ɔga ɔɔmɔsi ni, agyi anii bibo ngba,
na nwuna lɛƒɔndia lise aani ɔnantu
ɔni mɔɔna na lɛla biala lɛɛsɔ taabla ɔwɔdi.
16Ɔdia geen si ukyuli ebo lɛnunda utulo ka akɛ sika ugyiedi.
Na si ebo lɛlati lɛni mɔɔyá na ukyuli uunú ala kalɔ ni,
ɔdia utulo sika ɔƒualadi.
17Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔsia nwuna ablala anu kaduɛ ni,
nwuna ulu ulásia likpidi kavinkɔ.
Na ukyuli biala nda nwuna ngba lɛni ni, ubo bɔƒɔ.
18Lɛlɔ katɔ bɔtalaku mɔɔgyú taatɔ
asa na ukyuli ɔɔyii udu.
Na kayi kekpidi buse taabla ala mɔɔyá na ukyuli uubuli.
19Ɔdia si awɔ ku bawabane bilie na bɛɛdi lɛla lɛni na bɛ́kɛ
utulo si awɔ ku belikplune bilie
na bɛɛdi ala ani na béƒie báƒɔ bekyuli kudɔ.
20Bekyuli bani muunú bɔlɛ ni, ala adubɔtɛku-ma.
Na bekyuli bani na bana anu asia Unwoti lɛlɔ ni,
lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ-ma.
21Banundane ni, baanu-ma taati ɔkɛnku
kalɛ na beenú ala kalɔ kenye.
Si ásia ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ átina ukyuli ala ni,
anwu mɔɔyá na ɔɔƒɔ́-ɔ litemi ku ebiti.
22Lɛla bɔti bɔbla ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ ni,
ɔdi libiɔ ute bekyuli bani mɔɔbla lɛni
na baaní ntu bɔmmɔ teelie ngba.
Nsu si átina badɔlɔdi ulu
ɔmmɔ ni,
keeke na eebó abi, ɔsika balakpete-ɔ.
23Ɔnundane ni, lɛnunda etemila na ɔɔtɛmi.
Na nwuna etemila aatu ukyuli teenwini.
24Etemila ani mɔɔyu kayi ni, ese aani uwɔ.
Aayu kɔyu emini na ɔlɔna ɔɔkɛ́ ɔlɔkplu.
25Ukyuli biala ɔɔnu kasiakɔ kadi
na nwuna ngba kemmo ka nka kadia.
Nsu ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ ni,
kekpine kani na ɔɔdá taalɛ.
26Útebie si adila adi ɔkwɛ ɔɔda kabla ɔblane.
Kaƒɔkplu kaayá na ukyuli ɔɔbla kabla
kpakplaa na ɔkɛ ɔdi.
27Balalane beenye taawia kuƒi kɔni na babla likyulikpi,
na bana etemila adi ogya bonwu
ɔni mɔɔkywí teebile ala.
28Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia ka bekyuli beteekpoku lɛlɔ ni,
lɛsɛ ogya na ɔɔkya bekyuli akɔ.
Na bekyuli anyikpi bɔlɔ ni,
uugyingya bakpana babuni muedi ntɛ.
29Likyulikpi ala bablane baatɔ́lɔ bana bakpana
na baasia ulu ukpidi lɛlɔ teetéduo ɔgbankpi kemmo.
30Bébile anumi, nsu baanu taavi ukyuli kalɔ.
Belébimi kenye taatɛmi,
nsu baabla bana likyulikpi kɔkwɛ.
31Liliƒuala lɛdi kagabwa kani muukeye.
Na Unwoti uuti-ka teete bekyuli bani muulie ngba buni.
32Kayi buɛɛ kadia ketulo kenyekɔ ɔyikun.
Si aakana ƒula lɛlɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi ni,
ɔdia utulo si ékpo ádi ɔma unengudi ɔdi lɛlɔ.
33Adubɔkana na ebo egulabi akɔliku katɔ,
nsu Unwoti mɔɔtina ɔƒɛnyi ɔni lɛlɔ na ɔdubo bɔyu.

english_text:
Our Thoughts Are Tested by the Lord
1A dry crust of bread eaten
in peace and quiet
is better than a feast eaten
where everyone argues.
2A wise slave
will be placed in charge
of a no-good child,
and that slave will be given
the same inheritance
that each child receives.
3Silver and gold are tested
by flames of fire;
our thoughts are tested
by the Lord.
4Troublemakers listen
to troublemakers,
and liars listen to liars.
5By insulting the poor,
you insult your Creator.
You will be punished
if you make fun
of someone in trouble.
6Grandparents are proud
of their grandchildren,
and children should be proud
of their parents.
7It sounds strange for a fool
to talk sensibly,
but it's even worse
for a ruler to tell lies.
8A bribe works miracles
like a magic charm
that brings good luck.
9You will keep your friends
if you forgive them,
but you will lose your friends
if you keep talking about
what they did wrong.
10A sensible person
accepts correction,
but you can't beat sense
into a fool.
11Cruel people want to rebel,
and so vicious attackers
will be sent against them.
12A bear robbed of her cubs
is far less dangerous
than a stubborn fool.
13You will always have trouble
if you are mean to those
who are good to you.
14The start of an argument
is like a water leak—
so stop it before
real trouble breaks out.
15The Lord doesn't like those
who defend the guilty
or condemn the innocent.
16Why should fools have money
for an education
when they refuse to learn?
17 A friend is there to help,
in any situation,
and relatives are born
to share our troubles.
18It's stupid to guarantee
someone else's loan.
19The wicked and the proud
love trouble and keep begging
to be hurt.
20Dishonesty does you no good,
and telling lies
will get you in trouble.
21It's never pleasant
to be the parent of a fool
and have nothing but pain.
22If you are cheerful,
you feel good;
if you are sad,
you hurt all over.
23Crooks accept secret bribes
to keep justice
from being done.
24Anyone with wisdom knows
what makes good sense,
but fools can never
make up their minds.
25Foolish children bring sorrow
and pain to their parents.
26It isn't fair
to punish the innocent
and those who do right.
27It makes a lot of sense
to be a person of few words
and to stay calm.
28 Even fools seem smart
when they are quiet.
translation_text:
1Si ákɛ lɛla lɛni uwi utu-ni lɛlɔ ádi ku kayi ƒaa ni,
ɔdia utulo si ésie kadikɔ bonwu ku ala lidu lidu
na kadɔ kakya mmɔ.
2Kabla ɔblane ɔni na ɔ́da anu ni,
ɔɔdi ɔtɔlati bebi bani mɔɔbla kɔƒa ala lɛlɔ,
na anwu ku bebi bammɔ muule bana ɔti ala.
3Ogya kemmo baakya sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi taanu-nwu bɔdia.
Nsu Unwoti ni, ukyuli kayi na ɔɔkɔ́ku taanu-nwu bɔdia.
4Alaekpidi bablane ni, likyulikpi atɛ na beesé atu teenu.
Na ɔkɔ banyine ni, beesé atu teenu atɛ ani muubile ala.
5Bekyuli bani muudumi bawabane taama ni,
bana Unwoti ɔni nédie-ma na beedumi.
Na bani mɔɔmá bekyuli na bana ɔgbankpi kemmo ni,
Unwoti ɔdubo-ma kɔtu bɔni.
6Bawɔ bani na ukyuli ɔ́bi lɛlɔ ɔ́ƒɔ ni,
ama ndi-nwu kagabwa kani muukeye.
Na bebi bani mbo bawɔne babune ni,
kɔƒa kulekpo-ma na bekyuli akɔ.
7Kɔtɛ bɔtɛmi pii ni, útamanku ɔdɔlɔdi.
Na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdi bekyuli lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ni,
ɔkɔ bɔnyi bútamanku-nwu.
8Ala ani beete ukyuli na bɔbɛ kemmo ni,
etulo kuvo ete bani mɔɔbla udu ɔmmɔ.
Baasia ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ala aatɛ teete-ma.
9Si alásia ukyuli bamba alaekpidi anu ni, bɔyɔ buláyii udu.
Na si aaká ukyuli bamba ekpidi taasu bekyuli ni, eegyingya bakpana babuni muedi ntɛ.
10Si ádɔnku ukyuli ɔni muunú ala kalɔ kunwi pɛ ni,
uubunku-nwu teetulo si ébo ɔdɔlɔdi kugyiimi eti anyɔ.
11Bekyuli bekpidi baawia bata benye lɛlɔ badine lɛlɔ,
nsu badubo-ma kɔtu bɔni geen.
12Si awɔ ku ebuo ukpidi ɔni na lɛla lɛdi líƒie-nwu bebi bɛ́sa ni,
ebo bɔƒɔ utulo ka enwini ɔdɔlɔdi kasusu na nwuna kɔdɔlɔ ulu lɛlɔ.
13Si éti likpidi áƒɔ lɛbuni lɛni na ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́bla-a kayu ni,
ɔgbankpi ulása-a kaduli kudii.
14Si ése kadɔ kalɔ ni, use aani kalɛ na baalɛmi kuƒi teete ketu
kani báda-ka kavinkɔ ulu na kéyi.
15Unwoti ulayɔ bekyuli bani mɔɔyá na
baanyonu bekyuli bani litemi neeebo ubo
na baadú bekyuli babuni kɔtɔ.
16Si ɔdɔlɔdi ulásia lɛnunda ulu ni,
ɔɔɔdi kasusu buni ka ebile egulabi anii ɔtɛya lɛla lɛdi.
17Ɔkpana buni ɔɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ uwi ndi uwi.
Na ukyuli ɔnwani ni, bɔwɔ na báwɔ-nwu ka
ute kebunku uwi ɔni na ɔnwani ɔɔwia lɛla lɛdi.
18Si átákya kɔnu ɔku kemmo éte ƒula ɔkpana anii
eenye-nwu kayu kenye ni,
kasusu kammɔ kétedu-ɔ.
19Ukyuli biala mɔɔyɔ́ kadɔ ni, ɔɔyɔ́ likpidi.
Na ukyuli biala mɔɔtɛmi taakun lɛmɛnɛ ni,
ɔgbankpi na ɔɔwia.
20Kayi kani naaasia ulu unwi lɛlɔ ni, ala alátɛku-nwu.
Na unyemi ɔni mɔɔtu ala teenwini ni,
ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔɔbla gyoli gyoli teetéduo lɛbibo kemmo.
21Si áwɔ ɔdɔlɔdi ni, ɔdi lɛla lɛni muukpóku ukyuli.
Na lɛlɔ lilayɔ ubi ɔti ɔni ubi mɔɔta teenye bekyuli lɛlɔ.
22Ebiti bɔkɛ na kayi kemmo ɔdi kuvo ute ukyuli ɔmmɔ.
Nsu kɔyu kɔni nsɔ neeebo lɛnunsia
ɔɔyá na ɔyikun ɔɔsá ukyuli ɔmmɔ.
23Bekyuli bekpidi baabɛ́ taaƒɔ ala bekyuli kudɔ
kalɛ na batu litemi benwini.
24Bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kasusu buni ni,
bana anu aasia lɛnunda lɛlɔ uwi ndi uwi.
Nsu badɔlɔdi ni, bana kasusu kelélie liku linwi,
mmomu kakɛ ala ƒui lɛlɔ ɔɔwia lɛla lɛni na ɔɔɔdubo bɔkɛ.
25Ubi ɔdɔlɔdi ni, ɔɔyá na ɔti uunú ɔlɛ na kayi kemmo.
Na ngba bɔɔyu uni ɔdu.
26Ɔɔɔdia munu munu ka ebo ukyuli ɔbuni kayu
ka ɔsiaku lɛbuni ɔsu,
iye ani ɔyikune kɔtu ka ɔ́di nwuna litemi lɛlɔ geen ɔsu!
27Ukyuli ɔni náda anu geen ni, ɔɔkɔ́si bɔtɛmi.
Na ukyuli ɔni mbo lɛlati na uunú ala kalɔ ni,
nwuna kɔnyi kuse buɛɛ.
28Badɔlɔdi muedi baatina-ma kalɛ na bada anu si bába lɛsɛ.
Na si báda bana inye ni, baatina aani si bebo kasusu.

english_text:
It's Wrong To Favor the Guilty
1It's selfish and stupid
to think only of yourself
and to sneer at people
who have sense.
2Fools have no desire to learn,
instead they would rather
give their own opinion.
3Wrongdoing leads to shame
and disgrace.
4Words of wisdom
are a stream that flows
from a deep fountain.
5It's wrong to favor the guilty
and keep the innocent
from getting justice.
6Foolish talk will get you
into a lot of trouble.
7Saying foolish things
is like setting a trap
to destroy yourself.
8There's nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
9Being lazy is no different
from being a troublemaker.
10The Lord is a mighty tower
where his people can run
for safety—
11the rich think their money
is a wall of protection.
12Pride leads to destruction;
humility leads to honor.
13 It's stupid and embarrassing
to give an answer
before you listen.
14Being cheerful helps
when you are sick,
but nothing helps
when you give up.
15Everyone with good sense
wants to learn.
16A gift will get you in
to see anyone.
17You may think you have won
your case in court,
until your opponent speaks.
18Drawing straws is one way
to settle a difficult case.
19Making up with a friend
you have offended
is harder than breaking
through a city wall.
20Make your words good—
you will be glad you did.
21Words can bring death or life!
Talk too much, and you will eat
everything you say.
22 A man's greatest treasure
is his wife—
she is a gift from the Lord.
23The poor must beg for help,
but the rich can give
a harsh reply.
24Some friends don't help,
but a true friend is closer
than your own family.
translation_text:
1Ukyuli ɔni muudie lɛlɔ
lɛti ni,
nwuna lɛla biala lɛ́ƒɔ-nwu anu.
Na ngba ulu buni bamba biala kasusu na baakya-nwu ni,
ulátunaku-mu munu munu!
2Ala kalɔ bunu ogya ɔdi ulákya badɔlɔdi kudi kudii!
Ama bana kasusu kani na beebó kudu.
3Kesii kani na bekyuli bekpidi báda bálɛ ni,
ukyuli tabu ku kɔƒa ala ku anumi kalɔ buwi ala kani
mɔɔsia-ma kama.
4Ukyuli etemila akana na enwini ntu bɔnidi
bɔni nete ukyuli ngba.
Na lɛnunda etemila aayu kayi buɛɛ
aani libiɔ ntu bamamba bɔni mɔɔyu.
5Ɔɔɔdia ka litemi ɔtɛne unye ukyuli
ɔni na nwuna litemi liiibo ubo kama
iye ɔdu ukyuli ɔbuni kɔtɔ.
6Badɔlɔdi beeebo kadɔ bɔdɔ,
na bana kama ku ugyii.
7Badɔlɔdi kenye muubó-ma kalɔ,
na bana enyekpi mɔɔkya-ma lɛbibo kemmo.
8Ɔkɔ etemila ani nse aani lɛna wɛlɛ wɛlɛ ebo emini
na anya mɔɔyu teduo ukyuli kayi kemmo.
9Ɔkɔsɔne ɔdi ukyuli ukpidi
aani ukyuli ɔni muubile bekyuli ala.
10Unwoti lɛnyi lɛdi lɛtakpɛ bonwu
lɛni na ukyuli ukpo kama.
Na nwuna kudɔ na bekyuli babuni beekeli
teesie na baakɛ́ bɔƒɔ.
11Balakɛne baanu bana lɛlakɛ aani kɔbi bonwu
kɔni na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana bɔƒuaala.
Baanu-ni aani kowodu kangyaa kɔni na kɔ́da ama
ku bekyuli ntɛ na balakana-ma.
12Lɛlɔ bɔtina ku ukyuli tabu mɔɔgyú taatɔ
asa na ukyuli ɔɔyii udu.
Na lɛlɔ kalɔ buboku mɔɔtɔ asa na ɔbu ɔɔsia.
13Baláka ukyuli bɔlɛ asa na enu lɛla lɛni nébo,
amu kɔƒa kɔdubo-ɔ bukpo na abla lɛlɔ ɔdɔlɔdi.
14Ukyuli kɔyu kɔɔkya ɔlɔna ɔni muuƒi kemmo.
Nsu ni, ɔma na si nwuna kɔyu kɔ́yii udu
na nwuna ɔlɔna ɔdubɔkana bunye?
15Banundane baawia kpakplaa ka baƒɔ bekyuli bamba kasusu.
Na sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka baawia ka bekyuli bete-ma kasusu.
16Ukyuli ala bute bɔdanku ala enengudi.
Ɔkana na uti-ɔ usienku benengu bani mbo kenyekɔ geen anumi.
17Kenye biala na ukyuli ɔsu ni,
bekyuli beenú-ka aani litemi geen,
wetédu uwi ɔni na lɛla lɛni geen nálɛ ni,
básɔku-ni básu kaduɛ.
18Baakana na baatu egulabi taanu
na bayikune inyɔ bani mɔɔkya unyeƒi ɔdi lɛlɔ
na unyeƒi ɔsa.
19Si bɔƒiɔ búduo awɔ ku ƒula ɔkpana ntɛ ni,
ubo ɔkplu ka abla lɛla lɛdi ete-nwu na bɛsɔ bɛbla unwi
utulo kalɛ na ekpo adi ɔma unengudi
ɔni na bátu bámana lɛlɔ.
Unyeƒi kpakplaa uule bakpana inyɔ ntɛ
aani kalɛ na baakalɛ ɔban kenye na babala.
20Etemila aayá na kɔyu kuumó
aani kalɛ na adila aayá na kaƒɔ keemó.
Lɛni na etemila ani mɔɔlɛ́ ukyuli kenye
na uwi ɔni na ɔ́manku lɛlɔ eemó ukyuli.
21Bekyuli bani na atɛ aayu emini
ku lɛla lɛni mɔɔsiáku akpanabi,
ɔsika unyemi ɔɔkana na ɔdu ukyuli
iye ubunku ukyuli ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ.
22Ukyuli ɔni nákɛ uleku ɔ́kɛ lɛlakɛ,
na lɛƒɔndia lɛmmɔ lɛ́si Unwoti kudɔ.
23Ɔwabane muuvele ka banu-nwu kɔnyana,
na ɔlakɛne uudie kenye ku edumi.
24Bakpana badi bakya bani ɔbladu mɔɔyila lɛlɔ udu.
Nsu badi beebó taada lɛlɔ geen utulo banwa muedi.

english_text:
It's Wise To Be Patient
1It's better to be poor
and live right
than to be a stupid liar.
2Willingness and stupidity
don't go well together.
If you are too eager,
you will miss the road.
3We are ruined
by our own stupidity,
though we blame the Lord.
4The rich have many friends;
the poor have none.
5Dishonest witnesses and liars
won't escape punishment.
6Everyone tries to be friends
of those who can help them.
7If you are poor,
your own relatives reject you,
and your friends are worse.
When you really need them,
they are not there.
8Do yourself a favor
by having good sense—
you will be glad you did.
9Dishonest witnesses and liars
will be destroyed.
10It isn't right for a fool
to live in luxury
or for a slave to rule
in place of a king.
11It's wise to be patient
and show what you are like
by forgiving others.
12An angry king roars
like a lion,
but when a king is pleased,
it's like dew on the crops.
13Foolish children bring disgrace
to their fathers.
A nagging wife goes on and on
like the drip, drip, drip
of the rain.
14You may inherit all you own
from your parents,
but a sensible wife
is a gift from the Lord.
15If you are lazy
and sleep your time away,
you will starve.
16Obey the Lord's teachings
and you will live—
disobey and you will die.
17Caring for the poor
is lending to the Lord,
and you will be well repaid.
18Correct your children
before it's too late;
if you don't punish them,
trouble will come their way.
19People with bad tempers
are always in trouble,
and they need help
over and over again.
20Pay attention to advice
and accept correction,
so you can live sensibly.
21We may make a lot of plans,
but the Lord will do
what he has decided.
22What matters most is loyalty.
It's better to be poor
than to be a liar.
23Showing respect to the Lord
brings true life—
if you do it, you can relax
without fear of danger.
24Some people are too lazy
to lift a hand
to feed themselves.
25Stupid fools learn good sense
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being corrected.
26Disgraceful children
rob their father
and chase their mother away.
27If you stop learning,
you will forget
what you already know.
28A lying witness makes fun
of the court system,
and criminals think crime
is really delicious.
29A stupid fool should expect
to be punished.
translation_text:
1Ɔdia si adi ɔwabane na aadi litemi geen lɛlɔ
utulo si adi ɔdɔlɔdi na aanyi ɔkɔ.
2Si anumi égyie-ɔ kabla lɛlɔ na eeebo lɛlati ni, ɔɔɔdia.
Na si eesié pla pla taagya ni, adubɔkana na ayii ulu.
3Bekyuli beebile bana ngba na bana kɔdɔlɔ ɔsu,
na beeti kɔnyi taakya Unwoti.
4Lɛlakɛ liiboku bakpana pii,
nsu kɔwaba kɔɔgyá-ma.
5Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ teedie etemila kenye ni,
ulékeli kɔtu bɔni.
Na ɔkɔ ɔnyine ɔdi ulakana na wekeli.
6Bekyuli pii beevele ɔga ubi ka ɔbla-ma lɛƒɔndia lɛdi.
Lɛni kani na ukyuli biala uudie ukyuli
ɔni muute bekyuli ala kɔkpana.
7Si ɔwabane lɛlɔ bekyuli beení-nwu ni,
bi ɔsu na nwuna bakpana beléni-nwu?
Ɔwabane ɔmmɔ ɔdubo bɔkpali-ma,
nsu bana ƒui badubukeli-nwu.
8Si ákɛ lɛnunda ni, ɔɔtina ka aayɔ́ lɛlɔ.
Na bekyuli bani muunye kpakplaa ka bakɛ lɛlati
na beteenu ala kalɔ ni,
enu ku akɔkɔ adubuyi-ma.
9Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ teedie etemila kenye ni,
ulékeli kɔtu bɔni.
Na ɔkɔ ɔnyine ni, badubo-nwu bɔyila ku udu.
10Utalɛ ka ɔdɔlɔdi ulie kesii kani muukeye na utaadi ngba
iye kabla ɔblane ɔdi utaadi baga bebi lɛlɔ.
11Bekyuli bani mbo kasusu buni baabala bana kɔnyi.
Na bekyuli badubo-ma bɔbu na baƒɔ lɛnyi
si bédie bekyuli ekpidi atu.
12Si ɔga úti kɔnyi ni, use aani kalɛ na gyata uubó lɛdi.
Nsu nwuna lɛƒɔndia lise aani amii na livo lɛlɔ.
13Ubi ɔdɔlɔdi ɔdi ɔgbankpi ute ɔti.
Na uleku ɔni mɔɔkya unyeƒi use aani ɔtɔ ɔni muudú.
14Lɛlakɛ ku kaduli kani na bawɔne badubɔkana
na bese bana bebi kama.
Nsu uleku ɔbuni ɔni muunú ala kalɔ bɔkɛ buti ni,
Unwoti kudɔ na ɔɔsí.
15Ɔkɔsɔne mɔɔtɛ teesie ɔgyu,
na anwu lɛnɔ kɔka kɔɔda.
16Si ádi Unwoti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ni, adubɔkɛ ngba.
Nsu si éni-mu ni, adubo bukpi.
17Si ébunku bawabane ni, Unwoti na eevó ala teete,
na ɔdubɔƒɔ kayu kammɔ ɔsɔku ute-ɔ.
18Tumini ƒula bebi kpakplaa na uwi ɔni amu ebo-ma lɛlɔ ɔyikun.
Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, adubo-ma ngba bubile.
19Bekyuli bani muuti kɔnyi
pla pla ni,
badubɔƒɔ ama alati lɛtuni kayu.
Si áƒɔ-ma kunwi ni, agyi anii asɔ adubo-ma bɔƒɔ kunyɔdi.
20Bɔlɛ ku ala ani ƒui na badubɔtina-a ni,
ƒɔ-mu kalɛ na adubɔkana,
na adubɔda anu ƒula ngba emeyi akladi ƒui.
21Adubɔkana na eti kasusu
kɔkwɛ pii,
nsu Unwoti lɛƒɔyɔ kani ndubo bunye.
22Ukyuli lɛlɔ lɛɛda kubiti si aadi ƒula linyese lɛlɔ.
Si adi ɔwabane ni, ɔdia utulo ka ataatuala
na ataasu inye inyɔ inyɔ.
23Si aayia Unwoti ni,
ɔɔyá na eelie ngba
na ɔɔgyumana-a kalɛ na ɔgbankpi ulálɛku-ɔ.
24Kɔkɔsɔ kɔɔdi ɔkɔsɔne lɛlɔ
geen ɔni na
kalɛ na ɔmini adila ɔkya
kenye muedi
ɔɔda-nwu kɔkɔsɔ.
25Ukyuli ɔni muudumi bekyuli taakya-ma lɛlɔ lɛma,
si áni-nwu kɔtu ni, bekyuli bani na bana kasusu kásɔ
badubɔtɛya lɛla lɛdi. Na si ádɔnku ɔnundane ni,
ɔdubo anu bɔda bubu.
26Bebi bani mɔɔbla bana bati ulikplu
iye benwini benye bana beni lɛlɔ ni,
kɔƒa kɔdi-ma kadi anumi na bénwini lɛla lɛni
mɔɔdu bekyuli lili.
27Ubi, si éni anii ukyuli utatina-a lɛla ni,
énwini kama ákya lɛlati.
28Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ teedie litemi kenye ni,
uudumi na ɔɔmá litemi bɔtɛ ulu ɔni ntɛ nse.
Na balalane baaƒɔ́ likpidi teebweli aani adila.
29Bekyuli bani muudumi bekyuli taama ni,
Unwoti ɔdubo-ma kɔtu bɔni.
Na badɔlɔdi kama kadubo kugyiimi butaaƒɔ.

english_text:
Words of Wisdom Are Better than Gold
1It isn't smart to get drunk!
Drinking makes a fool of you
and leads to fights.
2An angry ruler
is like a roaring lion—
make either one angry,
and you are dead.
3It makes you look good
when you avoid a fight—
only fools love to quarrel.
4If you are too lazy to plow,
don't expect a harvest.
5Someone's thoughts may be
as deep as the ocean,
but if you are smart,
you will discover them.
6There are many who say,
“You can trust me!”
But can they be trusted?
7Good people live right,
and God blesses the children
who follow their example.
8When rulers decide cases,
they weigh the evidence.
9Can any of us really say,
“My thoughts are pure,
and my sins are gone”?
10Two things the Lord hates
are dishonest scales
and dishonest measures.
11The good or bad
that children do
shows what they are like.
12Hearing and seeing
are gifts from the Lord.
13If you sleep all the time,
you will starve;
if you get up and work,
you will have enough food.
14Everyone likes to brag
about getting a bargain.
15Sensible words are better
than gold or jewels.
16You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
17The food you get by cheating
may taste delicious,
but it turns to gravel.
18Be sure you have sound advice
before making plans
or starting a war.
19Stay away from gossips—
they tell everything.
20Children who curse their parents
will go to the land of darkness
long before their time.
21Getting rich quick
may turn out to be a curse.
22Don't try to get even.
Trust the Lord,
and he will help you.
23The Lord hates dishonest scales
and dishonest weights.
So don't cheat!
24How can we know
what will happen to us
when the Lord alone decides?
25Don't fall into the trap
of making promises to God
before you think!
26A wise ruler severely punishes
every criminal.
27Our inner thoughts are a lamp
from the Lord,
and they search our hearts.
28Rulers are protected
by God's mercy and loyalty,
but they must be merciful
for their kingdoms to last.
29Young people take pride
in their strength,
but the gray hairs of wisdom
are even more beautiful.
30A severe beating can knock all
of the evil out of you!
translation_text:
1Ntɛ muuboku budumi taama.
Na muna bɔda lɛnɔ muuboku kekpo.
Anwuɔsu si ukyuli ɔ́ya na ntɛ bɔ́di-nwu lɛlɔ ni,
ɔɔɔdubo anu bɔda.
2Ɔga kɔnyi kuse aani gyata bɔkwanyi.
Si ákya-nwu kɔnyi ni,
ƒula ngba na ákya ɔgbankpi kemmo.
3Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔda kekpo ni,
ɔbu likpose lɛdi nsia-nwu lɛlɔ.
Badɔlɔdi kani mɔɔkya ka ogya.
4Si kɔkɔsɔ kɔ́da-a kɔ́gya na átakana na aƒɔ ɔƒɔwi ni,
aaadubo edula adi bɔkɛ na edula ɔƒɛwi.
5Etemila buni ani beeti taalɛ ukyuli ni,
kayi ɔkwalɛ kemmo na ábɛ akya,
nsu banundane baaní-nya taalɛku mmɔ.
6Bakpana pii baasu ka badi bakpana buni
bani naaalɛ bana bakpana kama,
nsu ɛlɛɛ na badubɔnu na bana akɔ ka
baadi bana litemi lɛlɔ sɔsɔ.
7Bekyuli babuni beedie lɛgba lɛni mɔɔtina ka
baadi bana litemi lɛlɔ geen.
Na bana bebi bani nsia-ma kama ni,
bekyuli badubute-ma kusɛ kusɛ.
8Si ɔga ɔdi ɔ́tɛ litemi na uukulo-ni ni,
ɔɔkali kenye kani ƒui na bekyuli bédie
na litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ taanu,
na ɔƒuna ala ƒui kemmo ɔnu asa na ukulo litemi lɛmmɔ.
9Ɔma ndubɔkana bɔsu ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni amu lɛ́bla mina kayi sɛɛn,
na nse kedee ɔsu likpidi lɛdi lɛsɔ lɛɛɛma-mi lɛlɔ?”
10Unwoti ukisi beyedine bani mɔɔkɔ́ku ala ulu biala lɛlɔ
taanya bekyuli taakya.
11Lɛnamu uwi ƒui na baanu bebi taati
si udu ɔbuni iye ukpidi ndubo-ma bɔkya
na bana udu ɔni na béti baakɔ́ kenye.
12Atu ani na beenú ku anumi ani na baanu ni,
etela na adi na ási Unwoti kudɔ.
13Ukyuli ɔni na aayɔ́ lɛlɛɛ ni, kɔwaba ndubo-ɔ bɔda.
Nu nwaa na abla lɛla lɛdi na adubɔkɛ adila pii na adi emo.
14Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia lɛla lɛdi uye ni,
ɔɔní kuye kɔmmɔ kpakplaa,
na ɔɔsu ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛmmɔ kuye kútedu mmɔ.”
Na anwu mɔɔtina kalɛ na basɔku kuye badi.
Na uunwini taakun lɛmɛnɛ ɔɔtina lɛlɔ.
15Lɛnunda etemila aaabɔ na áƒɔ kuye lɛnɔ
etulo sika ugyiedi ku asɛɛ ani náƒɔ kuye geen.
16Nu ka áƒɔ lɛla lɛdi ényene kama ásiku ukyuli
ɔni muunye ɔƒɔ kama na nwuna kayu ɔsu.
Ya na baka kayu kadi bɔƒɔ bute-ɔ
na ɔƒɔ ɔni kayu kenye na ɔdi uunye lɛlɔ.
17Bodobodo uyudi ɔɔyu emini geen si étu-nwu kenye,
nsu uunwíni atabi si uwi ɔni na adaku bɔnwanta.
18Ukyuli kɔkwɛ kɔni na ɔɔkya kabla kadi lɛlɔ
kaatɛ si úye kasusu.
Tata kekpo si bátaka-a kasusu bute.
19Kɔtɛ keeke ɔtɛmine uugyingya kɔbɛtɛ.
Anwuɔsu tadiku ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu kɔkpana.
20Ukyuli ɔni muuwida ɔti iye
uni ni,
nwuna ngba ogya uuni.
21Si ɔnamu úyile nwuna kadikɔ kani na ɔti úse-nwu bɔƒɔ ni,
kusɛ kusɛ ulásiaku-nwu taatáwɔlɔ.
22Tasu ukyuli ɔdi anini, “Ndubɔƒɔ-ɔ likpidi lɛni na ábla-mi kayu.”
Ya na Unwoti ɔtɛ-ni ute-ɔ.
23Ukyuli ɔni na ulakɔku lɛla liyedi ulu lɛlɔ ni,
Unwoti ulayɔ-nwu litemi.
Na lɛkɔkula lɛni beeti taanya ukyuli taakya ni,
liiƒí Unwoti livo.
24Unwoti mɔɔtɔnku bekyuli na bana ngba ulu busie kemmo.
Na ukyuli ulakana nwuna ngba ulu ɔni na uusié kalɔ bunu bɔwɔlɔ.
25Si átaka lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ bɔbu
bɔnu ni,
tababla tese Unwoti
kenye kadi.
Ɔsika si átakana-ni bɔbla ni,
ɔgbankpi ɔkya-nwu kemmo.
26Si ɔga ɔnundane ɔdi kɔnu kútuku belikplune ni,
uuti-ma teewi kukɔ lɛlɔ aani antabi
na uuti lɛklɔyi taakɔ-ma kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.
27Bukeye bɔni na Unwoti uuti
taanu ukyuli kalɛ na
use ni,
uukeye teeduo-nwu kɔyu kemmo
na uudie abɛla ƒui na kagyudikɔ keyi.
28Kalɛ na ɔga ɔɔyɔ́ bekyuli
uwi ndi uwi
na ɔɔdi nwuna etemila
lɛlɔ lɛnɔ
ɔɔgyumana-nwu na ɔɔyá
na nwuna lɛga kadikɔ
keenye kpakplaa na bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ ɔsu.
29Bakloƒu ɔyikun ndi bana bukeye.
Na benengu liliƒuala mɔɔtina bana lɛnunda bukeye
na ala ani bánu dii ɔsu.
30Ɔlɔna kɔtu bɔni buudie likpidi na ukyuli lɛlɔ.
Na kɔtu bɔni bɔmmɔ bɔɔyá na ukyuli kayi kaabla sɛɛn.

english_text:
The Lord Is In Charge
1 The Lord controls rulers,
just as he determines
the course of rivers.
2We may think we are doing
the right thing,
but the Lord always knows
what is in our hearts.
3Doing what is right and fair
pleases the Lord
more than an offering.
4Evil people are proud
and arrogant,
but sin is the only crop
they produce.
5If you plan and work hard,
you will have plenty;
if you hurry to get rich,
you will end up poor.
6Cheating to get rich
is a foolish dream
and no less than suicide.
7You destroy yourself
by being cruel and violent
and refusing to live right.
8All crooks are liars,
but anyone who is innocent
will do right.
9 It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
10Evil people want to do wrong,
even to their friends.
11An ignorant fool learns
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being instructed.
12God is always fair!
He knows what the wicked do
and will punish them.
13If you won't help the poor,
don't expect to be heard
when you cry out for help.
14A secret bribe will save you
from someone's fierce anger.
15When justice is done,
good citizens are glad
and crooks are terrified.
16If you stop using good sense,
you will find yourself
in the grave.
17Heavy drinkers and others
who live only for pleasure
will lose all they have.
18God's people will escape,
but all who are wicked
will pay the price.
19It's better out in the desert
than at home with a nagging,
complaining wife.
20Be sensible and store up
precious treasures—
don't waste them
like a fool.
21If you try to be kind and good,
you will be blessed with life
and goodness and honor.
22One wise person can defeat
a city full of soldiers
and capture their fortress.
23Watching what you say
can save you
a lot of trouble.
24If you are proud and conceited,
everyone will say,
“You're a snob!”
25If you want too much
and are too lazy to work,
it could be fatal.
26But people who obey God
are always generous.
27 The Lord despises the offerings
of wicked people
with evil motives.
28If you tell lies in court,
you are done for;
only a reliable witness
can do the job.
29Wicked people bluff their way,
but God's people think
before they take a step.
30No matter how much you know
or what plans you make,
you can't defeat the Lord.
31Even if your army has horses
ready for battle,
the Lord will always win.
translation_text:
1Ɔga ɔni mɔɔdi lɛlɔ kayi kese aani ketu kani mɔɔgbá.
Na Unwoti mɔɔtɔnku-ka na kaagbá taavi kesii kani na ɔɔyɔ́.
2Ukyuli ɔɔnu ka ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na ɔkɛ ɔdia geen,
nsu Unwoti mɔɔnu-nwu kayi kemmo taati kalɛ na kese.
3Lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ Unwoti si bɔɔbla ala ani mɔɔyɔ́-nwu kaƒɔ
teetulo si búti akpala búboku-nwu.
4Anumi ani mɔɔnu ɔnusɛ ku kayi kani mɔɔtalaku lɛlɔ katɔ
ku likyulikpi ala bɔbla ƒui adi likpidi.
5Kabla lɛlɔ bɔbu bɔnu na
enye-ka lɛlɔ kpakplaa uute kɔsia.
Nsu ulu klukui lɛlɔ bɔsia
anii aakɛ́ lɛkɛ ɔɔyá na kɔwaba kuuƒie ukyuli.
6Lɛkɛ lɛni na ukyuli ɔ́sia ɔkɔ ulu lɛlɔ ɔ́kɛ ni,
lɛɛyii taakya aani ulɔyɔ
na lɛdi kakpagyuɛ kekpidi kani muudie ukyuli.
7Ka belikplune balayɔ ka babla ala ulu lɛlɔ ɔsu ni,
bana likyulikpi ala
adubo-ma buyu bɔtu na ayila-ma udu.
8Bekyuli bani na bana kayi
kaadú-ma kɔtɔ na bana ablala ɔsu ni,
lilu lɛni neeese siin lɛlɔ na baaví.
Na bani na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma ni,
baasia lilu siin lɛlɔ.
9Si awɔ lɛti elie ƒula lɛyu lɛdi kemmo kpoo ni, ɔdia-a
utulo ka awɔ ku uleku ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ ɔgyani kenye ɔdi
bɛkya lɛgbanya lɛdi kemmo.
10Balalane ebiti ndi ka babla bana bakpana kalala.
Na bekyuli beeebo bɔnwuna bɔdi na bana enu kemmo.
11Si uwi ɔni na baaní bekyuli bani muuti lɛla biala
taabla lɛmala kɔtu ni,
uwi ɔmmɔ na bekyuli bani na bana kasusu kásɔ
baatɛya lɛla.
Nsu banundane ni, si bálɛ-ma lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ ni,
baatí lɛlɔ bɔda.
12Bekyuli bani nse siin
baatí ala ani
mɔɔlɛ́ku bekyuli bekpidi na bana kɔduli.
Na belikplune bammɔ badubɔsiaku ɔgbankpi.
13Bekyuli bani muutile atu
si bawabane beewulo kɔnyana ni,
ama lɛnɔ belénu belete-ma si baayaki lɛla lɛdi.
14Etela ani baabɛla teete ukyuli
aayá na kɔnyi kɔɔyɔ́ ukyuli.
Na etela ammɔ udu
aayala kayi.
15Ala bɔbla ulu lɛlɔ bɔɔyɔ́ bekyuli bani mɔɔyia Unwoti kaƒɔ.
Na ɔɔyá na liƒu lɛɛda alaekpidi bablane.
16Ukyuli ɔni naaasiaku kasusu kabuni
kani na baakya-nwu lɛlɔ ni,
anwu ku bekpine ndubo kɔkpana bɔdi.
17Bekyuli bani na ebiti keeke kama bɔsiaku
bɔdia-ma ni,
bawabane na beenwíni.
Ntɛ ku adikpi lɛlɔyɔ alaya na ukyuli ɔɔkɛ́ lɛkɛ.
18Uwi ɔdi ɔkya na baaní balalane kɔtu
kalɛ na bekyuli bani mɔɔyia Unwoti banwuna.
Lɛni kani baabla belikplune na bekyuli bani nse siin ɔsu.
19Ɔdia si awɔ lɛti akya ketele ntɛ
utulo awɔ ku uleku ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ ɔgyani kenye.
20Banundane bebo lɛkɛ ku ala ani mɔɔdia bɔnu.
Nsu badɔlɔdi baadi lɛla ndi lɛla teedie ku udu.
21Ukyuli ɔni anumi muugyie na Unwoti lɛƒɔyɔ bɔbla lɛlɔ
na Unwoti utaayɔ-nwu ni,
ɔdubulie ngba ku udu buni,
na bekyuli badubo-nwu butaabu.
22Banundane baadi bayikune lɛlɔ
na beeƒie bana ala taaƒɔ,
na baaƒɛ-ma awodu ani lɛlɔ
na békpo kama ƒui
teewi kalɔ.
23Si áti ƒula kenye bɔda kpoo ni,
eleti lɛlɔ alatákya litemi lɛdi kemmo.
24Bekyuli bani mɔɔkun lɛmɛnɛ
na baatalaku lɛlɔ katɔ
na baanu ka ama kani
ntulo ni,
baata teenye bekyuli lɛlɔ uwi biala.
25Lɛla lɛni kani na bakɔsɔne badubɔsia anu
ndi ka badubɔyii ku udu,
ɔsika béni banii balabla kabla kadi.
26Ama belemo kudii. Mmomu kalɛ na bakɛ bebu ni,
nwuna kasusu kani na beeti.
Nsu bani mɔɔyia Unwoti ni,
ama beete ala ku kaƒɔ ƒaa.
27Unwoti ukisi ukyuli ukpidi akpala.
Na ɔni nsɔ ntulo ƒui ndi ka ute-nya ku kasusu kekpidi
ka ɔkɛ nwuna lɛla lɛdi ɔsu.
28Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ teedie litemi kenye ni,
badubutile-nwu kuƒi.
Na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔsu lɛla lɛni nálɛ geen ni,
anwu na badubɔya na udie ala kenye.
29Ulikplune ɔɔƒwɛ anumi momoomo.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla ala
siin ni,
ɔɔnu kaduɛ na nwuna
ablala lɛlɔ.
30Kɔkwɛ kɔni na bekyuli baakya ƒui
si ina dɛ na béti lɛnunda kemmo bákya-ku ni,
kulakana Unwoti lɛlɔ bɔdi kudii.
31Si ina dɛ báklibi bapɔnkɔ béte kekpo ni,
Unwoti kani mɔɔyá na baadi lɛlɔ.

english_text:
The Value of a Good Reputation
1A good reputation and respect
are worth much more
than silver and gold.
2The rich and the poor
are all created
by the Lord.
3When you see trouble coming,
don't be stupid
and walk right into it—
be smart and hide.
4Respect and serve the Lord!
Your reward will be wealth,
a long life, and honor.
5Crooks walk down a road
full of thorny traps.
Stay away from there!
6 Teach your children
right from wrong,
and when they are grown
they will still do right.
7The poor are ruled by the rich,
and those who borrow
are slaves of moneylenders.
8Troublemakers get in trouble,
and their terrible anger
will get them nowhere.
9The Lord blesses everyone
who freely gives food
to the poor.
10Arguments and fights
will come to an end,
if you chase away those
who insult others.
11The king is the friend of all
who are sincere
and speak with kindness.
12The Lord watches over everyone
who shows good sense,
but he frustrates the plans
of deceitful liars.
13Don't be so lazy that you say,
“If I go to work,
a lion will eat me!”
14The words of a bad woman
are like a deep pit;
if you make the Lord angry,
you will fall right in.
15All children are foolish,
but firm correction
will make them change.
16Cheat the poor to make profit
or give gifts to the rich—
either way you lose.
Thirty Wise Sayings
17Here are some sayings
of people with wisdom,
so listen carefully
as I teach.
18You will be glad
that you know these sayings
and can recite them.
19I am teaching them today,
so that you
may trust the Lord.
20I have written thirty sayings
filled with sound advice.
21You can trust them completely
to give you the right words
for those in charge of you.
–1–
22Don't take advantage
of the poor
or cheat them in court.
23The Lord is their defender,
and what you do to them,
he will do to you.
–2–
24Don't make friends with anyone
who has a bad temper.
25You might turn out like them
and get caught in a trap.
–3–
26Don't guarantee to pay
someone else's debt.
27If you don't have the money,
you might lose your bed.
–4–
28Don't move a boundary marker
set up by your ancestors.
–5–
29If you do your job well,
you will work for a ruler
and never be a slave.
translation_text:
1Si élie ngba buni na bekyuli baalɔ-ɔ lɛnyi buni ni,
ɔdia utulo lɛlakɛ linengudi.
Ɔsika si bekyuli bényene-ɔ keliekɔ kenengudi na ƒula lɛnyi ɔsu ni,
ɔdia utulo ka akɛ sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ƒui.
2Balakɛne ku bawabane ƒui badi likeke na ulu unwi lɛlɔ,
na anwu ndi ka Unwoti nédie bana inyɔ.
3Ukyuli ɔbuni ɔni mɔɔsia nwuna lɛlɔ anu ni,
ɔɔnu ɔgbankpi ɔni mebo taatualaku anumi
na uunye lɛlɔ kagyumana.
Na bani na bana kasusu kásɔ ni,
bɔkɛ kani na baakɛ gyoli gyoli
teetéduo ɔgbankpi ku lɛbibo kemmo.
4Lɛlɔ kalɔ buboku ku Unwoti bɔyia ulu geen lɛlɔ
ɔɔyá na lɛlakɛ ku ɔbu ku ngba buumomo ukyuli.
5Ɔkɔ banyine ni, liyu ku ɔgbankpi mɔɔkya-ma ulu lɛlɔ.
Na ukyuli ɔni na ngba bɔ́ƒɔ-nwu kuye ni, uláda udu ɔmmɔ.
6Tina ƒula bebi kasiakɔ kabuni na si bábi lɛlɔ ni,
na balasia kesii bamba.
7Kalɛ na balakɛne baadi bawabane lɛlɔ ni,
lɛni na bekyuli bani muuvó ala bekyuli kudɔ
beenwíni kabla bablane teete-ma.
8Bekyuli bani na litemi lɛlɔ tadi ulu lɛlɔ ebi
na baavá na bekyuli akɔ ni,
ɔgbankpi ebi na badubo bɔƒɛ.
Na bana liƒu lɛni baakya bekyuli
na baadi-ma lɛlɔ kenye kadubo buklo.
9Bekyuli bani mbo lɛƒɔndia na beete bawabane ala ni,
kusɛ kusɛ ɔdubɔsiaku-ma.
10Bɛbɔku bekyuli bani muudumi bekyuli
taama bɛlɛku bina akɔ,
na kekpo ku kadɔ ku bekyuli budumi bɔdubɔyii ƒui.
11Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia ka nwuna kayi kemmo kese sɛɛn
na ɔɔtɛmi lɛƒɔndia etemila ni, ɔdi ɔga ɔkpana.
12Unwoti ɔɔgyumana ukyuli ɔni mbo lɛlati,
na uubile ɔkɔ ɔnyine kɔkwɛ kɔni na ɔɔkya.
13Ɔkɔsɔne ubo kɔkɔsɔ kɔkwɛ pii
na uuti teete lɛlɔ kuƒi na ɔɔsu ɔnini,
“Ɔƒɛni kalɛ si lɛ́lɛ lísie ntábla lɛla lɛdi ni,
ndubo gyata bɔsiaku na ulu lɛlɔ na ɔdu-mi!”
14Uleku ɔyalɛ kenye kemmo kágyu voo aani ubu bonwu ɔdi.
Na bekyuli bani naaabla Unwoti lɛyɔla ni,
ama ndubo bɔnu buduo ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo.
15Ɔnamu ɔni na ɔƒɛni na ɔ́si
ɔɔkɔ́ ni,
adɔlɔla éyi-nwu lɛlɔ
kemmo tɛɛ.
Nsu si átumini-nwu kaduɛ ni,
ɔmmɔ ƒui ɔɔlɛ́-nwu lɛlɔ.
16Ukyuli ɔni na bawabane
na ɔɔnya taakya asa
na ɔɔkɛ́ taadi
iye balakɛne na uute ala
kalɛ na ɔkɛ lɛla lɛdi
bana kudɔ ni,
kɔwaba ndubo-ma buƒie.
Banundane Básu Ala Avlaatɛ Adi
17Se atu na enu banundane butemi. Ya na ƒula kayi kasia mina ala ani mɔɔtina-a lɛlɔ. 18Ɔsika ɔdia geen ka aya na etemila amɛni eduo-ɔ kayi kemmo ƒui na asia-a unyemi lɛlɔ. 19Mɔɔtina-a ala ɔmwi. Geen ni, awɔ mɔɔtina lɛla lɛdi kalɛ na ƒula anu ƒui asia Unwoti lɛlɔ. 20Línweni ala avlaatɛ adi líte-ɔ, na bɔlɛ ku lɛlati ala sɔɔn na adi. 21Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na adubɔsia na ati litemi geen lɛmmɔ. Na adubɔkana na edie lɛla biala kenye ulu lɛlɔ atɔ asia ete bekyuli bani nákya-a kabla kadi kɔnu.
– 1 –
22Tasia ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ na eyu bawabane anii kɔwaba kɔda-ma ɔsu. Na tasia ulu ukpidi ɔdi lɛlɔ na akɛ bekyuli bani mɔɔyaki lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ kɔsia na litemi katɛkɔ. 23Ɔsika Unwoti uukpó teete-ma. Na ukyuli ɔni makya-ma ɔlɛ ni, Unwoti lɛnɔ ɔdubɔkya-nwu ɔlɛ.
– 2 –
24Da lɛlɔ mami na bekyuli bani muuti kɔnyi pla pla lɛlɔ. 25Na si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, awɔ lɛnɔ adubɔtɛya-ma na eti ƒula kɔyu akya ɔgbankpi kemmo.
– 3 –
26Tatákyaku ukyuli ɔdi ɔku kɔnu anii eenye-nwu kama na kayu kadi ɔsu. 27Si átakana kayu kammɔ bɔƒɔ ni, ƒula atɛla muedi badubɔni-nya bedie-ɔ kalɔ.
– 4 –
28Teyu ƒula ɔdɔsane ɔdi lɛlakɛ anii aavumana ɔmii ugyii ɔnii na ati bene bálɛ kenyekɔ.
– 5 –
29Bekyuli bani na ánu ka bebo kogyoklo geen ni, baga kabla na baabla na ɔɔɔdi bekyuli keeke.

english_text:
–6–
1When you are invited
to eat with a king,
use your best manners.
2Don't go and stuff yourself!
That would be just the same
as cutting your throat.
3Don't be greedy for all
of that fancy food!
It may not be so tasty.
–7–
4Give up trying so hard
to get rich.
5Your money flies away
before you know it,
just like an eagle
suddenly taking off.
–8–
6Don't accept an invitation
to eat a selfish person's food,
no matter how good it is.
7People like that take note
of how much you eat.
They say, “Take all you want!”
But they don't mean it.
8Each bite will come back up,
and all your kind words
will be wasted.
–9–
9Don't talk to fools—
they will make fun of you.
–10–
10Don't move a boundary marker
or take the land
that belongs to orphans.
11God All-Powerful is there
to defend them against you.
–11–
12Listen to instruction
and do your best to learn.
–12–
13Don't fail to correct
your children.
You won't kill them
by being firm,
14and it may even
save their lives.
–13–
15My children,
if you show good sense,
I will be happy,
16and if you are truthful,
I will really be glad.
–14–
17Don't be jealous of sinners,
but always honor the Lord.
18Then you will truly have hope
for the future.
–15–
19Listen to me, my children!
Be wise and have enough sense
to follow the right path.
20Don't be a heavy drinker
or stuff yourself with food.
21It will make you feel drowsy,
and you will end up poor
with only rags to wear.
–16–
22Pay attention to your father,
and don't neglect your mother
when she grows old.
23Invest in truth and wisdom,
discipline and good sense,
and don't part with them.
24Make your father truly happy
by living right and showing
sound judgment.
25Make your parents proud,
especially your mother.
–17–
26My son, pay close attention,
and gladly follow
my example.
27Bad women and unfaithful wives
are like a deep pit—
28they are waiting to attack you
like a gang of robbers
with victim after victim.
–18–
29Who is always in trouble?
Who argues and fights?
Who has cuts and bruises?
Whose eyes are red?
30Everyone who stays up late,
having just one more drink.
31Don't even look
at that colorful stuff
bubbling up in the glass!
It goes down so easily,
32but later it bites
like a poisonous snake.
33You will see weird things,
and your mind
will play tricks on you.
34You will feel tossed about
like someone trying to sleep
on a ship in a storm.
35You will be bruised all over,
without even remembering
how it all happened.
And you will lie awake asking,
“When will morning come,
so I can drink some more?”
translation_text:
– 6 –
1Si awɔ ku lɛlɔ ɔdine bɛ́sala bɛɛdi ni, taanu kaduɛ na lɛla lɛni na uusé-ɔ anumi lɛlɔ. 2Na si aayɔ́ bɔdi pii ni, na akɔsi bɔdi! 3Na ala mini mini ani na ɔɔla teebese-ɔ anumi akɔsi-ɔ ɔkwɛ bɔda. Ɔsika ɔƒɛni kalɛ katɔlɔ lɛkwɛ lɛdi lɛkya-nwu kemmo.
– 7 –
4Tetu lɛlɔ anii eenwíni ɔlakɛne. Bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka eteebile lɛlɔ uwi? 5Ɔsika lɛlakɛ lɛɛyii na ukyuli anumi, na lɛɛtɔlɔ aani kalɛ na aasɛ uuveyi taatɔlɔ!
– 8 –
6Bekyuli bani na bebo lɛnumi ni, awɔ ku-ma bitelie bitadi. Na bana adila mini mini atada-a ɔkwɛ. 7Badubɔsu-ɔ banini, “Di na ani,” nsu ɔɔɔdi ku bana kaƒɔ ƒaa. Benye baabu ala ani na aadi akunta kalɛ na édu. 8Na adubo ala abuni ani na béte-ɔ mmɔ ƒui bɔdala budie. Na adubɔyɔ ka nka átagya-ma enu na lɛƒɔndia lɛni na banii bábla-a mmɔ ɔsu.
– 9 –
9Tebile ƒula uwi na badɔlɔdi lɛlɔ anii aalɛ-ma, ɔsika lɛnunda litemi lɛdi biala lɛɛɛdubo-ma anu bɔƒɔ.
– 10 –
10Tagyu bati ɔmii ugyii ɔdi na eƒie bekpinebi kalɔ aƒɔ anii beeebo ubunkune ɔdi ɔsu. 11Ɔsika bana Ɔƒɔne ubo ɔyikun geen. Na anwu ɔmmɔ ɔlati ndubɔwia-a litemi.
– 11 –
12Nu ka ábla ásiaku ala ani na bátina-a lɛlɔ. Na aklibi atu ese na enu lɛlati ala.
– 12 –
13Tada ƒula bebi bɔtɛmiku kalɛ na badia taya. Baaadubo bukpi si ébo-ma kugyiimi. 14Si áni-ma kɔtu ɔlɔna lɛlɔ ni, ɔkana udie-ma na kukpi kemmo.
– 13 –
15Mina ubi, lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ-mi geen si nka ebenwini ɔnundane. 16Sɔsɔ ni, mina kayi kadubɔma si línu ka aatɛmi etemila geen ani nkɛ ulu lɛlɔ.
– 14 –
17Alaekpidi bablane lɛlɔ litegyie-ɔ anumi. Mmomu taayia Unwoti uwi ndi uwi. 18Ɔsika ƒula ngba emeyi ani ndubo adubɔyɔku-ɔ, na alasia lɛla lɛdi anu alanɔ.
– 15 –
19Ubi, se kɔtu na enu litemi na ada anu. Na aya ƒula kayi kasia ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ. 20Tasiaku ntɛ bekpine ku adikpi badine ɔbladu kama! 21Ɔsika kɔwaba ulu lɛlɔ na bakɛ bésela. Lɛlɛɛ bɔlɛɛ pii mɔɔyá na beenyimi adikpi.
– 16 –
22Ƒ'ɔti ɔni néte-ɔ ngba na ébo kayawi kamɛni kemmo ni, nu-nwu litemi. Na si ƒ'ini ɔ́bi lɛlɔ na uli ɔtɔ ni, teni lɛla lɛni na wasu wasiku lɛla lɛni na ɔ́nu dii lɛlɔ. 23Ƒɔ litemi geen bɛla se lɛlɔ, na teti-ni teye. Na ada anu na aya batumini-ɔ kalɛ na anu ala ati kaduɛ. 24Ubi ɔti ɔni mbo bebi babuni ni, ɔɔnu lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ɔlɛka ebiti ataada-nwu. Bi nsɔ ntulo bɔdia si ebo bebi bani na báda anu. 25Anwuɔsu ni, bebi, bɛya lɛlɔ lɛyɔ bina bawɔne. Na bɛya na ebiti ada uleku ɔni náwɔ-ɔ.
– 17 –
26O mina ubi, ti ƒula kayi te-mi. Na ƒula anu asia lɛnunda ulu ɔni mɔɔtina-a lɛlɔ. 27Uleku ɔyalɛ ni, ubu voo na ɔdi. Na uleku ɔsɔnɔdine ni, ɔgbankpi na ɔdanku. 28Bɔbɛ na ɔɔbɛ́ teenye taagya bekyuli aani uyune. Na ɔɔnu ulu teete ɔnana ɔni malɛ ulekudi kama.
– 18 –
29Ukyuli ɔmani udu na kayi kaakpulu? Na ɔmani muukpóku lɛlɔ na ɔkɛ ɔɔdɔ anwu lɛti uwi biala? Na ɔma mɔɔƒɔ́ lɛlɛ lidu lidu na anumi égyie-nwu kɔɔ? 30Ukyuli ɔmmɔ ulata ntɛ bɔdi kalɔ kudii, ɔsika bɔdi biala bɔdia-nwu. 31Taya na kalɛ na ntɛ avlɔvɔ eeƒuƒuo na aadia bɔnu na bɔɔyu emini lɛnɔ atɔlɔ-ɔ. 32Ɔsika kawɔlɔkɔ ni, bɔdubo-ɔ lɛlɔ bɔdu aani si kɔlakpi nádu-ɔ, na utulo kɔlakpi kɔni ugyulo kenye mbo ɔkplu geen! 33Adubo ana buteegye taanu liƒu ala, na ataatɛmi aani ubuokpine. 34Na adubo butaagbanta aani ukyuli ɔni nnye ɔkɔlɔ kemmo na ɛpu anumi, na úƒie ɔkɔlɔ kemmo lɛbuli lɛmmɔ ɔda. 35Na adubo bɔsu anini, “Báƒiɛmi-mi ugyii, nsu útabla-mi lɛla lɛdi. Na uwi ɔni beebó-mi muedi ńtati. Uwi ɔmani na ndubɔta na lɛsɔ ntáni bɔdi?”

english_text:
–19–
1Don't be jealous of crooks
or want to be their friends.
2All they think about
and talk about
is violence and cruelty.
–20–
3Use wisdom and understanding
to establish your home;
4let good sense fill the rooms
with priceless treasures.
–21–
5Wisdom brings strength,
and knowledge gives power.
6Battles are won
by listening to advice
and making a lot of plans.
–22–
7Wisdom is too much for fools!
Their advice is no good.
–23–
8No one but troublemakers
think up trouble.
9Everyone hates senseless fools
who think up ways to sin.
–24–
10Don't give up and be helpless
in times of trouble.
–25–
11Don't fail to rescue those
who are doomed to die.
12Don't say, “I didn't know it!”
God can read your mind.
He watches each of us
and knows our thoughts.
And God will pay us back
for what we do.
–26–
13Honey is good for you,
my children,
and it tastes sweet.
14Wisdom is like honey
for your life—
if you find it,
your future is bright.
–27–
15Don't be a cruel person
who attacks good people
and hurts their families.
16Even if good people
fall seven times,
they will get back up.
But when trouble strikes
the wicked,
that's the end of them.
–28–
17Don't be happy
to see your enemies trip
and fall down.
18The Lord will find out
and be unhappy.
Then he will stop
being angry with them.
–29–
19Don't let evil people
worry you
or make you jealous.
20They will soon be gone
like the flame of a lamp
that burns out.
–30–
21My children, you must respect
the Lord and the king,
and you must not make friends
with anyone who rebels
against either of them.
22Who knows what sudden disaster
the Lord or a ruler
might bring?
More Sayings That Make Good Sense
23Here are some more sayings
that make good sense:
When you judge,
you must be fair.
24If you let the guilty
go free,
people of all nations
will hate and curse you.
25But if you punish the guilty,
things will go well for you,
and you will prosper.
26Giving an honest answer
is a sign
of true friendship.
27Get your fields ready
and plant your crops
before starting a home.
28Don't accuse anyone
who isn't guilty.
Don't ever tell a lie
29or say to someone,
“I'll get even with you!”
30I once walked by the field
and the vineyard
of a lazy fool.
31Thorns and weeds
were everywhere,
and the stone wall
had fallen down.
32When I saw this,
it taught me a lesson:
33 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
34Suddenly poverty hits you
and everything is gone!
translation_text:
– 19 –
1Bekyuli bekpidi lɛlɔ litegyie-ɔ anumi. Na tawia anii aakya-ma kasala kemmo lɛnɔ. 2Ɔsika bekyuli kalɔ bɔvi na bebile-ma ngba na bataakya kekpo ku etemila ani mɔɔkya lɛsɛ ogya kasusu kani na beelie taabla.
– 20 –
3Lɛnunda na beeti taatu ɔtɔ. Na kasusu kabuni lɛlɔ na uunye kpakplaa. 4Na ɔkɛnku lɛnunda lɛlɔ na adubɔkana na eyile lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ku ala abuni lidu lidu ku akɛla lɛnɔ.
– 21 –
5Ɔnundane ubo ɔyikun utulo ukyuli ɔni mbo ɔlɔkplu. Na ukyuli ɔni mbo lɛlati ni, nwuna ɔyikun uusié ɔgyu teetulo ukyuli ɔni mbo ɔlɔkplu. 6Anwuɔsu tata kekpo si átaƒɔ kasusu na banundane kudɔ. Asa na adubɔdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́si kasusu bakyane pii bani na ebo ɔsu.
– 22 –
7Ɔdɔlɔdi ɔɔnu lɛnunda kakaaka. Na si batɔnkune bása beli ni, ɔdɔlɔdi ulakɛ lɛla lɛni na ɔsu.
– 23 –
8Ukyuli ɔni muulie taabla likpidi kasusu ni, lɛsɛ ɔkyane lɛnyi na ɔɔƒɔ́. 9Na ɔdɔlɔdi kɔkwɛ ni, ekpidi sɔɔn na adi. Na ukyuli ɔni muudumi bekyuli taama ni, ɔdi balayɔ-nwu.
– 24 –
10Si ánu ka átakana lɛla lɛdi bɔbla na bukpoku bɔdi ɔsu ni, agyi anii ƒula ɔyikun ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́sɔ.
– 25 –
11Nye na aƒɔ bekyuli bani na bátɛku litemi na bádu-ma kukpi kɔtɔ na ulu ɔni naaadia lɛlɔ. Na tenye tanu na badu-ma. 12Tekeli kabla kadi na akya kakwɛ anii átati anii awɔ na ɔlɛka abla-ka. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔgyi ukyuli biala kayi kemmo na ɔɔnu awɔ lɛnɔ. Anwu mɔɔnu ƒula kɔyu lɛlɔ na ɔgyi ka áti kabla kammɔ lɛlɔ litemi. Na ɔdubɔtɛku bekyuli ƒui litemi na lɛla lɛni na bábla lɛlɔ.
– 26 –
13Mina ubi, uwɔ ɔdi lɛla lɛni mbo emini, si ákɛ na adi. Na uwɔ kɔtakɛ lɛnɔ si étuku-ku unyemi ánu ni, kubo emini. 14Lɛni kani na lɛnunda libo ƒula kɔyu emini. Anwuɔsu si ákɛ lɛnunda ni, ƒula ngba emeyi ani ndubo adubo bukeye. Na ala ani na asia anu iye aanu ulu teete ni, aláwɔ ulu.
– 27 –
15Tatábɛ tebi bekyuli babuni badi kaduli ulu aani ukyuli ukpidi. Na tetéyu-ma tatu ekpoku-ma na eti-ma ala lɛnɔ! 16Ɔsika si ina bébuli maatɛ muedi badubɔsɔ bata. Nsu si ɔgbankpi ɔ́siaku bekyuli bekpidi ama ni, ɔɔyila-ma ku udu kɔnakunwi.
– 28 –
17Lɛlɔ litayɔ-ɔ si ánu ka ƒula bekisine bébuli. Na ebiti atada-a na kayi kemmo si bétulo. 18Ɔsika ɔmmɔ udu uláyɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ, na ɔdubɔda-ma kɔtu bɔni ɔya.
– 29 –
19Tekpoku lɛlɔ ulu biala lɛlɔ na alaekpidi bablane lilidia lɛdi lɛlɔ. Na balalane lɛlɔ litegyie-ɔ anumi. 20Ɔsika bekyuli bekpidi beeebo lɛnunsia na ngba bɔni ndubo kemmo, ɔsika bana asogya ɔdubo buni.
– 30 –
21Ubi, yia Unwoti ku ɔga ɔni mɔɔdi-mii lɛlɔ. Na bekyuli bani náta bénye lɛlɔ badine lɛlɔ ni, tadiku-ma kɔkpana. 22Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, awɔ ku-ma ƒui ndubo ɔgbankpi kemmo bɔyu butéduo, na bɛyii udu ƒui.
Banundane Básu Ala Bébu
23Binu ala bamba ani na banundane básɔ básu.
Ɔɔɔdia ka banu ukyuli anumi batɛ litemi na batu litemi geen lɛmmɔ benwini. 24Na ukyuli ɔni masu alaekpidi ɔblane ɔdi ɔnini, “Adi ukyuli ɔni nse siin” ni, bekyuli badubo-ɔ buwida na kadi bekyuli ƒui badubukisi-ɔ. 25Nsu bani mɔɔdú bani litemi neeebo ubo kɔtɔ belikplune na bana ablala ɔsu ni, bana lɛlɔ lɛɛda bekyuli ebiti na kusɛ kusɛ lɛnɔ ɔdubɔsiaku-ma.
26Si bédie litemi lɛdi kenye béte-ɔ ulu lɛlɔ ni, ɔbu na béte-ɔ.
27Nu ka ƒula kabla kélie kalɔ asa na atu ɔtɔ.
28Tanyi ɔkɔ tedie kenye ada ƒula ukyulikpana ɔni nátabla lɛla lɛdi kenye. 29Na tasu anini, “Lɛ́kɛ kasiakɔ na lɛbla lɛla lɛni na bábla-mi dii lɛsia-ma!”
30Dii ni, nkɛ lɛ́vi ɔkɔsɔne ɔdi kemo. 31Lɛ́nu ka liyu lɛ́kwɛ lɛ́ƒɔ-ka ƒui. Livo bamba lɛnɔ limomo na awodu ammɔ lɛnɔ ábwɛ éwi kalɔ. 32Na ka lɛ́nu-ka na lɛ́bla kasusu ni, lɛ́tɛya lɛla lɛdi. 33Na ani ndi ka si álɛɛ ávili na átɛ lɛnɔ ágya anii aanwuna blii ni, 34kɔwaba kɔdubo-ɔ buyu bɔtu aani uyune kalɛ. Na ayaki adubo-ɔ bukpoku aani kekpo ukpone kalɛ.

english_text:
More of Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some more
of Solomon's proverbs.
They were copied by the officials
of King Hezekiah of Judah.
2God is praised
for being mysterious;
rulers are praised
for explaining mysteries.
3Who can fully understand
the thoughts of a ruler?
They reach beyond the sky
and go deep in the earth.
4Silver must be purified
before it can be used
to make something of value.
5Evil people must be removed
before anyone can rule
with justice.
6 Don't try to seem important
in the court of a ruler.
7It's better for the ruler
to give you a high position
than for you to be embarrassed
in front of royal officials.
Be sure you are right
8before you sue someone,
or you might lose your case
and be embarrassed.
9When you and someone else
can't get along,
don't gossip about it.
10Others will find out,
and your reputation
will then be ruined.
11The right word
at the right time
is like precious gold
set in silver.
12Listening to good advice
is worth much more
than jewelry made of gold.
13A messenger you can trust
is just as refreshing
as cool water in summer.
14Broken promises
are worse than rain clouds
that don't bring rain.
15Patience and gentle talk
can convince a ruler
and overcome any problem.
16Eating too much honey
can make you sick.
17Don't visit friends too often,
or they will get tired of it
and start hating you.
18Telling lies about friends
is like attacking them
with clubs and swords
and sharp arrows.
19A friend you can't trust
in times of trouble
is like having a toothache
or a sore foot.
20Singing to someone
in deep sorrow
is like pouring vinegar
in an open cut.
21 If your enemies are hungry,
give them something to eat.
And if they are thirsty,
give them something
to drink.
22This will be the same
as piling burning coals
on their heads.
And the Lord
will reward you.
23As surely as rain blows in
from the north,
anger is caused
by cruel words.
24It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
25Good news from far away
refreshes like cold water
when you are thirsty.
26When a good person gives in
to the wicked,
it's like dumping garbage
in a stream of clear water.
27Don't eat too much honey
or always want praise.
28Losing self-control
leaves you as helpless
as a city without a wall.
translation_text:
Salomo Ɔ́sɔ Úbo Agba Bamba Adi
1Salomo ɔ́sɔ úbo agba bamba, na Ɔga Hesekia kasusu bakyane bani nkya Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ bénweni-nya bése.
2Unwoti ala ani na ɔ́bɛla
bekyuli ni,
anya mɔɔtina kalɛ na úbomo
na uukeye.
Na ɔga ɔni mɔɔwia-nya kalɔ
taati ni,
ɔɔƒɔ́ lɛnyi na baabu-nwu.
3Ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi kalɛ na katɔ kákuku kétédu,
iye kesii kani na kalɔ lɛnɔ kágyu kétédu,
iye ɔti lɛla lɛni nkya ɔga ɔdi kasusu kemmo.
4Si ákya sika ɔƒualadi ogya na
kɔtakɛ kɔni
nányi kɔ́kpi mmɔ kɔ́lɛ-nwu
lɛlɔ ni,
ugyii ɔni na ukyuli biala ɔɔnu ka ɔ́ƒɔ kuye mmɔ
únwini kabla lɛblala teete ɔkywɛne ɔmmɔ.
5Lɛni kani na si bekyuli bekpidi
bálɛ ɔga ɔdi lɛga kadikɔ ni,
nwuna lɛga kadikɔ
kadubuse kaduɛ
na bataabla ala siin
na ulu lɛlɔ.
6Takpali ɔga tasu anii uteenu lɛla lɛni na adubo bɔsu
iye anwanɛ lɛlɔ anii aakɔ́ esie kesii
kani na benengu bani ntulo-ɔ beli.
7Nye na bakpali-ɔ bene banii, “Ni de kenengudikɔ mɛni,”
utulo ka babɔku-ɔ batɔlɔku
keliekɔ kenengudi
kani na aanwanɛ ka elie
ku kɔƒa.
Tanu lɛla biala,
8na eti litemi lɛmmɔ
esienku litemi katɛkɔ,
ɔsika kɔƒa kɔdubo-ɔ bukpo
si útádi-ɔ ubo.
9Si ƒula ɔkpana ɔ́ƒiɔ-ɔ ni,
awɔ ku-nwu bɛsu-ni kani na ɔwɔ mmɔ.
Tatásu ukyuli bamba na edie lɛbɛla lɛmmɔ keyi.
10Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, awɔ ɔmmɔ ɔlati
adubo ebenwini lɛmala na bekyuli anumi,
na adubɔnu ka bada atɛ ammɔ baatɛmi uwi ndi uwi.
11Kasusu kani beete ukyuli na uwi ɔbuni lɛlɔ
use aani adingyii ebi ani négyie kaduɛ
na bátɛ-nya bákya sika ɔƒualadi lɛkyami kemmo.
12Si édie ukyuli bɔƒiɔ na éti-nwu ásia ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ ni,
ɔdi lɛla lɛbuni geen ute ukyuli ɔni muunú bɔlɛ bɔmmɔ
aani asɛɛ abuni ani na béti sika ugyiedi bábla.
13Ukyuli ɔni muusié bɔtala taatábla kalɛ kani na básu-nwu ni,
nwuna ala aayu kayi buɛɛ aani kalɛ na
etubankɛ aabla kadi kani na káƒɔ ogya buɛɛ.
Bekyuli bammɔ udu baayá na bekyuli
bani bɔtala na beesié mmɔ ayu aakɛ́ lɛlɔyɔ.
14Ukyuli ɔni muusé kenye kekpludi na ulábla
taasia lɛni ni,
use aani ulɔyɔ ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ
ɔni naaakana ɔnantu bɔna.
15Kayi buɛɛ kadubɔkana
na kenwini ɔgabi ɔdi kasusu.
Na lɛdi buɛɛ butemi
bɔdubɔkana na bɔdi ukyuli
ɔni mɔɔkyaku-ɔ unyeƒi lɛlɔ.
16Si ákɛ uwɔ ni, tadi-nwu taavili
amu ɔdububo-ɔ ɔlɛ.
17Si eesié ƒula ɔkpana kudɔ busie busie ni,
ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo bɔdia
na bete-ɔ éduo.
18Ɔkɔ bɔnyi taasia bekyuli uuduo teetulo
ka eti kadadi iye kewii iye lɛtula atu ukyuli.
19Si éti ƒula kayi ásia ukyuli
ɔni na balaƒɔ taadi lɛlɔ ni,
use aani si lɛnyi lɛɛkunku-ɔ
na ada-ni aanwánta
iye akɛ eesié ɔgba ɔni
násɔ-ɔ lɛlɔ.
20Si ukyuli ɔkya kɔnyana kemmo na eedie ebiti lɛnu
taakya-nwu atu ni,
ɔɔdu lɛlɔ teetulo si éƒie kɔyɔ awu áƒɔ ukyuli kudɔ na kɔyɔ uwi
iye akɔ mma akya-nwu ɔlɛ kemmo.
21Si kɔka kɔɔda ƒula ukisine ni, te-nwu adila na ɔdi.
Si utukwɛ mɔɔda-nwu ni, te-nwu ntu na ɔni.
22Ɔsika si ábla lɛni ni, édie ogya ku agyabi éwi-nwu lili.
Na Unwoti ɔdubɔƒɔ-ɔ kayu.
23Kalɛ na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni muukpó taasi katɔ
taayu uuboku ɔnantu ni,
lɛni kani na katɛ ɔtɛne keeke ɔɔkya ukyuli kɔnyi.
24Si awɔ lɛti elie ƒula lɛyu lɛdi kemmo kpoo ni,
ɔdia-a utulo ka awɔ ku uleku
ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ ɔgyani kenye ɔdi
bɛkya lɛgbanya lɛdi kemmo.
25Kenye buni kani mɔɔsí ɔgyu teebo ukyuli
kese aani ntu bamamba bɔni mɔɔdú utukwɛ.
26Si bekyuli babuni ku bekpidi básala lɛlɔ
na ɔbladu buɛ ɔdi lɛlɔ ni,
use aani kalɛ na beebwiiile ntu bɔdi
iye beti aba taakya libiɔ lɛdi kemmo.
27Si uwɔ ɔɔɔdia bɔdi bɔvili ina ka ubo emini ni,
lɛni kani na ɔɔɔdia ka ukyuli elie ataakali
lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka bete-ɔ na ƒula kenyekɔ kenye.
28Ukyuli ɔni na ulakana lɛlɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi ni,
use aani ɔma ɔni na awodu ani mɔɔgyumana-nwu ábwɛ.

english_text:
Don't Be a Fool
1Expecting snow in summer
and rain in the dry season
makes more sense
than honoring a fool.
2A curse you don't deserve
will take wings and fly away
like a sparrow or a swallow.
3Horses and donkeys
must be beaten and bridled—
and so must fools.
4Don't make a fool of yourself
by answering a fool.
5But if you answer any fools,
show how foolish they are,
so they won't feel smart.
6Sending a message by a fool
is like chopping off your foot
just to spite yourself.
7A fool with words of wisdom
is like an athlete
with legs that can't move.
8Are you going to honor a fool?
Why not shoot a slingshot
with the rock tied tight?
9A thornbush waved around
in the hand of a drunkard
is no worse than a proverb
in the mouth of a fool.
10It's no smarter to shoot arrows
at every passerby
than it is to hire a bunch
of worthless nobodies.
11 Dogs return to eat their vomit,
just as fools repeat
their foolishness.
12There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who says,
“I'm really smart!”
13Don't be lazy and keep saying,
“There's a lion outside!”
14A door turns on its hinges,
but a lazy person
just turns over in bed.
15Some of us are so lazy
that we won't lift a hand
to feed ourselves.
16A lazy person says,
“I am smarter
than everyone else.”
17It's better to take hold
of a mad dog by the ears
than to take part
in someone else's argument.
18It's no crazier to shoot
sharp and flaming arrows
19than to cheat someone and say,
“I was only fooling!”
20Where there is no fuel
a fire goes out;
where there is no gossip
arguments come to an end.
21Troublemakers start trouble,
just as sparks and fuel
start a fire.
22There is nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
23Hiding hateful thoughts
behind smooth talk
is like coating a clay pot
with a cheap glaze.
24The pleasant talk
of an enemy
hides more evil plans
25than can be counted—
so don't believe a word!
26Everyone will see through
those evil plans.
27 If you dig a pit,
you will fall in;
if you start a stone rolling,
it will roll back on you.
28Watch out for anyone
who tells lies and flatters—
they are out to get you.
translation_text:
1Ɔbu ɔdi ulásiaku badɔlɔdi kalɛ kani na
etubankɛ aláyu kaƒɛndi iye ɔnantu ɔna edula ɔƒɛwi.
2Kalɛ na lɛsɛɛmɛɛ liibó avwi
na lɛkpaƒɛɛlɛ liiveyi
taatɔlɔ ni,
lɛni na si éwida ukyuli kekeeke,
nsu útabla lɛla lɛdi
na eewida ammɔ eeveyi
taatɔlɔ-nwu kudɔ.
3Uƒiɔ na beeti taatina ɔpɔnkɔ kesii kani na ɔsia.
Na kabuli na baakya ebuo ala utine kenye
taani na batina-nwu kasiakɔ.
Na ɔdɔlɔdi ni, kugyiimi na beebó-nwu kama.
4Si awɔ ku badɔlɔdi bɛɛkya unyeƒi ni,
tedie bana kɔdɔlɔ ala ani beeye-ɔ kenye
amu awɔ lɛnɔ adubɔbla ala kɔdɔlɔ kemmo aani bana kalɛ.
5Si awɔ ku badɔlɔdi bɛɛní lɛla lɛdi teenene ni,
die bana ala ani na beeye-ɔ kenye
na aya basɔ bakya bana kɔdɔlɔ kemmo.
6Si áƒɔ ɔdɔlɔdi ádi anii watásu kenye kalɛ na ásia-ka ni,
ɔdi kɔdɔlɔ kakali kani nse aani kalɛ na
ekulo awɔ ɔlati ɔgba edie iye ani kuvo kukpidi.
7Si ɔdɔlɔdi ɔnii uubó lɛgba ni,
úlieku aani kalɛ na ɔgba uukpi ukyuli gbinigbini.
8Si émwi ɔdɔlɔdi na ákɔliku-nwu lɛnyi katɔ ni,
use aani kalɛ na baabala lɛtabi
taakya kavwinvwi kemmo kalɛ na lilálɛ.
9Ɔdɔlɔdi lɛgba bubo buse aani kalɛ na ntɛ ukpine
ɔɔgyú liyu kagba taada kɔnu teeƒwimi.
10Ukyuli ɔni mbo kabla na úti-ka ɔ́kya ɔdɔlɔdi lɛkɔkɔ ni,
use aani ukyuli ɔni muubó kataminta
taakya kayaa lɛla lɛdi tanu tanu.
11Kalɛ na akpewe ɔsɔ uuti nwuna kɔdala ni,
lɛni na ɔdɔlɔdi ɔɔsɔ teenwini
teesie nwuna kɔdɔlɔ ala bɔbla kudɔ.
12Badɔlɔdi lɛnunsia na ala lɛlɔ ni,
ɔdia utulo bekyuli bani mɔɔkali ka
báda anu, nsu bátada anu.
13Ɔkɔsɔne ubo kɔkwɛ pii kɔni na uuti
taawia kuƒi teete lɛlɔ na ɔɔsu ɔnini,
“Ɔƒɛni kalɛ gyata unye-mi ulu
na ɔdubuƒie-mi si lɛ́lɛ lísie ntábla lɛla lɛdi.
Sɔsɔ ngyi ka gyata ɔdi unye mmɔ!”
14Kalɛ na ɔpunu ɔɔlɛmi teesie teebo ni,
lɛni na ɔkɔsɔne ɔɔtɛ nwuna atɛla lɛlɔ teebo teeminime.
15Kɔkɔsɔ kɔɔdi ɔkɔsɔne lɛlɔ geen
ɔni na kalɛ na ɔmini adila ɔkya kenye muedi
ɔɔda-nwu kɔkɔsɔ.
16Bakɔsɔne baanu lɛlɔ ka ama mmomu náda anu
betulo banundane kasusu betine maatɛ.
17Si ákya ukyuli kɔtɛ kenye na aaagyi-ku lɛlɔ lɛla lɛdi ni,
ɔdi kɔdɔlɔ ala bɔbla.
Na use aani si áda akpewe ɔni na aaagyi kɔtu aaní.
18Kalɛ na si ubuokpine ɔda lɛtula
lɛni mɔɔkana na liibile ala na ɔɔda liƒu ni,
19lɛni kani na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́nyi ɔkɔ ɔ́su nwuna ɔkpana lɛla lɛdi
na ɔ́ƒɔ-ni ku kayi asa kama na ɔnini,
“Bɔƒia kani na nda” ni, ubo liƒu.
20Si ekyweni aakywí laa na ása ni, buni na ogya uuni.
Lɛni kani na si kɔtɛ keeke kɔ́sa bɔtɛmi ni,
kadɔ lɛnɔ kása.
21Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ kadɔ uuubo kekpo bɔkya
aani kalɛ kani na ogya egyiiku akukudi eeebo ogya bɔƒɔ
iye agyabi aayá na aƒɛ aaƒɔ́ ogya.
22Ɔkɔ etemila ani nse aani lɛna wɛlɛ wɛlɛ ebo emini
na anya mɔɔyu teduo ukyuli kayi kemmo.
23Kɔtɛ kɔni baakya emini aabɛla kasusu kekpidi
kani nkya ukyuli ɔdi kayi kemmo
aani kalɛ baanwamana sika ugyiedi ntu taakwaa libui.
24Bekyuli bani na bekyuli litemi lɛkya-ma kayi ni,
uwi ɔdi baatina ka badia geen, nsu taƒɔ-ma tadi.
25Ina ka bekyuli bamɛni baabla lɛlɔ aani bebo lɛƒɔndia ni,
likpidi lɛ́ƒɔ-ma kayi kemmo tɛɛ.
26Ina ka badubɔkya lɛkwɛ na babɛla lɛla lɛmmɔ ni,
ɔdubo ubalɛ keyi na bekyuli ƒui banu.
27Si ákywɛ ƒula ɔkpana
kakpagyuɛ ni,
awɔ ɔlati ndubo-ka kemmo bɔnu buduo.
Na si éminime lɛtakpɛ bonwu lɛdi anii litásia bekyuli lɛlɔ ni,
lɛdubɔsɔ linwini libasia-a.
28Unyemi ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ taasia ukyuli ni,
uláwia ukyuli ɔmmɔ bɔdia.
Na katɔlɔ kaadú ukyuli.

english_text:
Don't Brag about Tomorrow
1 Don't brag about tomorrow!
Each day brings
its own surprises.
2Don't brag about yourself—
let others praise you.
3Stones and sand are heavy,
but trouble caused by a fool
is a much heavier load.
4An angry person is dangerous,
but a jealous person
is even worse.
5A truly good friend
will openly correct you.
6You can trust a friend
who corrects you,
but kisses from an enemy
are nothing but lies.
7If you have had enough to eat,
honey doesn't taste good,
but if you are really hungry,
you will eat anything.
8When you are far from home,
you feel like a bird
without a nest.
9The sweet smell of incense
can make you feel good,
but true friendship
is better still.
10Don't desert an old friend
of your family
or visit your relatives
when you are in trouble.
A friend nearby is better
than relatives far away.
11My child, show good sense!
Then I will be happy
and able to answer anyone
who criticizes me.
12Be cautious and hide
when you see danger—
don't be stupid and walk
right into trouble.
13You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
14A loud greeting
early in the morning
is the same as a curse.
15The steady dripping of rain
and the nagging of a wife
are one and the same.
16It's easier to catch the wind
or hold olive oil in your hand
than to stop a nagging wife.
17Just as iron sharpens iron,
friends sharpen the minds
of each other.
18Take care of a tree,
and you will eat its fruit;
look after your master,
and you will be praised.
19You see your face in a mirror
and your thoughts
in the minds of others.
20Death and the grave
are never satisfied,
and neither are humans.
21Gold and silver are tested
in a red-hot furnace,
but we are tested by praise.
22No matter how hard
you beat a fool,
you can't pound out
the foolishness.
23You should take good care
of your sheep and goats,
24because wealth and honor
don't last forever.
25After the hay is cut
and the new growth appears
and the harvest is over,
26you can sell lambs and goats
to buy clothes and land.
27From the milk of the goats,
you can make enough cheese
to feed your family
and all your servants.
translation_text:
1Takun lɛmɛnɛ na kɔnaadi kadi kani mebo lɛlɔ,
ɔsika aaagyi lɛla lɛni mebo kɔnaadi.
2Temwi lɛlɔ.
Ya na bekyuli bemwi-ɔ mmomu.
3Lɛtabi libo unu na kɔnwinimi kuse gbɛn,
nsu kayi kemmo ɔlɛ ɔni na ɔdɔlɔdi ɔɔkya ukyuli kayi ni,
ubo unu utulo alakpa anyɔ ammɔ ƒui.
4Kɔnyi kɔdanku ulikplu na livoƒi lise aani ketu buyi.
Nsu ala ani na kogyulo kuubile ni,
ɔdi ulakana-ku kenye bunye.
5Si édie lɛla lɛdi álɛ ukyuli kɔnakunwi ni, ɔdia utulo
si anii aayɔ́ ukyuli na bɔbɛ kemmo.
6Si ƒula ɔkpana ɔ́kya-a ɔlɛ lɛlɔ ni, ɔdia utulo
ɔni na ƒula ukisine úbakya-a kɔgbu ɔnii bɔƒianku na ɔda-a.
7Si ukyuli úmo ni, uwɔ muedi ɔsɔ ulati-nwu emini.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni na kɔka kɔɔda momoomo ni,
ina dɛ na lɛla lɛdi libo ɔdu muedi ni, lɛɛyu-nwu emini.
8Ukyuli ɔni náyii ɔtɔ ulu ni, use aani
aasɛ ɔni náyii nwuna lɛyu ulu.
9Bɔlɛ bɔni na ƒula ɔkpana ɔ́lɛ-ɔ na bɔ́ƒɔ-ɔ anu ni,
buse aani ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni baakyula
iye nnɔmii ƒɛƒɛɛ bɔni baawɛɛ.
10Tenwini kama takya ƒula bakpana ku ƒ'ɔti bakpana
na adubɔkɛ bebunkune uwi ɔni na ala étulo-ɔ,
na elésie ƒula ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli kudɔ.
Ɔsika ɔdia ka esie ƒula ɔkpana ɔni nde-ɔ kudɔ utulo ka
esie ƒula ɔtɔ kemmo ukyuli ɔni nkya ɔgyu kudɔ.
11Ubi, ɔɔɔdi ebiti blii ndubo-mi bɔda
si ákana na énwini ɔnundane.
Ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na lɛkana linye lɛsiaku bekyuli
bani mɔɔtu-mi kenye na beedie-mi bɔƒiɔ.
12Ukyuli ɔbuni ɔni mɔɔsia lɛlɔ
anu ni,
ɔɔkana na ɔɔnu ɔgbankpi
ɔni ndubo ubalɛ teemene na ɔɔgyumana lɛlɔ.
Nsu bekyuli bani na bana kasusu kásɔ ni,
baakɛ gyoli gyoli teetéduo ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kemmo.
13Sia anumi na aƒɔ lɛla lɛdi enyene kama asiku ukyuli
ɔni muunye ɔƒɔ ɔdi kayu kenye kudɔ.
Na si uleku ɔsɔnɔdine kayu kenye na ukyuli ɔdi ɔnii uunye ni,
ya na ɔka kayu kadi bɔƒɔ buse.
14Si áta ɔtanta tutuutu na aakpali ƒula ɔdukɛne
na aava teegyele-nwu ni,
ɔdubuti-nwu kɔnyi mmomu.
15Uleku unyeyɔne lɛlɔ liiƒí livo teetulo ɔnantu wɛɛwɛɛ
ɔni náƒɔ kadi limeyi limodi.
16Na si anii aabala-nwu ni, ubo ɔkplu utulo ka
abala ɔƒɛƒɛɛ na ɔda bukpo ɔya,
iye eti kɔnu edu nnɔ ada.
17Kalɛ na lɛbuala lɛɛdɔ́ lɛbuala ni,
lɛni kani na ɔkpana ɔɔklibi ɔkpana.
18Kabla bablane bani mɔɔnu kɔdingyii kɔdi lɛlɔ
bebo kuƒi ka badi-ku ebi.
Lɛni kani na kabla bablane
bani mɔɔgyumana
kabla ɔlati ɔdi kabla ka
katɛ ni,
badubo lɛyuƒɔla bɔƒɔ.
19Kalɛ na ukyuli ɔkana na ɔnu nwuna anumi na ntu kemmo ni,
lɛni kani na ukyuli kayi keedie ukyuli umodi ɔmmɔ udu taatina.
20Kukpi ku lɛla lɛni mɔɔyila lɛla lɛdi udu belemo.
Lɛni kani na kayawi ala ani mɔɔda ukyuli ɔkwɛ elemo-nwu.
21Ogya kemmo baakya sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi
taanu-nwu bɔdia.
Lɛni kani na ukyuli bumwi buudie nwuna udu taatina.
22Si éti badɔlɔdi éwi kaawɛ kemmo
na égyuo-ma muedi ni,
alakana bana kɔdɔlɔ bule bɔsiku bana kɔdɔlɔ kudɔ.
23Sia ƒula bebuo anumi kaduɛ
na eti ƒula kayi ƒui anu-ma lɛlɔ.
24Ɔsika lɛlakɛ lilese uwi ƒui.
Na kagabwa lɛnɔ kelébi ukyuli lili taasi kaba útédu kaba.
25Si ékulo bebuo livo aklibi ese kama ni,
anwu asa adubɔkɛ adila ete-ma,
26na ƒula baƒonu badubɔbla linwini yuu na bedi adi.
Na adubuye ƒula bese lɛnɔ na eti eye katumalɔ.
27Na bese bammɔ badubɔyu anyi ntu pii
bete awɔ ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli ku kabla bablane.

english_text:
The Law of God Makes Sense
1Wicked people run away
when no one chases them,
but those who live right
are as brave as lions.
2In time of civil war
there are many leaders,
but a sensible leader
restores law and order.
3When someone poor takes over
and mistreats the poor,
it's like a heavy rain
destroying the crops.
4Lawbreakers praise criminals,
but law-abiding citizens
always oppose them.
5Criminals don't know
what justice means,
but all who respect the Lord
understand it completely.
6It's better to be poor
and live right,
than to be rich
and dishonest.
7It makes good sense
to obey the Law of God,
but you disgrace your parents
if you make friends
with worthless nobodies.
8If you make money by charging
high interest rates,
you will lose it all to someone
who cares for the poor.
9God cannot stand the prayers
of anyone who disobeys
his Law.
10By leading good people to sin,
you dig a pit for yourself,
but all who live right
will have a bright future.
11The rich think highly
of themselves,
but anyone poor and sensible
sees right through them.
12When an honest person wins,
it's time to celebrate;
when crooks are in control,
it's best to hide.
13If you don't confess your sins,
you will be a failure.
But God will be merciful
if you confess your sins
and give them up.
14The Lord blesses everyone
who is afraid to do evil,
but if you are cruel,
you will end up in trouble.
15A ruler who mistreats the poor
is like a roaring lion
or a bear hunting for food.
16A heartless leader is a fool,
but anyone who refuses
to get rich by cheating others
will live a long time.
17Don't give help to murderers!
Make them stay on the run
for as long as they live.
18Honesty will keep you safe,
but everyone who is crooked
will suddenly fall.
19Work hard, and you will have
a lot of food;
waste time, and you will have
a lot of trouble.
20God blesses his loyal people,
but punishes all who want
to get rich quick.
21It isn't right to be unfair,
but some people can be bribed
with only a piece of bread.
22Don't be selfish
and eager to get rich—
you will end up worse off
than you can imagine.
23Honest correction
is appreciated
more than flattery.
24If you cheat your parents
and don't think it's wrong,
you are a common thief.
25Selfish people cause trouble,
but you will live a full life
if you trust the Lord.
26Only fools would trust
what they alone think,
but if you live by wisdom,
you will do all right.
27Giving to the poor
will keep you from poverty,
but if you close your eyes
to their needs,
everyone will curse you.
28When crooks are in control,
everyone tries to hide,
but when they lose power,
good people are everywhere.
translation_text:
1Ukyuli ɔdi ulábɔku bekyuli
bekpidi asa na ama
alati beekeli.
Nsu bekyuli babuni baakya kayi aani bagyata.
2Si ala bɔbla kalɛ kalɛ bɔ́ƒɔ
kalɔ kadi aban lɛgadi
kemmo ni,
baavumana lɛlɔ badine
uwi ndi uwi.
Nsu batɔnkune bani náda anu
na bebo lɛlati ni,
baayá na lɛla biala lɛɛbla siin.
3Lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔni mɔɔnya bawabane taakya ni,
use aani ɔnantu ɔni mɔɔna taavili na uubile edula.
4Bekyuli bani muuní ɔda bubo ni,
ama muumwi bekyuli bekpidi.
Nsu bekyuli bani mɔɔdi ɔda bubo lɛlɔ balátunaku-ma.
5Bekyuli bekpidi belenu ala bɔbla ulu lɛlɔ kalɔ.
Nsu bani mɔɔsiaku Unwoti kama geen ni,
beenú ɔmɛni kalɔ nwaa.
6Ɔdia si adi ɔwabane na aabla ala ulu lɛlɔ siin,
utulo si adi ɔlakɛne na udunkpi ɔ́ƒɔ-ɔ keliela kemmo.
7Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdi ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ɔdi ubi ɔni mɔɔdá anu.
Nsu ubi ɔni mɔɔdiku bakpana bekpidi ku badivone kɔkpana ni,
ɔɔkya ɔti kɔƒa.
8Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla egulabi
na bekyuli bamba lɛlɔ
ɔkɛnku kuvonsia bonwu
ɔsu ni,
lɛkɛ lɛmmɔ lɛdubɔyii-nwu kɔnu
lisie ukyuli ɔni mbo lɛƒɔndia
ute bawabane kudɔ.
9Unwoti ulenu bekyuli bani naaadi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ
ina baakpali-nwu.
10Bekyuli bani mɔɔtɔ́lɔ bekyuli bani nse siin
taatákya likpidi kemmo ni,
ama alati bana kakpagyuɛ ndubo-ma budie.
11Balakɛne baanu lɛlɔ aani banundane kalɛ,
nsu bawabane baanu bana ayaki taati nwaa.
12Si ala aadianku bekyuli babuni ni, lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ukyuli biala.
Nsu si bekyuli bekpidi benye ala kenye ni, ukyuli biala ɔɔbɛ́.
13Bekyuli bani muuti ala teebi bana ekpidi ni,
ala aládianku-ma.
Nsu si bédie-nya kalɔ na béni-nya ni,
Unwoti ɔdubɔnu-ma kɔnyana.
14Kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku bekyuli bani na bana kasusu kese siin.
Nsu belikplune bésela betéduo ɔgbankpi bonwu kemmo.
15Ukyuli ukpidi ɔni mɔɔdi bekyuli lɛlɔ ni,
ɔdanku ɔgbankpi bonwu ute bawabane
aani kalɛ na ebuo ukpidi uuƒie bekyuli.
16Ɔgadine ɔni na ɔ́dɔlɔ kani mɔɔnya nwuna bekyuli taakya.
Nsu ɔga ɔni na ukisi si ukyuli uládi litemi geen lɛlɔ
iye ɔɔbɛ́ taaƒɔ ala bekyuli kudɔ ni, uulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ.
17Bekyuli ɔdune ɔni kasusu muukpóku-nwu ni,
kaakpanku-nwu teetéduo kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo.
Tada-nwu ulu!
18Bekyuli babuni ni, Unwoti ɔdubudie-ma,
na lɛla lɛdi lilabla-ma.
Nsu bani na bana kasiakɔ kese gontii ni,
Unwoti ɔdubɔyila-ma udu.
19Bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla kpakplaa
bebo adila pii na badi bemo.
Nsu si éni kabla na akɛ eebile uwi taavi ni,
ayaki adubɔda-a.
20Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔsia ala anu taabla-nya ulu lɛlɔ ni,
ɔdubɔkɛ lɛyuƒɔla bonwu.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia ka unwini ɔlakɛne kɔnakunwi ni,
ɔdubuduo ɔgbankpi kemmo.
21Bekyuli anumi bɔnu taatu ala teenwini
ɔɔɔdia munu munu.
Nsu badi baaadaku-ni ka baƒɔ bodobodo kakɛ blii suɛ
na batuna babla likpidi.
22Ukyuli ɔni mbo sika lɛnungyie mɔɔwia ka ɔkɛ lɛkɛ pla,
nsu ɔɔɔgyi ka kɔwaba kemmo na úsela utéduo.
23Na lɛla biala kawɔlɔkɔ ni,
bekyuli baayɔ́ lɛla bɔsu bɔlɛku nwaa
utulo katɔlɔ bumwi.
24Bawɔne buyu na asu anini,
“Ɔmmɔ útebile lɛla lɛdi” ni,
use aani ukyuli bɔdu.
25Sika lɛnungyie muuboku kekpo.
Na anu buti bɔsia Unwoti lɛlɔ
mɔɔyá na keyi kaadianku ukyuli.
26Kɔdɔlɔ kɔdi ukyuli ɔni mɔɔkali ɔnii uláwia bɔlɛ.
Nsu bani mɔɔda lɛlɔ na lɛnunda kemmo ni, keliela kaatɛ-ma.
27Ukyuli ɔni muute bawabane ala ulayaki lɛla lɛdi.
Nsu ewida adubɔsiaku bekyuli bani mɔɔnu bawabane teedie lili.
28Si belikplune baadi bekyuli
lɛlɔ ni,
bɔbɛ na bekyuli baabɛ́.
Nsu si belikplune básiaku ɔgbankpi ni,
bekyuli bani nse siin beemomo.

english_text:
Use Good Sense
1If you keep being stubborn
after many warnings,
you will suddenly discover
you have gone too far.
2When justice rules a nation,
everyone is glad;
when injustice rules,
everyone groans.
3If you love wisdom
your parents will be glad,
but chasing after bad women
will cost you everything.
4An honest ruler
makes the nation strong;
a ruler who takes bribes
will bring it to ruin.
5Flattery is nothing less
than setting a trap.
6Your sins will catch you,
but everyone who lives right
will sing and celebrate.
7The wicked don't care
about the rights of the poor,
but good people do.
8Sneering at others is a spark
that sets a city on fire;
using good sense can put out
the flames of anger.
9Be wise and don't sue a fool.
You won't get satisfaction,
because all the fool will do
is sneer and shout.
10A murderer hates everyone
who is honest
and lives right.
11Don't be a fool
and quickly lose your temper—
be sensible and patient.
12A ruler who listens to lies
will have corrupt officials.
13The poor and all who abuse them
must each depend on God
for light.
14Kings who are fair to the poor
will rule a long time.
15Correct your children,
and they will be wise;
children out of control
disgrace their mothers.
16Crime increases
when crooks are in power,
but law-abiding citizens
will see them fall.
17If you correct your children,
they will bring you peace
and happiness.
18Without guidance from God
law and order disappear,
but God blesses everyone
who obeys his Law.
19 Even when servants are smart,
it takes more than words
to make them obey.
20There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who speaks
without thinking.
21Slaves that you treat kindly
from their childhood
will cause you sorrow.
22A person with a quick temper
stirs up arguments
and commits a lot of sins.
23Too much pride brings disgrace;
humility leads to honor.
24If you take part in a crime
you are your worst enemy,
because even under oath
you can't tell the truth.
25Don't fall into the trap
of being a coward—
trust the Lord,
and you will be safe.
26Many try to make friends
with a ruler,
but justice comes
from the Lord.
27Good people and criminals
can't stand each other.
translation_text:
1Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla atuɔkplu na úni ɔnii
ukyuli ɔdi utedie-nwu bɔƒiɔ ni,
ɔdubo lɛlɔ udu bɔyila
na ɔdi ɔsɔ ulakana-nwu bɔbwi.
2Si ala aatɛku bekyuli babuni ni,
bekyuli baakɛ́ lɛlɔyɔ.
Nsu si bekyuli bekpidi mɔɔdi bekyuli lɛlɔ ni,
bekyuli beedumo.
3Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ lɛnunda ni, lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ɔti.
Nsu si anwu ku beleku bayalɛ mɔɔví ni,
nwuna lɛlakɛ lilélie.
4Ɔga ɔni mɔɔdi bekyuli lɛlɔ ulu lɛlɔ siin ni,
