ɔɔyá nwuna kalɔ keesé kpoo na baakɛ́ atu bɔyɔ.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia ka utaaƒɔ ala bekyuli kudɔ
na bɔbɛ kemmo taadi uwi ndi uwi ni,
uubile kalɔ kammɔ.
5Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnyi ɔkɔ teemwi ukyuli ni,
kakpagyuɛ na ɔɔkywɛ-nwu ka ɔnu-ka kemmo.
6Bekyuli bekpidi ni, bana likpidi kakpagyuɛ muudie-ma.
Nsu bekyuli bani nse siin ni, baakɛ́ lɛlɔyɔ ku kudu.
7Bekyuli babuni baasia anu ka babla
ala ulu lɛlɔ siin bete bawabane,
nsu bekyuli bekpidi baaadaku ɔmmɔ.
8Bekyuli bani muudumi bekyuli taama baakya ɔma lɛsɛ.
Nsu banundane ama ni, baayila kɔnyi ala ƒui.
9Si ɔnundane úti ɔdɔlɔdi úsienku litemi katɛkɔ ni,
kɔvanu kukpludi ku kɔdɔlɔ ala kani
na mɔɔlɛ́ ɔdɔlɔdi ɔmmɔ kenye
na uléboku keyi buɛɛ.
10Bekyuli bani mɔɔwia ka bewi ubugya kalɔ
bekisi bekyuli bani mɔɔdi litemi geen lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.
Na baawia ka badu bekyuli bani nse siin.
11Ɔdɔlɔdi uuti kɔnyi taayila kalɔ na ulanu kama.
Nsu ɔnundane anwu ɔɔda lɛlɔ na ɔɔbɛla nwuna kɔnyi.
12Si lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔdi ɔɔbu ɔkɔ banyine ni,
nwuna kasusu bakyane ƒui badubunwini belikplune.
13Bawabane ku bekyuli bani mɔɔnya-ma taakya ƒui ni,
badanku lɛla linwi lɛdi lɛni ndi ka
Unwoti úti anumi ani mɔɔnu bukeye úte bana inyɔ.
14Ɔga ɔni mɔɔtɛ bawabane litemi ulu siin lɛlɔ ni,
nwuna lɛgadi liinye kpakplaa teetu uwi.
15Si ada kegyimi aatumini ubi
na aadɔnku-nwu kpakplaa ni, ɔɔdá anu.
Nsu ubi ɔni na bédie atu na ulie úte nwuna lɛlɔ ni,
ɔɔyá na kɔƒa kuukpó uni.
16Si bekyuli bekpidi baalɛ́ lili ni,
lɛni kani na likpidi bɔbla bɔɔkɔ́ katɔ.
Nsu bekyuli bani nse siin badubulie
na banu kalɛ na belikplune bammɔ beebó kalɔ.
17Tumini ƒula bebi kaduɛ na badubɔya na akɛ atu bɔyɔ.
Na badubɔya ƒula kɔyu lɛlɔyɔ.
18Si bekyuli bátanu budie bɔtina bɔdi ni,
beení ka bunyimi bɔdi bɔdi-ma lɛlɔ.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-nwu.
19Kabla ɔblane ni, ɔɔɔdi kenye etemila kani na beeti taaklibi-nwu,
ɔsika ina ka uunú-nya kalɔ ni, ulábla taasiaku lɛni.
20Áasia anu ánu kenye ɔkplu ukyuli ɔdi dii?
Baakana na baasia ɔdɔlɔdi muedi lɛnu
teetulo ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu.
21Si ákya kabla ɔblane ásiku lɛnamu uwi ni,
ɔdubo ubaya na kɔnyana kuƒie-ɔ kama.
22Ukyuli ɔni muuti kɔnyi pla pla ni, ɔɔkya kekpo.
Na kɔnyi kɔmmɔ kɔɔyá na ɔɔbla ekpidi lidu lidu.
23Ukyuli lɛlɔ katɔ bɔkɔliku muuboku nwuna kalɔ bubo.
Na si éboku lɛlɔ kalɔ ni, bekyuli badubɔbu-ɔ na aƒɔ lɛnyi.
24Ukyuli ɔni nébunku uyune ni, anwu ɔlati muukisi lɛlɔ.
Ɔsika ulakana kenye buse na ɔsu lɛla lɛni nálɛ.
25Si ada lɛlɔ na bekyuli lɛlɔ liƒu ɔsu ni,
akya ɔgbankpi bonwu ɔdi kemmo.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni néti anu ásia Unwoti lɛlɔ ni,
lɛla biala lilékpoku-nwu
26Bekyuli pii baawia ka bada bana litemi bava lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔdi anumi.
Nsu litemi bɔtɛ ulu siin lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti kudɔ na ɔɔsí.
27Bekyuli babuni balayɔ bekyuli bekpidi.
Na bekyuli bekpidi lɛnɔ balayɔ bekyuli babuni.

english_text:
The Sayings of Agur
1These are the sayings
and the message
of Agur son of Jakeh.
Someone cries out to God,
“I am completely worn out!
How can I last?
2I am far too stupid
to be considered human.
3I never was wise,
and I don't understand
what God is like.”
4 Has anyone gone up to heaven
and come back down?
Has anyone grabbed hold
of the wind?
Has anyone wrapped up the sea
or marked out boundaries
for the earth?
If you know of any
who have done such things,
then tell me their names
and their children's names.
5Everything God says is true—
and it's a shield for all
who come to him for safety.
6Don't change what God has said!
He will correct you and show
that you are a liar.
7There are two things, Lord,
I want you to do for me
before I die:
8Make me absolutely honest
and don't let me be too poor
or too rich.
Give me just what I need.
9If I have too much to eat,
I might forget about you;
if I don't have enough,
I might steal
and disgrace your name.
10Don't tell a slave owner
something bad about one
of the slaves.
That slave will curse you,
and you will be in trouble.
11Some people curse their father
and even their mother;
12others think they are perfect,
but they are stained by sin.
13Some people are stuck-up
and act like snobs;
14others are so greedy
that they gobble up
the poor and homeless.
15Greed has twins,
each named “Give me!”
There are three or four things
that are never satisfied:
16The world of the dead
and a childless wife,
the thirsty earth
and a flaming fire.
17Don't make fun of your father
or disobey your mother—
crows will peck out your eyes,
and buzzards will eat
the rest of you.
18There are three or four things
I cannot understand:
19 How eagles fly so high
or snakes crawl on rocks,
how ships sail the ocean
or people fall in love.
20An unfaithful wife says,
“Sleeping with another man
is as natural as eating.”
21There are three or four things
that make the earth tremble
and are unbearable:
22A slave who becomes king,
a fool who eats too much,
23a hateful woman
who finds a husband,
and a slave who takes the place
of the woman who owns her.
24On this earth four things
are small but very wise:
25Ants, who seem to be feeble,
but store up food
all summer long;
26badgers, who seem to be weak,
but live among the rocks;
27locusts, who have no king,
but march like an army;
28lizards, which can be caught
in your hand,
but sneak into palaces.
29Three or four creatures
really strut around:
30Those fearless lions
who rule the jungle,
31those proud roosters,
those mountain goats,
and those rulers
who have no enemies.
32If you are foolishly bragging
or planning something evil,
then stop it now!
33If you churn milk
you get butter;
if you pound on your nose,
you get blood—
and if you stay angry,
you get in trouble.
translation_text:
Agur Úbo Agba
1Yake ubidi Agur ɔ́su kenye kadi úse. Ɔ́su Itiel lɛla lɛdi. Na ɔ́su Itiel ku Ukal ɔnini,
“Lɛlɔ lítu-mi, O Katɔti,
na lɛ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.
2“Ami ndi bekyuli ƒui akɔ ukyuli ɔni na ɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛdi.
Na liiibo ala kalɔ bunu bɔni na bekyuli bebo.
3Ńtatɛya lɛnunda lɛla lɛdi,
iye lɛlati lɛdi na anwu ɔni nse kedee mmɔ lɛlɔ.
4Ɔma nákɔ úsie katɔ na ɔ́sɔ únwini úbo?
Na ɔma násala ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔ́kya nwuna lɛkɔkɔ kemmo?
Ɔma násala ntu ƒui ɔ́kya nwuna awu bonwu
ɔni mbi-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo?
Na ɔma nátu kalɔ kammɔ
lɛvi ƒui
únyene kalɔ útédu kana kawɔlɔkɔ?
Dɛ na baalɔ anwu ku ubidi?
Su-mi si agyi!
5“Lɛla biala na Unwoti ɔ́su ni, ɔkɔ uuubo-nwu kemmo.
Ɔdi lɛgyumanala ute bani nátamiku-nwu.
6Teti lɛla bamba lɛdi tebunku nwuna etemila lɛlɔ.
Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, ɔdubɔdɔnku-ɔ na enwini ɔkɔ ɔnyine.
7“O Unwoti, alakpa anyɔ adi kani na muuvele-ɔ.
Na teni-mi ala ammɔ bute asa likpi.
8Die katuala ku ɔkɔ bɔnyi mina lɛlɔ ƒui.
Tete-mi kɔwaba, na tete-mi lɛkɛ lɛnɔ.
Mmomu te-mi mina limeyi adila kani.
9Ɔsika ɔƒɛni kalɛ lɛ́kɛ lɛmmɔ lɛdubumo-mi lɛvili
na lini-ɔ,
na ndubuye nnini,
‘Ɔma ndi Unwoti?’
Na si kɔwaba lɛnɔ nda-mi
kɔ́vili ni,
ɔƒɛni kalɛ ndubo buyu
na bekyuli balabu mina Katɔti lɛnyi kedee.
10“Tebile kabla ɔblane ɔdi tete nwuna ɔtɔlati.
Si ábla lɛni ni, ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔdubo-ɔ buwida
na adubɔƒɔ lɛla lɛmmɔ kayu.
11“Bekyuli badi beewida bana bati,
na belete bana beni kusɛ kusɛ.
12Baanu lɛlɔ ka badia bagya nsu geen ni,
beesé lɛlɔ geen na bátalɛ bɔkpi.
13Baakɔliku lɛlɔ katɔ
teetuloku lɛlɔ
na baanu lɛla biala tapii.
14Bana kenye anyi etulo kuwii,
na lɛsika blii yayaaya nlɛ-ma linungla,
kalɛ na baduli bawabane bebweli balɛku kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.
Na bayila bani ƒui mɔɔyaki ala balɛku bayawine akɔ.
15“Ntu kebweyi kadi kakya na kebo bebi belekubi inyɔ.
Ama bana keku kani ndi
‘Te-mi! Te-mi!’
“Alakpa atɛ adi akya na elemo kudii.
Na ene adi aaagyi bɔsu anii, ‘Ɔ́bɔ!’
16Kaƒiɔtɔ ku udinkɔ
ku kalɔ kani na ntu bulaƒɔ-ka kudii
ku ogya ɔni mɔɔkywí teebile ala na ulásu ɔnii, ‘Ɔ́bɔ!’
17“Anumi ani mɔɔnu ɔti ɔnusɛ teedumi
na ulánu ɔnii ɔ́manku ka unu uni litemi ni,
baasɛ bekpidi bani nkya kɔwɛ kemmo
ndubo bebedie-ma anumi na livuo kemmo
na begbini baduli-ma bebweli ƒui.
18“Na alakpa atɛ adi akya na ana lɛlɔ lɛɛbla-mi dɛye dɛye.
Na ene adi anya neeenu-nya kalɔ.
19Kalɛ na kɔdigbo aasɛ uuveyi taavi kayaa,
ku kalɛ na kɔlakpi kuusié taavi lɛtakpɛ lɛlɔ,
ku kalɛ na ɔkɔlɔ bonwu ɔɔkɛ́ kasiakɔ na ntu anumi,
ku kalɛ na ɔnana kayi kaayɔ́ uleku.
20“Na ɔni nsɔ mɔɔbla-mi yaa ndi
kalɛ na uleku ɔsɔnɔdine ɔɔbla ala.
Kalɛ na ɔɔdi teeni kenye
na ɔsu ɔnii, ‘Ńtabla lɛla likpidi lɛdi.’
21“Alakpa atɛ adi aakya kalɔ liƒu kpakpaakpa,
na ene kalɔ na ulakana lɛlɔ budie.
22Ukyuli ɔdi kabla ɔblane ɔni nénwini kadi ɔga
ku ɔdɔlɔdi ɔni mbo adila pii geen
23Kalɛ na uleku ɔni na bekyuli balayɔ ɔɔkɛ́ kɔgya.
Kalɛ na ulekubi kabla ɔblane ɔɔƒɔ́ nwuna kɔduni ɔgya teelieku.
24“Alakpa ene adi akya kayawi na ese blii suɛ,
nsu ana lɛnunda lísie ɔgyu geen.
25Balalɛ badi bebuo bani neeebo ɔlɔkplu,
nsu baaklibi adila teese lɛlɔ na kaƒɛndi.
26Besi udu bebuo badi bakya na beeebo ɔyikun,
nsu beedie libu na atakpɛ kemmo na baakɛ́ keliekɔ.
27Baalɔlɔ beeebo ɔga,
nsu baakɛ otogyi buni kemmo atɔ asia.
28Basamuda belede buƒie,
nsu adubɔnu-ma na baga lɛgbanya.
29“Na alakpa atɛ adi akya kayawi na bana bɔnya bɔɔtina lɛgadi.
Na ene mɔɔkɛ na lɛgadi kemmo.
30Gyata, bebuo ƒui ɔga
ɔni na lɛla biala lilagyila-nwu ɔtɔtɔ na usie kama.
31Akɔkɔ ɔgyani ku ketukpa
ku ɔga ɔni na nwuna bekpone báka bámana-nwu.
32“Si ábla adɔlɔla na ákun lɛmɛnɛ
iye eeti likpidi kasusu ni,
tebo kɔnu kayi!
Ti enu bi kenye ku kɔƒa.
33Kalɛ na si eebó akɔ lɛnyi ntu na uumi taayu ɔkplu,
na si lɛla lɛdi lɛ́wɔ-ɔ enwu na ɔɔdá ni,
lɛni kani na kɔnyi kuuboku kadɔ.”

english_text:
What King Lemuel's Mother Taught Him
1These are the sayings
that King Lemuel of Massa
was taught by his mother.
2My son Lemuel, you were born
in answer to my prayers,
so listen carefully.
3Don't waste your life
chasing after women!
This has ruined many kings.
4Kings and leaders
should not get drunk
or even want to drink.
5Drinking makes you forget
your responsibilities,
and you mistreat the poor.
6Beer and wine are only
for the dying or for those
who have lost all hope.
7Let them drink and forget
how poor and miserable
they feel.
8But you must defend
those who are helpless
and have no hope.
9Be fair and give justice
to the poor and homeless.
In Praise of a Good Wife
10A truly good wife
is the most precious treasure
a man can find!
11Her husband depends on her,
and she never
lets him down.
12She is good to him
every day of her life,
13and with her own hands
she gladly makes clothes.
14She is like a sailing ship
that brings food
from across the sea.
15She gets up before daylight
to prepare food for her family
and for her servants.
16She knows how to buy land
and how to plant a vineyard,
17and she always works hard.
18She knows when to buy or sell,
and she stays busy
until late at night.
19She spins her own cloth,
20and she helps the poor
and the needy.
21Her family has warm clothing,
and so she doesn't worry
when it snows.
22She does her own sewing,
and everything she wears
is beautiful.
23Her husband is a well-known
and respected leader
in the city.
24She makes clothes to sell
to the shop owners.
25She is strong and graceful,
as well as cheerful
about the future.
26Her words are sensible,
and her advice
is thoughtful.
27She takes good care
of her family
and is never lazy.
28Her children praise her,
and with great pride
her husband says,
29“There are many good women,
but you are the best!”
30Charm can be deceiving,
and beauty fades away,
but a woman
who honors the Lord
deserves to be praised.
31Show her respect—
praise her in public
for what she has done.
translation_text:
Ɔga Lemuel Ɔ́tɛmi Asugba
1Ala ani bɔdubo bunu mɛni ndi lɛsuse na Masa Ɔga Lemuel lɛlɔ lɛni na uni ɔ́tina-nwu.
2“O mina ubi, mina kaƒɔ ubi,
ubi ɔni lɛlɔ na líse kenye,
3tebile ƒula ɔyikun na beleku lɛlɔ
na ayila ƒula ɔlɔkplu na ama bani muubó baga muedi kalɔ lɛlɔ.
4“Lɛla lɛdi lɛkya na lɛɛɛdia liiite baga.
Lemuel, ɔɔɔdia uuute baga ka bataani ntɛ.
Útalɛka ntɛ butaada batɔnkune ɔkwɛ.
5Ɔsika si báni ntɛ ni, ɔƒɛni kalɛ badubɔyiƒala
lɛla lɛni na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔtina
na balakana litemi bɔtɛ budie
bani na baanya taakya na bakɛ bana kuƒi kadikɔ.
6Nyonu ntɛ te bani néedu kaƒiɔtɔ kɔtu,
ama mɔɔní ntɛ ku bani na kayi kaakpulu-ma geen.
7Ya na bekyuli bammɔ udu bani ntɛ na bayiƒala bana kɔwaba
na basɔ beléteenyimo ala ani muukpóku-ma.
8“Nye bani naaakana bɔtɛmi kenye na atɛmi ete-ma.
Na bawabane bani neeebo lɛla lɛdi bɔbla
bakɛ bana kuƒi ƒaa.
9Geen ni, tɛmi na atɛ litemi na ulu siin lɛlɔ,
na edie bawabane ku bani neeebo bebunkune.”
Uleku Ɔni Mbo Udu Buni Mɔɔbla Uleku Ɔbuni
10Ɔma ndubɔkɛ uleku ɔbuni?
Uleku ɔmmɔ udu ɔ́ƒɔ kuye utulo sika asɛɛ ani náƒɔ kuye geen.
11Ɔgyani ɔdubuti nwuna anu ƒui ɔsia-nwu lɛlɔ.
Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ulayaki lɛla lɛbuni lɛdi.
12Ɔdubɔya na ɔgyani ɔkɛ lɛbuni
na ulabla-nwu ukpidi ɔdi nwuna ngba uwi ƒui.
13Ɔɔƒuna bebuo linwini ku unwo ɔbuni
na nwuna enu alanɔ ala budi uwi ɔdi.
14Use aani beyedine ɔkɔlɔ
ɔni mɔɔsíku edula ɔgyu teeboku kaduli.
15Ɔɔta ɔtanta tutuutu uwi ɔni na kadi kátada tɔ
na ɔɔbla lɛdila teete nwuna kaduli bekyuli,
na uute nwuna kaduli kabla bablane belekubi
bana limeyi kabla.
16Uusié taatávi taanu mmo
na uye bɔni ndia.
Na kɔsia bamba kɔni na
ɔɔkɛ́ ni,
uuti-ku teese kemo.
17Uusé nwuna kabla kalɔ ku ogya,
na lɛlɔ lɛ́sa-nwu
na ubo ɔlɔkplu ute nwuna kabla.
18Ɔɔsia nwuna kabla kani mete-nwu kɔsia anu kaduɛ.
Na nwuna asogya uleni usien uwi ɔdi.
19Nwuna enu eeebo bɔnwuna na unwo bɔta lɛlɔ,
na nwuna animi aatu kedetila uwi ndi uwi.
20Ɔɔnu bawabane kɔnyana
na bekyuli bani mɔɔyaki lɛla lɛdi ni,
uute-ma ala.
21Liƒu liláda-nwu si kɔyɔ uwi ɔdubo,
ɔsika ubo kɔyɔ adala ute nwuna kaduli bekyuli.
22Uudí ala ani na ɔɔvá nwuna katɛnkɔ.
Na ɔɔda lɛlɔ ku adi ani na áƒɔ kuye geen.
23Bekyuli baabu ɔgyani kaduɛ
na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔban kenye
kesii kani na baasa, ɔsika ɔdi ukyuli
ɔni mɔɔkya kadi benengu kasusu bakyane akɔ.
24Na ulekudi uudí lɛwu gyɔlɔɔ lɛbuni
lɛni na bákya-ni bɔdia kaduɛ teeye
ku lɛwu lidu lidu bamba teete beyedine lɛnɔ.
25Si ánu uleku ɔmmɔ ni, aanu ka
ubo ɔbu ku ɔyikun.
Ɔƒɛni si ɔɔmá ni, aatí ka
liƒu lɛdi liiibo-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo na uwi ɔni mebo lɛlɔ.
26Ɔɔtɛmi lɛnunda etemila,
na ɔɔlɛ ukyuli ku lɛƒɔndia na ulu geen ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.
27Na ɔɔsia lɛla biala mɔɔlɛ́ na nwuna kaduli anu kaduɛ,
na ulákya enu lɛgba akɔ taakɛ nwuna lɛdila.
28Nwuna bebi baalɔ-nwu lɛnyi teete kusɛ kusɛ.
Lɛni kani na ɔgyani ɔɔtɛmi-nwu lɛlɔ kɔtɛ
na uumwi-nwu ɔnini,
29“Beleku babuni bakya kayawi na baada kaduli,
nsu awɔ ƒula udu ɔɔɔbɔ!”
30Ala ani mɔɔda kayi aatɔ́lɔ ukyuli.
Na uleku bɔdia bɔnu bulétu uwi.
Nsu uleku ɔni mɔɔyia Unwoti ni,
ɔlɛka bemwi-nwu.
31Ƒɔ uleku ɔmmɔ udu kayu na ala ani na ɔ́bla kenye.
Na nwuna kabla alati kebo-nwu kudu
na ɔma bekyuli ƒui akɔ.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
1Ala ɔtinane ɔni ndi Ɔga Dawid ubidi ɔni nádi lɛga na Yerusalem etemila ani na ɔ́su ndi ani na bɔdubo bunu mɛni.
Lɛla Biala Liiibo Na Ukyuli Adubɔkana-ni Kalɔ Budie Geen Bɔwɔlɔ
2Ala ɔtinane ɔmɛni ɔɔsu ɔnini,
“Lɛla biala liiibo kalɔ budie geen bɔdi,
mmomu ala ƒui ese-bu suu geen!”
3Bi ndi ukyuli kɔsia
na nwuna lɛbibo kanaa kama?
4Kaba kaba béebo bátɔlɔ,
nsu alanu lɛla lɛdi bɔvumana geen lɛni.
5Ɔƒɛ ɔɔtu taatánu
na ɔsɔ ɔɔsí taabatu lɛnɔ.
6Na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ uukpó teesie katɔ ku kada
ku ɔƒɛnyi ɔni ku ɔni,
na ɔɔkya ligede teesie teebo
nsu ulesie kesii kadi.
7Ntukpa bɔɔgbá teetéduo ɛpu kemmo
nsu ɛpu uleyi kudii.
Ɔmmɔ kama ntu bɔmmɔ bɔsɔ buunwíni teesie taatágba
taasi ntukpa bɔni kemmo na bɔ́si teebeduo ɛpu kemmo.
8Lɛla biala ni, bɔnɔ ku lɛlɔ butu kani na bɔdi!
Ina bi na bɔ́nu ni, uledu bula anumi ɔkwɛ.
Na ina bi etemila na búnu
lɛnɔ ni,
bula atu eléyii na bɔnɔ bunu.
9Ánu dii etemila ni, ala kama bɔsia kani na bɔdi.
Ana ƒui áalɛ dii.
Lɛla lɛwɔdi lɛdi liiibo ɔƒɛ kalɔ kesii kadi
na lɛdi lɛla lɛni na lítebo tɔ kudii.
10Lɛla lɛdi lɛkya na ukyuli ɔdi ɔdubɔkana na ɔsu ɔnini,
“Bɛnu! Aanu lɛla lɛwɔdi mɛni?”
Lɛkya ɔ́si kukuuku,
na líitu uwi asa na bula uwi úbo.
11Bula ɔdi ɔsɔ ulenyimo kuuku uwi ala ani nébo ábavi.
Lɛni kani na bula bawɔ bawɔ bani mebo dii limeyi lɛdi
basɔ belenyimo bula ala ani na bɔ́bla.
Ukyuli Lɛnunda Lɛ́sɔ Na Lítedu Lítawɔlɔ
12Ami ndi ala ɔtinane ɔni nélie Yerusalem, na lɛ́di lɛga na Israel ƒui lɛlɔ. 13Líti mina uwi líte ka lɛwia ala kalɔ linu na liti lɛnunda kemmo liduo ala ani mɔɔlɛ́ kayawi kamɛni kemmo ƒui lɛti. Ńtesie ɔgyu asa na lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka bɔnɔ etila lɛka na Katɔti údi ɔ́sia bayawine kaba bekyuli ƒui lili. 14Lɛla biala na lɛkya ɔƒɛ ɔmɛni kalɔ liiibo ukyuli kalɔ budie geen bɔdi. Buse na use aani kalɛ na ukyuli ɔɔbi taasiaku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ.
15Lɛla lɛni na líbie ni, ukyuli ulakana-ni bɔklibi.
Na lɛla lɛni na lɛ́yii lɛ́kya-nwu lɛnɔ ni, ɔsɔ ulanu-ni.
16Lɛ́kali ala adi lɛ́nu na lɛ́su lɛlɔ nnini, “Nu, mbo lɛnunda ntulo ɔga bamba biala nélie Yerusalem asa na líbo. Lɛ́da anu na ngyi lɛla ntulo bana ƒui. 17Ɔmmɔ ɔsu líkpoku lɛlɔ nnii muudie kavumana kani nkya lɛnunda ku kɔdɔlɔ ntɛ keyi. Nsu ɔƒɛni mɔɔnu taati ka ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ úlieku ka ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kani na lɛ́bi nsiaku.”
18Ɔsika kalɛ mɔɔnu ka mina lɛnunda líisie ɔgyu ni,
lɛni kani na mina bɔnɔ lɛnɔ bɔɔkɔ́ katɔ.
Na si ukyuli ɔnii ɔ́da anu ni,
kɔnyana ku lɛbibo mɔɔkɔ́ katɔ teebu.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Kayawi Ablala Ásɔ Na Étedu Átawɔlɔ
1Lɛ́kali na lɛ́su lɛlɔ nnii ɔƒɛni amu mɔɔta lɛsia kayawi ebiti kama blii lɛnu. Na lɛwia kayawi kamɛni kemmo ngba ala abuni. Nsu ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ uuubo kalɔ budie bɔdi. 2Kaƒɛgya na kadi ka ukyuli elie ataama uwi ndi uwi. Lɛbuni lɛmani na ukyuli adubɔkɛ si enye aawia ebiti sɔɔn? 3Lɛ́bla kasusu laa na lɛ́kali ka muuti ntɛ lɛkya lɛlɔ ebiti blii. Nsu na mina lɛnunda lɛni na ndanku ƒui ni, kɔdɔlɔ lɛlɔ na ńtálɛ. Na lɛ́kali ka mɔɔsia ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na lɛti lɛbuni lɛni geen nse nte ukyuli, na uwi klukui ɔni na úbo kalɔ kamɛni kemmo bulie na nwuna ngba kemmo.
4Lɛ́tu lɛtɔ bonwu líte lɛlɔ nnii mɔɔnu lɛlɔyɔ lɛni ndubɔkya-nwu kemmo ute-mi. Na líse adingyii mmo bɔbuni. 5Na lɛ́bla kevoma mmo ku lɛlɔ ebiti kɔkyakɔ kɔbuni ku adingyii abuni lidu lidu. 6Lɛ́tu ntu kewikɔ bonwu na ńtaaƒɔ ɔnantu ntu teewi edula mmo ku egyii bamba mmo bɔmmɔ na bɔ́lɛ lili kaduɛ. 7Líye banana ku beleku kabla bablane, na báwɔ bebi bamba udu lɛnɔ bákya-mi kaduli. Na mbo bebuo pii geen, ntulo baga bani náka-mi bulie ƒui akɔ ɔdi biala na Yerusalem. 8Na lɛ́ƒɔ sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi pii lɛ́siku baga ku bana kɔlɛkɛ egulabi kɔvumi kemmo. Na lɛ́ƒɔ banana ku beleku lɛnu bediene babuni ɔkpa. Na mbo basɔnɔ pii bani mɔɔdia bɔnu geen. Na lɛla biala na lɛkana lɛda ɔnana ɔkwɛ ni, líse-mi. 9Ɔmmɔ ɔsu lɛ́ƒɔ lɛnyi lítulo ɔga biala ɔni nélie Yerusalem ɔ́di lɛga asa na líbo. Nsu ala amɛni ƒui kemmo ni, mina anu ese nwaa kalɛ na lɛnu ala amɛni ƒui kemmo kavumana ku bɔdia ku tadia lɛti.
10Lɛla biala mɔɔwia ni, kɔnu kani muunene liti-ni.
Na ńteni mina ɔlɔna lɛla lɛni mɔɔda-nwu ɔkwɛ lɛdi.
Nsu ka lɛ́sia anu lɛ́nu ala ani ƒui na líkpoku lɛlɔ nnii
mɔɔwia-nya kalɔ linu mɛni ni,
lɛ́nu ka ana ƒui eeebo-mi kalɔ budie bɔdi.
11Na lɛ́nu ka úlieku
kalɛ na ukyuli ɔɔbi taasiaku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔnii uuƒie-nwu.
Na geen ni, lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛdi lɛla geen lɛni nnye kaduɛ.
Kavumana Keeebo Lɛnunda Ku Kɔdɔlɔ Ntɛ
12Lɛ́bla kasusu ka liti lɛnunda ku kɔdɔlɔ lɛ́kɔku lɛlɔ,
na mɔɔkali ka lɛla linwi pɛ kani na ukyuli biala
ɔdubɔsu aani mina kalɛ.
13Lɛnunda lɛ́ƒɔ kuye ƒui litulo kɔdɔlɔ
kalɛ kani na bukeye bɔdia butulo lɛdisa.
14Na ɔnundane ɔɔnu nwaa, nsu ɔdɔlɔdi anwu
ɔɔnya-nwu taakya gyuma gyuma lɛnumbwɛ kemmo.
Nsu lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka banundane ku badɔlɔdi ƒui ni,
kawɔlɔkɔ kenwi kani nse nte bana ƒui.
15Bana inyɔ ƒui beekpi.
Na kalɛ kani na ɔdɔlɔdi ɔdubo bukpi ni,
lɛni na ami lɛnɔ ndubo bukpi.
Na bi ndi mina lɛnunda kɔsia?
Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na lɛ́su lɛlɔ nnini,
“Ɔmɛni ƒui uuubo kalɔ budie bɔdi!”
16Ɔsika ɔnundane o-o,
ɔdɔlɔdi o-o ni,
bana inyɔ ƒui beekpi
na uwi ɔdubo
na bekyuli badubo bana inyɔ ƒui bɔyiƒala.
Lɛlɔ Butu Buuubo Kalɔ Budie
17Anwuɔsu muukisi ngba bumodi bɔmmɔ, ɔsika lɛlɔ lɛni na ukyuli uutú na ɔƒɛ kemmo bɔdi etila geen. Na ɔmɛni ƒui uuubo kalɔ budie. Mmomu use aani kalɛ na beekeli taasiaku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ. 18Ala ani ƒui na lítu lɛlɔ na ɔƒɛ kemmo na lɛ́kɛ ni, álɛ-mi kayi na naaayɔ-nya, ɔsika ndubo-nya bɔda búwi ukyuli bamba ɔni masia-mi kama. 19Na ɔma ngyi si ɔnundane na ukyuli ɔmmɔ wabla iye ɔdɔlɔdi? Nsu ala ani ƒui na lítu lɛlɔ ku mina lɛlati ku lɛnunda na lɛ́bla ku lɛbibo na ɔƒɛ kemmo ni, anwu ndubo-nya lɛlɔ ɔyikun bɔkɛ. Na uuubo kalɔ budie bɔdi. 20Ɔmɛni ɔsu na kayi kaakpulu-mi na mina lɛlɔtu ɔsu. 21Bi ɔsu na nka ukyuli uti nwuna lɛlati ku lɛnunda ku ɔyikun ɔbla kabla na ɔnyonu nwuna lɛlakɛ lɛmmɔ use ukyuli bamba ɔni na útetu lɛlɔ lɛdi? Alánu ka uuubo kalɔ kadi? 22Na bi kɔsia geen na ukyuli ubo na lɛbibo kanaa bɔmɛni kama. 23Uuubo bɔnwuna bɔdi limeyi kemmo. Nwuna emeyi ƒui adi lɛlɔ bususu ku ɔlɛ bunu na lɛlɔ lɛɛdu-nwu. Na si ɔtɛ usien lɛnɔ uláda kasusu buti taaya. Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui uuubo kalɔ budie bɔdi.
24Lɛla lɛni mɔɔnu ka ukyuli ɔkana bɔbla ndi ka unye nwuna kabla lɛlɔ, na ɔdi adila na ɔni na ɔkya lɛlɔ kubiti aani lɛla lɛni na Katɔti úte-bu. 25Ɔsika si anwu ulete-bu lɛla lɛdi ni, ɔma ndubɔkɛ adila ɔdi iye ɔkɛ lɛlɔyɔ? 26Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla Katɔti lɛƒɔyɔ ni, anwu na Katɔti ɔɔyá na ɔɔdá anu na uunú ala kalɔ na ɔɔyá na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ukyuli ɔmmɔ. Nsu si bɔɔbla likpidi ni, bɔdubo lɛlɔ bususu geen bute bula lɛdila, nsu Katɔti ɔdubɔƒɔ bula akɛla ute ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla-nwu lɛƒɔyɔ. Na nwuna kalɔ budie bɔbambadi bɔdi buuubo buuutulo ka ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kama bɔbi taasiaku kani na ɔdi.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
translation_text:
Lɛla Biala Libo Nina Uwi
1Lɛla biala libo nina uwi na kabla biala lɛnɔ kebo kana uwi.
2Uwi ɔni na bawɔ ubi ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na ukyuli ukpi lɛnɔ ɔkya.
Edula ɔkyawi ɔkya,
na ana ɔƒɛwi lɛnɔ ɔkya.
3Uwi ɔni baadú lɛla lɛdi ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na baabwi lɛnɔ ɔkya.
Na uwi ɔni na baabwɛ lɛnɔ ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na baatú lɛnɔ ɔkya.
4Uwi ɔni na beewulo ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na baamá lɛnɔ ɔkya.
Na uwi ɔni na beewulo kɔnyana ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na baatɔ́ lɛnɔ ɔkya.
5Uwi ɔni na beegyingya atabi ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na baasála-nya lɛnɔ ɔkya.
Na uwi ɔni na baakya lɛlɔ kɔgbu ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na beegyingyaku lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ɔkya.
6Uwi ɔni na baawia lɛla lɛdi ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni beedie-ni atu lɛnɔ ɔkya.
Na uwi ɔni na baada lɛla teese lɛlɔ ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na beevakun-ni lɛnɔ ɔkya.
7Uwi ɔni na baaní lɛla taabwɛ ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na baaka-ni taasala lɛnɔ ɔkya.
Na uwi ɔni na beebile kenye kpoo ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na baatɛmi lɛnɔ ɔkya.
8Uwi ɔni na baayɔ́ lɛlɔ ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na beekisi lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ɔkya.
Na uwi ɔni na beekpó kekpo ɔkya,
na uwi ɔni na beewi kenye ntu taabla unwi lɛnɔ ɔkya.
9Bi kɔsia na ukyuli ɔni na unye nwuna kabla lɛlɔ ɔɔkɛ́ taasiku nwuna lɛlɔ bususu kemmo? 10Lɛ́nu etila ani na Katɔti úti ɔ́sia bekyuli lili. 11Katɔti ɔɔyá na lɛla biala lɛɛlɛ́ na uwi lɛlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nsu bula ɔdi biala ulenu ala ani ƒui na ɔ́bla kalɔ taawɔlɔ geen. Na ɔɔyá na bula kasusu keekpóku-bu, na buuye lɛlɔ ala ɔ́siku ala ani na Katɔti ɔ́bla, ɔ́si uwi ɔni náavi úti úsela uwi ɔni ndubo lɛlɔ. 12Anwuɔsu lɛla lɛbuni ƒui lɛni na ɔlɛka bɔbla ndi ka ɔdi biala unye nwuna kabla lɛlɔ ku kubiti, na utaabla lɛbuni na nwuna ngba kemmo. 13Ɔsika lɛla lɛni na Katɔti úte-bu ndi ka bunye bula kabla lɛlɔ na bɔkɛ adila bɔdi, na bɔni, na lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-bu. 14Ngyi nwaa ka lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́bla ni, ani kani ndubo bunye uwi ƒui. Na ɔdi ulakana lɛla lɛdi buti bubunku iye ɔda ɔdi udie. Na Katɔti ɔ́bla ɔmɛni kalɛ na bekyuli beti ɔbu ku bɔyia bete-nwu.
15Ala ani ƒui mɔɔlɛ́ ɔƒɛni ni, áalɛ ábavi.
Na ani ndubo abálɛ lɛnɔ áakya dii.
Katɔti ɔɔyá na ala ani náalɛ dii
aasɔ teebo taabalɛ.
16Na lɛ́nu lɛla bamba lɛnɔ ka na kesi kesii.
Kekpo ku ala tabla ulu lɛlɔ siin kani nkya
na lɛbuni kenye mmomu.
17Anwuɔsu mina kasusu kátina-mi
ka Katɔti ɔdubɔtɛku bekyuli babuni ku bekpidi ƒui litemi,
ɔsika uwi ɔdubo ute lɛla biala na ukyuli ɔ́bla na kesii biala.
18Na lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka bɔkɔku na Katɔti ɔɔkɔ́ku abu bekyuli bayawine ƒui taanu na bɔnu bɔti ka bútavumanaku bebuo. 19Ukyuli ngba bulie ku nwuna kawɔlɔkɔ kátavumanaku ebuo ɔdi. Ɔƒɛƒɛɛ unwi na bɔɔnwuna aani bana kalɛ. Anwuɔsu ukyuli uuubo kenyekɔ kadi na kadia ketulo ebuo kadi. 20Ala ani na Katɔti údie na ebo ngba ni, likpo linwi na bana ƒui baasɔ teenwini teesie. Ɔsika lɛti kemmo na bédie bula ƒui bálɛku na lɛti kani na bɔdubɔsɔ bunwini. 21Ɔma geen ngyi si ukyuli kɔyu aku katɔ na kɔɔkɔ́ teesie, na ebuo kɔyu aku kalɔ kemmo na kɔɔyu teeduo?
22Anwuɔsu lɛla bamba lɛdi liiibo liiite ukyuli uuutulo ka lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-nwu na nwuna kabla lɛlɔ, ɔsika ɔɔɔdubo lɛla lɛni malɛ bɔti na nwuna kama.

english_text:
1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
1Lɛ́nu lɛla bamba lɛnɔ lɛ́ka lɛ́mana na lɛ́nu ulikplu ku kalala kani udu na bekyuli baabla bekyuli na kalɔ lɛlɔ.
Na keku buwulo sɔɔn kani nda,
nsu kɔnu ɔsiane ɔdi uuubo.
Na bani mɔɔbla udu ɔmɛni lɛnɔ
bebo ɔkplu geen.
2Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na lɛ́su kɔnakunwi nnini,
“Bekpine bebo bɔnwuna betulo bayawine.
3Na bani na bétemonku-ma
bɔwɔ ni,
bana ɔdi ɔsɔ ɔdia utulo ƒui,
ɔsika ama bátanu likyulikpi ala
ani mɔɔlɛ́ na kayawi mɛni kudii.”
4Na lɛ́nu kabla kani lɛlɔ na bekyuli benye ku ala enengudi ani na baabla na bɔɔnu ƒui kási lɛlɔ kogyulo bukpo ku lɛnungyie lɛni nkya bekyuli ɔsu. Na ɔmmɔ ƒui uuubo kalɔ kadi, ɔsika use aani kalɛ na baabi taasiaku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ.
5Ɔdɔlɔdi muuti enu taasia nwuna kayi na anu ka ɔkɛ ɔɔví,
na anwuɔsu lɛnɔ na kɔka kɔɔdú-nwu.
6Lɛdilabɔ blii lɛni na ákɛ ádi ku atu bɔyɔ ni,
ɔdia utulo si étésusu lɛlɔ na ému-nya ada
na use aani kalɛ na baabi taasiaku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ.
7Lɛ́nu lɛla bamba lɛnɔ na liiibo kalɔ bunu bɔdi na kalɔ lɛlɔ.
8Ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́kya ɔni na
uuubo ubi ɔnanabi
iye ɔnwani ɔdi,
nsu ulada lɛlɔ butu taaya,
na nwuna akɛla ani na ubo lɛnɔ
elemo-nwu.
Amu na úye lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Ɔma geen ɔsu na muubó abi,
na líni lɛla lɛbuni biala líte lɛlɔ ku kalɛ na lɛkya lɛlɔ ebiti muedi?”
Bi keyi udu na kadi mɛni
na ukyuli ulenu lɛla lɛdi kalɔ?
9Nkyuli inyɔ kelie kadia ketulo ukyuli unwi.
Ɔsika lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ-ma
si bása baadi lɛla lɛni na bákɛ.
10Ɔƒɛni si ɔdi nébuli ni,
ɔkpanadi ɔdubo-nwu bubunku na ɔta.
Nsu si anwu lɛti kani na ɔdi ni,
nwuna bɔta bɔdubo-nwu bude.
11Na si badi inyɔ na báyu bátɛ ni,
bana lɛlɔ ogya ɔdubɔƒɔ ɔda-ma gugungu.
Nsu si awɔ ukyuli unwi na ɔdi
ntɛ ni,
dɛ na adubɔƒɔ ogya ada lɛlɔ gugungu?
12Baakana na badi ukyuli unwi lɛlɔ si biikpó.
Nsu si bibo inyɔ ni,
bɛdubɔsala na bɛdi lɛlɔ.
Anwuɔsu baasu banii kabuli
kani na bámii básala
ɛtɛ ni,
kalatuna bukulo pla.
13Si adi okloƒu ɔwabane na áda anu ni, ɔdia ƒui utulo ɔga ɔdɔlɔdi ɔni na ulie na ulaƒɔ bekyuli kasusu. 14Na okloƒu ɔmmɔ udu ni, ina aban ɔtɔ katɛkɔ na ɔ́si úbo iye bawabane kaduli na báwɔ-nwu bákya na baaadi baga liku bekyuli muedi ni, ɔkana na unwini ɔga. 15Lɛ́ɛnu dii ka kayawi bekyuli ƒui básiaku okloƒu ɔmmɔ udu na ɔga ɔdi kukpi kama. 16Na ɔdi ulakana nwuna basiakune bɔka. Nsu na uwi ɛlɛɛ kama ni, bekyuli bani na bébebo kama ɔdi ulayɔ-nwu litemi. Na ɔmɛni ƒui úlieku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kama bukeli taasia.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
Sia Lɛlɔ Anu Kaduɛ Na Katɔti Kakpakɔ
1Ti lɛlɔ bɔda si éduo Katɔti kakpakɔ. Na esie atábla kpoo na ese atu enu ala na tababla asu ka atábla akpala aani ɔdɔlɔdi kalɛ na alati anii adaku Katɔti bɔƒiɔ.
2Da ƒula kenye na ati bɔtɛmi na Katɔti anumi.
Na tese-nwu kenye kadi
asa na abla kasusu asiku lɛla lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.
Ɔsika katɔ na Katɔti ulie na awɔ akya kalɔ mɛni
anwuɔsu na akɔsi bɔtɛmi.
3Si lɛla lɛdi lɛkya-a kasusu uwi ndi uwi ni,
eeti-ni teegye kɔna.
Lɛni kani na si ɔdɔlɔdi ɔɔtɛmi uwi ndi uwi na ɔɔƒiɔ́.
4Si ánu ka ése Katɔti kenye kadi ni, taya na uwi utu-ka lɛlɔ. Babla na abla linyese lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ete-nwu, ɔsika kaƒɔ kalayɔ-nwu na kɔdɔlɔ ala bɔbla lɛlɔ. 5Ɔdia si étese Katɔti kenye kadi utulo ka ese-nwu kenye na aladi-ka lɛlɔ. 6Taya na ƒula kenye keti-ɔ katákya likpidi kemmo. Na tasu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnu lɛkpa lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ anii kenye kani na ése ni, ɔɔɔdi litemi geen na ada na bɔsu kani na ásu. Ɔsika Katɔti ɔkana na ubile ƒula kabla ƒui na kayii udu. Anwuɔsu tabla lɛla lɛni makya-nwu kɔnyi. 7Taayia Katɔti ku ɔbu na tataabla kasusu na ala ani na étulo-ɔ lɛlɔ si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, adɔlɔtɛ kani na adubo butaatɛmi.
8Si ánu ka baanya bekyuli bani na bese kpɛtɛ taakya na ƒula kalɔ lɛlɔ, na ala tabla ulu lɛlɔ búti ala bɔbla siin kenye ni, utabla-a dɛye dɛye, ɔsika bekyuli bani nkya lɛlɔ badine kalɔ ni, ɔlɛka benu bana batɔnkune litemi. 9Na ka ɔga ndi ukyuli ɔni na utulo ƒui na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, kalɔ kammɔ kuyii kɔni na báda béte bekyuli na baaƒɔ ni, anwu ndubɔdi kenengudikɔ.
10Ukyuli ɔni mbo egulabi ku akɛla bɔyɔ ni,
sika ulemo-nwu na akɛla lɛnɔ alabɔ-nwu.
Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui use aani kalɛ na baabi taasiaku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ.
11Si akɛla eemomo ukyuli ni,
lɛni kani na badine lɛnɔ beemomo.
Na akɛla ammɔ elebunku-ɔ
úti útulo ka enye aanu na bekyuli badi-nya bete-ɔ.
12Ukyuli bamba kabla ɔblane ni,
lɛlɛɛ lɛɛyu-nwu
ina útakɛ lɛla bonwu lɛdi útadi.
Nsu ɔlakɛne ala pii ani na ubo ɔsu ni,
lɛlɛɛ línwini-nwu etila.
13Lɛ́ɛnu likyulikpi ala enengudi geen na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ ɔni na
akɛla ani na ɔlakɛne ɔ́tɛ úse lɛlɔ
énwini-nwu ɔgbankpi.
14Na lɛ́nu kalɛ na akɛla ammɔ udu lɛnɔ aayii
ɔkɛnku lilikpi lɛla lɛni
nálɛ ɔsu.
Na si ukyuli ɔmmɔ ubo ubi ɔnanabi ni,
na lɛla biala lɛ́sɔ lítebu liiise-nwu.
15Kasɔngya na ukyuli ɔɔlɛ́ taasi uni kaƒɔ kemmo.
Na kalɛ na ɔkɛ úbo ni, lɛni kani na ɔdubɔsɔ unwini ɔtɔlɔ.
Na ɔɔɔdubo lɛla lɛdi buti bɔda bɔtɔlɔku.
16Ɔmɛni ɔdi kɔnyana litemi lɛni naaadia bɔnu na ɔdi ɔƒɛƒɛɛ bɔbi taasiaku.
17Na nwuna ngba emeyi ƒui ni, ulátuna bulie taadi nwaa ku ebiti
mmomu úmii na nwuna kayi ku kasusu kemmo ku ɔdu kati kati.
18Lɛla lɛni kani na mɔɔnu ka ukyuli ɔlɛka ɔbla ndi ka bɔdi adila na bɔni lɛnɔ na ebiti ataada-bu na bula kabla lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ kani ndi lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔɔwia ka butaabla. 19Ɔƒɛni si ukyuli ɔdi ubo lɛlakɛ na limomo-nwu, na ɔɔdi na ɔɔní taakɛ lɛlɔyɔ ni, unye nwuna kabla lɛlɔ ku ebiti, ɔsika Katɔti néte-nwu-ni. 20Na Katɔti ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔda-nwu na nwuna kayi kayɔ ɔni na ulenye uléteekpoku lɛlɔ kasusu na nwuna ngba emeyi lɛlɔ.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
7We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied. 8We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right. 9It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
10Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us. 11The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk? 12Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_text:
Teti Anu Tasia Lɛkɛ Lɛlɔ
1Lɛla bamba lɛnɔ lɛkya na lɛɛɛdia munu munu lɛni na muukpóku bekyuli kasusu. 2Katɔti uute ukyuli egulabi ku lɛlakɛ bonwu na ɔɔyá na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ lɛnyi ɔni na ɔsɔ uláyaki lɛla lɛdi mmomu kayi kaayɔ́-nwu buɛɛ. Nsu Katɔti ulaya na uulie taadi ala ammɔ mmomu ɔƒɔ muubo taabadi-nya. Na ɔdi kɔnyana litemi lɛni ndi ɔgbankpi na uuubo kalɔ bunu.
3Ukyuli ɔkana na ulie ngba ɔƒɔ akwa pii na ɔwɔ bebi ina eti anyɔ muedi. Nsu si lɛlɔ lítayɔ-nwu na nwuna ngba kemmo na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ukpi na bátava-nwu kaduɛ ni, ubi ɔni nékpi na ntu kemmo muedi ɔ́ƒɔ kuye utulo-nwu. 4Ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi ubi ɔmmɔ udu bɔwɔ kalɔ. Mmomu ɔɔsɔ teenwini aani kalɛ na lɛdisa lɛɛyila lɛla lɛdi taakya. Na útebo na ɔdia lɛnyi lɛdi muedi bɔsia. 5Ina ka útanu ɔƒɛ iye ɔti lɛla lɛdi ni, ubi ɔmmɔ ubo bɔnwuna utulo bebi pii ɔti ɔni nélie útu uwi mmɔ. 6Anwuɔsu si ina akwa mpim inyɔ na úlie na lɛlɔ lítayɔ-nwu na nwuna ngba bulie ku kabla kani na ɔ́bla lɛlɔ ni, bi na ɔ́kɛ ka likpo linwi kani na bana inyɔ ƒui bátáyii bákya?
7Kenye bɔdi kani na ukyuli ulie uususu lɛlɔ teete
nsu ala eledu-nwu ɔkwɛ kudii.
8Kenyekɔ kamani na ɔnundane ubo
utulo ɔdɔlɔdi?
Na ɔwabane lɛnɔ ni, dɛ na ɔdubɔkana ngba bulie
na ɔti lɛlɔ bɔda utulo bakladi
na ayaki ani nda-nwu kemmo?
9Si bɔ́di lɛla lɛni nse-bu ku
kubiti ni,
ɔdia utulo ka butaasia lɛla bamba anu.
Ɔsika uuubo kalɔ bunu bɔdi
na buse kani na use
aani kalɛ na baabi taasiaku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ.
10Lɛla biala mɔɔlɛ́ ni, lɛdi lɛla lɛni na Katɔti
ɔ́ɔlɛ ugyii úse kukuuku.
Na abu bekyuli bɔgyi kalɛ na buse ɔsu ni,
buuubo unyeƒi ɔdi na bɔɔkyaku Katɔti,
ɔsika ubo ɔyikun utulo-bu ƒui.
11Si bɔnii butaatɛmi pii ni,
lɛni kani na bɔdubo kɔdɔlɔ keyi buteedie.
Anwuɔsu kɔsia kɔdi kuuubo-nwu kemmo ka bunye butaaka ala.
12Ngba buse klukui geen na buuubo kalɔ bunu bɔdi. Na bɔɔyii taakya aani ɔƒɛ kɔyu. Ɔma ndubɔti lɛla lɛni ndia lite-bu utulo ƒui? Na ɔma ndubɔti lɛla lɛni ndubo bɔlɛ uwi ɔni na abu bɔsɔ buuubo?

english_text:
The Best in Life
1 A good reputation
at the time of death
is better than loving care
at the time of birth.
2It's better to go to a funeral
than to attend a feast;
funerals remind us
that we all must die.
3Choose sorrow over laughter
because a sad face
may hide a happy heart.
4A sensible person mourns,
but fools always laugh.
5Correction from someone wise
is better by far
than praise from fools.
6Foolish laughter is stupid.
It sounds like thorns
crackling in a fire.
7Corruption makes fools
of sensible people,
and bribes can ruin you.
8Something completed is better
than something just begun;
patience is better
than too much pride.
9 Only fools get angry quickly
and hold a grudge.
10It isn't wise to ask,
“Why is everything worse
than it used to be?”
11Having wisdom is better
than an inheritance.
12Wisdom will protect you
just like money;
knowledge with good sense
will lead you to life.
13Think of what God has done!
If God makes something crooked,
can you make it straight?
14When times are good,
you should be cheerful;
when times are bad,
think about what it means.
God makes them both
to keep us from knowing
what will happen next.
Some of Life's Questions
15I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper. 16So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart! 17Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool. 18Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
19Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
20No one in this world always does right.
21Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you. 22Haven't you cursed many others?
23I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me. 24The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep. 25So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
26Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for. 27With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together, 28but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman. 29I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_text:
Ukyuli Ɔdi Ɔɔɔgyi Lɛla Ku Uwi Ɔni Mebo
1Lɛnyi buni bɔƒɔ bɔdia butulo nnɔmii ku ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ.
Na likpimeyi lɛdia litulo lɛwɔmeyi.
2Na kekwa kalɔ busie bɔdia butulo
ka esie limeyi buni kadikɔ.
Ɔsika kukpi ndi ukyuli biala
kawɔlɔkɔ ku kesiekɔ.
3Kɔnyana kɔdia kutulo lɛma.
Ɔsika anumi ani muuwulo kɔnyana
aayá na ukyuli kayi kemmo ablala
eeboku ukyuli kubiti.
4Ɔnundane kayi kaasia ala
ani mɔɔlɛ́ na kɔnyana kewulokɔ lɛlɔ.
Nsu ɔdɔlɔdi uuti nwuna kayi
taasia ebiti kakɛkɔ ala lɛlɔ.
5Ukyuli bɔdɔnku kpakplaa bɔdia butulo
si badɔlɔdi beedie lɛnu teemwi-ɔ.
6Ɔdɔlɔdi lɛma ni, buse na use
aani kalɛ na liyu alakpi eetulo
na ogya kemmo na libui kalɔ.
Na ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ uuubo kalɔ bunu bɔdi.
7Ala buƒu taakya ɔɔyá na
ɔnundane uunwíni ɔdɔlɔdi.
Na ala bɔbɛ taaƒɔ taadi ulaya
na ukyuli kayi keeti-nwu taasiaku
ala bɔbla ulu lɛlɔ siin.
8Litemi kawɔlɔkɔ kadia ketulo litemi kalɔ kesekɔ.
Na kayi buɛɛ kadia ketulo lɛlɔ bɔtina.
9Tataababla ku kɔnyi buti na ƒula lɛlɔ kemmo. Ɔsika badɔlɔdi lɛgba akɔ na kúti-ɔ kúsela kutálɛlɛ.
10Teye anii bi ɔsu kuuku uwi
ɔdia utulo uwi
ɔni kemmo na bɔkya mɛni.
Ɔsika kɔdɔlɔ litemi na lɛdi.
11Si ukyuli ebo lɛnunda ni,
ɔdia utulo kese bamba
biala ƒui.
12Ɔsika lɛnunda lɛdubudie-ɔ
na lɛla biala kemmo
aani egulabi.
Na lɛlati ku kasusu buni
kadubo-ɔ bɔgyumana
ngba uwi ƒui.
13Bla kasusu na Katɔti ala ani ƒui na ɔ́bla lɛlɔ na anu anii adubɔkana lɛdi bunyene si ánu ka lɛdi lɛ́bu? 14Si ala aatɛku ukyuli ɔdi ni, lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-nwu. Na si bubie na ala eebieku-nwu ni, na ulie kalɔ na uye lɛlɔ lɛla lɛni kudɔ na ɔ́si. Ɔsika Katɔti nábla alakpa anyɔ ammɔ kalɛ na ukyuli ɔsia lɛlɔ anu ka ɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni nsɔ ndubo bɔlɛ ɔsu.
15Na mina ngba bɔni neeebo-mi kalɔ mɛni kemmo ni, lɛ́nu
kalɛ na ukyuli ɔni nsiaku Katɔti kama siin
ɔɔkana na uukpi taayii udu.
Na lɛ́nu kalɛ na ukyuli ukpidi lɛnɔ
ɔɔkana na uulie ngba taabi lɛlɔ geen
na nwuna likyulikpi ala bɔbla kemmo.
16Anwuɔsu tabla lɛlɔ aani ukyuli kedee tagya,
na tabla lɛlɔ ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́da anu ɔ́gya lɛnɔ.
17Telie tabla ulikplu tavili
na ekulo ƒula ngba liku iye tadɔlɔ,
na ƒula kɔdɔlɔ kɔya na ƒula ngba bɔda liku.
18Nu ka akɛ ulu ntɛntɛ
na étedeyi étésie kakɛ kadi átavili.
Na ɔmɛni bɔbla ulayu-ɔ ɔkplu ulavili
si aabu Katɔti.
19Lɛnunda lɛɛyá na ukyuli unwi ɔɔkɛ́ ɔyikun
teetulo lɛlɔ badine leevu na ɔma unengudi ɔdi kemmo.
20Ukyuli ɔdi uuubo na banii anwu use siin
na ɔɔbla lɛla biala kaduɛ
ɔsu na ulábla likpidi lɛdi na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ.
21Tese atu anii eenú lɛla biala na ukyuli ɔɔsu,
si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni,
ésela eténu ka ƒula kabla ɔblane unye
uudumi teewida-a.
22Ɔsika awɔ ɔlati agyi nwaa
ka áabla lɛni kɔlɛ kɔlɛ.
23Ala amɛni ƒui na lɛ́nu laa kpoo na lɛ́su ka ndubɔda anu na lɛnu lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ala amɛni ese lɛni lɛti, nsu útulo-mi.
24Ina bi anu na ukyuli ɔ́da ni,
litemi geen lɛmmɔ lɛ́gyunku-bu
na nina kemmo bunu
bɔ́gyu geen
ɔni na ɔdi ulakana kalɔ bunu bɔwɔlɔ.
25Anwuɔsu na lɛ́bla kasusu nnii
mɔɔtɛya lɛla biala na makana
kalɛ na lɛda anu na lɛti lɛla lɛni
na ngba bumodi bɔmmɔ bɔdanku.
Na lɛti kɔdɔlɔ ku libuokpi lɛni udu
nkya likyulikpi bulie taabla lɛnɔ kemmo.
26Lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka uleku ukpidi ubo ɔdu utulo kukpi.
Na úbimi enu ku kayi ƒui úse
aani kakpagyuɛ ka uƒie ukyuli.
Na ɔnana ɔni mɔɔdi Katɔti litemi
lɛlɔ ni,
ɔkana na ukeli-nwu.
Nsu ukyuli ɔni na uládi-ni lɛlɔ ni,
ɔdubo-nwu buƒie aani kakpagyuɛ
na ɔyii udu kede kede.
27Ala ɔtinane ɔnini,
“Lɛ́sia mina lɛnunda lɛni ƒui na mbo lɛlɔ nnii
mɔɔnu kalɛ na ala amɛni ámanku lɛlɔ.
28Nsu lítuku laa lɛ́nɔ.
Mmomu lɛ́nu ka na nkyuli apim unwi kemmo ni,
bakana na bakɛ ɔnana ɔbuni unwi
nsu beleku ama lítuku lɛ́nɔ
na ńtakɛ ɔdi na bɔka bɔmɛni kemmo.
29Lɛla linwi nábla-mi nwaa ƒui
ndi ka Katɔti ɔ́bla-bu
na nka bɔdi bekyuli siin,
nsu búbavumana kasusu bɔ́sia ala bamba pii lɛlɔ
na búƒu bula kasusu.”

english_text:
1Who is smart enough
to explain everything?
Wisdom makes you cheerful
and gives you a smile.
Obey the King
2If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise. 3Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind. 4The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?” 5If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it. 6Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything, 7though no one can tell the future. 8We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil. 9I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another?
Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
10I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense. 11When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime. 12They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying:
Everyone who lives right
and respects God
will prosper,
13but no one who sins
and rejects God
will prosper or live very long.
14There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens. 15So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
16Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world. 17I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_text:
1Ɔma mbo lɛlati lɛni
na ɔkana lɛla biala kalɔ budie?
Lɛnunda lɛɛbla ukyuli anumi nwaa
na anumi aaƒɛnimi-nwu.
2Si énye Katɔti anumi ése kenye ka adubɔdi ɔga ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ni, amu mɔɔsu-ɔ kpakplaa nnii di ƒula linyese lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. 3Tababla na akyaku ɔga unyeƒi si ɔ́ɔlɛ nwuna lɛla lɛdi ugyii iye ata enye-nwu lɛlɔ. 4Ɔga litemi lɛdi ɔda bubo na ɔdi ɔɔɔdubo bɔta kalɛ kalɛ na uye-nwu ɔnii bi ɔsu na ɔɔbla lɛla lɛdi na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ.
5Si aabu ɔga ni, eleduo ɔgbankpi kemmo.
Anwuɔsu sia anu na ati lɛla lɛni na abla
ku uwi ɔni na abla-ni.
6Ngba bulie bubo ukyuli ɔkplu geen
nsu lɛla biala bɔbla bubo kalɛ na abla-ni asiaku
ku uwi ku kesii kani na babla-ni,
7ina ka ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni mebo uwi ɔni ndubo.
8Ukyuli ɔdi ulakana ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ulu bɔtina
iye ɔti nwuna likpimeyi.
Na kama busie lɛnɔ buuubo si kekpo kálɛ.
Lɛni kani na ɔdi ulakana na wabɛ na nwuna likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla kama.
9Lɛ́nu ɔmɛni ƒui lɛ́ti na líti-nwu kasusu kpakplaa na ala ani mɔɔlɛ́ kayawi kamɛni kemmo lɛlɔ. Dɛ na ɔ́bla na ukyuli ɔdi anwu ɔɔkɛ́ ɔyikun ɔdi utulo bakladi na anu ka ɔɔbla kalala? 10Lɛnɔ ni, lɛ́nu kalɛ na baavá bekyuli bekpidi ku ɔbu, nsu Katɔti bekyuli bávi bálɛ ɔma kedee ɔmmɔ kemmo na báyiƒala-ma. Na ɔmɛni lɛnɔ uuubo kalɔ bunu bɔdi.
11Si bɔ́nu kalɛ na bekyuli bekpidi benye baabla likyulikpi ala taasia kama na balakɛ lɛtuni lɛdi ni, na ɔɔbla-bu aani abu lɛnɔ buse kalɔ buteelie ngba bɔmmɔ udu. 12Bɔɔnu kalɛ na bekyuli bekpidi bani muulie taabla ekpidi liti liti taasia kama beelie ngba na uwi uutu ina ka nka básu banii bekyuli bani mɔɔsiaku Katɔti kama siin na baabu-nwu na ala adubo bɔtɛku. 13Na ɔɔɔdi bani muuní-nwu na baabla ekpidi na ala adubo bɔtɛku.
14Lɛla bamba lɛnɔ lɛkya lɛni neeebo kalɔ budie bɔdi. Bekyuli babuni na baabla kalala aani bekyuli bekpidi. Na bekpidi mmomu na baatu lili aani bekyuli babuni. 15Anwuɔsu na mɔɔtí nwaa ka lɛla bamba lɛdi liiibo liiite ukyuli na ɔbla utulo ka ɔdi adila na ɔni na ebiti ada-nwu asa na ɔkana kayawi kemmo bɔsia bɔlɛ aani lɛla lɛni na Katɔti úte-bu.
16Mɔɔtɛ usien ku ɔƒɛ lɛlɛɛ talɛɛ talɛɛ na muuti kasusu taasiku ala ani ƒui mɔɔlɛ́ na kalɔ kamɛni kemmo lɛlɔ. 17Lɛ́nu ala ani ƒui na Katɔti ɔ́bla na lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka ukyuli biala uuubo na wakana-nya kalɔ bunu iye ɔnu lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔti nwaa kudi kudii ina dɛ na ɔnii ɔ́da anu.

english_text:
One Day at a Time
1I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad. 2But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
3It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die. 4As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion. 5We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten. 6Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
7So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do. 8Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best. 9Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth. 10Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
11Here is something else I have learned:
The fastest runners
and the greatest heroes
don't always win races
and battles.
Wisdom, intelligence, and skill
don't always make you healthy,
rich, or popular.
We each have our own share
of misfortune.
12None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap.
Better To Be Wise than Foolish
13Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me. 14It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls. 15But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten. 16So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
17Words of wisdom spoken softly
make much more sense
than the shouts of a ruler
to a crowd of fools.
18Wisdom is more powerful
than weapons,
yet one mistake can destroy
all the good you have done.
translation_text:
Kawɔlɔkɔ Kenwi Nse Nte Ala Ƒui
1Ka lɛ́bla kasusu lɛ́siku ala amɛni ƒui lɛlɔ ni, línu kalɔ ka Katɔti ubo ɔyikun na ukyuli biala lɛlɔ, ku abu bani náda anu na bɔsiaku-nwu kama siin lɛnɔ lɛlɔ. Lɛla biala udu lɛkana na lɛlɛku bula akɔ ɔdi biala. Na bulakana bɔti si ngba bɔdubɔtɛku-bu iye bɔdububieku-bu. 2Lɛlakpa linwi lɛmmɔ kani udu ndubo bɔlɛku bula ƒui na kawɔlɔkɔ.
Bɔsiaku na bɔsiaku-nwu kama siin
na bɔɔbu-nwu o-o, bɔbu na bulabu-nwu o-o ni,
kawɔlɔkɔ kenwi kammɔ kani nse nte-bu.
Akpala na bɔɔkyula teete-nwu o-o,
bɔkyula na bulakyula adi teete-nwu o-o,
si bɔɔdi bula linyese lɛlɔ o-o, buladi-ni lɛlɔ o-o ni,
kawɔlɔkɔ kammɔ kani na kadi.
3Nka ubo ɔkplu na ɔɔɔdia ka kɔnyana litemi lɛmɛni udu lɛlɛku bekyuli babuni ku bekpidi ɔsala. Bula ngba uliewi ƒui ni, bɔdi bekyuli bani na bɔ́sɔ na bɔ́dɔlɔ lɛnɔ. Ɔmɛni kemmo kani na bɔɔkya laa na buti bukpi. 4Nsu si bulie ngba bɔdi ni, bɔdubo anumi butaanu ka lɛbuni lɛdi lɛdububo. Ɔsika si ina akpewe ɔni nkya ngba ɔdia utulo gyata ukpine!
5Bayawine bagyi ka badubo bukpi
nsu bekpine ama basɔ balasia lɛla lɛdi anu,
ɔsika basɔ baaagyi lɛla lɛdi.
Na basɔ beeebo lɛyuƒɔla lɛdi lɛnɔ.
Na ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ulényimo-ma muedi.
6Bana bekyuli bɔyɔ ku bekyuli bukisi
ku bana lɛnungyie ƒui ni, békpi bátɔlɔku-ni
ɔni bana kɔnu kɔsɔ kulakya
kayawi kamɛni lɛla lɛdi bɔbla kemmo.
7Di adila na ani na akya lɛlɔ kubiti, ɔsika Katɔti nése ɔmɛni úse úte ukyuli ɔ́si kukuuku. 8Tada lɛlɔ tese kalɛ kalɛ mmomu da lɛlɔ na egyeli lili na aklibi lɛlɔ kaduɛ. 9Ngba bútene, na ka aayɔ́ ƒ'ulekudi ɔsu ni, bitesie bitaya lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni na ɔ́lɛka bɛbla na uwi ɔni kemmo na bɛkya kayawi kamɛni kemmo biisusu lɛlɔ. 10Kabla biala na ɔdi aabla ni, nye-ka lɛlɔ kpakplaa. Ɔsika uwi uletu asa na adubo-ka bɔda búwi na atɔlɔ etéduo kekpine, kesii kani na ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ulabla kabla kadi iye ulie uteeti kasusu kadi iye ɔti lɛla lɛdi muedi.
11Lɛ́nu lɛla bamba lɛnɔ lɛ́ti na kayawi.
Ɔɔɔdi bekyuli bani ngyi usi bukeli kaduɛ
kani muukeli taadi lɛlɔ.
Na ɔɔɔdi bekpone bani ngyi kekpo lɛlɔ ala
kani muukpó taadi lɛlɔ.
Lɛni kani na ɔɔɔdi banundane
kani mɔɔkɛ́ adila abuni taadi.
Na ɔɔɔdi bani kasusu kemmo nse nwaa
kani muunwíni balakɛne
iye bani ngyi bana kabla kadi lɛlɔ ala mɔɔƒɔ́ lɛnyi.
Mmomu uwi ku lilidia kuƒi kubunku.
12Na lɛnɔ ni, ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi uwi ɔni na nwuna uwi ɔdubo ubedu.
Kalɛ na kabɛ keeduo agyakuo kemmo
iye aasɛ ɔɔnú kamia ni,
lɛni na uwi ukpidi uubo taabasiaku bekyuli
aani kalɛ na baanú kakpagyuɛ.
13Na kayawi mɛni ni, lɛ́nu lɛnunda udu bamba ɔdi lɛnɔ lɛ́ti ɔni néte-mi kasusu geen. 14Úbebo úte uwi ɔdi kemmo, ka ɔma unengudi ɔdi na nkyuli ɛlɛɛ badi kani nkya-nwu kemmo ni, ɔga ɔdi ɔ́ta ka ubekpo ɔma ɔmmɔ. Anwuɔsu nwuna bekpone bábaka bámana-nwu na bábla kunyekɔ ƒui bése ku kɔbɛkɔ kunengudi kesii kani na badubunye na bekpo badi ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. 15Na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ɔwabane ɔdi ɔ́kya na ɔ́da anu geen. Na anwu náƒɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ úse na nwuna lɛnunda ɔsu. Nsu útaƒɔ uwi asa na báyiƒala ɔnana ɔmɛni. 16Anwuɔsu lɛ́su nnini, “Lɛnunda lɛdia litulo ɔyikun.”
17Banundane kabɛnsɛ kani baatɛmi ni,
kadia kétulo badɔlɔdi batɔnkune kɔvanu.
18Si ukyuli ubo lɛnunda ni, ɔdia utulo si ada ekpola.
Nsu ukyuli ukpidi unwi ɔɔkana na ubile ala abuni pii.

english_text:
1A few dead flies in perfume
make all of it stink,
and a little foolishness
outweighs a lot of wisdom.
2Sensible thoughts lead you
to do right;
foolish thoughts lead you
to do wrong.
3Fools show their stupidity
by the way they live;
it's easy to see
they have no sense.
4Don't give up your job
when your boss gets angry.
If you stay calm,
you'll be forgiven.
5Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair: 6They honor fools, but dishonor the rich; 7they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
8 If you dig a pit,
you might fall in;
if you break down a wall,
a snake might bite you.
9You could even get hurt
by chiseling a stone
or chopping a log.
10If you don't sharpen your ax,
it will be harder to use;
if you are wise,
you'll know what to do.
11The power to charm a snake
does you no good
if it bites you anyway.
12If you talk sensibly,
you will have friends;
if you talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
13Fools begin with nonsense,
and their stupid chatter
ends with disaster.
14They never tire of talking,
but none of us really know
what the future will bring.
15Fools wear themselves out—
they don't know enough
to find their way home.
16A country is in for trouble
when its ruler is childish,
and its leaders
party all day long.
17But a nation will prosper
when its ruler is mature,
and its leaders
don't party too much.
18Some people are too lazy
to fix a leaky roof—
then the house collapses.
19Eating and drinking
make you feel happy,
and money can buy
everything you need.
20Don't let yourself think about
cursing the king;
don't curse the rich,
not even in secret.
A little bird might hear
and tell everything.
translation_text:
1Kalɛ na si balɔlɔ békpi bákya nnɔmii ƒɛƒɛɛ kemmo
na ɔɔyá na nnɔmii bɔmmɔ ɔnyi ɔɔbla buɛ buɛ ni,
lɛni na kɔdɔlɔ kɔɔyá na lɛnunda ku ɔbu ɔɔyii udu.
2Banundane kayi kaatɔnku-ma na baabla ala abuni.
Lɛni kani na badɔlɔdi kayi kaatɔnku-ma na baabla likpidi.
3Si ina ɔgbami na ɔdɔlɔdi ɔkɛ muedi ni,
nwuna busie lɛti lɛti bɔɔtina-a kalɛ na ɔ́dɔlɔ.
4Si ƒula ɔtɔnkune ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi ɔ́kya-a ni,
teni ƒula kabla na ada-ka ewi.
Ɔsika lɛlɔ kalɔ buboku buɛɛ uutile
na uuboku kɔnyi ku ala pii kalɔ.
5Lɛ́nu likpidi bamba bɔbla na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ.
Na batɔnkune bani mɔɔdi bekyuli lɛlɔ
mɔɔbla likpidi lɛmɛni.
6Na ama muuti badɔlɔdi teenyene kunyekɔ kɔni mbo ɔbu
na balakɛne mmomu na beeboku kalɔ.
7Lɛ́nu ka bekyuli bani nkya bekyuli kudɔ baabla-ma kabla
mmomu nlie bapɔnkɔ kama
na bagabi bakɛ lɛgba aani ama mmomu ndi kabla bablane.
8Bekyuli bani muukú libu teese bana bakpana ni,
ama alati mɔɔnú-ni kemmo.
Lɛni kani na bekyuli bani mɔɔbwɛ kɔwodu taawia kasiakɔ ni,
balakpi mɔɔdu-ma.
9Ukyuli ɔni na atabi na aabwɛ ni,
akana na aƒɔ ɔlɛ na ana bɔbwɛ kemmo.
Na si egyii lɛnɔ na aabwɛ ni,
ɔgbankpi ɔkana na ɔsiaku-ɔ.
10Oloma ɔni neeebo ɔbi ni,
amu ntu ébeyi ku ɔyikun momoomo.
Nsu si agyi-nwu kemmo ni,
adubɔbwɛ lɛla lɛni na aayɔ́ abwɛ.
11Si kɔlakpi kɔ́ɔdu ukyuli kɔ́wɔlɔ asa na ukyuli ɔni ngyi bɔkanti
ɔnii ɔɔbala-ku bɔdu ni, kekeeke na ɔdi.
12Ɔnundane etemila ani mɔɔlɛ́-nwu kenye aatina lɛƒɔndia.
Nsu ɔdɔlɔdi etemila mɔɔyila-nwu udu.
13Badɔlɔdi balabla kasusu si baatɛmi.
Na ɔmmɔ muuboku-ma ɔgbankpi na kawɔlɔkɔ.
14Na badɔlɔdi bammɔ
beemomo atɛ
nsu bula ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni masia.
Lɛni kani na bɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni ndubo kama.
15Ɔdɔlɔdi kabla ni, lɛlɔ butu bukpludi na bɔdi,
ɔsika ɔɔɔgyi ulu ɔni na ɔsia uduo ɔma.
16Kalɔ kani ɔtɔnkune mɔɔbla anamula
na bɔdi ku bɔni emeyi bɔdi kani na nwuna benengu belie bete ni,
bɔbuɛ na beete kalɔ kammɔ.
17Nsu kalɔ kani ɔtɔnkune ndi ukyuli ɔni náni ɔ́kɔ
na nwuna benengu baládi taani kani ni,
kalɔ kammɔ keesié anumi.
18Kɔkɔsɔ kuutulo bekyuli geen
ɔni na si ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo beli muedi uudú ni,
balakana na betile liƒi lɛmmɔ.
Na beenye taanu na ɔtɔ umodi ɔmmɔ ɔƒɛ uwi kalɔ.
19Bɔdi ku bɔni bɔɔyá na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ukyuli geen
nsu egulabi mɔɔbla lɛla biala.
20Tabɛ takya ƒula ɔtɔ kemmo na ataalɔ ɔga
iye ɔlakɛne ɔdi lɛnyi eteedumi na eteewida-nwu.
Ɔƒɛni kalɛ aasɛ blii ɔdi úveyi ɔɔví eli
na ɔdubuti-ɔ litemi utásu-ma.

english_text:
It Pays To Work Hard
1Be generous, and someday
you will be rewarded.
2Share what you have
with seven or eight others,
because you never know
when disaster may strike.
3Rain clouds always bring rain;
trees always stay
wherever they fall.
4If you worry about the weather
and don't plant seeds,
you won't harvest a crop.
5No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
6Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce.
Youth and Old Age
7Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun. 8Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
9Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
10Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_text:
Kogyoklo Bɔbla Kɔdia
1Taabla lɛƒɔndia
na adubɔkɛ ƒula lɛyuƒɔla limeyi lɛdi.
2Le lɛla lɛni na ákɛ
te nkyuli maatɛ ku maane ƒaa,
ɔsika aaagyi limeyi lɛni na
ayaki adi
adububo ebeyu-ɔ atu.
3Si ɔnantu ava bonwu bonwu
asia kayaa ni,
aana ɔnantu.
Na kesii biala na kugyii kɔ́ƒɛ kúsie ni,
mmɔ kani na kɔɔtɛ.
4Si áyia ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni muukpó ni,
alakana edula bɔkya,
lɛni kani na si ánu ɔnantu ava
na alakana edula bɔƒɛ.
5Kalɛ na ukyuli ɔɔɔgyi kesii kani na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ uukpó teesie
iye kalɛ na kaƒɔ keenwíni ubi na uleku kaƒɔ kemmo ni,
lɛni kani na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana Katɔti kalɔ bunu
kalɛ na ɔɔbla ala. Anwu nábla ala ƒui.
6Nye kabla lɛlɔ kpakplaa
na akya edula lɛdigye ku useyi uwi
ka aaagyi ani geen ndubo bɔdia
iye si ana ƒui madia.
7Lɛla lɛdi liládia bɔnu
teetulo ɔtanta ɔƒɛ ɔni nátu ɔdubo.
8Ina dɛ na élie ábi lɛlɔ ni,
ya na lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-ɔ na ƒula ngba emeyi ƒui kemmo.
Ɔsika ɔƒɛ ɔdubo ubasa ɔkya-a
na asɔ akya lɛdisa lɛmmɔ kemmo na uwi utu.
Na kalɔ bunu bɔdi buuubo ɔmɛni kemmo.
Bɔlɛ Úte Bakloƒu
9Lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-ɔ na ƒula lɛkloƒu uwi
na enu ngba emini.
Na teni lɛbuni biala na ánu
iye ƒula kayi kaayɔ́ tete lɛlɔ.
Nsu tayiƒala ka Katɔti ɔdubɔtɛku-ɔ litemi
na lɛla biala lɛni na ábla lɛlɔ.
10Taya na kasusu kekpoku-ɔ na ulu biala lɛlɔ
na akya lɛlɔ ɔlɛ,
ɔsika lɛkloƒu uwi ala abuni ammɔ
adubo abavi ɔƒɛni kani.

english_text:
1Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
2Someday the light of the sun
and the moon and the stars
will all seem dim to you.
Rain clouds will remain
over your head.
3Your body will grow feeble,
your teeth will decay,
and your eyesight fail.
4The noisy grinding of grain
and the voices of singers
will be shut out
by your deaf ears,
but even the song of a bird
will keep you awake.
5You will be afraid
to climb up a hill
or walk down a road.
Your hair will turn as white
as almond blossoms.
You will feel lifeless
and drag along
like an old grasshopper.
We each go to our eternal home,
and the streets here are filled
with those who mourn.
6The silver cord snaps,
the golden bowl breaks;
the water pitcher is smashed,
and the pulley at the well
is shattered.
7So our bodies return
to the earth,
and the life-giving breath
returns to God.
8Nothing makes sense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense.
Respect and Obey God
9I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied. 10Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
11Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together. 12My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these.
There is no end to books,
and too much study
will wear you out.
13Everything you were taught can be put into a few words:
Respect and obey God!
This is what life
is all about.
14God will judge
everything we do,
even what is done in secret,
whether good or bad.
translation_text:
1Taakali ƒula udiene lɛlɔ taanu uwi biala
na ƒula lɛkloƒu uwi!
Ɔsika uwi ɔdubo ɔni na
kayawi ala adubukpi-ɔ ɔkwɛ
na etila ani nsia-a lɛlɔ ɔsu.
2Uwi ɔdubo ɔni na ɔƒɛ ku kɔbuli
ku ayabi bukeye ƒui bɔdubɔbla-a suu.
Na kayaa kadubɔbla-a aani ɔnantu kadi
na ƒula eli.
3Ƒula lɛlɔ ekpo adubɔyɔ na abla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.
Na ƒula kenye anyi ese kalɔ atayii udu.
Na ƒula anumi asɔ alanu nwaa.
4Ƒula atu asɔ aaadubo buteenu kaduɛ
na ina kukɔ mɔɔkɔ́ ala muedi asɔ elénu.
Nsu aasɛ ɔnu budie muedi bɔdubɔya
na ekeyi lɛlɔ agyinya.
5Adubo butaayia ina lɛbinkpo na aakɔ́ iye bɔyu
na ada ulu ɔni nénwini ɔ́yu.
Ƒula lili linwini lɛdubɔta lɛƒuala
aani kɔdingyii anwula ƒuala ƒuala.
Na adubɔkɛ ataakpɛ lɛgba kalɔ aani kɔɔgyu
kɔni náabi na ɔɔyɔ́ ɔvumana livuo.
Bula ƒui bɔdubɔsɔ bunwini busie bula kasikɔ
na bekyuli bani muuwulo-bu
baƒɔ lɛblɔnu lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.
6Nyimo ƒula Udiene asa na lɛkun lɛni nda-a
aani ɔkun mmɔ ukulo
iye sika ugyiedi lɛkyami lɛni náƒɔ-ɔ kuye mmɔ lɛbwɛ,
iye ƒula ketubui kabwɛ
iye ɔbuli ɔni na eeti taani ntu
taalɛku libiɔ kemmo mmɔ ukulo.
7Lɛni na bula ɔlɔna ɔɔsɔ teenwini teesie kalɔ kemmo
na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni nkya-bu lɛlɔ kemmo uute-bu ngba mmɔ
ɔsɔ uunwíni teesie Katɔti kudɔ.
8Ami lɛ́ɛnu lɛ́ti ka lɛla lɛdi
liiibo kalɔ bunu bɔdi.
9Ndi ala ɔtinane ɔni muunú ala kalɔ geen na lɛ́da anu na lɛ́sala agba adi na líduo mu kemmo kaduɛ. 10Ɔmmɔ kama lɛ́kya ɔkplu na lídie-mu kalɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kalɛ na ɔ́manku.
11Lɛnunda etemila ese aani ugyii ɔni na umonsene uuti taakpanku nwuna bebuo. Asugba amɛni ási Katɔti ɔlati kudɔ na ese kɔbuɛlɛ ani na beeti taakana ligyii taadanku lɛlɔ. 12Ubi, mɔɔlɛ-ɔ kpakplaa nnii die ala bɔtina bamba biala atu na eti bɔmɛni kani.
Lɛku liiibo kawɔlɔkɔ. Na ala ƒui bulie taatɛya lɛnɔ ɔɔyá na ukyuli ɔɔyii udu.
13Ala ani ƒui na bátina-a ni,
akana na asala-nya akya
etemila klo klo amɛni kemmo anini,
“Di Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ na abu-nwu.
Lɛla lɛni ƒui na ngba bumodi bɔmmɔ
bɔdanku kani na lɛdi mmɔ.”
14Katɔti ɔdubɔtɛku-bu litemi
na lɛla biala na ukyuli ɔ́bla lɛlɔ
ina bɔbɛ na ábɛ ábla-nya
na adi likpidi iye lɛbuni.

english_text:
Love Is Better than Wine
1 This is Solomon's
most beautiful song.
She Speaks:
2Kiss me tenderly!
Your love is better than wine,
3and you smell so sweet.
All the young women adore you;
the very mention of your name
is like spreading perfume.
* 4Hurry, my king! Let's hurry.
Take me to your home.
The Young Women Speak:
We are happy for you!
And we praise your love
even more than wine.
She Speaks:
Young women of Jerusalem,
it is only right
that you should adore him.
5My skin is dark and beautiful,
like a tent in the desert
or like Solomon's curtains.
6Don't stare at me
just because the sun
has darkened my skin.
My brothers were angry with me;
they made me work in the vineyard,
and so I neglected
my complexion.
7My darling, I love you!
Where do you feed your sheep
and let them rest at noon?
Don't let the other shepherds
think badly of me.
I'm not one of those women
who shamelessly follow
after shepherds.
He Speaks:
8My dearest, if you don't know,
just follow the path
of the sheep.
Then feed your young goats
near the shepherds' tents.
9You move as gracefully
as the pony that leads
the chariot of the king.
10Earrings add to your beauty,
and you wear a necklace
of precious stones.
11Let's make you some jewelry
of gold, woven with silver.
She Speaks:
12My king, while you
were on your couch,
my aroma was a magic charm.
13My darling, you are perfume
between my breasts;
14you are flower blossoms
from the gardens of En-Gedi.
He Speaks:
15My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
your eyes are those of a dove.
She Speaks:
16My love, you are handsome,
truly handsome—
the fresh green grass
will be our wedding bed
17in the shade of cedar
and cypress trees.
translation_text:
Ɔnu Ute Ɔyɔne
1Salomo lɛnu ƒui ɔnu ɔni na ɔ́nwi na bɔdubo bunu mɛni.
2Bo na abakya-mi kɔgbu na ada-mi amana lɛlɔ.
Ɔsika ƒula bɔyɔ bɔɔyɔ́ kayi teetulo ntɛ.
3Ebo ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔdi ɔni na si línu ka ɔdi ɔ́kpali-ɔ lɛnyi ni,
na ɔnyi ɔmmɔ kani na muunú.
Na unyeƒi ɔdi uuubo-nwu kemmo
ka ɔmmɔ ɔsu geen na begblebi ƒui baayɔ́-ɔ!
4Kpanku-mi da na bɔtɔlɔ pla!
Na awɔ ɔga eti-mi eduoku ƒula kɔtɔma.
Lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-bu na ƒula lɛlɔ.
Na kalɛ na aayɔ́ bekyuli ubo emini utulo ntɛ mini mini.
Ɔdia geen ka bemwi-ɔ.
5Yerusalem beleku, ɔlɔgyii otondi na ɔdi-mi,
nsu mɔɔdia bɔnu geen.
Na nse aani kevo kani na bátu
bényene Kedar ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo
iye Salomo kayakun aduni abuni ammɔ adi.
6Bitanu-mi ɔnusɛ bɛnii
lɛ́sɔ ka ɔƒɛ ɔ́ya na
mina ɔlɔgyii ɔdi otondi ɔsu.
Mina benibi bananabi béti kɔnyi bákya-mi
na báya na mɔɔbla kabla na adingyii kemo
na lídie mina ɔlɔna atu na nsɔ lɛɛɛdaku-nwu lɛda.
7Ɔyɔne, su-mi kesii kani na adubuti ƒula bebuo esienku
na batádi ku kesii kani na badubɔtɛ banwuna ɔƒiiwi.
8Beleku babuni ƒui ɔbuni,
bɔsu na ada anii aaagyi kesii kammɔ?
Amu ni, Ɔyɔne, siaku baƒonu bammɔ agyobi kanyakɔ
na etiku ƒula bese na batádi na baƒonu badane nvo anumi.
9Aanya kalɔ ligblebi kemmo aani ɔpɔnkɔ
ɔni mɔɔní Ɔga Ƒarao kɛɛkɛ.
10Asɛɛ ebi ani nkya-a atu ku kɔsɛɛ kɔni na akya ɔkwɛ
áya na ƒula litugya liikeye na aadia bɔnu geen.
11Nsu bɔdubɔvɔ sika ugyiedi asɛɛ ebi ani na akya atu bute-ɔ
na bɔkya-nwu bɔdia ku sika ɔƒualadi.
12Mina ɔga, uwi ɔni na elie kadikɔ na ƒula liboku kemmo ni,
mina ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ɔ́ƒɔ ntɛ mmɔ ƒui.
13Mina ɔyɔne use ute-mi aani ugyulo ɔni baalɔ nard ɔsii
na ɔtɛ-mi anyii lɛlɔ.
14Na úlieku egyii anwula abuni ani muudie ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ
taasiku egyiibi kemo na kesii kani baalɔ En-Gedi.
15Ɔbuni, ése álɛ ligblebi na aadia bɔnu geen.
Na ƒula anumi eekeyi aani lɛmangbɛ.
16Ɔyɔne, lɛni na álɛ lɛkloƒu geen ɔni na balásu.
Livo lɛwɔdi lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ wɔwɔɔwɔ,
mmɔ ndubɔbla bula katɛnkɔ si búti lɛlɔ.
17Kesii kani na bɔkya ni, egyii enengudi
ani nnye mmɔ ákya ɔyuli.

english_text:
Love Makes Everything Beautiful
She Speaks:
1I am merely a rose
from the land of Sharon,
a lily from the valley.
He Speaks:
2My darling, when compared
with other young women,
you are a lily among thorns.
She Speaks:
3And you, my love,
are an apple tree
among trees of the forest.
Your shade brought me pleasure;
your fruit was sweet.
4You led me to your banquet room
and showered me with love.
5Refresh and strengthen me
with raisins and apples.
I am hungry for love!
6Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
7Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Winter Is Past
She Speaks:
8I hear the voice
of the one I love,
as he comes leaping
over mountains and hills
9like a deer or a gazelle.
Now he stands outside our wall,
looking through the window
10and speaking to me.
He Speaks:
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
11Winter is past,
the rain has stopped;
12flowers cover the earth,
it's time to sing.
The cooing of doves
is heard in our land.
13Fig trees are bearing fruit,
while blossoms on grapevines
fill the air with perfume.
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
14You are my dove
hiding among the rocks
on the side of a cliff.
Let me see how lovely you are!
Let me hear the sound
of your melodious voice.
15Our vineyards are in blossom;
we must catch the little foxes
that destroy the vineyards.
She Speaks:
16My darling, I am yours,
and you are mine,
as you feed your sheep
among the lilies.
17Pretend to be a young deer
dancing on mountain slopes
until daylight comes
and shadows fade away.
translation_text:
1Buse na mina ligblebi lise aani eveteli ku anwula gyie gyie
ani nálɛ enye sɛsɛɛ na Saron kalɔ lɛlɔ,
na nsɔ nse aani eveteli ku anwula ƒuala ƒuala
na ɔkwalɛ ɔdi kemmo.
2Ɔbuni, si banii beti-ɔ bakɔku begblebi bamba ni,
ese aani eveteli ku anwula ƒuala ƒuala
ani nédie lɛlɔ sɛsɛɛ na liyu alakpi akɔ.
3Na awɔ ni, mina Ɔyɔne, lɛni na álɛ salalaa
aani kɔdingyii na lɛku kemmo egyii akɔ
si béti-ɔ bákɔku banana bamba.
Na ƒula ɔyuli ɔni na ákya-mi ɔ́ya na lɛ́nwuna buɛɛ.
Na ƒula ebi ani na éte-mi na lɛ́di áyu-mi emini geen.
4Átɔnku-mi éduoku ƒula ɔtɔ bonwu
ɔni kemmo na aadi ƒula limeyi bɔdi adila.
Na mmɔ nédie ƒula bɔyɔ átina-mi.
5Te-mi ƒula egyiibi buni lidu lidu lɛmmɔ
na asɔku-mi abla ɔwɔdi na lɛkɛ ɔyikun ɔwɔdi,
ɔsika ƒula bɔyɔ kɔka kɔɔda-mi na lɛ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.
6Ti ƒula kɔmiinu kɔnu kya-mi
lili kalɔ
na eti ƒula kɔdianu kɔnu abala-mi kayi.
7Yerusalem begblebi,
muubó-mii ɔda
ɔkɛnku bakwa ku bete
ɔyikun lɛlɔ,
na bise-mi kenye ka bɛɛɛdubo busie butágyila tɔ bɔyɔ
wetédu ka uwi údu ka ulu ɔ́lɛmi úte bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ alati.
8Muunú mina ɔyɔne kɔku ka ɔ́si ɔdubo
na ɔkɛ ɔɔba agyu taavia abi ku abinkpo.
9Ɔkɛ aani akwa iye kete ɔdubo.
Na ɔƒaani ni, unye kowodu kama na ɔɔnu taavinku ƒansili.
10Na ɔɔtɛmiku-mi ɔnini,
“Ɔbuni, ta na asiaku-mi.
11Nu, ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ku ɔnantu uwi ɔ́ɔvi,
12na egyii anwula lidu áƒɔ kayawi ƒui,
na ɔdi lɛlɔyɔ uwi ute ala ƒui ku lɛnu budie.
Na beenú bamangbɛ kudu bɔbla na aku kemmo.
13Anwingyie eesé kalɔ ku bɔnwu
na egyiibi anwula ɔnyi ɔmmɔ ɔɔƒɔ́ kayaa ƒui aani ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ.
Ɔbuni, mɔɔyɔ́-ɔ geen! Anwuɔsu ya na bula inyɔ bɔtɔlɔ.”
14Ese ete-mi aani mina lɛmangbɛ lɛni nábɛla lɛlɔ
ɔkya atabi ubu kemmo na lɛtakpɛ bonwu lɛni nƒa kemmo.
Nwini na aya na lɛsɔ lɛnu ƒula bɔdia!
Na aya na linu ƒula lɛdi mini mini lɛmmɔ.
15Bula adingyii ebi kemo kani na búse éwi anwula,
anwuɔsu ɔlɛka buƒie beƒukutu
bani nkya muubile kemo kammɔ edula.
16Mina Ɔyɔne, awɔ ɔni mɔɔnyuɛ ƒula baƒonu
na eveteli ani nédie
anwula akɔ,
awɔ mbo-mi na ami lɛnɔ
mbo-ɔ.
17Bla lɛlɔ aani akwa ɔkɔdi ɔni nnye abi lɛlɔ ɔɔƒulu ku lɛlɔyɔ
úti útédu uwi ɔni na kadi kadubugye na ala ɔyuli ɔ́yii ɔkya.

english_text:
Beautiful Dreams
She Speaks:
1While in bed at night,
I reached for the one I love
with heart and soul.
I looked for him,
but he wasn't there.
2So I searched through the town
for the one I love.
I looked on every street,
but he wasn't there.
3I even asked the guards
patrolling the town,
“Have you seen the one
I love so much?”
4Right after that, I found him.
I held him and would not let go
until I had taken him
to the home of my mother.
5Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles,
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
The Groom and the Wedding Party
Their Friends Speak:
6What do we see approaching
from the desert
like a cloud of smoke?
With it comes the sweet smell
of spices, including myrrh
and frankincense.
7It is King Solomon
carried on a throne,
surrounded by sixty
of Israel's best soldiers.
8Each of them wears a sword.
They are experts at fighting,
even in the dark.
9The throne is made of trees
from Lebanon.
10Its posts are silver,
the back is gold,
and the seat is covered
with purple cloth.
You women of Jerusalem
have taken great care
to furnish the inside.
11Now come and see the crown
given to Solomon by his mother
on his happy wedding day.
translation_text:
1Uwi ɔni na bɔtɛ usien ni, lísienku kɔnu
nnii muutúku mina ɔyɔne
ɔni na mɔɔyɔ́ ku mina kayi ku kɔyu ƒui.
Nsu ɔɔɔtɛ, anwuɔsu líbo kɔnu lɛ́nɔ na ńtanu-nwu.
2Anwuɔsu lɛ́ta ńtávi ɔma kemmo
lɛ́wia-nwu na lɛblɔnu ƒui lɛlɔ, nsu ńtanu-nwu.
3Líye bagyumane bani nkɛ mɔɔkɔ́ taayu
na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo muedi nnini,
“Bɛ́nu ukyuli ɔni na mɔɔyɔ́
ku mina kayi ku kɔyu ƒui mmɔ?”
4Nsu mina mmɔ bɔgyu
ku tagyu kani
na lɛ́nu-nwu na lɛ́tu lɛ́da-nwu,
na ńtanyonu-nwu úti útédu uwi ɔni na lɛ́kpanku-nwu
lísienku mina uni kaduli,
na búduo ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na báwɔ-mi.
5Yerusalem begblebi,
muubó-mii ɔda
ɔkɛnku bakwa ku bete ɔyikun lɛlɔ,
na bise-mi kenye ka bɛɛɛdubo busie butágyila tɔ bɔyɔ
wetédu ka uwi údu ka ulu ɔ́lɛmi úte bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ alati.
6Ukyuli ɔmani na bɔɔnu ka ɔ́si kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ
ɔdubo mɛni aani liƒlukutu uyɔ ɔdi udu?
Uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔdanku nard ugyulo ku oloƒui
ku kutu akyala ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔnyi.
7Bɛnu! Salomo na ɔdi na badanku badububoku
na uli nwuna lɛgaboku lɛlɔ,
na Israelƒuɔ bekpone benengudi ƒui liti ku leevu
báka bámana-nwu.
8Kewii kama ɔdi biala ligu.
Na badi bekyuli bani na kekpo káma-ma enu
ɔni na usien muedi benye kagyumana bete lɛla biala.
9Lebanon egyii na béti bánwi lɛga boku lɛmmɔ.
10Liboku lɛmmɔ lɛgba lɛdi sika ɔƒualadi
na nina kama kekpokɔ kadi sika ugyiedi.
Na liboku lɛmmɔ alati egu keliekɔ geen ni,
kɔdi kugyiedi kɔni náƒɔ kuye geen
na béti bébi keliekɔ kammɔ.
