12God said, “Ezekiel, do you see what horrible things Israel's leaders are doing in secret? They have filled their rooms with idols. And they say I can't see them, because they think I have already deserted Israel. 13But I will show you something even worse than this.”
14He took me to the north gate of the temple, where I saw women mourning for the god Tammuz. 15God asked me, “Can you believe what these women are doing? But now I want to show you something even worse.”
16I was then led into the temple's inner courtyard, where I saw about 25 men standing near the entrance, between the porch and the altar. Their backs were to the Lord's temple, and they were bowing down to the rising sun.
17God said, “Ezekiel, it's bad enough that the people of Judah are doing these disgusting things. But they have also spread violence and injustice everywhere in Israel and have made me very angry. They have disgraced and insulted me in the worst possible way. 18So in my fierce anger, I will punish them without mercy and refuse to help them when they cry out to me.”
translation_text:
Esekiel Ɔ́nu Lɛƒiɔkpa Na Kakpakɔ Kemmo
1Uwi ɔni na béti Ɔga Yehoiakim ku abu bakladi bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ kama akwa aku ni, Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune béteebo-mi kudɔ na mina kesii taabasiaku-mi na mmɔ. Na kɔbuli kɔkundi limeyi lɛlɔndi lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikun ɔ́ƒɔ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui 2na lɛ́nu lɛla lɛdi aani ukyuli ɔyawine. Na ɔ́si nwuna kavobi mmɔ ɔ́yu ubo nwuna lɛgba kakɛ ni, use aani ogya. Na ɔ́si-nwu kavobi úti ɔ́kɔ úsie nwuna lili kakɛ use aani lɛbuala lɛni na békuo-ni kede kede na liikeye geen. 3Na lɛ́nu aani si kɔnu na údie na ɔ́da-mi linwini. Na mina kɔyu kemmo ala bɔnu bɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Unwoti Kɔyu kútiku-mi kúsienku kayaa na úti-mi úsienku Yerusalem.
Kɔyu kɔmmɔ kúti-mi kúsienku kakpakɔ kaduli geen kemmo na ɔban kayakun kani nkya kɔtɔ kakɛ mmɔ. Na lɛ́nu ka bávɔ baƒiɔ badi bálɛ bani muusé Unwoti lɛlɔ na ɔ́ya na úti kɔnyi kpakplaa geen. 4Ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛ́nu ka Israel Katɔti bukeye bɔ́ƒɔ mmɔ aani kalɛ na lɛ́nu na Keba Ketu kɔtu.
5Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, nwini nu katɔ kakɛ.” Amu ka línwini lɛ́nu ni, lɛ́nu baƒiɔ bani muusé lɛlɔ mmɔ ka balɛ bede lɛkpabi lɛni nlɛ katɔ kakɛ mmɔ kudɔ.
6Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ánu kɔbɔ ala ani muusé lɛlɔ ani na Israelƒuɔ baabla? Bana alaekpidi amɛni aayá na mina kakpakɔ keesé lɛlɔ na mmɔ kasɔ kaaadia keeete ka bakpa-mi. Na adubo ala ani nébie étulo amɛni muedi bɔnu.”
7Ɔmmɔ kama ni, béti-mi bésienku kaduli kammɔ ɔban kenye na lɛ́nu ka báƒuaala liƒi lɛdi na kowodu kɔmmɔ kemmo.
8Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Bla liƒi lɛmmɔ na libomo libu.” Na ka lɛ́bla lɛni ni, lɛ́nu ka kayakun na kadi.
9Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Sia duo mmɔ na anu kɔbɔ ala ku alaekpidi ani udu na bekyuli baabla mmɔ.”
10Na ka líduo ni, lɛ́nu ka bátaa ala lidu lɛni mɔɔkpɛ́ kaƒɔ kalɔ ku bebuo babambadi bani neeese sɛɛn na beesé lɛlɔ lɛnɔ básia awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na bátaa baƒiɔ bamba bani na Israelƒuɔ baakpá lɛnɔ básia mmɔ. 11Ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Yaasania na ɔdi Saƒan ubidi ɔnanabi ku Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune bamba bani ndubɔbla nkyuli liti ku aavlanyɔ benye mmɔ na ɔdi biala ɔda oloƒui bɔkyula kɔlɛkɛ unye na ɔnyi ɔmmɔ ɔ́ƒɔ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui.
12Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Esekiel, aanu kɔbɔ alaekpidi ani udu na Israel kadi batɔnkune bɔmmɔ benye baabla taabɛ? Bávɔ baƒiɔ béyile bana lɛtɔ kemmo bálɛ na baasu banii lɛɛɛdubo-ma bɔnu, ɔsika baakali banii líidie Israel atu kukuuku. 13Nsu nsɔ ndubo-ɔ lɛla lɛni návi ntu litulo amɛni bɔtina.”
14Ɔ́kpanku-mi úsienku ɔban kayakun kani na katɔ kakɛ na ńtanu ka beleku badi belie beewulo Tamus baƒiɔ. 15Katɔti úye-mi ɔnini, “Áƒɔ adi anii Israel beleku ndubɔbla lɛmɛni udu? Nsu awɔ bo na abanu ani násɔ ébie étulo ɔmmɔ.”
16Ɔmmɔ kama bákpanku-mi bésienku kakpakɔ kaduli geen kebliidi kemmo kesii kani na lɛ́nu ka banana aavlanyɔ-ɛlɔ benye bede kayakun kammɔ na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ keyi ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kaƒɔkɔ ntɛ na bénwini kama bákya Unwoti kakpakɔ kammɔ na benye beebó kalɔ teete ɔƒɛ ɔni nátu ɔdubo mmɔ.
17Mmɔ na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ɔdi likpidi geen ka Yuda kadi bekyuli benye baabla ala ani muuƒí livo mɛni udu. Na ɔɔɔdi amɛni lɛti mmomu etemila tatɛ ulu lɛlɔ ku kalala káaƒɔ Israel kalɔ kemodi kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui kesi kesii na bákya-mi kɔnyi geen. Na ulu ukpidi ƒui ɔni lɛlɔ na badubɔsia na bakya-mi kɔƒa na bedumi-mi na ɔdi mɛni. 18Anwuɔsu ami lɛnɔ kɔnyi kpakplaa kemmo na ndubo-ma kɔtu bɔni na lɛɛɛdubo-ma kɔnyana bɔnu munu munu. Na si ina baava taakpali-mi teevele muedi lɛɛɛdubo bunu bute-ma.”

english_text:
The Lord Gives the Command To Punish Jerusalem
1After that, I heard the Lord shout, “Come to Jerusalem, you men chosen to destroy the city. And bring your weapons!”
2I saw six men come through the north gate of the temple, each one holding a deadly weapon. A seventh man dressed in a linen robe was with them, and he was carrying things to write with. The men went into the temple and stood by the bronze altar.
3The brightness of God's glory then left its place above the statues of the winged creatures inside the temple and moved to the entrance. The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, 4 “Walk through the city of Jerusalem and mark the forehead of anyone who is truly upset and sad about the terrible things that are being done here.”
5-6He turned to the other six men and said, “Follow him and put to death everyone who doesn't have a mark on their forehead. Show no mercy or pity! Kill men and women, parents and children. Begin here at my temple, but be sure not to harm those who are marked.”
The men immediately killed the leaders who were standing there.
7Then the Lord said, “Pollute the temple by piling the dead bodies in the courtyards. Now get busy!” They left and started killing the people of Jerusalem.
8I was then alone, so I bowed down and cried out to the Lord, “Why are you doing this? Are you so angry with the people of Jerusalem that everyone must die?”
9The Lord answered, “The people of Israel and Judah have done horrible things. Their country is filled with murderers, and Jerusalem itself is filled with violence. They think that I have deserted them, and that I can't see what they are doing. 10And so I will not have pity on them or forgive them. They will be punished for what they have done.”
11Just then, the man in the linen robe returned and said, “I have done what you commanded.”
translation_text:
Bádu Baƒiɔ Bakpane
1Na ala amɛni kama ni, línu ka Unwoti údie lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Amii bani na báƒuna bése ka bɛkyula ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni ni, bibo Yerusalem mɛni ku bina ekpola!” 2Amu na lɛ́nu banana ɛku badi ka bási kayakun katɔdi kammɔ bálɛ na bada ekpola ekpidi. Na ukyuli maatɛdi ɔdi ɔsiaku-ma na ɔkya awu ƒuala ƒuala gyɔlɔɔ na ɔda ala ani na ɔkana na uti unweni ala. Na bekyuli bammɔ béduo bésie kakpakɔ kemmo na béténye lɛbuala ligyiedi lɛbi lɛmmɔ kudɔ.
3Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti bukeye bɔmmɔ bɔ́ta bebweyi bani na bávɔ bényene kakpakɔ mmɔ na bebo avwi mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na búnwini búsie kayakun mmɔ. Na Unwoti ɔ́su ukyuli ɔni na ɔkya awu gyɔlɔɔ mmɔ ɔnini, 4“Sie vi ɔma Yerusalem ɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo na abla likposela asia ukyuli biala geen na alaekpidi ani na baabla na ɔma ɔmɛni kemmo aadá-nwu ɔƒɛ lɛtɛntɛ.”
5-6Amu na únwini na ɔ́su nkyuli ɛku bakladi ɔnini, “Bɛsiaku-nwu kama na bɛdu ukyuli biala na uuubo likposela lɛmmɔ na nwuna lɛtɛntɛ. Na bitanu ɔdi biala kɔnyana! Bɛdu banana ku beleku ku bawɔne ku bana bebi. Bise kalɔ bɛsiku mina kakpakɔ kemmo mɛni, nsu bɛsia anumi kaduɛ na biládu ukyuli ɔni na ubo likposela lɛmmɔ na nwuna lɛtɛntɛ.”
Kɔnakunwi ni, banana bammɔ bádu batɔnkune bani nnye kakpakɔ ɔtɔ kemmo mmɔ.
7Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bibile kakpakɔ kammɔ ekisila na bɛla bekpine bammɔ bɛsiaku lɛlɔ na kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ kemmo mmɔ. Bɛsɔ bitebile uwi ɔdi bise kabla kalɔ!” Bátɔlɔ mmɔ na bése kalɔ baadú Yerusalemƒuɔ bammɔ. 8Na ami lɛti nébu mmɔ na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo, anwuɔsu líbo kalɔ na lívele Unwoti nnini, “Bi ɔsu na aabla ala amɛni udu? Bubo na ƒula kɔnyi kúbo kɔ́vi kútédu kesii kani na ɔya na Yerusalemƒuɔ ƒui bekpi?”
9Amu na Unwoti údie kenye ɔnini, “Israel ku Yuda kadi bekyuli bábla ekpidi ani ndi ekisila geen. Na bekyuli badune béyii kalɔ kammɔ kemmo na Yerusalem alati ni, kalala kábɔ mmɔ geen na baakali ka lídie-ma atu ɔsu naaanu ala ani na baabla. 10Anwuɔsu lɛɛɛdubo-ma kɔnyana bɔnu iye liti lɛkyiɛ-ma lɛnɔ. Ndubo-ma kɔtu bɔni na ala ani na bábla kenye.”
11Uwi útetu asa na ukyuli ɔni nkya awu gyɔlɔɔ mmɔ únwini úbo na úbasu ɔnini, “Lɛ́bla lɛla lɛni na ásu-mi anii mbla.”

english_text:
The Lord's Glory Leaves the Temple
1 I saw the dome that was above the four winged creatures, and on it was the sapphire throne. 2 The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, “Walk among the four wheels beside the creatures and pick up as many hot coals as you can carry. Then scatter them over the city of Jerusalem.” I watched him as he followed the Lord's instructions.
3The winged creatures were standing south of the temple when the man walked among them. A cloud filled the inner courtyard, 4and the brightness of the Lord's glory moved from above the creatures and stopped at the entrance of the temple. The entire temple was filled with his glory, and the courtyard was dazzling bright. 5The sound of the creatures' wings was as loud as the voice of God All-Powerful and could even be heard in the outer courtyard.
6The man in the robe was now standing beside a wheel. 7One of the four creatures reached its hand into the fire among them and gave him some of the hot coals. The man took the coals and left.
8I noticed again that each of the four winged creatures had what looked like human hands under their wings, 9 and I saw the four wheels near the creatures. These wheels were shining like chrysolite. 10Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it, 11so that they could move in any direction without turning. The wheels moved together whenever the creatures moved. 12 I also noticed that the wheels and the creatures' bodies, including their backs, their hands, and their wings, were covered with eyes. 13And I heard a voice calling these “the wheels that spin.”
14 Each of the winged creatures had four faces: the face of a bull, the face of a human, the face of a lion, and the face of an eagle. 15-17These were the same creatures I had seen near the Chebar River. They controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels stayed beside them.
18Then I watched the brightness of the Lord's glory move from the entrance of the temple and stop above the winged creatures. 19They spread their wings and flew into the air with the wheels at their side. They stopped at the east gate of the temple, and the Lord's glory was above them.
20I knew for sure that these were the same creatures I had seen beneath the Lord's glory near the Chebar River. 21-22They had four wings with hands beneath them, and they had the same four faces as those near the River. Each creature moved straight ahead without turning.
translation_text:
Unwoti Bukeye Bɔ́tɔlɔ Kakpakɔ Kammɔ Kemmo
1Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, lɛ́nu lɛla lɛni mbi bebweyi ine ku ngba ku ngba bammɔ eli. Na lɛla lɛni na nse aani lɛgaboku lɛni nse aani Saƒira lɛtabi lɛni muukeye mmɔ lɛlɛ. 2Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su ukyuli ɔni na ɔkya awu gyɔlɔɔ mmɔ ɔnini, “Sie vi kɛɛkɛ ebi ene ani nkya bebweyi bammɔ kalɔ mmɔ akɔ na edie ogya agyabi ani na adubɔkana bɔda. Na egyingya-nwu ewi Yerusalem ɔma enengudi ɔmmɔ ƒui.” Na nnye mɔɔnu kalɛ na ɔɔbla lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́tina-nwu ɔnii ɔbla mmɔ.
3Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, bebweyi bani mbo avwi mmɔ benye kakpakɔ kammɔ kada kakɛ ka asa na ukyuli ɔmmɔ úsie ɔ́vi-ma ntɛ. Na ulɔyɔ ɔdi ɔ́ƒɔ kakpakɔ kaduli geen kebliidi kammɔ kemmo mmɔ ƒui. 4Na Unwoti bukeye bɔni mɔɔtu anumi mmɔ bɔ́ta bebweyi bammɔ lɛlɔ na bútédi búnye kakpakɔ kammɔ kayakun. Na kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui keekeye na bukeye bɔni mɔɔtu anumi mmɔ bɔ́ƒɔ kaduli kammɔ kemmo ƒui. 5Na kɔku kɔni na bebweyi bammɔ avwi aabla aaku momoomo aani Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui lɛdi, na kɔɔku teesie kaduli kamaadi kemmo muedi.
6Na ukyuli ɔni na nkya awu gyɔlɔɔ mmɔ úubo úbedi unye kɛɛkɛ libi lɛdi kudɔ. 7Na bebweyi ine bammɔ akɔ unwi únene kɔnu na usienku ogya ɔni nnye mɔɔda na kɛɛkɛ ebi ammɔ ntɛ na údie ogya agyabi adi úte ukyuli ɔmmɔ na ɔ́tɔlɔ. 8Mmɔ na lɛ́nu lɛti ka bebweyi ine bani mbo avwi mmɔ ɔdi biala ubo enu aani bekyuli adi kalɛ na bana avwi ammɔ kalɔ.
9Na lɛ́nu ebi ammɔ lɛnɔ ka ede bebweyi bammɔ. Na ebi amɛni eekeye aani sika atabi bamba ani baalɔ Krisolit. 10Ebi ammɔ ƒui udu élieku lɛlɔ asa na ebi bamba éƒie ammɔ ntɛ ékulo na ɔdi biala ntɛ. 11Anwuɔsu aakana na eesié lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ, nsu balatu teenwini. Na ebi ammɔ ƒui eesié ku lɛlɔ uwi biala na bebweyi bammɔ beeveyi. 12Lɛ́nu lɛnɔ ka ebi ammɔ ku bebweyi bammɔ ɔlɔna kesii biala ku bana kama ku enu ku avwi ƒui ni, anumi áka ámana. 13Na línu ka lɛdi lɛdi lɛɛkpali taasu lɛnini, “Ebi ani muunwíni lɛlɔ.”
14Bebweyi ine bammɔ ɔdi biala ubo anumi na lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Ɔmantɛ akɔ anumi ku ukyuli anumi ku gyata anumi ku kɔdigbo aasɛ anumi.
15-17Na bebweyi bamɛni badi bani kani na lɛ́nu ka Kedar Ketu kudɔ mmɔ. Na anya mɔɔtina ebi ammɔ uwi ku kesii kani na ɔlɛka esie. Na si bebweyi bammɔ báta ni, ama ku ebi ammɔ mɔɔkɛ na si édi énye lɛnɔ na edi enye. Lɛni kani na si kayaa na béveyi baaví lɛnɔ na ebi ammɔ asiaku-ma.
18Amu na nnye mɔɔnu uwi ɔni na Unwoti bukeye bɔmmɔ bɔ́sɔ bɔ́gyu kakpakɔ kayakun mmɔ bɔ́tɔlɔ búsie bútédi búnye bebweyi ine bammɔ eli. 19Na bénene bana avwi na béveyi bésie kayaa na ebi ammɔ akɛ-ma kɔmadɔ. Bétédi bénye kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na Unwoti bukeye bɔmmɔ bɔkɛ-ma eli.
20Na ɔ́bla-mi nwaa ka bebweyi bamɛni kani na lɛ́nu na Kedar Ketu kɔmadɔ ka Unwoti bukeye bɔsiaku-ma na bana eli mmɔ. 21-22Bana ɔdi biala ubo avwi ene na bekyuli enu akya-nya kalɔ na bebo na anumi ene na lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ aani bani na ketu kɔtu mmɔ. Na ɔdi biala ɔɔtɔ nwuna anumi siin na ulenwiniku lɛlɔ.

english_text:
Ezekiel Condemns Jerusalem's Wicked Leaders
1The Lord's Spirit lifted me up and took me to the east gate of the temple, where I saw 25 men, including the two leaders, Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah. 2The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, these men are making evil plans and giving dangerous advice to the people of Jerusalem. 3They say things like, ‘Let's build more houses. This city is like a cooking pot over a fire, and we are the meat, but at least the pot keeps us from being burned in the fire.’ 4So, Ezekiel, condemn them!”
5The Lord's Spirit took control of me and told me to tell these leaders:
I, the Lord God, know what you leaders are saying. 6You have murdered so many people that the city is filled with dead bodies! 7This city is indeed a cooking pot, but the bodies of those you killed are the meat. And so I will force you to leave Jerusalem, 8and I'll send armies to attack you, just as you fear. 9Then you will be captured and punished by foreign enemies. 10You will be killed in your own country, but not before you realize that I, the Lord, have done these things.
11You leaders claim to be meat in a cooking pot, but you won't be protected by this city. No, you will die at the border of Israel. 12You will realize that while you were following the laws of nearby nations, you were disobeying my laws and teachings. And I am the Lord!
13Before I finished speaking, Pelatiah dropped dead. I bowed down and cried out, “Please, Lord God, don't kill everyone left in Israel.”
A Promise of Hope
14The Lord replied:
15Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in Jerusalem claim that you and the other Israelites who were taken to Babylonia are too far away to worship me. They also claim that the land of Israel now belongs only to them. 16But here is what I want you to tell the Israelites in Babylonia:
It's true that I, the Lord God, have forced you out of your own country and made you live among foreign nations. But for now, I will be with you wherever you are, so that you can worship me. 17And someday, I will gather you from the nations where you are scattered and let you live in Israel again. 18When that happens, I want you to clear the land of all those idols I hate so much. 19 Then I will take away your stubbornness and make you eager to be completely faithful to me. You will want to obey me 20and all my laws and teachings. You will be my people, and I will be your God. 21But those who worship idols will be punished and get what they deserve. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
The Lord's Glory Leaves Jerusalem
22 After the Lord had finished speaking, the winged creatures spread their wings and flew into the air, and the wheels were beside them. The brightness of the Lord's glory above them 23left Jerusalem and stopped at a hill east of the city.
24Then in my vision, the Lord's Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to the other exiles in Babylonia. The vision faded away, 25and I told them everything the Lord had shown me.
translation_text:
Esekiel Ɔ́du Yerusalemƒuɔ Batɔnkune Kɔtɔ
1Unwoti Kɔyu kɔmmɔ kútiku-mi kúsienku kakpakɔ kammɔ kayakun na ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ kesii kani na lɛ́nu banana aavlanyɔ-ɛlɔ úbunku Yaasania ku Asur ku Benaia ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ banii Pealatia. 2Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, bekyuli bamɛni bakya beeti kasusu kekpidi na baakya Yerusalemƒuɔ kasusu kekpidi kammɔ. 3Na ala ani bene na baasu adi ndi ɔnini, ‘Bɛya na bɔtu lɛtɔ na limomo libu. Bula ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni use aani libui lɛni nsia ogya. Na abu ndi lɛna lɛni nkya libui lɛmmɔ kemmo ɔni na libui lɛmmɔ liitile ogya ɔmmɔ kuƒi ka ɔkyula-bu.’ 4Anwuɔsu ni, Esekiel, du-ma kukpi kɔtɔ!”
5Unwoti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo na ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nsu batɔnkune bammɔ, “Ami Unwoti ngyi ala ani na amii batɔnkune bammɔ bɛɛsu. 6Bɛ́ɛdu bekyuli pii ɔni na bekpine báƒɔ ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ƒui!
7“Sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni ɔdi libui, nsu bekyuli bani na bɛ́du ɔlɔna ndi lɛna lɛmmɔ. Anwuɔsu ndubo-mii lɛlɔ bunye na lɛbɔku-mii lɛlɛku Yerusalem. 8Na ndubuti bekpone kasala limene na bekpo-mii kalɛ kani na amii alati bíise kalɔ bɛɛyia kukuuku mmɔ. 9Na kadi bamba bekpone badubo-mii buƒie na bani-mii kɔtu. 10Badubo-mii bɔdu na amii alati bina kalɔ lɛlɔ, nsu ndubo bɔya na bɛnu bɛti ka ami Unwoti nábla ala amɛni nwaa asa na badu-mii. 11Amii batɔnkune bammɔ bɛɛsu taatina ka lɛna na bɛdi bɛkya libui lɛmmɔ kemmo, nsu ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni ɔɔɔdubo-mii bɔgyumana. Kudii, bɛdubo bukpi na Israel ɔmii lɛlɔ. 12Bɛdubo bɔnu bɔti ka uwi ɔni na bɛsiaku kadi bamba bekyuli bani nde-mii mmɔ ɔda bubo kama mmɔ ni, bíni ami bɔdi ku ala ani na mɔɔtina. Nsu ami ndi Unwoti!”
13Uwi ɔni na ntaawɔlɔ bɔtɛmi kani na Petalia úbuli úbi kalɔ na úkpi. Líboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na lɛ́va ku lɛdi momoomo lɛ́su nnini, “Unwoti buvele bekyuli bani nébu bakya Israel ni, tadu bana ƒui.”
Linyese Lɛni Ndanku Lɛnunsia
14Amu na Unwoti údie kenye ɔnini, 15“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, bekyuli bani nkya Yerusalem baasu ka awɔ ku bekyuli bani ƒui na béƒie béboku Babilon mɛni bɛ́gyu kakyakɔ bɛ́gya, anwuɔsu bilakana-mi bɔkpa. Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ ni, Israel kalɔ kénwini ama lɛti ɔdi.
16“Nsu se atu na enu lɛla lɛni na mɔɔwia ka lɛsu Israelƒuɔ bani na nkya Babilon. Sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka ami Unwoti Katɔti nábɔku-mii lɛ́lɛku amii alati bina kalɔ lɛlɔ nnii bitélie kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ. Nsu ɔƒaani ndubulieku-mii kesii biala na bɛkya kalɛ bɛkana na bɛkpa-mi.
17“Na limeyi lɛdi ni, ndubo-mii bɔsala bɔsiku kɔlɔ kɔni lɛlɔ na bígyingya bɛkya na lɛya na bɛsɔ bibelie Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ.
18“Na si uwi ɔni na ala amɛni álɛ ni, ndubɔyɔ ka ada baƒiɔ ala ani muusé lɛlɔ mmɔ ƒui edie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. 19Na ndubɔda bina atuɔkplu bɔbla ƒui lidie-mii lɛlɔ na lɛya na anumi eteegyie-mii kalɛ na bɛsiaku-mii kama siin na biteenu-mi litemi 20na bitaadi mina ɔda bubo ku mina ala ani mɔɔtina-mii lɛlɔ. Na bɛdubɔbla mina kadi bekyuli na ami lɛbla bina Katɔti. 21Nsu bekyuli bani mɔɔkpá baƒiɔ ni, ndubo-ma kɔtɔ kɔni námanku-ma bɔni. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.”
Katɔti Bukeye Bɔ́tɔlɔ Yerusalem
22Amu ka Unwoti ɔ́wɔlɔ bɔtɛmi ni, bebweyi ine bammɔ bégyingya bana avwi na béveyi bésie kayaa na kɛɛkɛ ebi ammɔ akɛ-ma kɔmadɔ na Unwoti bukeye bɔkɛ-ma katɔ. 23Na bɔ́tɔlɔ Yerusalem búsie bútédi búnye abi adi eli na unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. 24Na mina kɔyu kemmo ala bɔnu uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Katɔti Kɔyu kútiku-mi na kɔ́sɔku-mi kúboku Babilon na mina bakpana bakladi bani na abu ku-ma na béƒie mmɔ kudɔ.
Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ala bɔnu bɔmmɔ bɔ́yii bɔ́kya. 25Na lɛ́sɔku ala ani ƒui na Unwoti údie ɔ́tina-mi ƒui lɛ́su-ma.

english_text:
Ezekiel Acts Out Israel's Captivity
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, you are living among rebellious people. They have eyes, but refuse to see; they have ears, but refuse to listen. 3So before it gets dark, here is what I want you to do. Pack a few things as though you were going to be taken away as a prisoner. Then go outside where everyone can see you and walk around from place to place. Maybe as they watch, they will realize what rebels they are. 4After you have done this, return to your house.
Later that evening leave your house as if you were going into exile. 5Dig through the wall of your house and crawl out, carrying the bag with you. Make sure everyone is watching. 6Lift the bag to your shoulders, and with your face covered, take it into the darkness, so that you cannot see the land you are leaving. All this will be a warning for the people of Israel.
7I did everything the Lord had said. I packed a few things. Then as the sun was going down, and while everyone was watching, I dug a hole through one of the walls of my house. I pulled out my bag, then lifted it to my shoulders and left in the darkness.
8The next morning, the Lord 9reminded me that those rebellious people didn't even ask what I was doing. 10So he sent me back to tell them:
The Lord God has a message for the leader of Jerusalem and everyone living there!
11I have done these things to show them what will happen when they are taken away as prisoners.
12The leader of Jerusalem will lift his own bag to his shoulders at sunset and leave through a hole that the others have dug in the wall of his house. He will cover his face, so he can't see the land he is leaving. 13 The Lord will spread out a net and trap him as he leaves Jerusalem. He will then be led away to the city of Babylon, but will never see that place, even though he will die there. 14His own officials and troops will scatter in every direction, and the Lord will track them down and put them to death.
15The Lord will force the rest of the people in Jerusalem to live in foreign nations, where they will realize that he has done all these things. 16Some of them will survive the war, the starvation, and the deadly diseases. That way, they will be able to tell foreigners how disgusting their sins were, and that it was the Lord who punished them in this way.
A Sign of Fear
17The Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, shake with fear when you eat, and tremble when you drink. 19Tell the people of Israel that I, the Lord, say that someday everyone in Jerusalem will shake when they eat and tremble when they drink. Their country will be destroyed and left empty, because they have been cruel and violent. 20Every town will lie in ruins, and the land will be a barren desert. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
The Words of the Lord Will Come True
21The Lord said:
22Ezekiel, son of man, you've heard people in Israel use the saying, “Time passes, and prophets are proved wrong.” 23Now tell the people that I, the Lord, am going to prove that saying wrong. No one will ever be able to use it again in Israel, because very soon everything I have said will come true! 24The people will hear no more useless warnings and false messages. 25I will give them my message, and what I say will certainly happen. Warn those rebels that the time has come for them to be punished. I, the Lord, make this promise.
26-27Ezekiel, the people of Israel are also saying that your visions and messages are only about things in the future. 28So tell them that my words will soon come true, just as I have warned. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Esekiel Ɔ́tina Israelƒuɔ Kalɛ Na Badubo-ma Buƒie Bɔtɔlɔku
1Unwoti ɔnini, 2“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, bekyuli bani mɔɔkya lɛsɛ akɔ na akya. Bebo anumi, nsu béni banii balanu baláti. Na bebo atu, nsu béni banii belese atu na benu.
3“Anwuɔsu asa na ɔƒɛ wasa ni, si atu na enu lɛla lɛni na mɔɔyɔ́ ka abla. Bo ƒula ala alɛɛ ani obo aani si buti bada-a batɔlɔku aani ɔtɔntɛne kalɛ. Na alɛ eténye kesii kani na ukyuli biala wanu-ɔ kaduɛ na akɛ eteesie taavi. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ si benye baanu lɛla lɛni na aabla ni, badubo bɔnu bɔti lɛsɛ bakyane bani udu na badi. 4Si uwi ɔni na ábla ɔmɛni áwɔlɔ ni, na enwini esie ƒula kaduli. Na ɔmmɔ kama si uwi ɔni na ɔ́bla usien ni, na avi alɛ kaduli aani si buƒie na béƒie-ɔ bátɔlɔku béselaku kalɔ bamba kadi lɛlɔ. 5Ya na ukyuli biala unye utaanu-ɔ asa na edie liƒi na ƒula ɔtɔ kowodu kɔdi kemmo na eti ƒula obo ada na akpɛ alɛ kowodu liƒi lɛmmɔ kemmo. 6Gyu ƒula obo ɔmmɔ sia ƒula amangba na eti lɛla lɛdi ebi anumi na alɛ eduo lɛdisa lɛmmɔ kemmo kalɛ na alanu ɔmii ɔni kemmo na ésela aláti. Na ala amɛni ƒui enwini Israelƒuɔ kati bute kpakplaa.”
7Amu na lɛ́bla ala ani ƒui na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnii mbla mmɔ. Lɛ́sala ala alɛɛ adi. Na uwi ɔni na ɔƒɛ úsela bɔni ni, na ukyuli biala lɛnɔ unye ɔɔnu-mi ni, lídie liƒi lɛdi na mina ɔtɔ kowodu kemmo. Na lɛ́ni mina obo lɛ́lɛku lɛ́sia mina lɛmangba na liduo kadi suu kammɔ kemmo.
8Kadi kegye ɔtanta ni, Unwoti 9únyimene-mi ka lɛsɛ bakyane bammɔ ɔdi biala utakana na uye lɛla lɛni na mɔɔbla mmɔ kalɔ.
10Anwuɔsu ɔ́sɔku-mi ɔ́tala ɔnii ntásu-ma ɔnini, “Unwoti ubo kenye kadi na ɔsu Yerusalem ɔtɔnkune ku bani na ɔtɔnku mmɔ ƒui! 11Lɛ́bla ala amɛni lɛ́tina-ma kalɛ na banu bati ala ani ndubo-ma bɔlɛku uwi ɔni na badubuti-ma batɔlɔku aani bekyuli beƒiedi kalɛ. 12Na Yerusalem ɔtɔnkune ɔdubuti nwuna obo ɔsia lɛmangba useyi uwi na ɔsia kowodu liƒi lɛni na bekyuli bamba bédie na nwuna ɔtɔ awodu kemmo. Na ɔdubuti lɛla lɛdi ubi nwuna anumi na uláti ɔmii ɔni lɛlɔ na úsela. 13Unwoti ɔla ndubo nwuna asawu bubo na udie-nwu uwi ɔni na ɔ́si ɔɔlɛ́ Yerusalem ɔma kemmo. Na ɔmmɔ kama na bakpanku-nwu besienku Babilon, nsu ɔɔɔdubo mmɔ bɔnu ku nwuna anumi kudii. 14Na badubo nwuna benengu alati ku nwuna bekpone bɔgyingya bɔkya kesii biala na Unwoti ɔdubo-ma budie ƒui bute unwi unwi na badu.
15“Na Unwoti ɔdubo bekyuli bani nébu bakya Yerusalem lɛlɔ bunye na babɔku-ma batákya kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ kesii kani na badubusie batánu bati ka ami nábla ala amɛni ƒui. 16Badi badubɔlɛ kekpo ku kɔka ku lɛlɛ likpidi enu kemmo. Na ama ndubo baƒɔ bammɔ bɔsu kalɛ na bábla ekpidi ani ndi ekisila bonwu bonwu ɔsu na Unwoti ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu lɛni.”
17Unwoti ɔnini, 18“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, ya na lɛlɔ litaatɔ-ɔ na kadikɔ ku liƒu na ƒula enu eteeboku lɛlɔ si aaní ntu. 19Su Israel kadi bekyuli anii ami Unwoti násu nnii limeyi lɛdi lɛdubo ɔni na lɛlɔ lɛdubo-ma butaatɔ si baadi na bana enu eteeboku lɛlɔ di baaní ntu. Na badubo kalɔ kammɔ ƒui udu bɔyila na ɔsɔ uwi ukpludi, ɔsika bábla ulikplu ku kalala geen. 20Badubo ɔma biala bubo bɔbwɛ na lɛla biala lɛsɔ liladia na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo, ɔsika kalɔ kammɔ kadubunwini kɔnwinimi kalɔ kakwiidi. Na badubo bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.”
Unwoti Etemila Adubudie Lɛlɔ Atina Ka Adi Etemila Geen
21Unwoti ɔnini, 22“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, eenú ka bekyuli beebó lɛgba lɛmɛni na Israel bubo bubo banini, ‘Lɛla biala uwi ɔɔví, na kenye bediene ala ani baanu muedi asɔ alalɛ kalɛ na básu.’ 23Na ɔƒaani ni, ya na kadi bekyuli bammɔ bati ka ni, ami Unwoti ndubo-ma ɔkɔ bɔsia ka lɛsugba lɛmmɔ lɛɛɛdi litemi geen na ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo bunwini lɛla lɛni na bataasu na Israel. Ɔsika uwi klukwii kemmo ni, mina etemila ani ƒui na lɛ́su adubo ete lɛni! 24Bekyuli bammɔ basɔ baaadubo etemila keeke ku ɔkɔ bɔlɛ bɔdi bunu. 25Ndubute-ma mina linyesia na ala ani na masu adubo bɔlɛ lɛni kani. Tɛmiku lɛsɛ bakyane bammɔ kpakplaa ka uwi údu ka bani-ma kɔtu. Ami Unwoti muusé kenye kamɛni.
26-27“Esekiel, Israel kadi bekyuli baasu lɛnɔ banii ƒula etemila ku kɔyu kemmo ala bɔnu ƒui bɔdanku uwi ɔni mebo kama kama.
28“Anwuɔsu su-ma anii mina etemila amɛni adubo-nwu kemmo lɛni uwi klukwii ɔmɛni kemmo kani aani kalɛ na lɛ́su-ma kpakplaa líse. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_text:
Lying Prophets
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the prophets of Israel who say they speak in my name, but who preach messages that come from their own imagination. Tell them it's time to hear my message.
3I, the Lord God, say those lying prophets are doomed! They don't see visions—they make up their own messages! 4Israel's prophets are no better than jackals that hunt for food among the ruins of a city. 5They don't warn the people about coming trouble or tell them how dangerous it is to sin against me. 6Those prophets lie by claiming they speak for me, but I have not even chosen them to be my prophets. And they still think their words will come true. 7They say they're preaching my messages, but they are full of lies—I did not speak to them!
8So I am going to punish those lying prophets for deceiving the people of Israel with false messages. 9I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. They will not be allowed to call themselves Israelites or even to set foot in Israel. Then they will realize that I am the Lord God.
10 Those prophets refuse to be honest. They tell my people there will be peace, even though there's no peace to be found. They are like workers who think they can fix a shaky wall by covering it with paint. 11But when I send rainstorms, hailstones, and strong winds, the wall will surely collapse. 12People will then ask the workers why the paint didn't hold it up.
13That wall is the city of Jerusalem. And I, the Lord God, am so angry that I will send strong winds, rainstorms, and hailstones to destroy it. 14The lying prophets have tried to cover up the evil in Jerusalem, but I will tear down the city, all the way to its foundations. And when it collapses, those prophets will be killed, and everyone will know that I have done these things.
15The city of Jerusalem and its lying prophets will feel my fierce anger. Then I will announce that the city has fallen and that the lying prophets are dead, 16because they promised my people peace, when there was no peace. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Women Who Wear Magic Charms
The Lord said:
17Ezekiel, son of man, now condemn the women of Israel who preach messages that come from their own imagination. 18Tell them they're doomed! They wear magic charms on their wrists and scarves on their heads, then trick others into believing they can predict the future. They won't get away with telling those lies. 19They charge my people a few handfuls of barley and a couple pieces of bread, and then give messages that are insulting to me. They use lies to sentence the innocent to death and to help the guilty go free. And my people believe them!
20I hate the magic charms they use to trick people into believing their lies. I will rip those charms from their wrists and set free the people they have trapped like birds. 21I will tear the scarves from their heads and rescue my people from their power once and for all. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.
22They do things I would never do. They lie to good people and encourage them to do wrong, and they convince the wicked to ruin their own lives by not turning from sin. 23I will no longer let these women give false messages and use magic, and I will free my people from their control. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Bádu Ɔkɔ Kenye Bediene Kɔtɔ
1Unwoti ɔnini,
2“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, du Israel kenye bediene kɔtɔ. Bekyuli bani na banii mina kenye na beedie na baasu ala na mina lɛnyi kemmo, nsu ama alati ala ani na baakali taanu ku kasusu etemila kudu na beebó. Na asu-ma ku uwi údu ka benu-mi litemi.
3“Ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu ka ɔkɔ kenye bediene bammɔ ɔdi ɔ́sa ɔƒaamu. Ɔsika ɔɔɔdi mina kɔyu kemmo ala na baanu mmomu bana kasusu kemmo ala kenye na beedie! 4Israel kenye bediene bátavumanaku beƒukutu bani mɔɔkɛ taawia adila na ɔma ɔni nábwɛ únwini aani kebu alakpi akɔ. 5Balálɛ bekyuli bammɔ kpakplaa taasu-ma ɔgbankpi ɔni ndubo-ma lɛlɔ iye lɛbibo lɛni na ekpidi ani na baabla taaƒiɔ-mi adanku. 6Kenye bediene bammɔ baanyi ɔkɔ taasu ka mina lɛnyi kemmo na baasu etemila, nsu ɔɔɔdi ami náƒuna-ma muedi. Na baakali ka bana etemila ammɔ adububo-nwu kemmo ete-ma kalɛ na básu. 7Baasu ka mina etemila lɛsa na baakɔ́, nsu ɔkɔ etemila sɔɔn na adi na ɔɔɔdi ami mɔɔsu-ma lɛla lɛdi!
8“Anwuɔsu ndubo ɔkɔ kenye bediene bammɔ kɔtu bɔni, ɔsika baatɔ́lɔ Israel kadi bekyuli bammɔ ku ɔkɔ etemila. 9Ndubɔta linye-ma lɛlɔ na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na babla mina bekyuli lɛnɔ. Na basɔ baaadubo lɛnyi bɔdi muedi banii Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ iye bakya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ muedi. Na badubɔnu bati ka ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti.
10“Kenye bediene bammɔ béni banii balasu litemi geen lɛdi. Na baasu mina bekyuli ka badubɔkɛ keyi buɛɛ ina ka balanu keyi lɛla lɛdi na bana akɔ. Bese aani kabla bablane bani mɔɔkali banii si béti kɔba bákwaa kowodu kɔni ndaku bɔƒɛ ni, na kɔwodu kɔmmɔ kɔdubo bunye kpakplaa. 11Nsu si uwi ɔni na lɛ́ya na ɔnantu ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ku etubankɛ ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa úbo uukpó ni, ɔ́bla bi ɔ́bla dɛ ni, ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ɔdubo bɔƒɛ. 12Mmɔ na bekyuli badubo buye lɛla lɛni ɔsu na kɔba kɔmmɔ kútakana kowodu kɔmmɔ bɔda buse na kulabwɛ.
13“Kowodu kɔmmɔ ndi Yerusalem, na ami Unwoti Katɔti ndubo ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ku ɔnantu ku etubankɛ ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa bumene na ubaƒɛ kowodu kɔmmɔ ubi kalɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. 14Ɔkɔ kenye bediene bammɔ baakya ɔkplu ka beti ala bebi ekpidi ani nkya Yerusalem, nsu ndubo ɔma ɔmmɔ bubo bɔbwɛ butálɛ ɔka ɔni a bákya ɔma ɔmmɔ kalɔ muedi. Na si uwi ɔni na ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔ́bwɛ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, kenye bediene bammɔ bekyuli ƒui badubɔti ka ami nábla ala ammɔ.
15“Yerusalem ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ku nwuna ɔkɔ kenye bediene bammɔ ƒui badubo mina kɔnyi ala bɔbla bɔnu. Na lɛkɔ lɛsa lite bekyuli ƒui ka Yerusalem ɔdi ɔ́sa na nwuna kenye bediene lɛnɔ békpi. 16Ɔsika bése keyi buɛɛ kenye béte mina bekyuli na uwi ɔni na beeebo keyi buɛɛ kadi. Ami Unwoti násu.
17“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, du Israel beleku kɔtɔ. Ama bani mɔɔkɔ́ lɛsa na ala ani na ama alati bana kasusu kátina-ma lɛlɔ. 18Ya na bati anii ama ɔdi ɔ́sa! Baakya evo ala na kavobi na baamána lɛduku eli lɛni lɛlɔ na evo ala ada. Na baatɔ́lɔ bekyuli na baaƒɔ́ taadi ka badubɔkana na basu ala ani ndubo bɔlɛ uwi ɔni mebo. Nsu baaadubo ɔkɔ ɔmɛni ƒui bɔnyi na balɛ sɛɛn na lɛla lɛdi lilálɛku-ma. 19Baayá na mina bekyuli beete-ma antabi ku bodobodo blii ɔdi kani na beedumi-mi na bana linyesia lɛni na bebo kemmo. Na baasia ɔkɔ etemila ammɔ lɛlɔ na baadú bekyuli bani na nka bátabla lɛla lɛdi na beebunku bekyuli bani na nka báƒiɔ na baatɔlɔ kɔtu tani tani. Na mina bekyuli baaƒɔ́-ma taadi.
20“Nkisi evo ala ani na baabla teeti taatɔlɔ bekyuli na baaƒɔ́ bana ɔkɔ etemila taadi. Ndubo lɛbuli lɛni nda-ma kuvobi mmɔ bukulo budie-ma egu na lɛya na bekyuli bani na bana evo ala éƒie aani baasɛ na kɔkpagyuɛ kemmo bakɛ bɔnwuna. 21Ndubudie ala ani na beeti teebile-ma anumi, na lidie bana ɔyikun ɔmmɔ na bekyuli bani na béƒie lɛlɔ kalɛ na ɔsɔ uladi-ma lɛlɔ. Mmɔ na badubɔti ka ami Unwoti nábla ala amɛni.
22“Baabla ala ani na ami lɛɛɛdubo bɔbla kudi kudii. Baatɔ́lɔ bekyuli babuni na baakya-ma ogya ka babla likpidi na baayá na kayi keelie bekyuli bekpidi kalɔ ka bataabla bana ekpidi na bayila bana ngba bumodi bɔmmɔ ƒui. 23Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na beleku bamɛni bataasu bana ɔkɔ kenye kadi. Na lɛya na mina bekyuli balɛ bana lɛlɔ bɔdi kalɔ. Na badubɔti ka ami Unwoti nábla ala amɛni.”

english_text:
Ezekiel Encourages the People To Turn Back to the Lord
1One day, some of Israel's leaders came to me and asked for a message from the Lord. 2While they were there, the Lord said:
3Ezekiel, son of man, these men have started worshiping idols, though they know it will cause them to sin even more. So I refuse to give them a message!
4Tell the people of Israel that if they sin by worshiping idols and then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will give them the answer their sins deserve. 5When they hear my message, maybe they will see that they need to turn back to me and stop worshiping those idols.
6Now, Ezekiel, tell everyone in Israel:
I am the Lord God. Stop worshiping those idols I hate so much and come back to me.
7Suppose one of you Israelites or a foreigner living in Israel rejects me and starts worshiping idols. If you then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will answer 8by turning against you. I will make you a warning to anyone who might think of doing the same thing, and you will no longer belong to my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord and that you have sinned against me.
9If a prophet gives a false message, I am the one who caused that prophet to lie. But I will still reject him and cut him off from my people, 10and anyone who goes to that prophet for a message will be punished in the same way. 11I will do this, so that you will come back to me and stop destroying yourselves with these disgusting sins. So turn back to me! Then I will be your God, and you will be my people. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
Judgment on a Sinful Nation
12The Lord God said:
13Ezekiel, son of man, suppose an entire nation sins against me, and I punish it by destroying the crops and letting its people and livestock starve to death. 14 Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living in that nation, their faithfulness would not save anyone but themselves.
15Or suppose I punish a nation by sending wild animals to eat people and scare away every passerby, so that the land becomes a barren desert. 16As surely as I live, I promise that even if these three men lived in that nation, their own children would not be spared. The three men would live, but the land would be an empty desert.
17Or suppose I send an enemy to attack a sinful nation and kill its people and livestock. 18If these three men were in that nation when I punished it, not even their children would be spared. Only the three men would live.
19And suppose I am so angry that I send a deadly disease to wipe out the people and livestock of a sinful nation. 20Again, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living there, I, the Lord, promise that the children of these faithful men would also die. Only the three of them would be spared.
21 I am the Lord God, and I promise to punish Jerusalem severely. I will send war, starvation, wild animals, and deadly disease to slaughter its people and livestock. 22And those who survive will be taken from their country and led here to Babylonia. Ezekiel, when you see how sinful they are, you will know why I did all these things to Jerusalem. 23You will be convinced that I, the Lord God, was right in doing what I did.
translation_text:
Esekiel Ɔ́kya Bekyuli Bammɔ Ogya Ka Basɔku Lɛlɔ Bete Unwoti
1Limeyi linwi ni, Israel kadi batɔnkune badi bébo-mi kudɔ bébeye-mi si Unwoti ubo kenye kadi ute-ma. 2Na uwi ɔni na bakya-mi kudɔ mmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini,
3“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, bekyuli bamɛni béese kalɔ baakpá baƒiɔ ina ka bagyi nwaa ka ɔmmɔ adubɔya na beduo ekpidi pii bamba bɔbla kemmo. Anwuɔsu líni nnii lɛɛɛdubo-ma kenye kadi bɔkya! 4Su Israel kadi bekyuli anini, ‘Si baaƒiɔ́-mi na bana baƒiɔ bɔkpa kemmo asa na básɔ báta bésie kenye udiene ɔdi kudɔ banii betéye-nwu si mbo kenye kadi nte-ma ni, ndubo-ma kenye kani na bana ekpidi ani na bábla bɔ́manku búte. 5Na si bénu-mi kenye kamɛni ni, ɔƒɛni kalɛ badubo kasusu bɔsɔku bɔbla na bada baƒiɔ bammɔ bɔkpa baya na benwini bebo-mi kudɔ.’
6“Ɔƒɛni ni, Esekiel, su Israelni biala anini, ‘Ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti. Bɛda bina baƒiɔ bani muusé-mi lɛlɔ mmɔ bɔkpa bɛya.
7“ ‘Si amii Israelƒuɔ iye baƒɔ bani na bakya-mii kudɔ ɔdi úni-mi na úse kalɔ ɔɔkpá baƒiɔ ɔmmɔ kama na ɔ́sɔ úsie kenye udiene ɔdi kudɔ ɔnii mina kenye kadi na ɔɔwia unu ni, kenye kani na ndubo-nwu budie ndi ka 8ndubo bunwini bunye bɔsiaku-nwu na liti-nwu linwi lɛla lɛni na bakladi bani makali banii ama lɛnɔ baabla lɛni banu batɛya. Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔsɔ ulabla mina kadi bekyuli akɔ unwi. Na ɔdubɔnu ɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti na ɔ́bla likpidi ɔ́ƒiɔ-mi sɔsɔ.
9“ ‘Si kenye udiene ɔdi ɔ́su ɔkɔ kenye kadi ni, ami náya na ɔ́nyi ɔkɔ. Nsu ina amu ni, ndubuni-nwu na likulo kɔna kɔni nkya anwu ku mina kadi bekyuli ntɛ. 10Na ukyuli biala ɔni mesie kenye udiene ɔmmɔ kudɔ ɔnii utáƒɔ mina linyesia lɛdi lɛnɔ ni, ndubo-nwu kɔtu kɔmmɔ udu kani bɔni. 11Ɔsika mɔɔwia ka binwini bibo-mi kudɔ na bɛsɔ bilayila lɛlɔ udu na ekpidi ani muusé-mi lɛlɔ mɛni bɔbla kemmo. Anwuɔsu binwini bibo-mi kudɔ! Na lɛbla bina Katɔti na amii bɛbla mina kadi bekyuli. Ami Unwoti Katɔti muusé-mii kenye kamɛni.’ ”
Unwoti Ɔ́tɛku Kadi Bani Mɔɔbla Likpidi Kɔtu
12Unwoti ɔnini, 13“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, si úbo úte ka kadi ƒui bekyuli badi báƒiɔ-mi ni, ndubo-ma kɔtu bɔni na bana edula áyii udu na lɛ́ya na kɔka kɔ́du bekyuli bammɔ ku bana bebuo ƒui. 14Ina Noa ku Daniel ku Hiob bakya kalɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, kalɛ na basiaku-mi kama siin ɔɔɔdubo kalɔ kammɔ bɔƒɔ, mmomu ama alati kani ndubɔkɛ bɔƒɔ.
15“Na lɛnɔ ni, ndubɔkana na lɛni kadi bekyuli badi kɔtu si báƒiɔ-mi na lɛya na beƒiebuo beduo-ma lɛlɔ na bakun-ma na babɔku belusiene bani ƒui nkɛ mmɔ kalɛ na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kenwini kalɔ kakwiidi kani kemmo lɛla lɛdi liiibo. 16Na muusé kenye ka ɔni na ami Unwoti nli uwi ƒui mɛni ni, ina nkyuli ɛtɛ bani na lɛ́su mɛni bakya mmɔ ni, bana babi muedi balákɛ bɔƒɔ. Na nkyuli ɛtɛ bammɔ ama badubulie ngba, nsu kalɔ kammɔ aka kadubɔyii udu kenwini kalɔ kakwiidi.
17“Na lɛkana na limene bekisine bekpone na bebekpo ɔmii ɔni bekyuli mɔɔbla ekpidi mmɔ na badu bekyuli bammɔ ku bana bebuo ƒui. 18Na si nkyuli ɛtɛ bamɛni bakya mmɔ ni, bana bebi muedi ɔdi ulálɛ-nwu kemmo, mmomu ama alati kani.
19“Na kɔnyi kɔkana na kɔkɔ-mi na lɛya na ɔlɛ ukpidi ɔkyula kadi bani náƒiɔ-mi mmɔ bekyuli ku bebuo ƒui. 20Na lɛni kani na si Noa ku Daniel ku Hiob bakya mmɔ ni, ami Unwoti muusé kenye ka bana bebi muedi badubo bukpi na balákɛ bɔƒɔ.
21“Ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti na muusé kenye ka ndubo Yerusalem kɔtɔ bɔni geen. Ndubo bɔya na kekpo ku kɔka ku lɛlɛ likpidi ku beƒiebuo bebo babadu bekyuli ku bebuo bammɔ ƒui. 22Na bani na bétekpi na ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ndubo bɔya na bakpanku-ma batɔlɔku mmɔ aani bekyuli beƒiedi beboku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni. Na awɔ Esekiel ɔlati adubɔnu ati lɛla lɛni ɔsu na lɛ́bla Yerusalem ala amɛni ƒui si banii ánu alaekpidi ani udu na baabla taaƒiɔ-mi. 23Na ɔdubo-ɔ bɔbla nwaa na atunaku-mi ka lɛla lɛni na ami Unwoti Katɔti lɛ́bla lɛdi ulu lɛlɔ.”

english_text:
Jerusalem Is a Useless Vine
1Some time later, the Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, what happens to the wood of a grapevine after the grapes have been picked? It isn't like other trees in the forest, 3because the wood of a grapevine can't be used to make anything, not even a small peg to hang things on. 4It can only be used as firewood. But after its ends are burnt and its middle is charred, it can't be used for anything. 5The wood is useless before it is burned, and afterwards, it is completely worthless.
6I, the Lord God, promise that just as the wood of a grapevine is burned as firewood, 7I will punish the people of Jerusalem with fire. Some of them have escaped one destruction, but soon they will be completely burned. And when that happens, you, Ezekiel, will know that I am the Lord. 8I will make their country an empty wasteland, because they have not been loyal to me. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Yerusalem Ɔdi Kɔdingyii Kukpidi Kɔni Neeebo Kɔsia
1Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, 2“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, bi mɔɔlɛ́ku atoo kabuli si béde ebi bédie-ka lɛlɔ ƒui báwɔlɔ? Kabuli kammɔ keeese aani lɛku kemmo egyii bamba. 3Ɔsika kabuli kammɔ kaaadi kugyii kɔni na kubo ɔkplu na ɔdia lɛla lɛdi bɔbla. Na nwuna kɔgba lɛnɔ kuladia bukulo bɔbla ewele na bebo balɛ kesii kadi na baƒala ala. 4Bɔmɛnɛ kani na bakana bamɛnɛ-ku bakya ogya. Na si ekuku ammɔ ákywi áwɔlɔ na énwini ntɔ ni, ɔsɔ uuubo kɔsia kɔdi. 5Kabuli kammɔ keeebo kɔsia kɔdi asa na badubo bɔkyula-ka muedi. Na si bákyula-ka báwɔlɔ lɛnɔ ni, ɔsɔ uuubo lɛblakula lɛdi munu munu.
6“Ami Unwoti Katɔti muusé kenye nnii kalɛ na baakyula atoo kabuli aani ekyweni kalɛ ni, 7lɛni na ndubo ogya buti bɔkyula Yerusalem bekyuli. Na si uwi ɔni na ala amɛni álɛ ni, awɔ Esekiel adubɔnu ati ka ami ndi Unwoti. 8Ndubo bɔya na bana kalɔ kenwini kalɔ kekpludi kani neeebo kɔsia kɔdi, ɔsika kaladia lɛla lɛdi bɔbla na ɔni na baládi litemi geen lɛlɔ teete-mi ɔsu. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.”

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Unfaithful
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, remind the people of Jerusalem of their disgusting sins 3and tell them that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Jerusalem, you were born in the country where Canaanites lived. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite. 4When you were born, no one cut you loose from your mother or washed your body. No one rubbed your skin with salt and olive oil, and wrapped you in warm blankets. 5Not one person loved you enough to do any of these things, and no one even felt sorry for you. You were despised, thrown into a field, and forgotten.
6I saw you lying there, rolling around in your own blood, and I couldn't let you die. 7I took care of you, like someone caring for a tender, young plant. You grew up to be a beautiful young woman with mature breasts and hair, but you were still naked.
8When I saw you again, you were old enough to have sex. So I covered your naked body with my own robe. Then I solemnly promised that you would belong to me and that I, the Lord God, would take care of you.
9I washed the blood off you and rubbed your skin with olive oil. 10I gave you the finest clothes and the most expensive robes, as well as sandals made from the best leather. 11I gave you bracelets, a necklace, 12a ring for your nose, some earrings, and a beautiful crown. 13Your jewelry was gold and silver, and your clothes were made of only the finest material and embroidered linen. Your bread was baked from fine flour, and you ate honey and olive oil. You were as beautiful as a queen, 14and everyone on earth knew it. I, the Lord God, had helped you become a lovely young woman.
15You learned that you were attractive enough to have any man you wanted, so you offered yourself to every passerby. 16You made shrines for yourself and decorated them with some of your clothes. That's where you took your visitors to have sex with them. These things should never have happened! 17You made idols out of the gold and silver jewelry I gave you, then you sinned by worshiping those idols. 18You dressed them in the clothes you got from me, and you offered them the olive oil and incense I gave you. 19I supplied you with fine flour, olive oil, and honey, but you sacrificed it all as offerings to please those idols. I, the Lord God, watched this happen.
20But you did something even worse than that—you sacrificed your own children to those idols! 21You slaughtered my children, so you could offer them as sacrifices. 22You were so busy sinning and being a prostitute that you refused to think about the days when you were young and were rolling around naked in your own blood.
23Now I, the Lord God, say you are doomed! Not only did you do these evil things, 24but you also built places on every street corner 25where you disgraced yourself by having sex with anyone who walked by. And you did that more and more every day! 26To make me angry, you even offered yourself to Egyptians, who were always ready to sleep with you.
27So I punished you by letting those greedy Philistine enemies take over some of your territory. But even they were offended by your repulsive behavior.
28You couldn't get enough sex, so you chased after Assyrians and slept with them. You still weren't satisfied, 29so you went after Babylonians. But those merchants could not satisfy you either.
30I, the Lord God, say that you were so disgusting that you would have done anything to get what you wanted. 31You had sex on every street corner, and when you finished, you refused to accept money. That's worse than being a prostitute! 32You are nothing but an unfaithful wife who would rather have sex with strangers than with your own husband. 33Prostitutes accept money for having sex, but you bribe men from everywhere to have sex with you. 34You're not like other prostitutes. Men don't ask you for sex—you offer to pay them!
Jerusalem Must Be Punished
The Lord said:
35Jerusalem, you prostitute, listen to me. 36You chased after lovers, then took off your clothes and had sex. You even worshiped disgusting idols and sacrificed your own children as offerings to them. 37So I, the Lord God, will gather every one of your lovers, those you liked and those you hated. They will stand around you, and I will rip off your clothes and let all of those lovers stare at your nakedness. 38I will find you guilty of being an unfaithful wife and a murderer, and in my fierce anger I will sentence you to a violent death! 39Then I will hand you over to your lovers, who will tear down the places where you had sex. They will take your clothes and jewelry, leaving you naked and empty-handed.
40Your lovers and an angry mob will stone you to death; they will cut your dead body into pieces 41and burn down your houses. Other women will watch these terrible things happen to you. I promise to stop you from being a prostitute and paying your lovers for sex.
42Only then will I calm down and stop being angry and jealous. 43You made me furious by doing all these disgusting things and by forgetting how I took care of you when you were young. Then you made things worse by acting like a prostitute. You must be punished! I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Jerusalem's Two Sisters
The Lord said:
44People will use this saying about you, Jerusalem: “If the mother is bad, so is her daughter.” 45You are just like your mother, who hated her husband and her own children. You are also like your sisters, who hated their husbands and children. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite. 46Your older sister was Samaria, that city to your north with her nearby villages. Your younger sister was Sodom, that city to your south with her nearby villages. 47You followed their way of life and their wicked customs, and soon you were more repulsive than they were.
48As surely as I am the living Lord God, the people of Sodom and its nearby villages were never as sinful as you. 49They were arrogant and spoiled; they had everything they needed and still refused to help the poor and needy. 50They thought they were better than everyone else, and they did things I hate. And so I destroyed them.
51You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent. 52So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins.
Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed
The Lord said to Jerusalem:
53Someday I will bless Sodom and Samaria and their nearby villages. I will also bless you, Jerusalem. 54Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you. 55When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
56Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom. 57But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks. 58You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem
The Lord said:
59Jerusalem, you deserve to be punished, because you broke your promises and ignored our agreement. 60But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever. 61When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement. 62I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord. 63I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Yerusalem Ɔɔɔsiaku-mi Kama Siin
1Unwoti ɔnini,
2“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, nyimene Yerusalemƒuɔ bana ekpidi ani na baabla na eesé-mi lɛlɔ mmɔ. 3Na asu-ma anii ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu nnini,
“ ‘Yerusalem, ɔmii ɔni kemmo na Kanaanƒuɔ bélie ni, mmɔ na báwɔ-ɔ. Na Amorini na ƒ'ɔti ɔdi, na ƒ'ini ɔdi Hitini. 4Uwi ɔni na báwɔ-ɔ ni, ukyuli ɔdi útekulo ƒula lɛkun kabuli útada-a útamami ƒ'ini lɛlɔ iye ɔkpila-a ntu bɔdi. Na ɔdi lɛnɔ úteti mma iye nnɔ útesusu-ɔ ɔlɔna na uti-ɔ ɔkya adi bonwu ani nábɛla-a kɔyɔ kemmo. 5Na ukyuli ɔdi útatina-a bɔyɔ bɔni udu náya na ɔbla ala amɛni ɔdi ute-ɔ. Na ɔdi muedi útanu ƒula kɔnyana na unuku-ɔ ɔlɛ ɔdi. Mmomu béni-ɔ na bébo-ɔ bátákya alakpi akɔ na báyiƒala-a.
6“ ‘Lɛ́nu uwi ɔni na atɛ ƒula ubugya kemmo eebó teeminime na ńtakana na linye lɛnu na ekpi. 7Lɛ́nu-ɔ lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na baanu kugyii blii kɔdi lɛlɔ na kɔɔlɛ́ lili. Na ébenwini ugblebi ɔkɔdi ɔni nákɔ anyii na ubo lili linwini gyɔlɔɔ, nsu kasɔngya kani na amu akɛ aaví.
8“ ‘Na uwi ɔni na lɛsɔ lɛnu-ɔ na ɔmmɔ kama ni, na éedu kalɛ na ati ɔnana. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu líti mina awu gyɔlɔɔ ɔmmɔ kakɛ kadi líbi-ɔ lɛlɔ na lɛ́bɛla-a kasɔngya líti lɛ́tina-a ka ndubo-ɔ bɔgyumana. Na líse-ɔ kenye kpakplaa na búnyimi ka enwini Unwoti Katɔti ami ɔdi na ntaanu-ɔ lɛlɔ.
9“ ‘Lɛ́ƒɔ ubugya ɔmmɔ lídie-ɔ lɛlɔ na líti nnɔmii lɛ́wɛɛ-ɔ. 10Líte-ɔ adi abuni ku lɛwu lɛbuni lɛni náƒɔ kuye litulo ku lɛgbanvuo lɛni na béti ebuo ɔku ɔbuni ƒui bábla. 11Na líte-ɔ limɔ asɛɛ abuni lidu lidu. 12Na líte-ɔ asikpɛɛ abuni ani na akya enwu ku atu ku kagabwa kabuni geen. 13Na ƒula asɛɛ ebi adi sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi sɔɔn. Na linwo lɛbunidi ƒui na béti bédi ƒula adala na béti adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ani muukeye na adia geen bekpo-nya atu. Ɔlaaƒɔ ɔbuni ƒui na béti béƒi ƒula bodobodo. Na uwɔ ku nnɔ ala na aadi na aadia bɔnu geen aani uleku ɔga. 14Na ukyuli biala na ulie kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ ɔgyi ɔmɛni. Na ami Unwoti Katɔti nébunku-ɔ na énwini ugblebi ɔkɔdi ɔbuni ɔmɛni udu.
15“ ‘Amu na ebo ábanu áti ka aadia bɔnu na akana na akɛ ɔnana biala na aayɔ́, anwuɔsu na éti lɛlɔ éte ulusiene biala nási ɔɔví. 16Átu kuliekɔ kɔni nse-ɔ kedee éte lɛlɔ na éti ƒula adi abuni ammɔ ákya-nya akya. Na mmɔ na eeti ƒula bayɔne bani muubo-ɔ kudɔ teeduoku na biisié taatáyɔ lɛlɔ. Na ala amɛni udu átalɛ ka alɛ lɛni kudii! 17Sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi asɛɛ ebi ani na líte-ɔ na éti ávɔ baƒiɔ ése éte lɛlɔ na aakpá na ɔdi likpidi na aabla taaƒiɔ-mi. 18Na adala ani na líte-ɔ ni, anya na ada aakya-ma. Na nnɔ ku oloƒui ɔni na líte-ɔ ni, anya na eeti teete-nya. 19Líte-ɔ ɔlaaƒɔ ɔbuni ku nnɔ ku uwɔ, nsu ala amɛni ƒui na eeti taakpa teete baƒiɔ bammɔ taakya-ma ebiti. Ami Unwoti Katɔti nnye mɔɔnu uwi ɔni na aabla ala amɛni ƒui.
20“ ‘Nsu ásɔ ábla lɛla lɛni na líbie litulo amɛni ƒui. Na éti ƒula kɔƒɔ bebi muedi ákpa éte baƒiɔ bamɛni! 21Ádu mina bebi kalɛ na eti-ma abla akpala. 22Ɔƒɛni amu asɔ eeebo kɔnu na likpidi bɔbla lɛlɔ kani na enye na éti lɛlɔ énwini ɔyalɛ. Na asɔ alabla kasusu taasiku uwi ɔni na adi ɔnamu na atɛ ubugya kemmo ku kasɔngya eebó teeminime.
23“ ‘Na ɔƒaani ni, ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu-ɔ nnii awɔ ɔdi ɔ́sa, áyii udu! Na ɔɔɔdi ekpidi amɛni kani na ábla, 24mmomu ásɔ átu bamba ákya lɛblɔnu lɛmmɔ ƒui ɔkɔkɔ biala lɛlɔ. 25Na mmɔ na aabla kɔƒa ala na ɔni na awɔ ku ukyuli biala nási ɔɔví bɛɛtɛnku lɛlɔ. Na aabla ɔmɛni kɔlɛ kɔlɛ limeyi ndi limeyi! 26Na kalɛ na akya-mi kɔnyi ɔsu ni, éti lɛlɔ éte Egyipteƒuɔ bani nnye kagyumana ka awɔ ku-ma bɛtɛ. 27Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na lɛ́ni-ɔ kɔtu na ɔni na lɛ́ya na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekisine badivone bammɔ bébeƒie ƒula kalɛkɛ kadi báƒɔ. Nsu ama muedi ni, bina ala adi bene bɔbla bɔdi lɛla lɛni muusé-ma lɛlɔ. 28Bina bɔtɛ taavi bɔmɛni bútedu-mii ɔkwɛ, anwuɔsu bɛ́sɔ bɛ́ta bɛsiaku Asiriaƒuɔ na bísie bɛɛtɛ-ma kudɔ. Nsu ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ útemo-mii. 29Anwuɔsu ɔƒaamu bɛnii Babilonƒuɔ. Nsu beyedine bammɔ lɛnɔ bana ablala átakana na edu-mii ɔkwɛ.
30“ ‘Ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu ka biisé lɛlɔ geen ɔni bɛɛkana na bɛɛsia ulu biala lɛlɔ na bɛkɛ lɛla lɛni na bɛɛwia. 31Amii ku bana bɛ́tɛ ɔblɔnu ɔkɔkɔ biala lɛlɔ. Nsu ka bɛ́wɔlɔ ni, bíni egulabi adi bɔƒɔ. Na ɔmmɔ úbie utulo ɔyalɛ ɔni mɔɔtɛ banana kudɔ taaƒɔ egulabi adi!
32“ ‘Bítavumana ku uleku ɔni mɔɔlɛ́ ɔgyani kama taatátɛ baƒɔ kudɔ utulo ɔni na ɔtɛ ɔgyani kama. 33Bayalɛ ni, bɔtɛ na baatɛ banana kudɔ taaƒɔ́-ma egulabi adi. Nsu amii ni, amii mmomu muuti bina ala taatálɔ banana na bɔbɛ kemmo na beebo taabatɛnku-mii. 34Biiise aani bayalɛ bamba. Ɔsika ɔɔɔdi banana bammɔ muubo teebeye-mii banii amii ku-ma bɛɛtɛ. Amii mmomu mɔɔƒɔ-ma kayu kadi ka bebo babatɛnku-mii!
Ɔlɛka Bani Yerusalem Kɔtu
35“ ‘Yerusalem, ɔyalɛ ubendi, se kɔtu na enu. 36Awɔ nábi asiaku ƒula bayɔne na áda kɔdi édie na bátɛnku-ɔ. Na ákpa baƒiɔ bani muusé lɛlɔ na ádu ƒula kɔƒɔ bebi muedi éte-ma. 37Anwuɔsu ami Unwoti Katɔti ndubo ƒula bayɔne bammɔ bɔsala bani na aayɔ́ ku bani na ekisi ƒui na babasala asa na lidie-ɔ kasɔngya na bana anumi na benye bataanu-ɔ kasɔngya kammɔ. 38Ndubo-ɔ kɔtɔ bɔdu aani uleku ɔni na ulasiaku ɔgyani kama siin na ɔdi ukyuli ɔdune. Na ndubɔdu-ɔ kukpi kɔtɔ na mina kɔnyi kemmo! 39Na liti-ɔ lite ƒula bayɔne na ama ndubo ekpo ani na átu na bítaatɛnku lɛlɔ mmɔ bubo bɔbwɛ. Na beti ƒula adala ku asɛɛ ebi abuni ammɔ na bada-a bava kasɔngya ku enukplu. 40Ƒula bayɔne ku kasalakɔ bekyuli bani ndubuti kɔnyi bakya-a mmɔ ndubo-ɔ atabi bubo bɔdu na bebeyi ƒula ɔlɔna ukpine ɔmmɔ bewi kɔkɛ kɔkɛ 41na bakyula ƒula kaduli ƒui. Beleku bamba badubunye banu lɛla likpidi lɛni ndubɔlɛku-ɔ mɛni. Na muusé kenye ka ndubutile-ɔ kuƒi ka asɔ abla ɔyalɛ na asɔ ataaƒɔ ƒula bayɔne kayu kadi anii babatɛnku-ɔ. 42Uwi ɔmmɔ asa na mina kayi kadubɔyɔ na lɛda kɔnyi ku kogyulo bukpo lɛya.
43“ ‘Ákya-mi kɔnyi geen na ala ani na ábla na eesé lɛlɔ mɛni ɔsu ku kalɛ na áyiƒala kalɛ na lɛ́nu-ɔ lɛlɔ uwi ɔni na ɔdi ɔnamu. Ɔmmɔ kama asa na ébenwini ɔyalɛ na ƒula ala bɔbla kemmo. Ɔlɛka akɛ ƒula kɔtu bɔni! Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.
44“ ‘Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, lɛsugba lɛmɛni ndubɔkya bekyuli kenye na awɔ Yerusalem lɛlɔ banini, “Kalɛ na ubi uni use ni, lɛni kani na ubidi ulekubi lɛnɔ ɔdubuse.” 45Ƒ'ini ɔni nékisi ɔgyani ku anwu ɔlati kaƒɔ bebi ni, anwu nálɛ. Na átavumanaku ƒula banwani belekubi bani lɛnɔ nékisi bana bagya ku bana bebi. Amorini na ƒ'ɔti ɔ́di na ƒ'ini lɛnɔ Hitini na ɔ́di. 46Ƒula ɔnwani ulekubi unengudi ndi Samaria ɔma unengudi ɔni na ƒula katɔ kakɛ ka akpaklɔ lɛma lɛni náka lɛ́mana-nwu. Na ƒula ɔnwani ulekubi ɔnamudi ndi Sodom ɔma unengudi ɔni nkya úsie kada kakɛ ku akpaklɔ lɛma lɛmmɔ ƒui. 47Bana ngba uliedu kama na ásia ku bana kalala ɔdi ala bɔbla kama, anwuɔsu na uwi útetu asa na ƒula bubie búbetulo na eesé lɛlɔ geen teetulo-ma muedi. 48Ɔni na ami Unwoti Katɔti nli ngba uwi ƒui mɛni ni, mɔɔsu ka Sodom ku lɛma lɛni na nwuna amadɔ mmɔ muedi bana ekpidi étedu awɔ ɔdi ɔmɛni udu.
49“ ‘Bátaatalaku lɛlɔ katɔ na bébile lɛlɔ. Na ala ƒui ása-ma, nsu ina amu béni na bétebunku bawabane ku bani na balakana na bebunku lɛlɔ na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ. 50Bákali ka bádia betulo ukyuli biala na baabla ala ani na nkisi. Anwuɔsu na lɛ́yila-ma udu.
51“ ‘Amii Yerusalemƒuɔ bɛ́bla ekpidi ani na etulo Samariaƒuɔ adi kunyɔ. Na bina alaekpidi ani udu na bɛ́bla ni, ɔ́ya na mɔɔnu Samaria ku Sodom aani si lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma na bátabla ekpidi adi munu munu. 52Anwuɔsu bana kɔtu bɔni bɔdubo-ma bɔbla ƒaa ƒaa butulo amii adi ƒui. Kɔƒa kɔdubo-mii bukpo na anumi ewi-mii kalɔ, ɔsika bina ablala eesé lɛlɔ geen.
Kɔƒa Kɔdubo Yerusalem Bukpo
53“ ‘Limeyi lɛdi lɛdubo lɛni na ndubute Sodom ku Samaria ku bana lɛma lɛni na amadɔ kusɛ kusɛ. Na awɔ Yerusalem lɛnɔ ndubute-ɔ kusɛ kusɛ. 54Na kɔƒa kɔdubo-ɔ bukpo na ala ani na ábla ɔsu. Na Sodom ku Samaria lɛnɔ ni, bana kayi kadubɔyɔ na banu ka bátabla alaekpidi ani udu na awɔ Yerusalem ábla. 55Si uwi ɔni limeyi lɛmmɔ lídu ni, awɔ ku Sodom ku Samaria ƒui ni, ala adubɔsɔ adianku-mii ku akpaklɔ lɛma lɛni na amadɔ ƒui na bɛsɔ binwini bibese kalɛ na bíse kukuuku. 56Yerusalem átalaku lɛlɔ katɔ kakaaka ɔni na átaapii Sodom muedi. 57Nsu ɔƒaani ni, ukyuli biala ɔ́nu ɔ́ti kalɛ udu na ebo kalala. Siria ku Ƒilistia ku ƒula liku bekyuli ƒui balálɔ-ɔ lɛnyi lɛbuni lɛdi. 58Anwuɔsu na ala ekpidi bonwu ku ekisila ani na ébile ƒui ɔlɛka aƒɔ-nya kayu. Ami Unwoti násu.
59“ ‘Yerusalem, ámanku kɔtu bɔni, ɔsika ébila mina linyese ku ala ani na línyimiku-ɔ. 60Nsu mina anumi asia lɛla lɛni na línyimiku-ɔ uwi ɔni na átabi tɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. Anwuɔsu ndubo-ɔ kenye kadi buse kani ndubuse kete uwi ƒui. 61Na si ákali ánu ala ani na ábla ábavi ni, na kɔƒa kukpo-ɔ. Na ɔni ntulo ƒui ndi si uwi ɔni na lɛ́sɔku ƒula banwani bani ndi Sodom ku Samaria líboku-ɔ aani ƒula bebi kalɛ ina ka ɔmmɔ ɔɔɔdi lɛla lɛni na línyimiku-ɔ. 62Ndubɔsia linyese lɛmɛni anu geen, ɔsika kese-mi kedee, na adubɔnu ati ka ami ndi Unwoti. 63Ndubuti lɛla biala lɛkyiɛ-ɔ, nsu adubɔkali ala ani na ábla anu na kɔƒa kukpo-ɔ kɔvili ka asu lɛla lɛdi muedi. Ami Unwoti násu.’ ”

english_text:
A Story about Two Eagles and a Vine
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story, 3so they will understand what I am saying to them:
A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree, 4then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities. 5The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream. 6The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
7There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil. 8But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
9Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army. 10The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither.
The Lord Explains the Story
11The Lord said:
12 Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means.
Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners. 13He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens, 14so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
15But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
16As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king. 17Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people. 18The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
19He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done. 20I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me. 21His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
22Someday, I, the Lord,
will cut a tender twig
from the top of a cedar tree,
then plant it on the peak
of Israel's tallest mountain,
23where it will grow
strong branches
and produce large fruit.
All kinds of birds will find
shelter under the tree,
and they will rest in the shade
of its branches.
24Every tree in the forest
will know that I, the Lord,
can bring down tall trees
and help short ones grow.
I dry up green trees
and make dry ones green.
I, the Lord, have spoken,
and I will keep my word.
translation_text:
Kɔdigbo Baasɛ Inyɔ Ku Kɔdingyii Kabuli Kadi Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ
1Unwoti ɔnini,
2“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, ti litemi lɛmɛni tásu Israel kadi bekyuli 3kalɛ na benu lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu kalɔ. Kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔdi na avwi ebo-nwu ɔkplu geen na nwuna kɔgya kɔɔdia bɔnu ni, úveyi limeyi lɛdi úsie Lebanon. Na ɔ́ƒɛ kugyii kpakplaa kɔdi kagba katɔdi. 4Na úti-ka úsienku kalɔ kadi lɛlɔ bekyuli mɔɔdi kuye mmɔ na ɔ́da-ka ɔ́va bana ɔma unengudi unwi kemmo.
5“Aasɛ ɔmɛni úti kugyii kebi kadi na kuna kugyii kɔɔbla ntu pii ɔ́siku Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na úti-ka útáva kalɔ kabuni kadi lɛlɔ na ketu kadi kɔtu. 6Kebi kamɛni kákwɛ na kábla kugyii kabuli na kébimi na kéde kégyingya kéwi kalɔ lɛlɔ. Kubo evete pii ku ligyiitu kpakplaa na kuna kɔgba kɔ́kɔ kúsie kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔmmɔ kudɔ.
7“Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔbambadi ɔdi ɔkya na nwuna avwi ebo ɔkplu geen na nwuna lɛgya lɛnɔ lítigbli. Anwuɔsu kugyii kabuli kamɛni kénwiniku lɛlɔ ku ligyiitu ƒui lísienku kási ɔmii ɔni kemmo na báva-nwu úsienku aasɛ ɔmɛni kudɔ ku kasusu ka ɔdubɔkɛ ntu bɔsiku-nwu kudɔ utulo kesii kani na báva-nwu mmɔ. 8Nsu nka kesii kani na unye mmɔ kadi kalɔ kabuni kani na kebo lɛmwi ku ntu pii na ɔkana na udie evete kaduɛ na ɔnwu ebi bonwu bonwu.
9“Na ɔƒɛni ni, Esekiel, su-mi ƒula kasusu. Aabu ka kugyii kabuli kamɛni kadubo ngba bulie? Munuu kɔdigbo aasɛ udeedi ɔmmɔ ɔdubo-ku bɔgyu budie mmɔ na ude ebi ammɔ udie-ku lɛlɔ na evete ani ƒui na ɔdaku budie mmɔ ayɛyɛ? Ɔsika kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔkana na ɔdu-ku kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ɔni na ɔɔɔdi bekpone pii badi na ɔdubo busie butétiku. 10Kugyii kabuli kammɔ kebo ɔkplu na kálɛ lili kaduɛ, nsu uwi ɔni na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔkula ala ɔdubuse kalɔ uteekpo ɔ́si kakɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ kani ni, ɔdubo bɔyɛyɛ na ukpi.”
Unwoti Údie Litemi Lɛmmɔ Kalɔ
11Unwoti ɔnini, 12“Esekiel, ye Israelƒuɔ lɛsɛ bakyane bammɔ si bagyi lɛla lɛni na litemi lɛmɛni lɛdanku. Su-ma anii Babilon ɔga úbo Yerusalem na úbeƒie Yuda ɔga ɔ́tɔlɔku ku nwuna benengu lɛnɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ. 13Na ɔ́ƒuna ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́siku Yuda ɔga kaduli bekyuli akɔ na bényi lɛla lɛdi anwu ku-nwu 14kalɛ na Yudaƒuɔ bakladi ƒui bataabu ukyuli ɔmɛni kani na ama alati beeebo kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ɔyikun ɔni na bataadi-ka lɛlɔ.
15“Nsu ukyuli ɔni na bése lɛga mɛni ɔ́ta únye Babilon lɛlɔ na ɔ́tala nwuna benengu bamba ɔnii besie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na betétiku bapɔnkɔ ku bekpone basiku mmɔ beboku. Aabu anii ɔga ɔmɛni kasusu kani na ɔ́bla mɛni kadubo-nwu bɔsia na ɔkana na ɔbwɛ lɛla lɛni na bényimiku Babilon mɛni bubile? Munuu kɔtu na badubo-nwu bɔni na lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔsu?
16“Ɔni na ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na uli ngba uwi ƒui mɛni ni, muusé kenye ka Yuda ɔga ɔdubo bukpi na Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika úbile lɛla lɛni na anwu ku Babilonƒuɔ ɔga ɔni náƒuna-nwu úse mmɔ bényimi. 17Na Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ku nwuna bekpone kpakplaa bani na Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni bététiku muedi baaadubo kɔsia kɔdi bɔlɛ bute Yudaƒuɔ si uwi ɔni na Babilonƒuɔ bábasi libili bámana Yuda lɛma linengudi ka benye bekpo lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ na badu bekyuli bammɔ. 18Yudaƒuɔ ɔga útadi nwuna linyese lɛlɔ na útabu lɛla lɛni na únyimiku Babilonƒuɔ. Anwuɔsu badubo-nwu kɔtu bɔni!
19“Úse kenye na mina lɛnyi kemmo na ɔ́kpali-mi lɛnɔ ɔ́su ka ɔdubɔdi-ka lɛlɔ. Nsu úbile linyese lɛmmɔ na útadi-ka lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́kpali-mi lɛnyi keeke na úwi-mi anumi kalɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka bani-nwu kɔtu na lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔsu. 20Ndubo-nwu kakpagyuɛ kadi bɔkywɛɛ na lidie-nwu. Na ndubɔni-nwu lisienku Babilon na bani-nwu kɔtu, ɔsika ɔ́lɛmi kama na útasiaku-mi kama siin. 21Badubo nwuna bekpone babuni ƒui bɔdu na kekpokɔ na babɔku bani nébu ƒui begyingya bakya lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ. Ami Unwoti násu.
22“Limeyi lɛdi ni, ami Unwoti ndubo kugyii kpakplaa kɔni kagba mɔɔlɛ́ ɔwɔdi bukulo na liti-ku lɛlɛ Israel Kɔbi kɔni nákuku kutulo ƒui lili. Na kɔdubunye mmɔ kɔbi lɛlɔ kunwini kugyii bonwu kpakplaa na kɔnwu ebi bonwu bonwu lɛnɔ. 23Baasɛ lidu ƒui badubɔkɛ kabɛkɔ na kugyii kɔmmɔ kemmo. Na badubɔkya-ku kɔgba akɔ bakɛ bɔnwuna ku ɔyuli. 24Na lɛku kemmo kugyii biala kɔdubɔti ka ami Unwoti ndubɔkana na liboku egyii kangyaa ƒui kalɔ na lɛya na ani na átakuku alɛ lili. Na mɔɔyá na egyii ɔwɔdi eenwíni akwiidi Na mɔɔyá na ani na ákwii lɛnɔ eenwíni awɔdi. Ami Unwoti násu na ndubo mina litemi lɛlɔ bɔdi.”

english_text:
Those Who Sin Will Die
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying,
“Sour grapes eaten by parents
leave a sour taste in the mouths
of their children.”
3Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel. 4The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
5Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right. 6He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period. 7He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor 8and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone 9 and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
10But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins 11his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife, 12cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things, 13and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
14But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him. 15He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife. 16He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor 17and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father. 18It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
19You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws. 20 Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
21Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death. 22All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right. 23I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
24But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
25You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are! 26If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned. 27And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 28They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death. 29But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
30I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished. 31Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins? 32 I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_text:
Bekyuli Bani Muulie Taabla Ekpidi Badubo Bukpi
1Unwoti ɔnini, 2“Esekiel, muunú Israelƒuɔ lɛsugba kukuuku lɛdi lɛni na ɔdi biala ɔɔsu ɔnini, ‘Ebi ekpidi ani na bawɔne bádi ni, nyana ɔdu mɔɔƒɔ́ lɛlɔ taakya bana bebi nnye kemmo.’
3“Nsu su-ma ɔƒaani anii ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti na ɔni na ami nli ngba uwi ƒui mɛni ni, lɛsugba lɛmmɔ kenye kadubo bukulo na basɔ baaadubo-ni butaasu na Israel. 4Ɔsika ngba bɔni na bawɔne ku bebi bammɔ ƒui belie ni, ami na belie-mu bete. Na bani nábla likpidi lɛdi kani ndubo bukpi.
5“Ɔƒɛni kalɛ ukyuli ɔbuni ɔdi ɔkya ɔni na use siin
na lɛbuni kani na ɔɔbla.
6Na úni ka ɔkun lɛna lɛni na
béti bákpa
béte kadi bamba baƒiɔ
na ɔƒiɔtɔ kesii
kani na Israelƒuɔ báƒɔ-ma
bábakya mmɔ kemmo.
Na úni lɛnɔ ka ɔkpa Israel
baƒiɔ badi.
Na ulesie bekyuli bamba beleku kudɔ
iye beleku bani nánu kɔbuli lɛnɔ kudɔ.
7Na ulanya ukyuli taakya iye uyu ɔdi lɛnɔ.
Na lɛla biala na ukyuli ɔdi úti úse lɛlɔ kama
úte-nwu asa na úvo lɛla lɛdi ni,
ɔɔsɔku-ni teete-nwu.
Na uleyu bekyuli.
Na uute bawabane adila.
Na bani nkɛ ku kasɔngya ni, uute-ma adala.
8Ulevo ala teete bekyuli
na ɔƒɔ-ma lɛla lɛdi uye,
iye ɔƒɔ kuvonsia
kunengudi kɔdi.
Na ulayɔ ka ɔbla ukyuli ɔdi
likpidi lɛdi.
Na si litemi líbo badi ntɛ ni,
ɔɔtɛ-ma ntɛ litemi ulu siin lɛlɔ.
9Na ulalɛ mina ɔda bubo
ku etemila kama.
Mmomu ɔɔsia-mu kama siin.
Ukyuli ɔmɛni udu ɔdi
ukyuli ɔbuni.
Na muusé kenye ka
ɔdubulie ngba.
10“Nsu ɔƒɛni kalɛ ukyuli ɔmɛni ubo ubi ukpidi ɔni mɔɔdú bekyuli na ɔɔbla ekpidi bamba, 11ina ka ɔti útabla ala ammɔ udu kudii.
“Na ɔkɛ aƒiodu ɔɔkun lɛna,
na ɔɔtɛnku bekyuli beleku.
12Na ɔɔnya bawabane taakya,
na uuyú bekyuli.
Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ ni, ala ani na bekyuli
béti bése lɛlɔ kama
béte-nwu ni,
ulásɔku teete-ma.
Na ɔɔkpá baƒiɔ,
na ɔɔbla ala ani muusé lɛlɔ.
13Na uuvó ala teete bekyuli
na ɔɔƒɔ́-ma ala teeye
na ɔɔƒɔ́ kuvonsia pii lɛnɔ.
Ukyuli ukpidi ɔni na use lɛni ni, ulakana na welie ngba bukpi kani na ɔdubo bukpi na anwu ɔlati ɔdubuti nwuna etila.
14“Nsu ɔƒɛni kalɛ ukyuli ukpidi ɔdi lɛnɔ ubo ubi ɔni mɔɔnu ka ɔti ɔɔbla udu ɔmɛni na anwu úni na ulabla lɛni.
15“Ɔɔɔkɛ ulakun lɛna
taavi na aƒiodu.
Na ulakpa Israel baƒiɔ badi lɛnɔ.
Na ulatɛnku bekyuli bamba beleku.
16Ulanya bekyuli taakya.
Na ulaƒɔ lɛla lɛdi teese kama
si bévo-nwu lɛla lɛdi.
Uleyu bekyuli.
Uute bawabane adila.
Na bani nkɛ ku kasɔngya ni,
uute-ma adala.
17Na ulevo ala teete bekyuli
na ɔƒɔ-ma ala uye,
iye ɔƒɔ-ma kuvonsia
kunengudi kɔdi.
Ɔɔdi mina litemi ku ɔda bubo
lɛlɔ siin.
Ukyuli ɔmɛni udu ulekpi na ɔti likpidi ɔsu, mmomu ɔdubulie ngba. 18Nsu ɔti ɔmmɔ ndubo bukpi na bekyuli bɔnya taakya ku kuyu ku likyulikpi ala bɔbla ɔsu.
19“Ngyi ka lɛla lɛni ɔsu na balani ubi kɔtu na ɔti alaekpidi lili ɔdi lɛla lɛni ndubo-ɔ bɔbla kalɛ kadi. Na ani ndi ka ubi ɔmmɔ ɔɔbla lɛla lɛni ndi ulu na ɔɔdi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. 20Bekyuli bani muulie taabla likpidi kani na badubo bɔdu. Bebi baaadubo abi adi bubo na bana bawɔne ablala ɔsu. Na lɛni kani na bawɔne lɛnɔ baaadubo abi bubo na bana bebi ablala kenye. Mmomu bekyuli bani nábla likpidi kani na badubo bɔdu. Bebi baaadubo abi bubo na bana bati ekpidi ɔsu. Na bawɔne lɛnɔ baaadubo abi bubo na bana bebi ekpidi ɔsu. Na badubo kayu kabuni bɔƒɔ bute bekyuli babuni na ala ani na bábla ɔsu.
21“Na si bekyuli bekpidi báda bana ekpidi bɔbla báya na bése kalɔ baabla lɛbuni na baadi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ni, baaadubo-ma bɔdu. 22Badubuti bana ekpidi ƒui bakyiɛ-ma na belie ngba, ɔsika bábla lɛbuni. 23Ami Unwoti Katɔti naaayɔ ka lɛnu ka ukyuli ukpidi ukpi. Mmomu ɔɔda-mi kubiti ka lɛnu ka únwini kama ɔ́kya nwuna ekpidi bɔbla na ulie ngba.
24“Nsu si bekyuli bekpidi bése kalɔ ku ngba bukpidi bulie na baabla ala ani muusé lɛlɔ ni, ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na belie ngba? Oowo! Mmomu bana lɛbuni lɛni na bábla bávi ƒui lɛdubo bɔyii na bayiƒala-nya. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu badubo-ma bɔdu na bana ekpidi ɔsu.
25“Amii Israelƒuɔ bɛɛdú-mi kɔtɔ ka naaatɛ litemi ulu siin lɛlɔ! Nsu ni, binu, ɔɔɔdi lɛni na use! 26Si bekyuli babuni bese likpidi bɔbla kalɔ ni, ɔlɛka badu-ma, ɔsika bábla likpidi. 27Na si alaekpidi bablane bése kalɔ ku lɛbuni bɔbla ni, badubudie lɛlɔ kɔtu bɔni kemmo. 28Badubo bana alaekpidi ani na bábla bávi bɔkali bɔnu na bada-nya bɔbla baya kalɛ na baládu-ma. 29Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui kama bɛmu binye bɛɛsu bɛnii naaatɛ litemi ulu siin lɛlɔ. Nsu ami mmomu nábla likpidi na bina ablala eeese siin!
30“Ndubo ɔdi biala litemi bɔtɛku na lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla kenye. Anwuɔsu bɛda likpidi bɔbla bɛya. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, ɔ́bla bi ndubo-mii kɔtɔ bɔni. 31Bini bina alaekpidi lilu lɛni ƒui lɛlɔ na bɛsia na bise kalɔ bitaabla kasusu kabuni na bɛsiaku-mi kama siin! Munuu bɔyɔ geen na bɛɛyɔ́ ka badu-mii na bina ekpidi bɔbla ɔsu? 32Ami Unwoti Katɔti naaayɔ ka lɛmmɔ udu lɛlɛku bina akɔ ɔdi. Anwuɔsu bɛda ekpidi bɔbla bɛya na bilie ngba!”

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Israel's Leaders
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
2Your mother was a brave lioness
who raised her cubs
among lions.
3She taught one of them to hunt,
and he learned to eat people.
4When the nations heard of him,
they trapped him in a pit,
then they used hooks
to drag him to Egypt.
5His mother waited
for him to return.
But soon she lost all hope
and raised another cub,
who also became fierce.
6He hunted with other lions
and learned to eat people.
7He destroyed fortresses
and ruined towns;
his mighty roar
terrified everyone.
8Nations plotted to kill him,
and people came from all over
to spread out a net
and catch him in a trap.
9They put him in a cage
and took him to Babylonia.
The lion was locked away,
so that his mighty roar
would never again be heard
on Israel's hills.
10Your mother was a vine like you,
growing near a stream.
There was plenty of water,
so she was filled with branches
and with lots of fruit.
11Her strong branches
became symbols of authority,
and she was taller
than all other trees—
everyone could see how strong
and healthy she was.
12But in anger, I pulled her up
by the roots
and threw her to the ground,
where the scorching desert wind
dried out her fruit.
Her strong branches wilted
and burned up.
13Then she was planted
in a hot, dry desert,
14where her stem caught fire,
and flames burned
her branches and fruit.
Not one strong branch is left;
she is stripped bare.
This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_text:
Bédie Ɔkwanu Béte Israel Batɔnkune
1“Esekiel, die ɔkwanu ɔkɛnku Israel bagabi lɛlɔ 2na asu anini,
“ ‘Ƒ'ini ɔdi gyata uni ɔdi udu.
Na ɔ́kya bagyata bamba akɔ!
Ɔɔyu taatɛ bagyatabi
bammɔ akɔ
na ɔɔnyuɛ nwuna bebi.
3Na ɔ́tina bana akɔ unwi kabui
na ɔdi gyata ɔni na ubo
ogya geen.
Na ɔ́tɛya kalɛ na ɔsiaku ebuo
na uƒie-nwu ɔduli.
Na ɔɔduli bekyuli teebweli.
4Kadi bekyuli ƒui bénu-nwu
kɔku kɔmɛni.
Na béku ubu bonwu ɔdi
bákywɛ-nwu kakpagyuɛ na úbanu-ka.
Na bábala-nwu abuala
na báni-nwu bésienku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.
5“ ‘Uni únye utaanu-nwu ulu ka unwini ubo,
nsu únye ɔ́nɔ.
Ka ɔ́yila lɛnunsia ɔsu ni,
ɔ́ƒuna nwuna ubi bamba
na ɔ́nyuɛ-nwu na ɔɔbla
ogya geen.
6Anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́kya útaabwi
na bagyata bamba akɔ
na ɔdi gyata ɔni na ubo
ogya geen.
Ɔ́tɛya kalɛ na baasia ebuo teeƒie-nwu.
Na útaaduli bekyuli taakun teebweli.
7Ɔ́bwɛ lɛma kɔgyumanakɔ kɔni na bátu bényene mmɔ úwi kalɔ,
na úbile ala na lɛma kemmo na lɛ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ liwi ukpludi.
Na kalɔ kemodi kammɔ ku bekyuli bani ƒui nkya-ka kemmo ni,
liƒu geen liiƒie-ma si ɔɔkwanyi.
8Kadi ƒui bekyuli bábata bénye-nwu lɛlɔ.
Na bási kɔlɛkɛ bonwu bonwu
kɔni na amadɔ mmɔ ƒui kemmo bébo
bébeku ubu bákywɛ-nwu kakpagyuɛ.
Na kakpagyuɛ kammɔ kédie-nwu.
9Bábala-nwu abuala adi na báni-nwu bákya lɛyu lɛdi kemmo
na béti-nwu bésienku Babilonƒuɔ ɔga kudɔ.
Mmɔ na bátábala-nwu bákya ɔtɔ katɛnkɔ kadi.
Anwuɔsu ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ulenu-nwu bɔkwanyi
na Israel abi lɛlɔ mmɔ
bene ƒui.
10“ ‘Ƒ'ini ɔdi kɔdingyii kabuli kani na kenye ketu kɔtu.
Na ka kɔɔƒɔ́ ntu pii na mmɔ ɔsu ni,
kúdie kɔgba ku ligyiitu pii.
11Nwuna kɔgba kpakplaa kɔmmɔ
kunye kute kenyekɔ ɔyikun
