Na baasɛ bakun bina bekpine 5bani ndubo bukpi buwi alakpi akɔ kesi kesii mmɔ. Ami Unwoti násu.
6“ ‘Ndubɔya na batu ogya bakya Magog ku kadi bani nli ɛpu kɔtu na baakali ka beli ƒaa na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma mmɔ. Na badubɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.
7“ ‘Mina kadi bekyuli badubo-mi bɔti na basɔ balakya-mi lɛnyi kɔƒa. Na badubɔti ka ami ndi Israelƒuɔ Ukyuli Kedee. 8Limeyi lɛsia ulu lɛdubo lɛni na ala amɛni adubo bɔlɛ kalɛ kani na líse kenye.
9“ ‘Na si limeyi lɛmmɔ lídu ni, Israelƒuɔ badubo bana bekisine bani nebekpi-ma kudɔ mmɔ ekpola bɔla na bana lɛma lɛni kemmo na beli mmɔ. Na kɔtaminta ku atula lidu ku kekpo agyumanala ani bada mmɔ ku bana ligyii buti butaakya ogya. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla bana ekyweni akwa maatɛ sɔɔn. 10Ekpola amɛni na badubo butaakyula na egyii ani na ɔlɛka bada iye ekyweni ani na bawia bavi kenye. Lɛni na Israelƒuɔ badubo bekyuli bani néyu-ma na bédumi-ma bábla-ma kalala udu biala kasi budie. Ami Unwoti násu.
Báva Ɔga Gog
11“ ‘Si báyila Ɔga Gog udu báwɔlɔ ni, ndubɔya na bava-nwu na nwuna bekpone akɔ na Israel mmɔ na kesii kani baalɔ banii Belusiene Kɔwɛ si éti ésela Ɛpugyie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na bekyuli kavakɔ kammɔ kadubo bubomo ɔni na kadubutile ukyuli biala masu ɔnii ɔɔsia mmɔ ɔvi ulu. Anwuɔsu na badubɔlɔ mmɔ ɔmmɔ kama banii Gog ku nwuna bekpone kɔwɛ.
12“ ‘Abuli maatɛ na Israelƒuɔ badubo buti bɔva bekpine bammɔ na babla bana kalɔ kammɔ sɛɛn. 13Na kalɔ kammɔ ukyuli biala ɔdubo bubunku na bekyuli bammɔ bɔva kemmo. Na limeyi lɛni na badubɔnu mina bukeye ni, ɔdubɔbla limeyi lɛni na ɔdi biala ɔdubɔkɛ ɔbu.
14“ ‘Si abuli maatɛ ammɔ ávi áwɔlɔ ni, mina kadi bekyuli bammɔ badubo bekyuli badi bɔƒuna na bavi banu si bekpine badi básɔ bébu bakya kesii kadi na bátava ama. Na badubɔbla ɔmɛni abuli maatɛ bamba kalɛ na bati nwaa ka ukpine ɔdi útaƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔɔɔtɛ kesii kadi na ubile ekisila adi na kalɔ kammɔ kalabla sɛɛn. 15Na kesii biala na bánu ukyuli likubi ni, badubɔbla likposela bese mmɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama na beyitaƒu bebeti-nwu batáva na Belusiene Kɔwɛ kemmo mmɔ 16na ude kesii kani na badubo lɛnyi bɔsia banii Gog Bekpone Ɔma. Na kalɔ kammɔ kadubɔsɔ kabla sɛɛn na ɔmmɔ kama.’ ”
17“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, ndubo limeyi bɔdi na Israel abi lɛlɔ na lɛbla akpala na mmɔ. Anwuɔsu ya na baasɛ ku bebuo ku alakpi akɔ bebuo na basi lɛƒɛnyi ƒui bebo na babakun akpala lɛna na bani ubugya lɛnɔ. 18Badubo bekpone ku baƒɔ lɛlɔ badine lɛna bɔkun. Bekyuli bammɔ na ndubo bɔdu bɔbla akpala aani kalɛ na baadú baƒonu ku bese ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ taabla akpala. 19Mɔɔwia ka baasɛ bammɔ bakun lɛna bemo na bani ubugya lɛnɔ na udu-ma ɔkwɛ aani kalɛ na baaní ntɛ teekpi. 20Badubo babadi mina kadikɔ na bakun bapɔnkɔ lɛna ku bekpone lidu lidu lɛna beyile eƒi. Ami Unwoti násu.”
Israel Ɔdubɔsɔ Unwini Ubenye Nwuna Kenyekɔ Kuuku
21Unwoti ɔnini, “Si lɛ́ni kalɔ lɛlɔ kadi bekyuli kɔtu ni, badubɔnu kalɛ na muukeye. 22Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ badubɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti, bana Katɔti. 23Na baƒɔ lɛnɔ badubɔnu bati ka bunye na bénye Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ na bábɔku-ma bálɛku bana kalɔ lɛlɔ ka bábla ekpidi báƒiɔ-mi ɔsu. Línwini kama lɛ́kya-ma na bana bekisine békpoku-ma na bádu-ma. 24Ulikplu ku bubie lidu lidu lɛ́ƒɔ-ma keliela kemmo, anwuɔsu na bámanku ka lɛni-ma kɔtu.
25“Ɔƒaani ni, ndubo Israelƒuɔ kɔnyana bɔnu na lɛkpanku-ma lɛsiku baƒɔ lɛma lɛni kemmo na bákya mmɔ lɛsɔku liboku bana kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika Yakob bebi ku bawɔ na badi, anwuɔsu ndubute-ma kusɛ kusɛ na lɛtina-ma ka nse kedee. 26Na badubo bulie ku keyi buɛɛ na ama alati kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na kɔƒa kukpo-ma si bényimo alaekpidi ani na bábla bábavi na bákya-mi kɔƒa. 27Kadi bamba bekyuli bani ndi baƒɔ badubunye banu kalɛ na ndubɔƒɔ Israelƒuɔ lɛlɛku bana bekisine enu kemmo lɛsɔku liboku bana ɔma. Na kadi bammɔ bekyuli badubɔnu ka nse kedee.
28“Mina bekyuli badubɔnu bati ka ami Unwoti, bana Katɔti, nábɔku-ma lɛ́lɛku bana kalɔ lɛlɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ. Na ɔƒaani ndubɔsɔku-ma liboku ama alati bana kalɔ lɛlɔ. 29Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo kama bunwini bɔkya mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ kudii, na mina Kɔyu kɔdubo bulieku-ma. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_text:
Ezekiel Sees the Future Temple in Jerusalem
1-2 Twenty-five years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, and 14 years after the Babylonians had captured Jerusalem, the Lord's power took control of me on the tenth day of the first month. The Lord showed me some visions in which I was carried to the top of a high mountain in Jerusalem. I looked to the south and saw what looked like a city full of buildings. 3 In my vision the Lord took me closer, and I saw a man who was sparkling like polished bronze. He was standing near one of the gates and was holding a tape measure in one hand and a measuring stick in the other. 4The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay close attention to everything I'm going to show you—that's why you've been brought here. Listen carefully, because you must tell the people of Israel what you see.”
The East Gate
5 The first thing I saw was an outer wall that completely surrounded the temple area. The man took his measuring stick, which was three meters long, and measured the wall; it was three meters high and three meters thick. 6-7Then he went to the east gate, where he walked up steps that led to a long passageway. On each side of this passageway were three guardrooms, which were three meters square, and they were separated by walls two and a half meters thick. The man measured the distance between the opening of the gate and the first guardroom, and it was three meters, the thickness of the outer wall.
At the far end of this passageway, I saw an entrance room that faced the courtyard of the temple itself. There was also a distance of three meters between the last guardroom and the entrance room 8-9at the end of the passageway. The man measured this room: It was four meters from the doorway to the opposite wall, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one meter. 10The three guardrooms on each side of the passageway were the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same thickness.
11Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide. 12In front of the guardrooms, which were three meters square, was a railing about 50 centimeters high and 50 centimeters thick. 13The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters. 14He measured the entrance room at the far end of the passageway, and it was ten meters wide. 15Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was 25 meters. 16The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees.
The Outer Courtyard
17The man then led me through the passageway and into the outer courtyard of the temple, where I saw 30 rooms built around the outside of the courtyard. These side rooms were built against the outer wall, and in front of them was a sidewalk that circled the courtyard. 18This was known as the lower sidewalk, and it was 25 meters wide.
19I saw the gates that led to the inner courtyard of the temple and noticed that they were higher than those leading to the outer courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gates, and it was 50 meters.
The North Gate
20Next, the man measured the north gate that led to the outer courtyard. 21This gate also had three guardrooms on each side of a passageway. The measurements of these rooms, the walls between them, and the entrance room at the far end of the passageway were exactly the same as those of the east gate. The north gate was also 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide, 22and the windows, the entrance room, and the carvings of palm trees were just like those in the east gate. The entrance room also faced the courtyard of the temple and had seven steps leading up to it. 23Directly across the outer courtyard was a gate that led to the inner courtyard, just as there was for the east gate. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was 50 meters.
The South Gate
24The man then took me to the south gate. He measured the walls and the entrance room of this gate, and the measurements were exactly the same as those of the other two gates. 25There were windows in the guardrooms of this gate and in the entrance room, just like the others, and this gate was also 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide. 26Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway. 27And directly across the outer courtyard was a gate on the south side of the inner courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was also 50 meters.
The Gates Leading to the Inner Courtyard
28We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall. 29-30In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide. 31The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
32Next, we went through the east gate to the inner courtyard. The man measured this gate, and it was the same size as the others. 33The guardrooms, the walls separating them, and its entrance room had the same measurements as the other gates. The guardrooms and the entrance room had windows, and the gate was 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide. 34The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
35Then the man took me to the north gate. He measured it, and it was the same size as the others, 36including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, and the entrance room. There were also windows in this gate. It was 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide, 37and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
38-39Inside the entrance room of the north gate, I saw four tables, two on each side of the room, where the animals to be sacrificed were killed. Just outside this room was a small building used for washing the animals before they were offered as sacrifices to please the Lord or sacrifices for sin or sacrifices to make things right. 40Four more tables were in the outer courtyard, two on each side of the steps leading into the entrance room. 41So there was a total of eight tables, four inside and four outside, where the animals were killed, 42-43and where the meat was placed until it was sacrificed on the altar.
Next to the tables in the entrance room were four stone tables 50 centimeters high and 75 centimeters square; the equipment used for killing the animals was kept on top of these tables. All around the walls of this room was a 75-millimeter shelf.
The Rooms Belonging to the Priests
44The man then took me to the inner courtyard, where I saw two buildings, one beside the inner gate on the north and the other beside the inner gate on the south. 45He said, “The building beside the north gate belongs to the priests who serve in the temple, 46and the building beside the south gate belongs to those who serve at the altar. All of them are descendants of Zadok and are the only Levites allowed to serve as the Lord's priests.”
The Inner Courtyard and the Temple
47Now the man measured the inner courtyard; it was 50 meters square. I also saw an altar in front of the temple.
48We walked to the porch of the temple, and the man measured the doorway of the porch: It was seven meters long, two and a half meters wide, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one and a half meters. 49The porch itself was ten meters by six meters, with steps leading up to it. There was a column on each side of these steps.
translation_text:
Esekiel Ɔ́nu Kakpakɔ Kani Mebo Na Yerusalem
1-2Akwa aavlanyɔ kama ɔni na béƒie Ɔga Yekonia ku abu bakladi bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ ni, Unwoti ɔyikun ɔ́ƒɔ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui na kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi leevudi lɛlɔ. Na ɔdi akwa leevu-ene ɔni na béƒie Yerusalem báƒɔ. Unwoti údie kɔyu kemmo ala adi ɔ́tina-mi na uwi ɔni na ɔ́ya na béti-mi bésienku kɔbi kangyaa kɔdi lili na Yerusalem. Na ka línwini lɛ́nu kada kakɛ ni, lɛ́nu aani si ɔma ɔdi nwi na lɛtɔ lɛ́ƒɔ-nwu kemmo tɛɛ. 3Na mina ala bɔnu bɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na lɛ́ni líde suɛlɛ suɛlɛ geen na lɛ́nu ɔnana ɔdi na unye na uukeye aani lɛbuala ligyiedi lɛni na békuo na liikeye taatu anumi geen. Na unye ɔban kayakun kenwi kadi kenye na ɔda kadii ku ugyii ɔni na baakɔ́ku ala na kɔnu kɔni ku kɔni. 4Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, sia anu kaduɛ na anu ala ani na ndubo-ɔ bɔtina mɛni, ɔsika anya ɔsu na béti-ɔ béboku mɛni. Se atu kaduɛ, ɔsika ala ani ƒui na ánu ni, adubo-nya bɔsɔku bɔsu Israelƒuɔ.”
Ɔban Kayakun Kani Nésie Ɔƒɛ Katukɔ Litemi
5Lɛla lideedi lɛni na lɛ́nu ndi kowodu kɔni nkɛ kama kakɛ na kɔ́ka kɔ́mana kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ ƒui. Ɔnana ɔmmɔ úti nwuna ugyii lɛkɔkula lɛni nákuku lɛgba leevu na úgbigbli lɛgba leevu na ɔ́kɔku kowodu kɔmmɔ na kuna bɔkuku ubo lɛgba leevu na kuna bugbigbli lɛnɔ ubo lɛgba leevu. 6-7Ɔmmɔ kama úsie ɔban ɔni nkya ɔƒɛ katukɔ na ɔ́kɔ libili lɛdi útédu ulu ɔdi na ɔtɛ úsela anumi ƒui. Na ulu ɔmɛni kɔmii ku kɔdianu ni, bátu lɛtɔ ɛtɛ ɛtɛ lɛni kemmo na beenye taagyumana bényene. Na lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ bunene ku bɔbɛbɛ ƒui bubo lɛgba leevu leevu. Na awodu ani bugbigbli ntulo lɛgba maane líle lɛtɔ lɛmɛni lɛ́siku ɔkpanadi kudɔ. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku kalɛ na bagyumanane ɔtɔ udeedi ɔ́gyunku ɔban ɔmmɔ kenye na ubo lɛgba leevu. Na bɔgyunku bɔmmɔ búlieku kowodu kɔmadi kɔmmɔ bugbigbli bɔni ndi lɛgba leevu.
Amu na ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na kama kama ƒui ni, lɛ́nu ɔtɔ ɔdi kayakun ka kéti anumi kéboku kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔlati kaduli. Na bagyumane ɔtɔ ukplodi ku ɔtɔ kayakun kamɛni ntɛ bɔgyu lɛnɔ bɔdi lɛgba leevu 8-9na ulu ɔmɛni kawɔlɔkɔ mmɔ.
Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ, na ɔ́si nwuna kayakun úsie kowodu kɔni na ɔvi unyɔdi ntɛ ɔdi lɛgba leevu-ɛtɛ. Na ɔ́si kayakun kammɔ útédu awodu anyɔ ani na nwuna lɛƒɛnyi inyɔ lɛmmɔ ɔdi lɛgba ɛtɛ ɛtɛ.
10Bagyumane lɛtɔ ɛtɛ ɛtɛ lɛni na linye ulu ɔmɛni lɛvi inyɔ bɔmmɔ bɔkɔku ku udu ɔdi unwi. Na awodu ani néle lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ lɛ́siku ɔkpanadi kudɔ lɛnɔ bɔdi bugbigbli bunwi pɛ.
11Kama ni, ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku ulu ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ lɛbɛbɛ na ubo lɛgba aavlanyɔ-inyɔ, nsu ɔban kɔyaku inyɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba leevu-ɛku kani. 12Na kɔgyumanakɔ lɛtɔ lɛni mbo lɛgba leevu leevu bɔbɛbɛ ku bune mmɔ anumi ni, awodu klukwii klukwii adi enye na ana bɔkuku ku bugbigbli bubo akɔkɔ kemmo bɔbɛbɛ ɛlɔ ɛlɔ. 13Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku ɔ́si bagyumanane ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kowodu kɔmadi ɔ́via ulu úsie ɔtɔ ɔni na ulu ɔvi unyɔdi kowodu kɔmadi na ubo lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ. 14Na ɔtɔ ɔni na ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ kammɔ ni, ɔ́kɔku anwu lɛnɔ na ubo lɛgba avlaatɛ-ine bɔbɛbɛ. 15Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, ɔ́kɔku ulu ɔmmɔ ƒui bune ɔ́si kowodu kɔmadi kɔmmɔ útédu ɔtɔ ɔni kayakun néti anumi kéboku kakpakɔ kaduli geen mmɔ, na ulu ɔmmɔ ubo lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ. 16Bédie ƒansili na bagyumanane lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ awodu ƒui kemmo ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ kemmo aani kalɛ na use na ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ mmɔ kemmo kalɛ. Na bánwi ala na ebo udu kenye béti bákya awodu ani na ulu ɔmmɔ lɛvi inyɔ bɔmmɔ akya.
Búsie Kaduli Kedeedi Kemmo
17Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́tɔnku-mi na bɔ́sia ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ bútéduo kakpakɔ kaduli geen kedeedi kemmo, na lɛ́nu ka bátu lɛtɔ avlaatɛ bámana kaduli kammɔ. Na bátu lɛtɔ lɛmɛni bámana kaduli kammɔ awodu ani náka ámana kudɔ kudɔ na kama kakɛ na lɛgba kasiakɔ kadi kakɛ lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ anumi ɔ́ka ɔmana kaduli kammɔ. 18Na mmɔ ndi ɔkwalɛ lɛgba kasiakɔ ka mmɔ kébo kánu ɔsu. Na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ ɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ.
19Lɛ́nu kayakun kɔni na baasia teeduo kakpakɔ kaduli geen geen kemmo. Na lɛ́nu ka aku kɔ́kuku kutulo kɔyakun kɔni na baasia teeduo kaduli kedeedi kemmo. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku ɔ́si kaduli kedeedi kɔyakun kenye útédu kaduli kebliidi kayakun kenye na ubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ.
Bákɔku Kayakun Kani Nkya Katɔ Kakɛ
20Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku kayakun kani nkya katɔ kakɛ. 21Kayakun kamɛni lɛnɔ kebo bagyumane lɛtɔ ɛtɛ na ulu ɔni ntɛ úsela lɛlɔ. Lɛtɔ lɛmɛni bɔkɔku ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ ku ɔban kayakun kani nkya ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ ƒui lɛnɔ use aani kalɛ kani na use na ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kayakun. Na ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie ɔban kayakun kani na katɔ kakɛ mmɔ lɛnɔ ɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ bune ku lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ bɔbɛbɛ. 22Na lɛƒansili ku ɔban awodu ku ala ani na bánwi na ebo udu kenye béti bákya awodu ammɔ bɔdia ni, ese aani kalɛ na use na ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kayakun mmɔ kemmo kalɛ. Kɔnyakɔ libili maatɛ na adubɔkɔ etédu ɔban ɔmɛni kenye na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo unye kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ. 23Na ulu ɔtɛ ɔ́si mmɔ úsie kakpakɔ kaduli geen geen kemmo kɔnakunwi aani kalɛ na ɔtɛ ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kayakun úsie mmɔ. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku kayakun kani na anumi mɛni úti úsie kayakun kamaadi na lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ.
Búsie Kayakun Kadani
24Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi na búsie na kayakun kani ka kada kakɛ. Na ɔ́kɔku awodu ku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kayakun úlieku kɔyakun kudeedi kɔni na ɔ́ka bɔkɔku pɛpɛɛpɛ. 25Na lɛƒansili lɛkya bagyumanane lɛtɔ lɛni ɔban ɔmɛni kemmo ku ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo ɔban ɔmɛni kayakun kemmo. Na ɔban ɔmɛni lɛnɔ bune bɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ. 26Kɔnyakɔ libili maatɛ na adubɔkɔ etédu ɔban ɔmɛni kenye na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo unye ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ lili ƒui. Na ɔtɔ anumi aatina kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ. Na bánwi ala na ebo udu kenye béti bákya awodu ammɔ akya na ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. 27Na si ánu ávia kaduli kedeedi kamɛni úsie kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya kemmo kada kakɛ ni, ɔban kayakun kadi kenye. Na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku kuƒi kɔni nkya ɔban kayakun kani na anumi mɛni ku kani kemmo ntɛ na ubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ.
Kasiakɔ Katɛ Lɛban Lɛmmɔ Kenye Líduo Kakpakɔ Kaduli Geen
28Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bɔ́sia ɔban kayakun kani na kakpakɔ kada kakɛ mmɔ bútéduo kaduli kani na kemmo. Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku ɔban kayakun kammɔ na kélie ku kɔni na kaduli kedeedi awodu kemmo. 29-30Na geen ni, lɛla biala na lɛkya ulu lɛlɔ lílieku ekpo edeedi adi. Na bagyumane lɛtɔ ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ ku ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na adubɔvia-nwu eduo ɔban ɔmmɔ kemmo ku lɛƒansili ƒui lise aani lideedi lɛdi kalɛ. Na ɔban ɔmmɔ ɔlati bune bubo lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ, na bɔbɛbɛ lɛnɔ bubo lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ. 31Na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia mɛni eduo ɔban ɔmmɔ kemmo anumi aatina kaduli kedeedi kammɔ na ala ani na bánwi aani ebo udu na béti bákya kasiakɔ kammɔ ulu akya. Na libili maane násia úsie ɔban ɔmmɔ kenye.
32Ka bɔ́si mmɔ ni, bɔ́sia ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kemmo bútéduo kaduli kani na kemmo mmɔ kemmo na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku mmɔ lɛnɔ. Na mɛni lɛnɔ úlieku kudeedi. 33Bagyumanane lɛtɔ ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ ku ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo ƒui bɔkɔku bɔdi unwi aani budeedi kalɛ. Na lɛƒansili lɛkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ƒui kemmo. Na ɔban ɔmmɔ bune bɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ. Na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ bubo lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ. 34Na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo mmɔ anumi aatina kaduli kedeedi kammɔ. Na bánwi ala na ebo udu kenye bákya awodu ani na ulu lɛlɔ. Na libili maatɛ násia úsie ɔban ɔmmɔ kenye.
35Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi úsienku ɔban ɔni na katɔ kakɛ. Na ɔ́kɔku ɔban ɔmmɔ na bɔkɔku bunwi pɛ kani na ɔdi ku lɛkladi. 36Bagyumane lɛtɔ ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ ku ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na baasia teeduo mmɔ ƒui ni, lɛƒansili lɛkya ɔna ƒui lɛlɔ. Nwuna bune bɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ. Na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ. 37Na ɔban ɔmɛni lɛnɔ aani lɛni nkya kaduli kani na kemmo mmɔ kalɛ ni, nwuna anumi aatina kaduli kedeedi na bánwi ala aani ebo udu bákya awodu ani na ulu lɛlɔ mmɔ akya. Libili maane nsia útédu ɔban ɔmmɔ kenye.
Lɛ́nu Ɔtɔ Ɔni Kemmo Na Baadú Bebuo Taakpa
38-39Na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo ɔban ɔmmɔ kemmo na katɔ kakɛ mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu ka ala kasiakɔ ine bɔlɛ. Inyɔ na ɔƒɛnyi unwi na inyɔ lɛnɔ na ɔƒɛnyi ɔkladi. Na nwuna lɛlɔ na baadú bebuo bani na baakyula taabla akpala. Na ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kamadɔ ni, ɔtɔ blii ɔdi unye ɔni kemmo na baakpila bebuo bamɛni asa na badu-ma bakyula ƒui bete Unwoti na ɔƒɔ-nwu anu iye bakpa babla ekpidi lili buvele akpala. 40Ala kɔsiakɔ ine bamba linye kaduli kedeedi kammɔ libili lɛni násia lísie ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na baasia teeduo mmɔ. 41Anwuɔsu ala kɔsiakɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui kubo maane. Ine na keyi na ine lɛnɔ na ɔtɔ kemmo kesii kani na baadú bebuo mmɔ 42-43ku kesii kani na baasia-ni asa na beti bakyula na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ.
Na kɔsiakɔ kɔni nlɛ ɔtɔ kemmo kɔmadɔ ni, atabi ala kɔsiakɔ kɔdi kɔlɛ na kɔ́kuku aani animi ntɛ kukolo aavlanyɔ na bɔbɛbɛ ku bune ƒui bɔdi aani animi kukolo avlaatɛ avlaatɛ. Na ana lɛlɔ na baasia ala ani na beeti taadu bebuo. Na bébo ewele aani bune ndi animi kukolo ɛtɛ ɛtɛ bálɛ awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ bámana.
Ɔtɔ Ɔni Kemmo Na Bakpane Baakya
44Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi na bútéduo kaduli kani nkya kemmo mmɔ kemmo. Mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu lɛtɔ inyɔ na unwi unye ɔban ɔni na kaduli kani na kemmo mmɔ katɔ kakɛ, na ɔkladi unye kaduli kani na kemmo mmɔ kada kakɛ. 45Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ɔtɔ ɔni na aanu ka unye ɔban ɔni na katɔ kakɛ mmɔ kɔmadɔ ni, anwu ndi bakpane bani mɔɔbla kabla na kakpakɔ ɔdi. 46Na ɔni nnye ɔban ɔni kada kakɛ mmɔ kamadɔ ni, mmɔ ndi bekyuli bani muubunku kabla na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ɔdi. Na bana ƒui Sadok bebi ku bawɔ bani ndi Lewiƒuɔ bani kani na Unwoti úte kuƒi ka babla Unwoti bakpane.”
Lɛ́nu Kakpakɔ Kaduli Geen Ku Kakpakɔ Kammɔ
47Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku kaduli kani kemmo mmɔ na kana bune bɔdi lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ na bɔbɛbɛ lɛnɔ lɛni kani. Na lɛ́nu lɛkpabi lɛdi na kakpakɔ kammɔ anumi.
48Búsie bútédu kakpakɔ lɛgbanya kemmo na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku kayakun kammɔ na nwuna bune bɔdi lɛgba aavlanyɔ-ine. Na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba maane. Na ɔ́si kayakun mmɔ úsie kowodu kɔmmɔ kudɔ ubo lɛgba ɛlɔ ɛlɔ ɔvi ɔni ku ɔni. 49Na lɛgbanya mmɔ geen anwu ubo lɛgba avlaatɛ-ine bune na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba aavlanyɔ. Na básia libili bétédu mmɔ. Na atabi akpa anyɔ enye libili lɛmɛni ɔdi biala ɔvi ɔni ku ɔni.

english_text:
1Next we went into the main room of the temple. The man measured the doorway of this room: It was 3 meters wide, 2five meters long, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was two and a half meters. The main room itself was 20 meters by 10 meters.
3-4Then the man walked to the far end of the temple's main room and said, “Beyond this doorway is the most holy place.” He first measured the doorway: It was one meter wide, 3 meters long, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was 3.5 meters. Then he measured the most holy place, and it was 10 meters square.
The Storage Rooms of the Temple
5The man measured the wall of the temple, and it was three meters thick. Storage rooms two meters wide were built against the outside of the wall. 6There were three levels of rooms, with 30 rooms on each level, and they rested on ledges that were attached to the temple walls, so that nothing was built into the walls. 7The walls of the temple were thicker at the bottom than at the top, which meant that the storage rooms on the top level were wider than those on the bottom level. Steps led from the bottom level, through the middle level, and into the top level.
8The temple rested on a stone base three meters high, which also served as the foundation for the storage rooms. 9The outside walls of the storage rooms were two and a half meters thick; there was nothing between these walls 10and the nearest buildings ten meters away. 11One door led into the storage rooms on the north side of the temple, and another door led to those on the south side. The stone base extended two and a half meters beyond the outside wall of the storage rooms.
The West Building and the Measurements of the Temple
12I noticed another building: It faced the west end of the temple and was 35 meters wide, 45 meters long, and had walls over 2.5 meters thick.
13The man measured the length of the temple, and it was 50 meters. He then measured from the back wall of the temple, across the open space behind the temple, to the back wall of the west building; it was 50 meters. 14The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also 50 meters.
15Finally, the man measured the length of the west building, including the side rooms on each end, and it was also 50 meters.
The Inside of the Temple
The inside walls of the temple's porch and main room 16were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood. 17The paneling stopped just above the doorway. These walls were decorated 18-20with carvings of winged creatures and had a carving of a palm tree between the creatures. Each winged creature had two faces: A human face looking at the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face looking at the palm tree on the other side. These designs were carved into the paneling all the way around the two rooms.
21The doorframe to the temple's main room was in the shape of a rectangle.
The Wooden Altar
In front of the doorway to the most holy place was something that looked like 22a wooden altar. It was one and a half meters high and one meter square, and its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said, “This is a reminder that the Lord is constantly watching over his temple.”
The Doors in the Temple
23Both the doorway to the main room of the temple and the doorway to the most holy place had two doors, 24and each door had two sections that could fold open. 25The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors. 26The walls on each side of this porch had small windows and were also decorated with carvings of palm trees.
translation_text:
1Ɔmmɔ kama bútéduo kakpakɔ ɔtɔ geen kemmo na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kayakun. Na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba leevu, 2na bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba leevu-maatɛ. Na ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ɔlati ɔdi lɛgba liti ku leevu-maane. Na ɔ́si kayakun mmɔ úsie kowodu kudɔ ubo lɛgba maane ɔvi ɔni ku ɔni.
3-4Ɔnana ɔmɛni úsie útédu ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ ƒui na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Si ávia kayakun kamɛni ni, ésela kesii kani ndi kakpakɔ katɔma kedee.” Ɔ́ka kayakun kammɔ bɔkɔku na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba lɛgba ɛtɛ na bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba leevu. Na ɔ́si kayakun mmɔ úse kowodu kudɔ ɔvi ɔni ku ɔni ubo lɛgba leevu-inyɔ. Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́kɔku katɔma kedee kammɔ na ubo lɛgba avlaatɛ-ine ɔƒɛni unwi ɔkladi lɛnɔ lɛni kani.
Lɛ́nu Kakpakɔ Ala Kesekɔ
5Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku kakpakɔ kowodu kɔmmɔ na nwuna bugbigbli bɔdi lɛgba leevu. Na bátu ala kesekɔ bámana kowodu kɔmadi lɛlɔ na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ ubo lɛgba maatɛ. 6Katu taamana kɔtɛ na ɔdi. Na bɔmana biala bɔda lɛtɔ avlaatɛ. Na bátu lɛtɔ wɛlɛ lɛmɛni básia atabi kɔlɛkɛ kɔni ndanku awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ na bátatu ala kusekɔ kɔmɛni bátakya awodu ammɔ kemmo. 7Kakpakɔ awodu ammɔ égbigbli na kalɔ kakɛ utulo katɔ kakɛ, anwuɔsu ala kusekɔ kɔni nkya katɔ kemmo kúwi kutulo kɔni nkya kada kakɛ. Na ubo kɔnyakɔ kanyakɔ ɔ́si bamana budeedi ku unyɔdi útédu ɔtɛdi lɛlɔ.
8Kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔlati kenye atabi ɔka ɔni nákuku lɛgba leevu lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kani ndi ɔka ute ala kusekɔ lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ lɛnɔ. 9Ala kusekɔ lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ awodu amadi égbigbli lɛgba maane na lɛla lɛdi liiibo awodu ammɔ ntɛ. 10Na ɔtɔ ɔni nákpɛ úde kakpakɔ kamɛni bɔgyu bɔdi lɛgba avlaatɛ-ine. 11Kayakun kenwi kani na adubɔsia étéduo ala kusekɔ kɔni nkya kusie kakpakɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ kemmo. Na kabambadi lɛnɔ kakya késie ala kusekɔ kɔni nkya kakpakɔ kammɔ kada kakɛ kemmo. Na lɛtabi ɔka ɔni lɛlɔ na kakpakɔ kammɔ kenye kábɛbɛ kávia késie kama lɛgba maane úbo ɔ́vi ala kusekɔ awodu amadi ammɔ.
12Ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛ́nu ɔtɔ bamba ɔdi ka unye na nwuna anumi aatina kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ. Nwuna bɔbɛbɛ ubo lɛgba eti anyɔ ku leevu-maatɛ na úne lɛgba eti atɛ na awodu ammɔ butigbli ɔdi lɛgba maane.
13Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku kakpakɔ kammɔ na nwuna bune ubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ. Amu na úsie útákɔku kakpakɔ kammɔ kowodu kɔmadi ɔ́vi kaduli kani nwi kakpakɔ kama mmɔ úsie útédu ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ɔƒɛ mmɔ kowodu kama na ubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ. 14Kalɔ ƒiaa kani nwi kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ anumi ku lɛƒɛnyi ƒui bɔkɔku lɛnɔ bubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ.
15Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ɔƒɛ kanukɔ mmɔ bune ku lɛtɔ lɛni na mma lɛƒɛnyi inyɔ bɔmmɔ na ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ.
Kalɛ Na Bábla Kakpakɔ Kemmo
Kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛgbanya kemmo awodu ku kesii kani ndi ɔtɔ keliekɔ geen ni, 16ligyii sɔɔn na bákana bámana awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ ku kalɔ ƒui útédu ƒansili. Na kayakun ku lɛƒansili wɛlɛ wɛlɛ lɛmmɔ ku lɛtɔ lɛni na lɛƒɛnyi ni, baakana na beebi-ni ligyii lɛmmɔ. 17Na kalɛ na béti ligyii bákana bámana awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ ni, kayakun katɔ kani na ɔ́wɔ. Na bákya awodu ammɔ akya geen 18-20ku ala ani na bánwi na bebweyi badi mbo avwi udu kenye na bánwi ebo udu bényene-ma ntɛ. Na bebweyi bani mbo avwi mɛni bebo anumi lɛtɔtɔ ku kama. Ukyuli anumi aanu ebo ani bényene mmɔ kakɛ kenwi na gyata anumi lɛnɔ aanu ebo ani nnye ɔvi unyɔdi. Na bánwi ala amɛni bákya ligyii lɛkanadi lɛmmɔ kemmo na awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́ka ɔ́ma lɛtɔ inyɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo.
21Na kakpakɔ kammɔ kayakun ugyii ɔni bákya kesii kani geen ndi ɔtɔ keliekɔ ni, nwuna bɔnu kemmo use aani adaka gyɔlɔɔ ɔni mbo lɛƒɛnyi ine.
Bábla Ugyii Lɛkpabi
Na kayakun kani néti késela kakpakɔ katɔma kedee kemmo ni, lɛla lɛdi linye na ɔɔtina aani 22ugyii lɛkpabi. Ɔ́kuku lɛgba ɛlɔ na nwuna bune ku bɔbɛbɛ ƒui bɔdi lɛgba ine ine. Na akpa ani nda nwuna lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ na ɔda kalɔ aani ɔka ni, ligyii na béti bábla-ni. Mmɔ na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ɔmɛni mɔɔtina ka Unwoti ɔɔsia nwuna kakpakɔ kammɔ anu uwi ndi uwi.”
Kakpakɔ Kɔkalɛkɔ
23Kakpakɔ ɔtɔ geen ɔmmɔ ku kakpakɔ katɔma kedee ƒui ni, ubo kɔlɛmikɔ lɛvi inyɔ. 24Na kɔlɛmikɔ kɔmɛni kubo ntɛ bule ɔni na bakana na báƒɛ-nwu basia ɔkpanadi lɛlɔ. 25Na ɔtɔ keliekɔ geen kammɔ kɔlɛmikɔ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bánwi bebweyi ku avwi ku ebo udu básia aani kalɛ na bábla na awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ na ɔtɔ kemmo. Na asa na adubuduo ɔtɔ kemmo kayakun anumi kesii kani ndi lɛgbanya mɛni ni, ligyii na béti bébi mmɔ. 26Na lɛgbanya awodu ammɔ ni, lɛƒansili lɛkya na bánwi bebweyi ku avwi bammɔ ku ebo udu bákya ani lɛnɔ akya.

english_text:
The Sacred Rooms for the Priests
1-2After the man and I left the temple and walked back to the outer courtyard, he showed me a set of rooms on the north side of the west building. This set of rooms was 50 meters long and 25 meters wide. 3On one side of them was the 10 meters of open space that ran alongside the temple, and on the other side was the sidewalk that circled the outer courtyard. The rooms were arranged in three levels 4with doors that opened toward the north, and in front of them was a walkway five meters wide and 50 meters long. 5The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level. 6The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard. 7-8To the north was a privacy wall 25 meters long, 9-10and at the east end of this wall was the door leading from the courtyard to these rooms.
There was also a set of rooms on the south side of the west building. 11These rooms were exactly like those on the north side, and they also had a walkway in front of them. 12The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.
13The man then said to me:
These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right. 14When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people.
The Size of the Temple Area
15After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area. 16He used his measuring stick to measure the east side of this wall; it was 250 meters long. 17-19Then he measured the north side, the south side, and the west side of the wall, and they were each 250 meters long, 20and so the temple area was a perfect square. The wall around this area separated what was sacred from what was ordinary.
translation_text:
Bakpane Ɔtɔ Ɔni Bédie Bése Sɛsɛɛ
1-2Kama ƒui uwi ɔni na bɔ́tɔlɔ kakpakɔ kesii mmɔ búnwini búbo kaduli kedeedi kammɔ kemmo ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́tina-mi lɛtɔ lɛdi nnye lisu na ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kudɔ katɔ kakɛ, na lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ bune ɔdi lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ. 3Na lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ɔƒɛnyi unwi ni, kalɔ ƒiaa kewi na kana bɔkɔku ɔdi lɛgba avlaatɛ-ine ɔdanku kakpakɔ kammɔ. Na ɔƒɛnyi ɔkladi ɔdi lɛgba kasiakɔ kani náka kámana kaduli kedeedi kammɔ. Na bátu lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ básiaku lɛlɔ esu ntɛ bule kɔtɛ. 4Na bálɛmi lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kɔyakun béwi úti úsie katɔ kakɛ na lɛgba kasiakɔ katɛ kɔyakun kɔmmɔ anumi na kábɛbɛ lɛgba leevu-maatɛ na úne lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ. 5Lɛtɔ lɛtɔdi kemmo lise blii suɛ litulo lɛni nkya ntɛntɛ. Na lɛni ntɛntɛ mmɔ lɛdi lɛnɔ lɛsɔ lise blii suɛ litulo lɛni na kalɔ. 6Lɛtɔ lɛni nkya kalɔ nda lɛni nkya ntɛ ku katɔ lɛdi ƒui, anwuɔsu akpa abambadi adi asɔ aaada lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ aani kalɛ na use lɛtɔ lɛbambadi lɛni nnye kaduli kemmo mmɔ. 7-8Na katɔ kakɛ ƒui ɔtɔ ɔdi údie lɛlɔ na úne lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ. 9-10Na ɔtɔ ɔmɛni ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ni, kayakun kadi kakya na ulu ɔtɛ ɔ́si kaduli kamɛni kemmo útéduo lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo.
Na lɛtɔ lisu lɛdi lɛnɔ lɛkya ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ɔƒɛ kanukɔ mmɔ kada kakɛ. 11Lɛtɔ lɛmɛni lise aani lɛni nkya katɔ kakɛ mmɔ udu na ani lɛnɔ libo lɛgba kasiakɔ na nina anumi. 12Na kayakun kani na baasia teesie lɛtɔ lɛmɛni kemmo ɔkya ɔtɔ nnye anumi mmɔ na nwuna kowodu kúti kúsie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kalɛ mmɔ.
13Mmɔ na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Lɛtɔ lɛni na nkya kakpakɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ ku kada kakɛ ni, ani bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte Unwoti bakpane badubɔdi akpala ani nse kedee etulo ƒui mmɔ. Na akpala amɛni ndi antabi udu akpala ku ekpidi lili buvele akpala ku unwi bɔbla akpala. 14Si uwi ɔni na bakpane báklibi lɛlɔ ka balɛ kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, lɛtɔ lɛmɛni kemmo na ɔlɛka basia asa na benwini besie kaduli kammɔ kemmo. Na bana adala ani na bábla bése sɛsɛɛ ute kabla kammɔ ni, mɛni na ɔlɛka bedie adala ammɔ bese na beti adala bamba bada asa na ama ku bekyuli bamba bataasala ku lɛlɔ.”
Bánu Kakpakɔ Kaduli Geen Bubomo
15Uwi ɔni na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ lɛtɔ lɛni nkya kakpakɔ kaduli geen mmɔ bɔkɔku ni, ɔ́kpanku-mi na bɔ́sɔ bútásia ɔban kayaku kani nkya ɔƒɛ katukɔ mmɔ na útákɔku kowodu kɔni náka kɔ́mana mɛni. 16Na úti nwuna ugyii lɛkɔkula na ɔ́kɔku kowodu kɔmɛni kakɛ kani nésie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ na kúne lɛgba eti maane ku aavlene. 17-19Lɛni kani na ɔ́kɔku katɔ kakɛ ku kada kakɛ ku ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ, na ekpo amɛni ƒui ɔdi biala bune bɔdi lɛgba eti maane ku aavlene. 20Anwuɔsu kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ katɛ lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na kowodu kɔni náka kɔ́mana mɛni ɔɔtina ka béle ala ani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ bete Unwoti ku ala aƒuƒuɛdi ntɛ.

english_text:
The Lord's Glory Returns to the Temple
1The man took me back to the east gate of the temple, 2 where I saw the brightness of the glory of Israel's God coming from the east. The sound I heard was as loud as ocean waves, and everything around was shining with the dazzling brightness of his glory. 3This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River.
I immediately bowed with my face to the ground, 4and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple. 5The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
6The man was standing beside me, and I heard the Lord say from inside the temple:
7Ezekiel, son of man, this temple is my throne on earth. I will live here among the people of Israel forever. They and their kings will never again disgrace me by worshiping idols at local shrines or by setting up memorials to their dead kings. 8Israel's kings built their palaces so close to my holy temple that only a wall separated them from me. Then these kings disgraced me with their evil ways, and in my fierce anger I destroyed them. 9But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
10The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it, 11then if they are truly sorry, describe for them the design and shape of the temple, the gates, the measurements, and how the buildings are arranged. Explain the regulations about worshiping there, then write down these things, so they can study and obey them.
12The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple.
The Altar
13 According to the official standards, the altar in the temple had the following measurements: Around the bottom of the altar was a gutter 50 centimeters wide and 50 centimeters deep, with a 25-centimeter ledge on the outer rim. 14-17The altar rested on a base and had three sections, each one of them square. The bottom section was 8 meters on each side and one meter high. The middle section was 7 meters on each side and 2 meters high, and it had a 25-centimeter rim around its outer edge. The top section, which was 6 meters on each side and 2 meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side.
The Dedication of the Altar
18 The Lord God said:
Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do: 19The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin. 20Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me. 21Then take the body of the bull outside the temple area and burn it at the special place.
22The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 23Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them, 24and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
25Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them. 26The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use. 27From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Unwoti Bukeye Búnwini Búbo Kakpakɔ Kammɔ Lɛlɔ
1Ɔnana ɔmmɔ útiku-mi na bɔ́sɔ búnwini búsie kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. 2Mmɔ na lɛ́nu Israel Unwoti Katɔti bukeye ka bɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ bɔdubo. Na línu kɔku kɔdi aani kalɛ na ɛpu ɔɔbla kɔku bonwu, na Unwoti bukeye bɔmɛni bɔ́ya na lɛla biala nkya amadɔ liikeye taatu anumi. 3Kɔyu kemmo ala bɔnu bɔmɛni búlieku bɔni na lɛ́nu uwi ɔni na Katɔti úbo úbakyula Yerusalem na ɔyila-nwu udu ku uwi ɔni na lɛ́nu na Keba Ketu kudɔ. 4Katɔti bukeye bɔmɛni bɔ́sia kakpakɔ ɔban kayakun na ɔƒɛ katukɔ mmɔ na búbeduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. 5Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́ya na lɛ́ta línye mina lɛgba lɛlɔ na kútiku-mi kúsienku kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya kemmo ƒui na mmɔ, na lɛ́nu ka Unwoti bukeye bɔ́ƒɔ kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ ƒui.
6Ɔnana ɔmmɔ unye-mi ɔƒɛnyi na línu ka Unwoti ɔ́tɛmi ɔ́siku kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ɔnini, 7“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, kakpakɔ kamɛni ndi mina lɛgaboku lɛni lɛlɔ na nli na kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni. Na mɛni na ndubo bulie na mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ akɔ úti úsela uwi ƒui. Na ama ku bana baga basɔ balakya-mi kɔƒa na basɔ batátaakpa baƒiɔ badi. 8Israel baga bátu bana lɛtɔ na lide mina kakpakɔ suɛlɛ suɛlɛ ɔni na kowodu kani nkya ntɛ. Nsu baga bamɛni bákya-ma kɔƒa na bana likyulikpi ala bɔbla ɔsu. Anwuɔsu na líti kɔnyi lɛ́kya-ma geen na lɛ́yila-ma udu. 9Nsu si bekyuli bamɛni báda baƒiɔ bɔkpa báya na bábwɛ ala ani na bávɔ na bánwi bése baanu mmɔ ni, ndubulieku-ma uwi ƒui. 10Ɔlɛka kɔƒa kukpo Israelƒuɔ na bebo abi na bana ekpidi ani na bábla ɔsu. Anwuɔsu tɛmiku-ma siku mina kakpakɔ lɛlɔ. 11Na si bana ekpidi éduo-ma sɔsɔ ni, na asɔku lɛla biala na ánu na kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ku lɛban lɛmmɔ ku kalɛ na bákɔku lɛla biala ku kalɛ na bényene lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ. Na edie ɔda bubo bɔni ndanku kalɛ na ɔlɛka bakpa na mmɔ na enweni lɛla biala ese kalɛ na batɛya kaduɛ na badi ala ammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.
12“Na mina kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani na kɔbi lɛlɔ mmɔ ni, ɔlɛka bada mmɔ edu aani lɛla lɛni na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte-mi! Ɔmɛni ndi ɔda bubo bɔni náƒɛ kuye butulo ƒui ɔ́siku mina kakpakɔ lɛlɔ.
Kalɛ Na Unwoti Lɛkpabi Lise
13“Aani kalɛ na Unwoti ɔlati ɔ́lɛ ugyii úse ni, lɛkpabi lɛni nnye kakpakɔ kemmo ni, ubo bɔkɔku bɔdi. Na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kalɔ kakɛ ni, bédie ɔvile ɔdi báka bámana-nwu na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi akɔkɔ ene bɔbɛbɛ ku bɔgyu lɛnɔ akɔkɔ ene. Na ɔvile ɔmmɔ kɔtu kɔtu na keyi kakɛ ni, béti atabi kɔlɛkɛ akɔkɔ anyɔ bɔbɛbɛ bálɛ bamana. 14-17Lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɛ ɔka ɔdi lɛlɔ na ubo bule akpa atɛ. Na ɔdi biala lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ bɔkɔku búlieku lɛlɔ. Bule budeedi bɔkɔku ndi lɛgba aavlanyɔ-maatɛ bune ku bɔbɛbɛ ƒui lɛni kani na nwuna bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba ɛtɛ. Na ntɛntɛ ubo lɛgba aavlanyɔ-ine bune ku bɔbɛbɛ ƒui lɛni kani na bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba maatɛ. Na atabi kɔlɛkɛ akɔkɔ anyɔ bɔbɛbɛ bɔ́ka bɔ́mana-nwu kalɔ na atu atu. Na bule bɔtɛdi bɔkɔku bɔdi lɛgba aavlanyɔ bune ku bɔbɛbɛ ƒui lɛni kani na bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba maatɛ na nwuna katɔ na baakyula akpala. Na nwuna ekpo ene ammɔ ni, ala adi alɛ aani akɔ ese. Ɔƒɛni ubili kakɔkɔ kani na básia bétédu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ ɔkya ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ.”
Bédie Lɛkpabi Lɛmmɔ Sɛsɛɛ Básɔku Bákya Katɔti Lɛkɔkɔ
18Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini,
“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, si uwi ɔni na bátu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ báwɔlɔ ni, ɔlɛka bakyula akpala nwuna lɛlɔ na bewi-ni ubugya na bedie-ni sɛsɛɛ basɔku bakya-mi lɛkɔkɔ. Na ndubɔtina-a ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na adubo ala ammɔ bɔbla. 19Ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Sadok bebi ku bawɔ bani nási Lewi kɔdua kemmo ni, ama kani na ɔlɛka babla kabla na mina kakpakɔ aani kalɛ na mina ɔda bubo bɔɔtina. Anwuɔsu ti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔkɔdi te-ma na badu bakyula babla alaekpidi lili buvele akpala. 20Na eti ubugya ɔmmɔ ɔdi ákwaa lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ekpo ene ammɔ. Na aya na ubugya ɔmmɔ ɔdi ususu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ bule bɔni ntɛntɛ mmɔ ekpo ammɔ. Na ɔdi lɛnɔ ususu atabi kɔlɛkɛ kɔni na bátu bámana mmɔ. Ɔmmɔ ndubɔya na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛbla sɛɛn kalɛ na bataabla akpala nwuna lɛlɔ teete-mi. 21Ɔmmɔ kama na beti ebuo ɔmmɔ balɛku kakpakɔ kaduli geen mmɔ na batákyula-nwu na kesii kani na báƒuna bése.
22“Kadi kegye ni, na beti ketukpa kani na kátasɔ kesii kadi na ɔ́manku batádu babla ekpidi lili buvele akpala. Na beti nwuna ubugya bakwaa lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ babla-ni sɛɛn aani kalɛ na bábla akɔ ɔkɔdi ɔmmɔ ɔdi. 23Ɔmmɔ kama na báƒuna akɔ ɔkɔdi ku koƒonu kɔgyani kɔkɔdi bani na bátasɔ kesi kesii 24na biti-ma biboku mina kakpakɔ. Ɔkpane ɔdubuti mma ɔkuna uwi-ma lɛlɔ na beti-ma babla kɔnu bɔsia akpala bete-mi na ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.
25“Emeyi maatɛ ani nsia kadi biala megye ni, ɔlɛka bɛdu ese ku akɔ ku koƒonu bete-mi aani alaekpidi lili buvele akpala. Na ɔlɛka bɛnu ka bátasɔ kesii kadi. 26Emeyi ammɔ kemmo ni, ɔkpane ɔdubo lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ bɔbla sɛɛn kalɛ na ɔmanku ute ka bakpa na nwuna lɛlɔ bete-mi. 27Na ɔ́si ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔkpane ɔdubo akpala butaabla na lɛkpabi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔyɔ-ni kaƒɔ na uvele kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiku-mi kudɔ ɔni ndi unwi bɔbla akpala. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_text:
The East Gate Must Remain Closed
1The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed. 2The Lord said:
I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it. 3The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate.
People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
4Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
5The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not. 6Tell those rebellious people of Israel:
I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways! 7My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement. 8Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
9And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel.
The Levites Are Punished
The Lord said:
10Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished! 11They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers. 12But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning, 13and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins. 14They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple.
Rules for Priests
The Lord said:
15The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices. 16They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
17 When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple. 18Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work. 19 And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
20 Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long. 21 They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
22 A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
23 Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean. 24They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
25 Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister. 26If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later, 27he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
28 I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own. 29 Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me. 30The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
31 Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_text:
Ɔlɛka Bakalɛ Ɔƒɛ Katukɔ Ɔban Kayakun Benyene
1Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔsɔku-mi úboku kaduli kedeedi kesii kani nde kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na lɛ́nu ka bákalɛ ɔban ɔmɛni kɔyakun kɔlɛmikɔ ƒui bényene. 2Unwoti ɔnini, “Ɔban ɔmɛni kayakun na ami Unwoti Israel Katɔti lɛ́sia líbo. Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka bakalɛ-nwu benyene usela uwi ƒui! Na ukyuli ɔni ɔsɔ utasia mmɔ uteduo iye ɔlɛ lɛnɔ. 3Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdi Israel lɛlɔ ɔkana na ɔsia ɔban ɔmɛni kemmo ɔtɔ kayakun uduo ubadi akpala ani na bábla béte-mi adila kedee na mmɔ kani na ɔdubɔkana na ɔsia.”
Bétete Bekyuli Badi Kuƒi Ka Beduo Kakpakɔ Kemmo
4Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ útiku-mi na bútásia ɔban kayakun kani na katɔ kakɛ na kakpakɔ anumi mmɔ. Na lɛ́nu kalɛ na Unwoti uukeye na bukeye bɔmmɔ bɔ́ƒɔ kakpakɔ mmɔ ƒui. Kɔnakunwi ni, líbo kalɔ na líti mina anumi líbi kalɔ.
5Unwoti ɔnini,
“Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, ndubo-ɔ ɔda bubo bɔni ndanku mina kakpakɔ bute. Anwuɔsu nu kaduɛ na ati bekyuli bani udu líte kuƒi ka beduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ku bani na ńtete kuƒi. Ami Unwoti Katɔti muubó-mii ɔda kpakplaa ka bɛda bina likyulikpi ngba bulie bɛya. 6Su Israel kadi bekyuli bani náta bénye-mi lɛlɔ mmɔ anii ami Unwoti Katɔti muubó-ma ɔda ka bada bana likyulikpi ala bɔbla baya. 7Bɛ́kya mina kakpakɔ kammɔ kɔƒa na uwi ɔni na bɛ́ya na baƒɔ bani na balabu-mi na bebo atuɔkplu bébeduo mmɔ uwi ɔni na baabla akpala teete-mi. Bɛ́ƒiɔ-mi na bíbile lɛla kedee lɛni na línyimiku-mii. 8Uwi ɔni na ɔlɛka bɛsia ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ bɛkpa-mi ni, baƒɔ mmomu na bíti bínyene kenye ka bataanu lɛkpa lɛmmɔ lɛlɛ na mina kakpakɔ. 9Anwuɔsu na ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu nnii naaawia ɔƒɔ biala na ulábu-mi na ɔdi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ka uduo mina kakpakɔ. Na ɔmɛni ɔdanku baƒɔ bani nli Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ.”
Unwoti Ɔ́ni Lewiƒuɔ Kɔtu
10Unwoti ɔnini, “Lewiƒuɔ bani bénwini kama bákya-mi na basiaku bana kadi bekyuli badi na baakpá baƒiɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔdi ka bani Lewiƒuɔ bamɛni kɔtu! 11Ndubɔsɔ lite-ma kuƒi na bataabla kabla teete-mi na mina kakpakɔ aani kayakun bɔgyumana ku bebuo bani na badubuti bakpa-mi bɔdu na beteebunku bakpane bammɔ. 12Nsu ka Lewiƒuɔ bamɛni bébunku Israelƒuɔ na bákpa baƒiɔ ɔsu ni, ami Unwoti Katɔti líse kenye kpakplaa ka bani Lewiƒuɔ kɔtu, ɔsika bátabala Israelƒuɔ na benwini na baƒiɔ bɔkpa kama. 13Ka ɔ́si ɔƒɛni ni, nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na Lewiƒuɔ badi mina bakpane iye bani bede mina ala ani nse kedee muedi. Ɔsika ɔdi ka kɔƒa kukpo-ma na anumi ewi-ma kalɔ na bebo abi lɛnɔ na ekpidi ani na bábla na eesé lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔsu. 14Na kabla kpakplaa biala na ɔlɛka babla na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, ama ndubo-ka bɔbla.”
Béte Bakpane Bammɔ Ɔda Bubo Bɔdi
15Unwoti ɔnini, “Lewi kɔdua bebi bani ndi bakpane na bási Sadok ɔtɔ kemmo ni, bátalɛmi kama uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bénwini kama bákya-mi. Anwuɔsu ama kani ndubo bakpane kabla butaabla teete-mi. Na ama ndubo bebuo ubugya ku lɛmwi buteeti taakpa-mi. 16Ama ndubuduo mina kakpakɔ na babla akpala bete-mi na batɔnku bakladi na lɛkpa lɛmmɔ kemmo.
17“Si uwi ɔni na bébeduo mina kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya kemmo ƒui ni, ɔdi ka banu ka bada ɔkpane adala ani ndi kugyii evuo awu kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ mmɔ. Útalɛ ka mina ɔkpane ɔdi ɔkya awu ɔni béti unwo iye bebuo linwini bábla uwi ɔni na unye mina kabla kadi lɛlɔ na kaduli kamɛni kemmo iye kakpakɔ kemmo. 18Bana lɛdiku lɛni na beebi lili ku awu ɔlɔndi ɔni nda-ma kavobi muedi ɔlɛka ɔbla awu kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ɔmmɔ udu kalɛ ewulu asɔ alatuku-ma si baabla kabla. 19Na asa na badubɔlɛ kakpakɔ mmɔ lɛnɔ ni, ɔdi bedie ɔkpane adala ammɔ bese likpo kedee lɛni na báklibi bése na lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo na beti ama alati adala bada asa na basɔ batásalaku bana bekyuli na kaduli kemmo mmɔ. Si bábla lɛni ni, ukyuli bamba ɔdi ulétuku adala ammɔ na weboku ɔgbankpi nwuna lɛlɔ.
20“Ɔɔɔdi ka bakpane bekpeyi bana lili linwini si beewulo kɔnyana. Nsu ɔlɛka bada bana linwini edu na lileyi lilagya. 21Útalɛ ka bani ntɛ asa na besie kakpakɔ kaduli geen kemmo mmɔ.
22“Útalɛ ka ɔkpane uti uleku ɔni na ukyuli ɔdi úuti ɔ́nyonu. Adagyaa kani na ɔdi uti ɔsiku Israel kadi bekyuli akɔ iye ɔkpane bamba ukpinele.
23“Ɔdi ka bakpane bammɔ batina bekyuli kavumana kani nkya ala ani nse kedee ku ala keeke ntɛ. Na batina-ma ala ani nse sɛɛn ku ani neeese sɛɛn ntɛ. 24Na badubɔbla kabla aani litemi batɛne na baklibi unyeƒi biala basiaku mina bunyimi lɛlɔ. Na ama alati badubɔbla basiaku mina litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na batɔnku bekyuli na mina emeyi buni bɔdi lɛlɔ, na babla mina lɛnwunameyi lɛnɔ kedee.
25“Si ukyuli ɔdi útuku ukpine ni, úbile lɛlɔ likisi na ɔsɔ uuuse sɛɛn. Anwuɔsu utalɛ ka bakpane bani bede bekpine si ɔɔɔdi nwuna bawɔne iye bebi iye banwani bananabi iye belekubi bani neeelie kɔgya kani. 26Si ɔkpane ɔdi útuku ukpine ni, úbile lɛlɔ likisi na ɔsɔ uuuse sɛɛn. Na ɔlɛka ɔbla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi. Na emeyi maatɛ kama ni, 27ɔdi ka usie kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya kemmo ƒui na utábla likpidi lili buvele akpala. Na ɔmmɔ kama asa na ɔsɔ ɔkana na utaabla mina kabla aani ɔkpane kalɛ. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.
28“Ami ɔlati ndubo mina bakpane lɛlɔ butaanu, anwuɔsu beeebo kadikɔ kalɔ kadi bele bete-ma. 29Na lɛla lɛni na badubule bete-ma kenye ni, antabi udu etela ani na bekyuli badubuti babakpa bete-mi ku ekpidi lili buvele akpala ani na bekyuli badubɔbla unwi bɔbla akpala ni, badubɔƒɔ ana kakɛ kadi. Na lɛla biala na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na bábla-ni kedee bése sɛsɛɛ béte-mi ni, ɔdi bana lɛdi. 30Na edula edeedi biala na báƒɛ lɛnɔ adi bakpane bammɔ. Na ala ani na ukyuli ɔdi úse kenye na adi etela ni, ama lɛnɔ badubɔkɛ kakɛ kadi. Lɛni kani si bodobodo na mina kadi bekyuli akɔ ɔdi úƒi ni, na uti udeedi uboku bakpane bammɔ, na ndubute ukyuli ɔmmɔ kusɛ kusɛ anwu ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui si bábla ɔmɛni.
31“Bakpane beeebo kuƒi ka bakun aasɛ iye ebuo ɔni na anwu alati nékpi nwuna kukpi iye eƒiebuo.”

english_text:
The Lord's Sacred Land
The Lord said:
1When the land of Israel is divided among the twelve tribes, you must set aside an area that will belong to me. This sacred area will be 12.5 kilometers long and 10 kilometers wide. 2The temple will be on a piece of land 255 meters square, and the temple will be completely surrounded by an open space 25 meters wide.
3-4I will give half of my sacred land, a section 12.5 kilometers long and 5 kilometers wide, to the priests who serve in the temple. Their houses will be in this half, as well as my temple, which is the most sacred place of all.
5I will give the other half of my land to the Levites who work in my temple, and the towns where they will live will be there.
6Next to my sacred land will be an area 12.5 kilometers long and 3 kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem.
Land for Israel's Ruler
The Lord said:
7-8The regions west and east of my sacred land and the city of Jerusalem will belong to the ruler of Israel. He will be given the region between the western edge of my land and the Mediterranean Sea, and between the eastern edge of my land and the Jordan River. This will mean that the length of his property will be the same as the sections of land given to the tribes.
This property will belong to every ruler of Israel, so they will always be fair to my people and will let them live peacefully in the land given to their tribes.
Israel's Rulers Must Be Honest
9The Lord God said:
You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
10 So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures. 11The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
12The standard unit of weight will be the shekel. One shekel will equal 20 gerahs, and 60 shekels will equal one mina.
13Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me. 14They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor. 15Finally, they must bring one sheep out of every 200 from their flocks.
These offerings will be used as grain sacrifices, as well as sacrifices to please me and those to ask my blessing. I, the Lord, will be pleased with these sacrifices and will forgive the sins of my people.
16The people of Israel will bring you these offerings. 17But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people.
The Festivals
(Exodus 12.1-20; Leviticus 23.33-43)
18The Lord God said:
On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple. 19The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
20The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
21 Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast. 22On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people. 23Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them. 24He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
25 The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_text:
Bédie Kalɔ Sɛsɛɛ Bése Unwoti
1Unwoti ɔnini, “Si uwi ɔni na béti Israel kalɔ kammɔ béle béte adua leevu-anyɔ ammɔ ni, ɔlɛka bidie kesii kadi bise sɛsɛɛ bite-mi. Na likpo kedee lɛmɛni bune ɔlɛka bɔbla lɛma inyɔ ntɛ eluku bɔkɔku maane na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ ɔbla eluku aku. 2Mmɔ na mina kakpakɔ kadubunye. Kalɔ kamɛni ntɛ ni, badubɔkɔku lɛgba eti leevu-maatɛ ku lɛgba aavlanyɔ-ɛlɔ. Bɔbɛbɛ ku bune ƒui likeke. Na kalɔ kani kana bɔkɔku bɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-maatɛ ɔ́mana kakpakɔ kalɔ kammɔ ni, kadubuwi ukpludi.
3-4“Na ndubukulo kalɔ kani na bídie bíse sɛsɛɛ mɛni kakɛ kadi kani bune ndi eluku maane úsie eluku atɛ bɔbɛbɛ lite mina bakpane bani mɔɔbla-mi kabla. Na kesii kani nse kedee mɛni ni, badubɔtu bana lɛtɔ benyene ku mina kakpakɔ.
5“Na liti kakɛ kakladi lite Lewiƒuɔ bani muubunku kabla na mina kakpakɔ na mmɔ kani na badubɔkɛ lɛma lɛni kemmo na badubulie.
6“Ɔƒɛni kalɔ kani na bídie bíse sɛsɛɛ mɛni kudɔ ni, bɛda kalɔ bamba kani bune ndi eluku maane úsie eluku anyɔ bɔbɛbɛ biwi mmɔ. Na mɛni kadubɔbla kesii kani na Israelƒuɔ ƒui bakana belie.”
Badubute Israel Lɛlɔ Ɔdine Kalɔ Kadi
7-8Unwoti ɔnini, “Ɔmii ɔni nwi mina ɔmii ɔni na bídie bíse sɛsɛɛ mmɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ ku ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ku Yerusalem ƒui ɔdubɔbla Israel lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔdi. Na ɔ́si mina kalɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ útédu Mediterenia Ɛpu ntɛ ku ɔmii ɔni nwi ɔ́si mina kalɔ kammɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ útédu Yordan Ketu ntɛ ƒui ɔdubɔbla anwu ɔdi. Na ɔɔtina ka kalɔ kammɔ bune ɔdubɔbla aani kesii kani na béte adua ammɔ ƒui.
“Na kese kamɛni kadubɔbla lɛlɔ ɔdine biala ɔni melie madi Israel lɛlɔ ɔdi.”
Ɔlɛka Israel Lɛlɔ Badine Basu Litemi Geen Lɛmmɔ
9Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini,
“Amii Israel batɔnkune, bíiyu na bɛ́nya mina kadi bekyuli bɛ́kya uwi útu! Na mɔɔwia ka bɛda ekpidi bɔbla bɛya na bise kalɔ bitaabla ala siin taasiaku ulu lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́sɔ útalɛka binye mina bekyuli lɛlɔ na bɛbɔku-ma na bavi balɛ bana kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ami Unwoti násu.
10“Anwuɔsu ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ni, biti unu ku bumomo akɔkula abuni bitaakɔku ala teete bekyuli. 11Na biti anta lɛkyami bɔkɔku binwini lɛla lɛni biti bitaakɔku edula ebi teete bekyuli. Na ɔsii keyile kenwini lɛla lɛni na biti bitaakɔku nnɔ ku ala ani na beedú taakɔku ala ammɔ udu teete bekyuli. Na ala amɛni ƒui akana na akɔ etédu kangyi keyile.
12“Limeyi lɛyuƒɔla sika ɔƒualadi ubi ɔdubunye ute unu lɛkɔkula. Na sika ɔƒualadi ubi unwi ɔmɛni ɔdubunye egulabi aavlanyɔ kenye. Na sika ɔƒualadi ebi liti ku leevu ndi koƒo kunwi.
13“Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune, bɛya na bekyuli bammɔ bele bana anta ani na bákɛ akpa liti ku leevu na beti lɛkpa linwi beboku-mi aani bana etela. 14Na bele nnɔ bɔni na bákɛ lɛnɔ akpa eti anyɔ na beti lɛkpa linwi beboku-mi. Na nnɔ ɔsii unengudi ɔni na baakɔ́ku ala na badubuti bakɔku bumomo bɔmɛni beboku-mi. 15Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, ukyuli biala na ubo baƒonu eti ene ni, ɔlɛka uti unwi uboku-mi.
“Na etela amɛni ni, adubunwini adila bɔsia lɛkpabi lɛlɔ teete-mi kalɛ na kaƒɔ kayɔ-mi na bevele kusɛ kusɛ basiku-mi kudɔ. Na akpala amɛni adubɔyɔ ami Unwoti kaƒɔ na liti mina bekyuli ekpidi lɛkyiɛ-ma.
16“Israel kadi bekyuli ndubuti etela amɛni beboku-ɔ. 17Nsu kɔbuli kɔwɔdi bɔlɛ emeyi bɔdi ku Lɛnwunameyi ku emeyi kedee bamba bɔdi ni, amii batɔnkune bammɔ na ɔlɛka bite bebuo bani na badubuti babla akpala ammɔ. Na amii kani ndubute kamu ku antabi udu biala ku ntɛ bɔni na badubuti babla akpala ammɔ. Na ala amɛni ƒui na badubuti babla adila bɔsia lɛkpabi lɛlɔ teete-mi ku ekpidi lili buvele ku unwi bɔbla akpala ku kalɛ na bevele kusɛ kusɛ basiku-mi kudɔ. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ na liti mina bekyuli ekpidi lɛkyiɛ-ma.”
Kalɛ Na Ɔlɛka Badi Emeyi Buni
18Unwoti ɔnini,
“Na kɔbuli kudeedi kɔni baalɔ Abib iye Nisan na Hebri lɛdi kemmo limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka beti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔkɔdi ɔni na útasɔ kesii kadi badu babla akpala na babla kakpakɔ kammɔ sɛɛn. 19Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ uti ebuo ɔmmɔ ubugya ɔdi ɔkwaa kakpakɔ kammɔ kɔyakun ligyii lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui. Na ɔkwaa ɔban kɔyakun kɔni na baasia teeduo kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya-ka kemmo mmɔ ligyii lɛlɔ.
20“Na ɔdi ka babla limeyi bɔdi ablala amɛni na kɔbuli kɔmmɔ limeyi maatɛdi lɛnɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́bla likpidi lɛdi na tati tati kemmo iye likpidi lɛmmɔ líyu-nwu lɛ́tu ni, na liti lɛkyiɛ-nwu kalɛ na kakpakɔ kammɔ kedee.
21“Na ɔ́si kɔbuli kudeedi kɔmɛni limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka ukyuli biala use kalɔ ku Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi bɔdi utálɛ limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ. Na bodobodo ɔni kemmo na bátakya bɔnyii na ukyuli biala ɔdubɔdi. 22Na limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti ɔmantɛ akɔ uboku na bakpa aani anwu ɔlati ekpidi lili buvele ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ekpidi lili buvele. 23Na limeyi biala na emeyi amɛni bɔdi kemmo ni, ɔdi ka uboku ɔmantɛ bakɔ maatɛ ku baƒonu maatɛ na beti babla akpala ani ndubɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ. Na uboku ese lɛnɔ na beti-nwu babla ekpidi lili buvele akpala. Na ɔdi ka banu ka bebuo bamɛni ƒui ɔdi útasɔ na kesii kadi. 24Na ɔdi ka uboku edula ebi ɔlaaƒɔ akyami aani leevu ku nnɔ lɛsii ine na beti bakpa ku ɔmantɛ akɔ unwi ku koƒonu kunwi biala.
25“Nvo kemmo bɔkya emeyi bɔdi bɔdubuse kalɔ na kɔbuli maatɛdi kɔni baalɔ na Hebri kemmo banii Tisri iye Etanim limeyi leevu-lɛlɔndi lɛlɔ. Na badubɔdi limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛni laa emeyi maatɛ. Na bebuo bani kani na úboku ku atabi ku ɔlaaƒɔ ku nnɔ bumomo bɔmmɔ kani na ɔdi ka uboku na beti babla akpala ammɔ.”

english_text:
Various Laws for the Ruler and the People
1The Lord said:
The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened. 2Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
3Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me. 4On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals. 5With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
6The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals. 7With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain. 8The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
9When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate. 10Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
11At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
12If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
13Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me. 14Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change— 15the lamb, the flour, and the olive oil will be offered to me every morning for all time.
Laws about the Ruler's Land
16The Lord God said:
If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property. 17 But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
18The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him.
The Sacred Kitchens
19The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard 20and said, “These are the kitchens where the priests must boil the meat to be offered as sacrifices to make things right and as sacrifices for sin. They will also bake the grain for sacrifices in these kitchens. That way, these sacred offerings won't have to be carried through the outer courtyard, where someone could accidentally touch them and be harmed.”
21We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners. 22At each corner I saw a smaller courtyard, 20 meters long and 15 meters wide. 23Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires. 24The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_text:
Unwoti Úte Batɔnkune Ku Bekyuli Bammɔ Ɔda Bubo Lidu
1Unwoti ɔnini,
“Na emeyi aku ani na bekyuli badubuti babla bana kabla na uyolu unwi kemmo ƒui ni, ɔdi ka bakalɛ kakpakɔ geen ɔban kayakun kani nésie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Nsu na Lɛnwunameyi ku limeyi lideedi na kɔbuli kemmo ni, ɔdi ka bakɛmi-ka bewi. 2Na Israel ɔtɔnkune ɔdubɔsi kaduli kedeedi kemmo na ɔsia uduo ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na baasia teeduo ɔban ɔmɛni kemmo. Na ubenye kayakun na uwi ɔni na ɔkpane unye ɔɔbla akpala teevele mina kusɛ kusɛ ku unwi bɔbla ute bekyuli bammɔ. Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔyu ubi anumi kalɔ ɔtina kalɛ na ɔɔkya lili kalɔ teete-mi, na ɔmmɔ kama na ɔtɔlɔ mmɔ na kayakun kammɔ kasɔ kewi lɛni utédu useyi uwi.
3“Na Lɛnwunameyi biala lɛlɔ ku kɔbuli biala limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔdi ka Israel kadi bekyuli bebo ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kenye mmɔ na babakya lili kalɔ bete-mi na mmɔ. 4Na Lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ ni, ɔtɔnkune ɔdi ka uboku baƒonu bakɔdi ɛku ku koƒonu kɔgyani na beti babla akpala ani ndubɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ bete-mi. Na bebuo bammɔ batasɔ na kesii kadi. 5Na ɔdi uti antabi akyami aani leevu ubunku koƒonu kɔgyani kɔmmɔ. Na baƒonu bakɔdi bammɔ ama ni, ɔkana na uboku kalɛ na anwu ɔlati ɔɔyɔ́.
6“Ɔƒɛni si kɔbuli kɔwɔdi kɔ́sia ni, ɔdi ka ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ uboku baƒonu bakɔdi ɛku ku ɔmantɛ akɔ ku koƒonu kɔgyani na beti babla limeyi bɔdi akpala ammɔ. Na bebuo bammɔ batasɔ na kesii kadi. 7Na ɔmantɛ akɔ iye koƒonu kɔgyani ni, ɔdi ka uti antabi akyami leevu ɔsia ku lɛlɔ uboku-mi. Na baƒonu bakɔdi ama ni, ɔkana na uboku kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́. Na ɔdi ka uti nnɔ lɛsii ine ubunku antabi akyami leevu biala lɛlɔ.
8“Si ɔga úbo ubakpa-mi ni, ɔban kayakun kani na ɔ́sia úduo ni, mmɔ kani na ɔdubɔsia ɔlɛ. 9Nsu si mina kadi bekyuli bébo bábakpa-mi na limeyi bɔdi biala kemmo ni, ɔdi ka basia kayakun bamba batɔlɔ na ɔɔɔdi kani na básia béduo. Anwuɔsu si kayakun katɔdi na ásia éduo ni, ɔdi ka asia kadani alɛ. Na si kadani lɛnɔ na ásia éduo ni, ɔdi ka asia katɔdi alɛ. 10Na uwi ɔni kani na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui beeduo ni, uwi ɔmmɔ kani na bana ɔtɔnkune lɛnɔ uduo. Lɛni kani na ɔlɛka basiaku lɛlɔ balɛ uwi unwi.
11“Na emeyi bamba biala bɔdi kemmo ni, ɔdi ka antabi akyami leevu na beti bebunku ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔmmɔ. Na beti akyami leevu ammɔ kani bebunku koƒonu kɔgyani akpala lɛnɔ. Nsu bekyuli bani nébo bababla akpala ammɔ bakana na beti antabi akyami ani na baayɔ́ bebunku baƒonu bakɔdi bammɔ ɔdi biala anwu lɛlɔ. Na beti nnɔ lɛsii ine bebunku antabi akyami leevu biala lɛlɔ.
12“Na si kaƒɔ ƒaa etela na ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ úti úboku ɔnii ubabla unwi bɔbla akpala iye uvele-mi na lite-nwu kusɛ kusɛ ni, badubɔlɛmi kakpakɔ geen kaduli ɔban kayakun kani na ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ bete-nwu. Na ɔdubɔbla nwuna akpala aani kalɛ kani na ɔɔbla na Lɛnwunameyi biala lɛlɔ. Na si ɔ́tɔlɔ ni, na bakalɛ kayakun kammɔ.
13“Na ɔtanta biala ni, koƒonu kɔkɔdi kɔni na kútasɔ na ɔdi ka beti bakpa bete-mi na kaƒɔ kayɔ-mi. 14Na ɔdi ka beti ɔlaaƒɔ akɔkɔ leevu bebunku nnɔ ɔsii unwi. Na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bulavumana úti úsela uwi ƒui. 15Na koƒonu kɔkɔdi ku ɔlaaƒɔ ku nnɔ na bɛdubo buti butaakpa-mi uwi ƒui.”
Unwoti Úte Ɔda Bubo Na Batɔnkune Kalɔ Lɛlɔ
16Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini,
“Si Israel ɔtɔnkune ɔdi úti nwuna kalɔ kakɛ kadi úte ubidi ɔdi ni, kalɔ kammɔ kadubunwini ubidi kadi na kabla ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo kese. 17Nsu si ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ úti nwuna kalɔ kakɛ kadi úte nwuna kabla ɔblane ni, kadubunwini kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ kadi butédu uwi ɔni na baadi bɔnwuna bɔkɛ lɛkwa limeyi, na kalɔ kammɔ kadubɔsɔ kenwini kesie ɔlati ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ kudɔ. Ɔsika ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ubidi geen kani na mbo kuƒi ka uti ɔmii ɔni na béte-nwu unwini anwu ɔdi ƒui.
18“Ɔtɔnkune ɔdi utetile mina bekyuli bana kalɔ lɛlati bɔdi kuƒi na uƒie-ma kalɔ ɔƒɔ. Na kalɔ biala na ɔdubute ubidi ni, ɔti nwaa ka anwu ɔlati kadi na kadi ɔ́si kukuuku.”
Bátina-mi Akpala Kanwakɔ Kedee
19Ɔnana ɔni mɔɔtina-mi kakpakɔ ala mɛni ni, ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi úsienku kakpakɔ kaduli geen kemmo. Na búti bɔ́sia kaduli kammɔ kada kakɛ na bútédi búnye lɛtɔ lɛni na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte bakpane mmɔ kayakun. Mmɔ na ɔ́tina-mi lɛtɔ pii úbu na kakpakɔ kaduli kammɔ ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ 20na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Mɛni ndi kanwakɔ kesii kani na ɔdi ka bakpane bammɔ beƒulo lɛna lɛni na beeti taabla unwi bɔbla akpala ku ekpidi lili buvele akpala. Na mɛni kani na baagyi antabi ani na beeti taabla akpala mmɔ. Ɔsika útalɛka beti akpala amɛni balɛku mɛni batásia kaduli kedeedi kemmo kesii kani na ɔƒɛni kalɛ ukyuli ɔdubutuku-nya na ɔsiaku ɔgbankpi ɔdi.”
21Ɔmmɔ kama búnwini búsie kaduli kedeedi kemmo na bɔ́sia bɔvi lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui. 22Na ɔkɔkɔ biala na lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui ni, lɛ́nu kaduli blii bamba kadi kani bune ndi lɛgba liti ku leevu-maane na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba liti. 23Na béti atabi bátu kowodu klukwii kɔdi bámana kɔduli kɔmɛni ɔdi biala kɔmadɔ kɔmadɔ. Na bálɛ asi bámana awodu amɛni lɛlɔ kudɔ kudɔ. 24Amu na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Mmɔ na kakpakɔ kabla bebunkune beeƒulo lɛna lɛni na bekyuli bani nébo babakpa Katɔti béboku.”

english_text:
The Stream Flowing from the Temple
1 The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
2We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
3The man walked east, then took out his measuring stick and measured 500 meters downstream. He told me to wade through the stream there, and the water came up to my ankles. 4Then he measured another 500 meters downstream, and told me to wade through it there. The water came up to my knees. Another 500 meters downstream the water came up to my waist. 5Another 500 meters downstream, the stream had become a river that could be crossed only by swimming. 6The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.”
We walked to the riverbank, 7where I saw dozens of trees on each side. 8The man said:
This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water. 9Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea. 10From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea. 11But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
12 Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people.
The Borders of the Land
13-14The Lord God said to the people of Israel:
When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
15The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad, 16Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran. 17So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
18The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
19The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
20The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
21That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel. 22It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive 23a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Lɛ́nu Ketu Blii Kadi Ka Kaagbá Taasi Kakpakɔ Mmɔ
1Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi na búnwini búsie kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ. Na mmɔ na lɛ́nu ketu blii kadi ka kaagbá taasi kayakun kammɔ kalɔ. Kése kalɔ kási kakpakɔ kammɔ kada kakɛ na ɔ́gba ɔkɛ lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ na ɔ́gba ɔkɛ kaduli kammɔ kemmo úsela ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ.
2Bɔ́gyu bɔ́tɔlɔ kakpakɔ amadɔ mmɔ na bɔkɛ bútávi ɔban kayakun katɔdi kudɔ na bɔ́ka bɔ́mana bútédu ɔban kayakun kani na ɔƒɛ katukɔ. Na lɛ́nu ka ketu blii kammɔ kágba késela ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ɔ́si ɔban kayakun kani na kada kakɛ mmɔ kudɔ.
3Ɔnana ɔmmɔ úti úsie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na lɛ́nu ka údie nwuna ugyii lɛkɔkula na ɔ́kɔku lɛgba budie eti leevu ku liti ku leevu ɔ́yula kada kalɛ na ketu kammɔ kéti késela mmɔ. Na ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nkya ketu kammɔ lɛgba nteebo. Na ntu bɔmmɔ búbedu-mi anikpo. 4Ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kɔku lɛgba budie eti leevu ku liti ku leevu ɔ́yula na ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nkya lɛgba na ntu bɔmmɔ búbedu-mi kavobi. 5Ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kɔku lɛgba budie eti leevu ku liti ku leevu ɔ́yula na ketu kammɔ kasɔ kaladia lɛgba bɔkya ntu bɔkpi na ákpi. 6Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, se atu na enu lɛla lɛdi asiku ala ani na ánu lɛlɔ.”
Bɔ́sia búsie ketu kammɔ kɔtu. 7Na ntánu egyii pii ka enye ketu ɔvi ɔnanyɔ. 8Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ntu bɔmɛni bɔ́gba bɔkɛ ɔƒɛ kanukɔ mɛni búsela Yordan Ketu ɔkwalɛ kemmo na bɔdubo kenye buti butákya Ɛpugyie kemmo kesii kani na ɔdubo mma ntu bɔmmɔ bunwini bɔbla ntu bɔbuni mamaama bɔni mɔɔdia bɔni. 9Na kesi kesii na ntu bɔmɛni bɔ́gba bɔkɛ ni, ketu kemmo lɛna ku kɔbɛ lidu lidu badubo mmɔ bɔkya. Ɔsika ɔdubo ngba ku ntu bɔbuni bɔni mɔɔdia bɔni buti buboku Ɛpugyie kemmo. 10Na ɔ́si ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Engedi útédu Eneglaim ɔma bekyuli badubo kɔbɛ buteedie na mmɔ na bakula bana lɛsawu na ɛpu kɔtu mmɔ. Na kɔbɛ lidu pii kɔdubɔkya Ɛpugyie kemmo aani kalɛ na kɔkya Mediterenia Ɛpu kemmo. 11Nsu lɛba lɛni ndubɔkya ɛpu amadɔ mmɔ ani ni, mma bɔdubɔkya-ni kemmo kalɛ na bekyuli bakɛ-mu bedie. 12Adingyii pii adubɔkwɛ ketu kamɛni kɔtu na ataanwu ebi kɔbuli biala. Na evete ammɔ aaadubo bɔkwii bɔnu kudii, ɔsika adubo ntu butaakɛ uwi biala taasiku ketu kani mɔɔgbá taasi kakpakɔ kudɔ mmɔ na bekyuli badubuti evete ammɔ babwi bekyuli.”
Básia Kalɔ Kammɔ Lɛmii
13-14Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su Israel kadi bekyuli ɔnini,
