Ɔsika lɛ́nu ka lɛla lɛni na bɛɛbla ni, lítedu tɔ lítawɔlɔ na Katɔti anumi. 3Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, binyimo lɛla lɛni na bátina-mii na bínu lɛnɔ, na bɛda-ni kaduɛ na bina ekpidi eduo-mii na binwini kama bɛkya-nya. Nsu si bítagyinya ni, ndubo-mii kudɔ aani uyune kalɛ na biláti uwi ɔni kemmo na meti mada malɛ-mii lɛlɔ. 4Nsu bibo nkyuli ɛlɛɛ badi na Sardi mmɔ bani nétebile bana adala. Na ami ku-ma bɔdubɔda ala aƒualadi na bɔkɛ butaavi, ɔsika bámanku ka babla lɛni. 5Ukyuli ɔni madi ekpidi lɛlɔ ni, ɔdubɔda ala aƒualadi aani bana kalɛ. Na lɛɛɛdubo-ma anyi bɔda budie ngba ɔku kemmo. Na ndubudie-ma kenye na mina Ɔti ku Katɔti batu ƒui anumi ka badi ami badi.
6“Si bibo atu ni, na binu lɛla lɛni na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔsu baƒɔtaadine akpa ammɔ.”
Ɔku Ɔni Na Únweni Úte Ƒiladelƒia Baƒɔtaadine Lɛkpa
7Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Nweni te Ƒiladelƒia baƒɔtaadine lɛkpa ɔtu anii,
“Lɛni na anwu ɔni nse kedee na nwuna litemi lɛdi litemi geen ɔɔsu. Anwu nda Ɔga Dawid ɔyikun ɔni na si ɔ́lɛmi kayakun kadi ni, ɔdi ɔsɔ ulakana-ka bɔkalɛ. Na si ɔ́kalɛ-ka ni, ɔdi ulakana-ka bɔlɛmi. 8Ngyi kalɛ na bɛɛbla bina kabla na ngyi ka bibo ɔyikun blii ɔdi. Bɛ́siaku mina ala bɔtina kama na bɛ́di mina etemila lɛnɔ lɛlɔ ulu lɛlɔ. Lɛ́lɛmi kayakun kadi líte-mii na bina anumi na ukyuli biala ulakana-ka bɔkalɛ. 9Bɛnu! Ɔkɔ banyine bani násala bewi Satan ku nwuna badi kasalakɔ ngye na baalɔ-ma Yudaƒuɔ nsu baaadi Yudaƒuɔ ni, ndubɔya na balɛ akɔnkɔ na ƒula lɛgba akɔ. Na bana ƒui badubɔsu banii mɔɔyɔ́-ɔ. 10Na ka bɛ́di mina ɔda ɔni na líbo-mii lɛlɔ, na bínye kpakplaa na bɛ́siaku ala ani ƒui muukpóku-mii ɔsu ni, ndubɔda-mii lidie lɛbibo lɛni mebo kayawi ƒui lɛlɔ libakɔku bekyuli bani nlie kalɔ lɛlɔ lɛnu kemmo.
11“Ndubo uwi klukui kemmo. Anwuɔsu bɛda lɛla lɛni nse-mii kaduɛ kalɛ na ukyuli ɔdi uláƒɔ bina lɛyuƒɔla ulásiku-mii enu kemmo. 12Ndubo ukyuli ɔni madi lɛlɔ bɔbla aani lɛkpa na mina Katɔti kakpakɔ ɔni na lɛsɔ lilágyu mmɔ kudii. Ndubo mina Katɔti lɛnyi ku nwuna ɔma kedee ɔmmɔ lɛnyi bunweni bɔsia-nwu lɛlɔ. Na ɔdi Yerusalem ɔwɔdi ɔni mayu masi katɔ na Katɔti kudɔ. Na ndubo ami ɔlati lɛnyi lɛwɔdi lɛnɔ bunweni bɔsia-nwu lɛlɔ. 13Si bibo atu ni, na binu lɛla lɛni na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔsu baƒɔtaadine akpa ammɔ.”
Ɔku Ɔni Na Únweni Úte Laodikea Baƒɔtaadine Lɛkpa
14Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Nweni te Laodikea baƒɔtaadine ɔtu anii,
“Lɛni na anwu ɔni mɔɔyá na lɛla biala lɛɛsia lɛni ɔɔsu. Na ɔdi Katɔti kenye udiene geen ɔni mɔɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ, na anwu mɔɔdi Katɔti ala ani ƒui na údie lɛlɔ. 15Ngyi lɛla lɛni na bɛ́bla na ngyi ka bítaba na bítaƒɔ ogya lɛnɔ. Nsu nka mɔɔyɔ́ si bɛ́ƒuna linwi. 16Nsu ka buse kani na bise gugungu na bítaba iye bítaƒɔ ogya lɛnɔ ɔsu ni, ndubo-mii butuo bɔlɛku mina kenye kemmo! 17Bɛɛsu bɛnii, ‘Mbo ala na ɔdianku-mi, na mbo ala ani ƒui na mɔɔwia.’ Nsu bɛɛɛgyi bɛnii biisé lɛlɔ na bina lɛlɔ libo kɔnyana, na biiibo lɛla lɛdi, na anumi ábwɛ-mii, na bɛkɛ kasɔngya. 18Anwuɔsu mɔɔlɛ-mii kpakplaa nnii bibo na bibeye sika ugyiedi ɔni bábla kede kede na ogya kemmo na mina kudɔ na binwini balakɛne. Na bibeye adiƒuala ani na binyimi na bekyuli basɔ balanu bina kasɔngya ku kɔƒa. Na biye kuvo bɛkya anumi na bitaanu kaduɛ.
19“Bekyuli bani na mɔɔyɔ́ ni, ama na mɔɔdɔnku na mɔɔní-ma kɔtu. Anwuɔsu bɛsia lɛlɔ anu kpakplaa na binwini kama bɛkya bina ekpidi. 20Binu! Nnye kayakun muubó kɔnu. Na si ukyuli ɔdi únu-mi lɛdi na ɔ́lɛmi úte-mi ni, ndubuduo-nwu kudɔ na ami ku-nwu bɔsala bɔdi.
21“Anwu ɔni madi ekpidi lɛlɔ ni, ndubute-nwu kuƒi na ulie-mi kudɔ na lɛgaboku lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na lɛ́di lɛlɔ na nli mina Ɔti kudɔ na lɛgaboku lɛlɔ. 22Si bibo atu ni, na binu lɛla lɛni na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔsu baƒɔtaadine akpa ammɔ.”

english_text:
Worship in Heaven
1After this, I looked and saw a door that opened into heaven. Then the voice that had spoken to me at first and that sounded like a trumpet said, “Come up here! I will show you what must happen next.” 2 Right then the Spirit took control of me, and there in heaven I saw a throne and someone sitting on it. 3The one who was sitting there sparkled like precious stones of jasper and carnelian. A rainbow that looked like an emerald surrounded the throne.
4Twenty-four other thrones were in a circle around that throne. And on each of these thrones there was an elder dressed in white clothes and wearing a gold crown. 5 Flashes of lightning and roars of thunder came out from the throne in the center of the circle. Seven torches, which are the seven spirits of God, were burning in front of the throne. 6 Also in front of the throne was something that looked like a glass sea, clear as crystal.
Around the throne in the center were four living creatures covered front and back with eyes. 7The first creature was like a lion, the second one was like a bull, the third one had the face of a human, and the fourth was like a flying eagle. 8 Each of the four living creatures had six wings, and their bodies were covered with eyes. Day and night they never stopped singing,
“Holy, holy, holy is the Lord,
the all-powerful God,
who was and is
and is coming!”
9The living creatures kept praising, honoring, and thanking the one who sits on the throne and who lives forever and ever. 10At the same time the 24 elders knelt down before the one sitting on the throne. And as they worshiped the one who lives forever, they placed their crowns in front of the throne and said,
11 “Our Lord and God,
you are worthy
to receive glory,
honor, and power.
You created all things,
and by your decision they are
and were created.”
translation_text:
Kalɛ Na Beemwi Katɔti Na Nwuna Lɛga Kadikɔ
1Ɔmɛni kama ni, Katɔti údie kɔyu kemmo ala adi ɔ́tina-mi. Na lɛ́nu kayakun kadi ka bálɛmi-ka na katɔ.
Amu na lɛdi lɛni na lɛ́ka bunu aani kakpɛɛ ni, línu ka lɛsɔ lɛɛtɛmiku-mi lɛnini, “Bo katɔ kakɛ mɛni na lɛtina-a lɛla lɛni ndubo bɔlɛ na ɔmɛni kama.” 2Kɔnakunwi ni, Kɔyu kɔmmɔ kúti-mi kɔ́kɔliku katɔ. Ka mɔɔnu ni, lɛgaboku lɛdi lise na Katɔti ulie liboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. 3Na uukeye kede kede! Na bukeye bɔmmɔ buse aani aseebi egyiedi ku aƒualadi ani náƒɔ kuye. Na bukeye bonwu bɔdi bɔ́ka bɔ́mana lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ ƒui aani evete awɔdi bukeye. 4Na agaboku aavlanyɔ-ene áka ámana lɛgaboku lɛmɛni. Na benengu aavlanyɔ-ine lɛnɔ belie-nya lɛlɔ. Na bebi adiƒuala lɛlɔ, na sika ugyiedi kɔgabwa kubi-ma eli. 5Na ogya ɔɔbwɛ ku bukeye geen taasi lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ kudɔ! Na muunú adi adi ku ɔnantu budu kɔku na mmɔ. Na lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ anumi ni, lɛsogya maatɛ lɛɛda. Na ani ndi Katɔti Kɔyu kɔni mbo ɔyikun maatɛ ɔni nnye Katɔti lɛgaboku anumi. 6Na kesii kani na lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɛ anumi ni, ɔdi kalɔ kani nwi aani ɛpu na use kede kede aani asogya.
Na lɛgaboku lɛmɛni amadɔ ni, ngba batu ine badi udu benye lɛƒɛnyi lɛna ƒui. Na anumi áka ámana-ma lɛlɔ lɛtɔtɔ ku kama ƒui. 7Ngba ɔtu udeedi ɔ́lɛ gyata. Na unyɔdi ɔ́lɛ akɔ. Na ɔtɛdi ɔ́lɛ ukyuli. Na unedi ɔ́lɛ kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔni muuveyi. 8Na ngba batu ine bamɛni ƒui bebo avwi aku aku, na anumi akya avwi amɛni kemmo ku kama. Usien ku ɔƒɛ ni, baláda bɔsu taaya banini,
“Kedee, kedee, kedee
ndi Blɔti ɔni mbo ɔyikun ƒui,
ɔni nélie, na uli, na ɔdubo bulie.”
9Ngba batu bammɔ beeti bumwi ku ɔbu ku linugya teete anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na uli ngba úsela ƒui. Na uwi biala na baabla lɛni ni, 10benengu aavlanyɔ-ine bammɔ beebimi bana kɔgabwa taava-nwu anumi, na baayu teebi kalɔ. Na beemwi anwu ɔni nli ngba úsela ƒui, na baasu banini,
11“Blɔti ku bula Katɔti!
Awɔ námanku éte bumwi ku ɔbu ku ɔyikun.
Ɔsika awɔ nédie ala ani ƒui,
na áya na ana ƒui eli ngba
na ƒula lɛƒɔyɔ kenye.”

english_text:
The Scroll and the Lamb
1 In the right hand of the one sitting on the throne I saw a scroll that had writing on the inside and on the outside. And it was sealed in seven places. 2I saw a mighty angel ask with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?” 3No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look inside it.
4I cried hard because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look inside it. 5 Then one of the elders said to me, “Stop crying and look! The one who is called both the ‘Lion from the Tribe of Judah’ and ‘King David's Great Descendant’ has won the victory. He will open the scroll and its seven seals.”
6 Then I looked and saw a Lamb standing in the center of the throne surrounded by the four living creatures and the elders. The Lamb looked as if it had once been killed. It had seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God, sent out to all the earth.
7The Lamb went over and took the scroll from the right hand of the one who sat on the throne. 8 After he had taken it, the four living creatures and the 24 elders knelt down before him. Each of them had a harp and a gold bowl full of incense, which are the prayers of God's people. 9 Then they sang a new song,
“You are worthy
to receive the scroll
and open its seals,
because you were killed.
And with your own blood
you bought for God
people from every tribe,
language, nation, and race.
10 You let them become kings
and serve God as priests,
and they will rule on earth.”
11 As I looked, I heard the voices of a large number of angels around the throne and the voices of the living creatures and of the elders. There were millions and millions of them, 12and they were saying in a loud voice,
“The Lamb who was killed
is worthy to receive power,
riches, wisdom, strength,
honor, glory, and praise.”
13Then I heard all beings in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and in the sea offer praise. Together, all of them were saying,
“Praise, honor, glory,
and strength
forever and ever
to the one who sits
on the throne
and to the Lamb!”
14The four living creatures said “Amen,” while the elders knelt down and worshiped.
translation_text:
Koƒonu Ubi Ɔmmɔ Ɔ́ƒɔ Kakunkɛ Kani Na Bényimi Mmɔ
1Amu na lɛ́nu ka anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔda kakunkɛ kadi na nwuna kɔdianu, na bénweni ala ani ndubo abalɛ básia-ka anumi ku kama. Na báƒɛ-ka, na béti kɔma bábala-nwu kenye ekpo maatɛ kalɛ na ukyuli keeke ulakana bubimi. 2Mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔyikune ɔdi ɔni násu ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Ɔma námanku ka ɔmami kɔma kɔmɛni na ɔƒɛnimi kakunkɛ kammɔ?” 3Nsu ukyuli ɔdi uuubo katɔ iye kalɔ lɛlɔ iye kekpine muedi ɔni makana kakunkɛ kamɛni bɔƒɛnimi na wanu ɔku ɔmmɔ kemmo.
4Mmɔ ni, líwulo geen ɔsika bátakana ukyuli ɔdi bɔkɛ na ɔkana ɔku ɔmɛni bɔƒɛnimi bɔka. 5Amu na benengu bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Sɔ tewulo. Nu! Yesu ɔni baalɔ banii Gyata ɔni nási Yuda kaba kemmo na ɔdi Dawid Kugyii Ugyiitu ni, ɔ́di lɛlɔ. Anwu námanku ka ɔƒɛnimi kɔma kɔni na béti bábala ekpo maatɛ ammɔ.”
6Ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛ́nu ka Katɔti Koƒonu Ubi ɔdi unye agaboku ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na ngba batu ine bammɔ ku benengu aavlanyɔ-ine bammɔ báka bámana-nwu. Na ɔɔtina aani si bɔkpa na béti-nwu bákpa. Ese maatɛ alɛ Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ lili, na ubo anumi maatɛ. Na alakpa maatɛ amɛni adi Katɔti Kɔyu kɔni mbo ɔyikun maatɛ kɔni na Katɔti ɔ́tala ɔ́kya kayawi ƒui. 7Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ úsie na útáƒɔ kakunkɛ kammɔ ɔ́siku anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ kɔnu kemmo. 8Na uwi ɔni na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmɛni ɔɔƒɔ́ kakunkɛ kamɛni ni, ngba batu ine bammɔ ku benengu aavlanyɔ-ine bammɔ báyu bébi kalɔ na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ anumi. Ɔdi biala ɔda agyala ani béti kɔbuli bábla na baagyá taatu lɛnu. Na ɔdi biala ɔda sika ugyiedi kɔlaku kɔni néyi ku oloƒui. Na oloƒui ɔmɛni unye ute Katɔti bekyuli katɔ bɔkpali. 9Bédie ɔnu ɔwɔdi ɔdi banini,
“Awɔ námanku ka aƒɔ
kakunkɛ kammɔ
na amami kɔma kɔmmɔ.
Ɔsika awɔ na bádu.
Na ɔkɛnku ƒula ubugya
akpala ɔsu ni,
áƒɔ bekyuli lili kayu,
na ásɔku-ma éte Katɔti.
Awɔ náƒɔ-ma ásiku
kadi ƒui bekyuli ku
adi lidu biala batɛmine
ku bekyuli lidu ƒui akɔ
na kalɔ biala lɛlɔ.
10Awɔ nábla-ma bénwini baga
ku bakpane bani
mɔɔkpanku bekyuli
teeboku bula Katɔti.
Na badubɔdi lɛga na kalɔ lɛlɔ.”
11Ka lɛ́sɔ lɛ́nu ni, lɛ́nu katɔ batu mpim ɛlɛ ɛlɛ ku mpim leevu akpa leevu alɛ alɛ ka bénye bámana lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ ku ngba batu ine ku benengu bammɔ. 12Na katɔ batu bamɛni bédie ɔnu ku lɛdi momoomo banini,
“Awɔ ndi Koƒonu Ubi
ɔni na béti bákpa.
Na ámanku éte ɔyikun ku lɛlakɛ
ku lɛnunda ku ɔlɔkplu
ku ɔbu ku bumwi ku linugya.”
13Na línu ka ala ani ƒui na Katɔti údie na katɔ ku kalɔ ku kekpine ku ɛpu ku kayawi beedie ɔnu banini,
“Linugya ku ɔbu ku bumwi
ku ɔyikun na beete
anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛlɔ
ku Koƒonu Ubi
ka ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui.”
14Amu na ngba batu ine bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ɔsia lɛni.” Na benengu bammɔ báyu bébi kalɔ na beemwi-nwu.

english_text:
Opening the Seven Seals
1At the same time I saw the Lamb open the first of the seven seals, I heard one of the four living creatures shout with a voice like thunder. It said, “Come out!” 2 Then I saw a white horse. Its rider carried a bow and was given a crown. He had already won some victories, and he went out to win more.
3When the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come out!” 4 Then another horse came out. It was fiery red. And its rider was given the power to take away all peace from the earth, so people would slaughter one another. He was also given a big sword.
5 When the Lamb opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come out!” Then I saw a black horse, and its rider had a balance scale in one hand. 6I heard what sounded like a voice from somewhere among the four living creatures. It said, “A liter of wheat will cost you a whole day's wages! Three liters of barley will cost you a day's wages too. But don't ruin the olive oil or the wine.”
7When the Lamb opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say, “Come out!” 8 Then I saw a pale green horse. Its rider was named Death, and Death's Kingdom followed close behind. They were given power over one fourth of the earth, and they could kill its people with swords, famines, diseases, and wild animals.
9When the Lamb opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of everyone who had been killed for speaking God's message and telling about their faith. 10They shouted, “Master, you are holy and faithful! How long will it be before you judge and punish the people of this earth who killed us?”
11 Then each of those who had been killed was given a white robe and told to rest for a little while. They had to wait until the complete number of the Lord's other servants and followers would be killed.
12 When I saw the Lamb open the sixth seal, I looked and saw a great earthquake. The sun turned as dark as sackcloth, and the moon became red as blood. 13 The stars in the sky fell to earth, just like figs shaken loose by a windstorm. 14 Then the sky was rolled up like a scroll, and all mountains and islands were moved from their places.
15 The kings of the earth, its famous people, and its military leaders hid in caves or behind rocks on the mountains. They hid there together with the rich and the powerful and with all the slaves and free people. 16 Then they shouted to the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us! Hide us from the one who sits on the throne and from the anger of the Lamb. 17 That terrible day has come! God and the Lamb will show their anger, and who can face it?”
translation_text:
Koƒonu Ubi Ɔmmɔ Ɔ́ƒɛnimi Kɔma Ekpo Ammɔ
1Amu na lɛ́nu ka Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma kɔni nda kakunkɛ kani mɔɔtina ala ani ndubo abalɛ mmɔ ekpo maatɛ ammɔ akɔ unwi. Na línu ka ngba batu bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔ́su ku lɛdi momoomo lɛni náku aani ɔnantu budu ɔnini, “Bo!” 2Na lɛ́nu ɔpɔnkɔ ɔƒualadi ɔdi ka unye. Ukyuli ɔni nlie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́da kataminta na béti kagabwa kadi béte-nwu. Ukyuli ɔmɛni ulie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ aani ukpone lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔni nésela utádi lɛlɔ.
3Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo linyɔdi na línu ka ngba batu bammɔ akɔ unyɔdi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bo!” 4Mmɔ na ɔpɔnkɔ ɔbambadi ɔni négyie aani ogya kalɛ ɔ́da ɔ́lɛ. Na Katɔti úti ɔyikun úte ukyuli ɔni nlie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmɛni lɛlɔ ɔnii uti kekpo uboku kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui kalɛ na bekyuli badu lɛlɔ. Na úte-nwu kewii bonwu kadi.
5Ɔmɛni kama ni, Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo lɛtɛdi. Mmɔ ni, línu ka ngba batu bammɔ akɔ ɔtɛdi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bo!” Na ka mɔɔnu ni, lɛ́nu ɔpɔnkɔ totonto ɔdi ka unye. Na ukyuli ɔni nlie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔda kakpagyuɛ kani na baakɔ́ku ala unu taanu. 6Línu ka kɔku kɔdi kɔ́si ngba batu ine bammɔ kudɔ aani ukyuli butemi, na lɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛ́su lɛnini, “Ya na kamu kalaku kenwi kuye kɔkɔ kutédu limeyi lɛyuƒɔla, na antabi kɔlaku ɛtɛ kuye lɛnɔ kɔkɔ kutédu limeyi lɛyuƒɔla. Nsu tavumana nnɔ iye ntɛ bɔmmɔ kuye!”
7Amu na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo linedi. Na línu ka ngba batu bammɔ akɔ unedi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bo!” 8Na mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu ka ɔpɔnkɔ ƒuƒuu ɔdi unye aani ɔlɛne. Na básia ukyuli ɔni nlie-nwu lɛlɔ lɛnyi banii Kukpi. Na ukyuli bamba ɔkpɛ-nwu kama ɔni baalɔ Kekpine. Béte-ma ɔyikun ka badu kalɔ lɛkpa linedi bekyuli ƒui. Na kekpo ku kɔka ku ɔlɛ ku beƒiebuo ndubɔdu-ma.
9Amu na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami likpo lɛlɔndi. Na lɛ́nu ayu adi na katɔ ka enye lɛbi lɛni lɛlɔ na baakpá mmɔ kalɔ. Badi bekyuli bani ƒui na bádu ayu ka básu Katɔti litemi buni ɔsu. Ama ndi bani nédie ala ammɔ kenye na ulu lɛlɔ. 10Ayu amɛni áva ku lɛdi momoomo anini, “Blɔti, ala ƒui lɛlɔ ɔdine, awɔ nse kedee na ƒula etemila lɛnɔ adi litemi geen. Uwi ɛlɛ sɔɔn na adubunye etédu asa na bekyuli bani nádu-bu na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ ni, atɛku-ma litemi na ani-ma kɔtu?” 11Mmɔ na úte bekyuli bamɛni ɔdi biala awu ɔƒualadi, na ɔ́su-ma ɔnii bakɛ kayi betédu uwi ɔni na kayawi bekyuli bádu bana kabla bablane bakpana bammɔ aani kalɛ na bádu ama lɛnɔ. Ɔsika bana bumomo bútedu bútawɔlɔ tɔ.
12Ɔmɛni kama ni, lɛ́nu ka Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo lɛkundi. Na kayawi kemodi kákunku kpakplaa, na ɔƒɛ ɔ́da bukeye ɔ́ya, na ala ƒui ábla suu. Na kɔbuli kumodi kɔmmɔ kɔ́vumana kɔ́bla aani ubugya. 13Ayabi ánu ébo kalɔ aani kalɛ na kugyii ebi aanú na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa kemmo. 14Kayaa káyii aani kalɛ na baaƒɛ ebuo ɔku. Na bágyu abi ku ntuntɛ kalɔ ƒui na ana kenyekɔ.
15Amu na kalɔ lɛlɔ baga ƒui ku bekyuli bani mbo kenyekɔ ku bekpone batɔnkune ku balakɛne ku bayikune ku bekyuli bamba lidu ƒui bani mɔɔbla bekyuli bamba kabla ku bani mɔɔbla ama alati kabla ƒui bábala lɛlɔ na libu ku atakpɛ kalɔ na abi lɛlɔ. 16Bákpali abi ku atakpɛ ammɔ banii, “Bibo na bibebi-bu lɛlɔ na bɛbala-bu kalɛ na anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ulanu-bu, na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ uláni-bu kɔtu! 17Ɔsika Katɔti ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ kɔnyi kpakplaa limeyi lídu! Na ɔma makana kɔnyi kɔmmɔ kenye bunye?”

english_text:
The 144,000 Are Marked for God
1-2 After this I saw four angels. Each one was standing on one of the earth's four corners. The angels held back the four winds, so that no wind would blow on the earth or on the sea or on any tree. These angels had also been given the power to harm the earth and the sea. Then I saw another angel come up from where the sun rises in the east, and he was ready to put the mark of the living God on people. He shouted to the four angels, 3 “Don't harm the earth or the sea or any tree! Wait until I have marked the foreheads of the servants of our God.”
4Then I heard how many people had been marked on the forehead. There were 144,000, and they came from every tribe of Israel:
512,000 from Judah,
12,000 from Reuben,
12,000 from Gad,
612,000 from Asher,
12,000 from Naphtali,
12,000 from Manasseh,
712,000 from Simeon,
12,000 from Levi,
12,000 from Issachar,
812,000 from Zebulun,
12,000 from Joseph, and
12,000 from Benjamin.
People from Every Nation
9 After this, I saw a large crowd with more people than could be counted. They were from every race, tribe, nation, and language, and they stood before the throne and before the Lamb. They wore white robes and held palm branches in their hands, 10as they shouted,
“Our God, who sits
upon the throne,
has the power
to save his people,
and so does the Lamb.”
11The angels who stood around the throne knelt in front of it with their faces to the ground. The elders and the four living creatures knelt there with them. Then they all worshiped God 12and said,
“Amen! Praise, glory, wisdom,
thanks, honor, power,
and strength belong to our God
forever and ever! Amen!”
13One of the elders asked me, “Do you know who these people are that are dressed in white robes? Do you know where they come from?”
14 “Sir,” I answered, “you must know.”
Then he told me:
“These are the ones
who have gone through
the great suffering.
They have washed their robes
in the blood of the Lamb
and have made them white.
15And so they stand
before the throne of God
and worship him in his temple
day and night.
The one who sits on the throne
will spread his tent
over them.
16 They will never hunger
or thirst again,
and they won't be troubled
by the sun
or any scorching heat.
17 “The Lamb in the center
of the throne
will be their shepherd.
He will lead them to streams
of life-giving water,
and God will wipe all tears
from their eyes.”
translation_text:
Ɔ́nu Israel Bekyuli Mpim Eti Anyɔ Ku Aavlene-ine
1Na ɔmɛni kama ni, lɛ́nu Katɔti batu ine badi ka benye kayawi ekpo ene ammɔ. Na bada ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni muukpó taasi ekpo ene ammɔ ƒui kenye, kalɛ na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ biala ulékpo na kalɔ lɛlɔ iye ɛpu anumi iye na egyii akɔ.
2Katɔti úte-ma ɔyikun ka babla kalɔ ku ɛpu kalala na beti bani bekyuli kɔtu. Nsu lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔdi ka ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔdubo na ɔda lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔni nli ngba ɔdubuti use bekyuli likpo. Na ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpali batu ine ku lɛdi momoomo, 3na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bitabla kalɔ iye ɛpu iye egyii adi kalala weti wetédu lebo lɛni na búse Katɔti kabla bablane likpo ku likposela lɛmɛni na bana atɛntɛ.” 4Na básu-mi ka bekyuli bani na béti Katɔti likposela lɛmmɔ bése-ma likpo na bana atɛntɛ bumomo bɔdubɔbla aani bekyuli mpim eti anyɔ ku aavlene-ine. Na bekyuli bammɔ bási Israel kaba leevu-inyɔ kammɔ kemmo.
5Nkyuli mpim leevu inyɔ bási Yuda kaba kemmo.
Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Ruben kaba kemmo.
Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Gad kaba kemmo.
6Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Aser kaba kemmo.
Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Naƒtali kaba kemmo.
Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Manase kaba kemmo.
7Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Simeon kaba kemmo.
Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Lewi kaba kemmo.
Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Isakar kaba kemmo.
8Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Sebulon kaba kemmo.
Na mpim leevu-inyɔ bási Yoseƒ kaba kemmo.
Na nkyuli mpim leevu-inyɔ na bése likpo na Benyamin kaba lɛnɔ kemmo.
Bekyuli Lisu Bonwu Lɛni Nkya Katɔ
9Na ɔmɛni kama ni, lɛ́nu ka bekyuli pii badi benye mmɔ bani na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana bɔka! Bekyuli bamɛni bási kalɔ biala kemmo ku kadi biala akɔ ku bekyuli lidu lidu ƒui akɔ ku adi lidu biala kemmo ka bénye lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ anumi, na bákya lɛwu lɛƒualadi na bada like. 10Na básu ku lɛdi momoomo banini,
“Ngba bɔƒɔ bɔɔsí bula Katɔti
ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛlɔ
ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ kudɔ.”
11Batu ƒui benye báka bámana lɛgaboku ku benengu ku ngba batu ine bani nnye mmɔ. 12Na báyu bébi kalɔ na lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ anumi na beemwi Katɔti, na baasu banini,
“Ɔsia lɛni!
Bula Katɔti uukeye,
na ubo lɛnunda ku ɔbu
ku kenyekɔ ku ɔyikun,
na ɔ́manku bumwi ku linugya
ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui!
Ɔsia lɛni.”
13Amu na benengu bammɔ akɔ unwi úye-mi ɔnini, “Ɔma bene ndi bekyuli bani nkya lɛwu lɛƒualadi mɛni lɛni? Na wɛ na bási?”
14Amu na lɛ́su-nwu nnini, “Ati, lɛɛɛgyi-ma. Awɔ ngyi bekyuli bamɛni.”
Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Bekyuli bamɛni ndi bani nénye lɛbibo bonwu lɛmmɔ kenye, na bálɛ-nwu kemmo. Bábla sɛɛn na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ubugya ɔsu, aani kalɛ na baaƒɔ lɛwu na lɛɛƒuala.
15“Anwuɔsu na benye Katɔti
lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ anumi
na baabla-nwu kabla usien
ku ɔƒɛ na nwuna kakpakɔ.
Ka anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔkya-ma akɔ ɔsu ni,
ɔdubo-ma bɔgyumana.
16Na kɔka iye utukwɛ
ɔsɔ uladu-ma kudii.
Na ɔƒɛ iye liwulu lɛdi
lɛsɔ lileƒi-ma.
17Ɔsika Koƒonu Ubi ɔni nlie
lɛgaboku lɛlɔ na mmɔ ni,
anwu ndubɔda-ma
aani baƒonu ɔdane buni.
Na ɔdubo-ma bɔtɔnku
busienku abiɔ ani kemmo
na ntu bɔni muute ngba buwi uwi biala.
Na Katɔti lɛnɔ ɔdubo-ma
imii buni.”

english_text:
The Seventh Seal Is Opened
1When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. 2I noticed that the seven angels who stood before God were each given a trumpet.
3 Another angel, who had a gold container for incense, came and stood at the altar. This one was given a lot of incense to offer with the prayers of God's people on the gold altar in front of the throne. 4Then the smoke of the incense, together with the prayers of God's people, went up to God from the hand of the angel.
5 After this, the angel filled the incense container with fire from the altar and threw it on the earth. Thunder roared, lightning flashed, and the earth shook.
The Trumpets
6 The seven angels now got ready to blow their trumpets.
7 When the first angel blew his trumpet, hail and fire mixed with blood were thrown down on the earth. A third of the earth, a third of the trees, and a third of all green plants were burned.
8When the second angel blew his trumpet, something like a great fiery mountain was thrown into the sea. A third of the sea turned to blood, 9a third of the living creatures in the sea died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
10 When the third angel blew his trumpet, a great star fell from heaven. It was burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on a third of the springs of water. 11 The name of the star was Bitter, and a third of the water turned bitter. Many people died because the water was so bitter.
12 When the fourth angel blew his trumpet, a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck. They each lost a third of their light. So during a third of the day there was no light, and a third of the night was also without light.
13Then I looked and saw a lone eagle flying across the sky. It was shouting, “Trouble, trouble, trouble to everyone who lives on earth! The other three angels are now going to blow their trumpets.”
translation_text:
Koƒonu Ubi Ɔmmɔ Ɔ́mami Kɔma Likpo Maatɛdi
1Lebo lɛni na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo maatɛdi ni, katɔ mmɔ ƒui kábla diin, na ɔdubɔbla aani ɔdɔ bubo kakɛ kemmo.
2Amu na lɛ́nu Katɔti batu maatɛ bani muunye Katɔti anumi, na úte-ma kɔkpɛɛ maatɛ.
3Na Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔ́da ɔ́lɛ ɔni nda sika ugyiedi libwi lɛni kemmo na baakyula oloƒui, na úbenye lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ. Béte-nwu oloƒui pii kalɛ na ɔkyula-nwu na sika ugyiedi lɛkpabi lɛni nnye lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ anumi lɛlɔ. Na oloƒui ɔmmɔ ku Katɔti bekyuli ƒui katɔ bɔkpali bɔbla akpala enwi. 4Oloƒui ɔni mɔɔkywí mmɔ uyɔ ku Katɔti bekyuli bammɔ katɔ bɔkpali ƒui bɔ́kɔ búsie Katɔti kudɔ ɔ́si Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ enu kemmo. 5Ɔmɛni kama ni, Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ úti oloƒui libui lɛmmɔ na úyile-ni ku ogya ɔni na údie na lɛbi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ, na úbo éwi kalɔ lɛlɔ na kayawi. Mmɔ ni, línu ɔnantu budu kudu ku kɔku bonwu, na kayaa kaabwɛ ogya, na kalɔ kaakunku.
Katɔti Batu Bɔmmɔ Bávwi Bana Kɔkpɛɛ
6Amu na batu maatɛ bani nda kɔkpɛɛ maatɛ kɔmmɔ báklibi lɛlɔ kalɛ na bavwi bana kɔkpɛɛ.
7Katɔti ɔtu udeedi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Mmɔ kani ni, etubankɛ ku ogya ɔni násalaku ubugya ɔ́bwɛ úbewi kalɔ lɛlɔ na kalɔ kemodi ku egyii lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛ́kywi. Na livo ƒui lɛ́kywi.
8Ɔmɛni kama ni, Katɔti ɔtu unyɔdi lɛnɔ ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Amu na úbo lɛla lɛni nálɛ aani kɔbi kɔni mɔɔda ku ogya útákya ɛpu kemmo. Na ɛpu lɛkpa lɛtɛdi ƒui línwini ubugya. 9Na ketu kemmo bebweyi lɛkpa lɛtɛdi ƒui békpi. Na lɛkɔlɔ linengudi ƒui lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛ́kywi.
10Katɔti ɔtu ɔtɛdi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Amu na lɛyabi bonwu lɛdi lɛni mɔɔda aani ogya lɛ́lɛ líbo lɛ́si kayaa na lɛ́yu ntukpa ƒui lɛkpa lɛtɛdi ku abiɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. 11Lɛyabi lɛmmɔ lɛnyi ndi Ɔdu Kati Kati. Ntu lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛ́yu ɔdu, na bekyuli pii badi békpi na ntu bɔmmɔ ɔdu ɔsu.
12Amu na ɔtu unedi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Na lɛla lɛdi lɛ́yila ɔƒɛ ku kɔbuli ku ayabi lɛkpa lɛtɛdi bukeye. Anwuɔsu usien ku ɔƒɛ limeyi lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛ́sɔ lítanu bukeye.
13Amu ka nnye mɔɔnu budie bɔtina bɔmɛni ni, lɛ́nu kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔdi ɔni néveyi ɔkɛ kayaa kakaaka, na ɔ́su ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Si uwi ɔni na Katɔti batu ɛtɛ bani nébu mɛni bávwi bana kɔkpɛɛ ni, muute bekyuli bani ƒui nli kalɔ lɛlɔ bɔbuɛ, bɔbuɛ, bɔbuɛ kɔtɛ!”

english_text:
1When the fifth angel blew his trumpet, I saw a star fall from the sky to earth. It was given the key to the tunnel that leads down to the deep pit. 2 As it opened the tunnel, smoke poured out like the smoke of a great furnace. The sun and the air turned dark because of the smoke. 3 Locusts came out of the smoke and covered the earth. They were given the same power that scorpions have.
4 The locusts were told not to harm the grass on the earth or any plant or any tree. They were to punish only those people who did not have God's mark on their foreheads. 5The locusts were allowed to make them suffer for five months, but not to kill them. The suffering they caused was like the sting of a scorpion. 6 In those days people will want to die, but they will not be able to. They will hope for death, but it will escape from them.
7 These locusts looked like horses ready for battle. On their heads they wore something like gold crowns, and they had human faces. 8 Their hair was like a woman's long hair, and their teeth were like those of a lion. 9 On their chests they wore armor made of iron. Their wings roared like an army of horse-drawn chariots rushing into battle. 10Their tails were like a scorpion's tail with a stinger that had the power to hurt someone for five months. 11Their king was the angel in charge of the deep pit. In Hebrew his name was Abaddon, and in Greek it was Apollyon.
12The first horrible thing has now happened! But wait. Two more horrible things will happen soon.
13 Then the sixth angel blew his trumpet. I heard a voice speak from the four corners of the gold altar that stands in the presence of God. 14The voice spoke to this angel and said, “Release the four angels who are tied up beside the great Euphrates River.” 15The four angels had been prepared for this very hour and day and month and year. Now they were set free to kill a third of all people.
16By listening, I could tell there were more than 200,000,000 war horses. 17 In my vision their riders wore fiery-red, dark-blue, and yellow armor on their chests. The heads of the horses looked like lions, with fire and smoke and sulfur coming out of their mouths. 18One third of all people were killed by the three terrible troubles caused by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur. 19The horses had powerful mouths, and their tails were like poisonous snakes that bite and hurt.
20 The people who lived through these terrible troubles did not turn away from the idols they had made, and they did not stop worshiping demons. They kept on worshiping idols that were made of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood. Not one of these idols could see, hear, or walk. 21No one stopped murdering or practicing witchcraft or being immoral or stealing.
translation_text:
1Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔlɔndi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Na lɛ́nu ɔtu ɔdi ka ɔ́nu ɔ́si katɔ aani lɛyabi úbayu kalɔ. Na Katɔti úte-nwu ɔyikun ɔni mɔɔbala kasuudikɔ ubu bonwu ɔmmɔ kenye. 2Ɔtu ɔmɛni ɔ́lɛmi ubu bonwu ɔmɛni na uyɔ ɔ́lɛ ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo aani uyɔ ɔni mɔɔlɛ́ taasi lɛgyavonku bonwu lɛdi kemmo. Na ɔƒɛ bukeye ku kayaa kábla suu na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔsu.
3Baalɔlɔ bani muubile edula badi báyu bási uyɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo bébo kalɔ, na Katɔti úte-ma ɔyikun aani ɔni na batamlukpa bebo kalɛ. 4Na ɔ́su baalɔlɔ bammɔ ka batabla livete iye livo iye kugyii kɔdi kalala ntu bekyuli bani na Katɔti útese likpo na bana atɛntɛ. 5Útete baalɔlɔ bammɔ ulu ka baya na ukyuli ɔdi ukpi, nsu babla-ma kalala na bebo abi na benu ɔlɛ abuli alɔ. Na ɔlɛ bunu ɔni nkya lɛbibo lɛmɛni kemmo ni, buse aani kalɛ na katamlukpa kaata. 6Ɔƒɛni na abuli alɔ ammɔ kemmo ni, badubo kukpi bɔwia, nsu balákɛ-ku. Badubɔwia banii beekpi, nsu kukpi kɔdubo-ma bukeli.
7Baalɔlɔ bammɔ bɔnu buse aani bapɔnkɔ bani nnye kagyumana bete kekpo. Na kɔbwa kɔni nálɛ sika ugyiedi kɔgabwa kubi-ma eli. Na bana anumi álɛ bekyuli anumi. 8Bana lili linwini lise gyɔlɔɔ, na bana kenye kemmo anyi ese aani gyata anyi. 9Na béti ala ani nse aani abuala lɛwu lɛni mɔɔgyumana kayi bákya. Na kɔku kɔni na bana avwi aabla ni, aaku aani kɛɛkɛ pii ɔni bapɔnkɔ báni béselaku kekpokɔ. 10Baalɔlɔ bamɛni bebo lɛka ku akpɛlɛ aani batamlukpa kalɛ na bana lɛka lɛmɛni kemmo, na bebo ɔyikun ɔni na badubo buti bɔbla bekyuli kalala abuli alɔ. 11Bebo ɔga ɔni ndi ɔtu ɔni mɔɔnu kasuudikɔ ubu bonwu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔtu ɔmmɔ lɛnyi na Hebri lɛdi kemmo ndi Abadon. Na Griki lɛdi kemmo ni, nwuna lɛnyi ndi Apolion ɔni kalɔ ndi Ɔkyulane.
12Bɔbuɛ lɛla lideedi lɛ́vi. Na alakpa anyɔ ani ndanku bɔbwɛ inyɔ bɔni nébu ni, adubo bɔlɛ.
13Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔkundi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Na línu lɛdi lɛdi ka lɛ́si sika ugyiedi lɛbi lɛni nnye Katɔti anumi ekpo ene ammɔ lɛlɔ lɛdubo. 14Lɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛ́su Katɔti ɔtu ɔkundi ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Táƒɛnimi batu ine bani na bényimi bése Euƒrate Ketu bonwu kudɔ!” 15Amu na báƒɛnimi batu ine bamɛni bani na bényimi-ma bése mmɔ bete ka báƒɛnimi-ma na ɔdɔ ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na limeyi lɛmɛni kemmo na kɔbuli kɔmɛni kemmo na lɛkwa lɛmɛni tutuutu kemmo kalɛ na badu bayawine ƒui lɛkpa lɛtɛdi.
16-17Ɔƒɛni na lɛla lɛni bédie bátina-mi mɛni kemmo ni, lɛ́nu bekpone pii bani nlie bapɔnkɔ lɛlɔ bésela kekpokɔ. Na básu-mi bana bumomo ɔni ndi bekyuli bɔka etili eti ene. Na abuala lɛwu lɛni mɔɔgyumana-ma kayi mmɔ égyie aani ogya, na eekeye aani ɛpu ku ogya atabi. Bapɔnkɔ bammɔ eli ese aani bagyata eli, na ogya ku uyɔ ku agyakpabi aalɛ́ taasi-ma inye kemmo. 18Na alakpa atɛ ani ndanku kukpi na ási bapɔnkɔ bamɛni inye kemmo ɔsu ni, bekyuli lɛkpa lɛtɛdi sɔɔn békpi. 19Ɔsika bapɔnkɔ bammɔ ɔyikun ɔkya bana inye ku lɛka kemmo. Bana lɛka libo eli aani balakpi kalɛ, na beeti taadu bekyuli.
20Bekyuli bakladi bani ƒui nétekpi na alakpa atɛ ani ndanku kukpi mmɔ kemmo ni, béténwini kama bátákya ala ani na ama alati béti bana enu bábla bése béte lɛlɔ ka bataakpa. Ala amɛni adanku ayu ekpidi ku bana baƒiɔ bani na béti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi bávɔ ku kalɔ kemmo abuala ku atabi ku egyii ani na bánwi. Nsu ala amɛni ƒui ni, alánu na elenu na elesie muedi! 21Bétenwini kayi na bana bekyuli bɔdu ku evo ala bɔbla kudɔ iye kɔsɔnɔ ala bɔbla ku kuyu kudɔ.

english_text:
The Angel and the Little Scroll
1I saw another powerful angel come down from heaven. This one was covered with a cloud, and a rainbow was over his head. His face was like the sun, his legs were like columns of fire, 2and with his hand he held a little scroll that had been unrolled. He stood there with his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land. 3Then he shouted with a voice that sounded like a growling lion. Thunder roared seven times.
4After the thunder stopped, I was about to write what it had said. But a voice from heaven shouted, “Keep it secret! Don't write these things.”
5 The angel I had seen standing on the sea and the land then held his right hand up toward heaven. 6He made a promise in the name of God who lives forever and who created heaven, earth, the sea, and every living creature. The angel said, “You won't have to wait any longer. 7God told his secret plans to his servants the prophets, and it will all happen by the time the seventh angel sounds his trumpet.”
8 Once again the voice from heaven spoke to me. It said, “Go and take the open scroll from the hand of the angel standing on the sea and the land.”
9When I went over to ask the angel for the little scroll, the angel said, “Take the scroll and eat it! Your stomach will turn sour, but the taste in your mouth will be sweet as honey.” 10I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it. The taste was sweet as honey, but my stomach turned sour.
11Then some voices said, “Keep on telling what will happen to the people of many nations, races, and languages, and also to kings.”
translation_text:
Katɔti Ɔtu Ɔda Kakunkɛ Blii Suɛ Kadi
1Amu na lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔyikune ɔbambadi ka ɔ́si katɔ ɔɔyu. Na ɔ́ka ɔ́mana-nwu aani kɔdi, na bukeye bɔ́ka bɔ́mana-nwu lili. Nwuna anumi eekeye aani ɔƒɛ kalɛ, na nwuna lɛgba lise aani akpa ani nnye kalɔ na aada aani ogya. 2Kakunkɛ blii suɛ kadi kébimi kakya-nwu kɔnu. Na úti nwuna kɔdianu ɔgba únyene ɛpu lɛlɔ, na úti kɔmiinu ɔgba únyene kalɔ lɛlɔ. 3Amu na údie lɛdi momoomo aani gyata kalɛ. Na ka ɔ́va ni, kayaa kábwɛ ogya ku kɔku bonwu maatɛ! 4Ka línu kɔku bonwu kɔmɛni ni, líse kalɔ nnii muunweni lɛla lɛni na línu. Nsu lɛdi lɛdi lɛ́si katɔ na lɛ́su-mi lɛnini, “Ɔlɛka abɛla lɛla lɛni na énu na kɔku bonwu kɔmmɔ kemmo ese, na tenweni-nya.”
5Amu na lɛ́nu ka ɔtu ɔni nnye kalɔ ku ɛpu lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔ́talaku kɔdianu kɔnu katɔ. 6Na ɔ́kpali ala ɔ́lɔ Katɔti lɛnyi. Ɔ́lɔ Anwu ɔni nli ngba ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui ɔni nédie katɔ ku kalɔ ku ɛpu ku ala ani nkya-nya kemmo ƒui. Na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔsɔ ulebile uwi! 7Kabla kabɛdi kani na ɔ́su nwuna kenye bediene bani ndi nwuna kabla bablane ka kadubɔlɛ ni, kadubo kete lɛni si Katɔti ɔtu maatɛdi ɔmmɔ ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ.”
8Ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛdi lɛni nátɛmiku-mi lɛ́si-ku katɔ mmɔ lɛ́sɔ lɛ́su-mi lɛnini, “Sie na atáƒɔ kakunkɛ kani nkya Katɔti ɔtu ɔni nnye ɛpu ku kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ kɔnu kemmo.”
9Amu na lísie ɔtu ɔmmɔ kudɔ na lɛ́su-nwu nnii uti kakunkɛ kammɔ ute-mi. Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ƒɔ, na eti-ka akun! Mɔɔsu-ɔ ka ɔdubo ɔdu bɔyu na ƒula kaƒɔ kemmo, nsu ɔdubɔyu-ɔ emini aani uwɔ na ƒula kenye kemmo.”
10Amu na lɛ́ƒɔ kakunkɛ kammɔ, na lɛ́kun. Na ɔ́yu-mi emini na kenye kemmo. Nsu ka líbweli-ka lɛ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́yu ɔdu na mina kaƒɔ kemmo. 11Nwuna kama ni, ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ɔlɛka asɔ esie anumi eteedie Katɔti litemi lɛni ndanku bekyuli lidu lidu na kalɔ pii lɛlɔ ku adi lidu lidu batɛmine ku baga pii lɛlɔ ete bekyuli.”

english_text:
The Two Witnesses
1 An angel gave me a measuring stick and said:
Measure around God's temple. Be sure to include the altar and everyone worshiping there. 2 But don't measure the courtyard outside the temple building. Leave it out. It has been given to those people who don't know God, and they will trample all over the holy city for 42 months. 3My two witnesses will wear sackcloth, while I let them preach for 1,260 days.
4 These two witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand in the presence of the Lord who rules the earth. 5Any enemy who tries to harm them will be destroyed by the fire that comes out of their mouths. 6 They have the power to lock up the sky and to keep rain from falling while they are prophesying. And whenever they want to, they can turn water to blood and cause all kinds of terrible troubles on earth.
7 After the two witnesses have finished preaching God's message, the beast that lives in the deep pit will come up and fight against them. It will win the battle and kill them. 8 Their bodies will be left lying in the streets of the same great city where their Lord was nailed to a cross. And this city is spiritually like the city of Sodom or the country of Egypt.
9For three and a half days the people of every nation, tribe, language, and race will stare at the bodies of these two witnesses and refuse to let them be buried. 10Everyone on earth will celebrate and be happy. They will give gifts to each other, because of what happened to the two prophets who caused them so much trouble. 11 But three and a half days later, God will breathe life into their bodies. They will stand up, and everyone who sees them will be terrified.
12 The witnesses then heard a loud voice from heaven, saying, “Come up here.” And while their enemies were watching, they were taken up to heaven in a cloud. 13 At that same moment there was a terrible earthquake that destroyed a tenth of the city. Seven thousand people were killed, and the rest were frightened and praised the God who rules in heaven.
14The second horrible thing has now happened! And the third one will be here soon.
The Seventh Trumpet
15 At the sound of the seventh trumpet, loud voices were heard in heaven. They said,
“Now the kingdom
of this world
belongs to our Lord
and to his Chosen One!
And he will rule
forever and ever!”
16Then the 24 elders, who were seated on thrones in God's presence, knelt down and worshiped him. 17They said,
“Lord God All-Powerful,
you are and you were,
and we thank you.
You used your great power
and started ruling.
18 When the nations got angry,
you became angry too!
Now the time has come
for the dead
to be judged.
It is time for you to reward
your servants the prophets
and all your people
who honor your name,
no matter who they are.
It is time to destroy everyone
who has destroyed
the earth.”
19 The door to God's temple in heaven was then opened, and the sacred chest could be seen inside the temple. I saw lightning and heard roars of thunder. The earth trembled and huge hailstones fell to the ground.
translation_text:
Katɔti Úte Kenye Bediene Inyɔ Ɔyikun
1Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti úti ugyii ɔdi úte-mi ɔni nse aani lɛkɔkula. Na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Sie na atákɔku mina kakpakɔ ku lɛbi lɛni lɛlɔ na baakpá na katɔ mmɔ, na aka bekyuli bani ƒui nkya mmɔ beemwi-mi. 2Nsu takɔku keyi, ɔsika béti mmɔ béte bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ. Badubo mmɔ ku ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui lɛgba butu bɔvi abuli aavlene-anyɔ. 3Ndubute mina kenye bediene inyɔ ɔyikun na bedie-mi kenye na emeyi apim unwi ku emeyi eti alɔ ku leevu kemmo. Badubunyimi adala ani mɔɔtina ka beewulo kɔnyana na bekyuli alaekpidi ɔsu.”
4Ɔkya Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo ka nnɔ egyii anyɔ ku sika ugyiedi ligyii inyɔ lɛni lɛlɔ na asogya ɔsia ni, linye Kayawi Ƒui Unwoti anumi na katɔ. Na akpa anyɔ amɛni enye ete Katɔti kenye bediene inyɔ bamɛni. 5Si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́kya ɔkplu ɔnii ɔɔbla-ma kalala ni, ogya ɔdubo bɔlɛ bɔsi bana kenye kemmo na ɔkyula bekisine bammɔ. Na ukyuli biala ɔni mɔɔwia ɔnii ɔɔbla-ma kalala ni, ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani na ɔdubɔsia ukpi. 6Bebo ɔyikun ka betile ɔnantu na ɔsɔ ulana na uwi ɔni kemmo na beedie Katɔti kenye mmɔ. Na bebo ɔyikun lɛnɔ na ntukpa ƒui lɛlɔ kalɛ na baya na bunwini ubugya. Na bebo ɔyikun lɛnɔ na baya na lɛlɛ lidu lidu libo kayawi ƒui lɛlɔ uwi biala na baayɔ́.
7Ɔƒɛni si bédie Katɔti kenye báwɔlɔ ni, eƒiebuo ɔni nási ɔɔlɛ́ kasuudikɔ ubu bonwu ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔdubukpoku-ma na ɔdi-ma lɛlɔ na ɔdu-ma lɛnɔ. 8Bana ɔlɔna ɔdubɔtɛ lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ na ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ na lɛsugba kemmo banii Egyipte iye Sodom. Mmɔ na bákana Blɔti bámana ugyii lɛlɔ. 9Ama bani nási bekyuli ku kadi ku adi lidu ƒui akɔ ku kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ni, badubo bekyuli bamɛni ɔlɔna bɔnu emeyi atɛ ku kakɛ sɔɔn. Nsu badubuni na baláva-ma. 10Na bekyuli bani nlie kalɔ lɛlɔ badubo kubiti bɔkɛ na nkyuli inyɔ bammɔ kukpi ɔsu. Badubo limeyi bɔdi na bete lɛlɔ ala, ɔsika kenye bediene inyɔ bammɔ béti lɛbibo pii béboku kayawi bekyuli lɛlɔ.
11Na emeyi atɛ ku kakɛ kama ni, ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni muute ngba ɔ́si Katɔti kudɔ úbo na úduo-ma lɛlɔ kemmo na báta bénye. Na bani ƒui nánu-ma ni, liƒu lɛ́da-ma. 12Mmɔ na kenye bediene inyɔ bammɔ bénu lɛdi bonwu lɛdi ka lɛ́si katɔ na lɛ́su-ma lɛnini, “Bibo katɔ mɛni!” Ka bana bekisine baanu ni, bákɔ bésie katɔ na kemmo.
13Kɔnakunwi ni, kalɔ bɔkunku kpakplaa bɔdi bɔ́lɛ na ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛkpa leevudi lɛ́bwɛ, na bekyuli mpim maatɛ békpi. Liƒu pim líƒie bekyuli bakladi, na bákɔliku Ati ɔni nkya katɔ lɛnyi katɔ!
14Bɔbuɛ lɛla linyɔdi lɛ́vi, na lɛtɛdi lɛdubo lɛmmɔ kama bɔsia uwi klukui.
Bávwi Kakpɛɛ Maatɛdi
15Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti ɔtu maatɛdi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Na línu ka bekyuli pii báva na katɔ mmɔ básu banini,
“Kayawi lɛga kadikɔ ƒui
kénwini bula Unwoti Katɔti
ku nwuna Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi kadi!
Na ɔdubo lɛlɔ bɔdi ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui!”
16Amu na benengu aavlanyɔ-ine bani nlie Katɔti anumi na bana agaboku lɛlɔ báyu bébi kalɔ na bémwi Katɔti. 17Na baasu banini,
“Blɔti ɔni mbo ɔyikun ƒui,
ɔni nli na úlie,
bɔɔgyá-a enu,
ɔsika áƒɔ ƒula ɔyikun ubendi
na ése kalɔ aadi lɛlɔ!
18Bekyuli bani ƒui nátaƒɔ-ɔ
bátadi ni, béti kɔnyi.
Anwuɔsu ƒula kɔtu bɔni
kúbo-ma lɛlɔ.
Ɔsika uwi údu ka atɛku
bekyuli bekpine litemi.
Ɔdi uwi ɔni na adubɔƒɔ
kayu kabuni ete ƒula kabla bablane
ku kenye bediene ku ƒula bekyuli ƒui.
Na benengu ku banamu bani ƒui
mɔɔbu-ɔ ni,
adubɔƒɔ-ma kayu kabuni.
Na adubɔkyula bekyuli bekpidi
bani nádu ƒula bekyuli na kalɔ lɛlɔ!”
19Amu na bálɛmi Katɔti kakpakɔ kedee, na bánu Bunyimi Adaka kedee ka use mmɔ. Na kayaa kábwɛ ogya ku kɔku bonwu. Na katɔ keedu taasia kama. Kalɔ kákunku, na etubankɛ áyu pii!

english_text:
The Woman and the Dragon
1Something important appeared in the sky. It was a woman whose clothes were the sun. The moon was under her feet, and a crown made of twelve stars was on her head. 2She was about to give birth, and she was crying because of the great pain.
3 Something else appeared in the sky. It was a huge red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and a crown on each of its seven heads. 4 With its tail, it dragged a third of the stars from the sky and threw them down to the earth. Then the dragon turned toward the woman, because it wanted to eat her child as soon as it was born.
5 The woman gave birth to a son, who would rule all nations with an iron rod. The boy was snatched away. He was taken to God and placed on his throne. 6The woman ran into the desert to a place that God had prepared for her. There she would be taken care of for 1,260 days.
Michael Fights the Dragon
7 A war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels were fighting against the dragon and its angels. 8But the dragon lost the battle. It and its angels were forced out of their places in heaven 9 and were thrown down to the earth. Yes, that old snake and his angels were thrown out of heaven! That snake, who fools everyone on earth, is known as the devil and Satan. 10 Then I heard a voice from heaven shout,
“Our God has shown
his saving power,
and his kingdom has come!
God's own Chosen One
has shown his authority.
Satan accused our people
in the presence of God
day and night.
Now he has been thrown out!
11“Our people defeated Satan
because of the blood
of the Lamb
and the message of God.
They were willing
to give up their lives.
12“The heavens should rejoice,
together with everyone
who lives there.
But pity the earth
and the sea,
because the devil
was thrown down
to the earth.
He knows his time is short,
and he is very angry.”
13When the dragon realized it had been thrown down to the earth, it tried to make trouble for the woman who had given birth to a son. 14 But the woman was given two wings like those of a huge eagle, so she could fly into the desert. There she would escape from the snake and be taken care of for a time, two times, and half a time.
15The snake then spewed out water like a river to sweep the woman away. 16But the earth helped her and swallowed the water that had come from the dragon's mouth. 17This made the dragon terribly angry with the woman. So it started a war against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God and are faithful to what Jesus did and taught. 18The dragon stood on the beach beside the sea.
translation_text:
Uleku Ku Ukisine Ɔmmɔ
1Amu na akɔla ala budie taatina bonwu adi áda álɛ kayaa. Na ɔƒɛ ɔ́ka ɔ́mana uleku ɔdi aani kɔdi kalɛ, na kɔbuli kɔkya-nwu lɛgba kalɔ. Na úbi ayabi leevu-inyɔ kagabwa kadi lili. 2Ɔda kaƒɔ. Na ka uwi údu ka ɔwɔ ni, ɔ́va momoomo ka uunú ɔlɛ ɔsu. 3Amu na lɛ́nu akɔla ala bɔnu bɔbambadi lɛnɔ! Liƒu kɔlakpi bonwu kɔdi négyie geen kɔ́da kɔ́lɛ kayaa. Na kubo eli maatɛ ku ese leevu. Na kagabwa kebi-ku lili biala lɛlɔ. 4Na kútiku kayaa ayabi lɛkpa lɛtɛdi ƒui ku nwuna ɔka úbo úbewi kalɔ lɛlɔ. Kunye uleku ɔmmɔ lɛtɔtɔ kalɛ na kuti ubi ɔni na uleku ɔmmɔ wawɔ ɔkun si ɔ́nya ɔ́wɔ-nwu. 5Na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́wɔ ɔnanabi ɔni madi kayawi ƒui lɛlɔ ku ɔyikun kpakplaa. Nsu Katɔti Kɔyu kúkpeli ubi ɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒɔ na kúti-nwu kúsienku Katɔti na nwuna lɛgaboku anumi. 6Na uleku ɔmmɔ úkeli úsie ketele kemmo likpo lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́klibi úse-nwu. Mmɔ na badubo-nwu lɛlɔ bɔnu emeyi apim unwi eti alɔ ku leevu.
7Amu na kekpo kálɛ na katɔ. Na Katɔti ɔtu unengudi ɔni ndi Mikael ɔ́tɔnku Katɔti batu bakladi na báta, na ama ku liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ ku kuna batu lɛnɔ békpo. 8Nsu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kútakana-ma kenye bunye. Anwuɔsu básɔ bátakɛ keliekɔ kadi na katɔ mmɔ. 9Na bábɔku liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ béboku kalɔ. Aku ndi kɔlakpi kɔkukudi bonwu kɔni baalɔ ukisine ɔmmɔ iye Satan, na ɔɔtɔ́lɔ kayawi kemodi ƒui. Bábɔku anwu ku nwuna batu ƒui bábava kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni.
10Ɔmmɔ kama línu lɛdi bonwu lɛdi na katɔ na lɛɛsu lɛnini,
“Ɔƒɛni na Katɔti ngba bɔƒɔ
ku nwuna ɔyikun
ku lɛgadi lɛ́da lɛ́lɛ.
Na nwuna Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi
ɔmmɔ kenyekɔ lɛnɔ
káda kálɛ.
Ɔsika bábɔku baƒɔtaadine ukisine
ɔmmɔ bálɛku katɔ mmɔ.
Anwu muunye bula Katɔti
anumi usien ku ɔƒɛ
taawia baƒɔtaadine
bammɔ litemi.
11Bula banwani bádi-nwu lɛlɔ
ɔkɛnku Koƒonu Ubi
ubugya lɛlɔ
ku litemi geen lɛni kenye
bédie lɛlɔ.
Ɔsika bénye kagyumana ka
beti bana ngba bakpa.
12Anwuɔsu lɛlɔ lɛyɔ
amii bani nkya katɔ mmɔ ƒui!
Nsu muute kalɔ
ku ɛpu ala ƒui bɔbuɛ!
Ɔsika Satan ɔ́ɔda ɔ́lɛ-mii lɛlɔ.
Na úti kɔnyi geen,
ɔsika ɔgyi ka uwi klukui
kani nébu-nwu.”
13Lebo lɛni na liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kɔ́nu kɔ́ti ka bábɔku-nwu bábava kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, úse kalɔ ɔ́bi ɔ́siaku uleku ɔni náwɔ ubi ɔnanabi ɔmmɔ. 14Amu na Katɔti úte uleku ɔmmɔ aasɛ bonwu avwi kalɛ na uveyi uteesie nwuna keliekɔ na ketele kemmo. Mmɔ na badubo-nwu bɔgyumana akwa atɛ ku kakɛ ɔsiku kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kudɔ.
15Ɔmmɔ kama ni, kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kútuo ntu pii bɔdi bɔ́lɛku nwuna kenye kemmo kalɛ na bɔgba butéƒie uleku ɔmmɔ na butiku-nwu bɔtɔlɔku. 16Nsu kalɔ kébunku uleku ɔmmɔ na kébimi kenye na káni ntu bɔni nálɛ bɔ́si kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kenye kemmo ƒui. 17Mmɔ ni, kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kúti kɔnyi kɔ́kya uleku ɔmmɔ geen, na kɔ́gyu kɔ́tɔlɔ kúsie kútékpoku nwuna bawɔ bakladi bani muunú Katɔti litemi na beedie Yesu kenye.
18Amu na kɔlakpi kukpidi kɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ kɔkya ɛpu kɔtu mmɔ.

english_text:
The Two Beasts
1 I looked and saw a beast coming up from the sea. This one had ten horns and seven heads, and a crown was on each of its ten horns. On each of its heads were names that were an insult to God. 2 The beast I saw had the body of a leopard, the feet of a bear, and the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over its own power and throne and great authority to this beast. 3One of its heads seemed to have been fatally wounded, but now it was well. Everyone on earth marveled at this beast, 4and they worshiped the dragon who had given its authority to the beast. They also worshiped the beast and said, “No one is like this beast! No one can fight against it.”
5 The beast was allowed to brag and claim to be God, and for 42 months it was allowed to rule. 6The beast cursed God, and it cursed the name of God. It even cursed the place where God lives, as well as everyone who lives in heaven with God. 7 It was allowed to fight against God's people and defeat them. It was also given authority over the people of every tribe, nation, language, and race. 8 The beast was worshiped by everyone whose name wasn't written before the time of creation in the book of the Lamb who was killed.
9If you have ears,
then listen!
10 If you are doomed
to be captured,
you will be captured.
If you are doomed
to be killed by a sword,
you will be killed
by a sword.
This means God's people must learn to endure and be faithful!
11I now saw another beast. This one came out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon. 12It worked for the beast whose fatal wound had been healed. And it used all its authority to force the earth and its people to worship that beast. 13It worked mighty miracles, and while people watched, it even made fire come down from the sky.
14This second beast fooled people on earth by working miracles for the first one. Then it talked them into making an idol in the form of the beast that did not die after being wounded by a sword. 15It was allowed to put breath into the idol, so it could speak. Everyone who refused to worship the idol of the beast was put to death. 16 All people were forced to put a mark on their right hand or forehead. Whether they were powerful or weak, rich or poor, free people or slaves, 17they all had to have this mark, or else they could not buy or sell anything. This mark stood for the name of the beast and for the number of its name.
18You need wisdom to understand the number of the beast! But if you are smart enough, you can figure this out. Its number is 666, and it stands for a person.
translation_text:
Yohane Ɔ́nu Beƒiebuo Bekpidi Inyɔ Bammɔ
1Ɔmɛni kama lɛ́nu eƒiebuo ɔdi ka ɔ́lɛ ɔ́si ɛpu kemmo ɔ́kɔ ɔɔlɛ́. Ubo eli maatɛ na ese leevu alɛ-nwu eli ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na lise biala lɛlɔ ni, kagabwa kebi. Na nwuna lili biala lɛlɔ ni, lɛnyi lɛdi lɛsia lɛni muudumi Katɔti. 2Eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ use aani ebuoƒuala, na nwuna lɛgba lise aani kegiti lɛgba, na nwuna kenye kese aani gyata kenye. Liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kúti kuna ɔyikun kúte eƒiebuo ɔmɛni ku kuna lɛgaboku ku kenyekɔ kenengudi.
3Eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lili linwi lɛ́tina aani si ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ ɔni na ɔlɛka ukpi nka. Nsu ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́ɔsa. Ɔmɛni ɔ́bla kayawi bekyuli ƒui dɛye dɛye, na basiaku eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ kama. 4Bekyuli bátaalɛ akɔnkɔ teete kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ, ɔsika kúte eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ kenyekɔ kenengudi. Na bátaalɛ akɔnkɔ teete eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ. Na baasu banii, “Ɔma nse aani eƒiebuo ɔmɛni? Na ɔma makana-nwu bukpoku? Ɔdi uuubo!”
5Eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun na ɔ́di ala lɛlɔ abuli aavlene-anyɔ, na ɔ́talaku lɛlɔ katɔ, na údumi Katɔti geen. 6Úse kalɔ uuwida Katɔti lɛnyi ku nwuna keliekɔ ku bekyuli bani ƒui nlie-nwu kudɔ. 7Ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun ka ukpo Katɔti bekyuli na ɔdi-ma lɛlɔ. Kaba biala ku bekyuli lidu ku adi ƒui ku ama bani nási kalɔ biala lɛlɔ béduo nwuna lɛlɔ bɔdi kalɔ. 8Na bekyuli bani ƒui nlie kalɔ lɛlɔ badubɔlɛ akɔnkɔ bete-nwu, ntu bekyuli bani anyi na bénweni bákya ngba ɔku kemmo bése asa na Katɔti údie kayawi. Ngba ɔku ɔmmɔ ɔdi Koƒonu Ubi ɔni na béti bákpa ɔdi.
9Si bibo atu ni,
na binu!
10Ukyuli ɔni na badubo buƒie ni,
badubuƒie-nwu.
Na ukyuli ɔni lɛnɔ na badubo bɔdu
na ɔkɛɛ kenye lɛnɔ ni,
badubo-nwu bɔdu.
Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, amii Katɔti bekyuli ɔlɛka binye lɛbibo biala kenye kpakplaa na bɛsiaku Blɔti ulu lɛlɔ.
11Amu na lɛ́nu eƒiebuo ɔbambadi ɔni nálɛ ɔ́si kalɔ kemmo. Ese anyɔ alɛ-nwu lili aani koƒonubi, nsu ɔ́talaku lɛlɔ katɔ aani liƒu kɔlakpi kɔni muuƒwi. 12Únye eƒiebuo udeedi ɔmmɔ kenye útaabla nwuna kabla. Na únye kayawi kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ beliene lɛlɔ ka balɛ akɔnkɔ bete eƒiebuo udeedi ɔni ɔlɛ nása mmɔ. 13Eƒiebuo unyɔdi ɔmɛni údie akɔla ɔ́tina-ma, na ɔ́ya na ogya muedi ɔ́si katɔ úbo kalɔ lɛlɔ na ukyuli biala anumi.
14Ɔ́tɔlɔ bekyuli bani ƒui nlie kalɔ lɛlɔ na nwuna akɔla bɔbla ani na ɔ́bla ɔkɛnku eƒiebuo udeedi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu. Ɔ́ya na bekyuli bammɔ bése baƒiɔ badi béte lɛlɔ, na bávɔ-ma na bese aani eƒiebuo udeedi ɔni náƒɔ ɔlɛ ka bébeyi-nwu ɔkɛɛ nsu ɔmu uli ngba. 15Eƒiebuo unyɔdi ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun ka ɔnwuna ngba ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔkya eƒiebuo baƒiɔ bani na bése béte lɛlɔ mmɔ kemmo kalɛ na ɔkana butemi, na ɔya na badu bekyuli bani ƒui naaadubo akɔnkɔ bɔlɛ bute-nwu.
16Na eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ únye bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ, banamu ku benengu, balakɛne ku bawabane ku bekyuli bani mɔɔbla bekyuli bamba kabla ku bani mɔɔbla ama alati kabla ka bese-ma likpo na bana kɔdianu kɔnu lɛlɔ iye bana atɛntɛ. 17Ukyuli ɔdi biala ulakana na weye lɛla lɛdi wasiku ɔdi kudɔ iye uye lɛla lɛdi ute ukyuli bamba lɛnɔ si uuubo likpose lɛmmɔ. Na likpose lɛmmɔ nnye nte eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lɛnyi iye bumomo bɔka bɔni nnye lɛnyi lɛmɛni kenye.
18Ntu ebo lɛnunda asa na ala amɛni adubɔbla-a nwaa. Ukyuli ɔni makana ni, ɔwia bumomo bɔni nnye eƒiebuo ɔmɛni lɛnyi kenye kalɔ unu. Ɔsika bumomo bɔmɛni bɔdi bɔka bɔni nnye nte ukyuli lɛnyi. Na bumomo bɔmmɔ ndi 666.

english_text:
The Lamb and His 144,000 Followers
1 I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion! With him were 144,000, who had his name and his Father's name written on their foreheads. 2 Then I heard a sound from heaven that was like a roaring flood or loud thunder or even like the music of harps. 3And a new song was being sung in front of God's throne and in front of the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn that song, except the 144,000 who had been rescued from the earth. 4All of these are pure virgins, and they follow the Lamb wherever he leads. They have been rescued to be presented to God and the Lamb as the most precious people on earth. 5 They never tell lies, and they are innocent.
The Messages of the Three Angels
6I saw another angel. This one was flying across the sky and had the eternal good news to announce to the people of every race, tribe, language, and nation on earth. 7The angel shouted, “Worship and honor God! The time has come for him to judge everyone. Kneel down before the one who created heaven and earth, the oceans, and every stream.”
8 A second angel followed and said, “The great city of Babylon has fallen! This is the city that made all nations drunk and immoral. Now God is angry, and Babylon has fallen.”
9Finally, a third angel came and shouted:
Here is what will happen if you worship the beast and the idol and have the mark of the beast on your hand or forehead. 10 You will have to drink the wine that God gives to everyone who makes him angry. You will feel his mighty anger, and you will be tortured with fire and burning sulfur, while the holy angels and the Lamb look on.
11 If you worship the beast and the idol and accept the mark of its name, you will be tortured day and night. The smoke from your torture will go up forever and ever, and you will never be able to rest.
12God's people must learn to endure. They must also obey his commands and have faith in Jesus.
13Then I heard a voice from heaven say, “Put this in writing. From now on, the Lord will bless everyone who has faith in him when they die.”
The Spirit answered, “Yes, they will rest from their hard work, and they will be rewarded for what they have done.”
The Earth Is Harvested
14 I looked and saw a bright cloud, and someone who seemed to be the Son of Man was sitting on the cloud. He wore a gold crown on his head and held a sharp sickle in his hand. 15 An angel came out of the temple and shouted, “Start cutting with your sickle! Harvest season is here, and all crops on earth are ripe.” 16The one on the cloud swung his sickle and harvested the crops.
17Another angel with a sharp sickle then came out of the temple in heaven. 18After this, an angel with power over fire came from the altar and shouted to the angel who had the sickle. He said, “All grapes on earth are ripe! Harvest them with your sharp sickle.” 19The angel swung his sickle on earth and cut off its grapes. He threw them into a pit where they were trampled on as a sign of God's anger. 20 The pit was outside the city, and when the grapes were mashed, blood flowed out. The blood turned into a river that was about 300 kilometers long and almost deep enough to cover a horse.
translation_text:
Yohane Ɔ́nu Koƒonu Ubi Ku Nwuna Bekyuli
1Ɔmɛni kama ni, lɛ́nu na budie taatina bɔmmɔ kemmo ka Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ unye Sion Kɔbi lɛlɔ. Na bekyuli bani mabla aani mpim eti anyɔ ku aavlene-ine benye mmɔ. Na bekyuli bamɛni atɛntɛ ni, bénweni Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ku Ɔti lɛnyi básia. 2Amu na línu lɛdi bonwu lɛdi lɛni nse aani ntu bɔni mɔɔgbá taayu lɛtakpɛ bonwu lɛdi lɛlɔ na lɛ́sɔ lɛ́lɛ aani si katɔ muudu ku kɔku bonwu. Lɛnɔ ni, use aani ɔnu na bagyane baagyá na lɛbentaa lɛlɔ.
3Na nkyuli mpim eti anyɔ ku aavlene-ine bamɛni badi bekyuli bani na bédie básiku kayawi na bákɛ ngba bɔƒɔ. Na bana ƒui benye lɛgaboku ku Katɔti ngba batu ine bammɔ anumi ku benengu bammɔ anumi. Na béteedie ɔnu ɔwɔdi ɔni na ama lɛti pɛ kani nákana-nwu bɔtɛya. 4Ama ndi bekyuli bani náda lɛlɔ sɛɛn. Na bana lɛlɔ lilese lɛlɔ na lɛsɔnɔdi ala lɛlɔ ɔsu. Ama mɔɔsiaku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ likpo biala na úsela. Ama na bédie bálɛku bayawine ƒui akɔ. Na ama ndi bekyuli bedeedi bani na béti béte Katɔti ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ. 5Likpidi lɛɛɛma bekyuli bamɛni lɛlɔ, na ɔkɔ lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma.
Yohane Ɔ́nu Katɔ Batu Ine Badi
6Ɔmmɔ kama lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔdi ka úveyi ɔɔví kayaa katɔ katɔ ku litemi buni lɛni nse nte uwi biala. Litemi lɛmmɔ lɛsa na úbo úbakɔ ute bekyuli bani nlie kayawi kamɛni lɛlɔ. Na ama ndi kalɔ biala lɛlɔ bekyuli ku kaba biala ku adi ƒui batɛmine ku bekyuli lidu ƒui. 7Ɔ́su ku lɛdi bonwu ɔnini, “Bɛbu Katɔti na bɛkɔliku-nwu lɛnyi katɔ! Ɔsika nwuna uwi údu ka ɔtɛku bayawine ƒui litemi. Bimwi anwu ɔni nábla katɔ ku kalɔ ku ɛpu ku ntukpa ƒui!”
8Katɔti ɔtu unyɔdi ɔsia udeedi kama na ɔɔva momoomo ɔnini, “Úbuli! Babilon bonwu ɔmmɔ úbuli geen! Kayawi bekyuli ƒui báni ɔma ɔmmɔ alaekpidi bɔbla békpi aani ntɛ. Na ɔ́tɔlɔ-ma aani kalɛ na ɔyalɛ ɔɔtɔ́lɔ bekyuli taatákya likpidi kemmo.”
9Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔsia bammɔ kama na ɔɔva ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Bekyuli bani mɔɔlɛ akɔnkɔ teete eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ku nwuna baƒiɔ bani na bávɔ béte lɛlɔ ni, ama náƒɔ eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ likpose na bana atɛntɛ iye kɔnu. 10Ama na Katɔti ɔdubɔya na bani nwuna kɔnyi lɛbibo ɔɔƒɛɛ ku ɔdu kati kati! Ogya ku ogya atabi adubo-ma bɔkyula na Katɔti batu kedee ku Koƒonu Ubi anumi. 11Na ogya ɔni mɔɔkyula-ma uyɔ ɔdubɔkɔ uteesie katɔ uwi ƒui. Na usien ku ɔƒɛ ni, bekyuli bamɛni balákɛ bɔnwuna! Ɔsika ama mɔɔlɛ akɔnkɔ teete eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ku nwuna baƒiɔ, na báƒɔ nwuna lɛnyi likpose.
12“Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔlɛka amii Katɔti bekyuli bani mɔɔdi Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ na bɛsiaku Yesu kama ulu lɛlɔ ni, binye lɛbibo kenye kpakplaa.”
13Ɔmmɔ kama línu lɛdi lɛdi ka lɛ́si katɔ na lɛɛsu lɛnini, “Nweni ala amɛni. Bekyuli bani na lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ-ma ndi bani ndubukpi ka básiaku Blɔti kama ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ɔsu.” Na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔtuna kɔnini, “Ɛɛn, badubɔkɛ bɔnwuna! Na badubɔkɛ bana kabla kɔsia!”
Baasála Kayawi Bekyuli
14Ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛ́nu ƒututuu ɔdi. Na lɛ́nu ka ukyuli ɔni nálɛ Ukyuli Ɔyawine Ubi ulie ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ, na sika ugyiedi kagabwa kebi-nwu lili. Na ɔda lɛsaka. 15Amu na ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔ́lɛ ɔ́si kakpakɔ mmɔ na ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔɔsu ukyuli ɔni nlie ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Awɔ, sala Katɔti bekyuli lɛku kayawi aani kalɛ na beeti lɛsaka taanwa edula. Ɔsika uwi údu ka basala-ma bete-nwu.” 16Amu na ukyuli ɔni nlie lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔ́sala-ma na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.
17Ɔmmɔ kama lɛ́sɔ lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ka ɔ́si Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ ɔ́yu úbo, na anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́da asɔsɔ ɔni mbo ɔbi.
18Na ɔtu ɔbambadi lɛnɔ ɔ́si Katɔti lɛbi lɛmmɔ kudɔ úbo. Na anwu ndi ɔni mɔɔdi ogya lɛlɔ. Ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo na ɔ́su Katɔti ɔtu ɔni nda asɔsɔ mmɔ ɔnini, “Awɔ, sala bekyuli bekpidi lɛku kayawi aani kalɛ na beeti asɔsɔ ɔni mbo ɔbi teede egyiibi. Ɔsika uwi údu ka basala-ma.”
19Anwuɔsu Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́sala bekyuli bammɔ na kayawi lɛlɔ, na úti-ma útéwi kesii kani na Katɔti ɔdubɔni-ma kɔtu aani ebi ani béde béwi ntɛ kablakɔ. 20Na ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu na ɔma ɔmmɔ kabanye aani kalɛ na baamana ntu teedie ebi ammɔ kemmo. Na ubugya ɔ́gba ɔ́si mmɔ, na ɔ́ƒɔ kalɛkɛ kammɔ ƒui. Na ubugya ɔmmɔ bɔgyu ɔdubudu ukyuli limɔ.

english_text:
The Last of the Terrible Troubles
1After this, I looked at the sky and saw something else that was strange and important. Seven angels were bringing the seven last terrible troubles. When these are ended, God will no longer be angry.
2Then I saw something that looked like a glass sea mixed with fire, and people were standing on it. They were the ones who had defeated the beast and the idol and the number that tells the name of the beast. God had given them harps, 3 and they were singing the song his servant Moses and the Lamb had sung. They were singing,
“Lord God All-Powerful,
you have done great
and marvelous things.
You are the ruler
of all nations,
and you do what is
right and fair.
4 Lord, who doesn't honor
and praise your name?
You alone are holy,
and all nations will come
and worship you,
because you have shown
that you judge
with fairness.”
5 After this, I noticed something else in heaven. The sacred tent used for a temple was open. 6And the seven angels who were bringing the terrible troubles were coming out of it. They were dressed in robes of pure white linen and wore belts made of pure gold. 7One of the four living creatures gave each of the seven angels a bowl made of gold. These bowls were filled with the anger of God who lives forever and ever. 8 The temple quickly filled with smoke from the glory and power of God. No one could enter it until the seven angels had finished pouring out the seven last troubles.
translation_text:
Katɔ Batu Badi Bada Lɛbibo Maatɛ
1Na lɛ́sɔ lɛ́nu akɔla budie taatina bonwu bɔbambadi na katɔ bɔni nábla-mi kalɛ kadi. Lɛ́nu batu maatɛ ka bada lɛbibo maatɛ lɛni ndi lɛbibo maatɛ likplodi. Ɔsika ɔmɛni kemmo na Katɔti kɔnyi kúdu kɔ́wɔlɔ.
2Na lɛ́nu kalɔ kani nwi aani ɛpu na use kede kede aani asogya kani kemmo na ogya ɔɔda. Na ɛpu ɔmmɔ amadɔ ni, bekyuli benye beedie lɛnu na baagyá lɛbentaa lɛni na Katɔti úte-ma. Ama nádi eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ku nwuna baƒiɔ ku bumomo bɔni nnye nte nwuna lɛnyi lɛlɔ. 3Na lɛnu lɛni na beedie mmɔ ni, lɛdi Mose ɔni ndi Katɔti kabla ɔblane ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ lɛnu. Na beedie banini,
“Blɔti ɔni mbo ɔyikun ƒui, ƒula ala bɔbla ébomo,
na bulakana-nya kalɔ bunu.
Na ƒula ablala ese siin, na ƒula etemila adi litemi geen.
Awɔ ndi Uwi Ƒui Ɔga.
4Ɔma makana-a anumi bunye na ulayia awɔ Blɔti,
na uleti bumwi ulete ƒula lɛnyi?
Ɔsika awɔ lɛti nse kedee,
na kalɔ ƒui bekyuli badubo babakya-a lili kalɔ.
Ɔsika bédie bátina ka aabla lɛla biala ulu siin lɛlɔ.”
5Ɔmɛni kama ni, lɛ́nu ka bálɛmi kakpakɔ kedee na katɔ. Na adaka ɔni kemmo na Katɔti bunyimi bɔkya ni, use mmɔ. 6Na Katɔti batu maatɛ bani nda lɛbibo maatɛ bammɔ bálɛ bási Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na bakya lɛwu lɛƒualadi lɛni muukeye na sika ugyiedi kɔbuli kɔ́da kɔ́mana-ma kayi. 7Amu na ngba batu ine bammɔ kemmo unwi úti sika ugyiedi kɔlaku kɔni na Katɔti ɔni nli ngba uwi ƒui kɔnyi kúyi úte batu maatɛ bammɔ. 8Na Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo kéyi ku uyɔ ɔni nási Katɔti ɔyikun ku bukeye kemmo. Na ukyuli biala ulakana kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo buduo, amu ntu batu maatɛ bammɔ béti lɛbibo maatɛ lɛmmɔ béboku kayawi báwɔlɔ.

english_text:
The Bowls of God's Anger
1From the temple I heard a voice shout to the seven angels, “Go and empty the seven bowls of God's anger on the earth.”
2 The first angel emptied his bowl on the earth. At once ugly and painful sores broke out on everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol.
3The second angel emptied his bowl on the sea. At once the sea turned into blood like that of a dead person, and every living thing in the sea died.
4 The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and streams. At once they turned to blood. 5Then I heard the angel, who has power over water, say,
“You have always been,
and you always will be
the holy God.
You had the right
to judge in this way.
6They poured out the blood
of your people
and your prophets.
So you gave them blood
to drink as they deserve!”
7After this, I heard
the altar shout,
“Yes, Lord God All-Powerful,
your judgments are honest
and fair.”
8The fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, and it began to scorch people like fire. 9Everyone was scorched by its great heat, and all of them cursed the name of God who had power over these terrible troubles. But no one turned to God and praised him.
10 The fifth angel emptied his bowl on the throne of the beast. At once darkness covered its kingdom, and its people began biting their tongues in pain. 11And because of their painful sores, they cursed the God who rules in heaven. But still they did not stop doing evil things.
12 The sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great Euphrates River, and it completely dried up to make a road for the kings from the east. 13An evil spirit that looked like a frog came out of the mouth of the dragon. One also came out of the mouth of the beast, and another out of the mouth of the false prophet. 14These evil spirits had the power to work miracles. They went to every king on earth, to bring them together for a war against God All-Powerful. But that will be the day of God's great victory.
15 Remember Christ says, “When I come, it will surprise you like a thief! But God will bless you, if you are awake and ready. Then you won't have to walk around naked and be ashamed.”
16 Those armies came together in a place that in Hebrew is called Armagedon.
17As soon as the seventh angel emptied his bowl in the air, a loud voice from the throne in the temple shouted, “It's done!” 18 There were flashes of lightning, roars of thunder, and the worst earthquake in all history. 19 The great city of Babylon split into three parts, and the cities of other nations fell. So God made Babylon drink from the wine cup filled with his anger. 20 Every island ran away, and the mountains disappeared. 21 Hailstones, weighing about 50 kilograms each, fell from the sky on people. Finally, the people cursed God, because the hail was so terrible.
translation_text:
Béwilimi Katɔti Kɔnyi Kɔlaku Maatɛ Béwi Kayawi Lɛlɔ
1Amu na línu lɛdi bonwu lɛdi ka lɛɛtɛmi taasiku Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ úte batu maatɛ bammɔ ɔnini, “Bisie na bitéwilimi Katɔti kɔnyi kɔlaku maatɛ kɔmmɔ biwi kayawi lɛlɔ!”
2Amu na Katɔti ɔtu udeedi úsie na útéwilimi nwuna kalaku úwi kayawi lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na alɛbi álɛ éwi bekyuli bani mbo eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ likpose na baalɛ akɔnkɔ teete nwuna baƒiɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ.
3Amu na Katɔti ɔtu unyɔdi úwilimi nwuna kalaku úwi ɛpu kemmo, na ntu bɔmmɔ búnwini ubugya aani ɔni nkya ukpine. Na lɛla biala lɛni mbo ngba na lɛkya ɛpu kemmo mmɔ líkpi.
4Amu na ɔtu ɔtɛdi úwilimi nwuna kalaku úwi ntukpa ku abiɔ ƒui kemmo na búnwini ubugya. 5Amu na línu ka ɔtu ɔni mɔɔnu ntukpa lɛlɔ ɔ́su ɔnini,
“Awɔ ɔni nli na élie ni,
awɔ nse kedee.
Ɔsika átɛ etemila amɛni ƒui na ulu siin lɛlɔ.
6Bekyuli bamɛni nádu ƒula bekyuli ku kenye bediene.
Anwuɔsu na éte-ma ubugya ukpidi ɔmɛni na báni.
Lɛla lɛni námanku-ma na baaƒɔ́!”
7Amu na línu lɛdi lɛni nási Katɔti lɛbi lɛmmɔ kudɔ ka lɛ́su lɛnini, “Blɔti ɔni mbo ɔyikun ƒui, ƒula litemi bɔtɛ buse siin, na ƒula etemila adi litemi geen.”
8Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔtu unedi úwilimi nwuna kalaku úwi ɔƒɛ lɛlɔ na béte kuƒi ka nwuna ogya ɔkyula bekyuli. 9Na bekyuli bákywi ɔ́si ogya liwulu kpakplaa lɛmmɔ ɔsu. Na béwida Katɔti lɛnyi, ɔsika nwuna ɔyikun ɔsu na lɛbibo lɛmɛni líbo-ma lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui ni, bétenwini kama bátakya bana ekpidi na bemwi Katɔti.
10Amu na ɔtu ɔlɔndi úwilimi lɛla lɛni nkya nwuna kalaku kemmo úwi eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lɛgaboku lɛlɔ. Na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ɔɔdi lɛga ƒui kábla suu kɔnakunwi! Na bekyuli baadu anyi na lɛbibo ɔsu. 11Na bekyuli bammɔ béwida Katɔti, ɔsika bana alɛbi áya na beenú ɔlɛ geen! Nsu bátada bana alaekpidi bɔbla bátaya.
12Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔtu ɔkundi úwilimi lɛla lɛni nkya nwuna kalaku kemmo úwi Euƒrate Ketu kebendi kammɔ kemmo. Na ketu kammɔ kákwii kalɛ na baga bani nási ɔƒɛ katukɔ bakɛ kavinkɔ. 13Amu na lɛ́nu ayu ekpidi atɛ ani nálɛ aani bapɔtɔlɔ ka bási baalɛ́ liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kenye ku eƒiebuo udeedi ɔmmɔ kenye ku eƒiebuo unyɔdi ɔni baalɔ ɔkɔ kenye udiene kenye kemmo.
14Ayu ammɔ ndi ukisine ayu ekpidi ani muudie akɔla taatina. Na ayu atɛ amɛni muusié kayawi baga ƒui kudɔ kalɛ na basala lɛlɔ na bekpo Katɔti bekyuli na Katɔti ɔni ndi Ɔyikune Ƒui limeyi linengudi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.
15“Binu! Ami Yesu ndubo bɔda bɔlɛ-mii lɛlɔ kɔnakunwi aani uyune kalɛ! Lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ ukyuli ɔni nnye kagyumana na ɔda adala ani mɔɔtina ka use siin uwi biala kemmo, kalɛ na ulakɛ kasɔngya ku kɔƒa na kadi akɔ!”
16Amu na ayu ekpidi ammɔ ásala baga bammɔ na likpo lɛni baalɔ na Hebri kemmo bani Armagedon.
17Amu na Katɔti ɔtu maatɛdi úwilimi lɛla lɛni nkya nwuna kalaku kemmo úwi kayaa. Na lɛdi bonwu lɛdi lɛ́ku lɛ́si lɛgaboku kudɔ na Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ, na lɛɛsu lɛnini, “Ɔ́sa!” 18Na kayaa kábwɛ ogya ku kɔku bonwu, na katɔ keedu taasia kama! Na kalɔ kaakunku ɔni na kalɔ bɔkunku bɔmmɔ udu bútalɛ kudii ɔ́si uwi ɔni na Katɔti údie ukyuli! 19Na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔ́bwɛ úle akpa atɛ, na lɛma linengudi lɛkladi lɛni nkya kayawi ekpo ƒui lɛ́bwɛ ƒui. Mmɔ ni, Katɔti únyimo Babilon ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ekpidi na ɔ́ya na ɔ́ni nwuna kɔnyi lɛbibo ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ƒui. 20Na ntuntɛ kɔlɔ ku abi ani ƒui nkya ni, áyii ákya. 21Etubankɛ bonwu adi aani atakpɛ áyu ási kayaa ábaƒiɛmi bekyuli, na béwida Katɔti ɔ́si ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni ɔsu.

english_text:
The Prostitute and the Beast
1 One of the seven angels who had emptied the bowls came over and said to me, “Come on! I will show you how God will punish that shameless prostitute who sits on many oceans. 2 Every king on earth has slept with her, and her shameless ways are like wine that has made everyone on earth drunk.”
3 With the help of the Spirit, the angel took me into a desert, where I saw a woman sitting on a red beast. The beast was covered with names that were an insult to God, and it had seven heads and ten horns. 4 The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet robes, and she wore jewelry made of gold, precious stones, and pearls. In her hand she held a gold cup filled with the filthy and nasty things she had done. 5On her forehead a mysterious name was written:
I AM THE GREAT CITY OF BABYLON, THE MOTHER OF EVERY IMMORAL AND FILTHY THING ON EARTH.
6I could tell that the woman was drunk on the blood of God's people who had given their lives for Jesus. This surprising sight amazed me, 7and the angel said:
Why are you so amazed? I will explain the mystery about this woman and about the beast she is sitting on, with its seven heads and ten horns. 8 The beast you saw is one that used to be and no longer is. It will come back from the deep pit, but only to be destroyed. Everyone on earth whose names were not written in the book of life before the time of creation will be amazed. They will see this beast that used to be and no longer is, but will be once more.
9Anyone with wisdom can figure this out. The seven heads that the woman is sitting on stand for seven hills. These heads are also seven kings. 10Five of the kings are dead. One is ruling now, and the other one has not yet come. But when he does, he will rule for only a little while.
11You also saw a beast that used to be and no longer is. That beast is one of the seven kings who will return as the eighth king, but only to be destroyed.
12 The ten horns you saw are ten more kings, who have not yet come into power, and they will rule with the beast for only a short time. 13They all think alike and will give their power and authority to the beast. 14 These kings will go to war against the Lamb. But he will defeat them, because he is Lord over all lords and King over all kings. His followers are chosen and special and faithful.
15The oceans you saw the prostitute sitting on are crowds of people from all races and languages. 16The ten horns and the beast will start hating the shameless woman. They will strip off her clothes and leave her naked. Then they will eat her flesh and throw the rest of her body into a fire. 17God is the one who made these kings all think alike and decide to give their power to the beast. And they will do this until what God has said comes true.
18The woman you saw is the great city that rules over all kings on earth.
translation_text:
Katɔti Ɔdubo Ɔyalɛ Unengudi Ɔmmɔ Kɔtu Bɔni
1Amu na batu maatɛ bani nda kɔlaku kɔmmɔ kemmo unwi úbo-mi kudɔ na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Bo, na lɛtina-a kalɛ na badubo ɔyalɛ ɔni náƒɔ lɛnyi mmɔ kɔtu bɔni. Anwu ndi ɔma unengudi ɔni na bátu bényene ntukpa pii kudɔ. 2Na kayawi baga bákya béteesie teesie ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo aani kalɛ na banana beesié ɔyalɛ kudɔ. Na ɔma ɔmmɔ ekpidi bɔbla bɔ́ƒɔ kayawi bekyuli lɛlɔ kemmo aani kalɛ na baaní ntɛ teekpi.”
3Ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi úsienku ketele kemmo na kɔyu kemmo. Mmɔ na lɛ́nu uleku ɔdi ka ulie eƒiebuo ugyiedi lɛlɔ. Na bénweni anyikpi ani muudumi Katɔti ƒui básia eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ mbo eli maatɛ ku ese leevu. 4Uleku ɔmmɔ unyimi adi otondi ku egyiedi na úti sika ugyiedi ku asɛɛ ku aseebi ɔ́klibi lɛlɔ. Na ɔda sika ugyiedi ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔdi ɔni kemmo na ala ani na Katɔti ukisi na eesé lɛlɔ éyi tɛtɛɛtɛ ɔkɛnku nwuna lɛyalɛ ala bɔbla ɔsu. 5Na nwuna lɛtɛntɛ ni, bénweni lɛsugba lɛnyi lɛdi básia.
Babilon, Ɔma Unengudi.
Bayalɛ Ƒui Uni Ku Ekisila Ƒui Uni.
6Amu na lɛ́nu ka uleku ɔmmɔ úkpi ntɛ na Katɔti bekyuli bani ubugya na ɔ́ni ku bani na ɔ́du ɔsika benye Yesu kama kpakplaa ɔsu. Uwi ɔni na lɛ́nu-nwu ni, ɔ́bla-mi kalɛ kadi. 7Amu na ɔtu ɔmmɔ úye-mi ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ɔ́bla-a kalɛ kadi? Ndubudie lɛsugba lɛmɛni kalɔ lite-ɔ. Lɛkɛnku uleku ɔmmɔ ku eƒiebuo ɔni lɛlɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ ulie mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ mbo eli maatɛ, na ese leevu alɛ eli ammɔ lɛlɔ. 8Eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ni, úlie ngba dii, nsu ɔsɔ uuubo. Na ɔdubo bɔlɛ bɔsi kasuudikɔ ubu bonwu ɔmmɔ kemmo, na usie na Katɔti ɔyila-nwu udu ƒui. Na bekyuli bani nli kayawi lɛlɔ na bétenweni-ma anyi bátakya ngba ɔku kemmo asa na Katɔti údie kayawi ni, ɔdubo-ma bɔbla kalɛ kadi si banu eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ. Ɔsika úlie ngba dii, nsu ɔsɔ uuubo, na ɔsɔ ɔdubo bɔda bɔlɛ.
9“Asa na ukyuli wenu lɛsugba lɛmɛni kalɔ ni, amu ntu ubo lɛnunda. Eƒiebuo eli maatɛ ku uleku ɔyalɛ ɔmmɔ benye bete ɔma ɔni bátu bálɛ abi maatɛ lɛlɔ. Na eli ammɔ lɛnɔ enye ete baga maatɛ badi. 10Baga ɛlɔ bádi lɛga bávi, na unwi ɔmu ɔɔdi lɛga, na ɔkladi anwu útadi tɔ lɛga. Nsu si úbo ni, ɔdubo lɛga bɔdi uwi klukui ɔdi kani. 11Eƒiebuo ɔni nélie ngba dii nsu ɔsɔ uuubo mmɔ ni, anwu ndi ɔga maanedi. Na nwuna udu use aani baga maatɛ bammɔ kalɛ, na ɔdubo busie na Katɔti ɔyila-nwu udu ƒui.
12“Na ese leevu ani na ánu mmɔ ni, adi baga leevu bani nétese tɔ kalɔ ku lɛga bɔdi. Nsu badubo-ma kuƒi bute uwi klukui na badi lɛga ku eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ. 13Baga leevu bamɛni ƒui bada kasusu kenwi, na beeti bana ɔyikun ku kenyekɔ teete eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ. 14Na badubɔta na bekpoku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ. Nsu Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ku nwuna bekyuli baƒunadi ku nwuna baƒɔtaadine geen badubo-ma lɛlɔ bɔdi. Ɔsika anwu ndi Blɔti ɔni ndi Bati Ƒui Ɔti ku Baga Ƒui Ɔga.”
15Amu na ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ntukpa bɔni kudɔ na ánu ka ɔyalɛ ɔmmɔ ulie ni, amu nnye nte kalɔ ƒui bekyuli ku bani nkya kaba ku kadi ku kalɔ ku adi ƒui kemmo. 16Ese leevu ani nnye nte baga bani na ánu ku eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ni, badubukisi ɔyalɛ ɔmmɔ. Na badubo ala ani nse-nwu ƒui bɔƒɔ bɔsiku-nwu kudɔ na ɔsɔ ɔkɛ utaavi kasɔngya. Badubo-nwu lɛna bɔkun na bakyula lɛni nébu. 17Ɔsika Katɔti úti ɔ́kya-ma kayi kemmo kalɛ babla lɛla lɛni na anwu Katɔti ɔɔwia. Na bénu lɛlɔ kalɔ ka beti bana ɔyikun bete eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ na ɔdi lɛga uti utédu ka Katɔti etemila ani na ɔ́su úse ébo-nwu kemmo lɛni. 18Uleku ɔni na ánu mmɔ ni, anwu unye ute ɔma unengudi ɔni mbo ɔyikun na kayawi baga ƒui lɛlɔ.”

english_text:
The Fall of Babylon
1I saw another angel come from heaven. This one had great power, and the earth was bright because of his glory. 2 The angel shouted,
“Fallen! Powerful Babylon
has fallen
and is now the home
of demons.
It is the den
of every filthy spirit
and of all unclean birds,
and every dirty
and hated animal.
3 Babylon's evil and immoral wine
has made all nations drunk.
Every king on earth
has slept with her,
and every merchant on earth
is rich because of
her evil desires.”
4 Then I heard another voice
from heaven shout,
“My people, you must escape
from Babylon.
Don't take part in her sins
and share her punishment.
5 Her sins are piled
as high as heaven.
God has remembered the evil
she has done.
6 Treat her as she
has treated others.
Make her pay double
for what she has done.
Make her drink twice as much
of what she mixed
for others.
7 That woman honored herself
with a life of luxury.
Reward her now
with suffering and pain.
“Deep in her heart
Babylon said,
‘I am the queen!
Never will I be a widow
or know what it means
to be sad.’
8And so, in a single day
she will suffer the pain
of sorrow, hunger, and death.
Fire will destroy
her dead body,
because her judge
is the powerful Lord God.”
9 Every king on earth who slept with her and shared in her luxury will mourn. They will weep, when they see the smoke from that fire. 10Her sufferings will frighten them, and they will stand at a distance and say,
“Pity that great
and powerful city!
Pity Babylon!
In a single hour
her judgment has come.”
11 Every merchant on earth will mourn, because there is no one to buy their goods. 12 There won't be anyone to buy their gold, silver, jewels, pearls, fine linen, purple cloth, silk, scarlet cloth, sweet-smelling wood, fancy carvings of ivory and wood, as well as things made of bronze, iron, or marble. 13No one will buy their cinnamon, spices, incense, myrrh, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, slaves, and other humans.
14Babylon, the things
your heart desired
have all escaped
from you.
Every luxury
and all your glory
will be lost forever.
You will never
get them back.
15 The merchants had become rich because of her. But when they saw her sufferings, they were terrified. They stood at a distance, crying and mourning. 16Then they shouted,
“Pity the great city
of Babylon!
She dressed in fine linen
and wore purple
and scarlet cloth.
She had jewelry
made of gold
and precious stones
and pearls.
17 Yet in a single hour
her riches disappeared.”
